units.tr: Calvin to the ministers of the Church of Basel.

units.la: NEgotium, cuius causa hominem hunc data opera mittendum ad vos censuimus, paucis complectemur. Nemo enim non incelebri linguae, vt nunc vocant, Occitanae oppido, noua nuper impiorum saeuitia in miseros fratres qui illic dispersi agunt, efferbuit, cum nihil tale suspicaremur. Literas nō ita pridem publicas Senatus Argentoratensis & Basi lienfisobtinueramus, quibus omnium qui tunc per Galliam in vinculis tenebantur, salus & incolumitas commedabatur (omiti Guiliel-mo. Ille à Rege impetrasse dicebatur, vt soluerentur omnes. In hac spe securi acquiescebamus, dum renuntiarum nobis fuit, ignem illic vehementer flagrare. Duo combusti fuerunt de quorum morte ab ipso spectatore audietis. Siquidem Latine vobis narrare queat, quod nobis retulit. Iurimi in vincula coniecti sunt, qui de capite periclitantur, nisi mature obuiam eatur eorum furori, qui iam ebrij duorum sanguine, finem alii qui saeuiendi nullum facturi sunt. Duo illi singularem constantiam ad extremos vsque spiritus exhibuerunt: cum tamen exquisita crudelitate ipsorum patientia tentaretur. Verum qui scimus an eadem aliis constatura sit animi magnitudo? Ferendae ergo in tempore suppetiae, si qua ratione licet, ne terrore concidant, si qui sunt imbecilliores. Deinde summopere cauendum, ne vilescat nobis piorum sanguis, quem scimus esse in conspectu Domini pretiosum. Audimus recens fuisse à Principibus vestris percussum foedus cum Rege nostro, in quo mentio quaedam iniecta fuerit Re-ligionis, ligionis,nescilicet solita seueritate posthac plecterentur,quibus in Religionis sensu vobiscum conueniret. Id si verum est, non omittenda est nobis iuuandorum fratrum tanta opportunitas, quibus ad opem ferendam non modo clara voce nos Christus vocat, sed se deseri conqueritur, si deserantur. Proinde fratres optimi & pietissimi vos pro animi vestri synceritate in hanc causam totos impendite. Quod quia vos vltro facturos confidimus, pluribus non agemus vobiscum. Agedum ergo, apud Senatum vestrum efficite, vt serio Rex appelletur: idque quam fieri poterit breuissime, ne furiosi illi anteuertant. Scitis enim quàm sedula sit eorum improbitas. Dominus Iesus vos nouis Spiritus sui incrementis magis in dies locupletet, fratres eruditissimi, & nobis dilectissimi. Geneuae, xiii. Nouemb. M.D.XXXVII.
units.tr: I will briefly set out the business for which I have deliberately decided to send this man to you. Nobody has failed to hear that in the famous town of the Occitan language, as they now call it, the impious have lately raged with fresh cruelty against our unhappy brothers who live scattered there, though we suspected nothing of the kind. Not long ago we had obtained public letters from the Senates of Strasbourg and Basel, commending the safety and well-being of all who were then held in chains throughout France (leaving out William). It was said that he had obtained from the King that all should be released. Confident in this hope, we were at rest until we were told that a fire was blazing fiercely there. Two men were burned, and you will hear about their deaths from an eyewitness himself, for the man who reported it to us can tell you in Latin. Very many have been thrown into prison, and their lives are in danger unless their fury is quickly checked. Those men are already drunk with the blood of two, and they will make no end of raging. The two who died showed remarkable constancy to their last breath, although their patience was tested by exquisite cruelty. But who knows whether the same greatness of spirit will last in others? Help must therefore be brought in good time, if there is any way to do it, so that those who are weaker are not crushed by terror. Then we must take the greatest care that the blood of the godly does not become cheap in our eyes, for we know it is precious in the sight of the Lord. We hear that a treaty has recently been struck with our King by your princes, in which some mention was made of religion, to the effect that, with their usual severity, they would henceforth punish those who agreed with you in matters of faith. If this is true, we must not let slip such a welcome opportunity to help our brothers, to whom Christ calls us not only with a clear voice, but also complains that he is forsaken if they are forsaken. Therefore, most excellent and most devoted brothers, devote yourselves wholly to this cause, with the sincerity of your hearts. Because we are confident that you will do so of your own accord, we will not say more to you. Come now, bring it about before your Senate that the King is seriously petitioned, and that this be done as quickly as possible, so that those madmen do not get ahead of us. For you know how persistent their wickedness is. May the Lord Jesus enrich you more and more each day with the new increases of his Spirit, most learned brothers and most beloved to us. Geneva, 13 November 1537.

units.la: CALVINVS GRYNAEO S.
units.tr: Calvin to Grynaeus, greetings.

units.la: Quando mirificas & prope incredibiles esse Satanae artes, quibus vna cum opere nostro assidue nos impetit, satis iam experti sumus, minime nos fefellit malitiosa eius vafricies, qua nos per Carolum iuum nuper adortus est. Nam & eiusmodi certamina omnia multo ante opinione concepteramus, & ad ea sustinenda eramus animo parati. Itaque cum Arrianae primum haereseos, paulo post etiam Sabellianae insimulari nos audiuimus, nihil nos istorum valde pertubauit, cum & ad tales calumnias aures nostrae pridem obduruissent, & spes certa esset, in fumum mox exituras. Purgationem duntaxat, quae prae manibus erat, obiecimus, qua piis omnibus ac integris viris satisfieri abunde posset. Conscriptus enim aliquanto ante catechismus a nobis fuerat, Gallice etiam editus, vbi sub vna Dei essentia nos Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum complecti testabamur: alterum tamen ab altero sic distinguebamus, ne quis sinistrae suspicioni locus relinqueretur. Christum nempe docebamus verum & naturalem esse Dei Filium, qui vnam cum Patre diuinitatem ab aeterno possedit, carnem nostram suscepisset secundum tempus redemptioni nostrae destinatum. Cum pergeret rabiosa illa bestia, conuentum Ministrorum totius Bernensis ditionis dari no bis perimus, apud quem innocentiam nostram defenderemus. Fratres Gallicae linguae prius Laufannam coacti sunt, quo etiam duo e Senatu Bernensi, ac Ministri duo missi sunt. Quaecunque conflari mendacia potuerant, bonus ille vir in vnum fasciculum collegit. Venerat enim ad accusationem instructus, quo omodo Iurisconsulti praecipiunt, nempe cum sacco paratus. Verum totum illum saccum nostra refutatione sic exhausimus, vt ne minima quidem suspicio in hominum animis resideret. Demum
units.tr: Since we have now had enough experience of Satan's wonderful and almost incredible arts, with which he assails us constantly along with our work, we were not at all deceived by his malicious cunning, by which he has lately attacked us through your Charles. For we had long foreseen all such conflicts and had prepared our minds to endure them. So when we heard that we were first accused of Arian heresy and shortly afterwards of Sabellian heresy, none of this greatly disturbed us. Our ears had long since grown hardened to such calumnies, and we were confident that these charges would soon vanish into smoke. We only put forward the defence that lay to hand, one by which all godly and upright men could be fully satisfied. A catechism had been written by us some time before, also published in French, in which we testified that under the one essence of God we embrace Father, Son and Spirit. Yet we distinguished one from another in such a way that no room was left for sinister suspicion. Namely, we taught that Christ is the true and natural Son of God, who from eternity possessed one divinity with the Father, and who took on our flesh at the time appointed for our redemption. As that raging beast kept on, we asked that an assembly of the ministers of the whole Bernese territory be granted to us, before which we might defend our innocence. The brethren of the French tongue were first summoned to Lausanne, and to it two members of the Bernese Senate and two ministers were also sent. That good man gathered into one bundle whatever lies could be concocted. For he had come prepared for the accusation, as the jurists instruct, that is, equipped with a bag. But we so emptied that whole bag by our refutation that not even the least suspicion remained in men's minds.

units.la: Epist.5. ventum est ad nostrae confessionis recitationem, in qua lecem circiter errores ipse quidem animaduertit, alij pene omnes, nihil non pium efle ac sanctum iudicarunt. Ita nos Synodi sententia fuimus absoluti, ille indignus iudicatus, qui minsterio fungeretur. Tali exitu nihilo demissiorem factum argut perpetua eius impudentia: saccum illum futilem, magis quam antea refertum attulit: vbi a nobis excusa omnia fuerunt, quibus suspicionem aliquam de tempore praeterito iniicere conabitur, producta est confessionis nostrae reforma, quae omnibus aliis criminibus absoluta, vno duntaxat capite rea fiebat, quod Christus illic affirmatur ille efle Iehouah, qui a seipso semper habuit vt eflet, quam criminationem discutere promptum fuit. Nam fi distinctio specialis, quae est inter Patrem & Verbum, huncab illo efle dicemus. Si autem Verbi essentia consideratur, quatenus vnus est cum Patre Deus, quicquid dici de Deo potest, in illum competit. Iam quid nomen Iehouah significat? quid illud quod Moi dictum fuit? Ego sum qui sum. Huius dicti Christum auctorem facit Paulus. Apud te quidem, piosque omnes in approbanda eius sententiae veritate non laboramus, sed noluimus taciturn praeteriri perditi huius calumniatoris malignitatem, ne quidquam ad vos, secus quam res haberet rumor, deferret. Nihil enim dici apertius poterat, quam habet nostra confessio: Christum Sermonem esse illum aeternum ex Patre ante secula genitum. Verum nisi duplicem Deum comminisci libet, de eius essentia differamus oportet non aliter, ac de vnius Dei sententia. Atque hac ratione, cui non satisfaceret, nemo praeter ipsum repertus est. Fratres vt dignum erat fidis Christi Ministris, nos iniquissime in suspicionem aliquam adductos sibi videri pronunciarunt. In nostra autem confessione nihil improbandum fe animaduertifle. Dum haec geruntur, afferuntur a Myconio literae publicae ad conuentum scriptae. Aliae rursum a Capitone ad Farellum generatim mifle, quibus vtrisque intelle&um, est, horrendum longe lateque rumorem de nostra controuersia peruagatum efle. Denique ad excitandam erga nos gentium omnium inuidiam maliciose a certis hominibus fabrefactum. Quod autem homo nihili futilissima sua vanitate tantum proficere potuerit, vt tot Ecclesiis fiuistram de nobis opinionem iniiceret: id vero est, quod nos vehementer perturbauit. Siquidem non leuis momenti rem esse ducebamus, si caput Religionis nostrae praecipuum, inter nos controuerti aduersarij nostri audiunt, vel Ecclesiae quidquam de nobis tale suspicarentur. Eo autem grauius hoc nuntio perculsi fumus, quod id ne timere quidem nunquam in mentem venerit. Speramus tamen fore, vt Domini bonitate inanes illi fumi discutiantur propepropediem, ac in capita impiorum referdat, quicquid mali Christo, eiusque Ecclesiae intentarunt. Coepit enim iam affulgere Domini manus, atque virtus eius sese exerere, ad extinguenda haec qualiacunque exordia. Sycophanta ille Senatuscon-sulto in exilium actus est, nos plane absoluti, non a crimine modo, sed ab omni quoque suspicione. Quanquam vero se Athanasij titulo nunc venditet, qui poenas luat defensae fidei: nullum tamen fore periculum videtur, ut orbis pro Athanasio sacrilegum, scortatorem, homicidam sanctorum multorum sanguine madentem agnoscat. Qualem dum istum praedicamus, nihil dicimus, quam quod solidis testimoniis reuincere fumus parati. Haec tibi paucis significata volui, ne iniquis improborum delationibus absentes sic inaudIti (ut fit) opprimamur. Exemplar etiam Confessionis ad te mitto, quod cum tuis Collegis communices. Magnopere enim referre duco, ut ne obscuris rumoribus exagi emtur. Simul te obestor, ut tum Confessionem ipsam, tum has literas ad illos ipsos etiam fratres mittendas cures, aut potius ipse propriis tuis literis eorum animos placare intendas. Vale. Dominus Iesus vos omnes Spiritu suo impleat, quo vnanimes nominis sui gloriam propagare possitis. Bernae.
units.tr: Epist.5. the reading of our confession came round, and although he himself noted some ten errors in it, almost all the others judged that nothing in it was not pious and holy. Thus we were acquitted by the verdict of the Synod, and he was judged unworthy to hold the ministry. Yet his unfailing impudence was not in the least humbled by this outcome: he brought forward that trifling bag, now fuller than before. When everything he had tried to use to cast some suspicion on our past conduct had been answered by us, there was produced a revised version of our confession, which, though cleared of all the other charges, was guilty on one count alone: that it affirms Christ to be that Jehovah who has always had being from himself. This accusation was easy to answer. For if we speak of the special distinction that exists between the Father and the Word, we say that he is from the Father. But if the essence of the Word is considered, insofar as he is one God with the Father, whatever can be said of God applies to him. Now what does the name Jehovah mean? And what is that which was said to Moses: I am who I am? Paul makes Christ the author of this saying. We do not labour to convince you and all pious men of the truth of this view; but we did not want the malice of this lost calumniator to pass unnoticed, lest he report anything to you otherwise than the facts warrant. For nothing could be stated more plainly than our confession states it: that Christ is that eternal Word begotten of the Father before the ages. Unless we choose to invent two Gods, we must discuss his essence in the same way as we discuss the one God's. And by this reasoning, no one has been found, apart from himself, who was not satisfied. The brethren, as befitted faithful ministers of Christ, declared that we seemed to them to have been drawn into some suspicion most unjustly, and that they had noticed nothing in our confession that needed condemning. While these things were going on, public letters written to the assembly were brought from Myconius. Others again were sent generally from Capito to Farel, and from both we understood that a horrible rumour about our controversy had spread far and wide. And that it had been maliciously fabricated by certain men to stir up hatred of us among all nations. But that a man of no account, by his most trifling vanity, could have achieved so much as to give a sinister opinion of us to so many churches: this is what greatly disturbed us. For we considered it no small matter if our adversaries were to hear that the chief article of our religion was under dispute among ourselves, or if the churches were to suspect anything of this kind about us. We were struck all the more heavily by this news because we had never even thought to fear it. Yet we hope that, by the goodness of the Lord, those empty fumes will soon be dispelled, and that whatever harm they have aimed at Christ and his Church will be turned back upon the heads of the impious. For the hand of the Lord has already begun to shine forth, and his power to show itself, to quench these beginnings, whatever they were. That sycophant has been driven into exile by a decree of the Senate, and we have been fully acquitted, not only of the crime but of every suspicion. Although he now parades himself under the title of Athanasius, who suffers punishment for defending the faith, there seems to be no danger that the world will acknowledge as Athanasius a sacrilegious man, a whoremonger, a murderer, drenched in the blood of many saints. In describing him thus, we say nothing beyond what we are ready to prove by solid testimony. I wished these things to be indicated to you briefly, lest we, being absent, be overwhelmed, as usually happens, by the unjust denunciations of the wicked, and unheard. I am also sending you a copy of the Confession, so that you may share it with your colleagues. For I consider it of great importance that we should not be stirred up by obscure rumours. At the same time I urge you to see to it that both the Confession itself and this letter are sent to those brethren, or rather that you yourself seek to calm their minds by your own letter. Farewell. May the Lord Jesus fill you all with his Spirit, so that with one mind you may be able to spread the glory of his name. From Berne.

units.la: Tuus Calvinus.
units.tr: Yours, Calvin.

units.la: CAPITO FARELLO.
units.tr: CAPITO TO FAREL.

units.la: GRatiam & pacem. Eiectio ista ignominiosa non est, neque tantopere nocitura Ecclesiae Domini ac nos formidabamus. Nam de vobis neque hostes exstimati aliud praedicat, quam zelum feruen iorem. Peritiores vero rerum Ecclesiasticarum, cernunt in causa fuisse totam cohortem ministrorum, Evangelium docentium sine disciplina, imo nefasientium, an disciplina sit in Ecclesiam revocanda. Ociosam enim functionem quidam tueri malunt quam fructuosam, quidam licentiam pro Christi libertate induxerunt, quasi ab Euangelio stent quicunque iugum Pontificium abiecerint. Aliqui vero, id est plerique omnes, animaduertentes rem Christi in dies abire in peius, optaret quidem restitutam auctoritatem ministrorum, sed aut veram eius reparandae rationem ignorant, aut eam videntes desperant prorsus. Ex quo nostrae Ecclesiae omnes ad vnam sine disciplina sunt Ecclesiis necessaria. In qua re, quid incommodi vobis, quid improbis ansae ad turbandos datum, in manibus habemus. Auditis enim, Tyranni estis voluistis in liberam Ecclesiam, voluistis nouum pontificatum reuocare, atque id genus contumeliarum re-
units.tr: Grace and peace. That ignominious ejection is not what we feared, nor will it do so much harm to the Church of the Lord. For enemies themselves report nothing about you except a more fervent zeal. Those more experienced in ecclesiastical affairs see that the whole band of ministers who teach the Gospel without discipline was the cause, or rather, that they are doing wrong in asking whether discipline should be restored to the Church. For some prefer to defend an idle office to a fruitful one, and some have introduced licence in the name of Christian liberty, as if whoever has cast off the Papist yoke must therefore stand apart from the Gospel. But others, indeed most, notice that the cause of Christ is declining for the worse every day. They would certainly wish for the authority of the ministers to be restored, but either they do not know the true way of repairing it, or, seeing it, they despair of it altogether. From this it follows that all our churches, without exception, are without the discipline that is necessary for the churches. In this matter we have in our hands what harm has come to you and what occasion has been given to wicked men to stir up trouble. For, as you hear, they say that you are tyrants and that you wanted to bring back a new papacy into a free Church, and they hurl this kind of insult at you, though their own judgment fights against it. Seditious men accuse you of these things. The brothers, however, whom you think have pushed you to extremes, have nothing to complain of except your vehemence. Ah, my brother, I would like you to know what sweat I expend here, rolling the same stone.

units.la: Epist.6. pugnante animi iudicio in vos iactant seditiosi. Fratres autem quos putatis extrema vobis admolitos, nihil habent, quàn quod de vehementia queruntur. Ah mi frater, velim scires, quid sudore hic voluam idem saxum. Bucerus est totus in publicis & am plis rebus tractandis summa animi cötentione, respectu nostram Ecclesiam tumultuanter, neque enim ei curae vacare potest. Recte tamen praescribit nunc aliis de qua re Domino gratiam habeo. Ego qui reputo mecum, qua in parte Ecclesiae & quibus praesim, pastore reipsa agere nonnihil conor, at quanquam procellae à Symmyftis & à Senioribus in partem curarum vocatis! Nam semper existimat, ad nos nihil attinere, quid quisque agat, quasi nihil sit quod Christus ait, ouem centesimam abeuntem inuestigandam esse, & ea eius quaerendae ratio non sit, quam ibidem praescripsit Christus. Corripe inter te ipsum, adhibe testem admonitionis, dic Ecclesiae, sit vt Ethnicus &c. Deuorandi sunt multa indigna, sed interim hoc solatij Dominus dedit, vt optimo Symmyfta stipatus sim, patientissimo audiendarum contumeliarum. Deinde non successit infaelicissime, & quos putabamus deploratissimos, eos inuenimus obsequentissimos consiliis melioribus. Quid multis? Dominus videre dat, quid sit agere pastorem, & quantum praecipiti iudicio vehementiaque incosulta abiiciendi ita Pontificis, nocuerimus. Nam frenum prorsus excussit multitudo, qua afluecta est & educata propemodum ad licentiam, quasi auctoritatem pontificiorum frangendo, vim verbi, Sacramentorum & totius ministerij euacuaremus. Nam clamant, Teneo fatis Euangelij, ipse scio legere: quorsum mihi tua opera? Praedica volentibus audire, deferas eisdem optionem ampletendi quod velint. Iustum erga me iudicium Domini, quo erudior, ad verbi Dei virtute penitius insipiciendam, ad omnem ordinem Dei intelligendum. Ergo quia res difficilis reparatio disciplinae, & nostris Ecclesiis insoles, inuisa carni & sanguini, aut non animaduersa, aut neglecta synergis, neque extra Lutheri Ecclesiam una vspiam fit recte instituta, miraremur, quod vos duo semel tantam vrbe reformare non potueritis? Sic in negotij difficultatem reiicere causam praestiterit, & ita solent fere vel mediocriter periti rerum Ecclesiasticarum. Sunt tam crassa vitia in multis, vt iure boni offendantur: sed cum eos Deus vocatione atque officio dignatur, quid faciemus nos homunciones? Scimus quanti detrimenti ac damni sit vel simultatulam superesse in Ecclesia: & experimur Satanam nihil aeque admoliri, quàm vt ea late pertentet sanctissimos, quo perrahantur in contentionem, vel specie promouendi Euangelij. Docuit me id Christus meus experiundo munus pastorium. Neque dubito, quin sis expertus ampliora meis periculis. Vocatus es ad Neocomum Ecclesiam primam
units.tr: Epist.6. Bucer is wholly absorbed in public and wide-ranging affairs, with the greatest exertion of mind, so that he cannot give time to our church, which is in turmoil. Yet he rightly lays down the rules for others now, and for this I thank the Lord. As for me, when I consider within myself in what part of the Church and over whom I preside, I try somewhat to act as a true pastor. Yet what storms from the Symmystae and the elders, who have been called into a share of the cares! For they always think that it is no concern of ours what each person does, as if Christ's words meant nothing, that the hundredth sheep that has gone astray must be sought out, and as if there were no method of seeking it such as Christ prescribed in the same place: "Go and reprove him between you and himself, take a witness of the admonition, tell it to the Church," and so on. Many unworthy things must be swallowed, but meanwhile the Lord has given this comfort: that I have been supported by the best of Symmystae, most patient in hearing insults. Then it has not turned out most unhappily, and those whom we thought most desperate we have found most compliant with better counsels. What more shall I say? The Lord allows us to see what it is to act as a pastor, and how much harm we have done by our headlong judgment and ill-considered vehemence in casting off the Papal authority. For the multitude has altogether shaken off the bridle, having been reared and brought up almost to licence, as if by breaking the authority of the Papists we had emptied the power of the Word, of the Sacraments and of the whole ministry. For they cry out, "I hold the Gospel in my hands, I can read myself: why do I need your work? Preach to those who want to hear; leave them the choice of embracing whatever they wish." It is a just judgment of the Lord upon me: the more I am taught, the more I should examine into the power of God's Word and understand the whole order of God. Therefore, since the restoration of discipline is a difficult thing, and strange to our churches, hated by flesh and blood, either not noticed or neglected by the synergists, and since nowhere outside the Church of Luther has it been properly established, should we be surprised that you two could not reform so great a city at once? To place the cause in the difficulty of the task is the better course, and this is how even moderately skilled men in ecclesiastical affairs usually reason. There are such gross faults in many that good men are rightly offended; but when God deigns to call them to office and duty, what shall we poor little men do? We know how great a loss and damage it is for even a little quarrel to remain in the Church, and we see that Satan attempts nothing so eagerly as to spread it widely among the most holy, so that they may be dragged into contention, even under the pretext of advancing the Gospel. My Christ has taught me this by experience in the pastoral office, and I do not doubt that you have experienced worse things than my dangers. You were called to be the first minister of the church at Neuchâtel;

units.la: Mat. 18.12. & 15. mam tui ministerij: sequaris Domini, vt vt secus tibi sic debilitato grauissimis fluctibus videatur. Propone animo, eum populum vnice commissum. Iuuat alios sine offensione (quantum vales) bonorum: exemplo Ecclesiae ac ministerij tui prouocentur alij, ambobus defixus in Deum praesentem, qui ex praescripto suo vocationis ad aedificationem quenque vult agere, & videbis, mi frater, tantum successum, quantum sperare nullus potuisset. Dura patientia nobis opus est in hac dissolutione qua versamur: & animi vinciendi agglutinandique Christo rationibus charitatem redolentibus, quae tempera metum est ardentis animi, cum nos admonet iudicij syncerioris, vt quenque estimemus ex eius affectu corrigendum. Vale.
units.tr: Mat. 18.12. & 15. follow the Lord, so that, though to you, thus weakened, it may seem otherwise amid the heaviest waves. Keep before your mind that this people has been committed to you alone. It is a pleasure, without giving offence to the good (as far as you can), that others be stirred up by the example of your church and ministry, while you fix your eyes on God, who is present, and who wishes each man to act according to his calling for edification, by his own prescribed rule. Then you will see, my brother, a success greater than anyone could have hoped for. We need hard patience in this dissolution in which we are caught up, and the means of binding and joining our souls to Christ must be such as breathe charity. The measure of this is the fear of an ardent spirit, when it reminds us of a purer judgment, so that we may think each person is to be corrected according to his disposition. Farewell.

units.la: GRYNAEVS CALVINO S.
units.tr: GRYNAEUS TO CALVIN, GREETINGS.

units.la: Vae iste & quorum de vobis tam graues querelae sint, ego nescio. Nullae dum enim ad nos venerunt. Capito non semel ad me scribit vltro vestra omnia excusans, & valde Ecclesiae vestrae bene cupiens. Rumor principio grauis sane fuit, qui meipsum quoque turbauit, cum in isto praesertim argumento contendere vos audirem de appellationibus personarum diuinarum, & a consuetis vocibus instituere recedere. Ea enim res videbatur amplius prae se ferre. Verum vbi ad nos confessio tua venit, neminem video qui non satis sibi factum putarit. Mihi priuatim valde doluit, ab iis grauem in Ecclesia contentione esse exortam, quorum vterque mea esset amicitia & consuetudine visus diu. Etiam hoc mirabar, quomodo tantum incendium & tandiu durans, & vixdum extinctum me latuisset. Hoc queri apud Farellum memini, ac aliud praeterea nihil: nisi quod dicere veferi me, ne rudis & noua Ecclesia nisi caute administraretur sub initia, capere magnum incommodum possit ab istis conten-tionibus. Sic igitur ex me habe, neminem scire me qui de vobis queratur. Carolum talem esse qualem pingis, haud egre adducor vt credam, postquam ad illos a vobis secessionem facit. Quid enim instituit aliud, quam quod tu melius praedicis. Promiserat mihi & Mauro hic amplissime. Valeat igitur, valeat. Nostru est in ista magna rerum difficultate modis omnibus iugi & diuelli minime pati. Pestis est Ecclesiae nostrae vna haec pernitiosa maxime, quod suspicionibus valde inter nos laboramus: & fratres de fratribus raro candide vereque sentimus, cum lenire oporteat, & in partem optimam omnia trahere: & non ante finis tre de fratre suspicari, quam ipsa res euentufq; coegisset. Ah quam malum est eos quos nosse Christum credimus, in suspicione praue rapere subito. Ita quod suspectum erit nobis, inutile reddimus. Literas Capitonis quibus optime de vobis sentire & testatur, miserem ad te, nisi putem ipsum de re eadem ad te saepius scripsisse. Quod Farellus de comite consulit, exequar apud Capitonem. Tu valebis interea. Ametnus in Domino vere no, & illi toto corde seruiamus. Saluta fratres omnes diligenter Farellum, Viretum cumprimis diligentissime. Dominus Iesus nos in suam sanctam voluntatem feruet. Amen.
units.tr: What these complaints are, and who made such grave accusations against you, I do not know, for none have reached us. Capito has written to me more than once, excusing everything on your side and wishing your Church every good. At first the rumour was certainly serious and it troubled me too, since I heard that you were contending on this very question about the names of the divine persons and departing from the customary terms. That matter seemed to carry more weight. But when your confession came to us, I found no one who did not think himself satisfied. I was personally very grieved that such a serious dispute had arisen in the Church between men of whom each has long been counted among my friends and intimates. I was also surprised that so great a fire, burning so long, could have escaped my notice when it had scarcely gone out. I recall complaining of this to Farel, and nothing more, except that I said I feared that the rude and new Church, unless it were carefully governed at the outset, might suffer great harm from these contentions. So take it from me that I know of no one who complains of you. I am not hard to persuade that Caroli is such as you depict him, since he has broken away from you and gone over to those men. For what else has he done than what you say he does better? He had promised me and Mauro here very generously. Let him go, then, let him go. In this great difficulty of affairs it is our duty, in every way, to keep close together and by no means to allow ourselves to be torn apart. The single most pernicious plague of our Church is that we labour greatly under mutual suspicions, and that we seldom think of our brethren with candour and truth, when we ought to soothe matters and interpret everything in the best light, and not to suspect a brother before the outcome itself has forced us to. Ah, how wrong it is that we rashly seize on those whom we believe to know Christ in an evil suspicion! Thus we make useless whatever we have come to suspect. I would send you the letter of Capito, in which he testifies that he thinks very well of you, were I not sure that he has written to you about the same matter more than once. As to what Farel asks about the count, I shall attend to it with Capito. Farewell in the meantime. Let us truly love one another in the Lord, and let us serve him with our whole heart. Greet all the brethren diligently: Farel, and above all Viret, most diligently. May the Lord Jesus keep us to his holy will. Amen.

units.la: Grynaeus.
units.tr: Grynaeus.

units.la: GRYNAEVS CALVINO.
units.tr: GRYNAEUS TO CALVIN.

units.la: Gratia & Pax.
units.tr: Grace and peace.

units.la: TErnis tuis literis haec tandem, vir & frater amantissime & colendissime, respondeo. Piumest votum fratrum Geneuatium: & nostri sine officij praetermissione deesse voto illorum non possunt. Antonium audio & Morandum ea doctrina & syncerita te eximios haberi, qui haud quaquam dissimulaturi sint, si quid peccetur grauius a Geneuensibus. Equidem nec scio quid agatur Geneuae, nec quales homines isti duo sint. Verum dum non a vobis modo, sed a noltrisetiam hominibus didici, qui rerum modo Geneuae potiuntur, eos a Christi studio alienos esse, tum in vos etiam & disciplinam Ecclesiae admisisse tam atrocia, valde vereor & merito, vt istis Rempub. gubernantibus, Religio & disciplina morum miserè habeat. Qui enim non est cum Domino, & cum eo non colligit, is est contra eum, & dispergit. Iam successoribus vestris rem tolerabilem esse depulsos Pastores gregis Dominici a grege suo tanta peruersitate, tanta importunitate, documento est eos aut non intelligere quid sit esse Pastorem gregis Dominici, aut valde auersum a Christo animum habere. Sed quam tolerabile illis sit, vos a grege Domini depulsos eo furore, nescio. Dominus donet illis sensum suum. Vt vero nunc res habent, non est quod de legatione illa nobis polliceri valeamus. Dominus pia illa pastora seruet, & viam illis ostendat, & expediat, qua Ecclesia illa vere restituatur. Haec ad primas literas. Alterae nihil quam innocentis & vere pij adolescentis confessoris Domini commendationem in se continebant: cui ego adfui pro mea virili & adero. Ipse puto scribit: sic enim statuit. Iam ad tertias. Post multam deliberationem huc deuenimus, Capito, Sturmius & ego. Nisi luculenter spes obiiciatur fructus alicuius maioris, quam ex otio tuo & simul eo negotio quod te Christo hic suscipere cupimus, adhuc censemus te debere ad nos venire. Paruus quidem hic numerus est eorum quibus seruies: inter hos autem sunt in quibus multum fructus speres, tum etiam qui tua cura valde indigeant. Denique qualecunque ministerium hic fit, confidimus id non inutile fore ad illud, vt opus Domini quod Sabaudicis Ecclesiis per tuum ministerium exhibitum est, in suam fidem & auctoritatem restituatur. Id enim nunquam fine offensa Dei cogitandum, te ministerio vel tantillo tempore subducere, dum vllus ministerij locus offeretur. Facefle quod tua vnius grauissima culpa res Christi sic labefactæ sint Genevæ: non tamen pia erit eiusmodi pœnitentia, qua in ista Ministrorum, qui i lonei sunt, inopia, tu istis dotibus non tibi, sed Ecclesiæ ornatus, oblatum ministerium repudies. Quod ad Farellum attinet, nos liberè ei scriberemus, nobis videri, nec Ecclesiis nec tibi vtile, te eò loci nunc agere, vbi acceptum vulnus quotidie nouis incisionibus exacerbetur. Nec audimus res melius habere Genevæ, aut officium facere vestros successores. Iam metuo illis à iudicio grauissimo illo Domini, ne fi scientes & prudentes desint officio, in tanta Ecclesiæ afflictione, tradantur in reprobum sensum, vt indies designent atrociora. Hæc vero fi euenient, quod Dominus auertat, quid aliud eritte in eo loco confistuere, quàm te iugi detere carnificine? Merito enim ista cuiusque sanctI & pro domo Domini zelantis animum lancinent, & excrucient summopere. Sed fit vt mitius agat cum illis Dominus, adhuc tamen nescio vnde sperarem, non plus adhuc malorum extiturum illic, quàm tu etiamnum ferendo fis. Adderemus & nolle nos detinere te nostro tam parvo ministerio, sed tantum te cupere spatium tibi dari, te plenius ab illo labore recreandi. Hæc sane apposita nunc quidem haberemus, donec aliud tempus aliud consilium afferret. Vale in Domino charissime Caluine semper.
units.tr: At last I reply to your letters, my most loving and esteemed brother. The wish of the Geneva brethren is a pious one, and our people cannot fail that wish without neglecting their duty. I hear that Antonius and Morandus are held in high regard by you for their teaching and sincerity, and that they will by no means conceal it if anything more serious is done amiss by the Genevans. Indeed, I neither know what is going on at Geneva nor what sort of men those two are. But since I have learned, not only from you but also from our own people who now hold power at Geneva, that they are alien to the zeal for Christ, and that they have allowed such atrocities against you and against the discipline of the Church, I greatly and rightly fear that, while these men govern the commonwealth, religion and the discipline of morals are in a wretched state. For he who is not with the Lord, and does not gather with him, is against him and scatters. That your successors have driven the pastors of the Lord's flock from their flock with such perversity and such importunity is proof that they either do not understand what it is to be a pastor of the Lord's flock, or have a mind very averse to Christ. But how tolerable it is for them that you have been driven from the Lord's flock by that frenzy, I do not know. May the Lord give them his sense. As things now stand, we cannot promise anything about that embassy. May the Lord preserve those pious pastors, and show them the way and the means by which that Church may truly be restored. So much for your first letter. The second contained nothing but a commendation of an innocent and truly pious young man, a confessor of the Lord; I was present for him as far as my strength allowed, and I will continue to be. He himself, I think, is writing, for he has decided so. Now to your third letter. After much deliberation, Capito, Sturm and I have come to this: unless some clear hope is held out of a greater fruit than your leisure and, at the same time, the work we wish you to undertake here for Christ would bring, we still think you ought to come to us. The number of those you would serve here is indeed small, but among them are some from whom you may hope for much fruit, and others who greatly need your care. Finally, whatever ministry is done here, we trust it will not be useless toward restoring to its former trust and authority the work of the Lord that was carried out in the Savoyard Churches through your ministry. For it must never be thought, without offence to God, that you should withdraw from the ministry, even for a very short time, while any place of ministry is offered. Granted that through your one most grievous fault the cause of Christ has been so shaken at Geneva; yet it will not be a pious penitence of that kind if, in this lack of suitable ministers, you refuse the ministry offered to you, a ministry you are fitted for by those gifts, which adorn you not for yourself but for the Church. As for Farel, we would write to him frankly that it seems to us useful neither to the Churches nor to you that you should now be working in a place where the wound received is daily aggravated by fresh incisions. Nor do we hear that things are going better at Geneva, or that your successors are doing their duty. I fear that they, under that most grievous judgment of the Lord, lest knowingly and wisely they fail in their duty amid such great affliction of the Church, will be given over to a reprobate mind, so that they daily devise more atrocious things. But if these things happen, which the Lord forbid, what else will it be to set yourself in that place than to be torn to pieces by a constant executioner? For such things rightly gnaw at and torment the soul of anyone zealous for the house of the Lord. But may the Lord deal more gently with them; yet I still do not know from where I could hope that there will not arise there more evils than you are still enduring. We would add that we do not wish to keep you bound to our so small ministry, but only that you desire to be given time to recover more fully from that labour. These things, indeed, we would have to propose for now, until another time and another plan brings something else. Farewell in the Lord, dearest Calvin, always.

units.la: Grynæus tuus.
units.tr: Your Grynaeus.

units.la: CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: Calvin to Farel, greeting

units.la: Gratia tibi & pax à Domino frater animo meo dilectissime.
units.tr: Grace to you and peace from the Lord, my brother, most beloved to my heart.

units.la: ITa tumultuarie Basilea me proripui, vt quas ad te literas relicturum me promiseram, inter innumeras cerebri mei tricas mecum abstulerim. Neque iam res vlla præ manibus scriptione digna erat. Triduò postquam appuli, non defuit nuntius, & erat iam oblatum nonnihil argumenti. Sed quòd timebam ne literas periculosè committerem, malui hucvsque differre. N. suo more rescripsisse, non inficiatus est Bucerus. Nam hoc vnum causatus est cur mihi non recitaret, quia nollet
units.tr: I left Basel in such a headlong rush that I carried off with me, amid the countless tangles of my mind, the letter I had promised to leave you. Nor is there now any matter at hand worth writing about. Three days after I arrived there was no lack of a messenger, and some subject matter had already been offered. But because I feared I would be entrusting the letter to danger, I preferred to put it off until now. Bucer did not deny that N. has written back in his usual manner. For this was the one reason he gave for not reading the letter to me: he would not want to stir my bile to no purpose

units.la: Epist. 9. mihi frustra stomachum mouere. Hinc collige quantum amarulentiæ fuerit, quod ille iudicauit pro sua prudentia non posse à me sine graviori offensione transmitti. S. interim placidam eius comitatem deprædicat. Spem enim ducit, posse nobis & ipsum & Senatores, qui infesti hactenus fuerunt, nobis reconciliari, si priores beneuolentiam literis declaremus. Quod vt est perquā ridiculum, Bucerus pro nihilo habuit. Finge id sperari posse. Unde tamen inciperemus? An nos quasi offensionis auctores illos mitigare studebimus? Atque vt non detrectemus id quoque, quis eiit offensarum purgandarum tenendus modus? Ego vero neq; ita emendatum iri præterita, neque in posterum rite prouisum iri censeo. Siquidem, vt coram Deo & eius populo fateamur, im peritia, socordia, negligentia, errore nostro factum ex parte es-se, vt Ecclesia nobis commissa tam misere collapsa sit: ex officio tamen nostro est, innocentiam puritatemque nostram afferre aduersus eos, quorum fraude, malignitate, improbitate, nequitia, eiusmodi ruina procurata fuit. Libenter ergo apud Deum & pios omnes fatebor, dignam fuisse nostram tum infscitiam, tum incuriam, quæ tali exemplo castigaretur: culpa nostra corruisse miseram illam Ecclesiam, nunquam sum concessam. Longe enim aliter fumus nobis conscij in Dei conspectu. Neque enim quisquam hominum est, qui nobis vllam culpæ portiunculam transcribere queat. Iam in futuru quis non videat ludibrio nos expositum hac ratione iri? Nemo enim non protinus clamaret, nihil probri nos recusare, modo reflitueremur. Sed D. vt spero meliorem viam aperiet. Neque enim scribere desiit Bucerus: cuius auctoritas contemni ab illis non poterit: contemni autem apparebit, nisi tandem aliquid ei concedant. Hæc porro illi est spes vltima, vt si conuentum non impetrabit, vsque ad proximum, vel tunc saltem remedium inueniat. Et forte ita expedire Dominus prouidet, quo interim melius omnia maturescat. Concionem habui die Dominico: quæ vt omnium fratrum clogiis fuerat apud plebem commendata, multos habuit vel audiitores, vel spectatores. In animo est fratribus, si videbunt aliquam Ecclesiolæ faciem extare, Cœnæ quoque ministerium concedere. Cum apud Mediomatrices omnia Religioni infesta forent, & Senatu in eius excidium coniurato, & adnitentibus furiosè sacrificis, illuc quoque sex Anabaptistarum ad excitandam nouam offendicularum penetrauit. Duo in Mosellam præcipitati, tertius exilio cum stigmatis ignominia mulctatus. Quantum affec qui potui coniectura, consortille & comes Hermanni vnus eorum fuit. Vereor ne lues ista late inter simpliciores grassata sit ea iin vrbe. Dominus te reliquo sq; sei uos suos sibi conseruet, opusque suum per manus vestras fortunet. Eos omnes mihi salutabit. Nominatim Thomam & alios qui tecum mihi hospites fuerunt.
units.tr: (Epist. 9.). From this, gather how much bitterness there was, since he judged, in his prudence, that it could not be sent by me without a more serious offence. Meanwhile S. extols his placid courtesy. For he holds out hope that both he himself and the Senators, who have hitherto been hostile, can be reconciled to us, if we first declare our goodwill in letters. Bucer regarded this as utterly ridiculous. Suppose it could be hoped for. Where would we begin, though? Shall we eagerly try to soothe those men, as though we were the authors of the offence? And so that we may not refuse even this, what measure is to be kept in purging offences? For my part I think neither that past matters will be duly put right in this way, nor that the future will be duly provided for. For, to confess before God and his people, it is partly through our inexperience, sloth, negligence and error that the Church committed to us has collapsed so wretchedly; yet it is our duty to assert our innocence and purity against those by whose fraud, malice, wickedness and villainy such a ruin was brought about. I will gladly confess before God and all the godly that our ignorance and carelessness deserved to be chastised by such an example; that the wretched Church collapsed through our fault I have never conceded. For we are conscious of ourselves in God's sight quite differently. Indeed there is no one among men who could transfer to us any small portion of the blame. As for the future, who does not see that we will be exposed to mockery in this way? For no one would not at once cry out that we refuse no disgrace, provided we were restored. But the Lord, as I hope, will open a better way. For Bucer has not ceased to write; his authority cannot be despised by them, yet it will appear despised unless at length they concede something to him. This is his last hope: that if he does not obtain a meeting, he may at least find a remedy by the next one, or then at least. Perhaps the Lord so provides that it is expedient, so that meanwhile all things may ripen better. I preached on the Lord's day. As it had been commended to the people by the praise of all the brothers, it drew many hearers or spectators. The brothers intend, if they see some face of a little church standing, to grant the ministry of the Supper as well. When among the Mediomatrices everything was hostile to Religion, the Senate conspiring for its destruction and the priests striving furiously, six Anabaptists also made their way there to stir up a new crop of scandals. Two were thrown into the Moselle, and a third was punished with exile and the disgrace of branding. As far as I could conjecture, his companion and Hermann's comrade was one of them. I fear this plague has spread widely among the simpler folk in that city. May the Lord keep you and his own safe for himself, and prosper his work through your hands. Greet all of them for me, especially Thomas and the others who were my hosts along with you.

units.la: CALVINVS FIDELIBVS GENEVENSIBVS.
units.tr: CALVIN TO THE FAITHFUL OF GENEVA.

units.la: Dilectissimis fratribus ex Genevensis Ecclesiae dispersione. Misericordia Dei patris nostri, et gratia D.N. Iesu Christi, vobis semper multiplicetur per Spiritus sancti communicationem.
units.tr: To my most beloved brothers, from the scattered Church of Geneva: may the mercy of God our Father and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be multiplied to you always through the communion of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: ABstinui hactenus à scribendo fratres dilectissimi, cum mihi persuaderem Farelli literis, qui hoc in se communi nomine receperat, vobis satisfactum iri: ac simul occasionem maledicendi illis qui eam captant, ita praereptam vellem: ne videlicet nobis imponerent, quasi vos ad nos pelliciedo, vos ipsos inter vos scinderemus. Non potui tamen diutius me continere, quin scripto vobis & meum erga vos animum testarer, & vestri apud Dominum recordationem, quorum vtrunque ad officium meum pertinet. Sed neque obstabit deinceps ille timor qui me retinuit hactenus, cum mihi satis constet praetextum quem illi affingerent vt detraherent de nobis, plane vanum & inanem esse. Testis est nobis Deus, & veltra conscientia coram ipsius tribunali, nos quandiu versati sumus inter vos, vnice studuisse, vt vos omnes in pace & concordia foueremus. Ab illis autem qui abscesserunt à nobis vt partes seorsim ducerent, scissio accidit tum in vrbe tum in Ecclesia. Atque vbi illius incendij fumum percepimus, omne operam dedimus (vt coram Domino, cui seruimus) vt remedio adhiberemus. Quare tempus elapsum nos abunde asserit ab omnibus illorum calumniis. Nunc vero dum ad vos scribimus, vt nostri memoriam apud vos conseruetis, probro hoc nobis verti non debet. Confidimus enim in conscientiis nostris coram Domino, nos ex ipsius vocatione vobiscum coniunctos: vt penes homines non sit tale vinculum abrumpere. Ac prout nos ante gessimus, ita speramus Domino facientes nos porro gesturos, vt nullum obiectum vel materiam praebeamus turbae vel diuisionis, nisi illis qui sese ita obfirmarunt contra Dominum Iesum Christum atque vniuersum populum eius, vt nullam cum ipsius seruis coniunctionem admittant. Si enim istiusmodi hominibus optimus Seruator ille scandalum est & offendiculum, qui nobis aliter cedat, qui ipsius stigmata & corpore & spiritu circumferimus? Illud vero nos sustinet, quod illis causa à nobis non offeratur: vt neque optimus ille noster herus aduenit, vt vllam cuiquam molestiam afferret, sed vt esset omnibus via, per quam inoffensi incederet. Enimuero cum ma-
units.tr: I have held back from writing to you until now, most beloved brothers, because I was persuaded by Farel's letter, since he had taken this task on in our common name, that you would be satisfied by it. At the same time I wished to cut off from those who seek it the opportunity for slander, so that they could not charge us with drawing you to ourselves and thereby splitting you apart among yourselves. Yet I could no longer restrain myself from bearing witness to you in writing, both to my affection towards you and to my remembrance of you before the Lord. Both of these belong to my duty. Nor will the fear that has held me back until now stand in the way from here on, since it is clear enough to me that the pretext they invented to disparage us is wholly empty and vain. God is our witness, and your own conscience before his tribunal, that as long as we lived among you we aimed only at keeping you all in peace and harmony. But a schism came about, both in the city and in the Church, from those who withdrew from us to form separate parties. When we perceived the smoke of that fire, we did everything we could (as before the Lord whom we serve) to apply a remedy. So the time that has passed sufficiently shows that we are free from all their calumnies. Now, however, when we write to you so that you may keep us in your memory, this should not be turned into a reproach against us. For we trust in our consciences before the Lord that we are joined to you by his calling, so that it is not within human power to break such a bond. Just as we have conducted ourselves before, so we hope, by the Lord's doing, to conduct ourselves in future: giving no occasion or material for disturbance or division, except to those who have so hardened themselves against the Lord Jesus Christ and his whole people that they will admit no fellowship with his servants. For if that most excellent Saviour is a scandal and a stumbling block to such men, what else should we expect, who bear his marks in body and spirit? Yet this sustains us: that we do not give them any cause from our side. Indeed, our most excellent Master did not come to cause anyone trouble, but so that he might be a way along which all could walk without stumbling.

units.la: b. j. nus Domini in vos adhuc sit extenta, vt audio,ad vos exercen-dos: ac iusta ipsius permissione totus in eo sit Satã,vt Ecclesiam quæ inter vos erigi coeperat, prorsus dissipet, vos demum officij commonefieri expedit.Sic igitur statuite ac vobiscum reputate, quicquid mali infit in illis qui vos turbant & affligunt,eiusmodi tamen insultus quibus vos impetunt,non tam ab hominibus esse quàm ab ipso Satana,qui eorum nequitia vtatur,vt appositò instrumento ad vos impugnandos.Eò pertinet illa Apostoli exhortatio, cùm air, Non esse nobis collutationem aduersus carnem & sanguinem, id est aduersus homines, sed aduersus rectores tenebrarum & spirituales malitias. Noftis quam necesse sit exploratum habere quicum res nobis sit, vt teneamus qua via illi sit obsistendum.quare si in illud incumbimus, vt certando cū hominibus vltionem persequamur & nostras priuatas iniurias, quid effecturi simus in dubio est: illud verò extra controuersiam, ea ratione nos à Satana superatum iri. Contrà verò si eo animo cum hominibus congredimur, vt vnius Christi nomine illos infensos nobis habeamus, ita demum obsistemus machinationibus aduersarij illius spiritualis, instructi illis telis quibus suos armatos esse voluit Dominus: vt de victoriæ certitudine nullo modo dubitandum sit. Hoc si vobis est in animo, videte fratres ne malum malo retundatis: sed vt potius exuti omnibus affectibus prauis, vnius Dei zelo præditi sitis,què & Spiritus ipsius moderetur ex verbi præscripto. Illud præterea vobis cogitandum est,illa vobis non contigisse sine Domini dispensatione,qui opera tur etiam per malos pro consilio bonæ suæ voluntatis. Atque illa cogitatio appositæ erit vobis, vt à vestris illis aduersariis auersi,descendatis in vosmetipsos:sic agnoscetis quàm merito vestro ita vos nunc exerceat Dominus, vt vestram negligentiam castiget, atque verbi sui contemptum, cessationem etiam & defectum in illo legitima obedientia prosequendo. Quis enim vestrum hic se à peccato immunem obtedat?Liceat quidem apud homines iustitiam vestram afferre, atqui vestra vos conscientia apud Deum hac in parte accusabit.Hanc rationem tenuerunt nimirum serui Dei in summis suis angustiis: vt vndecunque illis mala imminerent animum semper ad Deum ipsum intendrent atque ad propria peccata, vt sibi ipsis imputarent quod ita à Domino tractarentur.Nouerat nempe Daniel quæ fuisset Regis Babylonij improbitas in opprimendo & excindendo populo Dei, vt suam vnius auaritiam ambitionem, impotentiam expleret.Conflabat illi inquam, quàm iniquè ab illo tyranno Iudæi illa paterentur:nihilominus sibi tatum & suis summam causam imputat, cum Babylonios nihil aduersum ipsos potuisse perse,statutum apud se habeat.Ergo vt rectum ordinem teneat, orditur à confessione peccatorum tum suorum, tum etiam Regum ac populi. Quod si ita se tantus Propheta deiecit, expendamus quæso, quàm iusta sit nobis illius imitandi ratio: si inquam ita ipsum se coram Deo humiliare oportuit, vt ab ipso miseri-cordiam eliceret, quàm præpostere fiet à vobis, si in vnam aduersariorum improbitatem defixi, in vos ipsos & vestra peccata potius non inspexeritis, quæ longè aliter se habent, quàm quæ ita tum in sese Propheta agnouit? Quod ad nos attinet, si causa nobis dicenda sit contra improbos calumniatores qui nos oppressos vellent, hoc habemus, non modo stare nos conscientiæ nostræ testimonio coram Domino, sed etiam superesse nobis quo nos apud vniuersum mundum purgemus. Atque hoc abunde ostendimus, cùm nos obtulimus ad reddendam omnibus rationem, adeoque coram nostris aduersariis. Omnino enim de suo iure constare illi debet, qui se ita iudicio sistat, vt præter vnam iuris sui certitudinem, omnibus in rebus futurus sit inferior. Quod autem de ipso Domini iudicio præfatus sum, sic accipio, vt non immerito nos hic etiam ab illo humiliatos agnoscam, vt nostram ignorantiam, imprudentiam & alias infirmitates in memoriam reuocaremus. Sic enim apud me sentio de meipso, sic etiam coram ipsius Ecclesia meos defectus proficeor. Neque sic nos notando aduersarios in iure superiores reddemus: vt neque Danielis mens fuit Nabucadnezarem culpa eximere, dum Iudæorum excidium ab ipsius tyrannide profectum, ipsorum peccatis adscriberet: illud potius ad cumulandum ipsius probrum pertinuit, cùm ita constitit tyrannum illum Dei flagellum extitisse, vt eo in genere primum locum Satan cum suis mancipiis occupat. Non magis etiam timendum nobis, ne ius nostrum hominum probris obnoxium reddatur. Cùm enim nos obtulerimus ad respondendum de nostra synceritate in muneris nostri functione coram vniuersis Ecclesiis, vt eodem animo nunc etiam fumus: quis inde colligat ansam illis oblatam à nobis esse, vt nos mordeant, atque nobis insultent? Quod si non datur nobis vt illos obstruamus, vti non defuerunt, qui non sua tantum intemperie aduersum nos abrepti, sed efferato impetu sese in omnia conuitia effunderent, constat tamen nobis certissima illa Domini promissio, Dominum nempe patefacturum innocentiam nostram vt auroram, & iustitiam nostram vt solem in meridie. Illa nos confidentia merito sustinet aduersum omnes improbos, vtcunque coram Domini tribunali infinitis modis obnoxios nos esse profiteamur. Nec tamen in nostra deiectione & humiliatione deferet nos Dominus, quin amplissimo solatio nos afferat atque confirmet. Imò illud nobis obuium est in ipsa Scriptura, cùm testatur fetulas illas suas quas erga seruos suos adhibet, ad illorum profectum & salutem spectare, si modo recturn illarum vsum tenuerint. Illud igitur dilectissimi fratres, vobis perpetuo in mentem veniat quo vos consolemini: tempe quantumuis impij vestram Ecclesiam euertere contenderint, vestra vero peccata non illud modo, sed quiduis etiam acerbius commerita sint, Dominum tamen eum finem allarum vestris afflictionibus, vt in salutem vestram cedant. Ira eius nimirum erga ipsius Ecclesiam ad momentum est, quia ipsam perdere non cogitat: Misericordia vero aeterna ad venturas generationes porrigitur, a patribus nempe in filios & filios filiorum. Iam si in vestros aduersarios oculos coniecceritis, aperte illic agnoscetis vt se ipsos in exitium dent praecipites, cum tamen in portu se iam nauigare sibi ipsis persuadeant. Ne igitur animum desponderetis eo nomine, quod ita Domino visum est vos humiliare ad tempus, cum ipse idem ille fit, Scriptura teste, exaltans nempe deiectum & contemptum ex puluere, pauperes ex coeno: Coronans gaudio gementes & in lacrymas effusos, restituens lucem iacentibus in tenebris, in vitam denique reuocans qui in vmbra mortis sedent. Sperate igitur optatum illum exitum ab optimo Domino, vnde nobis materia extet praedicandae gloriae singularis ipsius erga vos clementiae. Atque sub illa spe confirmate vos ipsos, vt subeatis ipsius ferulas, donec tandem suum vobis fauorem reipsa exhibeat. Neque vero hoc voto seriusaccidet, si omnia vt par est, prouidentiae ipsius permittere didicerimus, quae vna nouit tempora & occasiones: ac multo melius quam quisquam nostrum animo complectatur, tenet quid expediat. Imprimis vigilate in orationibus, & supplicationibus. Si enim spes omnis vestra in Deo sita est, vt esse debet, cor demum in coelum ferri, & illic versari oportet ad illum inuocandum, & implorandam ab eo quam expectatiis misericordiam: sic habete, quod vt plurimum remoratur exitum vororum fidelium suorum, illud eo spectare, vt eos magis afficiat ad ipsius bonitatem exquirendam. Atque adeo vana est omnis nostrae fiduciae in illum iactatio, nisi illam ita testificamur, cum ad ipsum nos precando recipimus. Neque etiam legitimus ille ardor constat nostris precibus, nisi continuo im illis perseueramus. Oro Deum totius consolationis, vt vos erigat & fulcientet magis ac magis in recta patientia, dum vos in istis tribulationibus exercet: atque suis illis promissionibus plane confirmet, Neminem suorum a se tentatum iri supra quam ferendo fit, sed cum probatione daturum & vires, & exitum tandem cum salute coniunctum. Valete. Argentorati 1. Octobr.
units.tr: Since the hand of the Lord, as I hear, is still stretched out against you to chastise you, and since by his just permission all of Satan's effort is directed at utterly destroying the Church that had begun to be built up among you, it is expedient at last to remind you of your duty. So settle this in your minds and reflect on it with one another: whatever evil there is in those who trouble and afflict you, the assaults by which they attack you come not so much from men as from Satan himself, who uses their wickedness as an instrument fitted for attacking you. To this belongs the Apostle's exhortation, when he says that our struggle is not against flesh and blood, that is, against men, but against the rulers of darkness and spiritual wickedness. You know how necessary it is to be clear about whom we are dealing with, so that we may know in what way he must be resisted. So if we set ourselves to pursue vengeance and our private injuries by contending with men, what we will accomplish is doubtful; but it is beyond dispute that in that way we will be overcome by Satan. On the other hand, if we engage with men in such a spirit that we hold them as enemies for the sake of Christ alone, then at last we will resist the schemes of that spiritual adversary, armed with the weapons with which the Lord wished his own people to be equipped, so that there is no room at all for doubt about the certainty of victory. If this is your intention, brothers, take care not to repel evil with evil. Rather, stripped of all depraved passions and filled with zeal for God alone, let his Spirit also guide you according to the rule of his Word. Moreover, you must consider this: these things have not befallen you without the Lord's dispensation, for he works even through the wicked, according to the counsel of his good will. This thought will also serve you well, so that, turning away from those adversaries, you may descend into yourselves. Thus you will recognise how rightly the Lord now exercises you, to chastise your negligence, your contempt of his Word, and also your slackness and failure in pursuing lawful obedience. For which of you here could claim to be free from sin? You may indeed bring forward your righteousness before men, but your conscience will accuse you before God on this point. The servants of God held to this principle in their greatest distress: whatever evils threatened them, they always directed their minds to God himself and to their own sins, so that they would impute to themselves that they were so treated by the Lord. Daniel knew well how wicked the king of Babylon was in oppressing and destroying the people of God, in order to satisfy his own greed, ambition and lust for power. He was well aware, I say, how unjustly the Jews suffered at that tyrant's hands; nevertheless he held it as settled that the main cause lay with himself and his own people, and that the Babylonians could accomplish nothing against them apart from that. So, to keep the proper order, he begins with the confession of sins, both his own and those of the kings and the people. If so great a prophet humbled himself in this way, let us consider, I beg you, how just it would be for us to imitate him. If he had to humble himself so before God in order to win mercy from him, how perverse will it be for you, if you fix your eyes only on the wickedness of your adversaries and do not look rather at yourselves and your sins, which stand quite differently from those that the prophet acknowledged in himself? As for us, if a cause must be argued against wicked calumniators who would oppress us, we have this: not only do we stand upon the testimony of our conscience before the Lord, but we also have the means to clear ourselves before the whole world. We have shown this well enough when we offered to give an account to everyone, and indeed before our adversaries. For he who submits himself to judgement in such a way must be certain of his right, yet be ready, in all other matters, to be the lesser party. As for what I have said about the Lord's own judgement, I take it in such a way that I rightly acknowledge that we too have been humbled by him, so as to call to mind our ignorance, imprudence and other weaknesses. For this is how I think of myself, and this is how I confess my failings before his Church too. Nor by thus censuring ourselves will we make our adversaries superior to us in right. Daniel's purpose was not to excuse Nebuchadnezzar of guilt when he ascribed the destruction of the Jews, which came from that tyrant's cruelty, to their own sins. Rather, it served to heap up the king's disgrace, since it was clear that the tyrant had been God's scourge in such a way that Satan with his henchmen held the first place in that kind of work. Nor should we fear, further, that our right may be made subject to men's reproaches. For since we have offered to answer for our sincerity in the discharge of our office before all the Churches, and since we are still of the same mind, who could infer from this that we have given them an occasion to bite us and to insult us? Even if we cannot stop their mouths, as some have not been lacking who, carried away not only by their own intemperance against us but also by a frenzied impulse, pour themselves out in every kind of abuse, we nevertheless hold fast to that most certain promise of the Lord, that the Lord will bring our innocence to light like the dawn and our righteousness like the noonday sun. It is rightly this confidence that sustains us against all the wicked, however much we may confess that before the tribunal of the Lord we are liable in countless ways. Nor will the Lord, in our dejection and humiliation, abandon us, but will bring us the greatest consolation and strengthen us. Indeed, this is evident in Scripture itself, where it testifies that the chastisements which he applies to his servants aim at their progress and salvation, provided they keep the right use of them. So, most beloved brothers, let this always come to your minds as your comfort: however much the wicked may strive to overthrow your Church, and however much your sins have deserved not only this but something even more grievous, the Lord has nevertheless determined that your afflictions shall turn out for your salvation. For his anger against his Church lasts only a moment, because he does not intend to destroy it; but his eternal mercy extends to coming generations, from fathers to sons and to the sons of sons. Now, if you look upon your adversaries, you will clearly see them hurling themselves headlong to their own destruction, though they persuade themselves that they are already sailing into harbour. So do not lose heart on this account, that the Lord has seen fit to humble you for a time. For he is the same one who, as Scripture testifies, exalts the cast down and the despised from the dust, and the poor from the mire; who crowns with joy those who groan and dissolve in tears; who restores light to those lying in darkness; and who at last calls back to life those who sit in the shadow of death. Hope, then, for that longed-for outcome from the best of Lords, from whom there is material for proclaiming the singular glory of his clemency towards you. And in that hope strengthen yourselves, so that you may bear his rod until he at last shows you his favour in fact. Nor will this happen later than the desired time, if we learn to commit everything, as is fitting, to his providence, which alone knows the times and the occasions, and which holds what is expedient far better than any of us can grasp in his mind. Above all, be watchful in prayers and supplications. For if all your hope is placed in God, as it ought to be, your heart must at last be lifted up to heaven and dwell there, in calling upon him and imploring from him the mercy you look for. Be assured that the delay in the outcome for his faithful ones is usually meant to stir them up the more to seek his goodness. Thus all our boasting of trust in him is empty, unless we bear witness to it when we betake ourselves to him in prayer. Nor is that lawful zeal genuine in our prayers unless we persevere in them without ceasing. I pray the God of all consolation to raise you up and to uphold you more and more in true patience, while he exercises you in these tribulations, and to confirm you fully by his promises, that no one of his people will be tempted beyond what he can bear, but that with the temptation he will also give the strength and at last an outcome linked with salvation. Farewell. Strasbourg, 1 October.
