Granuellanus cum spem omnem suo responso nostris abscidisset, postquam de Eckij Apoplexia audiuit, forte quoniam illius hominis importunitatem remoram concordiae afferre cernebat, iussit Pistorio quoque exclusò, reliquos quatuor inter se absque arbitris consultare: quantum potui intelligere, fiestemus dimidio Christo contenti, facile trásigeremus. Philippus & Bucerus formulas de transsubstantiatione composuerunt ambiguas & fucosas, vt tentarent an aduersariis possent satisfacere nihil dando. Consilium hoc mihi non placet: tametsi rationem habent quam sequuntur: sperant enim fore, vt breui haec sponte eluicescant, si patefactus erit aditus doctri nae. Itaque transfilire malunt, nec Hexiloquentiam istam reformidant, qua nihil alioquin esse nocentius potest: polliceor tamen & ubi & piis omnibus, vtrunque optimo esse animo, nec aliud cogitare quàm vt promoueant Christi regnum. Nec possis ab illis quicquam desiderare, quod non fideliter & constanter praestent, nisi quòd in modo agendi se tempori nimis accommodant. Male autem me habet quòd Bucerus inuidia se apud multos grauet. Quia sibi est optime consciuts, securior est quàm vtile sit. Neque enim sic contenti esse debemus conscientiae integritate, vt non habeamus fratrum respectum: sed haec apud te desireo mi Farelle, videergo ne effuant. Vnum hoc, vt in malis, mihi gratum est, quòd nemo est qui vehementius pugnet nunc contra impanatum Deum, quàm Brentius: sic enim ipse appellat.No o plura,quo auidius meum ad vos aduentum desideres,vt istis narrationibus aures tuas expleam. Vale mi optime frater. Freithus,Musculus,& Brentius te salutat, immo prorsus omnes. Eckius,vt aiunt,conualescet: nondum meretur mundus ista be-ftia liberari. Excidebat quod minime praeteritum oportuit. Habet Maurus famulum qui aliquando Ludouico & mihi seruiuit Basilez, probum iuuenem, fidum & modestum. Ille ante annos quinque,cum propemodum puer esset, inscio patre, inter pocula puellae coniugium promisit: cum pater re indicata reclamasset, iuuenis dixit sibi fuisse impositum. Re male cognita, peius expensa,pronuntiarunt vestri iudices, authore Marcutio, ratum debere esse coniugium. Ille vt hanc necessitatem effugeret patria cessit. Nunc nuncium accepit de morte patris, sed simul hortatu tantum eum fui,vt puellam accipiat, ad hanc rem hortator est etiam illi Mirabilis. Tentaui & penitus excussi animum eius, sic abhorret, vt non sustineam magis vrgere. Et tamen fatetur honestam esse puellam: sed alieuerat se nunquam ad eam animum adiecisse. Quia saluum cupio, velim si fieri queat amica transactione componi negocium: sic & puellae consuleretur. Ea de re scripsi ad Mirabilem. Nolo tamen in meam gratiam quidquam facias, nisi quod aequum esse iudicabis. Neque enim ipse plus facturus esset si res in meo arbitrio poneretur x 1 1. Maij. M. D. X L I.
units.tr: The messenger left one day later than I expected, and this day has brought us something. Granvelle, having cut off all hope for our side by his reply, after he heard of Eck's apoplexy, perhaps because he saw that this man's importunity was a hindrance to concord, ordered the four remaining men to confer among themselves without arbitrators, with Pistorius shut out as well. As far as I could understand, we would easily come to terms if we were content with half a Christ. Philip and Bucer have composed formulas about transubstantiation that are ambiguous and specious, to see whether they could satisfy the opponents by giving nothing. I do not like this plan, although they have a reason for following it: they hope that these matters will soon clear up of their own accord, once access to the teaching has been opened. So they prefer to leap across, and they do not shrink from that hexiloquence, which can be nothing but harmful. I promise, however, both to them and to all the godly, that both of them are of the best disposition and think of nothing but advancing the kingdom of Christ. You could ask nothing of them that they do not perform faithfully and steadily, except that in their manner of acting they accommodate themselves too much to the times. It troubles me, however, that Bucer is burdened with odium among many. Since he is very well aware of his own conscience, he is more secure than is useful. For we must not be so content with the integrity of our conscience that we have no regard for our brothers. But I desire these things be taken care of with you, my Farel, and see that they do not fail. One thing, as in evils, pleases me: no one fights more vehemently now against the incarnate God than Brenz; for that is what he himself calls him. But enough, so that you may desire more eagerly our coming to you, that I may fill your ears with these reports. Farewell, my best brother. Frecht, Musculus, and Brenz greet you, indeed absolutely everyone. Eck, so they say, will recover; the world does not yet deserve to be freed from that beast. What ought not to have been passed over has slipped out. Maurus has a servant who once served Ludovicus and me at Basel, a worthy young man, faithful and modest. Five years ago, when he was almost a boy, without his father's knowledge, he promised marriage to a girl over drinks. When the father objected after the matter came to light, the young man said he had been tricked into it. Your judges, on the authority of Marcutius, pronounced, with the matter badly known and worse weighed, that the marriage must stand. To escape this necessity he left his homeland. Now he has received news of his father's death, but at the same time he is urged only to take the girl, and Mirabilis also urges him to this. I have tried and thoroughly probed his mind, and he so shrinks from it that I cannot bring myself to press him further. And yet he admits the girl is respectable, but he says he never had any inclination toward her. Because I want the affair settled safely, I would like it, if it can be done, to be resolved by a friendly agreement; in that way the girl also would be looked after. I have written about this matter to Mirabilis. Yet do nothing for my sake, except what you judge to be fair. For he himself would not do more if the matter were left to my decision. 11 May 1541.

units.la: ZVICKIVS CALVINO.
units.tr: Zwick to Calvin.

units.la: Salus & pax Christi.
units.tr: Health and peace in Christ.

units.la: ARctiffima familiaritas est quam parit fides, sic mihi scripta tua familiarissima sunt. Erit autem gratissimum, si tuo adventu semel familiaritatem istam in Domino initam firmes:quod vt breui fiat etiam atque etiam rogo. De Comitiorum tractatione nescio quid dicam: statui autem, vt uno verbo dicam, ab euentu omnia aestimare: interim precibus interpellabo Dominum ne causae suae desit. Audimus autem Philippum, & reliquos constantes esse, & apertos, quae res nos ministros summo gaudio afficit, & decet certe nos nihil vacillare. Ah! quanto tempore adhuc regnabimus? Si primum vno ore glorificemus Deum & Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, deinde pergamus nobis non esse dissimiles: non decet in hac causa cum vulpibus vulpinari, & cum astutissimis huius mundi sapientibus astutia certare: certandum est nobis sola perseuerantia, pietate, simplicitate, adde & patientia crucis: hanc mentem donet nobis Christus Dominus. Proinde, quo diutius regnemus in Christo, exhortc.j.
units.tr: So close is the intimacy that faith brings about, and so intimate to me are your writings. It would be very welcome if, by your coming, you would strengthen that friendship begun in the Lord; I ask this again and again, that it may happen soon. About the handling of the Diet I do not know what to say. I have decided, to put it in one word, to judge everything by the outcome; meanwhile I will beseech the Lord with prayers not to fail his cause. We hear that Philip and the others are steadfast and open, which fills us ministers with the greatest joy, and certainly we ought not to waver at all. Ah! How long shall we still reign? If we first glorify with one mouth God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and then go on not to be unlike ourselves: in this cause it is not fitting to play the fox with foxes, nor to vie in cunning with the most cunning wise men of this world. We must contend only by perseverance, piety, simplicity, and, add, patience in the cross. May Christ the Lord grant us this mind. Therefore, so that we may reign longer in Christ, I urge

units.la: Epist.33. tare obsecro reliquos fratres omnes quâtis potes viribus, vt quoniam Ecclesiæ disciplina maxima ex parte euanuit, & forte sine grauiore malo restitui in ordinem vix potest, vt saltem & Principes & Magistratus nostri strenuè animaduerterent in vitia & scandala publica, quo saltem hac via purgetur Ecclesia, nomenque Christi apud reliquos melius audiat, quod ipsum quoque donet Christus suo Spiritu. Ah!ne opprimat nos ingratitudo & iniustitia qui de bonitate & iustitia Dei tantùm gloriamur. Quanta bonorum Ecclesiasticorum habenda sit ratio, non opus est recitare: tantùm da operam apud bonos omnes, vt nostros ad sanctum illorum vsum serio exhortentur. Huc enim ventum videtur (quod tamen non sine gemitu dixerim) vt magna nostrorum pars credat sese tum demum verè regnum Antichristi euasisse, si cum bonis Ecclesiæ ludant pro libito, nec vlli disciplinæ subsint. O egregium Christianismum! Da ergo operam vt non solum cum Papistis vobis negotiù sit, sed inter vos quoque & cum vestris tractate quæ in rem Ecclesiæ, Christíque gloriam facere possunt, quæque placare possunt Dominum: ne ingrati pessimè pereamus. Hanc solicitudinem & curam largiatur nobis filius Dei Iesus Christus. Amen. Illetc cum bonis omnibus diutissime feruet. Sed ne graueris meo nomine salutare omnes fratres, Philippum, Bucerum, Freckthum, Musculum & reliquos, & feruet eos omnes Spiritus Christi in vnitate, perseuerantia, simplicitate, veritate, & tolerantia. Otate verò omnes pro Ecclesia quæ est Constantiæ, vt in fide crescat. Salutant autem te & reliquos, Ambrosius & reliqui omnes symmystæ, rogantes Dominum strenuè vt in illo optimè habeatis, & Euangelij negotium bene succedat, Amen. Ex Constantia, XII. Maij. M. D. XLI.
units.tr: I beg all the other brothers, as earnestly as you can, that since the discipline of the Church has for the most part vanished, and perhaps can scarcely be restored to order without some graver evil, at least our princes and magistrates should vigorously take action against public vices and scandals, so that by this means at least the Church may be purged and the name of Christ may be better heard among others; may Christ also grant this by his Spirit. Ah! Let not ingratitude and injustice overwhelm us, who boast only of the goodness and justice of God. There is no need to recount how much account must be taken of the ecclesiastical revenues; only take care, among all the good men, that they earnestly exhort ours to their holy use. For it seems to have come to this (though I say it not without groaning) that a large part of our people believe they have then at last truly escaped the kingdom of Antichrist, if they may play with the goods of the Church at will and be subject to no discipline. O excellent Christianity! Therefore take care that you have to deal not only with the Papists, but also among yourselves and with your own people, to treat matters that can serve the interest of the Church and the glory of Christ, and that can appease the Lord, lest we perish most wretchedly as ungrateful people. May Jesus Christ, the Son of God, grant us this concern and care. Amen. He glows with all good men for a very long time. But do not hesitate, in my name, to greet all the brothers: Philip, Bucer, Frecht, Musculus and the rest, and may the Spirit of Christ make them all glow in unity, perseverance, simplicity, truth and tolerance. Indeed, all pray for the Church that is at Constance, that it may grow in faith. Ambrose and all the other fellow-initiates greet you and the rest, asking the Lord earnestly that you may fare very well in him, and that the business of the Gospel may succeed well. Amen. From Constance, 12 May 1541.

units.la: Tuus Ioannes Zuick.
units.tr: Yours, Johannes Zwick.

units.la: ILLVSTRISS. PRINCIPVM, ATQVE ORDINVM Imperij Protestantium ad Franciscum I. Galliæ Regem Epistola.
units.tr: The Letter of the Most Illustrious Princes and Estates of the Protestant Empire to Francis I, King of France.

units.la: SAlutem & obsequium nostrum Serenissime atque Christianissime Rex. Quoniam ea beneuolentiæ signa Regia dignitas vestra nobis semper exhibuit, quæ argumento esse possint, Regiam Maiestatem Vestram optimo esse, & amicissimo erga nos animo. Aliquando etiam experti sumus apud Regiam Celsitudinem Vestram nostras preces non parum habuisse momenti. Itaque nunc etiam de quorundam priuatorum incolumitate, qui partim in variis regni vestri locis, præsertim Gratianopoli, & aliis Prouinciæ vrbibus capti tenentur, partim cum paruis liberis miseri reliquerūt suas domos, & in cauernas fugere coacti sunt, propterea quòd de doctrina Christiana idem sentiunt quod Ecclesiæ nostræ profitentur: scribendum & apud Regiam Celf.Vestram intercedendum duximus. Magno dolore afficimur, quòd cùm negari non possit multos veteres abusus hærere in Ecclesiis: ita tamen exarserit iracundia passim, vt & salutares sententiæ obruantur, & non solùm homines priuati, sed etiam gentes totæ veniant in periculum. Quæ cùm supplices fiunt Regię Celf. Vestræ, existimet Regia Celf. Vestra non nos tantùm, sed ipsam Ecclesiam Christi lugentem iacere ad pedes summorum Regum & opem implorare ac petere, ne lux exorientis Euangelij extinguatur, & vt modestis hominibus ac Christi membris parcatur. Scimus hos qui propter piam doctrinam sunt in odio, interdum prægrauari aliis criminibus, ac dici seditiosos. Vidimus autem confessionem ærumnosorum illorum oblatam Curiæ Gratianopolitanæ, & purgationem obiectorum criminum. Quare magis deprecandum esse pro eis duximus, quia doctrinæ confessio pia est, & haud dubiè pura sententia Catholicæ Ecclesiæ Christi, quam & nos profitemur. Oramus igitur Regiā Celf. Vestram, vt tum captorum illorum, tum aliorum, si qui propter eam dem causas periclitātur, vitæ parcat, eósque dimittat incolumes. Audimus quidem nonnullis ita veniam concedi, vt abiiciant confessionem doctrinæ, quam ipsi piam esse non dubitāt: quod cum facere ipsa morte sit acerbius, oramus vt Reg. Celf. Vestra id quoq; propter Deum mitiget. Neque ignorat Maiestas Vestra, quàm graue sit aliquid præsertim in Religione contra conscien tiam approbare. Erit hæc clementia grata Deo & habebit præmia diuinitus, sicut Psal. inquit, Beatus qui intelligit super egenum & pauperé, in die mala liberabit eum Deus. Quare vt hac in re erga miseros illos, vbicunque sint, se clementem præstet Regia Maiestas Vestra, etiam atque etiam oramus. Idque erit tum nobis, tum omnibus istis qui nobiscum eandem Religionem profitentur, maximi beneficij loco, præsertim si intelligamus illos nostra intercessione fuisse liberatos: & apud bonos omnes non vulgarem clementiæ & moderationis laudem Regia Dignitas Vestra obtinebit. Hæc si impetrabimus, quemadmodum bona spes est, studebimus vicissim, quibus poterimus officiis memores & grato animos testari, optantes vt Deus Opt. Maxim. Celf. Vestram diu seruet incolumem & florentem.
units.tr: Greetings and our respect, most serene and most Christian King. Your royal dignity has always shown us such signs of goodwill that they give good reason to believe that Your Royal Majesty is well disposed toward us and feels a very friendly spirit. We have also at times found that our petitions carried no small weight with Your Royal Highness. We have therefore now judged that we should write to Your Royal Highness and intercede on behalf of the safety of certain private persons. Some of them are held captive in various places in your kingdom, especially at Grenoble and other towns of the Province. Others have left their homes miserably with small children and have been forced to flee into caves, for the sole reason that they hold the same view of Christian doctrine as our Church professes. We are greatly distressed that, although it cannot be denied that many old abuses cling to the Churches, anger has so flared up everywhere that both wholesome opinions are being crushed and not only private persons but whole peoples are coming into danger. Since they make their supplications to Your Royal Highness, may Your Royal Highness consider that it is not only we but the Church of Christ itself, in grief, that lies at the feet of great kings and implores and begs help, so that the light of the rising Gospel may not be extinguished and that modest men, who are members of Christ, may be spared. We know that those who are hated on account of their godly teaching are sometimes weighed down with other charges and called seditious. We have, however, seen the confession of those unhappy men that was presented to the court at Grenoble, and their answer to the charges laid against them. For this reason we have judged that we should plead for them all the more, because their confession of doctrine is godly and undoubtedly the pure teaching of the Catholic Church of Christ, which we too profess. We therefore beg Your Royal Highness that, both for those now captive and for others, if any are in peril for the same cause, you spare their lives and let them go unharmed. We hear indeed that some have been granted pardon on condition that they renounce the confession of a doctrine which they themselves do not doubt is godly. Since to do this is more bitter than death itself, we ask that Your Royal Highness also moderate this out of regard for God. Nor does Your Majesty fail to know how grave a matter it is to approve anything against conscience, especially in religion. This clemency will be pleasing to God, and it will receive its rewards from heaven, as the Psalm says: "Blessed is he who considers the poor and needy; in the day of trouble the Lord will deliver him." We therefore beg and beg again that Your Royal Majesty show mercy to those unhappy men wherever they may be. This will be the greatest of benefits both to us and to all who profess the same religion with us, especially if we understand that they were set free through our intercession; and Your Royal Dignity will win no ordinary praise for clemency and moderation among all good men. If we obtain this, as we hope we will, we shall in turn be mindful to show our gratitude by whatever services we can, wishing that God, the Best and Greatest, keep Your Highness safe and flourishing for many years.

units.la: Datæ Ratisponæ xxiii i. Maij. Anno Christianæ salutis. M. D. XLI.
units.tr: Given at Ratisbon, 23 May, in the year of Christian salvation 1541.

units.la: Principes, Legati, Status & Ordines coniuncti Augustanæ Confessionis iam Ratisponæ congregati.
units.tr: The princes, envoys, states and estates of the Augsburg Confession, now gathered together at Ratisbon.

units.la: CVM nullum amplius in conuentu vsum mei fore fufpicater, magna improbitate missionem extorsi magis quàm im petrauimnam & Bucerus me çgerrime à fe abire paticbatur, & Philippus qui fe mihi fore in ea re adiutorem semper recepe- rat, cùm tempus instaret, rogabat vt manerem. Ego tamen me quoquomodo explicui. Neque me tam priuatæ meæ rationes quàm publicæ, vt adeo instarem, impulerunt. Videbam scholam nostram ex quo coeperat capito laborare, deflitui. Verebar ne his nundinis Ecclesia præsentiam meam desideraret. His etiam causis vtcunque adducti sunt nostri, vt mihi tandem concederent. Exponam autem breuiter, quo in statu res fuerint cum discessi. Ex quo in quaestione Eucharistiæ semel diffiliimus, de nulla alia potuit amplius inter nos conuenire. Scis vnam fuisse inter nos omnes sententiam, transfubstantiationem, rem commeditiam esse, nec tantum cum verbo Domini, sed cum sacramenti etiam natura pugnare: adorationem esse vel idololatricam, vel nimis periculosam, repositionem superstitione non carere. Cùm in hac responsione tres illi delecti constanter pergerent, acerbis verbis inuectus in Philippum est Granuellus: quo fracto, sperabat à reliquis duobus non tantum fore negocij. Dum nihil extorqueri posse videt, ad alia pergere præcipit. Interim Marchio Brandeburgensis clanculum, non tamen sine conscientia Cæsaris, vnum ex Principibus ab Anhalt legatū Luthero mittit, quia sperabat magis in hac quaestione fore propitium Papistis quàm nos omnes, propter veterem illam concertationem. Quid attulerit, nondum rescivi. Confido tamen a omnino non male fuisse à Luthero responsum. Restabat in causa Eucharistiæ tres quæstiones disputandæ, de sacrificio missæ, de priuatis missis, de vtriusque speciei distributione. Aduersarij, sublata missarum nundinatione & multitudine, vnam tantum missam in singulis templis quotidie retinebant, idque ea lege, vt non sine aliquo coetu, cui mysterium exponeretur, deinde vt ad communionem exhortatio fieret. Calicis participationem volebant esse liberam, vt haberent qui peterent. Sacrificium fucabant sophistica expositione, quam vnde sumpserint, tu ipse comiice. Illa omnia sunt repudiata, scripti à Philippo in contrariam sententiam articuli, & oblati. Ventū deinde est ad confessionem, in qua moderationē dabat aduersarij, scrupulosam enumerationē remittendo, sed necessitatem exigebant confessionis & absolutionis. Formulā con trariam nostri dederunt. Sic de inuocatione sanctorum, de primatu Papæ, de authoritate Ecclesiæ collatum est: nec conuenire potuit. Articuli omnes nostri libro adiuncti. Cæsar delectis illis gratias liberalibus verbis egit, quod fidelem operam praestitis- sent. Ipse deinde totam deliberationem ad ordines retulit. Et quoniam nihil statui poterat, nisi descripto libro: oblatus est in medium cum articulis. Mox tamen Caesarem poenituit facti. Sed quod semel decretum erat, Ordines ratum esse voluerunt. Dum id agitur, datus est Senatus legatis Hungariae & Austriae, qui supplicitér auxilia sibi dari petierunt. Instituit quoque Caesar, ut omissa religionis actione ad illam cofultationem se conuerterent ordines. Cum illas inducias vidi datas esse, occasione praeterire nolui: sic elapsus sum. Rerum feriem breuiter perstrinxi. Quod ad secretiora consilia attinet, nonnihil audies cum venero. Velim autem id abs te impetratum, ut Buceri reditum expectemus. Quantum ad fratres attinet, qui ob Euangelium laborant, non feci quod volui. Causa enim grauem aliquam legationem flagitabat, quam minime ferunt tempora, id est, vitiosi hominum affectus. Literas ergo impetraui. Quod ipsum factum fuerat, antequam Senatus admitteret. Sed curaui mutari ac inferi nonnihil eorum quae mandabas. Charta plus non capit. Tu ista omnia, si videbitur, curabis Vireto: excusabisque apud eum quod non scripserim: opprimor enim, crede mihi, assiduis interpellationibus, ut aegre liceat respirare. Vale charissime frater. Saluta omnes diligenter. Dominus vos omnes conseruet. Argentorati, Iulio, M. D. XLI.
units.tr: Since I suspected that I would no longer be of any use at the conference, I wrung my dismissal from them by great importunity, rather than secured it by asking. Bucer found it very hard to let me go, and Philip, who had always promised me he would be my helper in this matter, when the time drew near asked me to stay. Nevertheless I extricated myself somehow. It was not so much my private affairs as public ones that drove me to press so hard. I saw that our school, since Capito began to be unwell, was left without its head, and I feared that at this fair the Church might be in need of my presence. Our people were also moved by these reasons, however far they were, to finally grant me leave. I will set out briefly how matters stood when I left. Since we once broke off over the question of the Eucharist, we could agree on nothing else between us. You know that all of us were of one opinion: that transubstantiation is an invented thing, contrary not only to the word of the Lord but also to the nature of the sacrament; that adoration is either idolatrous or too dangerous; and that reservation of the elements is not free from superstition. When those three chosen men persistently held to this reply, Granvelle attacked Philip with bitter words. When he gave way, Granvelle hoped there would not be much trouble from the other two. Seeing that nothing could be wrung from them, he ordered that they proceed to other matters. Meanwhile the Margrave of Brandenburg secretly, though not without Caesar's knowledge, sent one of the princes of Anhalt as envoy to Luther, because he hoped that on this question the Papists would be more favourable than all of us, on account of that old quarrel. I have not yet learned what he brought back. I trust, however, that Luther's reply was not at all bad. There remained three questions to be debated on the Eucharist: on the sacrifice of the Mass, on private masses, and on the distribution of both kinds. Our opponents, having removed the trade in masses and their multiplicity, kept only one Mass daily in each church, and that on condition that it be said not without some gathering, to whom the mystery would be explained, and then that an exhortation to communion be given. They wanted the participation in the cup to be optional, so that there would be people who might ask for it. They disguised the sacrifice with a sophistical explanation; you yourself can work out where they got it from. All those things were rejected, and articles written by Philip in the opposite sense were presented. Then the discussion came to the Confession, in which our opponents offered some moderation, dropping the scrupulous enumeration of abuses, but they insisted on the necessity of confession and absolution. Our side gave a contrary formula. In the same way the invocation of saints, the primacy of the Pope, and the authority of the Church were discussed, and no agreement could be reached. All our articles are attached to the book. Caesar thanked those chosen men in generous words for having faithfully done their work. He then referred the whole deliberation to the estates. And since nothing could be decided unless the book was drawn up, it was laid before them together with the articles. Soon, however, Caesar regretted what he had done. But the estates wanted what had once been decided to stand. While this was going on, an audience was given to the envoys of Hungary and Austria, who humbly asked for aid to be sent to them. Caesar also arranged that the estates, leaving aside business concerning religion, should turn to that consultation. When I saw that a truce had been granted, I did not want to let the opportunity pass, and so I slipped away. I have briefly sketched the course of events. As for the more secret counsels, you will hear something when I come. I would like you to see to it that we wait for Bucer's return. As for the brothers who are suffering for the Gospel, I have not done what I wished. For the case demanded some weighty embassy, which the times hardly allow, that is, the faulty dispositions of men. So I obtained letters. This was done before the council admitted it. But I have seen to it that some of what you ordered was changed and inserted. The paper holds no more. You will see to all these things, if you think fit, with Viret, and will excuse me to him for not having written, for I am overwhelmed, believe me, by constant interruptions, so that I can scarcely breathe. Farewell, dearest brother. Greet everyone diligently. May the Lord keep you all. Strasbourg, July 1541.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: Your John Calvin.

units.la: CAL. FARELLO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL.

units.la: CVM mihi allatae sunt tuae literae, iam habebam meas ad te paratas: quae tamen si non omnino cosentiunt cum tuis postulatis, mittedae tamen fuerunt, ut scias in quo affectu me deprehenderunt. Nunc postquam vidi te vlterius insistere, & illos etiam veteres nostros hospites palam se adiungere ad causam, adhibui de integro nostros. Lectis tuis & Geneuatum literis, consului ecquidnam factum opus fore censerent. Responderunt minime esse disputandum, an omisso concedere illuc exemplo concedere. Neque enim aut nunc esse integrum: aut opportuisse illud in dubium vocari, etiamsi nihildum esset decretum. Ergo ad iter nos accingimus: ut autem praesenti Ecclesiae illius necessitati succurratur, quam nolumus esse desertam, censent modis omnibus eo accersendum Viretum, interim dum alia vocatione distrahor: vbi redierimus non recusant, quinilucredeam. Quinetiam Bucerus se mecum venturum pollicetur. In eam sententiam visum est ipsis scribere, quo certior fides fieret: meis literis suas quoque Bucerus addidit. De meo animo
units.tr: When your letter was brought to me, I already had mine prepared for you. Although they do not fully agree with your requests, I decided they should be sent, so that you would know the state of mind in which I found myself. Now that I have seen you pressing further, and those old guests of ours openly joining your cause, I have again consulted our friends. After reading your letter and the one from Geneva, I asked what they thought should be done. They replied that there is no question of whether we should withdraw there, since that is no longer open to us, nor should it have been called into doubt, even though nothing had yet been decided. So we are preparing for the journey. But so that help may be given to that church's present need, which we do not want to be abandoned, they think Viret should by all means be summoned there in the meantime, while I am pulled away by another calling. When we have returned, they do not refuse, as I believe. Indeed Bucer promises to come with me. They thought it right to write to you to this effect, so that the assurance might be more certain, and Bucer has added his own letter to mine. As for my own mind:

units.la: Epist. 36. sic accipe:mihi fi detur optio,quiduis libentius sim facturus,quâ vt tibi hic obtemperem: sed quoniam non esse mei iuris memini, cor meum velut mactatum Domino in sacrificium offero. Itaque non est quod suspiceris tibi verba dari:nostri nihil nisi ex animo promittunt. Et ego nihil aliud obtestor, quàm vt nulla mei ratione habita, dispiciant quid maxime sit ex Dei gloria & Ecclesiæ utilitate.Tametsi non sum valde ingeniosus,nō tamen deficiunt me effugia,quibus ita clanculum elabar,vt facile apud homines excusem per me non stetisse. Verum scio mihi esse negocium cum Deo,qui huiusmodi astutias deprehendit.Ergo animum meum vinctum & constrictum subigo in obedientiam Dei:& quando proprio consilio destituor,me his regendum trado,per quos spero Dominum ipsum mihi locuturum. Cum Capito scripsit putauit,vt video, me prolixa Epistola,tibi expositurum totam deliberationis nostræ seriem, sed fatis est quòd summam habes. Quàquam eram id quoque facturus nisi tempus defuisset. Verum totus dies variis avocamentis mihi consumptus est.Nunc à cœna longiori lucubratione valetudinem alioqui dubiam tentare nolui.Hic se ad Natalem Domini rediturum promisit cum carruca,in qua poterit afferre Vendelino ex libris suis decem exemplaria Institutionis, sex commentarios in Ieremiam:ea dabis illi aduehenda.
units.tr: Epist. 36. Take it this way: if I were given the choice, I would gladly do whatever might let me obey you here. But since I remember that I am not my own master, I offer my heart, as it were, slain to the Lord as a sacrifice. So there is no reason for you to suspect that you are being fobbed off with words; our people promise nothing except from the heart. And I ask only this: that, with no regard to my own interests, they consider what is most in accordance with the glory of God and the advantage of the Church. Although I am not very clever, I still have excuses by which I could slip away so secretly that I could easily clear myself before men of having been at fault. But I know that I have to do with God, who sees through such tricks. So I bring my bound and constrained mind into obedience to God, and since I am deprived of my own counsel, I surrender myself to be ruled by those through whom I hope the Lord himself will speak to me. When Capito wrote, he evidently thought I would set out in a long letter the whole sequence of our deliberation; but it is enough that you have the summary. Though I was going to do that too, had there been time. The whole day has been consumed for me by various interruptions. Now, after a long evening's study, I did not want to test my health, which is in any case uncertain. Here Capito promised to return at Christmas with a cart, in which he can bring to Vendelinus ten copies of the Institutes from his books and six commentaries on Jeremiah; you will give them to him to carry.

units.la: BVCERVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: BUCER TO CALVIN, GREETING

units.la: DE motu illo idem omnino quod tu suaseram, quanquam non tam plane scripseram. Circunstantias causæ quas tu modo mihi exposuisti,ignorauiideo eam nunc petendam dilationem optaueram, dum remisisset sese illa animorum concitatio tam impie excitata,& recepissent sese fratres ad defnfio nem veritatis graucm & claram. Huius capita prima fuissent, disputationem nihil quàm crassam illam præsentiam damnare, & necessario fatendum veram percipi in Eucharistia corporis & sanguinis Domini communionem:tum cætera quæ discipulis sunt,clare à Domino præcepta esse, vt dissimulari tacereque, nisi Christo abnegato, non possint. Tu me tuis literis perturbasti. Expertus enim sum multis in locis quantum causæ veritatis nocuerit infyncera defensio, & neglectus communionis. Christus gaudet virtutem suam sic explicare, ne videatur malorum affectuum patronus,& caput factionis.Literæ meæ vt nunc quæritur N.non fuit ipsis allatę. Consilium à me petit. Scribam igitur illi de fyncerititate actionis, de necessitate communionis, de pia cautione, ne quid admisfcea ur ad causam Christi, de explicatione clara, & ex Scripturis ipsis manifeste deprompta, qualis tua
units.tr: Regarding that disturbance, I advised exactly what you did, though I had not written so plainly. Since I did not know the circumstances of the case, which you have only now explained to me, I had wished for a delay, until that agitation of minds, so impiously stirred up, had subsided and the brothers had withdrawn to a grave and clear defence of the truth. The first heads of such a defence would be: to condemn that crude presence as a mere matter of dispute, and to admit that a true communion in the body and blood of the Lord is received in the Eucharist. Then the rest, which are things the Lord has clearly commanded his disciples, cannot be concealed or kept silent without denying Christ. Your letter has disturbed me. For I have learned from experience in many places how much harm an insincere defence of the cause of truth, and the neglect of communion, have done. Christ wishes his power to be displayed in such a way that it does not seem to be the patron of evil passions and the head of a faction. My letter, as is now asked, was not brought to them (N.). He asks my advice. I will therefore write to him about the sincerity of the action, the necessity of communion, the pious caution that nothing be mixed into the cause of Christ, and a clear explanation, drawn plainly from the Scriptures themselves, such as yours, which not even the powers of hell could calumniate.

units.la: Epist.37. tua est, quam ne inferi quidem calumniari queant. Deniqúe de probis patronis, qui & Christi vere sint, & nostri tantum propter Christum. Illa tam execror de imaginibus, de adseruatione symbolorum, vt libenter fingerem mihi confi cta esse percalumniam. Nam vitiosa hæc sunt, & submouenda, vbi remanse-runt. De infirmorum communicatione motum aliquid audieram, & non improbabam. Tu verò pie & necessario facis, quod facis: etiam in infirmis, & vitiosis fratribus defendenda est causa Christi. Sed simul danda opera, vt infirmi aliquando roborentur, & vitiosi corrigantur. At dum ita partim ipsi fugimus, partim Satanæ prodimus pias Synodos, quid nobis polliceamur? Christus caput est vulgò omnium membrorum suorum, & aggregat per vniuersa non per singula. Exhilaratis me facta spe plenæ inter Bernates & vestram Rempub. conciliationis. Quanquam si non contrahatur & Ecclesiarum societas, & restituatur vna res Ecclesiasticas tractandi facultas, nihil præstabis via concilia-tionis. Videmus quotidie, vt Dominus eos qui ipsius nomen iaftant, coniungi non in se, non patiatur. Instabis igitur, & insta-bo ego tecum, vt causam Christi fratres quàm simplicissime, & totam, & ex verbo Dei ipso, & συμμάχως pure Christianis agant. Per ministerium testitui omnia necesse est: ergo ministerium ipsum prius. Id verò non fiet, nisi conspirantibus & communiter agentibus, quotquot inter se communicare poterunt. Meti Farellus vnam duntaxat concionem habuit, quod sciam, & in cœmiterio Dominicanorum: qui cùm aliud non possent, strepitu campanæ suæ verbum Domini populo auertere conati sunt. Sed Farellus nostrer voce intenta vsque ad summam raucedinem, campanç sonitum vicit. Postridie tria millia aderant audituri: sed præcipuj inter eos qui Euangelium petunt, & ipse Consul à Farello impetrarunt, vt quiescerent dum rem eò deducerent, vt fine metu motus ciuilis, concio haberi posset: quod breui forte pollicebantur. Vocatus Farellus eodem die ad summum consilium, & rogatus, quo iubente prædicasset, & quo petente, respondit, Christo iubenc, & petentibus membris: nec tamen voluit quemquam nominatim indicare. Et fatis grauiter ac pie coram illis de suo munere & prædicatione Euangelij disseruit, eosque officij fui admonuit. Dum verò illi deliberarent quid de eo statuerent, fratres deduxerunt eum domum: & impositum equo, qui magnitudine & habitu non absimilis esse Farello videbatur, fimularunt se fratres quidam educere Farellum. Interim quieuit Farellus, expectans legationem quam Euangelij initio statim cùm ipsè Metim vel niffet, miserant ad nostros, qui à nostris auxilium, & ab vniuerso sedere peterent. Visum enim fuit vt legati ex nostris
units.tr: Epist.37. It is yours, which not even the powers of hell could slander. Finally, as to upright patrons, who are truly of Christ and ours only on account of Christ. Those things about images and the retention of creeds I so abhor that I would gladly suppose the slander against me was invented. For these are faulty and must be removed wherever they remain. I had heard of some stir about communion with the weak, and I did not disapprove. But you do what you do both piously and necessarily: the cause of Christ must be defended even among weak and faulty brethren. Yet at the same time care must be taken that the weak are in time strengthened and the faulty corrected. But while we in part flee from them ourselves and in part betray the godly synods to Satan, what can we promise ourselves? Christ is commonly the head of all his members, and he gathers them together as a whole, not piece by piece. You have cheered me by holding out the hope of a full reconciliation between the Bernese and your commonwealth. Yet unless the fellowship of the Churches is drawn together, and the single power of handling ecclesiastical matters is restored, you will achieve nothing by the way of reconciliation. We see every day that the Lord does not allow those who boast of his name to be joined together in him. You will press on, and I will press on with you, that the brethren plead the cause of Christ as simply and wholly as possible, from the Word of God itself, and συμμάχως [symmachōs, in alliance], purely as Christians. Everything must be restored through the ministry, so the ministry itself must come first. This will not happen unless all who can communicate with one another act together in agreement. At Metz, as far as I know, Farel held only one sermon, and that in the Dominicans' cemetery. Since they could do nothing else, they tried to drive the Word of the Lord away from the people by the noise of their bell. But our Farel, straining his voice until he was utterly hoarse, overcame the sound of the bell. On the next day three thousand were present to hear him. But the chief men among those who seek the Gospel, and the consul himself, obtained from Farel that they should keep quiet while they brought the matter to the point where a sermon could be held without fear of civil disturbance, which they perhaps promised would be soon. Farel was summoned that same day before the supreme council and asked by whose command and at whose request he had preached. He replied, at Christ's command and at the request of the members, yet he would not name anyone individually. He spoke quite seriously and piously before them about his office and the preaching of the Gospel, and admonished them of their duty. While they deliberated what to decide about him, the brethren led him home, and, placing him on a horse which seemed not unlike Farel in size and bearing, some of the brethren pretended to lead Farel out. Meanwhile Farel kept quiet, awaiting the embassy which, at the very beginning of the Gospel, when he himself had gone to Metz or elsewhere, they had sent to our people, to seek help from our people and from the whole assembly. For it seemed good that envoys from our people

units.la: c.iiij.
units.tr: Chapter 4.

units.la: Electorem Sax.& Landgrauium adirent, & ab illis recipi in fœ- dus nostrum Rempub. Metensem, in saniore illa sui parte quæ Euangelium petit,postularent.Id factum est. Landgrauius cau- sam comprobauit,& ad Electorem statim retulit:interim tamè, quia res moram non ferebat, decreuit legationem mittendam ad Metenses,nomine communis fœderis,quæ postularet ab ad- uersariis, vt nostris vnum templum, & libertam concionem, & Sacramentorum administrationem concederent.Dedit ipse Le- gatum vnum,alterum Francfordienses,tertius noster erat.Hi in mandatis habent, nihil non tentare ab aduersariis, vt impetret, quod petitum missi sunt.Eo etiam adiuncto,fœdus nostrum nō posse deesse fratribus tam sanĉta & pia petentibus. Idque inter- esse totius Rom. Imperij.Vide vt audeamus.Spes itaque est,etiâ aduersarij quod petitur vltrò non cócedant, vt tamen quieturi sint,si nostri hac legatione animati per se Farellum concionari fecerint. Satan in eo quoque multum laboràuit, vt si Euangelio non posset omnino, tamen ex parte auerteret huic populo,ali- quo pro Farello obtrufo, qui non ... s. Ob- stitimus huic Satanæ quoad licuit. Cras spero aut hodie reuerso D.Iacobo,audiemus quid dederit Dominus. Multus illic popu- lus Christum admodum sitit. Consul cum fratre R.fortissimè a- git. Moram hanc Farellus ægerrimè tulit, nec immeritò. Nam peste illic multi quotidie tolluntur, qui grauissimè queruntur, se sine consolatione certa Euangelij & Sacramentorum hinc abripi.Si distulisset legatio vnam tantùm septimianam, indubiè rursus aliquid ausi fuissent. Habes summam ferè omnium quæ Meti hactenus in hac causa acciderunt. Bruno admodum con- stanter egit, quanquam ad id opus habuerit multis cohortatio- nibus.Bene vale.Vxorem & fratres diligenter,atque officiose sa- luta. Sed quàm mihi dolet illud de ignorata disciplina, de fa- ĉtiofa agendi ratione,de neglectu Synodorum,de offensione si- ue retenta, siue affectata. Sed tu meum cor, meus animus, sem- per tuo,imò Christi bono omnia omnium mala vinces, quoad licuerit.D.Iesus te feruet.Vale, Argentorati,v i. Octobr. M. D. XLI. D.Iacobus heri vesperi venit, sed proh dolor, nihil boni attulit. Aduersarij in vrbe dominantur. Nostri cùm legatio ad- ueniret,non aderant. Legationem itaque vrbe excluserunt, & nec equos eorum hospitio accipere voluerunt. Vix tandem im- petratum est,vtres mitterent aduersarij ex vrbe,qui Legatos au ditent. Auditis, nullum responsum dederunt causati senatum totum cogi non posse propter pestem quæ vno die 50. abfumir. Iurarunt omnino se extrema potius passuros, quàm quod nos petimus,id est, Regnum Christi admissuros. Consul volebat ad- mittere concionem.Frater repugnauit & retraxit eum.Si neque eum pro se adeant ciues pij, est iterum & hic misera Christi Ecclesia. Nostri sine cruce Christum quaerunt. Aduersarij propter Antichristum mille cruces subeunt. Oremus, supplicemus, flagitemus opem Domini.
units.tr: This was done. The Landgrave approved the cause and at once reported it to the Elector. Meanwhile, since the matter would not brook delay, it was decided that an embassy should be sent to the people of Metz in the name of the common covenant, to demand that the adversaries grant to our side one church, free preaching, and the administration of the sacraments. He himself gave one envoy, the people of Frankfurt another, and a third was from our side. They have it in their instructions to try everything with the adversaries to obtain what they were sent to ask, and to add that our covenant cannot fail brothers who ask for things so holy and so godly, and that this matters to the whole Holy Roman Empire. See how boldly we act! So there is hope that even if the adversaries do not concede what is asked of their own accord, they will nevertheless keep quiet, if our people, encouraged by this embassy, allow Farel to preach on his own. Satan also laboured greatly in this, so that if he could not altogether turn this people from the Gospel, he might at least turn them in part, by putting forward some substitute in place of Farel, who [...]. We have resisted this Satan as far as we could. I hope that tomorrow, or today when Jacob returns, we shall hear what the Lord has given. A great number of people there thirst greatly for Christ. The Consul, with my brother R., acts most resolutely. Farel bore this delay very badly, and not undeservedly. For many are carried off there daily by the plague, and they complain most bitterly that they are being snatched away without the sure consolation of the Gospel and the sacraments. If the embassy had been delayed for only a single week, they would undoubtedly have dared something again. You have almost the whole sum of what has happened at Metz so far in this cause. Bruno has acted quite steadfastly, although he needed many exhortations for that task. Farewell. Greet your wife and brothers diligently and dutifully. But how much it grieves me to hear of that matter of the disciplined ignored, of the rash manner of acting, of the neglect of the synods, and of the offence, whether retained or deliberately sought. But you, my heart, my soul, will always overcome all the evils of all men for your own good, and for the good of Christ, as far as you are able. May the Lord Jesus keep you. Farewell. From Strasbourg, 6 October 1541. Jacob came yesterday evening, but alas, he brought nothing good. The adversaries rule in the city. When the embassy arrived, our people were not present. So they shut the embassy out of the city and would not even accept their horses into lodging. At last it was barely obtained that the adversaries should send out some men from the city to hear the envoys. After they were heard, they gave no answer, pleading that the whole senate could not be assembled because of the plague, which carried off fifty people in a single day. They swore that they would sooner suffer the utmost than admit what we ask, that is, the kingdom of Christ. The Consul wanted to admit the sermon; my brother opposed him and held him back. If the godly citizens cannot approach it for themselves, there is here again a wretched Church of Christ. Our people seek Christ without the cross; the adversaries undergo a thousand crosses for the sake of Antichrist. Let us pray, supplicate, and beg for the help of the Lord.

units.la: Tuus totus Bucerus.
units.tr: Yours wholly, Bucer.

units.la: BVCERVS AD ITALOS.
units.tr: BUCER TO THE ITALIANS.

units.la: Christum puro fide invocantibus fratribus qui sunt Bononiae & Mutinae, sibi venerandis & charissimis.
units.tr: To the brethren who are at Bologna and Modena, men to be revered and most dear to us, who call upon Christ with a pure faith.

units.la: Gratia & pax a Domino nostro Iesu Christo, fratres venerandi, ac membra in hoc ipso Seruatore nostro dulcissima. Audimus vos cognitione Christi in dies proficere, vtque natura fert fermenti Euangelici, per vos eadem cognitione cop-lures quotidie imbui. Ea res nobis meritò magnam affert consolationem in Domino & laetitiam. Quem oramus vt numero, se apud vos pura certaque fide invocantium, semper aliquos adiungat, eademque fide magis magisque perficiat eos quos adiun xerit, ac quicquid liberae nominis sui invocationi & confessioni vobis omnibus obstiterit, clementer amoliatur, Satanamque pedibus vestris subiiciat. Amen. Nunciatum praeterea est, disputationem de sacra Eucharistia inter quosdam fratres agitari: qua in re eos fratres per Christum rogo, & hortor, vt ea inquisitione satis ducant, quae eo faciunt, vt carne Christi & sanguine vere pascantur, hoc est, vt in Christo viuant plenius, & illum viuentem in se potentius sentiat, & omni vita prolixius explicent ad proximos. Quae apud nos de hoc mysterio agitata quaestio est, dani nobis dedit plurimum. Quare vel nostro malo docti, artes hic Satanae diligetius cauere debetis. Haec docuit Dominus clare nostram carnem & sanguinem regni Dei hereditatem non posse percipere: hoc est, iustitiam, & vitam aeternam. Sua itaque nobis carne & sanguine opus esse: quibus qui non pascitur, eum vitam in se habere nequit: qui vero carnem hanc edit, & sanguinem bibit, hunc viturum in aeternum, quia mansurum in ipso, & ipsum habiturum manentem in se. Hanc vero carnem & hunc sanguinem dare vescendum & bibendum, & verbo quidem & singulariter symbolis sacrae Eucharistiae. Panem enim quem frangimus, non panis tantum, sed etiam corporis sui esse communicationem, & Calice gratiarum actionis sanguinis sui, non vini tantum. Unde praebens panem dixit Accipite, & manducate, hoc est corpus meum. Bibite, hic est sanguis meus. Verè enim pane corpus, vino sanguinem suum dabat in cibum & potum non periturum ventris, sed vivificum mentis indeque & totius hominis: at coelestem tamen: in cœlis enim est & manet Domi-nus,id est,in inaccelsa Patris gloria quæ nullo loco mundi alli-gatur: quia ille mundum reliquit & ad Patrem in vitam cœle-stem transiuit,hoc est,conditionem huius seculi exuit, & gloriā quam ab initio habuit repetiit:in qua tamen & hic cum suis est vsque ad consummationem huius seculi:nam & ipsos nos pater in ipso cõuiuificatos, & excitatos etiam in cœlestibus in eo iam collocauit & dedit in cœlis nostrum habere <bl>ςυλλ</bl>.Quo vt respiciamus Ecclesia etiam patrum tempore cum iam tractan-da essent mysteria sacra, inuitabat,iubens habere sursum corda. Nihil itaque hic terreni,nihil huius seculi cogitandum,etiam si & nos & propter nos symbola totaque externa actio mysteriorū huius adhuc seculi res sint.Addicit amicus amico fidem symbo-lo prębitæ dextræ,sed si verè & amicè res geritur, hic non con-tactum manus sed animum mentemque fidem suam obligantis amici, id est, sui fit promissio respicit, eique re mirificè recreatur & confirmatur:tamen si siuolè sæpe,& nulla certa beneuolentię significatione dexterę iungi soleant.Sufflabat in discipulos Chri-stus & iubebat tamen illos accipere Spiritum sanctum quem & verè illi seo Symbolo dabat,sed nec in eo oris Domini si flatu lo caliter inclusum aut idem vllâ huius seculi ratione adiunctum: vere tamē atque realiter eo signo exhibitum.Sic natura ab ipso Domino factifumus vt in promissionibus & exhibitionibus re-rum non visibilium,quæ sunt magni momenti & quarum cupi mus vel promissionem vel exhibitionem quàm grauissimè face-re,signa semper exhibeamus visibilia.Ita vt fieri videmus in ma gnis emptionibus & venditionibus,actis & fœderibus,collatio-neque magnarum dignitatum & potestatum.Deus ergo qu sua inter nos agi vult quàm grauissime & ardentissime,rectè & sym-bola & quæ pro ingenio nostro ad excitandum,& inflamman-dum animos consideratione & sancta cupiditate donorum su-rum valeant,adhiberi in exhibitione donorum suorum voluit. Hinc & ipse vt sanitates impositione manuum,digitorum,sputi linitione vel attractiua & benedictionem impositione manuū, & Spiritum sanctum flatu , & corpus & sanguinem uum pane & vino præbuit,suosque iussit ablutionem cœlestem qua regene ramur tinctione vel aspersione aquæ, sanitates, & benedictio-nem spiritualem,potestatemq; sacri ministerij imponendo ma-nus conferre. Ad eundem modum egit & cum populo veteri. Hanc itaque tantam patris & magistri nostri cœlestis Christi <bl>φιλανθρωπίαν</bl> in vsu sacrorum symbolorum pie excipiamus, & exosculemur, non curiosis & prophanis quæstionibus conm-melia afficiamus. Spiritus sanctus per Paulum & alios Aposto-los tradidit nobis quod illi acceperant à Domino. Hic autem instiinstituturus hoc mysterium discipulos suos sibi adiunxit qui adhuc sectabantur & doctrinae eius studiosi habebantur. Hoc nos vere esse studeamus,nec alios ad haec mysteria admittamus,dum penes nos eorum administratio fuerit: non minus demus operam tamen,vt quos licet,eius veros discipulos faciamus: id fi nequeamus nihil detrahet nobis, fi alij etiam palam Iudaei sint. Nec nos propter malos, bonis Domini fraudari decet. Deinde vt minister non sua sed Domini verba loquitur,ea nos fide vera vt verba Domini excipiamus.Agit gratias patri:agamus vnà:accipit panem & vinum, eáque distribuens iubet accipere : ea accipiamus & nos,minister ad distribuendum& fumendum,plebs ad lumendum : lubiunxit,edite bibite: edamus & bibamus,non circunferamus vel includamus. Addit, Hoc est corpus meum, hic sanguis meus : id credamus , nec dubitemus haec dari nobis his ipsis symbolis,& dari in cibum & potum vitae aeternae,vt magis magisque viuamus in Christo & habeamus illum viuentem in nobis. Adiunxit, quod traditur pro vobis, qui funditur in remissionem peccatorum pro vobis & pro multis, qui est nouum Testamentum:haec credamus & gratias Domino agamus,quod immolatione fui nostra peccata expiauit, & foedus gratiae nouum & aeternum inter patrem & nos fanciuit & confirmauit vt ille nobis pater , nos ei filij fimus : iubet denique haec facere in commemorationem fui:totum itaque circa haec mysteria Christum praedicemus,& quae pro nobis fecit omnia : addicamusque inuicem nos ei,& nostra omnia: idque testemur nostra confessione fidei piis laudibus, precibus, & oblatione munerum, nec enim vacuis in conspectum Dei veniendum est : sed pro esuriente & sitiente , nudo & hospite, infirmo & vincto Christo in suis,munusf-mper aliquod offerendum. Ista fi ita simpliciter credamus & geramus, vere discipuli Domini erimus, vereque ipso pascemur in vitam aeternam : superuacaneásque quaestiones,quae tanum ad inanem gloriam & contentionem valent facile euitantes, toti in id incumbemus vt hac sancta paftione Christum viuentem in nobis & plenius sentiamus ad nostram ipsorum consolationem, & pietatis profectum, & omni studio bonorum operum ad alios exprimamus & exibeamus.Quae inter nos Germanos de hoc mysterio dura nimis extitit concertatio opus carnis fuit. Nos D.Lutherum putabamus Christum coelestem terrenis signis nimis dicendo affigere.Nos illi nihil in Coena,quam panem & vinum agnoscere vel tradere: dedit tandem Dominus, vt tam de verbis, quam de re pulchre conuenerit:& ita vtrinque haec mysteria commendemus, vt nec ille nostris videatur indigna Christo tribuere,nec nos Coenam Domini fine Domino celebrare. Duas enim res hic percipi vtrinque confitemur:terrenam, panem & vinum:& cœlestem,corpus & sanguinem Christi Domini.Quidam re vera dilutius, nonnulli crassius de sacramentis his loquebantur: ij ad mediocritatem piam & verbis Domini consonam se receperunt: indeque est pia in Ecclesiis nostris etiam hac de re constituta consensio: hanc & vobis retinere aut restituere sicubi labefactata sit, studete, imitantes nos in eo quod Christi est, non in eo quod carnis erat:vt est omnis inter sanctos contentio & concertatio. Dominus nos ipse doceat sua mysteria omnia,perficiatque, & ad perfectionem salutis & beatæ cum ipso communionis largiatur. Amen.
units.tr: Grace and peace from our Lord Jesus Christ, revered brothers and members most dear to us in this same Saviour of ours. We hear that you grow daily in the knowledge of Christ, and that, as the nature of the Gospel leaven is, through you many more are being daily imbued with the same knowledge. This gives us good reason for great comfort and joy in the Lord. We pray that he will add to their number others who call upon him in your midst with a pure and certain faith, that he will bring those he has added to ever greater perfection in that same faith, and that he will graciously remove whatever has stood in the way of the free invocation and confession of his name among you all, and will put Satan under your feet. Amen. We have also been told that a dispute about the holy Eucharist is being carried on among some brothers. In this matter I ask and urge those brothers, through Christ, to be content with that inquiry which tends to make them truly fed on the flesh and blood of Christ, that is, to live more fully in Christ, to feel him living in themselves more powerfully, and to display him more abundantly in all their life toward their neighbours. The question that has been debated among us about this mystery has done us great harm. Therefore, taught by our own loss, you must take more careful heed of Satan's snares here. The Lord clearly taught that our flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, that is, righteousness and eternal life. Therefore we need his own flesh and blood; whoever is not fed on these does not have life in himself. But whoever eats this flesh and drinks this blood will live forever, because he will remain in him and will have him abiding in himself. Now this flesh and this blood he gives to be eaten and drunk, and indeed he gives them in the word and especially in the symbols of the holy Eucharist. For the bread which we break is not only bread but also a communion in his body, and the cup of thanksgiving is a communion in his blood, not merely in wine. Hence, in handing out the bread, he said: Take and eat, this is my body. Drink, this is my blood. Truly he gave his body under the bread and his blood under the wine as food and drink, not perishing for the belly but life-giving for the mind, and thereby for the whole man. Yet it is heavenly food: the Lord is in heaven and remains there, that is, in the inaccessible glory of the Father, which is bound to no place in the world. For he left the world and passed over to the Father into heavenly life, that is, he put off the condition of this age and resumed the glory which he had from the beginning; yet in that glory he is also here with his own until the end of this age. For the Father has also already placed us, quickened together with him and raised up even among the heavenly things in him, and has given us to have our (...) [συλλ] in heaven. To look to this, the Church, even in the time of the Fathers, when the sacred mysteries were now to be handled, used to urge, bidding them to have their hearts lifted up. Nothing earthly, then, nothing of this age, is to be thought of here, even though both we and, for our sake, the symbols and the whole external action of these mysteries are still matters of this age. A friend pledges his faith to a friend by the offered right hand; but if the thing is done truly and in friendship, the handshake looks not to the touch of the hands but to the mind and will of the friend who pledges himself, that is, it looks to his promise, and by it the man is wonderfully refreshed and strengthened, even though hands are often joined carelessly and without any sure sign of goodwill. Christ breathed on his disciples and yet bade them receive the Holy Spirit, whom he truly gave them with that sign; yet the Spirit was not enclosed in the breath of the Lord's mouth in a local manner, nor joined to it by any rule of this age, but was truly and really exhibited by that sign. Thus the Lord himself has so ordained that in the promises and exhibitions of invisible things, which are of great moment and whose promise or exhibition we most earnestly desire to make as firm as possible, we always offer visible signs. We see this done in great purchases and sales, in contracts and covenants, and in the conferring of great dignities and powers. God therefore, wishing the things he wills to be done among us to be done most seriously and ardently, rightly chose in the exhibition of his gifts to use symbols and such things as, according to our nature, may serve to rouse and inflame our minds with consideration and holy desire for his gifts. Hence he also, in giving healings by the laying on of hands, by the touch of fingers, by spittle and by anointing, and in conferring the blessing by laying on of hands, gave the Holy Spirit by breath, and gave his body and blood under bread and wine; and he commanded his people to confer the heavenly washing by which we are regenerated, by the dipping or sprinkling of water, and spiritual healing and blessing, and the power of the sacred ministry, by laying on of hands. He acted in the same way with the old people. Therefore let us devoutly receive and embrace this so great love of our Father and Teacher, the heavenly Christ, in the use of the sacred symbols, and not burden it with curious and profane questions. The Holy Spirit through Paul and the other apostles handed on to us what they had received from the Lord. Now he, about to institute this mystery, joined to himself disciples who were still following him and were regarded as zealous for his teaching. Let us strive to be truly such, and not admit others to these mysteries while their administration is in our hands; yet let us equally take pains to make, as far as we can, true disciples of him from those who are not, and if we cannot, this will take nothing from us, even if others remain openly Jews. Nor is it fitting that the good things of the Lord be denied to good people because of the bad. Then, since the minister speaks not his own words but the words of the Lord, let us receive them with true faith as the words of the Lord. He gives thanks to the Father; let us give thanks together with him. He takes bread and wine, and distributing them he bids them be received: let us also receive them, the minister to distribute and take, the people to receive. He added, Eat, drink: let us eat and drink, not carry them about or enclose them. He adds, This is my body, this is my blood: let us believe this, and not doubt that these very symbols are given to us, and given as food and drink of eternal life, so that we may live more and more in Christ and have him living in us. He added, which is given for you, which is poured out for the forgiveness of sins for you and for many, which is the new covenant: let us believe these things and give thanks to the Lord that by the sacrifice of himself he expiated our sins, and sanctioned and confirmed the new and eternal covenant of grace between the Father and us, so that he might be our Father and we his children. Finally he bids us do these things in remembrance of him. Therefore let us proclaim Christ wholly in connection with these mysteries, and everything he has done for us; and let us devote ourselves to him in turn, and all that is ours, and bear witness to this by our confession of faith, by pious praises, prayers, and the offering of gifts, for we must not come into the sight of God empty-handed; but in the person of Christ, hungry and thirsty, naked and a stranger, sick and in chains, some gift is always to be offered to his members. If we believe and do these things simply in this way, we will truly be disciples of the Lord, and truly be fed by him unto eternal life. Easily avoiding superfluous questions, which serve only empty glory and contention, let us apply ourselves wholly to this, that by this holy feeding we may feel Christ living in us more fully, for our own consolation and advance in godliness, and may express and display him to others by every effort of good works. The bitter and excessively harsh contention about this mystery which arose among us Germans was a work of the flesh. We thought that Dr. Luther was attaching Christ in heaven too closely to earthly signs. He for his part would acknowledge or hand over nothing in the Supper but bread and wine. At last the Lord granted that we agreed well both in words and in substance; and so let us commend these mysteries on both sides, so that neither does he seem to attribute to Christ things unworthy of him, nor do we celebrate the Lord's Supper without the Lord. For we on both sides confess that two things are received here: the earthly, bread and wine, and the heavenly, the body and blood of Christ the Lord. Some spoke of these sacraments rather loosely, others more coarsely; these have withdrawn to a godly moderation consonant with the words of the Lord, and hence in our churches there is a godly agreement established even on this matter. Strive to keep or restore this among yourselves wherever it has been weakened, imitating us in what belongs to Christ, not in what belonged to the flesh, as is all contention and strife among the saints. May the Lord himself teach you all his mysteries, perfect them, and grant you to the perfection of salvation and of blessed communion with himself. Amen.

units.la: Huic nos precibus diligenter commendare velitis, & hosce nostros fratres qui sanctissimè apud nos vixerunt & sedulo studuerunt visceribus Domini compleċti & fouere studeatis. Argentorati x.Septemb.anno Christi M. D. XLI.
units.tr: We ask you to commend us diligently in your prayers, and to strive to embrace and cherish, with the bowels of the Lord, these our brothers, who have lived most holily among us and have zealously sought to... Strasbourg, 10 September, in the year of Christ 1541.

units.la: Deditus vobis in Domino Martinus Bucerus manu mea.
units.tr: Given to you in the Lord, Martin Bucer, by my hand.

units.la: CALVINVS FARELLO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL.

units.la: NON est quod de mea expostulatione sis multum solicitus: magis enim iocari tecum quàm serio conqueri volueram. Satis enim scio me animo tuo non excidisse, etiam si centies in literis prætereas. Itaque te securum hac parte esse iubeo. Vtinam tam facilis tibi esset compositio cum iis, qui te & Ecclesiam tuam vexant & fatigant.Quanquam, vt dicis,bellum cū mundo & carne reformidare non debemus, si Christo seruire libeat,imò ex animo appetendum est:sed tamen optandum est, vt quicquid hodie cum Christo bellum gerit, in voluntariam obedientiam potius se dedat, quam vi & armis subactum frangatur,non corrigatur. Verum quoniam vult nos exercere Dominus in sua militia, nec quiescere nos patitur, pugnemus sanè forti & constanti animo: modò iis armis quibus nos instruxit. Nam sub eius auspiciis victoria semper erit in manu.Quod cœna Domini celebrata est, præsertim cum hac denunciatione quam refers,erit optima ratio,vt spero, ad recolligendam Ecclesiam. Et audio ea moderatione, quam nunc adhibes, partim sedari, partim frangi multorum animos. Dum succedit, nihil omittas,quod ad sanandum vulnus quouis modo valeat.Erit hîc pulcherrimus triumphus,si Satan cum paucis antesignanis à sua acie deseratur.Quod ad rationes nostras attinet,plus satis verum este experior, quòd scribis de iugo inæquali, sed tolero quod tollere non licet. Itaque si mihi Viretus auseratur,prorsus perij: nec hanc Ecclesiam saluam retinere potero. Quare te & alios mihi ignoscere par est, si omnem moueo lapidem, ne eo spolier. Volo interim consultum Laufannensi Ecclesiæ, idque ex piorum fratrum sententia, & tuo quoque ipsius arbitrio: tantum ille mihi maneat. Id Bernæ neruis omnibus contendo, verum ne in malam partem fratres acciperent, si ipsis præteritis ad alios me conuerterem, nuper veni Viuiacum. Effeci illic meis rationibus, quod vix sperabam: vt non modò annuerent se minimè intercessuros, si eum nobis concederent Bernates, sed asseretent sibi videri ex communi Ecclesiatum bono fore, si mihi ad tempus adiungeretur. Hic nolim te multis hominibus alioqui non facillimis, esse morosiorem: nam plus multo hic negocij nobis est quàm putas. Plebem habemus vtcunque obsequentem. Conciones saltem frequentantur diligenter: mores satis sunt compositi, sed multum adhuc vitij & in capite & corde: quod nisi curerur sensim, vereor ne in pessimum vlcus demum erumpat. Cum illis intestinis malis & absconditis pugnatur non sine summa difficultate, vt bene nosti, & scis quales habeam commilitones, hoc remoto. Fratri consuluimus fideliter quod videbatur. Cæterum quoties volet, reperiet me ad omnia paratum: verùm ideo nunc supersedi, quòd non putabam esse vtile. Si dissentias, sequar te potius, nec quidpiam eorum quæ mihi iniunges detrectabo. Quandiu aliquid valebimus nos duo, non est quod queraris te nihil posse, scis enim nos esse penitus tuos. Vale optime & integerrime frater. Saluta diligenter omnes, Corderium præsertim, cui cum primum licuerit respondebimus. Totam familiam cupimus esse saluam. Geneuæ 11. Nouembris M. D. XLI.
units.tr: You need not be very anxious about my complaint. I meant to joke with you rather than to complain in earnest. I know well enough that I have not slipped from your mind, even if you pass me over in your letters a hundred times. So I tell you to be easy on that score. I wish agreement with those who harass you and your Church were as easy to reach. Although, as you say, we should not dread war with the world and the flesh if we wish to serve Christ, indeed we should seek it with all our heart, still I hope that whoever now wages war against Christ will surrender to voluntary obedience rather than be broken by force and arms, and be corrected rather than crushed. But since the Lord wishes to exercise us in his warfare and does not allow us to rest, let us fight with a brave and steady spirit, only with the weapons with which he has equipped us. For under his leadership victory will always be in our hands. The fact that the Lord's Supper has been celebrated, especially with this announcement that you mention, will, I hope, be the best means of gathering the Church together again. I hear that by the moderation you now show, the spirits of many are partly calmed and partly broken. While this goes forward, leave nothing undone that might in any way help to heal the wound. It will be a splendid triumph here if Satan is deserted by his few standard-bearers. As for our affairs, I find it only too true what you write about an unequal yoke, but I endure what I may not remove. So if Viret were taken from me, I would be utterly lost, nor could I keep this Church safe. Therefore it is right that you and others should forgive me if I move every stone so as not to be stripped of him. Meanwhile I want provision made for the Lausanne Church, in accordance with the opinion of our pious brothers and with your own judgment too, provided that he remains with me. I am pressing this at Berne with all my strength. But lest the brothers take it amiss if I turned to others without consulting them, I have recently come to Vevey. There I achieved, by my arguments, something I scarcely hoped for: they not only agreed that they would not oppose it if the Bernese granted him to us, but they declared that it seemed to them for the common good of the Churches if he were attached to me for a time. Here I would not have you, being otherwise not very easygoing, be more difficult with many people who are not at all easy themselves; for here we have much more trouble than you think. We have a common people that is somewhat compliant. The sermons at least are attended diligently. Morals are reasonably well ordered, but there is still much vice both in head and heart, which, unless it is treated gradually, I fear will at last break out into a very dangerous sore. We fight against these inward and hidden evils not without the greatest difficulty, as you know well, and you know what fellow soldiers I have, apart from this. We have faithfully consulted the brother as far as seemed right. As for the rest, whenever he wishes, he will find me ready for everything; but I have for now held back because I did not think it useful. If you disagree, I will rather follow you, and I will refuse nothing of what you enjoin on me. As long as the two of us have any strength, you have no reason to complain that you can do nothing, for you know that we are wholly yours. Farewell, best and most upright brother. Greet everyone diligently, especially Corderius, to whom we will reply as soon as we can. We wish the whole household to be safe. Geneva, 11 November 1541.

units.la: CAL. FARELLO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL.

units.la: SCripturus eram longiores literas & accuratiores, ita enim res poscebat: verùm cùm mihi bonus hic frater nunciasset, subIatum esse nobis optimum patrem nostrum & sanctæ memoriæ Capitonem, Bucerum verò peste laborare, ita fui mente & animo perculsus, vt nihil aliud nunc queam quàm lugere. Ignosces igitur mi frater, quòd breues & confusas literas de re magna & seria à me accipis. Scis ita fuisse inter nos ab initio constitutum, vt si rediremtu me reduceres, quò vtriusque ministerium, quod vnum fuit, simul restitueretur. Non passus est hoc Satan, qui sub id tempus eam tempestatem excitauit, vt nō posses ab Ecclesia tua sine magno, immò præsentissimo naufragij periculo pedem mouere. Distulimus eousque dum te istis turbis Dominus liberaret. Nunc cùm eius beneficio resistic paciores esse audiamus, cùm ministerij nostri communis, tum
units.tr: I had meant to write a longer and more careful letter, as the matter demanded. But when this good brother told me that our excellent father, Capito of blessed memory, had been taken from us, and that Bucer was suffering from the plague, I was so struck in mind and spirit that for now I can do nothing but mourn. So forgive me, brother, for receiving from me a short and disordered letter on so great and serious a matter. You know that it was agreed between us from the beginning that, if you returned, you would bring me back, so that the ministry of each of us, which was one and the same, could be restored together. Satan would not allow this. At that time he stirred up such a storm that you could not move your foot from your Church without the great and immediate danger of shipwreck. We put it off until the Lord freed you from those troubles. Now, since we hear by his kindness that things are calmer, both for our common ministry and

units.la: Ep. fl. 40. mea priuatim,Ecclesiae etiam vniuersae interest, te semel huc venire: si nulla alia ratio effet, prestare, tamen te decet quam mihi fidem dedisti. Verum sunt, vt dixi,plures & maiores causae, quae nullam tibi excusationem relinquunt. Audiebam cum istic essem, praetextus nescio quos, qui mihi displicebant. Dicebas te a populo expulsum,non posse igitur a Senatu,hoc est a paucis hominibus restitui. Quasi vero tumultuosa illa perditorum hominum factio populus fuerit. Etsi fuit, quasi non illud plebiscitum satis superque tibi esse debeat,quo populus ipse pronunciauit,te iniuria pulsum esse. Constat eos qui te expulerunt,aut capite puniri, aut vrbe esse profugos,reliquos autem pudore tacere aut fateri suum scelus. Nodum illud plebiscitum factum fuerat, quo populus innocentiam nostram vna voce comprobauit, cum tu nimia importunitate a me extorfiras vt venturum me reciperem. Tunc tamen vt verum fatear, habebam in animo aliquid primo aduentu de innocentia nostra testari, & totam causam nostram exponere, vt omnis non tantum maledicendi, sed etiam mussitandi occasio improbis tolleretur. Tametsi nō sum optimus dicendi artifex,nō verebar tamen quin tam bona causa plausibilis futura esset vbi populus, sese damnando, & culpam suam confitendo anteuertit, putaui hac necessitate nos esse prorsus liberatos. Imo praeter id quod futurus erat superuacuus labor, videbam tentari hoc non posse sine specie aliqua inhumanitatis. Quid enim hoc aliud fuisset, quam prostratis hostibus insultare? Cum autem venissem, obiter quidem perstrinxi, qua fide & integritate in hac Ecclesia versati simul essemus. De aduersariis verbum vnum facere puduit: ne eorum causam,qui a Deo & hominibus, suoque ipsorum iudicio damnati essent, viderer in dubium vocare: sed haec coram tecum malo disputare. Nunc ad id quod instat:non rite te vocari dicis a Senatu, cum electus sis a populo. Atqui nondum annus est,cum primis Senatus literis contentus eras, & iam quodammodo aditer accinctus. Unde nunc ista noua religio? Quid quod latum est ad populum de te nominatim, cum populus sciuit,in vrbem reducendos esse eos quos expulerat? Neque enim aut de me aut alio quopiam facta mentio est,sed in haec verba,Nonne hic pronunciatis iniuriam esse factam Farello & sociis eius? Quid vltra requiris a populo, quam vt innocentiam tuam approbando reum se faciat? Additum est, Vultis vt Farellus cum sociis suis,&c. Dabis veniam mihi, opt. frater, si quid durius dixero: sed haec difficultas a morositate potius, quam a recto iudicio, proficisci videtur. Mihi sane perspecta est animi tui syncetitas: neque mihi tot exempla exciderunt, quibus satisdeclarasti, quam parum te respicias: sed vide ne quid tale fusipicari queant qui te non penitus nitus norunt: imo ij qui non suspicabuntur,ansam tamen arri-piant obtrectandi. At Ecclesia pro modo offensionis nequaquam satisfecit. Quis negat? verum si infspicias quàm res adhuc sint hic tenerae, ne quid asperius dicam, ipse consulas non esse vlterius progrediendum in hoc negocio. Te igitur per Christum obtestor,mi Farelle, vt non quoslibet audias consultores, sed eorum acquiescas consiliis, qui nec prudentia carent, & non minus de tui ministerij honore sunt solliciti quàm tu ipse. Quod si nos nihil sapere, nihil videre, nihil iudicare existimas, patere tamen ab amicis te semel exorari. Vale optime & charissime frater iii. Calend.Decemb. M. D. XLI.
units.tr: Ep. fl. 40. My own private interest, and that of the whole Church too, requires that you come here once. Even if there were no other reason, you ought to keep the promise you gave me. But, as I said, there are more and weightier reasons, which leave you no excuse. While I was there I heard some pretexts, I know not which, and they displeased me. You said that you had been expelled by the people and so could not be restored by the Senate, that is, by a few men. As if that riotous faction of worthless men were the people! Even if it was, as if the plebiscite were not enough and more than enough for you, the plebiscite by which the people itself declared that you had been wrongfully driven out. It is well known that those who drove you out have either been punished with death or have fled the city, and the rest keep silent out of shame or confess their crime. Not long ago that plebiscite was passed, by which the people with one voice approved our innocence, after you, with excessive importunity, had wrung from me a promise that I would return. Yet, to tell the truth, I had intended on my first arrival to bear witness to our innocence and to set out our whole cause, so that the wicked should be deprived of every occasion, not only for slander, but even for muttering. Although I am not a very skilled speaker, I did not doubt that so good a cause would be persuasive. Since the people had anticipated us by condemning itself and confessing its fault, I thought we were wholly freed from this necessity. Indeed, besides being needless labour, I saw that it could not be attempted without some appearance of inhumanity. For what else would it have been than to trample on enemies already laid low? When I came, I touched on only in passing the faith and integrity with which we had conducted ourselves together in this Church. I was ashamed to say a single word about our opponents, lest I seem to call into doubt the cause of those who had been condemned by God and by men, and by their own judgment. But I would rather discuss these things with you face to face. Now to the matter at hand: you say you are not rightly called by the Senate, since you were chosen by the people.
