units.la: k.ij. quàm vt flecti possent. Ac ne quid dissimulem, nó pauca illi obfuerunt. Necessitatem confl ituebat in morte soceri. Contrà obiiciebant fratres, scire fe iam vltra annú, hunc lapidem fuisse motum à Sonnerio. Dicebant alij, eum non inuenire aut villicos, aut redemptores, quia nimium exigeret. Omnes fere fcntiebant, non remedium quæri, sed compendium, quo fe magis ac magis immerg ret. Cùm fecundò rogare sententias instituerem, primus dixi meam (quod nó soleo facere) qua nihilominus Sonnerium admisi. Duo tantùm fuerunt, qui mihi assentirentur, Gallafius & Borgonius. Decem in proposito suo perstiterunt. Ita passus est repulsam. Quinetiam modis omnibus reiiftentem me classi cogunt scribere: cum laudetamen Sonnerij potius, quàm vlla nota. Valuit etiam non parum hæc ratio: quòd Ludouicum duabus Ecclesiis, ad quas traductus fuisset, longe imparem iudicabant. In eo mihi fecit iniuriam Sonnerius, quòd fe apud nonnullos iactauerat, quasi nihil fore difficultatis pollicitus effem. Dixit enim mihi in aurem Ferronius, ipsum ita gloriatum fuisse, quia recepissem in me onus illud: quod esse falsum, ipse testis es. Quomodo enim fratribus ius suum ac libertatem eriperem? sed hoc leue. Tu hominem, fi ad re venerit, consolaberis. Iterum atque iterum vale, cum vxore & familia. Dominus vos con feruet, ac regat Spiritu suo, Amen. Saluta fratres & vxorem diligenter, Tiliacam & reliquos amicos. Geneuæ, x v i. Maij.
units.tr: k.ij. And, not to conceal anything, not a few things told against him. He claimed that necessity lay in the death of his father-in-law. On the contrary, the brothers objected that they had known for more than a year that this stone had been moved by Sonnerius. Others said that he would find neither bailiffs nor contractors, since he demanded too much. Almost everyone felt that no remedy was being sought, but a gain, by which he would sink deeper and deeper. When I set about asking opinions a second time, I gave my own first (which I do not usually do), and in it I nonetheless admitted Sonnerius. Only two agreed with me, Gallafius and Borgonius; ten held firm to their proposal. So he suffered rejection. Moreover, although I resisted them in every way, they forced me to write to the classis, yet they praised Sonnerius rather than blaming him at all. This reason also weighed not a little: they judged Ludovicus far unequal to the two churches to which he had been transferred. In this Sonnerius wronged me, for he boasted to some people that I had promised there would be no difficulty at all. Ferronius whispered to me that he had gloried in this because I had taken that burden upon myself, which you yourself know to be false. For how could I snatch from the brothers their right and their liberty? But this is a small matter. You will console the man if it comes to that. Again and again, farewell, with your wife and household. May the Lord keep you and govern you by his Spirit, Amen. Greet the brothers and your wife warmly, Tiliac and our other friends. Geneva, 16 May.

units.la: M. D. X L V I I.
Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: CAL. VIRETO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO VIRET.

units.la: NVper hic fuit N. Postquam morbos expressi, remedium simul illud suggessi de quo inter nos locuti eramus. Probabat, sed putat difficile esse impetratu: fi tamen in tempore venerit, periculú faciet: fatetur enim in tanta necessitate omnia esse tentanda. Ego autem vereor ne prius mittantur, qui suo more post multam ostentationem nihil agant: ita res diu desiderata nimis citò elabetur. Verùm hoc vt alia omnia Dominus viderit. De caligis differtis fuit nobis hic nuper aliquid negotioli. Hic erat prætextus: sed iam erumpere cœperant in maximam licentiam. Cùm ducenti eorum rogatu vocati fuissent, omnes adfuimus: ego orationem habui quæ illis momento extorsit quod certa spe deuorauerant. Disserui enim de omnibus corruptelis in genere, præfatus me nihil morari illas nugas, quia non audent palàm clamitare, fremunt ac frendent dentibus. Vno tamè experimento didicerunt, quòd non putauerunt populú esse nostrum. Cæsar tragicus postridie iter arripui: ne pompæ interessent:
units.tr: N. was here the other day. After I had described the diseases, I also suggested that remedy we had talked about between ourselves. He approved of it, but thinks it will be hard to obtain. Still, if it arrives in time, he will give it a trial, since he admits that in such great need everything must be attempted. I am afraid, however, that they will be sent first, and after much showing off will accomplish nothing, so that the matter, long desired, will slip away too quickly. But the Lord will see to this, as to everything else. About the stuffed boots, we recently had a little trouble here. It was a pretext, but they had already begun to break out into the greatest licence. When some two hundred were summoned at their request, we were all present. I gave an address which wrung from them in a moment what they had gulped down in certain hope. For I spoke about all the corruptions in general, prefacing that I would not dwell on those trifles, since they did not dare to shout openly, but only growled and gnashed their teeth. Yet by one experiment they learned that they had not supposed the people to be on our side. Like a tragic Caesar, I set out on my journey the next day, so as not to attend the procession, which that tumult made ludicrous and childish, since he had hoped it would be a pledge of some kind of power. We have unexpectedly thwarted all their plans, so God makes sport of these Thrasos. Farewell, brother, and most upright friend. May the Lord be with you always and bless your holy labours. Greet your wife in my name. Geneva, 28 May 1547. (Epist. 76.)

units.la: Epist.76. set:quam conu ntus ille ludicram & puerile reddidit, cum spe- raret fore imperij cuiusdam pignus.Nos illi ex insperato omnia sua consilia difcuiflimus,ita Deus ludit istos Thrafones. Vale frater & amice integerrim .Dominus tibi adsit perpetuò,& sanctis tuis laboribus benedicat. Saluta vxorem tuam meo nomine. Genevæ,x xv iii.Maij. M. D. XLVII.

Greet your wife in my name. Geneva, 28 May 1547.

units.tr: Calvin to Viret, Letter 77.

units.la: NVnc feriò nobis cerrandum est.Vocata rursus ad Consistorium fuerat vxor Comici Cæsaris, ob suam petulantiam. Illic ne asperiore quidem verbo lacessita, plus veneni euomuit, quàm vnquam antea.Primùm negauit, si quid deliquisset, nostri fori esse cognitionem: deinde conquesta est, sibi grauem ignominiæ notam inuri, quòd in eum locum venire cogeretur, quò nonnisi sceleratos & maleficos accersi fas esset. Cùm ex assessoribus vnus cohibere intemperiem vellet, in eum furorem conuertit. Hiscùm se Abel interponeret, ac diceret, mirari se, initiò profeita esset adeò se verecundam aut elinguem, quç respondere pluribus non posset: cùn par futura esset quamplurimis, maledicendo: tota verò rabies effCrbuit. Nisi vi extrusa fuisset, fere nos obruisset suis fulminibus. Senatus decreuit, vt in carcerem arctiorem includeretur. Elapsa est opera matronæ illius, quæ malas omnes causas suscipere in suum patrocinium solet. Alter ex filiis se comitem fugitiuæ adiungit. Cùm non procul à porta vrbis forte in Abelem incidisset, noui insultus: & quidem proteruiores. Abel nihil, quemadmodum & in Consistorio moderatissimè se gesserat. Postridie reperitur charta in suggestu, qua mortem nobis minantur, nisi sileamus. Exemplar ad te mitto. Senatus tanta audacia perculsus, iubet seuere de conspiratione inquiri. Negotium paucis mandat: quia multorum suspicio in Gruetum cadebat. Statim arripitur: alia tamen erat manus. Sed dum eius chartas revoluunt, multa reperiunt non minus capitalia. Libellus supplex, quem offerre populo statuerat in Comitiis: vbi disputabat nihil esse legibus vindicandum, nisi quod Rempub. læderet. Ita enim Venetos facere gubernandi peritissimos. Periculum verò esse, nedum hæc vrbs vnius hominis melancholici cerebro obtemperat, excitata seditione, perdat mille cives. Repertæ sunt etiam literæ, partim ad Andreæm Philippum, partim ad aliosscriptæ Quibusdam me nominabat, alias inuoluerat figuris: quæ tamen crassum artificium adeò sapiunt, vt digitis attingere liceat quicquid tegere voluit. Paginæ etiam duæ compositæ Latina lingua, vbi ridetur Scriptura tota, laceratur
units.tr: Now at last I must close my letter. The wife of Caesar the comedian had been summoned again to the Consistory because of her insolence. There, though not even provoked with a harsher word, she poured out more venom than ever before. First she denied that our court had any jurisdiction over her, if she had done anything wrong. Then she complained that a serious mark of disgrace was being branded on her, because she was being forced to come to a place to which only criminals and wrongdoers were lawfully summoned. When one of the assessors wanted to restrain her outrageous behaviour, she turned her rage on him. When Abel intervened and said that he was surprised she had at first shown herself so modest or tongue-tied that she could not answer many points, since she would be a match for very many in slandering, her whole fury then boiled over. Had she not been forced out by violence, she would almost have overwhelmed us with her thunderbolts. The Senate decreed that she be shut up in a narrower prison. By the efforts of that matron, who is accustomed to take up every bad cause under her protection, she escaped. One of her sons joined the fugitive as her companion. When by chance they met Abel not far from the city gate, they launched a new attack, and a more shameless one at that. Abel said nothing, just as in the Consistory he had conducted himself with the greatest restraint. The next day a paper was found on the pulpit, threatening us with death unless we keep silent. I am sending you a copy. The Senate, struck by such audacity, orders a strict inquiry into the conspiracy. It entrusts the business to a few men, because suspicion of many fell on Gruet. He was seized at once, but the hand was another. However, while they were going through his papers, they found many things no less capital. There was a supplicating petition, which he had resolved to offer to the people at the assemblies, in which he argued that nothing should be punished by the laws except what injures the Republic. For that, he said, is how the Venetians, the most skilled of governors, act. And there is danger, he said, that this city, not to mention obeying the brain of one melancholy man, once sedition is stirred up, will destroy a thousand citizens. Letters were also found, some written to Andreas Philippus, others to different people. In some of them he named certain people, in others he had wrapped things in figures of speech; yet these are so crude a device that one may touch with a finger whatever he wished to conceal. There were also two pages composed in Latin, in which the whole of Scripture is mocked and torn apart

units.la: k. iij. Christus, immortalitas animæ vocatur somnium & fabula: denique tota Religio conuellitur. Non puto illum auctorem: sed quia est eius manus, causam dicere cogetur. Quamquam fieri potest vt ipse ab aliis audita in commentarium sua minerua redegerit. Suntenim mutilæ sententiæ, referte oleocifmis & barbarismis.
units.tr: Christ, the immortality of the soul is called a dream and a fable; in short, the whole religion is overthrown. I do not think he is the author, but since it is his handwriting, he will be forced to answer for it. Although it may be that he gathered together in his own fashion things he had heard from others and reduced them to a commentary. For the sentences are mutilated, stuffed with solecisms and barbarisms.

units.la: Nepotem ruum diutius retinui quàm vellet. Et enim vere cundus & timidus. Proinde cùm videret, non inueniri conditionem, nolebat mihi molestus esse. Ego tamen si parum sapei affulgeret, volebam omnia prius experiri, quàm eum termi tere. Per eum certe nō stetit. Nam mer atores nostri per fe, vt plurimum, tabernas custodiunt. Famulis & institoribus vtuntur ad colligen da nomina. Ita factum est, vt nemo industriæ eius periculum facere sustinuerit. Non est igitur quòd eum accusei. Nam ego & modestiæ, & frugalitatis, & industriæ testimonium deferre illi potuissem, si inuentus fuisset dominus. Sed ea est hodie ratio vrbis nostræ, vt tenuiter sedomi contineant boni: improbi autem & nos & nostros fugiant. Si Lugdunum velles mittere, illic forte locus esset. Mihi tamen non probatur. Mallem tempo rum iniqui atem redimi pecunia. Vale frater & amicè intergerrime, vnà cum familia, cui plurimam salutem precamur ego & vxor. Christophorum etiam compatrem nostrum, & Symmyftas salutabis diligenter amborum nomine. Dominus Iesus vos custodiat, vobis adsit, vos gubernet, vestris sanctis laboribus benedicat, Amé. Geneuæ, 11. Iulij. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: I have kept my nephew longer than he wished. For he is indeed modest and timid. Therefore, when he saw that no position could be found, he did not want to be a burden to me. Yet if even a little glimmer of hope shone, I wanted to try everything before dismissing him. Certainly it was not for want of effort on his part. For our merchants, for the most part, keep their shops themselves. They use servants and shop assistants to collect debts. So it happened that no one was willing to put his diligence to the test. There is therefore no reason to blame him. For I could have borne witness to his modesty, frugality and diligence, had his master been found. But such is the present state of our city that the good keep quietly to themselves, while the wicked shun both us and ours. If you wished to send him to Lyon, perhaps there would be a place there. Yet I do not approve of it. I would rather that the injustice of the times were bought off with money. Farewell, brother and most dear friend, together with your household, to whom my wife and I send our most hearty greetings. Greet also diligently, on behalf of both of us, our compère Christopher and the Symmystae. May the Lord Jesus keep you, be present with you, guide you, and bless your holy labours. Amen. Geneva, 11 July 1547.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: BVCERVS CALVINO S.D.
units.tr: BUCER TO CALVIN, GREETINGS.

units.la: OMi Caluine, ànne Deus ideo defuerit Verbo suo, quia nos illud tam secure contempsimus? tam subitò támque fœdè & miserè concidit omnis superbia nostra. Sic vltus est in nobis, & vlciscitur adhuc iustus Deus cotumeliam nominis sui, quam à nostra passus est tam diuturna & perniciosissima hypocrisi. Vindicabit nomen suum & ab Antichristis à quibus infinitis & petulantissimis hodie afficitur opprobriis. Sed cùm nos sentientes tandem sicut quo prolapsi fumus, ita etiam quàm grauiter istud fumus commeriti, conuerterimus ad ipsum cædentem nos Patrem: ora nobisque infanter Dominum Iesum largitorem poenitentiæ & fidei, vt nobis crassitiem cordis pertundat, & compungat illud vero impietatis nostræ sensu & dolore, atque det nos ipsi totos credere & consecrare, quò per eum Patrem veniam exorent nostrorum peccatorum, & remissionem prę-fentium. fentium flagellorum : quæ sane nisi citò à nobis remoueantur, exitium minantur nobis. Excitionem quidem regni Christi non metuo, verum confido illud præclare propagădum, & Antichristum in dies magis proterendum: sed vereor vt nobis Germanis Dominus ad rem hanc vti velit. Cætera hic noster. Dominus sit vobiscum. Saluta tuos omnes meis verbis officiosissimè. x i x. Iulij. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: My dear Calvin, can it be that God has failed his Word because we despised it so carelessly? So suddenly and so shamefully and wretchedly has all our pride collapsed. Thus has the just God avenged upon us, and still avenges, the insult to his name, which he has suffered from our long-standing and most ruinous hypocrisy. He will also vindicate his name against the Antichrists, by whom he is today assailed with countless and most insolent reproaches. But since we, at last perceiving into what a fall we have slipped, and how grievously we have deserved this, have turned to the Father who is striking us, I pray to the Lord Jesus, the giver of repentance and faith, to break through the hardness of our hearts, to pierce and prick them with a true sense and sorrow for our impiety, and to grant that we may wholly entrust and consecrate ourselves to him, so that through him we may obtain from the Father pardon for our sins and remission of the present scourges, which indeed threaten destruction to us unless they are quickly removed. I do not fear the overthrow of Christ's kingdom; rather I trust that it will be spread splendidly and that Antichrist will be crushed more and more each day. But I fear that the Lord may not wish to use this means for us Germans. The rest is as it is here. The Lord be with you. Greet all your people most dutifully on my behalf. 19 July 1547.

units.la: Tuus Bucerus.
units.tr: Yours, Bucer.

units.la: CALVINVS PIIS GALLIS.
units.tr: Calvin to the Pious Frenchmen.

units.la: Dilectissimi fratres non dubito quin multa ad vos perferantur in dies tam ex his regionibus quàm ex Germania, quæ scandalo cessura sint illis qui non satis firmas radices egerunt in Domini nostri Iesu Christi fide. Quod autem ad vos attinet, ita vos à Domino confirmatos esse confido, vt neque vlla re eiusmodi neque vlla etiam grauiore dimoueri vobis vnquam contingat. Equidem fieri nō potest cum semel solido illi fundamento Ecclesiæ innixi sumus, quin ad sequissimos quosque fluctus & tempestates excipiendas parati, ad illarum tantum impetum immoti perstemus. Adeò etiam expedit illis casibus obnoxios nos esse, quibus nempe constantia & firmitas fidei nostræ explo retur. In Germania Dominus ita fastum omnem nostrorum contudit, atque potentiam illius amplificauit, à quo nihil præter malū expectari poterat, vt simul videri posset velle afferere regnū suum spirituale omnibus iis in locis in quibus illud antè exerat. Et res est quidem pro hominum captu tenuissimæ spei omnino: sed ta mē si Ecclesiam afflictam & Christi fui regnum illi precibus cō mendare non cessabimus, spero illum vltra captum nostrū manum operi admoturum. Timendum est enim ne adhuc humana subsidia oculos nobis obliuerint: nunc cum nihil obstat quominus ad illius vnius opem respiciamus, reuocemus in memoriā quā constanter seculis elapsis Ecclesiæ suæ adfuerit, vt in illa etiā ipsum ita glorificandū adhuc non dubitemus, vt admirari plane subeat, quod nemo ante sperasset. Interea verò pergamus in nostra militia sub Christi crucis vexillo, quod vnū longè omnibus hominū triumphis antecellit. Quod ad rumores quidè nostris turbis volitarunt, primùm illi maxima ex parte in ipso itinere ab auctoribus confecti sunt: neque enim decimam partem hic positi comperiretis. Sane nimis multos habemus duræ ceruicis & indomitæ, qui iugum subinde excutere gestiunt, vt suis tumul tibus dissipent & aboleant legitimum Ecclesiæ ordinem: sunt eo in numero & senes & iuuenes. Iuuentus imprimis hic est depravatissima. Cùm igitur illis vagans licentia non conceditur,
units.tr: Beloved brothers, I do not doubt that many reports reach you every day, both from these regions and from Germany, which will be a cause of stumbling to those who have not struck deep enough roots in the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ. As for you, I am confident that the Lord has so confirmed you that you will never be moved by anything of that kind, or even by anything more serious. Indeed, once we have rested on that solid foundation of the Church, it cannot happen that we should not remain unmoved by the onslaught of the most troubling waves and storms, prepared to meet them. It is also so expedient for us to be exposed to such trials, in which the constancy and firmness of our faith may be tested. In Germany the Lord has so crushed all the pride of ours, and so magnified the power of him from whom nothing but evil could be expected, that he seems to wish to assert his spiritual kingdom in all those places where it previously flourished. By human reckoning the matter is indeed of the faintest hope. Yet we will not cease to commend the afflicted Church and the kingdom of Christ to him in prayer, and I hope he will put his hand to the work beyond our grasp. There is a fear that human aids may have blinded our eyes. Now, since nothing stands in the way of looking to him alone for help, let us call to mind how constantly, across the ages, he has been present with his Church, so that we do not hesitate to hope that he will be glorified in it even now, to such a degree that it will astonish us, something no one had hoped for before. Meanwhile let us press on in our warfare under the banner of Christ's cross, which far surpasses all human triumphs. As for the rumours that have flown about in our troubles, first of all, they were for the most part manufactured by their authors on the very journey; for you would not find even a tenth part of them here. Indeed we have far too many stiff-necked and untamed people, who are eager from time to time to shake off the yoke, to scatter and abolish the lawful order of the Church by their tumults. Among them are both old men and young; the youth here is especially depraved. Since unbridled licence is not granted to them, they kick out from time to time and lash out with their heels.

units.la: k.iiij. calcitrant subinde & calcibus petunt. Non ita pridem leuissima de causa valde commoti sunt, quod illis caligae diffedtae interdicerentur, quod ante annum duodecimum in urbe prohibitum fuit: non quod ea res per se nos moraretur, sed quod per illas caligarum rimas fenestra omni profusioni & luxui aperta a nobis animaduerteretur. Testati fumus nempe disciplionem illam in sese nullius momenti esse, sed illam occasionem adhibuimus vt ad certum scopum collimaremus, quo nempe illorum audacia & profusio coerceretur atque constricta teneretur. Inter illam velitationem Diabolus alia quaedam suggessit, unde graues strepitus & susurri. Atque vbi nos cordatiores experti sunt quam vellent, atque ad illis resistendum magis animatos, erupit tandem venenum ex pectoribus, quod latebat prius. Sed illud totum merus est fumus: ac minae istorum nihil aliud sunt quam spuma superbiae Moab, cuius ferocia cum fremitu concidat oportet. Vtut sit, non est quod illa vos perturbent. Longe alios motus experti sunt Moses & Prophetae qui populi Dei rectores erant: atque istiusmodi exercitia nobis necessaria sunt. Veltrum est autem precibus pro nobis apud Dominum adesse, vt det ne vnquam declinemus, sed vt vitae etiam, si opus erit, ipsius vnius cultum anteponamus: vtque prae vniusillius timore omnium impiorum furorem & minas posthabeamus. Fax et etiam vt sedentur tandem turbae omnes quae infirmorum animos pungerent: quod vnum mihi omnium grauissimum esse solet. Dignatus est nos Dominus singulari beneficio cum Magistratum optime affectum dedit ad remedium adhibendum malo. Vna etiam fratres mecum optime sentiunt, vt in officio pergamus omnes, & in omnibus exteт aequabilis constantia. Bene valete dilectissimi fratres. Dominus opus suum persequatur in vobis magis ac magis.
units.tr: k.iiij. Not long ago they were greatly upset over a very trivial matter, because slashed breeches were forbidden to them, a prohibition that had been imposed in the city before the twelfth year. The thing itself did not hinder us in any way; but through the slits in those breeches we noticed a window opened to all extravagance and luxury. We made it clear, of course, that the rule was of no importance in itself, but we used the occasion to aim at a definite target: that their boldness and extravagance might be restrained and held in check. During that skirmish the Devil suggested other things, whence came loud noises and whispers. And when they found us more shrewd than they wished, and more resolute in resisting them, the poison at last burst out from their breasts, where it had lain hidden before. But all that is mere smoke, and the threats of those men are nothing but the foam of Moab's pride, whose fierceness must collapse with a roar. However that may be, there is no reason for you to be disturbed by these things. Moses and the Prophets, who were the rulers of God's people, experienced far different disturbances, and such exercises are necessary for us. It is your task, however, to stand by us before the Lord in prayer, that he may grant that we never turn aside, but that, if need be, we put the worship of him alone before our very lives, and that, through fear of him alone, we set aside the fury and threats of all the impious. Pray also that all the disturbances which sting the minds of the weak may at last be calmed; for me this is usually the heaviest burden of all. The Lord has deigned to bless us with a singular benefit, in that he has given us a magistrate very well disposed to apply a remedy to the evil. The brothers also agree with me entirely, so that we all persevere in our duty and show an even constancy in everything. Farewell, most beloved brothers. May the Lord carry on his work in you more and more.

units.la: Iulij XXIIII. M.D.XLVII.
CALVINUS VIRETO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO VIRET.

units.la: Acceptis tuis literis vocaui ad me mulierem. Ea audita breuiter notaui, in quibus cum R.minus congruebat eius responsio. Vt ingenio est admodum feroci atque etiam protervo, plus satis in causae suae defensione se extulit. Cohibui tantum eius intemperiem vt potui, sed quemadmodum dicis, breui mouebit nobis maiores turbas, nisi recepta fuerit. Proinde R. cófulo vt periculo huic mature occurrat. Nam cum furiosi sint mulierum impetus in eiusmodi repulsis, tum vero hanc animaduerti non leuiter exarsuram. Quod ad me attinet, vt coniugium rite contractum non video, ita R.fidem iudico penitus obligatam. Frustra enim libertati suae cauere voluit, sic agendo. Fateor sano sanè coniugium rem esse magis sacram, quàm vt nutu vel ambiguis promissis contrahatur. Proinde non apparet in eorum cõuentionibus ea religio, quæ coniugalem reuerentiam decebat, Sed exaduerso res magis seria erat, quàm vt ludicris pollicitationibus eludere debuerit, tam mulierculam, quàm alios. Ita nõ possum statuere, quin fidem suam obstrictam habeat. Verùm an tequam illi pronunties, quæ sit nostra vtriusque sententia, ipsum de capitibus adhuc controuersis interrogari optarim. Nam erit forte eiusmodi responsio, quæ si quid reliquum est dubitationis tollat: Quicquid tamen responderit, hominem vrgeas iis argumentis, quæ res ipsa suppeditat, ne se & illum absque profectu fabulæ exponat. In rebus nostris nihil nouum. Gruci negotium Syndici protrahunt, Senatu inuito, nec tamen vt decebat reclamante. Scis enim paucos esse cordatos. Ego in exagitandis communibus vitiis ac præcipuè iuuenum corruptelis seueritatem meam exerceo. Pericula quæ mihi boni viri ex pluribus locis nuntiant, dissimulo: ne de me videar nimium solicitus. Dominus qualemcunque volet exitum dabit. Vale frater & amice integerrime vnà cum vxore & familia. Dominus Iesus te perpetuò gubernet, tibíque adsit. Salutem plurimam dices fratribus & vxori meo nomine. Vxor te & familiam tuam salutat. Genevæ, XXIIII.Iulij. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: I received your letter and sent for the woman. I took brief notes of what she said, and her answer agreed in few points with what R. had told us. She is a very fierce and even headstrong person by nature, and in defending her cause she went well beyond what was needful. I restrained her outbursts as far as I could. But as you say, she will soon stir up greater troubles for us unless the matter is settled. I therefore advise R. to meet this danger early. Women's attacks are furious when they have been rejected in this way, and I perceive that this woman will flare up badly. As for myself, I do not see that a marriage was properly contracted, but I judge that R. is thoroughly bound by his promise. By acting as he did, he tried in vain to guard his freedom. I grant that marriage is a matter far too sacred to be contracted by a nod or by ambiguous promises. Yet no such reverence for the married state appears in their agreements. On the contrary, the matter was too serious to be trifled with by playful pledges, whether to the little woman or to anyone else. So I cannot decide that he is not bound by his word. But before you tell him our joint opinion, I would like him to be questioned about the points still in dispute. His answer will perhaps be of such a kind as to remove whatever doubt remains. Whatever he replies, press the man with those arguments which the matter itself supplies, so that he does not expose himself and her to no purpose in this affair. Nothing new in our affairs. The Syndics are dragging out Gruet's case, against the wishes of the Council, though not, as it should be, with its protest. You know there are few men of sound judgment. I am directing my severity against common vices, and especially against the corruption of the young. I keep quiet about the dangers which good men report to me from several places, so that I do not seem overly anxious about myself. The Lord will give whatever outcome he pleases. Farewell, brother and most upright friend, together with your wife and household. May the Lord Jesus always guide you and be with you. Give my warm greetings to the brethren, and in my name to your wife. My wife greets you and your household. Geneva, 24 July 1547.

units.la: CAL. FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETING.

units.la: EGo vero maiorem tibi gratiam habeo, quàm verbis facilè testari queam, quòd fidem operámque tuam nobis vltrò detulisti, cùm nos magnis difficultatibus vrgeri putares. Quàquam nihil nouum fecisti, nec inexpectatum. Quòd autem non ium vsus, id in causa fuit, quòd volitabant circunquaque varij rumores quos extinctos optabam. Atqui excitati fuissent magis ac magis, si te ac Virctum aduocasset. Scis quibuscum hominibus nobis res sit, & quàm obloquendi cupidis. Quotidie literæ adferebantur, præsertim Lugduno, ex quibus intelligebam, me plus decies fuisse occisum. Tollenda igitur improborum sermonibus occasio fuit. Nunc pacatus est status. Senatum habemus bonæ causæ fauentem. Amedæus nosier adhuc est in Gallia. Vxor apud patrem, vbi suo more bacchatur. Et tamen petimus à Senatu, vt siquâ refipiscentiæ spem ostenderet, superiora omnia ignoscerentur. Hoc non est impetratum. Nam ecvsque progressa est, vt spem veniæ sibi præciderit. Quoniam dies Cœnæ appropinquat, Penthesileam conueniam. Nuper Frumentus de reconciliatione egit: sed volebat rem transfigi, & arbitro. Respondi, non adeo destitutam esse nostram Ecclesiam, quin fratres nostri huic prouinciæ subeundæ partes futuri essent. Tenta bimus omnia. Ettamen atrociter me læsit. Nam cum in Baptismo Iacobi nostri de vxoris meæ & prioris mariti lapsu confessus fuisset quod erat, apud suos calumniata est vxorem igitur meam scortum esse. Videsprocteruiam. Tractabo eam, non vt meretur, sed pro officij mei ratione. Addequod N fabulam composuerat ple nam calumniæ: me abs te & Vireto seuere fuisse castigatum, quod cum hic à vobis subrogatus forem tanquam vicarius, precaria auctoritate nimium abuterer. Nunc autem multo opportunius venires, quàm antehac. Audires omnia quæ literis committi nequeunt. Vulneribus manum admoueres, quæ nondum bene obduxerunt cicatricem. De occultis morbis fanandis inter nos consultaremus. Videbis ergo an quicquam tibi dabitur otij. Tridentinos Patres aggressus sum. Sed initia lente procedunt. Hoc fit, quia nulla hora mihi vacua est ab assiduis interpellationibus. Vale frater integerrime, & amice singularis. Saluta Symmystas & tuam familiam meo nomine diligenter. Dominus vo bis semper adsit, vos regat, vestris laboribus benedicat. Amen. Geneuæ, x x i. Augusti. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: I owe you far more gratitude than I can easily express in words, because you offered your faith and labour to us unasked, thinking that we were pressed by great difficulties. Yet you have done nothing new or unexpected. The reason I did not make use of your help was that various rumours were flying about on every side, and I wanted them stifled. Yet they would have been stirred up more and more if you had been summoned, along with Viret. You know what kind of men we have to deal with, and how eager they are to slander. Letters were brought to us daily, especially from Lyon, from which I understood that I had been killed more than ten times over. So the occasion for the wicked to gossip had to be removed. Now the state of affairs is calm. We have a Council favourable to our good cause. Our Amedeus is still in France. His wife is with her father, where she rages in her usual way. Yet we have asked the Council that, if she showed any hope of repentance, all past offences be pardoned. This has not been granted, for she has gone so far that she has cut off her own hope of forgiveness. Since the day of the Supper is approaching, I will meet Penthesilea. Recently Frumentus spoke to me about reconciliation, but he wanted the matter settled by an arbiter. I replied that our Church was not so destitute that our brethren would not be able to take on the role in this region. We will try everything. Yet she has hurt me bitterly. When our Jacob confessed at his baptism what had really happened concerning my wife and her former husband's fall, she slandered my wife among her own people, calling her a whore. See her impudence. I will deal with her not as she deserves, but as the duty of my office requires. Moreover, N. had composed a story full of slander: that I had been severely rebuked by you and Viret, because I, being appointed here by you as a substitute, had abused my borrowed authority too much. But now you would come at a much more opportune time than before. You would hear everything that cannot be committed to letters. You would apply your hand to wounds which have not yet closed well into scar. We would consult together on how to heal hidden diseases. See, then, whether any leisure can be given to you. I have made a start with the Fathers of Trent, but the beginnings move slowly. This happens because no hour is free from my constant interruptions. Farewell, brother most upright, and friend of rare integrity. Greet your fellow-workers and your household diligently in my name. May the Lord always be with you, guide you, and bless your labours. Amen. Geneva, 21 August 1547.

units.la: Ioannes Caluinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: CAL. VIRETO.
units.tr: CALVIN TO VIRET.

units.la: HOstes nostri ita sunt exæcati, vt nullum honesti respectum habeant. Hesternus dies suspicionem à nobis prius conceptam non parum comprobauit: eos certare tanta impudentia, vt tumultum aliquem mouerent. Vocati fuerant ducenti. Collegis meis pridie condixeram me in curiam venturum. Adfuimus & quidem ante tempus: quia multi adhuc in publico ambulabant, egressi fumus extra portam curiæ contiguam. Illinc multi clamores & confusi audiebantur. Nec mora, adeo creuerunt, vt certum ducerem seditionis signum. Ego mox accurro: horribilis erat rerum facies. In conferfiimas turbas me conii cio. Tamen fi omnes fere essent attoniti ad me tamen omnes facere concursum, huc illuc raptare, ne quid iniuriæ paterer. Ego Deum & homines testari, me ideo venisse vt corpus meum gladiis obiicerem. Hortari vt à me inciperent, si vellent sanguinem fundere. Multum ex feruore statim remiserunt, cum improbi, tum verò præcipuè boni. Tandem ad locum Senatus pertractus sum. Illic novæ pugnæ, quibus me interposui medium. Putant omnes factum meo interuentu fuisse, ne magna & fœda strages ederetur. Collegæ mei interea turbæ permixti erant. Obtinui vt compositi omnes sederent. Oratione longa & vehementi quam habui habu: pro temporis ratione, dicunt mirè fuisse omnes permo-tos, saltem paucis exceptis: qui tamen non minus laudarunt quàm boni,quod à me gestum erat. Hoc quidem priuilegio me hactenus & Collegas Deus muniuit,vt minimam lasionem nostri non aliter se detestari fingant, etiam qui sunt sceleratissimi, quàm parricidium. Eo tamen prorupit improbitas, vt retineri qualemcunque Ecclesiç statum diutius posse, meo praesertim ministerio vix sperem. Fractus sum, crede mihi, nisi manum Deus porrigat.Vale frater & amice integerrime.Saluta Symmy-ftam & omnes fratres. Ego & vxor mea plurimam salutem tibi optamus. Dominus vobis adsit perpetuò, xv11.Septembris. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: Our enemies have been so blinded that they have no regard for decency. Yesterday's events have not a little confirmed the suspicion we had conceived earlier: that they were contending with such shamelessness that they would stir up some tumult. Two hundred men had been summoned. I had told my colleagues the day before that I would come to the council chamber. We arrived, and indeed early, because many people were still walking about in the square; we went out through the gate adjoining the council chamber. From there many shouts and confused noises could be heard. Without delay they grew so loud that I judged it a certain sign of sedition. I ran over at once: the appearance of things was horrible. I threw myself into the thickest of the crowds. Although nearly everyone was dumbfounded, they all nevertheless made a rush towards me, dragging me this way and that, so that I should suffer no injury. I called God and men to witness that I had come there precisely to expose my body to the swords. I urged them to begin with me if they wished to shed blood. They soon relaxed a great deal of their heat, both the wicked and, above all, the good. At last I was drawn to the place of the Senate. There were fresh struggles there, into the midst of which I threw myself. Everyone thinks that the outcome was due to my intervention, so that a great and foul slaughter was not made. Meanwhile my colleagues had been mixed up in the throng. I managed to have them all sit down in order. With the long and vehement speech which I made, given the circumstances, they say that everyone was greatly moved, at least all except a few; yet these praised what I had done no less than the good men did. Thus far God has protected me and my colleagues with this privilege: even those who are most wicked pretend to detest any harm done to us no less than parricide. Yet wickedness has broken out to such a degree that I can hardly hope that any kind of state of the Church can be maintained much longer, especially through my ministry. I am broken, believe me, unless God stretches out his hand. Farewell, brother and most upright friend. Greet Symmystus and all the brothers. My wife and I wish you very many greetings. May the Lord be with you always. 17th September 1547.

units.la: CAL. FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: Calvin to Farel, greetings

units.la: IAM mihi placere incipit meum antidotum, ex quo tantopere tibi probatur:nam antehac mihi non satisfaciebat. Quanquam forte qui labores meos quotidianos nosti, adeoque pugnas quibus non tam exerceor quàm conficior, veniam mihi concedis, si quid minus est absolutum. Ego certè ipse miror, vllam scri-ptionem lectu dignam posse iam à me prodire. Quod me & Collegas meos hortaris vt infracto animo perstemus, mihi verò neque periculà, neque molestiæ animum minuunt: sed quia in rebus tam confusis interdum consilio destituor, missionem à Deo mihi dari cupio. Stultum votum, inquies, fateor: sed quid Moses tam insigne patientiæ exemplar? nónne impositum humeris suis conqueritur nimis graue onus? Atque his quidem cogitationibus solicitor duntaxat, non tamen acquiesco. Nostris homini-bus iniecimus aliquem metum: & tamen nihildum correctio-nis apparet. Tanta est impudentia, vt nostros omnes clamores patulis auribus & surdis absorbeant: denique multorum incura-biles sunt morbi. Tentauimus enim hactenus fere omnia, nullo profectu. Vltimus actus restat, cui te vellem interesse. Quàm tra-gicum tumultu Deus composuerit, arbitror te ex meis ad Viretum literis intellexisse: ita enim mandaueram. Ducenti iusserunt vt nos & alij decem pacificatores dissidia omnia tolleremus. Volui à meipso fieri initium. Negabat hesternus noster Cesar sibi quic-quam esse, mecum simulatis, ego autem plus statim expressi. Graui & æquabili oratione vsus sum, adhibui punctiones acu-tas, sed quæ minimè caederent. Tametsi refipiscentiam manu in manum implicita promisit, vereor ne frustrà surdo cecinerim fabulam. Vtinam aduentu tuo rursus me exhilares. Apud Vire-tum scio quosdam de immodica mea asperitate conquestos esse. Quid crediderit, nescio: subolfecitamen cum innere nc fetuori meo plus satis indulgeam. Rogaui vt huc veniret. Dicit ille apud Terentium, Si hic esses, aliter sentires. Idem liceret etiam mihi dicere. Tu si esses ego, nescio quid faceres, Verum inter mul tas acerbitates haec quoque est deuoranda. Non haec tibi au Vireto respondeo, sed aliis qui ociosi sua censura noscitigant. Vestram autem συμπαθείαν mihi videre videor, tantum abest, vt vos mihi iniquos esse putem. Vale frater optime & integerrime, vna cum tota familia, quam meo & vxoris nomine amanter salutabis, simul & omnes Collegas: adeóque bonos omnes. Genevæ, XXVIII. Decemb. M. D. XLVII.
units.tr: My antidote is at last beginning to please me, since you approve of it so highly; before this it did not satisfy me. Still, you know my daily labours and the struggles by which I am worn down rather than merely harassed, so perhaps you will pardon me if something is less than finished. I am truly astonished that any writing of mine can now come forth worth reading. You urge me and my colleagues to persevere with an unbroken spirit. But dangers and troubles do not diminish my courage. What wears me down is that in such confused affairs I am sometimes without counsel, and I long for God to grant me release. You will say this is a foolish wish, and I admit it. Yet what of Moses, that remarkable model of patience? Did he not complain that the burden laid on his shoulders was too heavy? I am troubled by such thoughts, but I do not find rest in them. We have put some fear into our people, yet no sign of amendment has appeared. Such is their shamelessness that they swallow all our outcries with open ears and deaf hearts; in short, many of their diseases are incurable. So far we have tried almost everything, with no result. One final step remains, and I wish you were present for it. I suppose you have learned from my letters to Viret how tragically the disturbance was settled, for I had instructed him to write. The Two Hundred ordered that I and ten other peacemakers should remove all the disputes. I wanted to make a start with myself. Our Caesar of yesterday denied that he was anything at all, pretending with me, but I at once drew more out of him. I spoke in a grave and even tone and applied sharp pricks, though not such as would cut deeply. Although he promised repentance, joining hands on it, I fear I have sung my tale to a deaf man in vain. I wish your coming would cheer me again. I know that some have complained to Viret about my excessive harshness. I do not know what he has believed, but I have sensed that I indulge my own ill temper rather too much. I asked that he come here. He says in Terence, "If you were here, you would think differently." I might say the same to him: "If you were I, you would not know what to do." But among so many bitternesses this too must be swallowed. I am not answering you or Viret here, but others who, idle, pry into things with their judgement. As for you, I seem to see your sympathy [συμπάθειαν], and I am far from thinking you unfair to me. Farewell, best and most upright brother, together with your whole household, whom I greet lovingly in my name and my wife's, and all my colleagues, indeed all of them, good men. Geneva, 28 December 1547.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: Your John Calvin.

units.la: MYCONIVS CALVINO S.
units.tr: Myconius to Calvin, greetings

units.la: VOluit hic commendari per me tibi, vt viro docto & pio. Obtemperaui non inuitus, nonnisi vt te meis salutarem. Fac igitur, si qua poteris illi commodare, commodes propter Dominum, cui mihi videtur se deuouisse. Calamitates huius temporis tatis non potes ignorare: augentur in dies magis ac magis, eoque inquietus ille nequit cessare, donec ambitioni suæ satisfactum sit. Vel periit. Rumor est occupasse in Pedemonte oppidum munitissimum (Binerol vocant) et constat, præmissis piram tormentis, gladibus, puluere bombardico multo, & ipsum eo intedere animum cum suis, quò, vt ferunt, per Lotharingiam & Burgundiam inuadat Regem, & Bernenses propter Sabaudum. Quia vero verisimili vix credi potest (simulat enim ac dissimulat pro occasione omnia) nescio quid credendum vel non credendum. Cæsarianum interim in Sueuia obtinuit Timetur Constantiensibus. Quod ante malum acceptum noluerunt, nunc dicuntur ambire miseri. Nominem habent auxiliantem: & prius neminem habuerunt, & tamen tantam præ se tulerunt constantiam. Potuit ut cum paruo damno, ut porali dico tenere quod nunc non valebunt post cladem & amissionem suburbij, & grauem ignominiam, vt taceam de damno animæ. Non curat quidam ex nostris, quod parietes ardet proximi. Equidem per dies aliquot fui in hac sententia, per istos futurum, vt Cæsar & nos vexaturus est cum nefario suo Interim: & adhuc hæ-o, adeo inuisus est illis Christus Quarta Augu. vestes lineæ & candidæ singulis ministris Angustanis singulæ sunt à nouo Senatu missæ, & simul mandatum vt semper pro sacris concionibus iis vtantur. Ab hoc munere tamen exclusi sunt nō vnti prius. Coacti sunt etiam iurare se nihil contra Cæsaream Maiestatem, & contra Interim dicturos: quod si factum fuerit secus, condigna pœna puniendos esse. Ex quo vides, quænam libertas sit permissa prædicandi Euangelij. Nugæ omnia. Apud Norimbergenses vnus tantùm dicitur esse qui miserit. Is dum ingreditur vel misfat, vel egreditur e templo stipatus est satellitibus, nequis noceat: tanto fortiores illi sunt Augustanis Argentinenses adhuc durant, nescio quàm diu. Ex potentibus multi dicuntur migrare, inter quos & N. esse fert rumor: numeratur enim inter eos, qui fabricarunt Interim. Nescio quid de eis diuinandum: sperant alii qui, nonnulli desperant. Docti dum scribunt, præ se ferunt magnum metum. Mihi videtur Dominum miserturum aliquando suæ Ecclesiæ. Vale fortis in Domino. Basileæ xxviii. Augusti, anno M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: This man wished to be commended to you through me as a learned and godly person. I complied, not unwillingly, and only so that I might greet you through my letter. Please, then, if you can offer him any help, do so for the Lord's sake, to whom he seems to have devoted himself. You cannot be ignorant of the calamities of this time: they grow greater day by day, and that restless man cannot rest until his ambition is satisfied, or he perishes. There is a rumour that he has seized the very strong town in Piedmont (they call it Pinerolo), and it is certain that, after sending ahead cannon, swords and much gunpowder, he himself has set his mind with his men on attacking the king through Lorraine and Burgundy, and the Bernese on account of Savoy. Since what is said is hardly credible (for he pretends and dissembles everything as occasion requires), I do not know what should be believed or disbelieved. Meanwhile the Emperor's Interim has prevailed in Swabia. The people of Constance fear what they refused before the harm was done; now, poor souls, they are said to be seeking it. They have no one to help them, and they never had anyone, yet they showed such constancy. They could have kept with small loss what they will now be unable to keep after the defeat and the loss of their suburb, and a grievous disgrace, not to mention the loss of their souls. Some of our people do not care that the wall of their neighbour is burning. Indeed, for some days I held the view that, through these men, the Emperor will harass us too, with his wicked Interim. Meanwhile they are so hostile to Christ... On 4 August a white linen robe was sent to each of the Augsburg ministers by the new Senate, and they were ordered to wear it always for the sacred sermons. Yet some of them were excluded from this office, not all of them at first. They were also forced to swear that they would say nothing against the Emperor's Majesty or against the Interim, and that if they did otherwise they would be punished with a fitting penalty. From this you can see what freedom is allowed for preaching the Gospel. Trifles, all of it. At Nuremberg, it is said, only one man is preaching; when he goes in or comes out of the church he is surrounded by guards, lest anyone harm him. The Strasbourgers, by contrast, still hold out, though I do not know for how long. Many of the powerful are said to be leaving, among them, rumour has it, N. too, for he is counted among those who drew up the Interim. I do not know what is to be divined from this: some hope, others despair. Learned men, while they write, show great fear. It seems to me that the Lord will one day have mercy on his Church. Farewell, strong in the Lord. Basel, 28 August 1548.

units.la: Of Myconius.
units.tr: Myconius.

units.la: BVCERVS CALVINO.
units.tr: BUCER TO CALVIN.

units.la: S.D. in Domino qui vestras Ecclesias diu seruet, vt vel alicubi vox pura sonet Euangelij. Quàm pauci domus suas non in arenam ædificarint, dies præsens testatur. Deo plus potentiæ perpauci tribuunt, quàm sufficere carnis ratio iudicare potest. Pendemus nos hic adhuc consiliis. Petierant nostri ab Imper. vt vel aliquas nobis Ecclesias relinqueret pro pura religionis ad ministratione: id quod ille pernegauit. Nunc quid facturi sint, nouit Dominus. Nonnisi miraculis seruari poterimus. Tu ora nobiscum. De fatragine nescio quid faciendum tibi statuam. Optatim, & vtile Ecclesiis agnosco, consilia & fraudes aduersarij detegi: tamen hæreo, an Ecclesiæ vtile sit inte irritari singulariter crabrones. Dominus dedit tibi insigne donum illustrandi Euangelium suum, cuius præclarum nobis munus iam iterum exhibuisti commentariis tuis in Epistolas ad Timotheum. Spiritus Domini ipsete regat, & certum reddat de hac re & de omni ministerio tuo. Hic si quid fermenti recipiatur, finem faciet ministerij mei hic Dominus. Tu forsan dabit, vt, quod experij toties, videam vestras Ecclesias. Salueant sancti istic omnes. Plurimum me recreat subsistere adhuc in sua statione Opt Virtum nostrum. Optimè vale cum vxore & domo tua tota. Pridie Calendas Octobr. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: Greetings in the Lord, who keep your Churches for a long time, so that somewhere at least the pure voice of the Gospel may sound. The present day shows how few have not built their houses upon sand. Very few grant God more power than human reason can judge sufficient for the flesh. We here are still hanging in suspense over our plans. Our people had asked the Emperor to leave us at least some Churches for the pure administration of religion; this he flatly refused. What they will now do, the Lord knows. We can be preserved only by miracles. Pray with us. About the fatragine I do not know what I should advise you to do. I recognise that it is useful for the Churches that the plans and frauds of the adversary are brought to light, yet I hesitate whether it is useful to the Church to stir up the hornets, one by one. The Lord has given you the remarkable gift of illuminating his Gospel, and this noble service you have again rendered us in your commentaries on the Epistles to Timothy. May the Spirit of the Lord himself guide you and make you certain in this matter and in all your ministry. If any leaven is admitted here, the Lord will bring my ministry here to an end. Perhaps he will grant that I see your Churches, which I have so often longed for. May all the saints there be greeted. It greatly refreshes me that our excellent Virtum still holds his post. Farewell, very well, with your wife and your whole household. The day before the Kalends of October, 1548.

units.la: Tuus totus Bucerus.
units.tr: Wholly yours, Bucer.

units.la: BVLINGERVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: BULLINGER TO CALVIN, GREETINGS.

units.la: Vas dilecte mi Caluine scriptas in Iulio, in Augusto demum accepi. His serius respondeo: nam nunc negotiis oppressus sum ita tantum non mœrore cotabesco propter interitum Ecclesiarum in Germania superiore. Pridie defecit etiam Constantia, decidit sese Romanorum regi, recepit milites praesidiarios 800. Ciues optimi, inter quos Blaurerus Consul Zuickius, Labhardus, Hutufius & alij insigniores multi relictis aedibus, & immobilibus excesserunt & fugerunt in Durgauiam. D. Ambrosius ante 5. septimanas improbitate ciuium compulsus ad foro rem in Durgauiam conceßit, & ibi hactenus delituit. Sustinet odium indicibile. Iam concessit ad ipsum etiam D. Thomas Cof. & frater, vir incomparabilis. Iam vero malum etiam nobis imminet. Expectamus quid vel hac hyeme, vel in vere hostes veri tatis contra nos tentaturi sint. Dominus adsit nobis & confirmet nos in sua sancta veritate, ne quid nostra professione indignum admittamus. Orate pro nobis. Sunt nostri alacres, intrepidi & constantes adhuc, parati quaeuis subire pericula: sed nisi vigilauerit Deus frustra vigilat qui custodit vrbem. Peccata nostra, sanguis, ingratitudo, auaritia, contentio, inuidia & alia his similia premunt nos omnes qui nomen Christi gerimus: ac meremur vt nos flagello excitet Dominus. Hic tamen clemens est & propitius, si vera fide & sanctis precibus ipsi occurramus. Si placet ei nos ex hoc eripere seculo, innumeris liberarit malis, vita donabit aeterna. Ipsi gloria semper. Ora pro nobis, & saluta fratres omnes. Salutant te D. Bibliander, Caltherus, Pellicanus, Vverdmullerus, denique fratres omnes. Tigurj x v. Octobris. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: My dear Calvin, I received your letter written in July only in August. I answer it late, because I am now so oppressed by business that I am wasting away, almost in grief, on account of the ruin of the Churches in Upper Germany. The day before yesterday Constance also surrendered, submitting itself to the King of the Romans; it received 800 garrison soldiers. The best citizens, among whom were Blaurer the consul, Zwick, Labhard, Hutufius and many other more prominent men, left their houses and property and fled into Thurgau. Master Ambrose, driven out five weeks ago by the wickedness of the citizens, withdrew to Thurgau and has hidden himself there until now. He bears an unspeakable hatred. Now also Master Thomas Kolb and his brother, an incomparable man, have gone to him. But now the evil threatens us too. We wait to see what the enemies of the truth will attempt against us, either this winter or in the spring. May the Lord be with us and confirm us in his holy truth, so that we admit nothing unworthy of our profession. Pray for us. Our people are still eager, fearless and steadfast, ready to undergo any dangers; but unless God keeps watch, he watches in vain who guards the city. Our sins, blood, ingratitude, avarice, strife, envy and other things like these press upon all of us who bear the name of Christ, and we deserve that the Lord should rouse us with the scourge. Yet he is merciful and kind here, if we meet him with true faith and holy prayers. If it pleases him to snatch us from this age, he will free us from countless evils and grant us eternal life. To him be glory forever. Pray for us, and greet all the brothers. Bibliander, Galtherus, Pellicanus, Werdmüller, and finally all the brothers greet you. Zurich, 15 October 1548.

units.la: H. Bullingerus tuus.
units.tr: Yours, H. Bullinger.

units.la: IOANNES CALVINVS PROTECTORI ANGLIAE.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO THE PROTECTOR OF ENGLAND.

units.la: ETsi pro ea prouincia quam nunc sustines, Amplissime Domine, Deus te singulari prudentia, fortitudine & aliis virtutibus quas muneris illius magnitudo postulat, instruxit: quia tamen me agnoscis pro Filij ipsius servo, cui ante omnia te approbare cogitas: sic mihi persuasi benigne a te susceptum iri, ipsius nomine ad te scriberem. Neque enim mihi aliud proposui, quam vt opus coeptum persequendo, magis ac magis ipsius gloriam promoueas, donec ipsius regnum in optatissimum illum statum perduxeris, qui in terris extare quidem potest. Ex ipsa porro lectione percipies quam nihil de meo attulerim, sed ex ipsius Scriptura, quicquid hic habes, in vsum tuum protulerim. Iam si in vnam magnitudinem intuerer, in quam istic euectus es, satis scio quam difficilis ad illam aditus esset tenuitati mea: quod vero no aspernaris illius Magistri doctrinam cui addictus sum, quin potius singularis priuilegij loco ducas te vnum haberi ex ipsius
units.tr: Although God has equipped you, most distinguished Sir, for the province you now hold with singular prudence, courage, and the other virtues that the greatness of that office demands, nevertheless, since you acknowledge me as the servant of his Son, whom you intend above all to please, I was persuaded that you would receive kindly a letter written to you in his name. I have had no other purpose than that, by pursuing the work begun, you may increasingly promote his glory, until you have brought his kingdom to that most desired state which can exist on earth. Moreover, from the reading itself you will perceive how little I have contributed of my own, and how whatever you find here I have drawn from his Scripture for your use. Now, if I looked only at the greatness to which you have been raised there, I know well how difficult the approach to it would be for my humble self. But since you do not spurn the teaching of that Master to whom I am devoted, and regard it rather as a singular privilege that you should be counted among his disciples, I need not make many excuses to you, since I judge you sufficiently well prepared to take up that which will be shown to have come from him.

units.la: Epist.87. Ex Gall. ipsius discipulis,nō est quòd pluribus me apu l te excusem, cùm te satis bene comparatum iudicem ad illud suscipiendum quod ab ipso profectum esse constabit. Est sane de quo gratias agamus Deo & Patri nostro, quòd opera tua vti voluerit ad tantu opus, vt per te imprimis purum & syncerum suum cultum in regno Angliæ restitueret: præstiterit etiam vt salutis doctrina audiretur passim, & fideliter annunciaretur omnibus qui aures arrigere dignarentur: q; etiam tantam fortitudinem & constantiam tibi indiderit, vt cōtra tot insultus & difficultates infracto animo pergeres, ac manu potenti te asseruerit hactenus, vt tua consilia & labores sua benedictione profequutus sit, atque prosperaue-rit. Totidem, inquam, illa sunt piis omnibus argumenta, pro quibus ipsius nomen concelebrent. Sed tamen quia Satan totus in eo est, vt nouas pugnas perpetuò accendat, ipsáque illa res per se omnium difficillima vna est, dare operam nempe vt Dei veritas placidè apud homines obtineat, cùm illi natura mendacio addicti sint: cùm etiam non desint alia quędam quę ipsius cutsum remorentur, ac nominatim q; superstitiones Antichristi tam altas radices egerűt, vt ex animis multorum ægrè reuelli queant: tu v-nus mihi tanto magis visus es ad opus tam arduū sanctis omnino exhortationibus confirmandus, vti ipsa experientia te hoc quoq; comperturum non dubito. Atq; hoc faciet vt apertius hic & liberius me geram: & sane quia meum consilium voto tuo, vt spero, respondebit, sic statuo te etiam exhortationem meā boni consulturum, vt ipsa non omnino necessaria fuerit, cùm zelus & solicitudo quæ me huc impulerűt, tibi nō probari nō possint. Ac tato magis illa quam ipse agnoscis necessitas faciet vt acceptius etiam hoc apud te meum studium reddatur. Quare à te peto, Amplissime Domine, vt me hic patienter audias in iis de quibus te admonere paucis instituí: ac vicissim spero, vbi illa attenderis, ipsa tibi solatium allatura, quò animosius deinde opus illud sanctum persequaris, ad quod Domino placuit te huc vsq; ministro vti. Equidem non dubito quin turbę illę ingentes quę ab aliquo tempore acciderunt, tibi valde molestæ & acerbę fuerint: præser-tim cùm inde plerique offendiculum captaret, quos ex parte mu-tatio in religionis causa concitabat. Fieri, inquam, non potest, quin te illa cernentem varij motus exceperint, siue ad animū & sensum tuum ipse tum illa referres, siue ad strepitus improborū, siue ad proborū consternatione teipsum cōuerteres. Et me enim rumor ille tam longe diffusum ita vehementer constrictum tenuit, donec accepi affulgere cœpisse auxilium à Domino. Sed quando vel ignis ille nondum plane consopitus est, vel non ita difficile sit à Satana rursus excitari, propone tibi ante oculos me morabile illud piissimi Regis Ezechię exéplū, quod à Scriptura tā
units.tr: Epist. 87. Ex Gall. There is indeed cause for us to give thanks to God our Father that he has been pleased to use your labours for so great a work, so that through you above all he might restore his pure and sincere worship in the kingdom of England. He has also granted that the message of salvation should be heard everywhere and faithfully proclaimed to all who deign to prick up their ears. He has also given you such courage and steadfastness that you have pressed on with an unbroken spirit against so many assaults and difficulties, and he has so far upheld you with his mighty hand that he has blessed and prospered your counsels and labours. These, I say, are all arguments for all the godly to celebrate his name. But since Satan is wholly intent on constantly stirring up new battles, and since that very task is in itself the most difficult of all, namely to see to it that God's truth prevails peacefully among men, who are by nature given to falsehood; and since there are not lacking other obstacles that delay its course, and in particular the superstitions of Antichrist have struck such deep roots that they can scarcely be torn from the minds of many, you alone seemed to me all the more to need to be strengthened by wholesome exhortations for so arduous a task, as I do not doubt that your own experience will also show you. And this will make me speak here more openly and freely. Indeed, since I hope my counsel will answer to your wish, I am confident that you will also take my exhortation in good part, so that it may not seem wholly necessary, since the zeal and concern that have moved me to write cannot fail to be pleasing to you. And the more the necessity that you yourself acknowledge, the more acceptable this my zeal will be to you. Therefore I ask of you, most distinguished Sir, that you patiently hear me here on those matters about which I have resolved to admonish you briefly. In return, I hope that, once you have considered them, they will bring you comfort, so that you may pursue more eagerly that holy work for which the Lord has been pleased to use you as his minister here so far. Indeed I do not doubt that the great disturbances which have arisen for some time past have been very troubling and bitter to you, especially since many have taken offence at them, and some have been stirred up by the change in religion. It cannot be, I say, that as you witnessed these things various emotions did not seize you, whether you turned them over in your own mind and feeling, or whether you were unsettled by the clamour of the wicked or the dismay of the good. For that rumour, spread so far and wide, held me in such great distress until I heard that help had begun to shine forth from the Lord. But since that fire has not yet been wholly quenched, or since it may not be very difficult to be rekindled by Satan, set before your eyes the memorable example of that most pious king Hezekiah, which Scripture hands down to us so clearly.

units.la: 2. Chron. 32. diserte traditum habemus: qui cum sublatis exludça superstitio-nibus putum Dei cultum ex ipsius lege constituillet, tanta subi-to belli mole exceptus est, vt pro homine perdito & deplorato habendus passim iudicari posset. Sic enim Scriptura apposite ista simul conuertit, quod cum totus ille in eo esset, vt verum Dei cultum suo loco reponeret, rem illi in speciem quàm infoelicis-simè successisse. Plane enim cum ira se cordate in Dei regno erigendo gessisset, regnum quoque ipsius cum summa tranquilli-tate coniunctum iri sperari poterat. Hinc igitur exemplum sibi statuant pij omnes Principes ac prouinciarum Rectores, quo se animosius gerant, tum ad ableganda omnia idola tum ad ve-rum Dei honorem, vti eo tendentur legitime procurandum, fi-dem ipsorum nempe per varias tentationes consimili examini subiiciendam esse. Sic permittit Dominus, sic vult denique, vt & suorum constantiam patefaciat, & illos comparatos reddat, vt oculos supra mundum attollere discant. Interea vero Satan sese immiscet, vt cum veram doctrinam aperte euertere non valet, obliquis artibus ac veluti per cuniculos idem moliri non desi-nat. Atque huc fact illa Iacobi admonitio, vt ad Iobi tolerantiā attenti, in illius etiam exitum intueamur. Perinde enim restan-dem illi piissimo Regi cessit, cui Dominus ita adfuit in summis ipsius angustiis, vt tandem victoriam insignem inde retulerit. Quare cum neque manus ipsius abbreuiata sit, neque porrò mi-nus illi sit nunc cordi, quàm superioribus seculis veritatis ipsius assertio, non est quod de illius ope desperes quicunque te fluctus excipiant. Maximam hominum partem Euangelio resistere, & omnes conatus eo conferre ne illud emergat: adeo mirum vi-deri non debet. Ea siquidem est perpetua mundi ingratitudo, vt Deo vocanti tergum obuertat & aduersus illum calcitret, vbi iu-gum suum illi imponere cogitat. Cumque natura homines ad-dicti sint hypocrisi, ferre non possunt, vt ad lumen verbi Dei adducantur, quod eorum foeditatem & probrum reuelet: aut vt ex superstitionum suarum latebris extrahantur, sub quarū vm-bra somnum suum dormiunt. Quare nouum non est vbi ab illa parte contradicitur, cum de redigendis ad Dei cultum & obe-dientiam hominibus agitur. Hoc tamen facere nō debet, vt ne-gligentes aut timidi hic deprehendamur. Tandem enim vbi tu-multuati fuerint fatis, ac suum furorem desfumauerint, momé-to confundi & cum suo tumore cocidere necesse est. Sane quod ad Deum attinet, omnes illi hominum fremitus & bullae ipsi tā-tum ludus erunt, vt est in 2.1 sal. adeoque quasi conniuentibus oculis ad illorum aestusipse conticescet, quasi res ea ad illum nō pertineret. Atqui tandem ipsius potentia comprimetur. Nos ve-rò eadem illa armati inuicto praesidio sustinebimur, quicquid
units.tr: 2 Chron. 32. When he had removed the high places and superstitions and had established the pure worship of God according to his law, he was met with such a sudden storm of war that he could be judged everywhere a lost and desperate man. For Scripture sets these things side by side in a striking way: while he was wholly intent on restoring the true worship of God to its place, things turned out for him, in appearance, most unhappily. For indeed, since he had acted zealously in setting up God's kingdom, it could be hoped that his own kingdom would also be joined with the greatest tranquillity. Let therefore all the godly princes and rulers of provinces take this example for themselves, so that they may act more boldly both in abolishing all idols and in procuring, as is lawfully directed, the true honour of God; namely, that their faith must be subjected to a similar testing through various temptations. Thus the Lord permits it, thus in the end he wills it, both to reveal the steadfastness of his own and to prepare them so that they learn to lift their eyes above the world. Meanwhile, however, Satan mixes himself in, and when he cannot openly overthrow the true doctrine, he does not cease to attempt the same by oblique arts, as it were by burrowing underground. To this point also applies that admonition of James, that, attending to the patience of Job, we should look also to the outcome of his story. For that most pious king, too, came to a resistance that ended well, since the Lord stood by him in his greatest distress, so that at last he brought back a notable victory. Therefore, since neither his hand is shortened nor is his concern for the defence of his truth now any less than in earlier ages, there is no reason for anyone who is struck by such waves to despair of his help. That the greater part of mankind resists the Gospel, and makes every effort to prevent its emergence, ought not to seem strange. For such is the perpetual ingratitude of the world that it turns its back on God when he calls, and kicks against him when he intends to place his yoke upon them. And since men are by nature given to hypocrisy, they cannot bear to be brought to the light of God's Word, which would expose their foulness and shame, nor to be drawn out of the hiding-places of their superstitions, under whose shadow they sleep their sleep. Therefore it is nothing new that, wherever people oppose the task of bringing men back to the worship and obedience of God, opposition comes from that quarter. Yet we must not allow ourselves to be found negligent or timid here. For when the tumult has at last risen high enough and they have vented their fury, they must necessarily be confounded in due time and fall away together with their swelling. Indeed, as regards God, all those roarings and bubbles of men will be mere sport to him, as it is said in Psal. 2; and so, as if with eyes half closed, he will fall silent at their surge, as though the matter did not concern him. Yet at last his power will be brought to bear. But we, armed with that same unconquerable protection, shall be sustained, whatever Satan may devise against us; and at last we shall actually perceive that the Gospel, as a messenger of peace, brings reconciliation with God and also serves to establish peace among men, as the Lord bears witness through Isaiah: when the kingdom of Christ has been set up through his teaching, swords will be beaten into ploughshares and spears into pruning hooks.

units.la: Iac. 5. aduersum nos moliatur Satan, tandemque reipfa percipiemus, Euangelium vt nuntium pacis afferet & reconciliationem cum Deo, ita etiam ad pacem inter homines constituendam pertinere, vbi apud Ifaiam testatur Dominus: Vbi regnum Christi per ipsius doctrinam erectum fuerit, futurum vt & gladij in vomeres & lanceę in falces transformentur. Interea vero quanuis ex hominum improbitate & peruicacia prodeant, quæ aduersus Euangelium insurgunt seditiones & turbæ, in nofipfos tamen descendere oportet, ac statuere, Dominum ita nos pleƈtere propter nostra ipsorum peccata, etsi vtatur illis instrumentis quæ verè Satanæ mancipia esse constet. Vetus est illa querimonia, qua in Euangelium deriuata est omnium malorum causa, quæ humano generi pridem incumbùt. Constat siquidem ex historia, iam ab ipso initio quo Ghriftianifmus per orbem spargi cœperat, vix vllum fuisse angulum qui non extremis malis premeretur. Bellorum motus extabant continui cuiufdam incendij instar, quo vniuersa cõflagrarent. Diluuies hinc, illinc pestes & fames: Extrema & rerum omnium & ordinum inuerfio, quasi orbis ter ræ in seipsum commissus plane dissiliret & confringeretur. Idé prorsus accidit hoc seculo, ex quo Euangelium cœpit emergere: miserabilis quædam exitit rerum omnium facies, vt passim volitet illa querimonia, nos scilicet infœliciffimo seculo natos esse, ac perpauci non sub tanta mole fatiscant. Atqui dum vulnera illa perfentimus, & ad manum ferientis attendere oportuit & ad causam: quænam illa porrò fit neque adeò obscurum est, neque perceptu difficile. Constat verbum Dei per quod ad viam salutis perducimur incomparabilem thesaurum esse: Excutiamus vero nos ipsos, quàm reuerenter nempe vti ab ipsius auƈto re oblatum nobis est, ita etiam à nobis admissum fit. Quando igitur ita vilescit apud nos quod est apud illum tanti momenti, quis nõ iustissimum agnoscat, qui nostram ingratitudinem ita vicissim vlciscatur? Audimus & illud Christi apud Lucam: ferue qui teneat voluntatem Domini, neque illam opere præstat, duplo grauiorem pœnam commereri. Cùm igitur tam negligentes fimus ad obediendum voluntati Dei, cuius centuplo vberior extat notitia inter nos, quàm superioribus seculis, alienum videri non debet, fi vehemetius in nos excandescat, qui omnium hominum minime excusabiles fumus. Cumq; operam non damus vt bonum femen promoueatur & incrementum capiat, merito inter nos spinæ & fentes artificio Satanæ fubcrefcunt, quarum deinde punƈtionibus infestemur. Cùm denique Creatori ipsi ius illud suum non exhibeamus in nobis ipsis, non minus æquum est hominum contumaciam aduersum nos ipsos experiri. Vt ad te vero me propius conferam, Amplissime Domine, audio esse
units.tr: Iac. 5. Meanwhile, although the seditions and tumults that rise up against the Gospel arise from the wickedness and obstinacy of men, we must nevertheless look to ourselves and conclude that the Lord strikes us because of our own sins, even though he uses those instruments which are clearly the servants of Satan. That ancient complaint is old, by which the cause of all the evils that have long weighed upon the human race is laid at the door of the Gospel. For it is established from history that from the very beginning, when Christianity began to spread through the world, there was scarcely any corner that was not oppressed by the greatest evils. Movements of war were continuous, like a kind of fire by which everything was set ablaze; floods on one side, plagues and famines on the other; the utter overturning of all things and of all orders, as if the orb of the earth, turned against itself, were bursting apart and breaking to pieces. Exactly the same has happened in this age, since the Gospel began to emerge: a miserable aspect of all things has appeared, so that everywhere that complaint flies about, that we were born in the most unhappy age, and few do not sink under so great a burden. But while we feel these wounds, we ought to look to the hand that strikes, and to its cause. What that cause is, is neither so obscure nor hard to perceive. It is agreed that the Word of God, through which we are led into the way of salvation, is an incomparable treasure. Let us, however, examine ourselves: how reverently we have received it from its Author, and how we have accepted it in turn. When, therefore, that which is of such great importance to him is so cheapened among us, who would not acknowledge that he most justly takes vengeance in turn on our ingratitude? We also hear that saying of Christ in Luke: the servant who knows the will of the Lord and does not carry it out deserves a double punishment. Since, therefore, we are so negligent in obeying the will of God, of which we now have a hundredfold richer knowledge than in earlier ages, it ought not to seem strange if he burns more fiercely against us, who are the least excusable of all men. And since we do not take pains that the good seed be advanced and grow, it is deservedly by Satan's craft that thorns and briars spring up among us, and by their pricks we are then troubled. Finally, since we do not render to the Creator himself that right which is his in ourselves, it is no less fair that we should experience the obstinacy of men against us. But to come closer to you, most distinguished Sir, I hear that

units.la: duo fcditioforum genera, quæ aduersus Regem ac regni sarum caput extulerunt. Alij enim, cereb osi quidam vid licet, iub Euangelij nomine ἀταξίαν passim inuectam vellent. Hij vero in superstitionibus Antichristi ita obdurauerunt vt earum reuulsionem ferre non possint. Ac merentur quidem, tum hi tum illi gladio vltore coerceri, quem tibi tradidit Dominus : cum non in Regem tantum insurgant, sed in Deum ipsum qui & Regem in Regia sede constituit, & te protectorem instituit, tum personæ tum ipsius etiam Regiæ Maiestatis. Illud vero hic ante omnia procurandum est, vt quantum fieri poterit illi qui eo Euangelij gustu præditi sunt vt illi iam addictose sse constet, ipsum porro ea animi deiectione reuerentia admittant, vt & sibi ipsis plane abrenuntient, & sese Deo in solidum vt par est, addicant. Sic enim illos cogitare oportet Dominum nempe istiusmodi occasionibus ipsos expergefacere, vt magis serio in ipsius verbo proficiant, quàm hactenus præstiterint. Frenetici quidem illi qui mundum in supinam quandam licentiam transuersum cuperent, excitantur à Satana nominatim, vt per illos Euangelium male audiat: quasi Euangelium causam præberet rebellioni aduersus prin cipatus, atque meram in mundum dissipationem inueheret. Pio rum est vero, ad tam infaustos conatus perditorum hominum ingemiscere, dum lucem à Domino qui illas tenebras serius o cius certissime discussura sit, sustinendo implorant. Papistæ vero dum idoli sui Romani fœditates & abominationes tueri student, apertum odium & beneficij Christi & omnium ipsius mandatorum magis ac magis produnt: quod tamen non potest non extremum mœrore illis afferre, apud quos vel gutta fynceri zeli superest. Quare sibi & ilta à Domino destinari pij agnoscat, quæ totidem sint ad ipsos castigandos flagella, quia nempe legitimos Euangelij fructus non ferant. Summa ratio igitur atque vnicè apposita esto ad istiusmodi motus semel consopiendos, vt qui Euangelio nomen dederunt, verè ad Dei imaginem reformati deprehendantur: atque ita testentur Christiani simum legitimum ab omni ἀταξία omnimodo abhorrere : æquabili modestia & temperantia approbent se Dei verbo regi, nedum vt exleges & effrænes habeantur: recta deniq; & sanĉta vita os impiorum obturent. Sic placatus Dominus ferulas demum subducet, atq; pro vindicta quam in verbi contemptores exerit illam suorum m refipiscentiam certissima benesictione prosequetur. Nominatim vero Nobilitas ipsa ac Magistratus hic exemplo præeant oportet, vt primi omnium colla submittant cum summo timore ac reuerentia, supremo illi omnium Regi Christo Dei Filio: ipsi inquam fidem & obsequium animæ & corporis syncere præstent, vt & ipse vicissim eorum tumorem & fastum comprimat, qui aduersus ipsos iniuste cristas tollunt Hoc est nimirum summum princ̃pum huius seculi munus, vt ita subditos suos regant, vt primi omnium Christo subesse gestiant, dentque omnem operam, vt illius vnius auctoritas supra omnes & summos & infimos emineat. Quare a te peto, Amplissime Domine, per Dominum ipsum & illam qua regnum Nepotis tui complecteris singulare charitatem, vt luculenter passim restaris, vt eo vnice omnem conatum ac vigilatiam adhibeas, vt & Dei veritas praedicetur cum plenissima auctoritate & efficacia, & vt fructus quoq; extent qui coelesti illi sementi respondeant: atque vt illud assequaris, nunquam manum remittas ab incepta plena & integra Ecclesiae reformatione prosequenda. Hic vero vt meam mentem facilius percipias, totum istud in tria capita coferam: quorum vnum sit, De vera ratione populi recte docendi. Alterum de extirpandis abusibus qui hactenus obtinuerunt. Tertium ac postremum, de vitiis exacte corrigendis, & adhibenda opera, ne scandala & luxus passim vigeant, vt inde nomen Domini blasphemetur. Ac quod ad primum illud attinet, non est q; in tradenda doctrinae substantia immorer. Est magis de quo Domino gratias agam, a quo ita illuminatus es purae doctrinae cognitione, vt eandem etiam publice doceri cures. Non es, inquam, mihi docendus quae sit Christianorum fides, & quae illis doctrina tenenda sit, cũ per te adeo veritas fidei in Ecclesiae coetu restituta personet. Quod si quis obiter coprehesum habere velit, quae sit Dei cultus summa, res nepe eo redit. Vt vnum Deum habeamus rectorem nostrarum conscientiarum, ad ipsarum regimen quod spirituale est, legis ipsius vnica adhibeamus pro singulari pietatis regula: ne quid ad ipsius cultum ex hominum traditionibus quae vanae sunt coferamus, ipsum porro pro sua natura, spiritus & cordis integritate ab omnibus colendum esse.
