Cum vero in omnibus nobis nihil extet praeter miserabile corruptionem, quae tum sensus omnes tum affectus nostros occupet, nostrum esse meram illa iniquitatum abyssum in nobis agnoscere, & agnitam exhorrescere: eo modo nobis probe cognitis, atq; in nobis penitus fractis, cotufis, perditis, exutis omni dignitatis sapientiae facultatis deniq; vllius ad bonum praesumptione, tum demum accurrere oportere ad vnicum fontem bonorum omnium Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, ab illo quicquid offert percipere, ac imprimis incoparabile illum mortis ac passionis ipsius thesaurum, vt ea vna ratione Deo Patri in solidum reconciliemur: purgatiq; a sperfione sanguinis ipsius certo persuasi simus nullas in nobis extaturas maculas, quae apud ipsius coelestem solium pudore nos suffundant: sic nobis certo constabit vis illa sacrificij perpetui, qua peccatorum gratuita remissio nobis ita obsignata est, vt illic praesidiu& anchora salutis constanter de figamus. Sic ipsius Spiritu sanctificati, in obedientiam iustitiæ Dei consecrabimur: ipsius gratia confirmati, victoriam de Satana, mundo, carne reportabimus. Postremo cum membra corporis ipsius simus, non dubitabimus quin Deus in filiorum suorum albo nos recefeat, vt vera fiducia ipsum illo Patris amantissimo nomine legitimè compellemus. Hic est nempe scopus veræ doctrinæ quæ & in Ecclesia Dei habenda est semper & ab omnibus audienda vt in eum scopum omnes syncerè collimet, dum sese à mundo sensim subducendo, ad caput illud suū quod est in cœlis intento affectu & apertis votis, moribus, institutis sin guli sese attollant. Qua te verè pretiosissima sua luce quæ tādiu sub Antichristi sepulta latuerat, cùm nunc ita vberrimè perfuderit Dominus, pluribus ista apud te non exequar. Tātum quod attigi de docendi forma eò pertinet, vt quæ sit idonea ratio sequenda in populo instituendo teneatur. Pungendi sunt nempe ad viuum, vt sentiatur in singulis illud Apostoli verbum Domini nempe gladium ancipitem esse, qui intima vsque cogitationum & affectuum configat, & ad ipsam vsque ossium & medullarum compaginem peruadat. Hoc inquam inculco nominatim, quoniam vereor ne paucæ extent in Regno viuæ concionis, maior pars autem in recitationis modum decurrat. Ac vi-deo quidem aliquam istius necessitatis occasionem inter vos: quia nempe, vobis nō sunt ad manum probi & idonei pastores, defectu ille suo quodam modo explendus est. Deinde cauendū est ab erraticis hominibus & temerariis, qui vt in rebus nouis accidit, plurimum extra metas abripe rentur, vt somnia sua pro Dei verbo effutiret: sed nulla eiusmodi ratio obstare debet, quin ipsa Christi institutio obtineat, quod ad Euangelij prædicationem. Porrò legitima prædicatio mortua esse non potest, sed viua & efficax ad docendum, exhortandum, arguendum, vti ad Timoth. testatur Apostolus: Adeò vt infideli ingrediente in cœtum fidelium, affici illum oporteat & quasi transfodi ipsa verbi auditione vt det gloriam Deo, vt alibi idem Apostolus ostendit. Neque etiam te latere potest, quod idem Apostolus tradit de vi & energia quæ in illis extare debet, qui se probos & legitimos verbi ministros approbare studeunt: vt abesse ab istiusmodi quidem velit omnem ornatum & fucum eloquentiæ, quo se homines theatro venditant: ita tamen vt tanto luculentius in eorum sermone sese prodat vis illa Spiritus, quæ potentissimè agat in animis auditorum. Nulla igitur præcautio facere debet, quomi-nus Spiritus ille Dei suam libertatem ac perpetuum vigorem retineat in illorum ministerio in quos sua dona contulit Domi-nus ad Ecclesiæ ædificationem. Expedit quidem prospicere desultoriis ingeniis quæ sibi nimium licere volunt: claudenda est etiam
units.tr: There are two kinds of sedition that have risen up against the King and the chief men of the kingdom. Some, certain frenzied people I suppose, want disorder [ἀταξίαν] introduced everywhere in the name of the Gospel. Others have hardened themselves in the superstitions of Antichrist so obstinately that they cannot bear to have them torn up. Both sorts deserve to be restrained by the avenging sword which the Lord has put into your hands, since they rise up not only against the King but against God himself, who set the King on his royal throne and appointed you protector, and against the person and the majesty of the King alike. Here, above all, care must be taken that, as far as possible, those who have tasted the Gospel, and whose attachment to it is plain, should with humble minds lay aside all self-reliance and devote themselves wholly to God, as they ought. For they must think that the Lord has stirred them up by such occasions so that they may make more serious progress in his Word than they have hitherto made. The frenzied men who would turn the world upside down into a sort of wild licence are roused by Satan himself, so that the Gospel may be ill spoken of through them, as if the Gospel gave cause for rebellion against the authorities and brought about the utter overthrow of the world. It is the part of the godly, however, to groan over these unhappy attempts of wicked men, while they beg the Lord to bring the light which will surely and speedily dispel those darknesses. The Papists, meanwhile, while they strive to defend the filth and abominations of their Roman idol, betray more and more their open hatred of the benefit of Christ and of all his commandments. Yet this cannot fail to cause the utmost grief to those in whom even a drop of genuine zeal remains. Therefore let the godly recognise that these troubles are sent by the Lord to them as so many scourges to chastise them, because they do not bear the true fruits of the Gospel. The surest course, then, and the only fitting one, for quieting such movements once and for all is that those who have professed the Gospel should be found truly reformed to the image of God. Thus let them bear witness that a Christian and lawful people abhors all disorder in every form. Let them show by an even modesty and self-control that they are ruled by the Word of God, not that they are regarded as lawless and unbridled. Finally, let a upright and holy life stop the mouths of the impious. So the Lord, being appeased, will at last withdraw the rods, and for the punishment he inflicts on the despisers of his Word he will bless his people with the most certain blessing of repentance. Above all, the nobility and the magistrates themselves must lead the way by example, so that they will be the first of all to bow their necks with the greatest fear and reverence before Christ, the supreme King of all, the Son of God. I say they must sincerely give him faith and obedience of soul and body, so that in turn he may humble the pride and arrogance of those who unjustly raise their crests against them. This is indeed the chief duty of the princes of this age: to rule their subjects so that they themselves eagerly submit to Christ before all others, and take every care that his authority alone stands out above all the greatest and the least. Therefore I ask you, most distinguished Lord, through the Lord himself and through that singular love which you embrace for the kingdom of your nephew, that you show clearly everywhere that you devote all your effort and vigilance to this one end: that the truth of God may be preached with the fullest authority and effectiveness, that fruits may also appear which correspond to that heavenly seed, and that you may achieve this by never relaxing your hand from carrying forward the reformation of the Church, begun, full and complete. Here, so that you may grasp my mind more easily, I will arrange the whole matter under three heads. The first will be on the true method of teaching the people rightly. The second on rooting out the abuses that have prevailed until now. The third and last on carefully correcting faults, and on taking pains that scandals and luxury do not flourish everywhere, so that the name of the Lord is blasphemed on their account. As for the first head, I need not linger on the substance of doctrine. Rather I have cause to thank the Lord, by whom you have been so enlightened in the knowledge of pure doctrine that you take care it be taught publicly as well. You do not need, I say, to be taught by me what the faith of Christians is and what doctrine they must hold, since through you the truth of the faith is so clearly restored in the assembly of the Church. But if anyone wishes to grasp briefly what the sum of the worship of God is, the matter comes to this: that we have one God as ruler of our consciences; that for the governing of those consciences, which is spiritual, we use his law alone as the sole rule of godliness; that we add nothing to his worship from the traditions of men, which are vain; and that he, according to his nature, is to be worshipped by all in spirit and in integrity of heart. But since in all of us there is nothing except a miserable corruption, which occupies both all our senses and all our affections, it is for us to acknowledge in ourselves that pit of iniquities, and, having acknowledged it, to shudder at it. When we have been thoroughly known to ourselves, and thoroughly broken, crushed, ruined and stripped of all presumption of dignity, wisdom or ability for any good, then at last we must run to the single fountain of all good things, our Lord Jesus Christ, and receive from him whatever he offers, above all the incomparable treasure of his death and passion, so that by this one means we may be wholly reconciled to God the Father. Cleansed by the sprinkling of his blood, and firmly persuaded that no stains will remain in us to shame us before his heavenly throne, we shall then be assured of the power of that perpetual sacrifice by which the free forgiveness of sins is so sealed to us that we may fix there, constantly, the defence and anchor of our salvation. Thus sanctified by his Spirit, we shall be consecrated to the obedience of God's righteousness; strengthened by his grace, we shall win the victory over Satan, the world and the flesh. Finally, since we are his members, we shall not doubt that God will number us in the register of his sons, so that in true confidence we may address him by that most loving name of Father. This is indeed the aim of true doctrine, which must always be held in the Church of God and always heard by all, so that all may aim at that end sincerely, while they gradually withdraw themselves from the world and, with an intent affection and open prayers, in their conduct and their institutions, raise themselves each to that Head of theirs who is in heaven. Since the Lord has now poured so richly over you that true and most precious light which had lain buried for so long under Antichrist, I will not pursue these matters further with you. I have only touched on the form of teaching so far as to show what suitable method must be kept in instructing the people. They must be pierced to the quick, so that each one feels that saying of the Apostle, that the Word of the Lord is a two-edged sword, which penetrates even to the thoughts and affections within and reaches to the very joints and marrow of the bones. I insist on this particularly, because I fear that few sermons in the kingdom are living, and that most run on in the manner of mere recitation. I see indeed some occasion for this necessity among you, because you have no upright and fit ministers at hand; this lack must somehow be supplied. Next, one must beware of wandering and rash men who, as happens with new things, are carried far beyond the bounds and utter their dreams in place of the Word of God. But no such consideration ought to stand in the way of Christ's own institution taking effect in the preaching of the Gospel. Moreover, lawful preaching cannot be dead, but is living and effective for teaching, exhorting and convicting, as the Apostle testifies to Timothy. So much so that when an unbeliever enters the assembly of the faithful, he must be affected and as it were pierced through by the very hearing of the Word, so that he gives glory to God, as the same Apostle shows elsewhere. Nor can it escape you what the same Apostle teaches about the power and energy which ought to be present in those who strive to approve themselves as upright and lawful ministers of the Word: that all ornament and show of eloquence, by which men peddle themselves on the stage, should indeed be far from such men; yet so that the power of the Spirit, which works most effectively in the minds of the hearers, shows itself all the more brightly in their speech. No precaution, therefore, should hinder that Spirit of God from keeping his freedom and perpetual vigour in the ministry of those on whom the Lord has bestowed his gifts for the building up of the Church. It is indeed fitting to look out for flighty wits who want to take too much liberty; and the ... [claudenda est etiam]

units.la: Heb. 4. etiam ianua curi< fis doctrinis. Ratio autem expedita ad eam rem vna est,fi extet nempe summa quædam doctrinæ ab omnibus recepta,quam inter prædicandum sequantur omnes:ad quâ etiam obseruandam omnes episcopi & parochi iureiurâdo adstringantur, vt nemo ad munus Ecclesiasticum admittatur,nisi spondeat sibi illum doctrinæ consensum inuiolatum futurum. Extet præterea communis formula catechismi in vsum puerorum,& siqui erunt rudiores in populo:sic ipsa veritas illis familiaris reddetur,ac simul eam ipsam discent ab impostumême & cor ruptelis discernere, quæ sensim apud cessantes irrepere solent. Plane enim tibi persuasum esse oportet, Ecclesiam Dei catechesi carere non posse: illic enim verum semen doctrinæ contineri, ex quo demum messis pura ac proba constatura, ac deinceps multiplicanda sit, magis ac magis. Quare si ædificium eiusmodi instituere cogitas,quod & diu stare possit,& à ruina tutum manet,da operam, vt pueri nominatim introducantur ad fidem catechismo ad eam rem edito, vnde discant breuiter& pro suo captu, in quo situs sit verus Christianismus. Neque vero in puerorum institutione stabit tantum catechismi vtilitas. Accedet enim & illa altera, vt tum populus per eum edoctus, melius ad proficiendum in ordinaria verbi auditione comparatus sit,tum vero vt si quis inflatus nouum aliquod dogma inuehere,ad catechismi examen reuocatus statim deprehendatur. Quod ad formulam precum & rituum Ecclesiasticorum,valde probo,vt cer ta illa extet, à qua pastoribus discedere in functione sua non liceat, tam vt consulatur quorundam simplicitati & imperitiæ, quàm vt certius ita constet omnium inter se Ecclesiarum consensus. Postremò etiam vt obuiam eatur desultorię quorundam leuitari qui nouationes quasdam affectant, vti eò pertinere catechismum ipsum ante ostendi. Sic igitur statum esse catechismum oportet, statam sacramentorum administrationem, publicam item precum formulâ. Sed non hoc eò pertinet vt istius politici ordinis in Ecclesia occasione, vigor ille natiuus prædicationis Euangelij vllo modo confenelcat. In illud potius incumbendum est tibi, vt idonei & sonori buccinatores conquirantur, qui ad intima vsque cordium vocis Euangelij clangorę peruadant. Periculum est enim ne mul ò tenuior fructus extet institutæ reformationis, nisi cum illa sese etiam exerat prædicationis verbi potentia quàm efficacissima. Non frustra de Christo scriptum est, Percussurum illum terram sceptro oris sui, ac percussurum impium Spiritu labiorum suorum. Hæc est nimirum vera ratio,qua nos sibi perdomitos sistit,dum verbi sui virtute euertit ac deiicit quicquid ipsius gloriæ obstat in nobisipsis. Atque inde etiam cōstat Euangelio nomen illud quod regnum
units.tr: Heb. 4. the door to curious doctrines. There is one ready means to this end: if there is some summary of doctrine received by all, which everyone follows in preaching, and to which all bishops and parish priests are bound by oath, so that no one is admitted to ecclesiastical office unless he promises that he will keep that agreement of doctrine inviolate. Let there also be a common catechism for the instruction of children and of any who are more ignorant among the people. In this way the truth itself will become familiar to them, and at the same time they will learn to distinguish it from the poisons and corruptions that tend to creep in gradually among the careless. For you must be persuaded that the Church of God cannot do without catechesis, since in it is contained the true seed of doctrine, from which at last a pure and sound harvest will spring up, to be multiplied more and more. So if you intend to establish a building of this kind that can stand for a long time and remain safe from ruin, take care that children are introduced by name to the faith through a catechism published for that purpose, from which they may learn briefly, and according to their capacity, in what true Christianity consists. Nor will the usefulness of the catechism stop with the instruction of children. There is also the further benefit that the people, taught by it, are better prepared to make progress in the ordinary hearing of the Word, and that if anyone puffed up with pride tries to introduce some new dogma, he will be immediately detected when he is called to the test of the catechism. As for a form of prayers and of ecclesiastical rites, I strongly approve of there being a fixed one, from which ministers may not depart in their office, both to provide for the simplicity and inexperience of some, and so that the agreement of all the Churches with one another may be more certainly established. Lastly, it also serves to check the fickleness of certain flighty men who aspire to novelties, as I showed earlier with regard to the catechism itself. So the catechism ought to be fixed, the administration of the sacraments fixed, and likewise a public form of prayer. But this does not mean that the living vigour of the preaching of the Gospel should in any way be weakened by the occasion of this political order in the Church. Rather you must give your attention to this: that suitable and sonorous trumpeters be sought out, who may penetrate to the innermost hearts with the clamour of the voice of the Gospel. For there is danger that the fruit of the reformation you institute will be far meagre unless the power of preaching the Word also shows itself, as effective as possible. Not without reason it is written of Christ that he will strike the earth with the sceptre of his mouth, and strike the wicked with the Spirit of his lips. This is indeed the true means by which he subdues us to himself, while by the power of his word he overturns and casts down whatever stands in the way of his glory within ourselves. And from this it is also clear that the Gospel bears that name which

units.la: Isa.11.14 Dei appellatur. Quare cum edicta & constitutiones Principum Christianorum magnum pondus habeant ad promouendum & asserendum Christianismi statum, Deus tamen singulari modo praecipuam illam vim suam exerere vult in gladio spirituali vel bi fui, quem pastoribus exercendum mandat in Ecclesia. Venio ad caput alterum de abolendis & euellendis radicitus a bufibus & corruptelis, quas inuexit Satan superioribus seculis in Dei ordinationem. Conflat Christianismum Papatus plane esse nohu & adulterinum, & qui Dei iudicio vltimo illo die damnandus sit cum iam ipsius verbo tam aperte repugnet. Quare si ab illa voragine plebem educere est animus, exemplo Apostoli vtendum est. Vbi enim agit de restituendo vero vsu cœnę Domini apud Corinthios, vt quae obrepserant additamenta valere iubeat semel, quod, inquit, accepi a Domino, hoc & tradidi vobis. Inde colligenda generalis doctrina, cum de legitima reformatione & quę Deo accepta sit agitur, ad ipsum purum Dei verbum redeundum nobis esse. Quot enim fuperierunt mixturę ex hominum ingenio prolatę, totidem extabunt pollutiones, quę homines distrahant a recto eorum vsu, quę Dominus in ipsorum salutem instituerat. Proinde dum istiusmodi sententia ex parte tantum exhauritur, res suo loco vere restituta dici non potest, vbi Christianismus laruatus pro syncero & natiuo deprehenditur. Atq; illud a me ideo dicitur, multos longe aliter iudicare intelligam: to lerandos esse nempe abusus neq; attingendos, dummodo crassissimę corruptelę sublatę dici possint. Atqui ex opposito ipsa experientia edocuit, quā fertilis sit mendaciorum seges humanum ingenium: vt vel minutulis granis cofperfum, in altissimum culmulu aflurgat, vti totum natura eo ferri cogitat. Longe alia vero est ratio, quā tradit Scriptura. Dauid enim de idolis agens, ne ipsorum quidem nominis se recordaturum testatur, vt ostendat quā illa sibi omnibus modis detestanda iudicet. Prefertim vbi attendimus quā grauiter eo nomine peccauerimus in Deum, cum in ignorantia versaremur, illud nos tanto magis ferio afficiat oportet, vt ab omni Satanę fermento quā longissime pede referamus.
units.tr: Isa.11.14 is called the kingdom of God. Therefore, although the edicts and constitutions of Christian princes carry great weight in promoting and securing the state of Christianity, God nevertheless wills to exercise his chief power in a singular way through the spiritual sword of his Word, which he commands to be wielded by the ministers in the Church. I come to the second head, concerning the abolition and uprooting of the abuses and corruptions which Satan has introduced into God's ordinance in past ages. It is clear that Papal Christianity is altogether new and adulterated, and that it will be condemned at God's last judgment, since it so openly contradicts his own Word. Therefore, if you have a mind to lead the people out of that abyss, the example of the Apostle must be followed. For when he deals with restoring the true use of the Lord's Supper among the Corinthians, he bids the additions that had crept in to be abolished once and for all: "What I received from the Lord, that I also delivered to you." From this a general doctrine is to be gathered: when the question is of lawful reformation, and of what is acceptable to God, we must return to the pure Word of God itself. For as many mixtures as human ingenuity has devised, so many pollutions will remain, drawing men away from the right use of what the Lord instituted for their salvation. Therefore, while such a judgment is only partly carried out, the matter cannot be said to be truly restored to its place, where a masked Christianity is taken for a sincere and native one. I say this because I understand that many judge quite differently: namely, that abuses are to be tolerated and not touched, provided that the very gross corruptions can be said to be removed. But experience itself, on the contrary, has taught how fertile the human mind is as a crop of lies: sprinkled with even the smallest grains, it rises up to the highest top, as nature itself tends to be carried entirely thither. The method taught by Scripture is quite different. For David, speaking of idols, testifies that he will not even remember their name, to show how he judges them utterly detestable. Especially when we consider how grievously we have sinned against God in this matter while we were in ignorance, this should affect us all the more seriously, so that we withdraw as far as possible from all the leaven of Satan.

units.la: Quid enim illę ceremonię aliud fuerit, quam totidem le nocinia quę miseras animas ad malu perducerét, vti ad ipsas illa quaedas omnino positę erant? Iam si de causione agitur, monebuntur ho mines, scilicet, ne ad illas nunc impingant, cum superioris vitae peccata hac in parte illis retegentur. Quis tamen non videt, obdurari ipsos nihilominus, nihil vt infeliciilla cautione obtineri possit? Quare si quid istiusmodi intactum relinquetur, certissimū erit grauioris obfirmationis in malum fomentum, idemq; velmen appositum ne syncera doctrina quę proponetur, admittatur vt par est. Fateor quidē moderationi locu esse oportere, vt exire mitates nimis abscisę neq; hic vtiles sint, neq; simpliciter vsurpandę, adeoq; ceremonias ipsas ad vsum & captum populi esse accomodandas sed non minus constater affirmo videndum esse ne sub illo prætextu toleretur quicquid quod à Satana vel Antichristo profectum sit. Quo pertinet illa Scripturę loquędi ratio quę in historiis regum Iuda non vno loco extat, in plerosq; nepe qui cum idola sustulisset, omnia tamen ad viuum non resecuerunt, hac inquā illis alpergit notam, q; nihilominus excelsa quę nos sacella dicimus, & loca illa stultę deuotioni dicata nō abstulerint. Cum igitur eousq; te Deus prouexerit, amplissime domine, da operam obsecro, vt veri tepli ipsius reformatoris nomē referas, ac seculum hoc sub rege nepote tuo piissimi Iosię seculo respondeat: atq; ita omnia suo loco repositia cures, vt Regę deinde vna solicitudo ordinis bene positi conseruādi maneat. Proferam tibi istiusmodi corruptelarum exemplum, quod instar fer menti esse potuit quo massa integra sanctę Cenę quodammodo acceret. Audio recitari istic in Cenę celebratione orationem pro defunctis: neq; vero hoc ad Purgatorij Papistici approbationę referri satis scio. Neq; etiam me latet proferri posse antiquum ritum mentionis defunctorum faciędę, vt eo modo communio fidelium omnium in vnum corpus coiunctorum declaretur: sed obstat inuictū illud argumentum, nepe Cenā Domini ręadeo sacrosanctā esse, vt vllis hominū additamentis eā conspurcare sit nefas. Præterea vbi Deū inuocamus non est indulgēdum nostris affectibus, sed potius regula illa retinenda est quā tradit Apostolus, v: verbum Dei pro fundamēto habeamus: illa verò defuncto rum cōmemoratio quę ipsorum venerationę vel cōmendationę coniunctā habet, non respōdet verę ac legitimę rectę ordi in-stitutionis, ac perinde assumēdum est, quod in Cœna Domini nul lo modo ferendum sit. Sunt & alia nō proinde damnāda fortasse, sed tamē eiusmodi vt excusari nō possint, chrismā videlicet & vnctionis ceremonia: siquidē chrismā illud inuētio est triuola illorum qui iā olim in Domini institutione per ignorantiā non acquieuerūt, & qui nouo illo signo Spiritum sanctū in Baptismo ita sibi repręsentandum duxerunt, quasi aquę signum ad illud nō sufficeret. Extrema vnctio verò ab illorum incōsiderato zelo emanauit, qui Apostolos æmulari voluerunt, cum eodē cum ipsis dono nō pollerēt. Cum enim Apostoli oleum in ęgrorum sana tione adhibuerunt, illud eo pertinebat vt sanationis miraculum eatesera quasi exhibitum obsignarę ur. Cessante demum miraculorum dono, vsum quoq; externę illius vnctionis cessare oportuit. Quāobrem illa omnia abscindi semel præstiterit, vt nihil in Ecclesia Dei vsurpetur, quod nō & ipsius verbo cōforme sit, & ad Ecclesię ędificationę pertineat: vtrō toleradi sunt infirmi vt & l.iiij. confirmentur sensim & ad meliora promoueantur. Neque interea stultis immorandum est, vt illis satisfiat quibus hoc vel illud arridet simpliciter,cum nulla idonea causa subest. Scio qua consideratione plerique vlteriusprogreffi non sint: quia nempe veriti sunt vt maior rerum mutatio ferri non posset, praesertim vbi vicinorum ratio habenda visa est, quibuscum pax fouenda eflet conniuendo ad plurima. Habeat sane hoc locum in rebus istius vitae, in quibus licet de iure suo tantum remittere, quantum pacis studium & amor requiret. Atqui alia prorsus est ratio regiminis Ecclesiae quod spirituale est, in quo nihil non ad Dei verbum exigi fas est: non est inquam penes vllem mortalem quicquam hic aliis date aut in illorum gratiam deflectere, cum non alia res Deo magis inuisa fit, quam vbi humana illa nostra prudentia calculum hic suum apponere audet, vt vel moderemur vel rescindamus vel retroferamur praeter ipsius vniuscuiuslibet arbitrium. Ergo nisi illi displicere volumus, ad omnem cari nis intuitum oculi nobis semel claudendi sunt: & quod ad periculaattinet quae instare videbuntur, sic illa vobis declinanda erunt quantum erit in nobis, vt tamen a recta via discedere fem per fit nefas. Extat Domini promiflio, qua fe nobis adfuturum statuit rectam insistentibus viam: superest igitur hoc vnum, vt partibus nostris strenue fungendo, euentum illi commedemus. Neque enim aliunde est, quod sapientes huius seculi suae spes frustrantur vt plurimum, quam quod Dominus recedit ab illis, quatenus ipsius auxilio diffisi sese ad media obliqua & quae Deo minus probantur conuertunt. Quare fi Dei ipsius potentiam a nobis stare volumus, sequamur simpliciter quod iubet: atque impiimis hoc fundamentum statuendum nobis est, reformatione Ecclesiae singulare manus ipsius opus est, vt hac in parte homines sese illi in solidum regendos tradant: quodque etiam maius est, solere Dominum vt plurimum, tam in restituenda quam in conferuanda Ecclesia sua operari ratione quadam plane admirabili, & quae omnium hominum captum omnino superet. Proinde nullam rationem sinere opus illud reformationis Ecclesiae ad humani sensus modulum exigi, & quod coeleste est, ad terrae & mundi formam compositum habere velle. Neque tamen ita exclusam rectam illam prudentiam velim, cuius maximus hic quidem est vsus, vt non appositae rationes ineantur, ne in hanc vel illam partem nimis propendeatur, dum omnes Domino lucrari volumus: sed prudentiam hic Spiritus non carnis regnare cupio, dum os Domini interrogabimus, ac precabimur vt nostro sensu valere iusso, vnus ille nos in omnibus dirigat atque manu perducat. Vbi nos ita geremus, facile erit ansam praecidere variis tentationibus quae nos in medio cursu remorari possent. sent. Tu igitur amplissime Domine vti feliciter illam Christianismi restitutionem integram in regno Angliæ instituisti non innixustibi sed potenti Dei manu, quæ te hactenus sustinuit & mirabiliter confirmauit,sic etiam in eadem illa fiducia tibi pergendū esse existima. Acsanècùm Dominus ipse tot passim principatus sustentet sua prouidentia qui tamen ipsi aduersantur, multo magis illos respiciet qui & in illum sunt defixi &toto suo conatu supremum illum herum sibi asciscere cupiunt. Venio ad tertium caput quod est tum de vitiis coercendis tum de scan dalis comprimendis.Ego verò non dubito leges & edicta posita isthic esse,quæ recta & laudanda sint,& quibus populum in honestis moribus contineri cõueniat:sed ingens illa ἀτα ξία quam in mundo animaduerto me cogit vt te hic etiam appellem, vt in illud incumbas vt homines sub bona & honesta disciplina habeantur.Imprimis vt Dei honorem in eo ass ras dum illa cri mina vlcisceris,quorum persequutio apud homines infuperhaberi solet. Cùm enim furta,cædes,rapinæ seuerissimè pleætatur, quia ad homines iniuria pertineat, conniuetur interea ad scortationes,adulteria, ebriositates, blasphemi as nominis Dei,tanquam ad res licitas,aut non ita grauiter vindicädas. Atqui Deus longè aliter iis de rebus pronuntiat : ostendit enim quàm pretiosum ipsi sit nomen suum,dum apud homines proscinditur& pedibus proculcatur. Neque vero fieri potest, vt tam horrenda probra diutiùs inulta sinat:nam & ex Scriptura colligi potest vel vna tantùm Benhadadi & Sancheribi profanorum regum in Deum contumelia, horrendum Dei iudicium ipsos cum suis omnibus tantumnon adobruisse. Et quòd ad adulteria attinet, quis pudor est,nos qui Christiano nomine cèsemur,in illis vindicandis ethnicis ipsis longè molliores deprehendi, cum adeò ioco etiam eiusmodi scelera transmittantur? Tanti est scilicet sacrum ipsum coniugium,imaginem inquam illam viuam sacratissimæ nostræ cum Dei Filio coniunctionis impune pollui: arctissimam verò supra alias humanas omnes confœderatione perfidissimè disfringi?scortationes vero(si Apostolum audimus) non alio quàm totidem sacrilegiorum loco habebimus, quatenus templa Dei nostra corpora nimirum manifestè ita polluta, à Dei Spiritu & Christo ipso indignissimè abscinduntur.Vnde & illud subiicit, Scortatores & ebriosos ad Dei regnum non pertinere: vt & istorum commerciûm fidelibus nominatim interdicat : exquo consequitur in Ecclesia Dei tales ferri nullo modo oportere. Atque his omnino malis accepta ferenda sunt flagella Domini quibus orbis terrarum concutitur: fit enim vt dum enormia ista scelera homines inter sese condonant, manum Dei vindicem in seipsos accersant. Quamobrem vt Dei iram auerti procures, à te peto, amplissime domine, vt frænum hac in parte serio adhibeas, desque operam vt qui se istic Christianos profitentur, illud demum reipsa & moribus qui sanctæ vocationi respondeant, exprimant atque commonstrent: quemadmodum enim doctrina ipsa est instar animæ ad Ecclesiam viuificandam, ita etiam disciplina & vitiorum correctio neruorum loco habere debent, quibus corpus integrum ac vegetum foveatur atque conseruetur. Episcopi & Parochi in illud præcipue intenti sint ne Cœna Domini polluatur, si ad illam ij admittantur quorum vita propter scandala male audiat. Te vero pro eo in quem te Deus euexit loco curare imprimis par est, vt alij omnes subditi pro suo quisque loco & vocatione manum operi admoueant, singuli partes suas impleant, vt ordo legitime positus perinde etiam obseruetur. Hic vero, amplissime domine, in excusanda epistolæ prolixitate non ero prolixior, neque valde deprecabor offensionem qua aperte animi mei sensum tibi aperuerim: confido enim exploratum esse tibi animum meum pro tua prudentia, ac pro eo vsu Scripturæ quem habes, facile agnituru ex quo fonte hauserim quæ superius comprehensa à me hic habes: Quare non est quod metuam, ne fastidium tibi attulerim aut importunius egisse videri possim, vbi ostendi pro mea tenuitate syncerum illum affectum, qui eo fertur vnice vt Dei nomen per te semper quàm amplissime glorificetur. Hoc ab illo supplex in dies postulo, ac precor vt sua in te dona cumulatè adaugeat, suo te Spiritu in vera & inuicta constantia confirmet, tueatur & sustineat contra omnes aduersarios, te tuosq; præsidio suo tegat, tuam illam administrationem ita prosperet, vt Regi argumentum inde extet ipsius concelebrandi, cui tam opportunus & fui rector & regni in illa ætate contigerit. Tandem igitur, perquam demissime salute à me tibi adscripta finem scribendi faciam. Geneuæ XXII. Octob. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: For what else would those ceremonies have been than so many enticements that led wretched souls into evil, since they seem to have been set up for exactly that purpose? Now if the matter is one of caution, people will be warned, namely, not to stumble into them now, since the sins of their former life in this respect will be revealed to them. Yet who does not see that they are nonetheless hardened, so that nothing can be gained by that ill-starred caution? Therefore, if anything of this kind is left untouched, it will certainly be fuel for a more serious hardening in evil, and a veil placed over the pure doctrine that is set forth, so that it is not admitted as it ought to be. I admit that there must be room for moderation, so that extremes cut off too sharply are neither useful here nor to be used indiscriminately, and that the ceremonies themselves are to be adapted to the use and understanding of the people. But I affirm just as firmly that care must be taken lest, under that pretext, whatever has come from Satan or Antichrist be tolerated. To this belongs the manner of speaking in Scripture that appears in more than one place in the histories of the kings of Judah, where it is said of many who had removed the idols that they nevertheless did not cut everything out to the quick. That, I say, is the mark it brands on them: that they did not remove the high places, which we call little shrines, and those places dedicated to foolish devotion. Since God has advanced you so far, most excellent lord, I beg you to take the trouble to bear the name of restorer of the true temple of God, so that this age, under your nephew the king, may match the age of most pious Josiah. And so see to it that everything is put back in its place, so that the king's one concern thereafter remains the preservation of well-ordered government. I will set before you an example of such corruptions, which could work like leaven to sour in some measure the whole lump of the holy Supper. I hear that a prayer for the dead is recited there at the celebration of the Supper; yet I well know this is not to be taken as an approval of the Papists' Purgatory. Nor am I unaware that an ancient rite of making mention of the dead can be brought forward, so that by this means the communion of all the faithful joined into one body may be declared. But that invincible argument stands in the way: the Lord's Supper is so sacred that it is wrong to defile it with any additions of men. Moreover, when we invoke God, we must not indulge our feelings, but rather hold to the rule the Apostle gives, that we should have the Word of God as our foundation. That commemoration of the dead, however, which has joined to it veneration or commendation of the dead, does not correspond to the true and lawful institution of right order. It must therefore be concluded that it cannot in any way be tolerated in the Lord's Supper. There are other things, perhaps not to be condemned on that account, but of such a kind that they cannot be excused: namely the chrism and the ceremony of anointing. For that chrism is a trifling invention of those who, even long ago, through ignorance were not content with the Lord's institution, and who thought that the Holy Spirit had to be represented in Baptism by that new sign, as if the sign of water were not sufficient for it. Extreme unction, however, sprang from the ill-considered zeal of those who wished to imitate the Apostles, though they did not possess the same gift as the Apostles. For when the Apostles used oil in healing the sick, it served to seal the miracle of healing, as it were, as a visible pledge. When at length the gift of miracles ceased, the use of that outward anointing had to cease too. Wherefore it would have been better to cut all those things away once for all, so that nothing is used in the Church of God that does not agree with his own Word and serve the building up of the Church. Yet on the other hand the weak must be borne with, so that they may be gradually strengthened and advanced to better things. Meanwhile we must not linger over trifles in order to satisfy those who simply like this or that, when there is no proper reason behind it. I know on what consideration many have not advanced further: namely, because they feared that a greater change could not be borne, especially where regard seemed to have to be paid to neighbours, with whom peace had to be cherished by overlooking very many things. This certainly has its place in the affairs of this life, in which one may give up some of one's rights as far as zeal for peace and love require. But the government of the Church, which is spiritual, is wholly different, and in it nothing may be demanded except what is in God's Word. It is not, I say, within the power of any mortal to give anything here to others or to bend it to their favour, since nothing is more hateful to God than when our human prudence dares to add its own reckoning here, so that we either moderate, or cut away, or turn back, apart from the judgment of God alone. Therefore, unless we wish to displease him, our eyes must once and for all be closed to every regard for the flesh; and as for the dangers that seem to threaten, they must be avoided as far as lies in us, yet so that it is never right to depart from the straight way. There is the Lord's promise, by which he declares that he will be with those who keep to the straight way. What remains, therefore, is this one thing: to discharge our part vigorously and commit the outcome to him. For the wise of this world mostly have their hopes frustrated for no other reason than that the Lord withdraws from them, inasmuch as, distrusting his help, they turn to crooked means that are less pleasing to God. Therefore, if we want God's own power to stand on our side, let us simply follow what he commands. Above all we must establish this foundation: that the reformation of the Church is the singular work of his own hand, so that men in this matter surrender themselves wholly to be ruled by him. And, what is still greater, the Lord is accustomed for the most part, both in restoring and in preserving his Church, to work in a certain wholly admirable way that altogether surpasses the grasp of all men. Therefore we must allow no method for that work of reforming the Church to be measured by the standard of human sense, nor wish what is heavenly to be fashioned to the form of earth and the world. Yet I do not wish that right prudence to be shut out altogether, whose greatest use here is that suitable measures be taken, lest we lean too far to this side or that while we want to gain all for the Lord. But I wish that the prudence here be the prudence of the Spirit, not of the flesh, while we ask the mouth of the Lord and pray that, bidding farewell to our own understanding, he alone may direct us in all things and lead us by the hand. When we conduct ourselves thus, it will be easy to cut off the occasion of the various temptations that might hold us back in mid-course. Therefore, most excellent lord, since you have happily established the full restoration of Christianity in the kingdom of England, not relying on yourself but on the mighty hand of God, which has sustained you until now and wonderfully strengthened you, think that you must press on in that same trust. And indeed, since the Lord himself by his providence sustains so many principalities everywhere which nevertheless oppose him, much more will he look upon those who are fixed upon him and with all their effort desire to take that supreme Lord for their own. I come to the third head, which concerns both the restraining of vices and the suppressing of scandals. I certainly do not doubt that laws and edicts have been enacted there which are right and praiseworthy, and by which the people ought to be kept in honest conduct. But that great disorder [ἀταξία] which I observe in the world compels me to appeal to you here too, that you apply yourself to this, so that men may be kept under good and honest discipline. Above all, that you vindicate God's honour in this matter, while you avenge those crimes whose prosecution is commonly disregarded among men. For while thefts, murders and robberies are punished most severely, because they injure men, meanwhile people connive at fornications, adulteries, drunkenness and blasphemies of God's name, as if these were lawful things or not to be punished so gravely. Yet God pronounces quite otherwise on these matters: for he shows how precious his name is to him, while among men it is torn to pieces and trampled underfoot. Nor can it be that he suffers such horrible reproaches to go unpunished for long. For it can be gathered from Scripture that the insult to God offered by the profane kings Ben-hadad and Sennacherib alone was enough for God's dreadful judgment to have all but overwhelmed them and all their people. As for adultery, what shame it is that we, who are called by the Christian name, are found to be far softer than the heathen themselves in punishing it, when such crimes are passed over even as a joke! Is marriage itself so little regarded that it may be defiled with impunity, I mean that living image of our most holy union with the Son of God, and that closest covenant, above all other human covenants, be most faithlessly broken? Fornications, however (if we listen to the Apostle), we shall count as nothing other than so many sacrileges, inasmuch as our bodies, which are the temples of God, being so manifestly defiled, are most unworthily cut off from the Spirit of God and from Christ himself. Whence he also adds that fornicators and drunkards do not belong to the kingdom of God, and he forbids the faithful by name to have dealings with them. From this it follows that such people ought by no means to be tolerated in the Church of God. And assuredly the scourges of the Lord with which the world is shaken must be received as the consequence of these evils. For while men forgive one another these monstrous crimes, they summon the avenging hand of God upon themselves. Therefore, that you may procure the turning away of God's wrath, I ask of you, most excellent lord, that you apply the bridle in earnest in this matter, and see to it that those who there profess themselves Christians express and show forth in deed and conduct what corresponds to their holy calling. For just as doctrine itself is like the soul for giving life to the Church, so discipline and the correction of vices ought to hold the place of the sinews, by which the body is kept whole, vigorous and preserved. Bishops and parish ministers should be especially intent on this, that the Lord's Supper not be defiled, if those are admitted to it whose life has a bad name on account of scandals. But for your part, in the position to which God has raised you, it is above all fitting that you take care that all other subjects, each in his own place and calling, put their hand to the work, each fulfilling his own part, so that the lawfully established order may likewise be observed. Here, most excellent lord, I will not be overly long in excusing the length of my letter, nor will I greatly beg pardon for the offence of having laid open to you the feeling of my mind so frankly. For I trust that my mind is well known to you through your prudence, and through the familiarity with Scripture that you have, so that you will easily recognise from what source I have drawn what I have set down above. So there is no reason for me to fear that I have caused you weariness or may seem to have acted too importunately, since I have shown, according to my slender ability, that sincere feeling which aims solely at this: that God's name may be glorified through you always and as widely as possible. This I ask of him daily as a suppliant, and I pray that he will add his gifts to you abundantly, confirm you by his Spirit in true and unconquered steadfastness, guard and sustain you against all adversaries, cover you and yours with his protection, and so prosper that administration of yours that there may be from it a ground for the King to celebrate him, since in this age he has been granted so opportune and faithful a ruler for his realm. Finally, then, with the greeting I add to you most humbly, I make an end of writing. Geneva, 22 October 1548.

units.la: Tuæ Excellentiæ deditissimus Ioannes Calvinus.
units.tr: Your Excellency's most devoted, John Calvin.

units.la: CALVINVS AMED. PERRINO CAPITANEO.
units.tr: Calvin to Amedée Perrin, Captain.

units.la: Lubenter te conuenisset, D. Capitanee, nisi aliter expedire mihi visum esset: causam suo tempore & loco audire ex me licebit. Optandum vero vt te stitiffimis Consistorio, quo aliis exemplo præires. Cùm in eo aliquid desideratum sit, quod tu fortasse admonitus non esses, optassem saltem te ad extremam concionem adesse hodie, vt illic Syndicus Corneus & ego tecum ageremus. Vnde fieri non video: illud vero te exististimare volo, non posse nos vti pondere ac pondere, atque impari bilance: & si in iure æquabilitas retinenda est, non potest sane in Ecclesia Dei inæquabilitas tolerari. Quis sim aut ipse scis, aut scire saltem debes: is nempe cui ita cordi sit ius cœlestis heri,vt ab illo recta conscientia asserendo nullius mortalis causa dimouendus sim. Alio te spectare ipse non sentio:sed illud aduerto,in sua causa parum oculatum quemque esse. Quantum ad me attinet, in hoc quidem negotio non tantum Ecclesiæ ædificationi & saluti tuæ, sed etiam commodo tuo, nomini & otio consultum cupio. Quàm enim odiosum erit quod in te redundaturum est, quasi à iure communi, quo nemo non tenetur, liber & solutus esses. Præstat vero pro meo in te studio periculum præuertere, quàm vtilla tibi nota infligatur:sane audiui quod ex domo tua prodierit, cauerem videlicet, ne ignem sopitum excitarem, ne perinde mihi atque ante annum septimum hoc cederet. Sed nullius sunt momenti voces illæ apud me. Neque enim Geneuam redij vel otij vel quæstus causa, neque rursum mihi dolendum erit cum Geneua erit egrediundum. Commodum & salus Ecclesiæ & Ciuitatis mihi redeundi animum dedit. Ac si dme vno ageretur nunc, omnibus semel dictum vellem quibus molestus esse videor,quod facis fac citius. Atqui non efficiet illa quorundam indignitas & ingratus animus, vt officio desim, atque studium illud erga hunc locum ad extremum spiritum deponam, cuius Deum auctorem habeo. Neque vnquam alieni hominis affectum admittam,vt corpore abesse deinde contingat. Ista ad te non spectant,sed ad proximum ate ex tuis ipsis. Neque etiam vt iurgia sparguntur, hæc scribo, sed vt constet qua constantia perresturus sim, quicquid accidat. Te vero imprimis tibi persuadere velim, primariam illam virtutem tibi affectandam esse, vt Deo obedias & ordinem communem atque politiam Ecclesiæ obserues. Dominus te præsidio suo tueatur,tibíque patesaciat, quantum verbera etiam certi amici præstent proditoriis aliorum blanditiis. Vale.
units.tr: I would gladly have met you, Captain, had I not thought it better otherwise. You may hear the case from me at the proper time and place. I wish indeed that you would attend the most crowded Consistory, so that you might set an example for the others. Since something is lacking there which you perhaps were not aware of, I had hoped at least that you would be present at today's final sermon, so that Syndic Corneus and I could deal with you there. I do not see how this can happen. But I want you to understand this: we cannot use one weight and another, an unequal balance. If equity must be kept in law, then surely inequity cannot be tolerated in the Church of God. Who I am, you yourself know, or at least ought to know: I am one who holds the heavenly law so dear that, in asserting it with a clear conscience, I must not be moved by the cause of any mortal. I do not sense that you are aiming at anything else, but I notice that everyone is rather short-sighted in his own cause. As far as I am concerned, in this matter I wish to provide for the building up and salvation of the Church and for your own advantage, your reputation and your peace. For how hateful it will be for you, what will fall upon you, as if you were free and exempt from the common law by which everyone is bound! Out of my goodwill toward you, it is better to forestall danger than to have that mark inflicted on you. I have indeed heard what came out of your house, and I should, of course, take care not to rekindle the smouldering fire, lest it turn out for me as it did seven years ago. But those voices carry no weight with me. For I did not return to Geneva for the sake of leisure or gain, nor, on the other hand, shall I grieve when I must leave Geneva. The advantage and safety of the Church and the City have given me the will to return. And if only my own person were at stake now, I would say once for all to all those whom I seem to bother: "What you do, do quickly." Yet the unworthiness and ungrateful spirit of certain men will not make me fail in my duty, nor will I lay down, until my last breath, that zeal for this place whose author I have in God. Nor will I ever admit a feeling of alienation, so that I might then be absent in body. These things do not concern you, but your neighbour, from among your own people. I write this not to scatter quarrels, but so that it may be clear with what constancy I shall persevere, whatever happens. And I would above all have you persuade yourself that the chief virtue for you to aim at is to obey God and to observe the common order and polity of the Church. May the Lord protect you with his help, and make clear to you how much the blows of a true friend are worth against the treacherous flatteries of others. Farewell.

units.la: Tibi addictus & ex animo frater I.C.
units.tr: Your devoted and sincere brother, J.C.

units.la: BRENTIVS CALVINO.
units.tr: Brentius to Calvin.

units.la: NON dubito,amicissime mi Caluine,te iamdudum accepisse quis sit status, imò quæ sit mutatio Ecclesiarum in nostra parte Germaniæ: quæ ruina etiam me ex ea Ecclesia, in qua Euangelium Filij Dei vigintiquinque annis docui, eiecit.Et cū mandato τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος,vel ad carceres vel ad mor te petitus fuerim, hactenus diuina clementia,& cura amicorū ita descensus sum,vt his diebus saluus ad Bafileam peruenerim. Statui autem hic hybernare. Et quanquam inuenerim omnia hic commoda,hospitium,vrbis amœnitatem,ciuium beneuolentiā, doctorum virorum familiaritatem, & (quo maxime delector) ministrorum Ecclesiæ humanitatem: tamen cum venit in mentem vastatæ Ecclesiæ, desertæ familiæ meæ,ac periculorum, quæ aliis & Ecclesiis & ministris earum imminere videntur,cogitare ipse potes nihil externarum rerum tam amœnum esse, quod in tali paroxysmo iucunditatem afferre queat.Quare,quę est tua pietas,non dubito, quin coniungas tuas preces cum nostris, vt Filius Dei incipiat iterum declarare se sedere ad dextram Dei Patris fui,& tueri Ecclesiam suam. Nam hoc officium nos vicissim vobis præstamus,& gratulamur tibi & tuę Ecclesię,quod hęc periculà ad vos nondum pertingant, ac precamur Deum Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi vt vos ita conseruet, quo perspicuè cognoscatur Ecclesiam Filij Dei non in cœlis tantum,verum etiam in terris suas habere mansiones & hospitia. De Argentorato, existimo te è Buceri literis cognoscere quæ vel spes sit, vel metus. Adhuc deliberatur ibi de recipiendo vel reiiciendo Interitu.Vvittembergum & reliqua Saxonia ac Misnia fortiter adhuc Interim recusant. Noriemberga agnoscit quidem τὸ μέτα ξύ :sed nihil adhuc ibi mutatum est.In Ducatu Vvittembergensi aliquibus in locis,vna diei hora missatur, alia Euangelii Christi prædicatur. Nec ibi quicquam mutatum est, nisi quòd veteres quidam sacrificuli faciunt Missas.Veri autem ministri Ecclesiæ receperint in administratione sacrorum vestitum, quem vocant choralem, & adiecti sint quidam sesti dies ad priores, præterea esus carnium publicus consuetis haftenus diebus interdicti sus sit. Cætera ita ibi salua sunt, vt pij ministri non solùm non exturbentur e suo ministerio,verum etiam ex aliis locis expulsi recipiantur. Dominus det vt Princeps eius regionis possit hoc institutum suum conseruare & tueri. In quibusdam Imperialibus Ciuitatibus restituitur non Interitus tantùm, sed etiam Papatus ipse, hoc est, extrema internecio. Optimus noster Frechtus adhuc tenetur captiuus cum Collegis suis in arce Kyrcheim, in ducatu Vvittembergensi, quam arcem Hispani præsidio suo tenent, τὸν αὐτοκράτορα aiunt hac hyeme redituru m ad Spirā. Qui reditus,quid allaturus sit incolumitatis reliquiis Ecclesiarum,res ipsa declarabit. Et fortassis suas etiam partes aget in hoc negocio iudicium Camerae his diebus Spirae instauratum. Ita vides,nihil nobis spei,nisi in cœlo repositum esse. Age igitur amicissime mi Caluine, conscende, quod facis, nobiscum precibus tuis in cœlum, vt excitemus Filium Dei ad seruandas reliquias suas. Bene ac feliciter vale. è Basilea. Reliqua Renatus ille, qui mihi iucundus cundus fuit comes ab Argentorato, vsque ad Basileam. vi. Octobris.
units.tr: I do not doubt, most friendly Calvin, that you have long since heard what the situation is, or rather what the upheaval of the churches in our part of Germany is. That ruin has also driven me out of the church where I taught the Gospel of the Son of God for twenty-five years. When I was sought, with an order from the emperor [τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος], either for prison or for death, divine mercy and the care of friends have so far brought me down safely, and I reached Basel safely in these days. I have decided to winter here. Although I have found everything here agreeable: lodging, the pleasantness of the city, the goodwill of its citizens, the friendship of learned men, and (what delights me most) the kindness of the ministers of the Church; yet when the thought comes to me of the devastated Church, of my deserted family, and of the dangers that seem to threaten other churches and their ministers, you can yourself imagine that nothing in external affairs is so pleasant as to bring enjoyment in such a crisis. Therefore, in your piety, I do not doubt that you will join your prayers with ours, that the Son of God may begin again to show that he sits at the right hand of God the Father, and may protect his Church. For this is the duty we in turn perform for you, and we congratulate you and your Church that these dangers have not yet reached you. We pray that God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ will preserve you so that it may be clearly recognised that the Church of the Son of God has its dwellings and lodgings not only in heaven but also on earth. About Strasbourg, I suppose you learn from Bucer's letters what hope or fear there is. Still, there they are deliberating whether to receive or reject the Interim. Wittenberg and the rest of Saxony and Meissen still firmly refuse the Interim. Nuremberg indeed accepts the Interim [τὸ μεταξύ], but nothing there has yet been changed. In the Duchy of Wittenberg, in some places mass is said at one hour, and the Gospel of Christ is preached at another. Nothing there has been changed except that some old priests say masses. The true ministers of the Church, however, have adopted in the administration of the sacraments the vestment which they call choral, some festival days have been added to the earlier ones, and public eating of meat, previously forbidden on the usual days, has been allowed. Otherwise everything there remains so intact that pious ministers are not only not driven from their ministry, but even those expelled from other places are received. May the Lord grant that the prince of that region may be able to preserve and maintain this arrangement of his. In some imperial cities not only the Interim but the Papacy itself is restored, that is, utter destruction. Our excellent Frecht is still held captive with his colleagues in the fortress of Kirchheim, in the Duchy of Wittenberg, which the Spaniards hold with their garrison. They say the emperor will return to Speyer this winter. What that return will bring for the surviving remnants of the churches, the event itself will show. Perhaps the court of judgment reopened at Speyer in these days will also play its part in this matter. So you see that nothing is stored up for us in hope except in heaven. Come then, most friendly Calvin, ascend with us in your prayers to heaven, that we may rouse the Son of God to save his remnants. Farewell, well and happily. From Basel. As for the rest, that Renatus, who was a pleasant companion to me from Strasbourg as far as Basel. 6 October.

units.la: Brentius tuus.
units.tr: Your Brentius.

units.la: CALVINVS NN. S.
units.tr: Calvin to N.N., greeting.

units.la: FLeri vt plurimum solet vt quæ superuacua sunt, non tædium modo pariant lectoribus, sed etiam non sine stomacho respuantur, atqui ego contra hac meam exhortationem quominus necessaria erit eò æquioribus animis exceptum iri à vobis confido. Nam qui sponte in prosequendo pietatis cursu sunt incitati non placidi tantùm, sed libenter quoque stimulos addi sibi patiuntur: tales autem vos esse quia mihi persuasi, non est quòd ad pergendum hortari dubitem: etsi, vt simpliciter dicam quod res est, nō ea vos alacritate pergere arbitror, quin magno adhuc vobis vsui sint piæ admonitiones, nondum certè eousque estis progressi quin longè vlterius sit enitendum.Semper cauendum est ne pretiosum illud femen quod accepimus, vel suffocetur vel degeneret: etiam si quotidie magna cura excolamur, restamen ostendit quàm facile spinæ suecrescant, quid si neglectus accedat? quid si multiplices obrepant hinc inde corruptelæ. Sed omnium peffimum si eas nobis accersimus: video aliqua ex parte, vos melius sentitis ipsi, quàm multa se auocamenta ingerant in eo viuendi genere, in quo fluctuatis: sic enim de inquieta turbulentaque vita loquendum est, vt maximè acres intentique sitis ad resistendum: difficilis tamen est victoria, quo maius periculum est ne securis & aliud agentibus inducatur Satanæ artificiis Christi obliuio, quæ vos in mundi abyssum demergat. Assiduè in mentem veniat illud Pauli, quosdam à fide excidisse, quòd alienari fuissent à bona conscientia, ne ipsi quoque tam horrendi naufragij simus exempla aliis: ac de vobis quidem nihil tale metuo. Sed quia nunquam possumus nimium cauti esse, hoc quoque dissimulare amor erga vos meus non permittit, & videmus vt sibi hodie plerique feré omnes delitias faciant, quasi impunè cum Deo ludatur: quare nihil melius quàm vt subinde quisque se ad torporem expergefaciat, sibi inflet, se ad calculum reuocet. Nec verò si quis in vobis aliquando fuit ardor, languescere nūc debet ob istas calamitates, quibus Ecclesiam cernimus oppressam vt parum ab interitu distare videatur: potius cogitare vos decet quàm miseras populi sui res & afflictas Moyses sciret esse quum vltrò se opibus, deliciis, honoribus Ægypti abdicans nonnisi probris & ærumnis socium se adiunxit. Quàquam non eadem omnes spiritus magnitudine peræquè excellimus, vocamur tamen ad vnum omnes ad imitandi studium. Hispau-
units.tr: Although superfluous things usually not only bore readers but are also spurned with irritation, I, on the contrary, trust that my exhortation, the less necessary it is, will be received by you with more equable minds. For those who are spontaneously stirred on in the course of piety not only are calm but also gladly allow goads to be added to them; and since I am persuaded that you are such, I do not hesitate to urge you onward; although, to say simply what the case is, I do not think you are proceeding with such eagerness that pious admonitions are no longer of great use to you, for you have certainly not yet advanced so far that you should not strive much further. We must always take care that the precious seed we have received is neither choked nor degenerates. Even if we are cultivated daily with great care, yet experience shows how easily thorns spring up; what if neglect is added? What if manifold corruptions creep in on every side? But the worst of all is if we invite them ourselves. I see that in some measure you yourselves understand better than I how many distractions press in upon that way of life in which you are tossed about. For we must speak of a restless and turbulent life in such a way that you should be most keen and intent on resisting. Yet victory is difficult, and the greater the danger that, while you are secure and busy with other things, the forgetfulness of Christ may be induced by Satan's devices and plunge you into the abyss of the world. Let that saying of Paul be constantly in your mind, that some have fallen from the faith because they had been alienated from a good conscience, lest we ourselves become examples of such a horrible shipwreck to others. Indeed I fear nothing of this kind concerning you. But since we can never be too cautious, my love for you does not permit me to pass over this point either. We see that nearly almost everyone today indulges himself in pleasures, as if one could mock God with impunity. Therefore nothing is better than that each person should from time to time rouse himself from torpor, take stock of himself, and call himself to account. Nor indeed, if there was once any ardour in any of you, should it now grow cold because of those calamities by which we see the Church so oppressed that it seems barely distant from destruction. Rather you ought to consider how wretched and afflicted were the affairs of his people, which Moses knew when, renouncing of his own accord the riches, delights and honours of Egypt, he joined himself as a companion only to reproaches and hardships. Although we do not all equally excel in the same greatness of spirit, we are all called to the one zeal of imitating. To a few

units.la: cis fi non plane testatam at saltem indicatam esse volui folicitudinem quam de salute vestra gero. Valete egregij & nobilissimi adolescentes. Dominus vos Spiritu suo gubernet semper,ac spiritualibus diuitiis magis ac magis locupletet, quo nomen suum gloriosum per vos illustretur. Nonis Nouembris. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: I wanted my anxiety for your salvation to be, if not plainly testified, at least indicated. Farewell, outstanding and most noble young men. May the Lord always govern you by his Spirit and enrich you more and more with spiritual riches, so that his glorious name may be made illustrious through you. Nones of November, M. D. XLVIII.

units.la: CALVINVS BRENTIO S.
units.tr: CALVIN TO BRENTIUS, GREETING.

units.la: Eximio Domini nostri Iesu Christi ministro D.Ioanni Brentio, Symmystae & fratri in Domino honorando.
units.tr: To the distinguished minister of our Lord Jesus Christ, Master John Brenz, my fellow minister and brother to be honoured in the Lord.

units.la: SI quid mihi iucundum in his tristissimis temporibus esse potest, iucundae imprimis suauesque fuissent tuae literae. Gratissimae certe fuerunt, multumque solatij attulerunt varijs meis doloribus, quod te scilicet de cuius vita diu anxij fuerant boni omnes,ereptum esse ex mortis faucibus nunciabant. Tametsi enim fieri nequit quin tibi acerba fit vita in praefenti rerum statu, dum ab ea Ecclesia te diuulsum cogitas qua & genuisti in Christo, & tanta folicitudine educafti, eamque vt est orbata suo Pastore, propemodum expositam vides Satanae libidini, simul tamen reputare debes non te frustra seruatum a Domino. Poteras iam in hac tua senecta quamlibet vegeta mori fatur annorum: & sane quid nunc est in mundo quod nos aliquo viuendi desiderio foliciter? Sed ego non dubito quin Dominus qui haetenus ministerio tuo feliciter & vberrimo cum fructu vsus est in Ecclesiae suae aedificationem aliquid habeat operis nobis incognitum, in quo te porro exercere velit: non quod melior spes saltem propinqua nobis appareat, quin potius ita fe vndique quocunque oculos verteamus nouorum malorum signa offendunt, vt nihil praeter vltimum Ecclesiae interitum reliquum esse videatur: deinde quemadmodum his calamitatibus causam praebuit nostra impietas & ingratitudo, sic etiam nos contumacia nostra hodie vrget vt multo plura & atrociora merito timenda sint quam haetenus senserimus, sed vna haec cogitatio mihi lominus me fultentat animumque reficit, quod ita mecum statuo Deum, quum mirificam hanc Ecclesiae instaurationem inchoauit, non inanem spem oftetaffe, quae mox euanesceret, sed opus esse aggressum quod no inuito tantum Satana, sed malitia quoque hominum reluctante tuebitur ac stabiliet. Interea purgationem qua nobis opus est, patienter feramus: fi semel huc peruerit Leonis furor, multo crudelius nobiscum agetur, & certe haetenus minas magis tentauit quam saeuitia grassatus est: sed pro-
units.tr: If anything can give me pleasure in these most sorrowful times, your letter would have given me especially great and sweet pleasure. It was most welcome indeed and brought much comfort to my various griefs, since it announced that you, for whose life all good men had long been anxious, had been snatched from the jaws of death. For although it cannot but be bitter for you to live in the present state of affairs, while you think of yourself as torn away from the Church which you begot in Christ and raised with such great care, and which, as you see, is bereft of its Pastor and almost exposed to the lust of Satan, you must nonetheless reflect that you have not been preserved by the Lord in vain. Already in this old age you could have died full of years, however vigorous you were. And indeed, what is there now in the world that makes us wish to live? But I do not doubt that the Lord, who has hitherto used your ministry happily and with most abundant fruit for the building up of his Church, has some work unknown to us, in which he wishes you to go on exercising yourself. Not that a better hope appears to us, even a near one; rather, wherever we turn our eyes, signs of new evils meet us, so that nothing but the final ruin of the Church seems to be left. Moreover, just as our impiety and ingratitude gave cause for these calamities, so our obstinacy now presses upon us, so that far more and more atrocious things are rightly to be feared than we have so far felt. Yet this one thought sustains me and refreshes my spirit: I reckon thus, that God, when he began this wonderful restoration of the Church, did not hold out an empty hope that would soon vanish, but has undertaken a work which he will defend and establish not only against the unwilling Satan but also against the resistance of human malice. Meanwhile let us patiently bear the purging that we need. If the fury of the Lion once comes here, we shall be treated much more cruelly; certainly until now he has tried threats more than he has raged in savagery, but he will pour

units.la: Epist.91. profundet quod hactenus continuit, simulac nihil iam sibi obstare cernet. Itaque non aliter nos comparatos esse decet quàm si exertus gladius esset supra ceruices, & ignes accensi:cæterùm, vt dicebam non dubito quin futurus sit modus aliquis castigationis, ac Deus propediem Ecclesiam ex miserrima hac dissipatione colligat. Vnum vereor ne prius tam fœdam Germaniæ mollitiem cum impia perfidia coniunctam seuerè vlcisçatur:quia tamen multas oues innoxias agnoscat, ab hircis robustioribus fuisse proditas, earum vt spero pro sua misericordia rationem habebit,vt iustam iram cohibeat. Nos hic, quoniam aliud non licet, tui & similium assiduè in precibus nostris sumus memores,vtinam aliis quoque officiis iuuare te possemus: sed hoc scilicet præcipuum nos simul omnes Deum supplicitèr orare, vt si nostris peccatis offensus fræna impiorum sæuitiæ ad tempus laxauit,nunc vicissim eorum ludibriis ac petulantia prouocatus se & suos respiciat:Christum deinde rogare vt non tantum apud Patrem sit nobis deprecator,sed iustum Ecclesiæ suæ vindicem se ostendat. Vale eximie vir, & frater in Domino mihi semper colende.Dominus cui seruis Spiritu suo gubernare te pergat,ac sanctos tuos labores benedicat,Amen.Geneuæ,Nonis Nouemb. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: Epist. 91. out what he has hitherto held back, as soon as he sees that nothing now stands in his way. So we ought to prepare ourselves as if a drawn sword were over our necks and fires were lit. Still, as I said, I do not doubt that there will be some measure of chastisement, and that God will shortly gather his Church out of this most wretched dispersal. One thing I fear: that first he will severely punish Germany's shameful softness, joined with impious treachery. Yet since he recognises that many innocent sheep were betrayed by stronger goats, I hope that in his mercy he will take account of them, so as to restrain his just anger. We here, since we can do nothing else, are always mindful of you and those like you in our prayers. Would that we could help you also by other services! But this above all: that we all together pray earnestly to God, that if, offended by our sins, he has for a time loosed the bridles of the wicked's cruelty, he may now in turn, provoked by their mockery and insolence, look upon himself and his own. Then that we ask Christ not only to be our advocate with the Father but to show himself the just avenger of his Church. Farewell, excellent man, and brother always to be honoured by me in the Lord. May the Lord, whom you serve, continue to govern you by his Spirit and bless your holy labours. Amen. Geneva, the Nones of November, 1548.

units.la: FARELLVS CALVINO S. Gratiam & Pacem à Domino.
units.tr: FAREL TO CALVIN, GREETING. Grace and peace from the Lord.

units.la: PER exemplar literarum ad Viretū missum, existimo te intellexisse in quibus versetur spinis verus Christi seruus Bucerus, quem merito pij omnes ardentissimis precibus D.commendare debent.Christus Iesus ei adsit,& plenè benedicat illius ministerio,ac omnium qui Ecclesiarum salutem quæ-runt. Mirum est Senatum tam esse fractum & tam exigua prædicium fide,quòd non cupit se totum D.committere,& quæ Christi sunt tueri & Antichristo resistere.Forte habet qui ita suadean & audit quosdam agere apud Vvittembergensem: nescio an Schnepfius sit:de Illibio res est notior,nimirum debere fieri Cæsaris imperata, & non licere interim reticere. Dominus Iesus faxit vt quod coepisti in Interim, ne quemquam interim at,scribere absoluas.Nam sanè expedit,cum procul à nostris(si vera audimus) non improbetur: nam Vincentius fertur non improbare, & passim qui se putant aliquid esse, & à nonnullis alicuius fiunt, illud commendant. Tollino eiusmodi,qui per ceremoniarum institutionem & additionem negotium fecerunt, verendum ne per Interim plus nunc faciant. Missatorem vnum habent, sed insignem ebrium, Mombelgardi, & alterum Blancmonte. Decanus vir peffimus, & qui diu sciens & volens Spiritui diuino reluctatus fuit, iubente Cæsare admissus fuit: hunc visitet D.vt meritus est. Nam nisi per D.improbitas viri compescatur, multu detrimenti Ecclesiæ afferet. Si Toffano & Bucero quoq; timeam aduersa vt opto prospera & Ecclesiis concreditis ipsis: tibi quid non metuam & quid non optem & isti Ecclesiæ non parû anxius vt res istic habeant, cum nihil audiuerim à die quo istac solui: & in hac anxietate ita respiro, quòd male res non habeat, cum fiquid mali effet, statim vulgaretur, vt nunc fit fi vnquam fuerit, bona cum tara sint, rarius annunciantur, mala cum inundent nunquam non audiuntur. Ruina inconstantis Conftantiç prius audiebatur, quàm perfecta effet, & nunc narratur talis esse, vt Sodomam esse dixeris. Nam Bacchantium in morem, choreis, ludis, ebrietatibus, & omni spurcitiæ ita feruntur operam dare, vt nemo iam iudicare possit honesti eos vnquam ratione vllam habuisse, nec dicam Christum & Euangelium audiuisse & excepisse. Pagi, qui in gratiam Cæsaris non solum non fuerunt auxilio Conftantiencfibus, sed aliis quoque fuerunt impedimento, cum reliquis agunt, vt Interim admittant: & quædam alia. Propediem responsum sunt accepturi. Pecunia & ingentia munera, verendum ne fœdera omnia rumpant. Sed quid fœderis tenebit is qui fe suosque salutem & fortunas venales habet? Si Satanas tam infestus hostis sese pro insigni amico venditat, & id plerisque suadet, ac quædam in hoc dat, mirum fi illius ministri hoc non persuadeant iis quos supra omne genus hominum oderunt, præcipue dum copiosum dant aurum: sed erit plufquam Tolofanum: sane stipendium & munera, vt videntur profufius erogata, hami erunt quibus non solum aurum omne principu acceptum, verum insuper corpora & quicquid est, capiantur & sint prædadatori, qui manibus suorum & sanguine fuso perlitabit ad satietatem illorum sanguine qui prius fuderunt. Sera erit pœnitentia, frustra tunc sapientiam inuocabunt, quam recipere & audire noluerunt. Quid Gallis immineat, & quo inftigatore orti sint motus, & ad quid, & qui proditioni seruierunt à proauis, iam est videre: sua iudicia exercebit D. qui nostri misertus corda tangat, vt ferio conuertamur omnes, & vera fide dignos factus edamus veræ refipifcentiç. D.Iesus te feruet incolumem, & diu Ecclesiæ suæ inseruientem. Vale cum coniuge & Collegis & piis omnibus. Seruet istos omnes D.qui tecum amant Christum, & Satanam perdat. Collega te salutat & mei fratres. Neocomi, XIX Nouemb. M. D. XLVIII.
units.tr: Through the copy of the letter sent to Viret, I think you have understood in what thorns the true servant of Christ, Bucer, is placed, whom all the pious ought to commend to the Lord with most ardent prayers. May Christ Jesus be with him and fully bless his ministry and that of all who seek the salvation of the Churches. It is strange that the Senate is so broken and of such little faith that it does not wish to commit itself wholly to the Lord, to defend what is Christ's and to resist Antichrist. Perhaps it has someone who advises this, and some men who act with the people of Wittenberg; I do not know whether it is Schnepf. The matter concerning Illyricus is better known: namely, that Caesar's commands must be obeyed and that it is not lawful meanwhile to keep silent. May the Lord Jesus grant that you finish writing what you have begun against the Interim, so that no one is taken in by it. For indeed it is expedient, since (if we hear true reports) it is not disapproved far from us; for Vincentius is said not to disapprove, and everywhere those who think themselves something, and are made much of by some, commend it. Men like Tollinus, who made trouble through the institution and addition of ceremonies, are to be feared, lest through the Interim they now do even more. They have one missionary, but a notorious drunk, at Montbéliard, and another at Blamont. The dean, a very wicked man who for a long time knowingly and willingly resisted the divine Spirit, was admitted at Caesar's command; may the Lord visit him as he deserves. For unless the wickedness of this man is restrained by the Lord, he will bring much harm to the Church. If I fear adversity for Tossanus and Bucer too (though I wish them prosperity), and for the Churches entrusted to them, what should I not fear for you, and what should I not wish? I am not a little anxious for that Church there, that matters are going well, since I have heard nothing since the day I sailed from there. In this anxiety I take some comfort, thinking that things are not going badly, since if there were something bad it would be published at once, as happens now if ever it does. Good things, since they are rare, are announced less often; bad things, since they flood in, are never not heard. The ruin of inconstant Constance was heard of before it was complete, and now it is reported to be such that you would say it is Sodom. For they give themselves over, in the manner of Bacchants, to dances, games, drunkenness and every kind of filth, so that no one can now judge that they ever had any regard for honesty, not to mention that they heard and received Christ and the Gospel. The villages, which in favour of Caesar not only did not help the people of Constance but also hindered others, are acting with the rest to admit the Interim; and certain other things. Shortly they are to receive an answer. Money and huge bribes: I fear they will break every covenant. But what covenant will he keep who has himself, his people, salvation and fortunes for sale? If Satan, so hostile an enemy, offers himself as a distinguished friend, and persuades most people of this, and gives some proof of it, it would be strange if his ministers did not persuade this to those whom they hate above every other kind of men, especially while they give abundant gold. But it will be more than Tolosan. Indeed the stipends and gifts, lavishly given as they appear, will be hooks by which not only all the gold received from the princes but also bodies and whatever else there is will be caught and given to the plunderer, who will bathe his hands in the blood of his own people, and will be sated with the blood of those who shed it first. Repentance will come too late; in vain then they will call upon the wisdom they refused to receive and hear. What threatens the French, by whose instigation the movements arose, and to what end, and who from their forefathers served treachery, is now to be seen. The Lord will exercise his judgments, and, having pity on us, may he touch our hearts so that we all may be seriously converted and, made worthy of true faith, bring forth the fruits of true repentance. May the Lord Jesus keep you safe and long serving his Church. Farewell, with your wife, your colleagues and all the pious. May the Lord keep safe all those with you who love Christ, and destroy Satan. My colleague greets you, and my brothers. Neuchâtel, 19 November 1548.

units.la: Existimo te refcifife Synodum tandem concessam & admissam, quanuis dies nondum dicta fit. Christus faxit vt Ecclesiis & fanêto sancto ministerio recte consulatur, & quæ corrigenda sunt, vt decet,corrigatur:tu vide quæso,quid in doctrina multorum desideretur & in vita, vt Epicurei secum tam multos non perdant. Per idoneos id opportune curandum est, magno cum timore Dei & precibus assiduis ne Satanas quos fouet & agit, suis dolis tegat & fucis efficiat, quominus cognoscantur & impune euadant.
