Shortly before the hand was laid on him, he had written to me that he was now wholly intent on getting his affairs in order and then hurrying to us by sea. He had decided to settle with the tyrants in such a way that, content with a third part of his property, he would leave the rest to them twofold. Among other things he related a remarkable sight that presented itself to him, which I do not wish to hide from you: amid the ruins of our city, my father's house, while all the others were reduced to ashes, stands intact. At last he adds: "I do not doubt that God wished to leave some sign against all those of your town who, eight or ten years earlier, burned in effigy Monsieur de Normandie and the rest." Moreover, this last thing he mentions was done by a decree of the Parisian court, which revealed its ridiculous stupidity in that, without any mention of me, it ordered Abel to be summoned in the market of Noyon, and declared that, unless he appeared, he should be held as convicted. The thing would be incredible to me, were it not for the memorable event that followed: when Normandy had placed in the square tower, which stood in the middle of the market, a bronze plaque to be fixed there for the lasting honour of Normandy by the same decree of the court, that tower was consumed by a fire in a private house. Now Normandy says he will hold back the execution of the sentence until our citizens restore his castle. N., who has been unlucky, thought that he had made a great profit from our unpopularity by delaying. I confess that he has scraped together a good sum of money here and there. But I deny that I helped him so much in this matter that, if anyone consulted me, I would not rather have dissuaded him. Yet the man's wickedness was so great that he never feared to attack even the most unknown person. Scarcely did he let go anyone whom he did not squeeze dry. The father-in-law of my brother, a man at times rather tight-fisted, was fined two crowns. But as for the fact that he tried with great importunity to force me to procure fifteen crowns for him, it is not worth mentioning. Yet at last I noticed the man's impudence and the deceitfulness of his lie, and I denied what he asked no less precisely than I firmly. I solemnly affirm that nothing was paid out from the poor-box. And this must be credited to me, that he did not deceive our deacons. For Vernolius was pressing on his behalf, and I flared up at him because he had foolishly made himself a minister to an impostor. Now when, despairing of me in private, he had asked the brothers for help in common, and had burst into our assembly against my wishes, I answered briefly in the meeting: not only would they not grant him anything in the way of favour, but they did not even wish to take up the deliberation. For it would be far too hateful and unjust, while the outcome of the judgment is still doubtful and the case is pending, to condemn the opposing party by our prejudgment. I have more than ten suitable witnesses, who were present with my consent, and who will affirm that no loan was made to him. Nor could I, while you were here, be brought in any way, by pretence before you, to defraud good men by commending them, though I was helping you. Indeed you remember that I then spoke rather harshly. If it is not even possible to escape false accusations in this way, what should I do? Except that the pain must be soothed by patience. In this I labour, yet I make less progress than I would like. For it does not lightly torment me that I see I have received with applause whatever the wicked have pleased to spew out against me in slander. Certain false rumours are spread, yet not without some colour, because people commonly suppose that a frivolous man of no account, without my support, was not found to have thirty gold pieces or more. But Graverius does not hesitate to boast that our Senate gave him officers to search my house. Indeed it is hard for me not to boil over, being far too emotional. Yet so far no one has heard me raising my voice. But what was the chief thing of all, I lack, namely to be trained by those rods of the Lord into true humility. All the more necessary is it that I be tamed by the chastisements of brothers. This is your duty toward me. For you not only admonish me timidly, but almost soothe me, as if you had no more right over me than what had been granted to you by favour. Indeed I see what you hope for. You judge that I should spare the moroseness that I have contracted from constant troubles. Although your kindness, which springs from love, is pleasing to me, nevertheless I am ashamed that you fear to offend me by your frankness. Farewell, most upright brother. May the Lord enrich you more and more each day with his gifts, and bless your holy labours. Greet the brothers and friends in my name. My colleagues and very many brothers send you their warmest greetings. Geneva, 15th February, 1553.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus vere tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, truly yours.

units.la: CAL: IOANNI CHIKO.
units.tr: Calvin to John Cheke.

units.la: HACTENUS ad te scribere distuli, vir ornatissime, ne aliud appetere forsan viderer, quàm animus meus ferebat. Nam ut fucosæ sunt mundi amicitiæ, atque ut passim regnat ambitio, & vanitas, paucissimi vero sunt, qui synceritatem colant: necesse est, suspectos fere nobis esse, quorum non penitus comperta est probitas. Tandem plusquam legitima scribendi causa visa est, quod cum iam aliquoties ad Regem ipsum ausus fuerim scribere: nihil vnquam ad te dare literarum minime deceat, cuius opera, secundum Dei gratiam factum est, ut mihi aliisque Christi servis ad illum pateret accessus. Ac præteriti quidem temporis facilis est excusatio, quòd initio veritus sum, ne parum sibi haberi fidei putarent, quorum hortatu scribebam, si aliorum opera visus forem in literis offerendis: & tibi quo cum nulla mihi familiaritas intercesserat, molestus esse nolebam. Quòd si quid peccatum est, pudori hoc meo potius, quàm negligentiæ tribuees. Nam cum pridem, & eximiæ tuæ pietatis, & excellentis doctrinæ famæ inductus meritò te coluerim: hæc vna ratio satis tibi conciliat bonorum omnium animos, quòd Regem non modò præstantissimæ indolis, sed etiam maturæ supra ætatem virtutis tuo labore formatum habet Anglia, qui laborantí, imò prorsus afflictæ Dei Ecclesiæ in his miserrimis temporibus manum porrigat. Certè Dominus, cum hoc te honore dignatus est, non eos solum tibi deuinxit, qui præsentem inde fructum capiunt, sed quicunque restitutam cupiunt Ecclesiam Dei, vel saltem collectas eius reliquias. Nunc si, quem diu apud me tacitus aluì, amoris affectum tibi testatum facerem, hoc meum officium tibi non fore ingratum, mihi persuasi. Cæterum, quando neque tu in isto fortunæ splendore priuatis mei similium officiis indiges: & ego tenuitate mea cötentus nihil tibi onerís mei causa impositum esse volo: mutuam inter nos benevolentiam colamus in hac caduca vita, donec in solidum ea fruamur in cœlo. Interim vno consensu studeamus regnum Christi ornare, nare,quantum in nobis est, propagare,& tueri. Videmus enim quàm multi sint palàm infesti hostes,quorum in dies magis crescit furor,& accenditur: ex eorum autem numero, qui nomen Euangelio dederunt, quàm pauci bona fide in asserenda Filij Dei gloria laborent: quàm sit in multis primoribus frigus,vel potius quanta ignauia: quantus denique totius mundi ltupor.
units.tr: I have put off writing to you until now, most distinguished sir, lest I seem to be pursuing something more than my feelings allowed. For worldly friendships are full of pretence, ambition and vanity hold sway everywhere, and very few people cultivate sincerity. So we must nearly always be wary of those whose integrity we have not thoroughly tested. At last, however, a more than adequate reason for writing seemed to present itself: I have already more than once ventured to write to the King himself, and it is not at all fitting that I should never write to you, through whose work, by God's grace, access to him has been opened to me and to other servants of Christ. As for the past, my excuse is easy. At first I feared that people whose urging prompted my letters would not be trusted, if I were seen to be offering letters through the agency of others; and I did not want to be a nuisance to you, with whom I had no intimacy. If I have done wrong here, you should put it down to my modesty rather than to carelessness. For although I have long cultivated you with good reason, drawn by the reputation of your outstanding piety and excellent learning, this one consideration is enough to win the hearts of all good men to you: England has in the King not only a prince of outstanding character but one whose virtue, mature beyond his years, has been formed by your labour, and who stretches out a hand to the God's Church that is labouring, indeed utterly afflicted, in these most wretched times. Certainly, when the Lord has deemed you worthy of this honour, he has bound to you not only those who reap the present fruit from it, but everyone who desires the restored Church of God, or at least its scattered remnants. Now, if I were to show you the affection of love that I have long nursed silently within me, I was persuaded that this duty of mine would not be unwelcome to you. Yet since you, in that brilliance of fortune, do not need the services of private persons such as me, and I, content with my meagreness, want nothing to be laid upon you on account of my burden, let us cultivate mutual goodwill in this fleeting life, until we enjoy it in full in heaven. Meanwhile, with one accord, let us strive to adorn the kingdom of Christ, to spread it as far as in us lies, and to defend it. For we see how many open enemies there are, whose fury grows and is kindled more every day; and of those who have given their name to the Gospel, how few labour in good faith to assert the glory of the Son of God; how much coldness, or rather how great indolence, there is among many leading men; and, finally, how great the stupor of the whole world is.

units.la: Quanquam autem adeò te voluntarium esse existimo, vt alienis stimulis minimè indigeas: quæ tamen humanitas tua est,nó dubito quin tibi familiariter hæc à me proponi, boni consulas, quæ sibi vnumquenque nostrûm assiduè suggerere conuenit. Id verò abs te nominatim peto,vt si quando Regem sereniffimum censueris meis exhortationibus excitari posse, monere, & ex re præsenti consilium dare ne grauęris. Vale præstantissime vir, & mihi ex animo colendę. Dominus te suo præsidio tueatur, Spiritu suo gubernare pergat, & sanctis tuis laboribus benedicere.
units.tr: Although I think you so willing that you need no outside spurs, still, since this is your kindness, I do not doubt that you will graciously take what I put before you here as a familiar matter, the kind of thing each of us ought constantly to remind himself of. What I ask of you by name is this: if at any time you judge that the most serene King can be stirred by my exhortations, please do not hesitate to advise me and to give counsel in the present situation. Farewell, most excellent sir, and be cherished by me from my heart. May the Lord keep you under his protection, continue to govern you by his Spirit, and bless your holy labours.

units.la: Geneuæ, Idibus Februarij. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Geneva, the Ides of February, 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETINGS.

units.la: Vum nuper extremis amici officiis erga te defunctus, vt mihi quidem videbar, quòd residuum instabat doloris nimis maturo discessu effugere optassem: tantæ festinationis quam merebar, pœnam dedi. Atque vtinam solus dedissem. Sed hoc aliquanto deterius fuit, quòd eodem complures bonos mœrore mecum implicui. Nunc tamen lætiore nuncio recreatus, stultitiam & pudorem meum obliuiscor. Et certè dignum est hoc singulare Dei beneficium, quod omnem tristitiæ materiam absorbeat. Nunc postquam morbo leuatus es, danda erit opera,vt animi vigorem, quem inter grauissimos conflictus nimis strenuè exercuisti, & corporis vires, quas prorsus collapsas fractasque esse oportet, paulatim recolligas. Faxit Dominus quando te ante tempus sepeliui, vt te mihi superstitem videat Ecclesia. In hac precatione cum publico fidelium bono coniuncta est priuata mea vtilitas: quia & breuior erit militiæ meæ cursus, & à morte tua deflenda eximar. Neque tamen interea, si ita Domino videbitur, tibi tandiu prorogari vitæ finem recusò, vt adhuc decennij labor mihi accedat. Cæterùm modò sic Christo viuamus, vt quotidie etiam parati simus illi mori, quid de nobis futurum sit, securos agere decet. Nunc solùm curandæ valetudini incumbe, vt breui conualescas. Quàm multi amici te salutent, frater melius ore exponet. Vale frater integerrime. Dominus qui te præter, spem nostram Ecclesiæ suæ restituit, de Satana & impiis per te semper triumphet. Symmystis & aliis plurimam salutem. Geneuæ, VI. Calendas Aprilis. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Since you were recently at death's door through your devotion to your friends, and it seemed to me that the rest of your grief was pressing on me, I had hoped to escape the grief of too early a departure. I paid the penalty for my haste, as I deserved. If only I alone had paid it! But it turned out worse, because I involved many good men in my sorrow as well. Now, however, I am refreshed by happier news, and I forget my foolishness and shame. Certainly this singular blessing of God deserves to swallow up every cause of sadness. Now that you have been relieved of your illness, care must be taken that you gradually recover the vigour of mind that you exercised too vigorously amid the most serious conflicts, and the strength of your body, which must be entirely broken and weakened. May the Lord grant that, since I buried you before your time, the Church may see you outlive me. In this prayer my own private advantage is joined with the public good of the faithful: for my course of service will be shorter, and I shall be spared from mourning your death. Yet in the meantime, if the Lord so wills, I do not refuse that your life be prolonged for so long that another decade of labour may be added to mine. Moreover, we should live in Christ in such a way that we are ready every day to die for him, and it becomes us to be untroubled about what will become of us. For now, devote yourself only to restoring your health, so that you may soon regain your strength. How many friends greet you, our brother will explain more fully by word of mouth. Farewell, most upright brother. May the Lord, who beyond our hope has restored you to his Church, always triumph through you over Satan and the wicked. Greetings in abundance to our fellow ministers and the others. Geneva, 27 March 1553.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus verè tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, truly yours.

units.la: CALVINUS VIRETO. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO VIRET, GREETINGS.

units.la: CVM Matthæus noster Bernam proficiscatur, ex eo audies. Quia videbam hominem tam iniquè variis modis tractari: non ausus sum vehementius dehortari à suscepto consilio. Negare etiam non potui, quin commendationem abs te peterë, quam vltrò daturus esses. Neque enim causa, tua suffragatione indigna est: & pro tua humanitate ostendere voles, eum à te in rebus suis miseris non contemni. Itaque mihi satis est, ut homini obsequar, vno te verbo monuisse. Cardinalis Bellaius hac trahens Paguetum misit, qui me accersseret. Non sum tunc domi repertus. Quieuit illè: puto quòd nō magnopere colloquium meum appeteret. Pagueto dixit, de fratribus nostris Bernatcs non impe tralle, quia Connestabilem prætereiunt. Spem facere melioris exitus visus est, si ad novas preces accederet illa commendatio. Ego verò metuum esse ludibrium arbitror. Nam Connestabilis antea rogatus, blando responso ipsos derisit, vt nosti. Quòd ta-men visum fuerit, aliquid rursus tentare: suppliciū eorum differri mandauit, donec alpes transisset. Senatum, meo iudicio, admoneri non erit inutile, vt inde consilium capiat: ne videamur fratrum salutem negligentius curasse. Reliqua in tuum aduentū. Vale frater integerrime. Saluta vxorem & filiolas diligenter meo nomine. Dominus vos tueatur, & Spiritu suo regere pergat. Geneuæ, VIII. Maij. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Since our Matthew is setting out for Berne, you will hear about it from him. Because I saw that the man was being treated so unjustly in various ways, I did not dare to dissuade him strongly from his chosen plan. Nor could I refuse to ask you for a letter of recommendation, which you would have offered of your own accord. For the cause is not unworthy of your support, and by your kindness you will want to show that he is not being despised by you in his wretched circumstances. So it is enough for me to comply with the man's wish, having advised you in a single word. Cardinal Bellay, dragging Paget along with these matters, sent him to summon me. I was not found at home. He kept quiet; I think he did not much desire a conversation with me. He said to Paget that our brothers of Berne could not obtain anything, because they bypass the Constable. It seemed to him that there was hope of a better outcome if that recommendation were added to fresh requests. But I think it is a mockery. For the Constable, when asked earlier, mocked them with a flattering reply, as you know. Nevertheless, since it seemed right to try something again, he ordered that their punishment be deferred until he had crossed the Alps. In my judgement it will not be useless to advise the Senate, so that it may take counsel from this; lest we seem to have been negligent in caring for the safety of the brothers. The rest I leave until your arrival. Farewell, most upright brother. Greet your wife and little daughters diligently in my name. May the Lord keep you and continue to rule you by his Spirit. Geneva, 8 May 1553.

units.la: FARELLVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: FAREL TO CALVIN, GREETINGS.

units.la: FVi Bernæ, quò me fratres ire iusserunt reluctatem, vt aliquibus flagitantibus Pastorem obtineremus, omnes probabant quod petebam. Si Christus propitius fauerit misericordiam, fiet aliquid alioqui spei nihil affulget. Vereor ne mihi contingat quod iis qui suaseniores clarigiti sunt iunioribus, qui pro gratia, gravestifunt oculis eorum de quibus bene meriti sunt. Scortum R. quod tam male audiuit ob anteactam vitam, ne quid dicam de morte mariti (nescio an ei liceat intrare solum Bernensem) egit, vt scis, non procul istinc apud Pontificios velut defectrix ab Euangelio: & puellam quam habebat iam initiatam Euangelio, & quæ fuit particeps Cœnæ D. elocauit viro infesto doctrinæ Christi: & ita locata puella defecit ab Euangelio sequē adiunxit Pōtificiis, & eorum scelestis sacris. Et cum hic agat, rogata fuit num vellet vale dicere Antichristo, & ad Euangelium redire, ac perpetuo in eo viuere. Respondit, oportere vt virum sequeretur, & viuere pro more eorum apud quos ageret. Haec fassa non se victuram iuxta Euangelium, peperit puellam. Alia puellae voluit natam offerre baptizandam. Ego respondi non admittendam, quod in foedere non sit cum neuter parens fidelis sit, neque in Ecclesia Christi agat & admittatur: nec posse nos quenquam intingere nisi fuerit in foedere: aioque R. id nunc velle in ruinam Ecclesiae moliri, quod olim pater, qui erronis filium voluit offerre intingendum, ex iis scilicet quos Aegyptios vocant. Cumque videret me adigente patrem erronem ad abnegadam omnem impietatem in qua vixerat, & stipulante vt iuxta Euangelium posthac viueret, & insuper cum vrgerem leuantes puerum, vt plene prouinciam eius suscipèrant patre consentiente, & filium permittente & cedente, si non viueret ex praescripto Euangelij: Praefectus ferre actione hanc non potuit, sed cum loqui vellet, reprehensus exiuit. Ita filia nunc turbare Ecclesiam vult indebita Baptismi administratione. Collega subdit auiam esse in foedere & suscipere filiolae curam, & quandiu viuet, daturam se operam, vt in Euangelio viuat: & quod sit in foedere palam esse, quia excepta sit ab Ecclesia, & admissa ad Coenam. Quare si vernae & emptitij, qui in aedibus erant Abrahami ad Circumcisionem admittebantur, multo magis hac, quae in aedibus auiae nata est. Ego ludi hic Ecclesiam affirmo. Scilicet mater quae filiam mancipauit Satanae, sub quo ea fatetur se victuram, & non sub Euangelio, dabit operam vt quam minus habet charam, formetur in Euangelio? det primum specimen in filia quam perdidit, reducat eam. Quod autem attinet ad receptionem auiae, ego pernego me vnquam in eam sententiam venisse neque venturum, nisi aliud cernam in ea: neque probo collegae factum, qui suo more non veretur profanare omnia, & improbissimos velle admittere cogit. Et quod attinet ad eos qui cum eo faciunt, res ita habet & quanto iniquior est tanto plausibilior. Nam siue ex Turcis siue ex Iudaeis vel quibusfuis puer offeratur, & quicquid est eiusmodi, intingi iubserent. Quare insolentia eorum magis cohibenda venit, quam fouenda.
units.tr: I was at Berne, where the brothers ordered me to go, though I was reluctant, so that with some of them urging it we might obtain a minister. All approved what I asked. If Christ mercifully favours it, something will happen; otherwise no hope shines forth. I fear that what happens to those who have been advised by the elders to be younger men, who for kindness are heavy in the eyes of those they have served well, may befall me. The harlot R., who had a very bad reputation because of her past life, not to mention the death of her husband (I do not know whether she is allowed to enter the Bernese territory alone), acted, as you know, not far from there among the Papists, as one who had defected from the Gospel. And the girl she had, already initiated into the Gospel and who had shared in the Lord's Supper, she let out to a husband hostile to the teaching of Christ; and the girl, so placed, defected from the Gospel and joined the Papists and their wicked rites. And since she lives here, she was asked whether she would say farewell to Antichrist, return to the Gospel and live in it for ever. She replied that she ought to follow her husband and live according to the custom of those among whom she dwelt. Confessing that she would not live according to the Gospel, she bore a daughter. She wished to present another girl of hers for baptism. I replied that she should not be admitted, since neither parent is in the covenant, neither is faithful, nor do they live and are admitted in the Church of Christ; nor can we baptize anyone who is not in the covenant. I say that R. now wishes to undermine the Church with the same ruin that the father once tried to bring about when he wanted to present the son of a harlot for baptism, namely from those whom they call Egyptians. And when he saw that I was urging the father, a vagabond, to renounce all the impiety in which he had lived, and was requiring that he henceforth live according to the Gospel, and moreover, when I pressed those who lifted the child to take the child's charge fully upon themselves, the father consenting and the son permitting and yielding, if he did not live according to the rule of the Gospel, the prefect could not bear the action, but when he wished to speak he was rebuked and went out. So now the daughter wants to disturb the Church by an improper administration of baptism. The colleague adds that the grandmother is within the covenant and undertakes the care of the little girl, and as long as she lives she will take pains that the child live in the Gospel; and that it is plainly within the covenant, because she has been received by the Church and admitted to the Supper. Therefore, if the home-born slaves and purchased servants who were in Abraham's house were admitted to circumcision, much more so should this child be admitted, who was born in the house of her grandmother. I affirm that here the Church is being mocked. Surely the mother who handed her daughter over to Satan, under whom she confesses she will live and not under the Gospel, will take pains that the child she values less be formed in the Gospel? Let her first give a sample in the daughter she has lost; let her bring her back. As for the admission of the grandmother, I firmly deny that I ever came to that opinion or will come to it, unless I see something else in her. Nor do I approve of the colleague's action, who, in his usual way, does not hesitate to profane everything and compels the most wicked to be admitted. As for those who side with him, the matter stands thus: the more unjust it is, the more plausible it becomes. For whether a child is offered from among the Turks, the Jews, or any other people, and whatever is of that kind, they would order baptism. Therefore their insolence should be restrained rather than fostered.

units.la: Quod attinet ad Abrahamum & vernas ipsius, dent micam fidei tanti serui D. in tam vili mancipio Satanae, quod tunc Ecclesiam adeo horrende foedauit vt stupendum sit. In Gallia quid no egit, vnde Euangelium male audiret suis scortationibus & diuortiis? Adde quod iudices omnes laici cum non possent eam conciliare viro, vbi iusta ferri debebat Ecclesiae excomunicatio, ausi sunt eam ab omnibus Ecclesiis excommunicare, sibi vsurpates quod non licebat. Sit vana actio, tamen quod iusta infligi debebat, vbi soluitur? Soluta est, ait aliquis, dum admissa fuit ad Coenam: nego id legitime factum. Sed quis audiuit vnquam Abrahamum aliquem ex suis mancipasse sacrilegiis idololatrarum, & rursus perseuerantem in impietate in aedes suas admisisse, & infidelis prolem tentasse circumcidere? Actum est cum fratribus: qui reparum expensa, pars suasit intingendam puellam, pars confulen das esse Ecclesias, pars non intingendam. Sed mira contentione collega egit & aliqui secum. Non pauci tantum quod vulgus ait nemini denegandum Baptismum petenti. Rogabam qua ratione puella munda esset: num patris? is prorsus est impius. Num matris? at illa defecit a Christo, & in ea defectione pergit. Cum ergo immunda sit, quis nisi maledictum incurrens mundam affirmabit? Et ut videas pietatem auiae, cum collega decreuisset scitari de fide ipsius, & astringere arctius ad procurandum ne vnquam puella adduceretur in papismum: illa resciens, adiit improbum Plebanum, qui dignus erat Deum Pontificium perpetuo euocare: ac se non ita miscere piis debebat. Habuit leuantes Pontificios & insuper milites & apud aliam Ecclesiam, quam hanc voluit intingi. Sane video collegam nimis praefractum, & plus sibi quam par fit tribuentem, Facile huic erit omnia efficere per Consistorium, si aliud non videam. D. nobis adsit. Tu cum fratribus tuum iudicium indicabis & aliud non addes quam sententiam. Rogabam Musculum de hac re Bernae & item Hallerum, ut hic nihil respondit nisi quod collaturus esset aliis, ita ille iussit ut tuum haberem iudicium, quod ei subindicarem tandem. Vale. Non molestę feras, quod tam ingrata scribam, leviora non habeo nunc. Faxit Christus ut meliora audiamus, ut feruntur aliquot episcopi admisisse Pastores Euangelicos, & iam non se cornutos episcopos, sed duces principesque dicere. Neocomi decimoquarto Iulij. M. D. LIII. Saluta pios omnes.
units.tr: As for Abraham and his servants, let them show a crumb of the faith of that great servant of God in so vile a bondage to Satan, which at that time defiled the Church so horribly that it is astonishing. What did she not do in France, by which the Gospel was ill spoken of because of her fornications and divorces? Add that all the lay judges, since they could not reconcile her to her husband, where the due excommunication of the Church ought to have been brought, dared to excommunicate her from all the churches, usurping what was not lawful for them. Even if the action is vain, yet what ought to have been justly inflicted, where is it dissolved? "It was dissolved," someone says, "when she was admitted to the Supper." I deny that this was done lawfully. But who has ever heard of Abraham handing over any of his household to the sacrileges of idolaters, and then, when they persisted in impiety, admitting them to his house and trying to circumcise the offspring of an unbeliever? The matter was discussed with the brothers: some, weighing the expense of repairs, advised that the girl be baptized, some that the churches be consulted, some that she not be baptized. But the colleague argued with remarkable obstinacy, and some with him. Not a few, as the common people say, held that baptism must not be denied to anyone who asks for it. I asked by what reasoning the girl was clean: is it by the father? He is utterly impious. By the mother? But she has defected from Christ and persists in that defection. Since, then, she is unclean, who, unless he incurs a curse, will affirm that she is clean? And so you may see the grandmother's piety: when the colleague had decided to inquire about her faith, and to bind her more tightly to take care that the girl would never be brought to Papism, she, learning of it, went to the wicked parish priest, who deserved to be called away for ever from the Papist god, and she ought not to have mixed herself so with the godly. She had Papists as sponsors, and besides soldiers, and she wanted the child baptized in another church rather than this one. Indeed I see that the colleague is too stubborn, and assigns himself more than is fitting. It will be easy for him to carry everything through the Consistory, unless I see otherwise. May the Lord be with us. You, with the brothers, will state your judgement and add nothing but your opinion. I asked Musculus about this matter at Berne, and likewise Haller; as the one replied only that he would confer with others, so the other ordered that I should have your judgement, which I should at last report to him. Farewell. Do not be annoyed that I write such unpleasant things; I have nothing lighter now. May Christ grant that we hear better news, such as that some bishops are said to have admitted evangelical ministers, and no longer call themselves horned bishops, but leaders and princes. Neuchâtel, 14 July 1553. Greet all the godly.

units.la: CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETING.

units.la: VTinam, mi Farelle, aptius malis tuis remedium inuenire possem quam hic tibi afferre cogito. Sed cum tu minime ignores, multa nobis esse toleranda, quae corrigere non liceat: pluribus verbis te non hortabor, ut te in certamine non pugnes hostili mansuetum moderatumque praebeas. Si tamen hoc vocari certamen debet, cum abs te Collega sine odio & tu multuandi libidine difficile: nitit. Quid in eo desiderem, quia tum hi optimus es testis, in praesentia non refero. Pium tamen esse hominem, & officij sui studiosum, cognoscimus. Huc accedit quod non modò te amat, séque tibi probari cupit, sed patris loco habet ac reueretur. Cur autem proteruius interdum se gerat, quàm par est, hæc mihi præcipua esse videtur ratio: quòd dum te nimis rigidum & morosum esse iudicat, popularitatem nescio quam affectat, quæ offensis medeatur. Ita bonus vir, dum vult consultum esse quieti tuæ, inuidiámque declinat, cui sustinendæ vos fo re pares difsidit, nec constantiam grauitatémque retinet Christi ministro dignam; & dum necessitatem resistendi tibi imponit, improbis arma suppeditat, quibus ministerium commune oppugnent. Quàm hæc odiosa res sit & acerba video: nec me latet, quantum reprehensionis mereatur eius vitium. Sed æquitatis ac prudentiæ tuæ est ex aduerso colligere, quæ ad subleuandam eius culpam valent. Si immodica confidentia exultat, scis tamen eam nullo malitiæ veneno aspersam: si qua peruicacia laborat, nihil tamen illi minus propositum, quàm Ecclesiam turbare, vel ex fratrum contemptu triumphum agere. Cur ergo non ignosceres eius imprudentiæ? Capunculum tulisti, non modò nihili hominem, sed qui ad lites natus totum Ecclesiæ ordinem insano saltu calcabat, qui virulentis cauillis impudenter eructare studebat quicquid rectè & ordine compositum foret, qui fatali quodam genio non minus quàm rabioso impetu ferebatur ad nocendum, qui data opera factiosos omnes stimulabat in Ecclesiæ perniciem. Quanto igitur magis fouendæ cum eo homine pacis habenda tibi ratio est, qui & tecum Domino fideliter seruire cupit, & ab hostilibus dissidiis abhorret? Quanquam non modò pax tibi cum eo alenda est, sed amicitia colenda. Nam si reputas, quàm pauci hodie sint tolerabiles ministri, hunc & probum & diligentem, & aliis dotibus laude dignis instructum minimè aspernaberis. Cæterum vt offensionem abs te hactenus cō ceptam silétio tegere forte expediet, ita in posterum si quid peccet, liberè cum eo expostulare præstabit: modò ne in dissidium res erumpat. Modò se amari intelligat, eum mediocriter, vt speroq, morigerum habebis. Proximo Sabbatho Lugduni exustus est mercator, qui mira constantia & pari moderatione ad suppli- cium perrexit: cum modis omnibus ad defectionem impellere ipsum cognati & populares tentarent. Mater etiam ter genibus eius aduoluta, flens supplicíter precata, vt vitæ suæ parceret, nihil obtinuit. Passim in Gallia sequiunt. Sed in Belsia præsertim vexatur nobilitas. Vale integerrime frater, & mihi verè obseruande. Dominus te Spiritu suo regere pergat, diúque seruet incolumem. Saluta fratrem tuum & amicos. Geneuæ, xIIII. Calend. Augusti. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: I wish, my Farel, that I could find a remedy better suited to your troubles than the one I am about to offer you. But since you are well aware that we must endure many things which we are not permitted to correct, I will not urge you at length to be gentle and moderate in this dispute, and not to fight in a hostile spirit. If indeed it ought to be called a dispute, since your colleague, without hatred, and you, without any desire for strife, struggle with difficulty. What I miss in him, you yourself are the best witness, so I shall not mention it for now. Yet we know that he is a godly man and zealous in his duty. Moreover, he not only loves you and wishes to be approved by you, but regards you as a father and reveres you. As for why he sometimes behaves more wantonly than is fitting, the chief reason seems to me to be this: while he judges you too stern and severe, he aims at a certain popularity, I know not what, by which he may heal offences. So this good man, wanting to secure your peace and avoiding unpopularity, which he doubts you two could bear together, does not keep the steadfastness and gravity worthy of a minister of Christ; and while he forces upon you the need to resist, he supplies wicked men with weapons to attack the common ministry. I see how hateful and bitter this matter is, and I am not unaware how much blame his fault deserves. But it is for your fairness and prudence to weigh, on the other side, what helps to lessen his fault. If he is carried away by an excessive confidence, you know that it is not tainted with any poison of malice; if he labours under some obstinacy, he has no purpose less than to disturb the Church or to triumph over the contempt of his brethren. Why then would you not pardon his lack of judgement? You have taken on a little nobody, but one who, born for quarrels, trampled the whole order of the Church with a reckless leap, who shamelessly strove to belch out venomous jibes at whatever was rightly and orderly arranged, who was driven to harm by a certain fatal spirit no less than by a raging impulse, who deliberately stirred up all the factious men to the ruin of the Church. How much more, then, must you consider how to keep peace with a man who desires to serve the Lord faithfully along with you, and who shrinks from hostile dissensions? Indeed, you must not only maintain peace with him but cultivate friendship. For if you consider how few ministers today are tolerable, you will by no means despise this one, who is both upright and diligent and endowed with other gifts worthy of praise. Moreover, though it may be expedient to hide under silence the offence you have so far conceived, in future, if he does wrong, it will be better to remonstrate with him frankly, provided the matter does not break out into dissension. Only let him understand that he is loved, and you will have him, as I hope, moderately compliant. Last Sabbath at Lyon a merchant was burned, who went to his punishment with remarkable constancy and equal moderation, although his relatives and fellow-citizens tried every means to drive him to recant. His mother, too, throwing herself at his knees three times, weeping, begged him humbly to spare his life, but obtained nothing. Similar things follow everywhere in France. But the nobility is especially harassed in Belsia. Farewell, most upright brother, and truly to be revered by me. May the Lord continue to guide you by his Spirit and keep you safe for many years. Greet your brother and friends. Geneva, 14th before the Calends of August, 1553.

units.la: Gratia tibi & pax à Deo Patre nostro & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: QVod de causa apud vos dubia sententiam nostram rogas frater & Symmysta in Domino venerande. Liceatne ordinis nostri ministris, qui puram Euangelij doctrinam profitentur ad Baptismum admittere infantem, cuius pater ab Ecclesiis nostris alienus est: mater vero ad Papatum defecit: ita vt parentes ambo sint papistæ, ita respondendum censuimus. Absurdum esse vt eos baptizemus, qui corporis nostri membra censeri nequeunt. Quum in hoc ordine sint Papistarum liberi, quomodo Baptismum illis administrare liceat, non videmus. Accedit etiam altera ratio. Stipulamur enim ab iis qui offerunt, vt adultos erudiant in ea fide, in qua baptizatur. Si nemo fideiubeat, profanari Baptismum certum est. Si vero promittant fideiussores quod non est in eorum potestate, palam luditur Deus, praesertim si hoc notum sit, non serio sed tantum defunctorie promittendo. Nam si astute fallunt, culpa vacuus est minister. Cæterum minimè dubitamus non alios esse idoneos sponsores, nisi penes quos sit præstandi facultas, hoc est, qui infantem habituri sint in sua potestate, vel qui patris aut matris rogatu fidem suam Ecclesiæ obligent. Sed præcipuam in eo difficultatem vobis esse intelligimus, quòd auia, pro matre Baptismum nepoti suo vel nepti petiisse dicitur. Nam quum Dominus gratiam suam in multas ætates extendat, eam astringere non est nostrum. Et certè locum hic habet vulgaris regula: fauores esse ampliandos. Sed duo consideranda sunt. An auia in se recipit infantis educationem, idque faciat iure suo, vt caueatur Ecclesiæ in grege manserit qui cooptatur. Neque enim in auiæ gratiam baptizandus erit nepos, in quem nihil habebit ipsa iuris, & qui alienus erit ab eius familia. Circuncisio nō tantùm vernis Abrahæ, sed emptitiis quoque seruis communis fuit: ad Loth verò non peruenit, qui ex eius domo migrauerat. Deinde videndum an ipsa quoque auia membrum sit corporis nostri, & in coetu piorum locum obtineat. Mulierem designas quæ si apud nos habitaret, quia tamen filiam elocauit extra Ecclesiam, & quantùm in se fuit, abdicauit à piorum communione, hac vna perfidia se priuauit iure sponsionis, ne audienda sit cùm de Baptismo agitur. Certè si vigeret legitima disciplina, excommunicatione digna erat quæ Ecclesiâ oue vna fraudauit. Quòd si culpam agnoscens poenitentiam suam hoc modo testatam faceret, factum saltem qui ex coniugio perperam contractonatus est, in matris locum vobis reliquit, sed forte fortè repudiare æquum non esset. Verùm quia nihil tale præ se fert, quin potius ut impura est ac profana mulier, ita tota suam sobolem prostituere Satanæ parat: est, nimiæ socordiæ fuerit Baptismum aperto eius ludibrio à nobis exponi. Certè quæ Ecclesiæ communione indigna est, multò minus potest aliis patefacere in eam aditum. Vale eximie vir, ac frater noster plurimùm observande. Symmystis tuis pluri-am salutem nostro nomine dices, nósque eorum precibus commendabis. Dominus vobis adsit, Spiritu suo vos gubernet, manúque sua tueatur. Genevæ, xvi. Calend. Augusti. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Since you ask our opinion on a matter in doubt among you, brother and fellow-minister, venerable in the Lord, we have judged that this answer should be given: whether ministers of our order, who profess the pure doctrine of the gospel, may admit to baptism an infant whose father is alien to our churches and whose mother has defected to the Papacy, so that both parents are papists. It is absurd that we should baptize those who cannot be counted members of our body. Since in this condition they are children of papists, we do not see how baptism may be administered to them. There is also another reason. For we require of those who present the child that they instruct him, when grown, in the faith in which he is baptized. If no one stands surety, it is certain that baptism is profaned. If sponsors promise what is not within their power, God is plainly mocked, especially if it is known that they promise not in earnest but merely as a formality. For if they deceive by craft, the minister is free of blame. But we have no doubt that other sponsors are suitable, namely those in whose power it lies to fulfil the obligation, that is, those who will have the infant in their charge, or who, at the request of the father or mother, pledge their faith to the Church. But we understand that the chief difficulty for you is that a grandmother is said to have asked for baptism for her grandson or granddaughter in place of the mother. For since the Lord extends his grace over many generations, it is not for us to restrict it. And certainly the common rule applies here: favours should be enlarged. But two things must be considered. First, whether the grandmother takes on the upbringing of the child herself, and does so by her own right, so that it may be ensured that the one to be admitted remains in the flock of the Church. For the grandson is not to be baptized for the grandmother's sake, since she will have no right over him and he will be alien to her household. Circumcision was common not only to the born slaves of Abraham but also to slaves bought with money; yet it did not reach Lot, who had migrated from his house. Second, it must be considered whether the grandmother herself is a member of our body and holds a place in the assembly of the godly. You describe a woman who, if she lived among us, would, because she has given her daughter in marriage outside the Church, and as far as she was concerned has renounced communion with the godly, have deprived herself by this one treachery of the right to stand as sponsor, so that she is not to be heard when baptism is under discussion. Certainly, if lawful discipline were in force, she would deserve excommunication, having defrauded the Church of one sheep. But if, acknowledging her fault, she showed her repentance in this way, the child born of a wrongly contracted marriage would at least have left you a place for her as mother; yet perhaps it would not be right to reject her outright. However, since she shows nothing of the kind, but rather, as an impure and profane woman, is preparing to hand over her whole offspring to Satan, it would be excessive carelessness for us to expose baptism to her open mockery. Certainly one who is unworthy of communion with the Church can much less open the way into it for others. Farewell, most excellent man and brother, greatly to be respected. Give my greetings in our name to your fellow-ministers, and commend us to their prayers. May the Lord be with you, govern you by his Spirit, and keep you under his hand. Geneva, 16th before the Calends of August, 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETINGS

units.la: Gitius eram scripturus, nisi me spes adventus tui quam literæ tuæ fecerant, haftenus tenuisset. Nunc longior mora vel mutatum abs te consilium esse arguit, vel aliquid quod pro sectione tuæ obstiterit, accidisse. Atqui hoc quidem posterius mallem, modo ne quid triste sit & adversum: deinde non nisi ad brevem tempus te impediat. Verùm quod nollem prope suspicari cogor, non eundem qui tunc fuit, hodie tibi manere animum. Equidem hîc falli cupio: etsi ita est, errorem meum extemplò refellere in tua potestate est: quod ut facias vehementer rogo. Si tibi factam à me iniuriam queraris, ego libenter culpam deprecabor: aut si rigidior fueris, poenam quam statues luere nō abnuam. Solùm aduentu tuo quæ nos adhuc suspensos tenet, dubitationem exime. Nec verò me fugit quàm multa isthic quotidie dici soleant ad turbandum quod cœperas consilium: quàm multa etiam tibi ultro venire in mentem potuerint. Verùm si meo consilio, aut saltem precibus obtemperas, duo abs te impetrare velim, ne te vanorum hominum blanditiis lactandum præbeas, sed potius in te defecendens conscientiam intus propriam roges quidnam facto sit opus. Deinde ne alium tibi iudicem vel arbitrum statuas, quàm Deum ipsum. Video enim quas sibi delitias faciant permulti, ac præsertim ordinis tui homines. Quanquam autem ex eorum numero te esse non arbitror, qui suis deliciis inebriati secure sibi indulgent, non videtur tamen superuacua monitio, ne forte per incuriam obrepat torpor, ut acrius tibi & sedulius insistes. Quòd nuper multorum animi spe nescio qua erecti sunt, vtinam firma esset ratio: Si quos iuuat multa sibi de nihilo promittere, voluntario eorum errori non invideo. Tibi vero denuntio, nisi sponte falli vis, non esse cur ista temere passim concepta opinio te moretur. Iam si migrandi tempus nondum esse maturum putas: saltem mensem vnum quo nos inuisas, futuri licet. Certè præstat semel coràm in sermonem venire, quàm
units.tr: I would have written earlier, but the hope of your arrival, which your letter had raised, held me back until now. This longer delay suggests either that you have changed your plan or that something has arisen to hinder your departure. Yet I would rather it were the latter, provided nothing sad or adverse is involved; and in any case it would hold you back only for a short time. But what I am almost forced to suspect, I would not wish to suspect: that your mind today is not the same as it was then. Indeed, I wish to be mistaken here; but even if it is so, it is in your power to refute my error at once, and I earnestly ask you to do so. If you complain that I have done you an injury, I will gladly beg your pardon; or if you have been more severe, I will not refuse the punishment you decide to impose. Only by your arrival, remove the doubt that keeps us still in suspense. Nor am I unaware how many things are said there every day to disturb the plan you had begun, and how many thoughts may have come to you of their own accord. But if you obey my counsel, or at least my prayers, I would wish you to grant me two things: that you not allow yourself to be puffed up by the flattery of vain men, but rather that you withdraw into yourself and ask your own conscience what must be done. Next, that you do not set up as your judge or arbiter anyone other than God himself. For I see what delights very many men make for themselves, and especially men of your order. Although I do not think you belong to the number of those who, drunk with their pleasures, indulge themselves in security, still this warning does not seem superfluous, lest sloth creep in through carelessness, so that you may press on more keenly and diligently. As to the fact that the spirits of many have lately been raised by some hope or other, I wish the reasoning behind it were sound. If it pleases some to promise themselves much from nothing, I do not begrudge them their voluntary error. But I warn you: unless you wish to be deceived of your own accord, there is no reason why that opinion, rashly conceived and spread everywhere, should hold you back. Now, if you think the time for departure is not yet ripe, at least allow us to see you for one month, even if it is to be in the future. Certainly it is better to come into conversation face to face once than

units.la: r.j. agitare per litteras, de quibus vix vnquam probè disceptabitur, donec in rem præsentem ventum fuerit. Simul tamen memineris, si alimentis mature prospicitur, & damni infecti cautio moram nullam admittit, minus esse in hac causa procrastinandum. Vale eximie vir & mihi plurimùm honorande. Dominus tibi sem per adsit, Spiritu prudentiæ & fortitudinis te gubernet, gressus tuos regat in gloriam nominis sui. Amen. v i i r. Calend. Augusti.
units.tr: to debate by letters matters that can scarcely ever be properly settled until we come to the thing itself. At the same time, remember that if provision for maintenance is made promptly, and the security against loss admits no delay, there should be less postponement in this matter. Farewell, distinguished sir and most honoured brother. May the Lord always be with you, may he govern you with the Spirit of prudence and fortitude, and direct your steps to the glory of his name. Amen. On the seventh day before the Kalends of August.

units.la: M. D. LIII.
CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETINGS

units.la: QVæ nuper ego ad te priuatim, & quæ simul cum Symmy-lis meis ad te scripsi, in bonam partem abs te accepta esse, vt omnia nostra æqui bonique cófulere soles, gaudeo. Faxit Dominus, vt iunioribus cófiliis parere discant, quibus multa inconsiderate efluunt: & tua moderatione concordiam foueas, quam paruis interdum dissidiis labefactare conatur Satan. Franciscus vester, cum iam ad discessum paratus foret, rogauit an vellem illuc scribere. A Fallesio redibat. Hortari vt punctum temporis maneret, ideo nolui, quia nec spes erat aliqua profectus, & hominem præfractum à suscepto consilio deducere, non ita facile erat. De morte Regis Angliæ incerti primùm rumores volitabant. Postea certiores quàm vellem subinde nuncij sunt sequuti. Successit in regnum consobrina ordinum suffragiis. Metuitur tamen seditio. Verissimum est quod dicis incomparabili thesauro priuatam esse terram illam, quo indigna erat. Equidem ita statuo, vnius pupilli morte totam gentem optimo patre esse orbatam. Breui forte audiemus, vt res habeant. Nostrū tamen est, in patientia animas nostras possidere. Vale frater integerrime. Saluta Collegam & reliquos Symmyftas, fratremque Claudium. Dominus vobis semper adsit, vos gubernet ac labores vestros benedicat. Collegæ mei tibi plurimam salutem dicunt. Idem etiam amici. Vale iterum. Geneuæ, v i i. Augusti.
units.tr: I am glad that what I recently wrote to you privately, and what I wrote to you together with my colleagues, has been taken by you in good part, as you are accustomed to interpret all our words in a fair and kindly sense. May the Lord grant that the younger men learn to obey counsels, by which many things slip out thoughtlessly; and may you foster concord by your moderation, which Satan sometimes tries to shake with small disagreements. Your Francis, when he was already prepared to leave, asked whether I wished to write there. He was returning from Fallais. I did not wish him to remain even a moment to urge it, because there was no hope of any progress, and it was not easy to turn a headstrong man from the course he had undertaken. Rumours about the death of the King of England at first flew about uncertainly. Afterwards more certain messengers followed, sooner than I would have wished. The king's cousin succeeded to the kingdom by the votes of the orders. Yet sedition is feared. It is most true, as you say, that that land has been given over to a private person, with an incomparable treasure of which it was unworthy. For my part I judge that by the death of one boy the whole nation has been bereaved of an excellent father. Perhaps we shall soon hear how matters stand. Yet it is ours to possess our souls in patience. Farewell, most upright brother. Greet my colleague and the rest of my colleagues, and brother Claude. The Lord be always with you, guard you and bless your labours. My colleagues send you very many greetings. So do the friends. Farewell again. At Geneva, on the seventh day before the Kalends of August.

units.la: M. D. LIII.
CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETINGS

units.la: EST vt dicis mi Farelle. Quanuis multis tempestatibus variè & duriter iactemur: quia tamen nauem qua vehimur, nauclerus gubernat, qui ne in mediis quidem naufragiis perire vnquam nos sinet: non est cur metu vel tædio mentes nostræ obruantur. Iam nouum habemus negotium cum Serueto. Hac transfire forte cogitabat. Necdum enim scitur, quo consilio venerit. Sed cum agnitus fuisset, retinendum putaui, Nicolaus meus ad capitale iudicium, poenæ talionis se offerens,ipsum vocauit. Quadraginta accusationis capita postridie in medium scripta attulit. Tergiuersatus est initio. Itaq; vocati sumus. Proterue mihi conuiciatus est, non secus acsi haberet sibi obnoxium. Ego, vt dignus erat, eum excepi. Tandem pronunciauit Senatus capita omnia probata esse. Dimissus est e carcere Nicolaus die tertio, quum fratrem meum sponsorem dedisset, quarto absolutus est. De impudentia hominis nihil dicam. Sed tantus fuit furor, vt non dubitauerit dicere diabolis inesse diuinitatem. Imo singulis plures inesse deos: quia deitas substantialiter tam illis quam ligno & lapidi communicata fuerit. Spero capitale saltem fore iudicium: poenæ vero atrocitatem remitti cupio. Vale. Collegæ mei te resalutant. Idem faciunt Budæus, & qui iam conualuit Normandius. Fratri etiam Claudio salutem dices meo nomine. Geneuæ, x x. Augusti. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: It is as you say, my Farel. Although we are tossed about in many storms, variously and harshly, yet because the pilot steers the ship in which we are carried, who will never allow us to perish even in the midst of shipwrecks, there is no reason for our minds to be overwhelmed by fear or weariness. Now we have a new affair with Servetus. He perhaps intended to pass through here. For it is not yet known with what purpose he came. But when he had been recognised, I thought he should be detained; my Nicolas, offering himself to the penalty of retaliation in a capital trial, summoned him. The next day he brought forward forty heads of accusation, set out in public. He evaded at first. So we were summoned. He railed at me insolently, as if he had me in his power. I, as he deserved, received him in turn. At last the Council pronounced that all the heads had been proved. Nicolas was released from prison on the third day, after my brother had given surety for him; on the fourth he was absolved. I will say nothing of the man's impudence. But his fury was so great that he did not hesitate to say that divinity dwells in devils; indeed, that several gods dwell in each one, because deity has been communicated substantially to them just as to wood and stone. I hope at least there will be a capital judgment; but I desire that the severity of the penalty be remitted. Farewell. My colleagues greet you in return. Budaeus does the same, and Normandius, who has now recovered. Give my greetings also to brother Claude. Geneva, on the twentieth day of August, 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS ECCLESIAE FRANCFORDIENSIS PASTORIBVS. S.D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO THE MINISTERS OF THE CHURCH OF FRANKFURT. Greetings.

units.la: Gratia vobis & pax a Deo Patre nostro & Domino Iesu Christo, eximii viri & mihi ex animo colendi fratres.
units.tr: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, distinguished men and brothers whom I hold in sincere regard.

units.la: NOmen Serueti Hispani vobis auditum esse non dubito, qui ante annos viginti virulento libello, multisque sacrilegis erroribus referto, Germaniam vestram infecit. Nebulo hic, quum ex Germania profugus sub fictitio nomine in Gallia latuisset, nuper ex priore illo libro, & nouis figmentis quæ sibi fabricatus est, maius volumen consarcinauit, quod Viennæ in urbe Lugduno vicina, clanculum excusum est. Eius autem multa exemplaria proximis nundinis paschalibus Francfordiam deuecta fuerant: verum institor Typographi vir pius & integer, quum admonitus foret nihil illic præter immensam errorum farraginem contineri, suppressit quicquid habebat. Quàm multis erroribus, imò prodigiosis in Deum blasphemiis scateat, longum esset referre. Fingite vobis rhapsodiam ex impiis omnium ætatum deliriis confutam. Nullum enim est impietatis genus, quod non hæc bellua velut ex inferis excitauerit. Et malo ex lectione ipsa vos iudicium facere. Certè reperietis fere in singulis paginis, quod vobis horrorem incutiat. Auctor ipse tenetur in carcere à Magistratu nostro, & propediem, vt spero, daturus est poenas. Vestrum autem est dare operam, ne hoc tam pestiferum venenum longius emanet. Nucius vobis referet in qua apotheca sint libri, & quo numero. Librarius, nisi fallor, exuri patietur.
units.tr: I do not doubt that you have heard the name of Servetus the Spaniard, who some twenty years ago infected your Germany with a virulent little book full of sacrilegious errors. This scoundrel, after fleeing from Germany and hiding in France under a false name, has recently cobbled together a larger volume out of that earlier book and the new fictions he has invented. It was secretly printed at Vienne, a town near Lyon. Many copies of it were carried to Frankfurt for the Easter fair, but the bookseller's agent, a pious and upright man, when he was warned that it contained nothing but a huge jumble of errors, withheld whatever copies he had. It would be tedious to list how many errors, indeed monstrous blasphemies against God, the book abounds in. Imagine a rhapsody of the impious follies of all ages, refuted. There is no kind of impiety that this beast has not, as if from the underworld, stirred up again. I prefer that you judge it from reading it yourselves. Surely you will find on nearly every page something to make you shudder. The author himself is held in prison by our magistracy and, as I hope, will shortly pay the penalty. It is your task, however, to take care that this so pestilent poison does not spread further. The messenger will tell you in which shop the books are and how many there are. The printer, unless I am mistaken, will allow them to be burned.

units.la: Epist.153: Quod si quid obstaculi esset, vos tam fore cordatos confido, vt mundus tam noxia corruptela purgetur. Et ratio vobis expedita erit. Quod si vestro arbitrio res permissa fuerit, necesse non erit a Magistratu petere, vt manum iniiciat. Quaquam autem ita de vestra integritate cum perspulsus, vt vos esse admonitos sufficiat: rei tamen magnitudo postulat, vt per Christum vos obtesteer, ne vobis effluat occasio, vt sed alò sitis ad officium vestrum intenti. Valete ornatissimi viri, & charissimi fratres. Dominus vos Spiritu suo regat, praesidio tueatur, & labores vestros benedicat. Genevae, v i. Calend. Septemb. M. D. L I I I.
units.tr: Epist. 153: If there is any obstacle, I trust you will be so prudent that the world is cleansed of such a harmful corruption, and the means will be ready to hand for you. If the matter is left to your judgment, there will be no need to ask the magistrate to lay hands on him. Although I am so persuaded of your integrity that it suffices to remind you, the importance of the matter nevertheless requires that I beseech you through Christ not to let the opportunity slip away, but to be all the more attentive to your duty. Farewell, most distinguished men and dearest brothers. May the Lord rule you by his Spirit, protect you with his help, and bless your labours. Geneva, 26 August 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS VIRETO. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO VIRET. Greetings.

units.la: DE rebus nostris volebam apud vos silere ne fructra moerorem vobis augerem. Sed quia veritus sum, ne grauius vos afficerent varij rumores, tandem mihi visum fuit, de summa ipsa breuiter vos certiores facere. Cum ante sesquian num interdictus foret vsus Coenae Berthelerio, tunc apud Senatum conquestus fuit: nos in gratiam nebulonis vocati fumus in curiam. Cum audita essent causa, pronunciauit Senatus iure fuisse excommunicatum. Inde quiruit ad hunc vsque diem, vel desperatione vel contemptu. Nunc vero ne Perrini Syndicatus effuerit, neglecto Consistorio se restitui a Senatu voluit. Ego iterum vocatus, mul o sermone disseri non rite neque ordine id esse facturos: imo fas non esse Ecclesiae disciplinam hoc modo labefactari. Metamen absente, nec audito Consistorio, data est illi recipiendae Coenae facultas. Simul ac mihi renunciatum fuit, modis omnibus curaui, vt Senatum Syndici vocarent. Ego ita sedulo in causam incubui, vt nihil meo iudicio praetermitterem, quod ad fiectendos eorum animos faceret: partim vehementia, partim moderatione ad sanam mentem reducere conatus sum. Iuraui etiam mihi potius statutum esse mortem oppetere, quam vt sacram Domini Coenam adeo turpiter prophanarem. Nihil enim esse indignius, quam vt ille sua contumacia Ecclesiae Dei illudens & insultans, pessimos quosque & suis similes, quasi elato vexillo, ad eandem proteruiam incitaret. Responsum est, Senatum de priore suo decreto nihil mutare. Ex quo perspicitis, mihi hac lege relinqui Ministerium, si Consistorij auctoritatem calcari patiar, ac Christi Coenam manifestis contemptoribus porrigam, qui pro nihilo sibi esse Pastores iactant. Atqui centies moriendum foret potius, quam vt Christum ita foedo ludibrio subiicerem. Quid heri in vtraque concione dixerim, non commemoro: quia multi coram narrabunt. Nunc igitur habeant impro bi & perditi homines quod captarunt. Me, vt par est, angit Ecclesiae clesiæ calamitas. Verùm si tantum licentiæ Deus Satanæ concedit, ut violentis imperiis opprimatur Ministrorum mei libertas, defunctus sum. Ipse verò qui vulnus inflixit, remedium inveniet, Et sanè, cùm tanta scelerum impunitas iam per annos complures grassata sit, Dominus forte iudicium aliquod parat, cuius cospectu sum indignus. Denique quicquid futurum sit, partes nostræ sent, nos eius arbitrio subiicere. Valete fratres integerrimi. Dominus vobis adsit semper, vos gubernet ac tueatur. Vicissim orate, ut miseram hanc Ecclesiam respiciat. Geneuæ, Pridie Nonas Septemb. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: I had wanted to say nothing to you about my affairs, so as not to add uselessly to your grief. But since I feared that various rumours might distress you more severely, I finally thought it right to inform you briefly of the whole matter. About a year and a half ago Berthelier was forbidden the use of the Lord's Supper, and then he complained to the Senate; we were summoned to the council chamber to please the scoundrel. When the case had been heard, the Senate pronounced that he had rightly been excommunicated. From then until today he has remained under that sentence, either in despair or in contempt. Now, however, since Perrin's syndicate has come to an end, he wanted to be restored by the Senate, ignoring the Consistory. I was called again, and I said at length that they would not be acting properly or in order if they did so, indeed that it was not lawful for church discipline to be undermined in this way. Yet, though he was absent and the Consistory had not been heard, he was given permission to receive the Supper. As soon as this was reported to me, I did everything in my power to have the Syndics summon the Senate. I threw myself into the cause so earnestly that, in my judgment, I left nothing undone that might bend their minds; partly with vehemence, partly with moderation, I tried to bring them back to sound sense. I also swore that I had rather be put to death than profane the Lord's holy Supper so shamefully. For nothing could be more outrageous than that he, mocking and insulting the Church of God by his obstinacy, should with a raised banner incite all the worst men and those like him to the same insolence. The reply was that the Senate would change nothing of its earlier decree. From this you see that the ministry is left to me only on this condition: that I allow the authority of the Consistory to be trampled underfoot and hand Christ's Supper to open contemners who boast that ministers are nothing to them. Yet I ought a hundred times to die rather than subject Christ to such a foul mockery. What I said yesterday in both sermons I will not repeat, since many will report it to you in person. Now, then, let the wicked and depraved men have what they have sought. As is right, I am distressed by the calamity of the Church. But if God grants Satan such license that the freedom of my ministers is crushed by violent commands, I am finished. He who inflicted the wound will find the remedy himself. And indeed, since such impunity for crimes has run rampant for many years now, the Lord perhaps is preparing some judgment, before whose sight I am unworthy. In short, whatever is to come, it is our part to submit ourselves to his will. Farewell, most upright brothers. May the Lord always be with you, guide you and keep you. In turn, pray that he will look upon this wretched Church. Geneva, 4 September 1553.

units.la: FARELLVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: Farel to Calvin, greetings.

units.la: Normendium rediisse ad pristinã valetudinem ac Marchionem ex Italia gratulor utrique, ne dicam tibi. Est sanè præterea quod inuideam piæ matronæ, ab his in quibus luctamur malis, solutæ, cui iam datur cum Christo esse & agere. Mira est Dei disposizione in Servetο, quòd istuc venerit. Utinam vel ferò sapiat. Magnum sanè miraculum erit si mortem perferat ferrio ad D. Conuersus, & occumbens una morte (qui multas myriades commeritus est) si omnes contendat ædificare præsentes, qui multis iam sublatis & qui superfuunt, adde etiã venturis nocere studuit. Valde crudeles erunt & admodum iniurij Christo, & doctrinæ pietatis, & veri Ecclesiæ hostes iudices, si non moveantur blasphemiis horrendis tam nefandi hæreticî, quibus diuinam maiestatem impetit, & Christi Euangelium conatus est labefactare, omnésque corrumpere Ecclesias. Sed spero D. factu rum ut qui laudantur ob iustas inflictas furibus & sacrilegis pœnas, ita se gerant, ut in hac parte merito bene audiant: sublato eo qui tandiu obstinatissime in hæresibus perseuerauit, quique tam multos perdidit. Quòd pœnæ atrocitatem leniri cupis, facis amici officium in inimicissimum tibi hominem. Sed te, quæso, ita geras, ne temere quiuis audeat nouã inferre in publicum dogmata, & tandiu omnia turbare impune, ut ille fecit. Vides arrogantem hæreticum Hieronymum, qui toties conuictus nondum in ordinem cogi potuit, & iudicum in dulgentia potius quàm equi tas, dum officium non faciant, non modo illi nocet & tantum non perdit, verumetiam multis. Verum hæc te non fugiunt, neque ideo dicuntur, ut opus tibi sit: sed & de aliis non paucis querimur, ita & hic licet. Plerique non nihil accedentes ad hæretin catabaptistarum, qui facinorosi, ut plurimum, noluntimprobos è medio tolli, quo liceat eis impune sua tradere & sequi flagitia: volunt non aliter agi cum hæreticis, quàm ut sinantur, quasi nihil interfit inter munus Pastoris & Magistratus. Si Pontifex pios damnet hæreseos, & furentes iudices iniquè exequuntur in innocentes id quod debetur hæreticis,quæ amentia est inde colligere non perdendos hæreticos,vt piis succurratur ? Sanè usmodi inaudita prius ratione sibi & aliis consulere voluerunt, præter viam quam tenuerunt omnes serui D.& veluti sese adiungentes hæreticis. Ego cùm legerem Paulum dixisse se non re fugere mortem siquid commeruisset,planè me obtuli sepius paratum ferre mortis iudicium, si quicquam contra pietatis doctrinam docuissem. Et addidi me quàm dignißimum esse quouis supplicio, si à fide & doctrina Christi quenquam auocarem. Sanè non potłum de aliis aliud sentire quàm quod de me statuo.Vale & tecum pij omnes.Mirum est quàm vtatur Satanas & sui omnes,quòd non peristis pridem Hodie legebam scriptum ad fratrem vnum te obiisse , sed prius Friburgum venisse ac vocasse sacerdotem , confessúmque te grauissimè errasse. Sic durent & locum habeant Pontificia, & tantùm posthac ex illis percipiant sacrificuli & tota sæx Pontificia quàm vera sunt,quæ ita sine fronte spargunt. Sed non tantùm Pontificij veteres, quin & noui Pontifices & bis monachi tantùm non rumpuntur. Christus omnibus meliorem det mentem, seque & istam seruet Ecclesiam, quam semper auditorem numero piorum , & donis, & cœlestibus benedictionibus locupletiorem reddat. Cupio Collegas siluos , cum reliquis piis. Collega te salutat, Gaspar & Claudius frater. Neocomi, viii. Septembris.
units.tr: I congratulate both Normendium on her return to her former health and the Marquis on his return from Italy, and I say nothing of you. There is also something I envy in the pious matron, who has been released from these evils we struggle with and is now granted to be and act with Christ. It is a wonderful arrangement of God that Servetus has come there. Would that he grew wise, even if late. It will be a great miracle if he undergoes death, and, dying once though he has deserved many myriads of deaths, he still strives to edify all who are present. He has already destroyed many, and he has tried to harm both those who survive and those who will come after. The judges will be very cruel, very unjust to Christ, to the doctrine of godliness, and enemies of the true Church, if they are not moved by the horrible blasphemies of so impious a heretic, by which he assails the divine majesty, tries to undermine the gospel of Christ, and seeks to corrupt all the churches. But I hope that, God willing, those who are praised for the just punishments inflicted on thieves and sacrilegious persons will conduct themselves so that in this matter they rightly earn good report, once he has been removed, he who has persisted so obstinately in heresies for so long and has ruined so many. As for your wish that the severity of the punishment be softened, you perform the office of a friend toward a man most hostile to you. But I beg you to conduct yourself so that no one rashly dares to bring new doctrines before the public and to disturb everything with impunity for so long, as he did. You see the arrogant heretic Hieronymus, who, though convicted so often, has not yet been brought into line. The indulgence of the judges, rather than their equity, while they do not perform their duty, not only harms him and nearly ruins him, but also harms many others. But these things do not escape you, nor are they said because you need them. We complain of not a few others as well, and so it is permitted here too. Many, not a little inclined to the Anabaptist heresy, who for the most part are wicked men, do not want the wicked removed from the midst, so that they may freely propagate and follow their crimes. They want heretics to be dealt with only by letting them be, as if there were no difference between the office of the minister and that of the magistrate. If the Pontiff condemns the godly of heresy, and raging judges unjustly inflict on the innocent what is owed to heretics, what madness is it to infer from this that heretics should not be destroyed, so that the godly may be helped? Indeed, they wished to provide for themselves and others by such an unheard-of method, contrary to the way all the servants of God have held, and as if joining themselves to the heretics. When I read that Paul said he did not refuse death if he had deserved it, I often offered myself plainly as ready to bear a sentence of death, if I had taught anything against the doctrine of godliness. And I added that I would be most worthy of any punishment if I drew anyone away from the faith and doctrine of Christ. Indeed, I cannot think of others otherwise than I judge of myself. Farewell, and all the godly with you. It is remarkable how Satan and all his people make use of the fact that you have not perished long ago. Today I read a letter written to one brother saying that you had died, but that first you had come to Freiburg, summoned a priest, and confessed that you had gravely erred. So may the Papist lies endure and keep their place. Henceforth, let the little priests and the whole Papist crowd learn from these how true the things are that they spread so shamelessly. But not only the old Papists, also the new popes and the monks are nearly bursting with it. May Christ give everyone a better mind, preserve himself and this Church, and always make it richer in number of the godly and in gifts and heavenly blessings. I wish my colleagues well, along with the other godly. Your colleague Gaspar and brother Claude greet you. Neuchâtel, 8 September.

units.la: M. D. LIII.
units.tr: M. D. LIII.

units.la: CALVINVS SVLTZERO s. D'
units.tr: CALVIN TO SULTZER, greeting

units.la: QVum Michaël Seruetus iam ante annos viginti Christianum orbem virulentis suis ac pestiferis dogmatibus infecerit: nomen tibi non ignotum esse arbitror. Quòd si librum non legisti,fieri tamen vix potest, quin de ipso genere doctrinæ aliquid audieris. Is est de quo fideli Christi minister, & sanctæ memoriæ D. Bucerus, cùm alioqui mansueto esset ingenio,pro suggestu pronuntiauit dignum esse,qui aulis viscerib sus discerperetur. Sicuti abeo tempore non desiit venenum suum spargere,nuper Viennæ miuus volumen,sed ex iisdem erroribus consarcinatum excudi clanculum curauit. Re verò patefactà, in carcerem est coniectus. Vnde nescio quomodo elapsus per Italiam errauit feré quatuor menses. Tandem huc malis aulspiciis appulsum, vnus ex Syndicis, me auctore, in carcerem duci iussit. Neque enim dissimulo,quin officij mei duxerim, hominem plusquam obstinatum & indomitum, quoad in me erat, compescere, ne longius manaret contagio. Videmus quàm licentiosè passim grassetur impietas, vt subinde noui errores scaturiant, quanta sit eorum ignauia, quos Deus gladio armauit, ad vindicandam nominis sui gloriam. Cùm tam acres inti & animosi superstitionum suarum vindices Papistæ, vt atrociter sæuiant ad fundendum innoxium sanguinem: pudeat Christianos magistratus in tuenda certa veritate nihil prorsus habere animi. Fateor equidem nihil minus esse consentaneum, quàm vt furiosam eorum intemperiem imitemur. Verùm, est aliqua moderationis ratio, ne impiis liceat quæsuis in Deum blasphemias impunè euomere, vbi est impediendi facultas. In hoc homine tria sunt consideranda. Quàm prodigiosis erroribus totam religionem corruperit: imò quàm detestandis ludibriis conatus sit euertere omnem pietatem: quàm fœdis deliriis intoluerit Christianismum, & omnia religionis nostræ principia funditus euerterit. Secundò, quàm se obstinatè gesserit: quàm diabolico fastu contempserit omnes monitiones: quàm desperata peruicacia præceps actus fuerit ad virus suum spargendum.
units.tr: Since Michael Servetus, now some twenty years ago, infected the Christian world with his virulent and pestilent doctrines, I think the name is not unknown to you. Even if you have not read his book, it is almost impossible that you have not heard something about this kind of teaching. He is the man about whom our faithful minister of Christ, the late D. Bucer, a man of gentle disposition otherwise, declared from the pulpit that he deserved to be torn apart with red-hot pincers. From that time he has not ceased to spread his poison. Recently he had a volume put together from the same errors printed secretly at Vienne, but once the affair came to light he was thrown into prison. From there, somehow or other he escaped and wandered through Italy for nearly four months. At last he came here under evil auspices, and one of the syndics, on my authority, ordered him to be taken to prison. For I do not hide that I thought it my duty, so far as lay in me, to restrain a man more than obstinate and untamable, lest the contagion spread further. We see how licentiously impiety rages everywhere, so that new errors spring up continually, and how cowardly are those whom God has armed with the sword to vindicate the glory of his name. Our Papists are such fierce, spirited avengers of their superstitions that they rage atrociously to shed innocent blood; it would be shameful if Christian magistrates had no spirit at all in defending the certain truth. I admit that nothing is less fitting than that we should imitate their frenzied intemperance. Yet there is some measure of moderation to be observed, so that the impious may not be allowed to vomit forth whatever blasphemies they please with impunity, when there is power to prevent it. In this man three things are to be considered. First, with what monstrous errors he has corrupted the whole of religion; indeed, with what detestable mockeries he has tried to overthrow all piety; with what foul delusions he has defiled Christianity and utterly overturned the foundations of our religion. Second, how obstinately he has behaved; with what diabolical arrogance he has despised all admonitions; with what desperate stubbornness he has rushed headlong to spread his poison.

units.la: Tertiò, quanto hodie fastu suas abominationes asserat. Tantùm enim abest à spe resipiscentiæ, vt non dubitet sanctis viris Caluitoni, & OEcolampadio aspergere hanc maculam, quasi socij fuerint. Cùm ostensæ essent OEcolampadij epistolæ, dixit se mirari, quo spiritu abductus foret à priore sensu. Sed quia tibi curæ fore spero, vt hominis impietas quibus meretur elogiis pinguatur, plura non addam. Tantùm vnius rei te admonitum volo, quæstorem vrbis, qui tibi has literas reddet, in hac causa recto esse animo, vt saltem exitum quem optamus, non fugiat. Vinam veteres tui discipuli eodem modo animati forent. De relus Gallicis nihil scribo, quia nihil hic esse noui arbitror, quod ton æque vobis notum sit: nisi quòd proximo Sabbathi die tres pij fratres Lugduni exusti sunt, quartus in vicinum oppidum missus ad similę supplicium. Vix credibile est cùm homines essent illiterati, quanta Spiritus Dei luce ad summam doctrinæ perfectionem illustrati, quoad res ferebat, & qua virtute diuinitatem constantiam instructi fuerint. Vnus metu consternatus initio à syncera confessione deflexerat. Cùm iudicibus certum fieret eum absoluere, de sua perfida simulatione prafatus, lacriter se ad ignem obtulit. In aliis quoque Galliæ partibus fragrant similia incendia: nec spes illa est mitigationis. Vale. Geneuæ v. Idus Septembris. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Third, with what arrogance he today defends his abominations. He is so far from any hope of repentance that he does not hesitate to smear this stain on the holy men Calvin and Oecolampadius, as if they had been his allies. When the letters of Oecolampadius were shown to him, he said he wondered by what spirit he had been led away from his earlier view. But since I hope you will take care that the impiety of this man is fattened with the titles it deserves, I will add nothing more. I only want to remind you of one thing: the city treasurer, who will deliver this letter to you, is upright in this matter, so that he at least does not shrink from the outcome we desire. Would that your old disciples were inspired in the same way. As to French affairs I write nothing, because I think there is nothing new here that is not equally known to you, except that last Sabbath three godly brothers were burned at Lyons, and a fourth was sent to a neighbouring town for a similar punishment. It is hardly believable, when these men were unlearned, how they were illumined by the light of the Spirit of God to the highest perfection of doctrine, as far as circumstances allowed, and with what courage and constancy they were equipped. One of them, terrified by fear, had at first turned aside from sincere confession. When it became clear to the judges that he would be acquitted, he confessed his treacherous pretence and offered himself to the fire, weeping. Similar fires are blazing in other parts of France too, and there is no hope of relief. Farewell. Geneva, 9th September 1553.

units.la: xiiij.
units.tr: xiiij.

units.la: BYLINGERVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: BULLINGER TO CALVIN, greeting

units.la: Simul & se abire iam, & si quid scribere velim Geneuam, hic mihi significauit. Idcirco vix ista scribere potui. Accepi tuas frater charissime.
