Audiui Gualterum nostrum, qui me solicitum & anxium reddidit. Ne recesseris, oro, ab ea ecclesia quae tot habet viros excellentes. Memineris illius ex actis Apostolicis. Ndi timere, nam multus est mihi adhuc in hac urbe populus. Tamen enim sunt porci & canes multo plures quam velimus, propter electos tamen multa sunt toleranda. Praeterea non ignoras quantum aduri sint tripudium, omnes qui in Gallia Christum coluerunt: quanto denique periculo exules Gallos exposueris, si discesseris. Mane ergo, mane & patere quaecunque Dominus immiserit probra, contemptiones, pericula, mala. Non deseret te Dominus. Per multas tribulationes oportet nos ingredi in regnum Dei. Obtulit quidem Dominus materiam per occasionem accommodatissimam Amplissimo Senatui Genevensi se & Ecclesiam expurgandi a labe seu foeditate haereticos, dum Servetum illum Hispanum in manus eius dedit. Novit hunc bona pars orbis Christiani vel ex blasphemis libris editis de erroribus Trinitatis, & iis quae edidit mere Iudaica pro iustificatione operum. Audis lum nunc alio edito libro semetipsum superasse impietate. Si ergo huic reponderet Amplissimus Senatus, quod blasphemo rebuloni debetur, totus orbis cerneret Genevenses blasphemosodisse, haereticos, qui vere sunt pertinaces haeretici, gladio iustitiae persequi, & gloriam maiestatis Divinae vindicare. Verum si hoc non fecerint, tuum tamen non fuerit deserta illa Ecclesia aliis quoque malis occasionem praebere. Pugna intrepide, Deo confide per Christum, implora eius consilium & auxilium, ut te eripiat. Iuuamus te certatim orationibus nostris. Viue & vale. XIIII.Septemb. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: He has just now told me here, both that he is leaving and that he wishes to send something to Geneva, so I have scarcely been able to write these lines. I have received your letter, dearest brother. I have heard about our Gualter, which has made me anxious and troubled. I beg you, do not withdraw from that church which has so many excellent men. Remember that passage from the Acts of the Apostles. Do not fear, for I still have a considerable people in this city. Although there are many more swine and dogs than we would wish, on account of the elect many things must be endured. Moreover, you are not unaware how greatly those who worshipped Christ in France are being set on fire and how much danger you would expose the Gallic exiles to if you departed. Stay, then, stay and endure whatever reproaches, contempts, dangers and evils the Lord has sent. The Lord will not forsake you. We must enter the kingdom of God through many tribulations. The Lord has indeed offered, by a most fitting occasion, to the most distinguished Senate of Geneva the opportunity of cleansing both itself and the Church from the stain and filth of heretics, since he has given into their hands that Spaniard Servetus. Much of the Christian world knows him, from the blasphemous books he has published on the errors concerning the Trinity, and from those works he has published, purely Jewish in teaching justification by works. You hear that now, by another book he has published, he has outdone himself in impiety. If therefore the most distinguished Senate should answer this blasphemer with what is owed to a blasphemer, the whole world would see that the Genevans punish blasphemers and persecute with the sword of justice heretics who are truly stubborn heretics, and vindicate the glory of the divine majesty. But if they do not do this, it would nonetheless not be right for that church, once deserted, to give occasion for other evils as well. Fight fearlessly, trust in God through Christ, implore his counsel and help, that he may rescue you. We help you with our prayers, each vying with the other. Farewell and live well. 14 September 1553.

units.la: CLARISSIMIS ET AMPLISSIMIS SYNDICIS, & Senatui Reipublicae Genevensis Dominis nostris colendissimis.
units.tr: TO THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS AND DISTINGUISHED SYNDICS AND THE SENATE OF THE REPUBLIC OF GENEVA, OUR MOST HONOURED LORDS.

units.la: AMplissimi Domini, quanuis de pia sedulitate, diligentiaque singulari charissimi nostri fratris Ioannis Calvini, caeterorumque eius collaboratorum nihil dubitemus, quin pro exquisita, & diligenti cura, & vigilantia, quam hucusque praestiterunt in Ecclesia Christi, satisfecisse nobis videri potuissent. Praeterea Ecclesiae Tigurinae Antistites, fratres nostri in Domino obseruandi, pro exacto iudicio, quo prae caeteris Ecclesiae Ministris dotati sint, suam (quam & nos videre voluerunt) sententiam quàm diligentissime ad vos scripserunt, potuissemus hisce contenti silere: Tamen quia A.V. visum est, etiam nostram hac in re audire sententiam, quantùm breuitas temporis admisit, contulimus concertationes Serueti, quas cum vestrae Ecclesiae Ministris habuit. Libros item ipsius blasphemiis in sanctissimam Trinitatem: vniuersam item Christi Ecclesiam refertos, quibus haeresei multis am annis sopitas, vnáque cum haereticis oppressas reuocare, magnoque cum simplicium scandalo euomere, obtrudereque Ecclesiae Christi conatur, percurrimus. Neque aliter pro domino nobis à Deo collato iudicare possumus, quàm diuersos à fama doctrina, neque tolerandos, vt vel proponantur, vel legantur in coetu piorum. Neque dubitamus, quin vos pro insigni prudentia vestra ipsius conatus repressuri sitis, ne blasphemiae ipsius, tanquam Cancer, depascantur Christi membra. Nam longis rationibus euertere ipsius deliramenta, quid aliud esset, quàm cum insanientè insanire? Subscribimus igitur vniuersi iudicio Tigurinae Ecclesiae Ministrorum fratrum nostrorum in Christo charissimorum, commendantes interim vestram amplitudinem vnà cum Ecclesia vestra gratiae diuinae. Datae Scaffusij v i. Octob. Anno M. D. L I I I.
units.tr: Most distinguished Lords, although we have no doubt about the devoted diligence and singular care of our dearest brother John Calvin and his other colleagues, and although we might well have considered them to have satisfied us by the exact and careful attention and vigilance they have hitherto shown in the Church of Christ, we nonetheless thought it right to keep silent, content with what has been said. The pastors of the Church of Zurich, our brothers in the Lord to be respected, have, by the sound judgment for which they are endowed above other ministers of the Church, written to you as diligently as possible with their opinion (which they also wished us to see). Yet since Your Honours thought fit that we too should hear our opinion in this matter, so far as the brevity of time allowed, we have gone through the disputations of Servetus which he held with the ministers of your Church, and likewise his books, full of blasphemies against the most holy Trinity, which seek to revive a heresy long since quieted, and, joined with the heretics, to overwhelm the whole Church of Christ, and to vomit forth and thrust upon it, to the great scandal of simple people. We cannot judge otherwise, as the Lord has given us to do, than that these books differ from sound doctrine and are not to be tolerated, whether they be put forward or read in the assembly of the godly. Nor do we doubt that you, in your remarkable prudence, will check his attempts, lest his blasphemies, like a cancer, feed upon the members of Christ. For to overthrow his ravings by long arguments would be nothing other than to rage along with a madman. We therefore subscribe to the judgment of all the ministers of the Tigurine Church, our brothers most dear in Christ, and meanwhile commend Your Honours, together with your Church, to the grace of God. Given at Schaffhausen, 1 October, in the year 1553.

units.tr: To the most distinguished Syndics and the most honourable Senate of the Genevan commonwealth, our most esteemed lords: greetings.

units.la: ACcepimus per hunc tabellionem, literas amplitudinis vestrae, vnà cum libro Serueti & articulis ex ipso consignatis, cum collatione scripta per amplitudinis vestrae concionatores, fratres nostros venerabiles & charos, & Michaelem Serue-tum. Ac quoniam illa omnia à nobis inspici, diligenterque expendi, & nostrum de his nos iudicium adiicere pietas vestra postulauit, amplitudini vestrae morem gerétes, quid de toto hoc negotio Vnitatis & Trinitatis Dei, denique de Filij Dei myste-rio sentiamus & doceamus, & quid de controuersia vel scriptis Ministrorum Ecclesiae vestrae & Serueti iudicemus, quanta poffumus breuitate & perspicuitate, Deo iuuante explicabimus. Mysterium adorandum Vnitatis & Trinitatis Dei benedicti in secula, nihil dubitamus ab exordio mundi ab omnibus sanctis & creditum esse firmiter, & posteris credendum fideliter traditum, sed & in Scripturas manifeste relatum, a Spiritu sancto inspiratis veracibus Prophetis. Hoc igitur theologiae veri principium & caput, ita est comprobatum Dei oraculis, ita confirmatum euidentibus signis, vnanimique consensione receptum a catholica & orthodoxa, tam veteris quam noui Testamenti Ecclesia, vt ipsum vel in quaestionem vocasse, nefas semper fuerit iudicatum. Fatemur itaque cum sanctis & vniuersali Dei Ecclesia, vnam esse Dei essentiam, tres personas distinctas non confusas. Pater enim de coelis testificans de Filio suo: Hic est Filius meus dilectus (inquit) in quo placatus sum. Filius is est, cui Pater misit testimonium. Spiritus sanctus vero in specie columbae apparuit, tres quidem distinctae in vna essentia diuina, personae. Emerserunt quidem ante concilium Nicenum, Praxeas, Noetus & Sabellius veteribus appellati Patripassiani, qui distinctionem personarum propter vnitatem Dei conseruandam confundebant, sed docte & irrefragabiliter a vigilibus Ecclesiae praesidibus sunt confutati, Scripturisque propugnatum & in Ecclesia conseruatum, adorandum trinae Vnitatis Dei mysterium. Vnde cernimus in concilio Niceno, Ecclesiae praesides non aliud novo symbolo conditum tradidisse, quam quod a temporibus Apostolorum, imo & Prophetarum, catholica & orthodoxa retinuerat Ecclesia. Quod ergo Seruetus Hispanus Trinitatem aeternam Dei, triceps monstrum & Cerberum quendam tripartitum, denique imaginarios deos, illusionis ac tres spiritus Daemonio- rum appellitat, aeternam Dei maiestatem nefande & horribiliter blasphemat. Quod Athanasium, Augustinum & alios Deifer uos eximios, illustriaque Ecclesiae lumina, Trinitarios atque adeo atheos appellat (ita enim omnes Trinitate agnoscentes nuncupat) non illos tantum: sed totum chorum sanctorum, adeoque totam Christi Ecclesiam, infandis & non ferendis conuiciis indignissime proscindit. Abominandum vero videtur illud esse in homine infelici, quod Iudaeorum quoque blasphemias in Christianam religionem effusas, excufit, & foeda Mahummetis verba, tres in Trinitate personas, vel vt ipse ait, tres deos, patribus fuisse incognitas, & esse filios Beelzebub approbat & extollit. Quid vero potuisset ab hoc homine magis impium in Deo, & indignius in intemeratam fidem Christianam, expui? quae obsecro aures Christianae ista patienter audiant? De Filio Dei concorditer credidit & docuit Ecclesia Dei ab initio, subsistere illum ab aeterno in proprio hypostasi, hoc enim docta fuerat ex verbo Dei,Christo ipso apertissimè in Euangelio dicente: Antequam Abraham esset,ego sum. Vtque subsistentia, non carnis quidem, sed Diuinitatis, iuxta quam Apostolus illum dixit esse expressum imaginem substantiæ paternæ. Vbi simul illud ex veteri Scriptura citat testimonium: Filius meus es tu, ego hodie genui te. Hic filius gloriæ ab æterno Filius,Deus verus,in tempore factus est hominis filius, homo verus, natus non ex substantia Dei Patris,sed ex substantia Mariæ virginis matris,quam Deus spiritu suo fœcundam reddidit. Vnde filius ille & semen benedictum mulieris,& germen Dauidis,& filius hominis appellatur.Manet autem in vna indiuisa persona,retinens tamen naturas duas impermixtas aut inconfusas,diuinam & humanam.
units.tr: We have received through this messenger your honours' letter, together with the book of Servetus and the articles extracted from it, and the written comparison made by your honours' preachers, our venerable and dear brothers, and by Michael Servetus. Since your piety has asked us to examine all of these carefully and to add our own judgment on them, we shall comply with your honours' wish. With God's help, we shall set out as briefly and clearly as we can what we think and teach about the whole matter of the unity and Trinity of God, and finally about the mystery of the Son of God, and what we judge concerning the controversy and the writings of the ministers of your church and of Servetus. We have no doubt that the adorable mystery of the unity and Trinity of the blessed God, blessed for ever, has been firmly believed by all the saints from the beginning of the world and faithfully handed down to posterity to be believed, and that it is also plainly reported in the Scriptures, inspired by the Holy Spirit through the true prophets. This principle and head of true theology has been so confirmed by the oracles of God, so established by manifest signs, and so received with unanimous consent by the catholic and orthodox Church of both the Old and New Testaments, that to call it into question has always been judged an outrage. Therefore we confess, with the saints and with the universal Church of God, that there is one divine essence and three distinct persons, not confused. For the Father, testifying from heaven concerning his Son, says: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." That is the Son to whom the Father gave testimony. The Holy Spirit appeared in the form of a dove. Thus there are three distinct persons in the one divine essence. Before the Council of Nicaea there arose Praxeas, Noetus and Sabellius, called by the ancients Patripassians, who, to preserve the unity of God, confounded the distinction of persons. But they were learnedly and irrefutably confuted by the watchful presidents of the Church, and the mystery of the threefold unity of God, which is to be adored, was defended by the Scriptures and preserved in the Church. Hence we see that at the Council of Nicaea the presidents of the Church did not hand down anything new in a new creed, but what the catholic and orthodox Church had held from the times of the Apostles, indeed of the Prophets. Therefore Servetus the Spaniard, who calls the eternal Trinity of God a three-headed monster and a kind of three-part Cerberus, and finally imaginary gods, illusions and three spirits of demons, blasphemes the eternal majesty of God in an impious and horrible way. He calls Athanasius, Augustine and other eminent men inspired by God, and illustrious lights of the Church, Trinitarians and even atheists (for so he names all who acknowledge the Trinity), and not only them but the whole company of the saints, and so the whole Church of Christ, he tears apart most shamefully with unspeakable and intolerable insults. Yet what seems most abominable in this unhappy man is that he excuses and extols the blasphemies of the Jews poured out against the Christian religion, and approves the foul words of Mahomet, that the three persons in the Trinity, or, as he himself says, three gods, were unknown to the fathers, and that they are sons of Beelzebub. What could this man have spewed out more impious against God, and more unworthy against the undefiled Christian faith? I beg you, what Christian ears could patiently hear such things? The Church of God has from the beginning believed and taught in harmony concerning the Son of God, that he subsists from eternity in his own hypostasis. For the Church had learned this from the Word of God, Christ himself saying most plainly in the Gospel: "Before Abraham was, I am." And the subsistence is not of the flesh, but of the Divinity, according to which the Apostle said that he is the express image of the Father's substance. There at the same time he cites the testimony from the Old Scripture: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you." This Son of glory, the eternal Son, true God, was made in time the Son of man, true man, born not from the substance of God the Father, but from the substance of Mary the virgin mother, whom God made fruitful by his Spirit. Hence that Son is also called the seed of the woman that was blessed, the branch of David, and the Son of man. He remains, however, in one undivided person, yet retaining two natures, divine and human, unmixed and unconfused.

units.la: Id quod adeò perspicuis& euidentibus Scripturæ testimoniis cò probatum,iam olim & nunc esse constat,vt qui addubitet,cum ratione insaniat.Nos igitur simpliciter &concorditer,ita vt iam exposuimus, firmiter credimus,& in Ecclesia fidei nostræ concredita,prædicamus.Rursus ergo blasphemus in Dei Filium deprehenditur Seruetus, qui illam ab æterno Filij hypostasin existentem & Patri coessentialem & coæqualem,diabolica ideam, & fabulosam quandam Chimæram,conuiciari non veretur. Insuper asserere audet corporalis filij patrem alium non esse vllum, quàm ipsum Deum Patrem, ex cuius substantia caro Filij nata sit.Longè aliter docuit Paulus doctor Gentium,qui dixit Filium Dei genitum fuisse ex femine Dauidis secundum carnem, & declaratum Dei Filium in potentia & Spiritu sanctificationis &c. Cæterum cur singula istius blasphemi hominis recolligere pergeremus? Satis diligenter & fideliter enormes aliquot istius errores & apertas hæreses collegerunt Ecclesiæ vestræ fidi Pastores & docti,eo scripto cui titulum præfixerunt,sententiæ vel propositiones excerptæ ex libro Michaelis Serueti. Eas nec per calumniam excerptas aut consignatas inuenimus, nec illas vlla ratione recipimus aut approbamus: sed execramur potius.
units.tr: This is so clearly and evidently proved by the testimonies of Scripture that it is agreed to be so both formerly and now, so that whoever doubts it is mad with reason. We therefore simply and in harmony, just as we have set out, firmly believe and proclaim what has been entrusted to the faith of the Church. Again, then, Servetus is found to be a blasphemer against the Son of God, for he does not hesitate to revile that hypostasis of the Son, existing from eternity and coessential and coequal with the Father, as a diabolical idea and a fabulous chimera. Moreover, he dares to assert that the father of the Son according to the flesh is no other than God the Father himself, from whose substance the flesh of the Son was born. Paul, the teacher of the Gentiles, taught quite differently, who said that the Son of God was born of the seed of David according to the flesh, and declared to be the Son of God in power, according to the Spirit of sanctification, and so on. But why should we go on gathering up the individual points of this blasphemous man? Our faithful and learned ministers of your church have collected, quite carefully and faithfully, several enormous errors and open heresies of his, in the writing to which they gave the title: sentences or propositions extracted from the book of Michael Servetus. We have found these neither falsely extracted nor distorted, and we accept or approve them in no way; rather we execrate them.

units.la: Nam Seruetus responsione sua mox subiecta rem inuoluit, non explicauit,depravatis interim multis veterum de Vnitate & Trinitate Dei , deque Filij Dei mysterio sententiis, id quod Ministri Ecclesiæ satis aperte opposita responsione euicerunt. Replica vel scholia Serueti præter extremam impudentiam & conuitia dira,parum aut nihil sunt. Toties enim illud suum Mentiris , Caluino impingit, toties magum, & Simonem Magum criminatur, vt meminisse pigeat ac pudeat. Præsertim cum res ipsa clamet , & scripta Serueti diligenter expensa testentur, nihil confinxisse Caluinum, Seruetum potius ea quæ dixit, rursus negare, ac fuco aliquo tingere. Caluini Pastoris vestri & fratris nostri fidem & diligentiam, denique egregia in exules & pios merita,illustriora esse speramus, quàm quæ istius crimina-tionibus indignißimis,vel apud Amplitudinem Vestram,vel apud alios viros bonos obscurari possint. Neque hoc dissimulat Amplitudo Vestra,quæ(quod non fine animi lætitia legimus)di ferte scriptis literis,significans iudicium à nobis non requirere, quòd Ecclesiæ vestræ Ministris diffidat:sed potius vt nostrum de his non nesciat iudicium. Porrò quomodo Amplitudo Vestra coerceat hunc hominem,qui olim ab Ecclesia per Scripturas contumacias & damnatas hæreses,renouat,ac prima fidei nostræ firma capita oppugnat,oppugnandóque,Deo & sanctis eius conuictatur,vestræ prudentiæ relinquimus æstimandum.Si nô fallit nos similitudo nominis, mouit hic Seruetus hoc ingens malum ante annos viginti, conante tum beatæ memoriæ D.I. OEcolampadio ipsum reducere in viam: ac tum quoque doctrina Serueti ab iis qui primi hisce regionibus Euangelium Christi prædicarunt,condemnata fuit. Ille verò fui sensus tenax, nihilominus anno 1531 curauit in Germania 7 libros de Trinitatis erroribus, & alios dialogos excudi, quibus dubium non est complures parum exercitatos in Scripturis,& infirmiores in fide,præcipites actos in graue tum animarum tum corporum discrimen. Quo ta men adeo satiatus non fuit,vt modò recisis pestilentissimis erroribus & blasphemiis non ferendis, semetipsum in impietate & blasphemia superare,& corruptissimam doctrinam sub specie restitutionis Christianismi Ecclesiæ obtrudere pergat.Multa ergo fide & diligentii cötra hoc opus esse iudicamus, præsertim cùm Ecclesiæ nostræ apud externos malè audiant,quasi hæretiçe sint & hæreticis fauant.Obtulit verò in præsenti sanctâ Dei prouidentia occasionem , repurgandi vos simul ac nos à prava mali huius suspitione,si vigilantes fueritis,diligenterque caueritis ne veneni huius contagio per hunc serpat latius, id quod facturos A.V.nihil dubitamus, Dominus Iesus Christus conferat pietati vestræ,sapientiam & fortitudinem,viam, rationem & modum instum faciendi voluntatem eius ad gloriam nominis ipsius & ad fidei synceræ Ecclesiæque fidelem conseruationem.Simul offerimus A.V.nostra obsequia, commendamusque eidem nos omnes.Cæterum per tres integros dies tabellarium hunc vestrum detinuimus,quòd non potuerimus nos citius explicate.Datum Tiguri,11.Octob.Anno M. D. LIII.
units.tr: For Servetus, in his response placed immediately after, entangled the matter rather than explained it, meanwhile distorting many opinions of the ancients concerning the unity and Trinity of God and the mystery of the Son of God. The ministers of the Church have shown this quite plainly in their opposing response. Servetus's replies and notes, apart from extreme shamelessness and dreadful insults, are of little or no value. He keeps throwing at Calvin that word of his, "You lie", and so often accuses him of being a magician and a Simon Magus that one is ashamed even to remember it. Especially since the matter itself cries out, and the writings of Servetus, carefully weighed, bear witness that Calvin invented nothing, but that Servetus, rather, denies again what he said and tries to colour it with some pretence. We hope that the faith and diligence of Calvin, our brother and your minister, and his excellent services to exiles and to the pious, are more illustrious than that they could be obscured by this man's most unworthy accusations, either before your honours or before other good men. Your honours do not conceal this either, for in your letter, as we read with no small joy, you signify that you do not ask our judgment because you distrust the ministers of your church, but rather so that you may not be ignorant of our judgment on these matters. Furthermore, how your honours should restrain this man, who, having long ago been condemned by the Church through the Scriptures, renews the rejected heresies and attacks the first firm articles of our faith, and in attacking them reviles God and his saints, we leave to your prudence to judge. If the similarity of the name does not deceive us, this Servetus stirred up this great evil twenty years ago, when the late Dr. Johannes Oecolampadius, of blessed memory, tried to bring him back to the right path; and then too the teaching of Servetus was condemned by those who were the first to preach the Gospel of Christ in these regions. But he, tenacious of his own opinion, nevertheless in 1531 took care to have seven books on the errors concerning the Trinity, and other dialogues, printed in Germany, by which there is no doubt that many men little trained in the Scriptures and weaker in faith were driven headlong into grave danger both to their souls and their bodies. Yet he has not been so satiated by this that, although the most pestilential errors and intolerable blasphemies have been cut away, he should now go on surpassing himself in impiety and blasphemy, and, under the appearance of restoring Christianity, press a most corrupt doctrine upon the Church. We therefore judge that much faith and diligence must be applied against this work, especially since our churches are ill spoken of among foreigners, as if they were heretical and favoured heretics. But in the present situation God's holy providence has offered an opportunity of purging both you and us of the wicked suspicion of this evil, if you are watchful and take care diligently that the contagion of this poison does not spread more widely through this man. We do not doubt that your honours will do this. May the Lord Jesus Christ give to your piety wisdom and strength, and the way, reason and just manner of doing his will, to the glory of his name, and to the faithful preservation of the pure faith and of the Church. At the same time we offer your honours our services and commend all of us to you. Moreover, we have detained your messenger here for three full days, because we could not explain ourselves more quickly. Given at Zurich, 11 October, in the year 1553.

units.la: V. Amplitudini dediti Pastores & Lectores, Ministri Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ.
units.tr: Ministers and readers devoted to your honours, the ministers of the Church of Zurich.

units.la: VIRIS CLARISSIMIS, PIENTISSIMISQVE DOMINIS Dominis Syndicis, & Senatui amplissimo Genevensis reip. Dominis nostris omni studio colendis & observandis.
units.tr: To the most illustrious men, the most pious lords, the Syndics, and the most august Senate of the Genevan commonwealth, our lords to be honoured and observed with all devotion.

units.la: QVod Dominus & Seruator noster Iesus Christus in agone vltimo precatus est ad Patrem pro suis, vt seruentur per nomen eius, qui dati sunt ipsi, vt sint vnum, sicut & ipse vnum est cum Patre: idem nobis etiam hoc tempore precandum esse maxime cernimus: quo sub hac mundi senecta omnes in hoc neruos intendit tenebrarum princeps, vt si quid est sanae professionis & fidei labefactet, sanctorum consensionem, vnitatemque Spiritus conuellat, & dissipet, religionem puram a fundamentis extirpet, sic permittente nimirum Deo Patre optimo, in hoc vt probetur Ecclesia, & exercitatione non insalubri firmetur, atque ad resistendum in fide excitetur, & animetur: tum vt suam potentiam declaret contra portas inferorum validam. Ac eiusmodi sane probationis genus vobis Amplissimi viri, vestraeque Ecclesiae hoc tempore contigit, quo Seruetus Hispanus vestras in manus peruenit, multis iam annis horrendae impietatis, & blasphemiarum in sacrosanctae Trinitatis mysterium assertor, & renouator: quam etsi molestiam vobis datam dolemus, tamen quia interest plurimum gloriae nominis Christi, atque vniuersae Ecclesiae, vt malo in exitium plurimorum graslanti occurratur, gaudemus eo loci autorem detineri, vbi nobis persuademus nec prudentiam Christianam, neque zelum sanctis dignum defutu-rum esse. Cumque super hoc ipso negotio censuerit. A.V.nos Ecclesiae huius Administros interpellandos esse, transmissis in hoc collationibus scripto a Pastoribus vestrae Ecclesiae fratribus nostris in Domino obseruandis, & Serueto exhibitis: tum libro eiusdem Serueti, quo sparsa esse sua dogmata cernimus, haud grauatim mentem nostram pro charitatis lege, nostraque in vos propitudine, sicut ea postulat, hisce aperimus: vtcunque & vester or do amplissimus consilio polleat & doctrina excellente, iudicioque praeditis viris prouisum sit Ecclesiae vestrae, quorum iudicio & sancto, & exquisito vobis satisfieri nihil dubitamus. Caeterum, quantum ex inspectione libri, Serueti confessionibus, refutationibusque perspicere licuit, deprehendimus plane in redemptionis nostrae mysterium strictum esse stylum: caputque fidei de Filio Dei vero Deo ab aeterno, vereque homine facto ex muliere, sicut Apostolus inquit, Iuxta promissiones factas Patribus, stupenda temeritate hunc impetere: personarum trium distinctionem in essentia vnitate simpliciter tollere: Christi gloriâ, quam
units.tr: That our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, in his final agony, prayed to the Father for his own, that they might be kept in his name, those who were given to him, that they may be one, just as he and the Father are one: we see that this same prayer must be offered by us also at this time, when, in this old age of the world, the prince of darkness bends all his strength to this end, to shake whatever remains of sound profession and faith, to tear apart the agreement of the saints and the unity of the Spirit, and to root out pure religion from its foundations. God the best Father, no doubt, permits this so that the Church may be tested, strengthened by no unwholesome exercise, and roused and encouraged to resist in faith, and so that he may show his power against the gates of hell, which are strong. And such a kind of trial has certainly fallen to you, most distinguished sirs, and to your Church at this time, when Servetus the Spaniard has come into your hands, a man who for many years has been the champion and renewer of a horrible impiety and of blasphemies against the sacred mystery of the Holy Trinity. Although we grieve that this trouble has been given to you, nevertheless, since it matters greatly to the glory of Christ's name and to the whole Church that a pestilence which rages to the destruction of many be checked, we rejoice that its author is being held in the place where we are persuaded that neither Christian prudence nor zeal worthy of holy men will be lacking. And since you have judged in this very matter that we, the ministers of this Church, should be consulted, and since the written comparisons made in this affair have been sent by our brothers in the Lord, the pastors of your Church, whom we must respect, and have been shown to Servetus, and since we have seen his book, in which we perceive his teachings to be scattered abroad, we do not hesitate, by the law of charity and out of our goodwill towards you, to lay open our mind in these pages, as it requires; so that, however your most distinguished council may be strong in wisdom and excellent learning, and however provision has been made for your Church through men endowed with judgement, we doubt not that you will be satisfied by their holy and carefully considered judgement. Moreover, as far as it has been possible to discern from the inspection of the book and from the confessions and refutations of Servetus, we have found that he plainly attacks the mystery of our redemption: with astonishing rashness he assails the article of faith concerning the Son of God, true God from eternity and truly made man of a woman, as the Apostle says, according to the promises made to the fathers; he simply abolishes the distinction of the three persons within the unity of the essence; and the glory which he has from the Father from eternity [...]

units.la: Epist. 16.
units.tr: Epist. 16.

units.la: habet à Patre ab æterno, cuacuarc:idq; contra apertæ Scripturæ oracula, atque orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ cófeffionem:quam cùm fratres nostri Tygurini perspicuè, doctéque expresserint, nos vt ei penitus consentientes repetere fuperfcdemus. Quales autem habiti sint, qui eos articulos vnquam tentare ausi sunt, notius est, quàm vt egeat explicatione nostra. Cancro morbo Paulus eiusmodi pestem assimilauit: & hæretîn definierunt veteres adeóq; & ipse Apostolus, crimen multò leuius, quàm ab hocdesigna-tur. Et pro hæreticis damnati sunt proclamatiq;, qui vna aliqua in parte impegissent, si errorem pertinaciter tueri pergerent. Atqui Seruetus non simplicem, sed ex multis impietatibus conflatam hæreticorum laruam profiteatur, puta, Arrij, Marcionis, Sabellij, Fotini, Manichæi, Pelagij, & cæterorum: & quod in pluribus, hisque diuersis impugnatû est à melioris notæ Ecclesiæ Doctoribus Patribusque, id ab hoc vno ore impudentissimo, atque blasphemo euomitur, vt vere illi Christus signum sit contradictionis: cui nec essentiam diuinitatis, neque hypostasin, nec carnis nostræ veritatem, neque animam humanam relinquat, iungenda in sacrosansta hac persona discerpat, & distincta confundat, redemptionis virtutem eneruet: præter alios prophanos errores quamplurimos, atque deliria omnia, vt vestri Pastores, cófratresque nostri inquiunt, à verbo Dei, & orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ consensu aliena. Atque hæc quidem tanta confidentia, præsumptione, & pertinacia, vt appareat illud sapientis in eo verum, Impius cùm in profundum venerit, contemnit: & illud item, Si contuderis pistillo in mortario, non recedet ab eo stultitia eius. Nâ neque captiuitate humiliatur ad modestiam, neque tam luculentis, veris, & euidentibus fratrum nostrorum institutionibus, qui bus errorum, luce clarius conuincitur, vel cedit, vel acquiescit: sed serpentis instar incitati, maledicos, atque contumeliosos in Caluinum syncerissimum Dei seruum, & blasphemos in Dominum subinde sibilos edit, & lubricus nonnunquam elabi conatur. In hoc enim Deum vnum, cùmque simplicem inculcat toties, quasi trium hypostaseon vera diuersitas naturæ simplicitati vllo modo repugnet: atque insaniat proinde Ecclesia Trinitate in vnitate, & vnitatem in Trinitate venerandam commendans. Sicut & Christo Dei Filio multa cùm præ se ferat tribuere, manifestè tamen duabus naturis constantem personam negat, quæ iuxta illam quidem ab æterno, & ante secula, nedum ante incarnationem à Patre genitum (Scriptura testante) vt cuius egressus à diebus æternitatis est, & per quem factæ sunt secula, si gnantis naturam per omnia referat: iuxta hanc verò in seculo natum, carnem de carne nostra, ex substantia Virginis, per omnia fratribus similem. Hoc ergo veritatis pede pressus, quantumlibet subdolus, vasėrque tenetur. Meminimus vero nos ante annos viginti tres in hac ciuitate domino OEcolampadio præstantissimo huius Ecclesiæ præsidi negotium ab hoc homine exhibitum, & vet bis scriptúsque serió interpellatum, nihilò factum emendationem: vt iam tum vir Dei sagacissimus sententiam tulerit, daturum religioni Christianæ graue dispendium, nisi manu Domini frangeretur. Quæ cùm ita sint, viri præstantissimi. primùm omnium merito gratias Deo æterno Patri Iesu Christi agitis, cuius benignitate synceram lucem veritatis inconcasse adepti estis, Spiritúsque sancti iudicium, vt praua & adulterina à veræ germanáque vitæ doctrina quæritis discernere: eundémque pro cibus ardentibus interpellare debetis, vt nos conseruet in syncerita e fidei, confirmétque vt haktenus stabiles, & immotos contra scandala tam horribilia, Satanæque assultus. Postremò, quod Seruetum attinet hortamur, vt quod facere vos apparet, omne studium in ipso sanando adhibeatis, modò quæ excitauit offendicula, & ipsa sanari queant. Verum si insanabilis in concepta semel peruersitate perstet, sic pro officio vestro, potestatéque à Domino concessa coerceatur, ne dare incommodum queat deinceps Ecclesiæ Christi, néve fiant nouissima primis deteriora. Quain re suppeditabit Dominus ipse Spiritum, robur, & sapientiam: quem vnà vobiscum cum Ecclesia nostra pro vobis serió, assiduéque orabimus. Vicissim nos nostrámque Ecclesiam amplitudinis vestræ fauori, & sacris orationibus commendantes. Valete, ex Basilea, die decima octaua Octobris. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: He has from the Father from eternity, from eternity; and this against the plain oracles of Scripture and the confession of the orthodox Church. Since our brothers of Zurich have expressed it clearly and learnedly, we will not repeat it, since we wholly agree with them. Who the men were who ever dared to attack these articles is better known than that it needs explanation from us. Paul compared such a plague to a cancer, and the ancients, and the Apostle himself, defined heresy as a crime far lighter than this. Those who stumbled in some single point were condemned and proclaimed as heretics if they persisted in stubbornly defending their error. Yet Servetus professes not a simple heresy but a mask of heretics compounded from many impieties: that of Arius, Marcion, Sabellius, Photinus, Manichaeus, Pelagius, and the rest. What has been opposed in many, and in diverse ways, by teachers and fathers of the Church of better repute, this one most impudent and blasphemous mouth vomits forth alone, so that Christ truly is for him a sign of contradiction. He leaves Christ neither the essence of the Godhead, nor the hypostasis, nor the truth of our flesh, nor a human soul. He tears apart what must be joined in this most holy person, and confuses what is distinct, and weakens the power of redemption. Besides many other profane errors and all manner of delirious notions, he is, as your ministers, our brothers, say, alien to the Word of God and to the consensus of the orthodox Church. This is said with such confidence, presumption and obstinacy that the saying of the wise man appears true in him: "The impious man, when he comes into the depths, scorns." And likewise: "If you crush him in a mortar with a pestle, his folly will not depart from him." For he is neither humbled to modesty by being held captive, nor does he yield or acquiesce to the so clear, true and evident instructions of our brothers, by which his errors are refuted more plainly than light. Rather, like an angry serpent, he hisses again and again against Calvin, the most sincere servant of God, with abusive and insulting words, and blasphemes against the Lord, and at times tries to slip away slipperily. For he keeps insisting on the one and simple God, as if the true diversity of three hypostases in any way contradicted the simplicity of nature, and thus he would have the Church rage, which commends the Trinity to be venerated in unity and the unity in Trinity. Likewise, though he ascribes many things to Christ the Son of God, he plainly denies that the person is constant in two natures. According to the one nature, Christ was begotten by the Father from eternity and before the ages, and not only before the incarnation (as Scripture attests), since his going forth is from the days of eternity and through him the ages were made, and so his nature is to be reckoned in all respects. According to the other nature, he was born in time, flesh of our flesh, of the substance of the Virgin, in all things like his brothers. Therefore, however crafty he is, he is held fast by the foot of truth, and is caught in it. We remember that twenty-three years ago in this city, when the most outstanding Oecolampadius, the president of this Church, was dealing with this man, the matter was brought before him, and though he was seriously and repeatedly called to account in writing, nothing was amended. So already then that most wise man of God pronounced that he would bring grave loss to the Christian religion unless he were broken by the hand of the Lord. Since these things are so, most outstanding men, first of all you rightly give thanks to God the eternal Father of Jesus Christ, by whose kindness you have obtained the pure light of truth unextinguished, and the judgment of the Holy Spirit by which you strive to distinguish what is perverse and adulterated from the teaching of the true and genuine life. You also ought to beseech him with burning prayers, that he may preserve us in the sincerity of the faith, and strengthen us, so that we may remain stable and unmoved, as hitherto, against such horrible scandals and the assaults of Satan. Finally, as for Servetus, we exhort you to bring all zeal to healing him, in whatever way you seem to do, provided that the stumbling-blocks he has raised can themselves be healed. But if he persists incurably in the perversity once conceived, then, by your office and by the power granted you by the Lord, let him be restrained, so that he can no longer cause harm to the Church of Christ, and so that the last things do not become worse than the first. In this matter the Lord himself will supply the Spirit, strength and wisdom, for whom together with you we will pray earnestly and constantly, and with our Church. In turn we commend ourselves and our Church to your magnificence's favour and to your holy prayers. Farewell. From Basel, the eighteenth day of October, 1553.

units.la: V.A. In Domino dedititsimi Pastores Ecclesiæ Basiliensis.
units.tr: Your most devoted ministers of the Church of Basel, in the Lord.

units.la: CALVINVS FARELLO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO FAREL, GREETING

units.la: ECce tibi morem aliqua ex parte gero. Epistolæ loco breuiculum habebis, quod multum temporis non auferet. Rediit ab Heluetiis nuncius. Vno consensu pronunciant omnes, Seruetum impios errores, quibus olim turbauit Satan Ecclesiam, nunc renouasse, & monstrum esse non ferendum. Cordati Basilienses. Tigurini omnium vehementissimi. Nam & impietatum atrocitas grauiter ab illis exprimitur, & hortantur Senatum nostrum ad seueritatem. Subscribunt Schaphusiani. Bernesium literis etiam appositis, accedunt & Senatus literæ quibus non parum stimulati sunt nostri. Cæsar comicus, simulato per triduum morbo, in curiam tandem ascendit, vt sceleratū istum pœna eximeret. Neque enim erubuit petere, vt cognitio ad ducēs veniret: sine controuersia tamē damnatus est. Cras ad supplicium
units.tr: I am meeting your wish in some measure. You will have a little letter in place of a longer one, which will not take up much of your time. A messenger has come back from the Swiss. All of them unanimously declare that Servetus has revived the impious errors with which Satan once troubled the Church, and that he is a monster who must not be tolerated. The wise men of Basel take this view. The Zurichers are the most vehement of all, for they express the atrocity of his impieties forcefully and urge our Senate to severity. The people of Schaffhausen agree. The Bernese have added their letters, and the letters of their Senate have also goaded our people not a little. Caesar Comes, after feigning illness for three days, finally went up to the court to rescue that criminal from punishment. He was not ashamed to ask that the case be referred to the Two Hundred, but he was condemned all the same. Tomorrow he will be led to execution. They have tried to change the manner of his death, but in vain. What more we have accomplished I will defer to tell in person. Farewell, most upright brother and outstanding minister of Christ. May God keep and guide you always. Give my greetings to all our friends. Our people send you their greetings in return. Geneva, 26 October 1553.

units.la: Epist. 161. ducetur.Genus mortis conati fumus mutare, sed frustra.Cuc nihil profecerimus,coràm narrandum differo. Vale integerrime frater & Christi minister eximie.Deus te conseruet ac regat sem per. Amicis omnibus plurimam salutem. Nostri te resalutant. Geneuæ,xxvi.Octob. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Epist. 161. Farewell, most upright brother and outstanding minister of Christ. May God keep and guide you always. Give my greetings to all our friends. Our people send you their greetings in return. Geneva, 26 October 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS BVLINGERO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO BULLINGER, GREETING

units.la: Ntelligo ex tuis literis obseruâde frater,tibi non satis nota fuisse mala nostra,de quibus apud te cõqueftus fueram. Quia me improbi sciunt irritabilem esse, sæpius & variis modis stomachum mihi mouendo,patientiam excutere conati sunt. Tametsi vero difficilis mihi fuit lucta nunquam tamen adepti sunt quod captabant,vt de via deflecterem. Et iam ad omnes eorum punctiones pridem obdurui. Dominus enim ita me intra breue tempus in hac gente exercuit, vt multis experimentis didicerim, quàm multa Christi ministris ferenda sint. Idem quoque vt spero, qui me hactenus sustinuit, non minori in posterum fortitudine instruet. Quare eius auxilio fretus stationem in qua me locauit,nunquam volens deseram. Nec vero, cùm hic nuper esset Dominus Gualtherus, vllis contumeliis, vel indignitatibus fractus,ad cedendum me parabam:Sed quoniam ab improbis inita erat ratio,quà me inuirum extruderent. Quid im ob effrænes suas libidines, & multa flagitia, Cœnæ vsu priuatus donec resipisceret, contempto Ecclesiæ iudicio, volebat nihil ominus admitti: & cum palàm,sua contumacia, ius consistorij euerteret, obtinuerat à Senatu,quòd recusare mihi necesse fuit. Cæterùm, quia ferreum os hominis mihi notum erat: & data opera eum improbi mihi opposuerant, vt vel sua proteruia me vincerent, vel tumultum concitaret,Senatū admonui quid facturus essem. Peruicit deterior factio,vt nihil æqui impetrarem. Postridie adest frater noster Dominus Gualtherus, vbi me potiùs mortem obiturum denunciaui, quàm vt sacrum Domini panem canibus prostituerem: qui ex professo non sine Euangelij cranio ludibrio,Ecclesiæ ordinem pedibus calcare statuerunt.A prandio quid dixerim malo ex oratione ipsa intelligas, quàm Beza noster vertendam curauit. Ne quid mutatum putes:ego nunquam inspexi:Sed à notario sumpta est,qualem ex ore meo exceperat. Postea res agitata in Senatu fuit, vbi cùm superior esset bona causa,destiterunt paulisper qui res turbatas cupiût, donec tumultuandi magis opportunum esset tempus. Instat autem solennis Comitiorum dies,vbi aliquid proculdubio tentabunt.Sed faciet Dominus,vt peruersi eorum conatus euanescant.Mihi discipli-nam,quæ hic & Senatus,& populi decreto recepta est,morte potius tius farcire certum est,quàm vt me videntę labefaćtari patiar. Si me ab officio prohibeant, coactus potius discedam,quàm libertate me abdicem , qua perdita Ministerium meum concideret. Nec verò ita ferreus sum, quin me excruciet horrenda,quà prospicio futuram, gregis dissipatio. Sed dum reputo quid mihi liceat,in proposito confirmor.Tu quod facis,precibus nos iuuare perges,vt hoc ouile sibi Christus conferuet. Iam agitur oćtauus dies, exquo à vobis rediit nuntius. Quantùm pro fideli vestra opera,cordatóque responso hæc Ecclesia debeat, verbis assequi nequeo.Iam verò quòd de me,& collegis meis tam amanter,& honorificè in doćtrinæ nostræ commedationem loquuti estis, hoc nomine priuatim nos vobis obstrićtos agnoscimus,&non vulgarem habemus gratiam.Vtinam mutuis officiis certare nobis daretur.Sed vos animis nostris scimus esse contentos. Quid de homine futurum fit,nondum scitur.Quantùm tamen coniećturis assequor,cras feretur in curia iudicium:perendie verò ad supplicium ducetur.In Gallia res nihilò melius habent,quàm solebant. Vbi sæuiendi est materia,sanguini non parcunt. Dtuione breui tres exurent,nisi forte id iam factum fit. Et periculum est,ne Scotiæ motus incendium exasperent. Hoc ideo commemoro,vt miseri fratres vobis sint commendati. Nemaufi enim septem, vel octo teneri in vinculis allatum est.In aliis Gallię vt bibus complures sunt. Vale ornatissime vir, & frater mihi plurimùm colende.Saluta diligenter Symmystas,vxorem,generos, & filios. Dominus vobis semper adsit,vos tueatur,& Spiritu suo regat.Collegæ mei plurimam vobis salutem dicunt. Geneuæ,v 1. Calend. Nouemb. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: I understand from your letter, honoured brother, that you were not fully aware of the troubles about which I had complained to you. Because the wicked know that I am irritable, they have tried in many ways, and more than once, to stir my temper and so wear down my patience. Yet although the struggle has been hard for me, they have never achieved what they were aiming at, namely to turn me from my course, and by now I have long been hardened against all their jabs. For the Lord has so exercised me among this people within a short time that I have learned by many experiences how much a minister of Christ must endure. I trust that the same Lord, who has sustained me until now, will equip me in future with no less fortitude. So, relying on his help, I will never willingly abandon the post in which he has placed me. Indeed, when Brother Gualter was here recently, I was not broken by any insults or indignities and was not preparing to give way. Rather, the wicked had devised a plan by which they might thrust me out. Since they wanted, on account of his unbridled desires and many scandals, to admit to the Lord's Supper a man who was barred from it until he repented, they meant to override the judgment of the Church. Openly, in their obstinacy, they were overturning the authority of the consistory, and they had obtained from the Senate something I had to refuse. But because I knew the iron face of that man, and because the wicked had deliberately set him against me, so that either by his insolence they might defeat me or stir up a tumult, I warned the Senate what I would do. The worse faction prevailed, so that I obtained nothing fair. The next day our brother Gualter arrived, and there I declared that I would sooner die than give the holy bread of the Lord to dogs. They decided, quite deliberately and not without mockery of the Gospel, to trample the order of the Church underfoot. As to what I said after dinner, you may better learn it from the speech itself, which our Beza took care to have translated. Do not think anything was altered: I never looked at it. It was taken down by a notary, just as he had caught it from my mouth. Afterwards the matter was taken up in the Senate, where, since the good cause prevailed, those who wish to stir up trouble held back for a little while, until the time was more suitable for rioting. The solemn day of the elections is approaching, when they will undoubtedly attempt something. But the Lord will make their perverse efforts come to nothing. I am resolved to defend with death the discipline which has been received here by decree of both the Senate and the people, rather than allow it to be weakened while I am watching. If they forbid me to perform my office, I shall be compelled to leave rather than give up my freedom, and once that is lost my ministry would collapse. Nor am I so iron-hearted that I am not tormented by the dreadful dispersal of the flock which I foresee. But as I consider what is permitted to me, I am strengthened in my purpose. As for you, continue to help us with your prayers, that Christ may preserve this fold for himself. It is now the eighth day since the messenger returned from you. I cannot express in words how much this Church owes to your faithful work and your wise reply. Moreover, since you have spoken of me and my colleagues so warmly and honourably in commending our teaching, we acknowledge that we are bound to you on this account, and we hold your favour in no common regard. I wish we were allowed to compete with you in mutual services, but we know that you are content with our hearts. What will become of the man is not yet known. As far as I can conjecture, the judgment will be delivered in court tomorrow, and the day after he will be led to execution. In France things are no better than they used to be. Where there is matter for cruelty, they do not spare blood. In a short time three will be burned, unless perhaps this has already happened. And there is a danger that the uprising in Scotland may inflame the fire further. I mention this so that you may commend the poor brothers to God. It has been reported that seven or eight young men are held in chains at Nîmes, and there are many in other prisons of France. Farewell, most distinguished man and brother whom I greatly respect. Give my careful greetings to your fellow-ministers, your wife, your sons-in-law and your sons. May the Lord always be with you, keep you, and rule you by his Spirit. My colleagues send you their warmest greetings. Geneva, 1 November 1553.

units.la: AMPLISSIMIS VIRIS SYNDICIS SENATVIQVE Reipub.Genevensis Dominis,& Conciuibus nostris colendissimis.
units.tr: To the most distinguished men, the Syndics and Senate of the Republic of Geneva, our most honoured lords and fellow citizens.

units.la: Gratiam & Pacem à Deo Patre nostro & Domino Iesu Christo.
units.tr: Grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: QVA denuo molestia, viri amplissimi, domini & amici in Christo venerandi,Ecclesia vestra turbetur ex scriptis,quæ misistis,abundè satis intelleximus. Videmus Satanam pertinacissimè hoc agere,vt emergentem veritatis lucem mille modis impetat:etsi extinguere nequeat, inductis saltem perniciosorum,& intricatorum dogmatum nebulis obscuret.Quòd ad prę sentė Serueti causam attinet,inspeximus illius dogmata, quoad eius fieri potuit,eo temporis spatio,quo tabellarius vester hic apud nos substitit. Et quoniam sententiam nostram exposcitis, s.j.
units.tr: We have understood well enough from the writings you sent that your Church is once again troubled, distinguished sirs, lords and venerable friends in Christ. We see that Satan is pursuing this with the utmost persistence, attacking the rising light of truth in a thousand ways; and although he cannot extinguish it, he at least tries to obscure it by spreading the clouds of pernicious and tangled doctrines. As for the present case of Servetus, we have examined his teachings, as far as it was possible in the time that your messenger has stayed with us here. And since you ask for our opinion, we have thought it best to reply briefly to your petition, on the basis of what we have found in Servetus' writings.

units.la: Epist. 1. ad ea quæ in scriptis Serveti deprehendimus, paucis visum est ad petitionem vestram respondere. Vt coram Domino loquamur, non possumus per conscientias nostras probare, quæ homo iste de substantia, ac forma Deitatis, de sanctæ Trinitatis mysterio, de verbo Dei, & illius incarnatione, de anima & carne Christi, de Spiritu Sancto, de Angelis, de animabus, & spiritibus nostris, de peccato mortali, de pædobaptismate non solum in corde suo sentire, sed editis scriptis non iam primum, sed olim dogmatizare coepit. Videmus hominem sibi ipsi tribuere plurimum, & parum spirare modestiæ. Permittit enim sibi liberum, quoties religionis nostræ capita vocare in quæstionem, & omnia vel novis expositionibus inuertere, vel renovata veterum hæreticorum labe prorsus corrumpere. Sic resuscitat nobis Sabellianos, Noetianos, Priscillianistas, Anthropomorphitas, Apollinaristas, Valentinianos: & ne à fanaticis nostrorum temporum fœdis abhorrere videatur, Baptismum infantum horrendis modis flagellat, & abominabilem reddere conatur: vt reliqua taceamus, quæ de suo in medium afferre non dubitat. Arbitramur autem pro vigilantia Ministrorum vestrorum omnia hæc satis esse in lucem producta, & reprehensa, nec id à vobis agi, vt examinationem huius causæ exactiorem ab aliis diuini verbi Ministris, quam à vestris recipiatis. Quare absque vllo tractatu sententiam nostram paucis assignare visum est, ne de fratrum nostrorum studio, & vigilantia quicquam addubitare videamur. Oramus Dominum, vt det vobis Spiritum prudentiæ, consilii & fortitudinis, vt & pe stem hanc ab Ecclesiis cum vestra, tum aliis auertatis: & simul nihil remittatis, quod Magistratui Christiano inconuenies censeri possit. Dominus Ecclesiam, & rempub. vestram in vera pietate, & pace iugiter seruet immotam. Bernæ. Vestri in Domino.
units.tr: To speak before the Lord, we cannot in good conscience affirm that this man does not merely think, in his heart, but has already begun to teach in published writings, and not for the first time, what he holds concerning the substance and form of the Godhead, the mystery of the holy Trinity, the Word of God and his incarnation, the soul and flesh of Christ, the Holy Spirit, the angels, souls and our spirits, mortal sin, and infant baptism. We see that the man thinks very highly of himself and breathes little modesty. For he allows himself the freedom, whenever he pleases, to call the articles of our religion into question and either to overturn them all with new interpretations or to corrupt them utterly with the revived stain of the old heretics. In this way he brings back to life for us the Sabellians, Noetians, Priscillianists, Anthropomorphites, Apollinarians and Valentinians; and, lest he seem to shrink from the foul fanaticisms of our own times, he lashes infant baptism in horrible ways and tries to make it detestable. We say nothing of the rest, which he does not hesitate to bring forward from his own resources. We judge, however, that thanks to the vigilance of your ministers all these things have been sufficiently brought to light and refuted, and that you are not seeking a more exact examination of this cause from other ministers of the divine Word than you have received from your own. Therefore we have thought it right to state our opinion briefly, without any lengthy discussion, lest we seem to doubt the zeal and vigilance of our brothers. We pray the Lord to give you the spirit of prudence, counsel and courage, so that you may turn this plague away from the Churches, both your own and others; and at the same time that you neglect nothing which could be judged unbecoming to a Christian magistrate. May the Lord keep your Church and commonwealth constantly unshaken in true piety and peace.

units.la: M. D. LIII.
units.tr: From Bern. Yours in the Lord.

units.la: Ministri Ecclesiæ Bernensis.
units.tr: The ministers of the Church of Bern.

units.la: CALVINVS BVLINGERO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO BULLINGER, GREETING

units.la: ENvobis iterum nouus labor. Disciplinam Ecclesiæ, quæ hic mediocris est, iam per integros septem annos oppugnant, quicunque cuperent sine iugo lasciuire. Sed homines dissoluti ex vulgo non tantum nobis facerent negotij, nisi duces haberent, qui ex eorum licentia sibi potentiam quærunt. Iam eo ventum est, vt labi factetur quicquid hactenus ordinis Ecclesiastici viguit, nisi iam afferatur remedium. Atque hac de causa non dubitauit optimus frater noster Dominus Budæus, hoc aspero anni tempore profectionem ad vos suscipere, vt vos de toto negotio admoneat. Breuis tamen summa est, vt amplissimus Senatus vester, verbo Dei consentaneam esse respondeat,quam hactenus fequuti fumus formam : deinde nouitatem improbet. Reliqua ex literis communibus intelliges, quas tamen ea lege scripsi,vt fi non expediat longius proferri,nominatim D. Gual-thero eas communices.Tuo iudicio totum hoc permitto. Si duo illa capita per vos impetro, vt leges nostras Senatus vester suo suffragio confirmet omni ambiguitate praecisa, & a nouitatis studio nostros deterreat, huic Ecclesiae in longum tempus parta erit quies.Literas meas tibi pridem redditas esse confido, in quibus gratias vobis omnibus agebam meo,& fratrum nomine pro fideli,sanctoque responso,quod in Serueti causa dedisti.Praeclara illa commendatio, qua nos ornaftis, apud bonos suum habuit pondus: effraenes ac perditos nondum frenare potuit, vt vides. Breui tamen spero meliora,fi istinc iuuabimur. Librum Serueti, & farraginem illam,quam petebas,ciuis quidam vester ad te tulit.De misera Angliae vastitate plura scis,quam expediat.Itaque a scribendo supersedeo. Vale ornatissime vir, & venerande frater. D.Gualthero,vxori tuae, genetis, & fidelibus salutem plurimam.Dominus vos omnes tueatur suo praesidio,& Spiritu regat. Geneuae,xxvi.Nouemb. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: Once again you have a new labour. For a full seven years now, those who wanted to revel without a yoke have been attacking the discipline of our Church, which here is only moderate. They would give us far less trouble if they did not have leaders who seek power for themselves through the licence of the common people. We have now reached the point where everything that has so far flourished in our church order is confessed to be collapsing, unless a remedy is applied at once. For this reason our excellent brother, Lord Budaeus, did not hesitate to undertake this journey to you in the harsh season of the year, so that he may lay the whole matter before you. The sum, however, is brief: that your most distinguished Senate should declare that the form we have hitherto followed is consistent with the Word of God, and then condemn the innovation. You will learn the rest from the joint letters, which I wrote on the condition that, if it is not advisable for them to be delayed further, you should share them with Lord Gualtherus by name. I leave all this to your judgement. If you obtain from your Senate, through your influence, those two points, namely that it confirm our laws by its vote with all ambiguity removed and deter our people from the zeal for innovation, then rest will be secured for this Church for a long time. I trust that my letter was handed to you some time ago, in which I thanked you all, in my own name and in the name of the brethren, for the faithful and holy reply you gave in the case of Servetus. That splendid commendation with which you honoured us carried weight with good men; it has not yet been able to restrain the unbridled and the depraved, as you see. Yet I hope for better things soon, if we are helped from there. A certain citizen of yours has brought you the book of Servetus and that medley you were asking for. You know more than is useful about the wretched devastation of England. So I refrain from writing further. Farewell, most distinguished man and venerable brother. Give my warmest greetings to Lord Gualtherus, to your wife, to your children and to the faithful. May the Lord keep you all under his protection and rule you by his Spirit. Geneva, 26 November 1553.

units.la: CALVINVS TIGVRINIS MINISTRIS Fratribus ac Symmyftis pl. obser-uandis S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO THE MINISTERS OF ZURICH, his brethren and fellow-ministers, to be held in high regard, greeting

units.la: ME quidem valde pudet,optimi & ex animo colédi fratres, cum nuper vobis in Serueti causa molestus fuerit Senatus noster,nouum iam rursus negotium exhibet. Est tamen aliqua eius rei iusta excusatio. Nam cum fe ferocius iactet quorundam improbitas, quam vt ad resistendum pares sint,qui recte pieque sentiunt,subsidium a vobis petere coguntur. Ego vero vt maxime vobis parcere cupiam ,ceflandum tamen in tanta necessitate non putaui.Ex quo ad hanc Ecclesia reuersus sum, disciplinae forma fi non perfecta,& qualis optanda foret,saltem tolerabilis viguit.Institutum enim erat Consistorium quod regendis moribus praeesset. Nulla in eo ciuilis iurisdictio,sed tantum reprehensiones ex verbo Domini: vltima vero poena, excommunicatio.Inter alia certamina,quae nobis subinde per continuum triennium mouerunt Satanae ministri, hoc nos violenter exercuit, quod quidam perditae impudentiae nebulo, contra Ecclesiae iudicium ad sacram mensam prorumpere conatus,vbi nos constanter furori suo resistere vidit,vrbem impleuit magno tumultu. Nec vero difficile hoc illi fuit, cum ab impiorum factione ad hanc fabulam agendam delectus foret. Et quia non
units.tr: I am truly ashamed, most excellent brothers and sincerely esteemed friends, that after our Senate lately gave you trouble in the matter of Servetus, it now presents you with a new business. There is, however, some just excuse for it. Since the wickedness of certain men boasts so fiercely that those who think rightly and piously are not equal to resisting it, they are forced to seek help from you. Although I most wish to spare you, I did not think I could hold back in such great necessity. Since I returned to this Church, a form of discipline has flourished that, if not perfect and such as one would wish, was at least bearable. For a Consistory was established to preside over the regulation of morals. It has no civil jurisdiction, only rebukes from the word of the Lord, and the final penalty is excommunication. Among the other conflicts which the ministers of Satan have stirred up against us from time to time over three continuous years, this one troubled us most violently: a certain scoundrel of desperate impudence, trying to break into the sacred table against the judgment of the Church, filled the city with great tumult when he saw us steadfastly resisting his fury. Nor was this difficult for him, since he had been chosen by the faction of the impious to play this part. And since not only did he have the same patrons, whom they were not ashamed to champion loudly in Servetus' cause, but also companions and instigators, with the utmost vehemence and such intemperance was it accomplished by them that the greater Senate suddenly overturned the order of the Church which had been received and kept until now.

units.la: f.ij. modò eosdem habebat patronos, quos Serueti causam clamosè tueri non puduit, sed etiam socios atque auctores, summa contentione, adeoque intemperie ab illis effectum est, vt Maior Senatus receptum, & hactenus seruatum Ecclesiæ ordinem repente conuelleret. Nos iterum restitimus. Qui errore lapsi fuerant, decernunt petendum esse ab Helueticis Ecclesiis consiliu. Quanquam autem ad vos non scribitur, quia tamen certum est, Clarissimi Senatus vestri responsum non nisi ex sententia vestra fore, ego vos in tempore monendos ac rogandos censui. Et optimus vir, ac imprimis cordatus, mihique vnicè dilectus frater profectionem hanc aduerso anni tempore, laboris & molestiæ plenam libenter suscepit Ecclesiæ nomine. Primum igitur vos per Christi nomen obtestor, vt cogitetis non vulgare aliquod negotium vobis tradendum esse; sed de toto huius Ecclesiæ statu consultationem haberi. Ego enim quod perfidæ ignauiæ esse arbitror, quandiu hanc perfidam sustineo, non acriter ad extremum vsque pugnare pro sancta & legitima disciplina, centies è vita potius, nedum ex hoc loco migrare statui, quàm vt patiar impie labefactari, quod ex Dei verbo sumptum esse probè cognosco. De excommunicatione non omnes hodie idem sentiunt. Nec me latet pios & doctos esse homines, quibus sub Christianis principibus non videtur necessaria esse excommunicatio. Atqui neminem fore confido sanæ mentis, rectìque studij, qui eius vsum improbet. Mihi certè non obscura est Christi doctrina. Sicubi à plebe impetrari non poterit, vt hoc Christi iugum suscipiat, post quam strenuè eo incubuerint Pastores, alia est eorum ratio, quàm nostra. Nimis enim turpe esset, ædificium quod nobis tuendum Christus commisit, viuis & videntibus nobis dirui, ac euerti. Nec vero or, vt pertinaciæ damnetis meum studium, vbi perspecta fuerit, quàm hactenus sequuti fumus ratio & quam nobis impij ceperunt moliuntur. Quòd si vobis liquebit nihil in ea contineri, nisi puræ Christi doctrinæ consentaneum, obsecro da te operam, vt idem testetur clarissimus Senatus vester. Hoc enim præcipuum est, vt intelligant nostri homines nouitatem, quam affectant, se non posse consequi, quin discedant à Christi regula, vel, si hoc durius videtur, quin defledant. Superest vt D. Budæus quod literis compleati non satis sit, coram vobis exponat. Dominus mihi & Collegis meis è cœlo testis erit, nihil ab annis quatuor omissum fuisse ab improbis hominibus, quò paulatim mediocrem huius Ecclesiæ statum possumus fundarent. Clandestinas eorum machinationes ab initio perspexi. Verùm, non habeo quid dicam, nisi quòd Dominus flagella parabat coram oculis nostris, vt timorem incuteret nos ad se reuocaret. Quia verò surdi, & cæci eramus, remedio locus non fuit. A biennio autem non alia fuit nostra conditio, quam si inter professos Euangelij hostes versandum nobis foret. Nunc extremus actus agitur. Multis enim victoriis potiti Euangelij hostes, magnificum de Christo, eiusque doctrina, & Ministris, denique membris omnibus triumphum agere cogitant. Quàm inhumaniter, contumeliose, & barbarè vexauerint Christi exules, quos in fidem suam receperant, dicere supersedeo. Quàm placidè, modestè & patienter omnes indignitates deuorauerint, quibus asylum in promptu erat, ne ipsi quidem iniuriarum auctores negare poterunt. Nunc ad summum peruenit nequitia, vt omni pudore excusso, templū Domini in lupanar conuertere obstinatè cupiāt. Atque vt sciatis, quàm foeda sit deformitas, cum hic nuper esset frater noster Farellus, cui se totos debent, vt satis nostis, & pro iure suo eos liberè monueret, tantus in eum furor exarsit, vt capitale iudicium in eum intentare non sint veriti. Scio equidem non debere nouum videri, si reperiantur in vrbe libera factiosi homines, qui turbas concitent. Sed deplorāda est Senatus nostri caecitas, quòd libertatis suae patrem, & patrem huius Ecclesiae sibi reum causae capitalis mitti à Neocomensibus poposcit. Dedecus huius vrbis proferre cogor, quod sanguine meo delere cuperem. Venit Farellus: antequam vrbem ingressus esset, denuntiauit domi meae Apparitor Senatus, ne suggestum cōscenderet. Reliqua non persequor: quia satis est eius ingratitudinis gustum dedisse, quae bonis omnibus, & ingenuis merito stomachum mouebit. Sed quoniam me complures causae impediūt, ne mala nostra aperte deplorem, sic breuiter habete, nisi per vos cohibeatur Satan, habenas ei laxatum iri. Perinde ergo sa agere vos decet, ac si in manu vestra essest huius Ecclesiae status. Nec morositate nostra fiet, vt loco potius cedamus, quàm sententia. Omnes enim boni nunt, vt turbis obuiam iremus, hactenus nos fuisse plus satis flexibiles: cùm tamen minimè dubium foret, patientiam nostram ab improbis tentari. Hanc autem victoriam illis tradere non licet, quin scientes & volentes totum ius Ecclesiae prodamus: nō modò quia pestum ibit Ministerij nostri auctoritas: sed quia foedissimis quibusque probris subiectum erit Christi nomen, effrenis malorum omnium licentia magis ac magis insolescet, piorum conditio non modò iniuriis quibusque obnoxia, sed prorsus afflicta miserè iacebit. Quò certius confido vobis curae fore, vt suffragio vestro subleuati qui hic sunt fideles, Deum paulò quietius colant. Valete optimi, & verè mihi colendi fratres. Dominus vobis adsit & Spiritu suo vos regat, prudentiamque suppediret, quae non tuendae modò vestrae Ecclesiae sufficiat, sed aliis quoque fulciendis. Collegae mei vos diligenter salutant, & commendant, quàm potuunt studiosissimè hanc Ecclefiam vestræ fidei, & prudentiæ. Geneuæ, xxvi. Nouembris. M. D. LIII.
units.tr: f.ij. Not only did these men have the same patrons, whom it was not ashamed to defend Servetus's cause loudly, but they were also their allies and instigators. With great zeal, and such recklessness, they brought it about that the Greater Council suddenly overturned the order of the Church that had been accepted and kept until now. We have resisted again. Those who had fallen into error have decreed that counsel must be sought from the Helvetic Churches. Although we are not writing to you, since it is certain that the answer of your most illustrious Senate will be nothing other than your own opinion, I have thought that you should be warned and asked in good time. And an excellent man, and above all a wise one, and my dearest brother, has willingly undertaken this journey in the name of the Church, at an unfavourable season of the year, full of toil and trouble. First, then, I beg you by the name of Christ to consider that the matter entrusted to you is no ordinary one, but that the whole condition of this Church is to be deliberated upon. For I judge it a faithless cowardice, as long as I remain in this place, not to fight fiercely to the very end for holy and lawful discipline; I have resolved to be cut down a hundred times rather than to depart from here, and I shall not suffer what I clearly know has been taken from the Word of God to be impiously overthrown. Today not everyone thinks the same about excommunication. I am not unaware that there are pious and learned men who do not think excommunication necessary under Christian princes. Yet I am confident that no one of sound mind and right zeal will disapprove of its use. For my part, the teaching of Christ is not unclear to me. If the common people cannot be brought to take up this yoke of Christ, after the ministers have strenuously applied themselves to it, then their reasoning is different from ours. For it would be too shameful for the building that Christ has committed to us to keep safe to be torn down and overturned while we are alive and looking on. Nor do I pray that you condemn my zeal as obstinacy when it has been fully examined, how far we have followed reason until now and what the wicked have devised against us. But if it shall be clear to you that nothing in it is contained other than what agrees with the pure doctrine of Christ, I beg you to take care that your most illustrious Senate bears witness to the same. For this is the chief thing, that our people understand that they cannot attain the novelty they aspire to without departing from the rule of Christ, or, if this seems too harsh, without falling back. It remains that Master Budaeus should set out in person before you what is not sufficiently complete in letters. The Lord, from heaven, will be witness to me and my colleagues that for these four years wicked men have left nothing undone by which they might gradually undermine the moderate condition of this Church. I saw their secret schemes from the beginning. But I have nothing to say except that the Lord was preparing scourges before our eyes to strike us with fear and call us back to himself. But because we were deaf and blind, there was no room for a remedy. For the past two years our condition has been no different than if we had to live among open enemies of the Gospel. Now the final act is being played out. For the enemies of the Gospel, having gained many victories, are thinking of celebrating a magnificent triumph over Christ, his doctrine, the ministers, and finally all his members. I shall say nothing of how inhumanly, insultingly and barbarously they have harassed the exiles of Christ whom they had received under their protection. How calmly, modestly and patiently everyone has swallowed all the indignities, when a refuge was ready at hand, even the authors of the injuries themselves will not be able to deny. Now wickedness has reached its height, so that, with all shame cast off, they are stubbornly eager to turn the temple of the Lord into a brothel. And so that you may know how foul this deformity is: when our brother Farel, to whom they owe themselves wholly, as you well know, was here recently and freely admonished them in accordance with his right, such fury blazed up against him that they did not hesitate to bring a capital charge against him. I know indeed that it ought not to seem new if factious men are found in a free city who stir up disturbances. But the blindness of our Senate is to be lamented, in that it demanded that the father of its liberty and the father of this Church be sent to it by the people of Neuchâtel as a defendant in a capital case. I am forced to bring forward the disgrace of this city, which I would gladly wipe out with my own blood. Farel came; before he had entered the city, an usher of the Senate forbade him at my house to mount the pulpit. I do not pursue the rest, because it is enough to have given a taste of this ingratitude, which will rightly stir the disgust of all good and honourable men. But since many reasons prevent me from openly lamenting our troubles, take this briefly: unless Satan is restrained through you, he will be given free rein. Therefore you ought to act as if the state of this Church were in your hand. Nor will it be through any obstinacy on our part that we give ground rather than yield in judgement. For all good men know that we have hitherto been more than flexible in meeting disturbances, though there is no doubt that our patience is being tested by the wicked. But it is not permitted to hand this victory over to them, unless we knowingly and willingly betray the whole right of the Church; not only because the authority of our ministry will perish, but because the name of Christ will be subjected to the foulest reproaches, and the unbridled licence of all evils will grow ever more insolent, and the condition of the pious will not only be exposed to every kind of injury but will lie utterly wretched and afflicted. The more surely do I trust that you will take care, so that those faithful who are here, relieved by your support, may worship God a little more quietly. Farewell, best and truly honoured brothers. May the Lord be with you, govern you by his Spirit, and supply you with prudence sufficient not only to protect your own Church but also to support others. My colleagues greet you warmly and commend this Church to your faith and prudence as earnestly as they can. Geneva, 26 November 1553.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus vester.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: Bvlingervs Calvino s. d.
units.tr: Bullinger to Calvin, greeting.

units.la: BReues Amplissimus Magistratus Geneuensis literas ad clarissimum vrbis nostræ Senatum scripsit. Quia vero Gallicè scriptæ erant, ornatissimus D. Consul Gualtero nostro vertedas in Germanicum misit: ita factum est vt & ego viderim & legerim. Tres proponunt quæstiones nostratibus. 1. Quomodo ex præcepto Dei & secundum Scripturas illibatámque religionem exercenda sit excommunicatio. 2. An non alia ratione quàm per Consistorium exerceri possit. 3. Quid hac in re in Ecclesia nostra fiat. Lectæ sunt in frequenti Senatu literæ: mox deputati sunt D.Cof.& ex Senatoribus illustres viri tres, qui à scitis tribus huius Ecclesiæ Pastoribus de responsione commoda danda cōsultarent. Consultauerunt & concorditer omnes consenserunt, scribendū Amplissimo Senatui Geneuensi, dolere nobis sic ipsorum turbari Ecclesiam, vt lis & contentio ex lite & contentione fieret. Dudum audiuisse nos de legibus istius Ecclesiæ Consistorialibus, & agnoscere illas pias esse, & accedere ad verbi Dei prescriptum: ideóque non videri admittendum vt per innouationē mutentur. Satius esse vt integræ conseruentur, hoc præsertim seculo, in quo subinde homines fiunt deteriores. Et quamquam nostra disciplina vestræ per omnia non respondeat, illam tamen pro ratione temporum, locorum & personarum esse temperatam, nec ideo vestram velle subuertere. Quoniam vero quid à nostris fiat, vestri scire postulárunt, paucis consignata summa mittitur. Hæc hodie concorditer statuta sunt, & cras responsio hæc ad totum referetur Senatum. An hic illam probaturus an reprobaturus sit ignoro. Dominum ex animo oro, vt omnia bene vertat ad gloriam nominis sui. Nos certè summis annixi viribus laborauimus, ne quid fieret à nostris quod in derogatione bonarum legum Ecclesiæ vestræ tenderet. Vos quoque hortamur, vt pergatis esse fideles Domino, & modum adhibeatis rebus omnibus, ne rigore nimio perdatis quos seruat s cupit Dominus, qui arundinem comminutam non confringit, neque linum fumigans extinguit. Vale vir colendissime & frater in D.charissime. Valeat æternum Budæus noster. Valeat Comes à Martinegis & cum his D.Gallasius & reliqui symmystæ & fratres. Festinantissimè Tigùri xii. Decembr. M. D. LIII. Iam mittitur ad me copia, vt vocant, literarum ex Amplissimo Senatu nostro:
units.tr: The most distinguished Council of the Geneva magistracy recently wrote a letter to the very illustrious Senate of our city. Since it was written in French, the most distinguished Consul sent it to our Gualther to be translated into German, so that both I and others could read it. It puts three questions to our people: (1) how excommunication is to be exercised according to the command of God and the Scriptures, and with the pure religion preserved; (2) whether it can be exercised in some way other than through the Consistory; (3) what is done in this matter in your Church. The letter was read in a full Senate. Shortly afterwards, Councillor D. Cof. and three distinguished men from the Senate were appointed to consult the three learned ministers of this Church and to give a suitable answer.
