They consulted, and all agreed unanimously that it should be written to the most honourable Geneva Senate that we grieve that your Church is so disturbed, so that strife and contention arise out of strife and contention. We have long heard about the Consistorial laws of your Church, and we recognise that they are pious and agree with the prescription of God's Word. Therefore it does not seem right that they should be changed by innovation. It is better that they be preserved whole, especially in this age, in which men are constantly becoming worse. And although our discipline does not in every respect match yours, it is nonetheless tempered to the circumstances of times, places and persons, and we do not therefore wish to overturn yours. Since your men have asked to know what is done among us, a summary, set down briefly, is sent. These things were agreed upon today unanimously, and tomorrow this response will be referred to the whole Senate. I do not know whether it will approve or disapprove it. I earnestly pray the Lord that he turn everything to the glory of his name. We, for our part, have laboured with the utmost effort that nothing be done by our men that tends to detract from the good laws of your Church. We also urge you to continue faithful to the Lord, and to observe moderation in all things, lest by excessive rigour you lose those whom the Lord desires to save, who does not break the bruised reed nor quench the smoking flax. Farewell, most esteemed sir and brother most dear in the Lord. May our Budaeus live forever. May the Count of Martinengo live, and with him D. Gallasius and the other fellow-initiates and brothers. Written in great haste at Zurich, 12 December 1553. Now a copy, as they call it, of the letter from our most distinguished Senate has been sent to me, and at the same time it is announced that the Senate yesterday approved the response prepared by us.

units.la: Epist.166. stro:simul nuntiatur approbasse Senatum heri à nobis paratum responsum. Video in summa nihil vtriusque scriptum publicum Senatus, ab iis quae heri in hisce consignaui literis: imò vestros studiose hortantur, vt in his permaneant, quae semel sunt recepta. Nos nostrae disciplinae formam non mittere vt vel tantillum praescribamus, praestare vt in senel receptis & sanctè quidem ex Scriptura receptis perseueren: Ecclesiae. Protinus ergo iam scribo literas D.Simperto Voghio,& D.Simoni Sulcero Pastoribus Schaffus.& Basil.Ecclesiae,de concordi responso Magistratus nostri,ne quid huius isti ignorent, vt & ipsi pacem quaerant & aedificationem Ecclesiae Genevensis, licet non per omnia similia habeant in suis Ecclesiis. Dominus per Spiritum suum benedicat negotio huic & dirigat corda vestra in viam pacis. Amen Amen. Iam scribam & Bernam ad D.Hallerum & Musculum.His istas mitto,orans,vt mature curent ad te perferri. Amanos in Domino mi Caluine & ora pro nobis vnà cum fratribus. Saluus sit optimus senex & optimè meritus de Ecclesia D.Farellus,primus istarum partium Apostolus.Vide mi Caluine vt diligenter & piè omnibus piis describas Seruetum cum suo exitu,vt omnes abhorreant à bestia.Tigurì x111.Decemb. Salutant te ac tuos nostri omnes.
units.tr: Epist.166. I see in summary that the public writing of the Senate of each side contains nothing from what I set down in these letters yesterday; rather, they earnestly urge yours to remain in those things that have once been accepted. We do not send the form of our discipline in order to prescribe even the slightest thing, but to ensure that your Church persists in those things that have once been received, and rightly received from Scripture. Therefore I am now immediately writing letters to D. Simpert Vogt and D. Simon Sulzer, ministers of the Churches of Schaffhausen and Basel, about the unanimous response of our magistracy, so that they may know nothing of this matter is hidden from them, so that they too may seek peace and the edification of the Church of Geneva, even if they do not have all things similar in their own Churches. May the Lord by his Spirit bless this business and direct your hearts into the way of peace. Amen, amen. I will now also write to Bern, to D. Haller and Musculus. I am sending these to you, praying that they be quickly arranged to reach you. Farewell in the Lord, my dear Calvin, and pray for us together with the brethren. May the excellent old man and one most deserving of the Church, D. Farel, the first apostle of those parts, be safe. See, my Calvin, that you diligently and piously describe Servetus with his end for all the pious, so that all may shrink from that beast. Zurich, 13 December. All our people greet you and yours.

units.la: SVMMA QVAEDAM CAPITA DISCIPLINAE Ecclesiasticae Genevensis.
units.tr: Some Summary Chapters of the Ecclesiastical Discipline of Geneva.

units.la: IAM elapsi sunt anni duodecim, ex quo instituta fuit Geneuae habendi Consistorij ratio, & praescriptae leges: quas non modo tulit Senatus, sed to us populus suis suffragiis recepit, ac sanciuit.Vnde fideliter, & ad verbum excerpta sunt capita, quae sequuntur.
units.tr: Twelve years have now passed since the arrangement for holding the Consistory was established at Geneva, and the rules were prescribed. These were not only enacted by the Senate, but the people also received and ratified them by their votes. Accordingly, the chapters that follow have been faithfully and word for word excerpted.

units.la: Si quis dogmata spargat receptae in Ecclesia doctrinę contraria, amicè & fraternè moneatur:si acquiescat,remittatur sine vlla infamiae nota: si peruicax fuerit, vel pertinacius addictus sit erroris suo,serio moneatur,donec iudicet Consistorium maiori seueritate opus esse:ac tunc quidem interdicatur illi vsus Coenę, & deferatur ad Senatum.
units.tr: If anyone spreads opinions contrary to the doctrine received in the Church, let him be admonished in a friendly and brotherly way. If he submits, let him be dismissed without any mark of infamy. If he is obstinate, or is more stubbornly attached to his error, let him be seriously admonished until the Consistory judges that greater severity is needed; then indeed let him be forbidden the use of the Supper, and be referred to the Senate.

units.la: Si qui sacros conuentus negligant, vt palam appareat id contemptu fieri:vt si qui Ecclesiasticum ordinem spernat,vt talium exemplo vilescat,& pessum eat fidelium communio:illi ad Consistorium vocati, moneantur. Qui sunt dociles & morigeros praeburerint, amicè remittantur domum. Si quos obstinatè in deterius pergant,postquam ter fuerint monit', prohibeantur ab usu Coenae Sacramenti indicetur.
units.tr: If any neglect the sacred assemblies, so that it clearly appears that this is done out of contempt, or if anyone spurns the ecclesiastical order, so that by the example of such men it becomes cheap and the fellowship of the faithful goes to ruin, let them be summoned before the Consistory and admonished. Those who show themselves teachable and compliant are to be sent home kindly. If any persist obstinately in worse conduct after being admonished three times, let them be prohibited from the use of the Sacrament of the Supper and so declared.

units.la: Quòd ad singulorum vitam spectat, teneatur in corrigédis vi-tiis ratio, quam Dominus praescribit: nempe ut occulta vitia primatim placidis admonitionibus castigentur: nec quisquam fratrem suum ad Ecclesiae iudicium vocet ob delictum, quod cum publico scandalo coniunctum non erit, donec ad ipsum delictum accesserit contumacia.
units.tr: As for the life of individuals, in correcting faults the method that the Lord prescribes shall be observed: namely, that secret faults be first chastised with gentle admonitions, and no one call his brother before the judgment of the Church for an offence that is not joined with public scandal, unless obstinacy is added to the offence itself.

units.la: Caeterum qui ludibrio habuerint priuatas monitiones, monentur rursus ab Ecclesia. Si praefracti fuerint, & quanuis legitimis testimoniis conuicti, pro veniae deprecatione pertinaciam opponant, arceantur ab vsu Coenae, vsque ad resipiscentiam.
units.tr: Moreover, those who have made light of private admonitions are admonished again by the Church. If they are unruly, and even when convicted by lawful testimonies they oppose obstinacy to a plea for pardon, let them be kept from the use of the Supper until they repent.

units.la: Quòd ad manifesta & famosa peccata spectat quae Ecclesia dissimulare nequit, hoc disciplinae adhibeatur: Mediocre delictum, cui castigando admonitio sufficiet, non vltra prosequantur Cófistorij seniores. Vocetur quidem propter aliorum exemplum, qui deliquit: sed petita venia remittatur. Si nulla appareat resipiscentia, repetatur feria obiurgatio. Qui vero in Ecclesiae scandalum pergent, tanquam Dei contemptores arceantur à sacra Coena, donec resipiscentiae signum dederint.
units.tr: As for manifest and notorious sins that the Church cannot overlook, the following discipline is to be applied. The Consistory elders are not to pursue a moderate offence, for which admonition will suffice for correction any further. The offender is indeed to be summoned for the sake of others' example, but once pardon is sought he is to be dismissed. If no sign of repentance appears, the admonition is to be repeated on another day. But those who persist to the scandal of the Church are, as despisers of God, to be kept from the Lord's Supper until they give a sign of repentance.

units.la: Quòd si grauius sit flagitium, & seueriore poena dignum, quàm vt verbis castigetur, de eo cognoscent Consistorij iudices, vt qui ita prolapsus fuerit, arceatur à Coena Domini ad breue aliquod tempus, vt se coram Deo humili t.
units.tr: But if the wrongdoing is more serious, and deserves a penalty too severe to be corrected by words, the judges of the Consistory shall take cognisance of it. Whoever has so fallen is to be kept from the Lord's Supper for some short time, so that he may humble himself before God.

units.la: Si quis contumaciter spreto Consistorij iudicio, ad sacrâ men sam se ingerat, repellatur à Ministro.
units.tr: If anyone, stubbornly disregarding the judgment of the Consistory, thrusts himself at the holy table, let him be repelled by the minister.

units.la: Ea seruetur moderatio disciplinae, ne querimoniis vlla detur occasio propter immodicum rigorem: atque vt correctiones nihil aliud sint, quàm vtiles medicinae.
units.tr: Let such moderation of discipline be observed that no occasion for complaints be given on account of excessive rigour, and so that corrections may be nothing other than useful medicines.

units.la: Sic etiam intra fines Ecclesiastici regiminis Consistorium se-se contineat, vt nihil ordinariae potestati Magistratus deroget, ac detrahat: ac verbi Ministri spirituali gladio contenti, ciuilem iurisdictionem non attingant, nec quicquam delibent ex iure Magistratus. Adeoque quoties ad Consistorium delatae errunt causae, quarum cognitio ciuilem poenam, vel coercitionem requiret, mittantur partes ad Senatum, vt ciuile iudicium suo arbitrio exerceat.
units.tr: Likewise, within the bounds of ecclesiastical government, the Consistory shall so restrain itself that it takes nothing from, and detracts nothing from, the ordinary power of the magistrate. The ministers of the Word, content with the spiritual sword, shall not touch civil jurisdiction, nor take anything from the right of the magistrate. Accordingly, whenever cases are brought before the Consistory whose hearing would require a civil penalty or coercion, the parties are to be sent to the Senate, so that it may exercise civil judgment at its own discretion.

units.la: Porrò scire operae pretium est, non solos verbi Ministros sedere iudices in Consistorio: sed numerum duplo maiorem, partim ex minori Senatu, ex delectis senioribus esse, vt vocant, partim ex maiori deligi: ad haec unum fere ex ipsis Syndicis praesidere.
units.tr: Moreover, it is worth knowing that the judges in the Consistory are not only the ministers of the Word, but there are twice as many, partly drawn from the lesser Senate from the chosen elders, as they call them, and partly chosen from the greater; and in addition, one of the Syndics almost always presides.

units.la: Per annos duodecim ita sibi temperauit Consistorium, vt sa-tis constet nemini factam fuisse iniuriam: vel plus oneris fuisse impositum, quàm causa exigeret. Pauci quidem interea proterui
units.tr: For twelve years the Consistory has so conducted itself that it is quite clear that no one has been wronged, or that more burden has been imposed than the cause required.

units.la: homines conquesti sunt. Verum Senatus re cognita semper iu-dicauit Consistorium rite officio suo esse func-tum.
units.tr: Meanwhile, a few shameless men have made complaints. But the Senate, having examined the matter, has always judged that the Consistory had duly discharged its office.

units.la: Inter alios praecipuus extitit nebulo quidam, cuius improbi-tas bis firmis ac validis rationibus ita refutata fuit, ut a Senatu pronunciatum sit, etiam iure excommunicatum esse. Cum per sefquiannum sacra communione priuati maluerit, quam poeni-tentiam apud Consistorium testari, nuper ius ac libertatem reci-piendae Coenae a Senatu impetrauit, Consistorio non audito: admissus tamen non fuit: quia Pastores fas sibi esse negarunt, leges in quas iurauerant, violare. Cum multi obstreperent, vocati sunt in Curiam Ministri, a quibus oblata fuit excusatio quae sequitur.
units.tr: Among the others, one particular scoundrel stood out, whose wickedness was so refuted by firm and strong arguments that the Senate pronounced that he had also been excommunicated lawfully. Since for a year and a half he preferred to be deprived of the sacred communion rather than attest his repentance before the Consistory, he recently obtained from the Senate, without the Consistory being heard, the right and liberty of receiving the Supper. Nevertheless he was not admitted, because the ministers denied that it was right for them to violate the laws to which they had sworn. When many made an uproar, the ministers were summoned to the Court, and from them was offered the following excuse.

units.la: Magnifici Domini, non longis verbis praefamur, quantopere vobis optemus morem gerere: sicut etiam vobis obstricti su-mus: quoniam obsequia nostra, sicuti hactenus nos fecisse co-gnoscitis, maluimus reipsa & veris documentis probare. Verè ta-men afferere possumus, nihil esse nobis magis in animo, quàm vobis obsequi, quoad licet. Verum si nobis obstat conscientia, quò minus sine exceptione vestris omnibus mandatis pareamus, vos obsecramus supplicite per nomen Dei, ne iustas excusatio-nes grauemini admittere. Quin potius quod recta ac Dei verbo consentaneum est docuerimus, vestra auctoritate sanciatis, ut fideliter possimus quae & Deo & vobis debemus officia praestare. Neque enim vnquam liberaliter & syncero animo vobis seruie-mus, nisi simpliciter, & qua decet integritate sequamur quod Deus nobis praescribit: & quidem ea constantia, vt ne huc vel il-luc flectamur in hominum gratiam.
units.tr: Most honoured Lords, we will not preface with long words how greatly we wish to comply with you, as we are also bound to you; since our obedience, as you have hitherto recognised, we have preferred to prove by deeds and true proofs. Yet we can truly affirm that nothing is more in our mind than to obey you, so far as it is permitted. But if our conscience stands in the way of our obeying all your commands without exception, we beseech you earnestly, in the name of God, not to be reluctant to admit our just excuses. Rather, let your authority sanction whatever we have taught that is right and consonant with the Word of God, so that we may faithfully perform the duties we owe both to God and to you. For we will never serve you freely and with a sincere mind unless we follow simply and with due integrity what God prescribes to us; and indeed with such constancy that we are not turned this way or that to win the favour of men.

units.la: Hoc in disceptationem trahitur: Ad quos ius & auctoritas excommunicandi pertineat. Nunc quia professi estis, nolle vos à vestris legibus discedere, superuacuum foret longo sermone offendere, quicquid quaerimus, esse prorsus verbo Domini con-sentaneum. Et certe ita sunt compositae illae leges, vt nihil con-tineant, quod non ex puro fonte Scripturae petitum sit. Dicimus ergo totam rem, de qua nunc controuersia nobis mouetur, cla-re illic esse expositam. Nam & quas ob causas excommunicandi sint qui peccarunt, dilucidè statuitur, & haec prouincia manda-tur Consistorio.
units.tr: The question now under dispute is this: to whom does the right and authority of excommunication belong? Now, since you have declared that you do not wish to depart from your laws, it would be superfluous to weary you with a long discourse in order to show that what we seek is wholly consonant with the Word of the Lord. And indeed those laws have been so framed that they contain nothing that is not drawn from the pure fountain of Scripture. We say, therefore, that the whole matter about which the controversy now arises has been clearly set out there. For both the reasons for which those who have sinned are to be excommunicated are plainly laid down, and this charge is committed to the Consistory.

units.la: Nunc friuolo cauillo ius suum Consistorio quidam eripere tentant, quia alicubi additum est, vt Consistorium de suo iudi-cio vos certiores reddat. Neque enim hoc modo impeditur Con-sistorij libertas, quò minus disciplinam sibi mandatam exer-ceat: sed in alium finem posita sunt haec verba, vt duros & indo-mitos homines coerceatis, quibus contemptui est spiritualis cor-rectio. Et sanè vobis denuntiare non iubetur, vt iudicium ad vos transferat,quisnam priuandus Cœna sit,necne: quemadmodum alibi diserte exprimitur, vt de poenis,& de tota ciuili iurisdictione vobis integra feruetur cognitio. Illic enim Consistorio frænum iniicitur, vt à iure veltro abstineat. Hic autem post-quam suis partibus fuerit functum, iubetur ad vos deferre, ne contemptores impunè aduersus Ecclesiam lasciuiant. Atque ita distincta est ratio, vt penes Consistorium ius excommunicandi maneat: vos autem imperio coerceatis rebelles, vbi ita visum fuerit.
units.tr: Now some men attempt, with a frivolous quibble, to snatch this right from the Consistory, because it is stated in one place that the Consistory is to inform you of its judgment. For in this way the freedom of the Consistory is not impeded from exercising the discipline entrusted to it; these words were put in for another purpose, namely that you might restrain hard and unruly men, for whom spiritual correction is held in contempt. And indeed it is not commanded that the Consistory should hand over to you the judgment as to who is to be deprived of the Supper, or not; as is expressly stated elsewhere, so that the cognisance of penalties and of the whole civil jurisdiction remains entire to you. For there a bridle is placed upon the Consistory, so that it abstains from its own right. Here, however, after it has performed its own part, it is ordered to refer the matter to you, lest contemners wantonly rage with impunity against the Church. And so the arrangement is so distinct that the right of excommunication remains with the Consistory, while you restrain rebels by the authority of the magistrate, where it seems fit.

units.la: Imò hoc non vbique præcipitur, vt quoscunque prohibuerit à Cœna Consistorium, vobis significet. Sed nominatim hoc ad duas species restringitur: nempe, Si qui spargendis falsis dogmatibus pertinaciter insistant: vel si qui in spernendo Ecclesiæ ordine obstinati sint: quia in ea parte plus est periculi, vt opus sit Magistratus imperio. Quod pertinet ad reliquos omnes, siue mo nitionibus non paruerint, siue delicta sua fuco obtegere conentur, siue culpam confessi ad ingenium mox redeant, vt appareat non ferio fuisse tactos: siue malo exemplo offenderint Ecclesiam: nulla illic veltri fit mentio: quia nondum eo vsque malum inualuit, vt à vobis subsidium petatur. In summa, non alio respicit illa denuntiatio, nisi vt vindices sitis, vbi ludibrio habebitur Ecclesia Domini, & spiritualis eius correctio pro nihilo ducetur.
units.tr: Indeed, it is not everywhere enjoined that the Consistory must notify you of whomever it has forbidden from the Supper. But this is specifically restricted to two kinds: namely, if any persist stubbornly in spreading false doctrines, or if any are obstinate in despising the order of the Church, because in that part there is more danger, so that the power of the magistrate is needed. As for all the rest, whether they have not heeded admonitions, or try to cover their faults with a pretence, or, having confessed their guilt, soon return to their former temper, so that it is apparent they were not touched seriously, or have offended the Church by bad example: no mention of you is made there, because the evil has not yet grown to such a point that aid is sought from you. In sum, that warning looks to nothing else than that you be avengers, where the Church of the Lord will be made a mockery and its spiritual correction will be held as nothing.

units.la: Videtis ergo, Magnifici domini, in veltris legibus nihil esse obscurum, vel ambiguum: ac sine controuersia excommunican di munus Consistorio iniungi.
units.tr: You see, therefore, most honoured Lords, that there is nothing obscure or ambiguous in your laws, and that without dispute the office of excommunication is enjoined upon the Consistory.

units.la: Cum autem eos, qui se temere & proterue ingerunt, à Ministro repelli oporteat, plusquam absurdum foret admitti crassos contemptores, qui palam & ex professo Ecclesiæ infulcant. Nisi forte permittere illis velitis, vt contumeliose spernendo qui à vobis creati sunt iudices, quique totum corpus Ecclesiæ repræsentant, tam de Deo ipso, quam de vobis triumphum agant. Atqui minime ferendum est, vt sanctum illud & spirituale regimen, quod Deo pretiosum esse scimus, & quod nobis tantopere commendat, profani homines pedibus calcare sibi permittant. Et sane præstaret nullum ordinem esse positum, quam vbi positus est, ita violari. Præstaret nullum esse Consistorium, quam exta re inane nomen tam fœdis ludibriis obnoxium.
units.tr: Moreover, since those who push themselves in rashly and shamelessly must be repelled by the minister, it would be more than absurd to admit gross contemners who openly and deliberately thrust themselves upon the Church. Unless perhaps you wish to permit them to celebrate a triumph, scornfully despising those whom you have created judges, and who represent the whole body of the Church, over God himself as well as over you. Yet it is by no means to be borne that profane men should be allowed to trample underfoot that holy and spiritual government which we know is precious to God and which he commends to us so earnestly. And indeed it would be better that no order were established at all than that, once established, it be thus violated. It would be better that there be no Consistory than that an empty name, emptied of its substance, be exposed to such foul mockery.

units.la: Interea non vos latet, obseruandi Domini, quoties conquestus est quispiam de nimia seueritate, nos semper ad reddendam rationem fuisse paratos & ita vobis satisfecisse, vt semper os ma ledicis obstruictum fuerit. Scimus enim quantopere ab officio nostro abhorreat eam tyrannidem nobis arrogare, vt pro ratione nobis sit voluntas. Nec verò, etiam si per homines liceret, quicquicquam talc nobis ipsi concederemus. Adde quod nunquam recusauimus vel minimis qu bufq; ex plebe officij causam nostram reddere, quoties rogati fumus. Tantum abest, vt grauemur eandem erga vos modestiam colere, quos omni reuerentia (vt par est) honoréque prosequimur. Et vos nobis huius rei optimi estis testes. Caeterum vt nos perspicitis ad omnes officij nostri partes implendas propensos & voluntarios, vicissim a vobis petimus, quoties vobis constabit iniquè nobis detrahi, vt manum nobis porrigatis: nec patiamini grassari eorū lascIuiam, qui fufq; deque habent omnia turbare, vt iugum discIplinæ excutiant. Memoria etiam repetite quod sæpius ex nobis audiftis, si obtinuerit hæc licentia, vt quo quisque contumacius se efferet, ac audacius ordinem labefactabit: eo meliore fit loco, & mercedis vice priuilegium reportet, quo legibus soluatur, fieri non posse, quin paulò post horribilis sequatur confusio.
units.tr: Meanwhile, honoured Lords, you are not unaware that whenever anyone has complained of excessive severity, we have always been ready to give an account and have so satisfied you that the mouth of the slanderer has always been stopped. For we know how far it is from our office to arrogate to ourselves such tyranny that our will should be our reason. Nor indeed, even if it were permitted by men, would we concede any such thing to ourselves. Add that we have never refused to render an account of our cause, when asked, even to the humblest of the common people. So far are we from being burdened by cultivating the same modesty towards you, whom we honour and respect with all reverence, as is fitting. And you are the best witnesses of this matter. Moreover, as you perceive us to be inclined and willing to fulfil every part of our office, so in turn we ask of you that, whenever it becomes clear to you that we are unjustly disparaged, you stretch out your hand to us, and do not suffer the wantonness of those to grow bold who care for nothing and seek to overturn everything, so that they may shake off the yoke of discipline. Remember also what you have often heard from us: if this licence prevails, that the more stubbornly each man exalts himself and the more boldly he overturns order, the better his position becomes and the reward he obtains in place of punishment is exemption from the laws, then it cannot but be that shortly a dreadful confusion follows.

units.la: Quare magnifici & obseruandi Domini, vestrarum partium est, huiusmodi scandalis ita in posterum mederi, vt colatur inter nos Deus omniū consensu: politia Ecclesiæ suo tenore fluat: vos extra molestiam sitis: & nobis liceat salutis doctrinam sine controuersia & tranquille ministrare. Tantum enim absumus à libidine minuendi iuris vestri, vt assiduè potius Dominum pro Reipublicæ vestræ statu precemur. Et certè nihil nobis magis expedit, quàm vos florere, & prosperè habere in Domini gloriam. Nec vero timendum est, ne vestræ auctoritati insidias tædamus, pro qua tuenda, si ita ferret necessitas, libenter quisque nostrum vitam impenderet. Quare si ius vestrum cupitis saluum tenere, non est cur nobiscum litigetis.
units.tr: Wherefore, most honoured and respected Lords, it is your part to remedy such scandals in future, so that God is worshipped among us with the consent of all, the polity of the Church flows on in its proper course, you are free from trouble, and we may be permitted to minister the doctrine of salvation without controversy and in tranquillity. For we are so far from any desire to diminish your right that we rather constantly pray the Lord for the state of your Commonwealth. And truly nothing is more useful to us than that you flourish and prosper to the glory of the Lord. Nor indeed need it be feared that we should grow weary of plotting against your authority, for in defending which, if necessity so required, each of us would willingly lay down his life. Therefore, if you wish to keep your right safe, there is no reason for you to contend with us.

units.la: CAL. D. AGNETI ANGLAE S. D.
units.tr: Calvin to the Lady Agnes of England, greetings

units.la: Quanuam scieba opus fore interprete, generosa Domina, vt literas meas intelligeres, scribendi tamen fiduciā mihi dederunt quidam amici: imò ad hoc officium tibi præstādum vehementer hortati sunt. Linguam verò Latinam potius elegi, quia sperabam tibi multos fore ad manum, qui Italicè exponerent, quum linguæ Gallicæ nulla fere vel rara sit apud vos cognitio. I rincipio autem ne fructu careant meæ literæ, mihi roganda es, vt eas comiter excipere ne grauetis. Quod facile abs te impetrabo, si consilij mei finem spectes. Quinetiam, quod postulo, sponte & libenter facturam promittunt, quorum hortatu scribo. Nec vero pietati tuæ consentaneum esset, quem vnum agnoscis ex feruis Christi, spernere, præsertim salutis tuæ studio loquentem. Ac iusta quidem causa est, vt à gratulatione Incipiam. Nam Euangelij fidem sic te amplexam esse audio,
units.tr: Although I knew that an interpreter would be needed for you to understand my letter, noble lady, certain friends gave me confidence to write, and indeed they urged me strongly to perform this service for you. I chose Latin rather than French, because I hoped that many would be at hand to explain it to you in Italian, since there is almost no or only slight knowledge of the French language among you. First, however, so that my letter may not lack fruit, I must ask you to kindly receive it. This I will easily obtain from you if you consider the purpose of my counsel. Moreover, those at whose urging I write promise that you will do what I ask willingly and gladly. Nor would it be consistent with your piety to spurn one whom you acknowledge as a servant of Christ, especially when he speaks out of concern for your salvation. There is indeed a just cause for me to begin with congratulation. For I hear that you have embraced the faith of the Gospel in such a way

units.la: Epist.168.
units.tr: Epist.168.

units.la: vt nihil tibi potius fit fyncero Dei cultu: cuius singulare ftudiū in eorum omnium animis vigere debet, qui suauitatem illam gratiæ,quæ nobis in Christo offertur,vere guftarunt. Ideo enim apparuit Filius Dei, & quotidie suos thesauros nobis proponit, vt mundi illecebris renuntiantes, cœlestem vitam meditemur. Ideo etiam femine incorruptibili suæ doctrinæ nos Deus regenerat, vt iustitiæ fructus proferat tota vita nostra, qui sacræ eius adoptioni respondeant. Multi quidē impiè hodie illudunt Christo, prætextum licentiæ quærentes ex eius doctrina: sed videmus quàm horrendis modis hæc sacrilegia Deus vindicet. Te verò in hoc totam esse,vt fincta vita Euangelium ornes,magnopere gaudeo. Atque hinc apparet Euangelium in te viuas egisse radices. Cæterum,quia innumeris hodie corruptelis refertus est mundus,non modò rectè animatam te esse conuenit ad pergendum in hoc cursu,sed inuicta quoque fortitudine esse armatam necesse est, vt sub Christo cœlesti duce milites. Nam sic hodie inualuit impietas, ac præsertim apud vos ficgraffatur tyrannis Antichristi,vt non possis fine magnis periculis,& certaminibus integrum Deo cultum præstare. Cuius rei tu optima testis es: atque in eo maximè refulget pietatis tuæ vigor, quòd non solùm tibi non indulgesin vitiis communibus,sicuti multi solent: sed quia pro tua prudentia vides quàm misera fit istic tua fructus, voluntarium exilium subire mauis, quàm in illis sordibus, quæ te contaminant, manere defixa. Porrò quando huc vsque te Deus Spiritu suo expergefecit, mearum partium esse duxi, currenti addere stimulos,& sanctum hoc consilium adiuuare. Si tibi istic esset integrum, Deum non fraudare debito obsequio: manere potius suaderem, quàm relicta patria, longo itinere, magno sumptu,& ingenti molestia longinquam & incognitam regionem petere. Nunc verò cùm minæ & terrores hostium Christi, tibi fidem tuam, vt decebat, profiteri non permittant, te etiā impediat carnis infirmitas,vt ab his laqueis exitialibus quampri-mum euoles, consulere & hortari non dubito: adeòque me tacente fieri non potest, quin te conscientiæ inquietudo ad quærendum remedium assidue folicitet. Interim cauendum tibi est, ne longa deliberatione frustra tempus terendo, exitum tibi præcludas. Fateor sanè in tam arduo negotio temere nihil esse tentandum: verùm fi tibi obscura non est Dei voluntas, non potes fine graui eius iniuria, perplexo animo hoc & illud diu agitare. Serio igitur statue,quod Deus præcipit statim esse exequendum, & simul te absque mora accinge. Nec te retineant vanæ & fallaces blanditiæ,quibus sibi plerique adulantur: sed in mentem subinde tibi recurrat,fidei confessionem Deo magis esse pretiosam, quàm vt leuè deliƈtum fit,impuris superstitionibus fe polluere. luere. Huc etiam accedit, quòd istic tanquam ouis famelica extra ouile,& pascua Christi in sterili deserto vagaris. Nec me latet, quàm tibi difficile ac molestum sit,ex patria migrare, vt in alieno solo procul à cognatis habites, ac iam proueƈtæ ætatis matrona non modò mutes domicilium, sed etiam commoditatibus te exuas,quibus in flore ætatis carere diurum & acerbum foret. Ad hæc omnia quid obiiciam non habeo præter hoc vnũ, quod tamen vt spero, abundè tibi sufficiet: si sapiat nobis cœlestis vita, nihil in terra esse tanti, quod ab illius studio nos retardet:deinde,Filium Dei non solum quia de nobis ita meritus est, sed quia summo imperio potitur, dignum esse cuius honorem omnibus mundi honoribus,deliciis, opibus,& commodis præferamus. Quòd si nobis locum incolere liceat, vbi purè colitur & inuocatur Deus, longè præstat illic exulare, quàm in patria quiescere,vnde Christus Rex cœli & terræ exulat. Si nulla te necessitas à nido discedere cogeret, filia tamen Dei non esses, nisi tibi peregrinatio esset terrena vita. Nunc quum te illinc violenter expellat sacrilega tyrannis Antichristi,& Dominus clara voce te exire iubeat, ne tibi adeo molesta sit peregrinandi conditio, donec in æternam hæreditatem nos simul Deus colligat, Vale nobilis & eximia Domina,mihíque ex animo colenda. Dominus te Spiritu prudentiæ regat, fortitudinem & constantiam tibi augeat,suòque præsidio tueatur.
units.tr: that nothing is more important to you than sincere worship of God. This singular zeal ought to flourish in the minds of all who have truly tasted that sweetness of grace which is offered to us in Christ. For this reason the Son of God appeared, and daily sets his treasures before us, so that, renouncing the allurements of the world, we may meditate on the heavenly life. For this reason too God regenerates us by the incorruptible seed of his teaching, so that our whole life may bring forth fruits of righteousness corresponding to his holy adoption. Many today mock Christ impiously, seeking a pretext for licence from his teaching; but we see in what horrible ways God avenges these sacrileges. I rejoice greatly that you are wholly devoted to adorning the Gospel with a life free of pretence, and from this it appears that the Gospel has taken deep roots in you. Furthermore, since the world is today filled with countless corruptions, it is fitting not only that you be rightly disposed to persevere in this course, but also that you be armed with invincible fortitude, so that you may serve as soldiers under Christ, the heavenly leader. For impiety has so prevailed today, and especially among you the tyranny of Antichrist rages so fiercely, that one cannot render pure worship to God without great dangers and conflicts. You are the best witness of this. In this especially the vigour of your piety shines forth: you not only do not indulge in common vices, as many are wont to do, but, in your prudence, seeing how wretched your fruit is there, you prefer to undergo voluntary exile rather than remain fixed in those filths that contaminate you. Moreover, since God has so far roused you by his Spirit, I have considered it my part to add spurs to your running and to help this holy resolve. If it were open to you there not to defraud God of due obedience, I would advise you to remain rather than, leaving your homeland, to seek a distant and unknown region by a long journey, at great expense and with immense trouble. But now, since the threats and terrors of Christ's enemies do not permit you to profess your faith as is fitting, and the weakness of the flesh also hinders you, I do not hesitate to counsel and urge you to escape from these deadly snares as soon as possible. Indeed, I cannot be silent: the unrest of your conscience must constantly press you to seek a remedy. Meanwhile you must take care that you do not, by wasting time in long deliberation, cut off your own way out. I admit that in so arduous a matter nothing should be attempted rashly; but if the will of God is not obscure to you, you cannot, without grave injury to him, turn this and that over for a long time with a troubled mind. Therefore decide seriously that what God commands must be carried out at once, and at the same time prepare yourself without delay. Let not vain and deceitful flatteries, with which many comfort themselves, hold you back; but let it recur to your mind from time to time that the confession of faith is more precious to God than that one should pollute oneself with impure superstitions as a slight wrong. To this is also added that you wander there like a hungry sheep outside the fold, and in a barren desert far from Christ's pastures. Nor am I unaware how difficult and burdensome it is for you to migrate from your homeland, to live in a foreign land far from your kin, and, now a matron of advanced age, not only to change your home but also to strip yourself of the comforts whose lack would have been long and bitter even in the flower of your age. To all this I have nothing to object except one thing, which nevertheless, I hope, will be quite sufficient for you: if the heavenly life has any value for us, nothing on earth is so great that it holds us back from its pursuit. Then, the Son of God, not only because he has so deserved of us but because he holds supreme dominion, is worthy that we prefer his honour to all the honours, delights, riches and conveniences of the world. But if it is permitted us to dwell in a place where God is purely worshipped and invoked, it is far better to be an exile there than to rest in one's homeland, from which Christ, King of heaven and earth, is exiled. If no necessity compelled you to leave your nest, you would nevertheless not be a daughter of God unless earthly life were a pilgrimage for you. Now, since the sacrilegious tyranny of Antichrist violently drives you out from there, and the Lord bids you depart with a clear voice, let not the condition of a wanderer be too burdensome to you, until God gathers us together into the eternal inheritance. Farewell, noble and excellent lady, to be cherished by me from my heart. May the Lord rule you with the Spirit of prudence, increase your fortitude and constancy, and protect you with his help.

units.la: FARELLVS CALVINO S., D.
units.tr: Farel to Calvin, greetings.

units.la: QVod accedet paci & ædificationi præter spem erit: potens est D.cui spe niti nos oportet, quanuis hîc omnia desperea videamus:nobis scentibus mundum lætari oportet. Verùm tristitia nostra in gaudium vertetur. Tu si es inter eos qui optime apud Antiochum audiunt,gratior indie bonis:quibus vt chatior in Domino sis,perge quæ dedit D.in wsum Ecclesiæ pro ferre,cùm in Christo vite sis, vt eas, fructúmque afferas qui maneat. N.fertur à Cæsare monita vt interimi se ferat excepto Interim.Christus suo Spiritu tandem illuminet tam parum videntes. Polono qui hac transiuit ad te tendens, plurimam dices salutem.Si huc venerit, dabo operam vt intelligat me ex animo ei bene velle ob Christum,cuius gratia exceptus fuit paulò durius, vt ex eius literis accepi. Sed cùm sit Christi seruus,videat quàm fuerit longè mitius exceptus quàm dominus, & sese apparet ad duriora.Graue est ab illis hæc fieri,qui dederunt nomen Euangelio,sed grauius fuit Apostolum vendidisse ac tradidisse seruatorem.Verax est Deus,non patietur nos tentari supra id quod possumus. Vale bene. Iste seruet tuúmque semper prosperum & omnibus frugiferum reddat ministerium, & omnium elidat co-natus qui impedire quouis modo tentant Christum, qui addat vt fis perpetuò pergens magis ac magis in gloriam Dei, & omnium aedificationem mente & corpore saniffimo. Collegas iube omnes saluere. Valde placuit quod per D. Tollanum respondi-stis. Neocomi, 1111. Calend. Martias. M. D. LIIII.
units.tr: What will be added to peace and edification will come beyond hope. God is powerful, and on him we must rest our hope, although here we see everything despaired of. Since we know this, we ought to rejoice in the world. Our sadness will indeed be turned into joy. If you are among those who hear best from Antiochus, you are more pleasing to the good. So that you may be more cheerful in the Lord, go on bringing forth what God has given for the use of the Church, since you are in Christ the vine, that you may bear such fruit as will remain. It is reported that Caesar has issued an edict that they should be put to death, except in the matter of the Interim. May Christ at last enlighten with his Spirit those who see so little. Greet the Pole who passed through here on his way to you; you will give him my warmest greetings. If he comes here, I will take care that he understands I sincerely wish him well for Christ's sake, by whose grace he was received somewhat roughly, as I learned from his letters. But since he is a servant of Christ, let him see how much more gently he was received than his Master, and let him prepare himself for harder things. It is grievous that these things are done by those who professed the name of the gospel, but it was more grievous for the Apostle to sell and betray the Saviour. God is true; he will not allow us to be tempted beyond what we can bear. Farewell and be well. May he preserve you, and make your ministry always prosperous and fruitful for all, and crush all the efforts of those who try in any way to hinder Christ; may he grant that you continue ever more and more to the glory of God and the edification of all, in mind and body in the best of health. Bid all your colleagues greet me. It pleased me very much that you replied through Master Tollanus. Neuchâtel, 26 February 1554.

units.la: GASPAR LISERVS NVRTINGENSIS PASTOR IO. CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: Gaspar Liservus, minister of Nürtingen, to John Calvin, greetings.

units.la: QVod ego homo tibi ignotus, vir praestantissime, ad te litteras dare non vereor, quaeso ne audaciae, aut temeritatis alicuius damnes, multominus aegre moleste queque feras. Hoc enim tibi velim persuadeas, me ad id audendum non nisi germano ac vere ἀληθῶς ἀδελφός (vt Apostolus vocat) amore erga te esse adductum. Ex quo enim primum Ecclesiae cura mihi mandata est (sexennium autem fere in exercendo hoc munere exegi) ac lucubrationes tuas euoluere coepi, tantus me tui amor incessit, vt interea vix aliud magis in votis habuerim, quam me tibi esse notum & amicum. Adeo etiam, vt cum ante quadriennium Augustanum illud τὸ μετάξυ, vt vocant, hinc inde grassaretur, ac pios syncerofque Euangelij doctores in exilium eiceret, mihi diu propositum aliud non fuerit, quam statim Geneuam me velle petere, simul ac ministerio prohiberer. Etiamsi vero id (Christo sit laus & gloria) non factum, & Deus ex mero suo fauore, quo nos nunquam non prosequitur, Euangelium suum purum nobis partim reliquerit, partim dispulsis τοῦ μετάξυ & Papatus tenebris, iterum restituerit, ego tamen te propterea amare non desij. Sed quo tu indies plures in Ecclesiae communis vtilitatem & aedificationem libros emittis, eo maiore quoque studio te semper ego prosequor. Quamobrem cum nuper ex bibliopola nostro, cum effet in nundinas illas Francfordienfes profecturus, quaererem, num etiam Geneuenses illuc venirent, ille vero non solum venire eos, verum etiam sibi nonnihil familiaritatis cum eis intercedere diceret, temperare mihi non potui, quin traderem bibliopolae literas, quas ab eo Geneuenses mercatores acceptas, ad te vsque perferrent. Accipe igitur, vir ornatissime, hanc epistolam tanquam μνημόσυνον amoris mei erga te summi, syncerh, ac vere Christiani: Christiani inquam, vtpote qui pietatis auspiciis consecratus, ab externis causis non pendeat: quemadmodum tu alicubi de eiusmodi amicitia loqueris. Hanc enim ego quoque, cum Hieronymo, pro vera amicitia & necessitudine habeo, quam nō vtilitas rei familiaris, non praesentia tantum corporum, non subdola & palpans adulatio, sed Dei timor & diuinarum literarum studium conciliant, ac sic Christi glutino copulatur: qualis reuera haec nostra erit, si modo me in album tuorum amicorum referre dignatus fueris. Tu autem, mi Caluine, in sancto illo tuo ac pio proposito susceptóque labore explanandae Scripturae, strenuè perge: nec prius desiste, quàm omnes libros Prophetieos & Apostolicos per curretis. Si modò tam diu (quod vnicè à Deo Patre Domini nostri Iesu Christi rogamus) vitam tibi Dominus prorogauerit. Placet enim mihi, imò piis omnibus purus ille ac verè latinus tuus stylus. Placet succincta illa breuitas, quae etiamsi non more aliorum interpretum, in locos communes vagatur, nihil tamen omittit, quod scitu dignum & necessarium est. Probatur etiam nobis illud pium pacis studium, quo conatris obliuione sepelire, contentionem illam, satis infaelicem, de Eucharistiae sacramento motam, quae multum nos iam diu exercuit, & haud dubie multis, ne Christo se totos addicerent, fuit impedimento ac obstaculo. Quoniam verò haec contentio, apud omnes obliuione obrui nequit, conaris diffidentes partes inter se reconcilia re, ac ita iuxta Christi verbum ειρηνοποιεῖν. Nec dubita, te non perdidisse in hoc studium & operam. Multi enim quos ego noui, qui antea aduersam partem tantùm non execrabantur, lecta tua hac de re ac diligentius perpensa sententia, æquiores Zuinglio & OEcolampadio facti, plenè in tuam sententiam manibus & pedibus eunt. Ex quorum numero me quoque vnum esse liberè profiteor. Verè enim tibi assentior alicubi dicenti: Nisi Lutherus, OEcolampadius, ac reliqui (viri certè nùquam satis laudati) partim sinistris opinionibus fuissent occupati, partim disputationis vehementia exacerbati, rem tantam non fuisse, quin potuissent inter se reconciliari. Hæc si bene memini, tua verba sunt. Verùm talem contentionem & offendiculum promeruit mundi ingratitudo, qui Christum sibi illucescentem, non quo par fuisset, honore ac reuerentia excepit. Quòd si alter alterum nonnunquam asperius tractauit, id tribuendum est infirmitati eorum, qua laborant etiam in hac vita sanctissimi. In istis enim altercationibus caueri nequit, quin multa non tam ex animo, quàm ex affectu dicantur. Id quod etiam in hac contentione factû, à Domino tamen eis condonatum, planè non dubito. Si quaeris in quo statu nostrae sint Ecclesiae (quae enim tua est pietas), pro nobis quoq; haud dubiè es solicitus) scias, omnes in hoc ducatu Papisticis ac metaxysticis sacrificis esse purgatas, idque nomine & mandato principis nostri verè Christophori, qui siue spectes virtutem, siue eruditionem, siue pietatem, nulli principum Germanorum erit secundus. Nisi fortasse ei, in quo victo & capto, heroicam magnanimitatem seculis omnibus spectandam proposuit Dominus.
units.tr: Although I am a man unknown to you, most excellent sir, I do not hesitate to write to you. I beg you not to condemn this as audacity or rashness, much less to take it amiss or be annoyed. I would have you be assured that I have been moved to dare this only by a brotherly and true love for you, truly a brother [ἀληθῶς ἀδελφός], as the Apostle calls it. For from the time when the care of the Church was first entrusted to me (and I have now spent nearly six years in this office), and I began to read through your writings, such love for you has grown in me that meanwhile I have scarcely desired anything more than to be known to you and to be your friend. Indeed, when about four years ago that Augsburg business, the so-called Interim [τὸ μετάξυ], spread on every side and drove pious and sincere teachers of the gospel into exile, my settled purpose for a long time was nothing other than to go to Geneva at once, as soon as I should be forbidden the ministry. Although this (thanks be to Christ) did not happen, and God, out of his pure favour, with which he never ceases to attend us, has partly left us his gospel pure, and partly, after the shadows of the Interim [τοῦ μετάξυ] and of Papistry were dispelled, has restored it again, I nevertheless did not cease to love you on that account. Indeed, the more books you bring out each day for the common use and edification of the Church, the greater the zeal with which I always follow you. Therefore, when recently I asked our bookseller, who was about to set out for that fair at Frankfurt, whether the Genevans would also be going there, and he replied that they would not only be going, but that he had some acquaintance with them, I could not refrain from entrusting to the bookseller a letter, which he might deliver to you through the Genevan merchants. Accept, then, most distinguished sir, this letter as a memorial [μνημόσυνον] of my love for you, which is supreme, sincere, and truly Christian: Christian, I say, since it is consecrated under the auspices of piety and does not depend on external causes, as you yourself somewhere speak of such friendship. For I too, with Jerome, hold that friendship to be true and genuine which is brought about not by advantage in worldly affairs, nor by mere bodily presence, nor by deceitful and fawning flattery, but by the fear of God and devotion to the divine Scriptures, and so is joined by the glue of Christ. Such, truly, this friendship of ours will be, if only you deign to enrol me in the list of your friends. As for you, my dear Calvin, press on vigorously in that holy and pious purpose of yours and in the labour you have undertaken of expounding Scripture, and do not stop until you have run through all the prophetic and apostolic books, if only the Lord prolongs your life so long (which we ask of God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ alone). For that pure and truly Latin style of yours pleases me, and indeed all pious people. That concise brevity pleases me, which, though it does not wander into commonplaces after the manner of other interpreters, nevertheless omits nothing that is worth knowing and necessary. We also approve that pious zeal for peace by which you strive to bury in oblivion that rather unhappy controversy concerning the sacrament of the Eucharist, which has long troubled us and has undoubtedly been a hindrance and obstacle to many, so that they have not given themselves wholly to Christ. But since this controversy cannot be overwhelmed by oblivion among all, you strive to reconcile the disagreeing parties with one another, and so, according to the word of Christ, to make peace [ειρηνοποιεῖν]. Do not doubt that you have not lost your zeal and labour in this. For many whom I know, who before only execrated the opposing side, after reading your opinion on this matter and weighing it more carefully, have become fairer to Zwingli and Oecolampadius, and go wholeheartedly, with hands and feet, into your view. I frankly profess that I myself am one of their number. For I truly agree with you where you say somewhere: "Unless Luther, Oecolampadius and the rest (men certainly never praised enough) had been partly occupied with mistaken opinions, and partly inflamed by the vehemence of disputation, such a great matter would not have been so great that they could not have been reconciled with one another." These, if I remember rightly, are your words. But the ingratitude of the world has deserved such a controversy and stumbling-block, since it received Christ shining upon it without the honour and reverence that were due. And if one has sometimes treated the other more harshly, this is to be attributed to the weakness of those who labour under it, even the holiest men in this life. For in such disputes it cannot be avoided that many things are said not so much from the heart as from passion. This also happened in this controversy, but I have no doubt that the Lord has forgiven them. If you ask in what state our Churches are (for what is your piety, since you are certainly anxious about us too, I should know), know that in this duchy all have been purged of Papistical and Interim sacrifices, and this in the name and by the command of our prince, truly Christopher, who, whether you look at his virtue, his learning or his piety, will be second to none of the German princes. Unless perhaps it is he to whom the Lord has set forth, in his defeat and capture, a heroic magnanimity to be looked upon by all ages.

units.la: Sic enim tu in libello, qui de Scandalis inscribitur, de Iohanne Friderico, Saxoniæ duce ac olim Electore (tacito tamen eius nomine) loqueris. Documenta pietatis suæ satis luculenta princeps noster edidit. Solus ex omnibus Germaniæ principibus confessionem suæ fidei, eámque typis excusam Tridentino illi concilíabulo ausus fuit exhibere. Viros propter Euangelij confessionem exulantes, liberaliter excipit, ac perhumane habet, imo magnis præmiis ad se invitat. Sub tali principe, non possunt non fœlices esse Ecclesiæ. Est tamen quod non immerito pius quispiam adhuc desideret. Mittuntur adhuc ex aula Pastores, & nonnunquam satis rudes ac ignaui: non eliguntur veteri more, ab vniuersa Ecclesia: qui mos vtinam iterum quasi postliminio revocaretur etiam apud nos. Nec ordinantur Ministri impositione manuum ac precibus. Excommunicatio nulla apud nos adhuc est in vsu. Adeo vt opus vobis fit Paulo, vt Titum admoneat, vt pergat ea quæ desunt corrigere. Magnæ exstim tionis est apud principem Iohannes Brentius, quod si his de rebus ad eum scriberes, non faceres rem tuo ministerio indignam, & Ecclesiis nostris, opinor, valde vtilem. Tu quid hac in re faciendum sit, quæso, diligenter tecum deliberes, & ad me perscribere proximis nundinis Francfordiensibus ne dedignetis. Quicquid enim alij sint facturi, ego certe qui se manifestis flagitiis ac scelectibus contaminant, mox Satanæ tradere incipiam: quia autem rem tantam ac viribus meis maiorem sum tentaturus, plane consilio mihi opus esse iudico. Cum ante triennium Antidotum tuum contra Acta Tridentina legerem, statim in ipsa præliminari epistola deprehendi, te libelli cuiusdam abs re editi, de necessitate reformandæ Ecclesiæ, mentionem facere, ac rogare lectorem, vt eum quoque percurrere non grauetur. Ego vero cum hactenus studiose apud omnes bibliopolas quæsierim, nacisci tamen adhuc non potuí, eum, quæso, post semestre exactu, cum iterum tui mercatores Francfordiam sunt petituri, tuis typis graphis trade, quò ad oras nostras aliquando etiam appellat. Vale bene ac fœliciter vir eruditissime, ac me amicis tuis, seu potius filiis veré γνήσιοις (quantum addoctrinam pietatis) accense: ego te patris loco habere, colere, venerarique nunquam desinam. Vale iterum Nurtingæ, quod est oppidum ducatus Vvittemberg-ensis. Anno M. D. LIII. XXVI. Februarij, quo die ante annos tres fidus ille & eximius seruus Christi Martinus Bucerus Cantabrigiæ in Anglia mortuus est.
units.tr: For so you speak in your little book which is entitled On Scandals, about John Frederick, Duke of Saxony and formerly Elector (though without naming him). Our prince has put forth sufficiently clear proofs of his piety. Alone of all the princes of Germany, he dared to present his confession of faith, and that printed, to that Tridentine conciliabulum. He receives liberally and treats most kindly those who are exiled for confessing the Gospel, and even invites them to himself with great rewards. Under such a prince the Churches cannot but be happy. Yet there is something which some pious person may not unreasonably still wish for. Ministers are still sent from the court, and sometimes quite unskilled and idle. They are not chosen, as in the old custom, by the whole Church; I wish that this custom might be recalled among us too, as if by right of return. Nor are ministers ordained by the laying on of hands and prayer. No excommunication is yet in use among us. So that there is need for you, as for Paul, to admonish Titus to go on correcting what is lacking. John Brenz is of great standing with the prince. If you were to write to him about these matters, you would not be doing something unworthy of your ministry, and, I think, very useful to our Churches. I beg you to deliberate carefully with yourself what ought to be done in this matter, and please do not disdain to write back to me at the next Frankfurt fairs. For whatever others may do, I at least, who stain themselves with manifest disgraces and crimes, shall soon begin to hand over to Satan; but since I am about to attempt a matter so great and beyond my own strength, I judge that I plainly need counsel. When three years ago I was reading your Antidote against the Acts of Trent, I noticed at once in the preliminary letter itself that you mention a little book published out of its proper place, on the necessity of reforming the Church, and ask the reader not to hesitate to run through it as well. Now, though until now I have eagerly sought it from all the booksellers, I have not yet been able to get hold of it. I beg you, therefore, when after six months your merchants are again going to Frankfurt, to entrust it to your printers, so that it may sometime reach our shores. Farewell and be well and happy, most learned sir, and count me among your friends, or rather among your truly legitimate sons [γνήσιοις], as far as the doctrine of piety goes. I will never cease to regard you as a father, to cultivate you and venerate you. Farewell again, from Nurtingen, which is a town of the Duchy of Württemberg. In the year 1553, on the 26th of February, on which day three years ago that faithful and excellent servant of Christ, Martin Bucer, died at Cambridge in England.

units.la: CALVINVS
units.tr: CALVIN

units.la: Vderet me,eximie vir, & colede Frater,quod iam binis tuis literis nihil respônderim,nisi quia fuit aliqua tacendi ratio.
units.tr: I am ashamed, distinguished sir and dear brother, that I have not replied at all to your two letters, except that there was some reason for my silence.

units.la: Nolebam enim nisi rebus compositis scribere, ne te certamina nostra perplexum atque anxium tenerent, quæ molestia tibi cum optimis & fidelissimis nostris fratribus futura erat communis.Et subinde in tanta varietate agitati sumus,vt nullus dies nobis affulserit,qui non à crastino penderet. Tandem huc ventum est,vt inter se omnes reconciliarentur.Nam Senatus palàm in factiones diuisus erat:sicque palàm erupérant odia,vt improbi suis ceruicibus sentirent instare Dei vltionem. Neque tamen bonis tantum fuit animi,vt statum Ecclesiæ,de quo tam acris erat dimicatio,componere studerent. Tantùm datæ sunt dexteræ, iureiurando interposito, ne quis posthac malis causis faueret.Atque hoc quidem præiudicio se pars aduersa tacitè damnauit.Verùm plausibili pacis colore factum est, vt legitimus ordo, vnicus pacis custos neglectus fuerit,vel saltem posthabitus.Ego vocatus in Curiam,profeffusfum me omnibus ignoscere,qui ex animo resipiscerent:me tamen vnum duntaxat esse ex Cōsistorio, centies igitur potius moriturum, quàm vt mihi arrogarem, quod totius Ecclesiæ commune erat. Hoc à nobis fuit animaduersum , Satanam nihil magis cupere ,quàm vt rebus dubiis & suspensis,aliqua in posterum turbandi occasio suppetat. Nobis autem in animo est anteuertere. Etsi autem minore forte vehementia quàm prius,tumultuabuntur hostes,breui tamen rursus certandum erit. Vides apertius causam silentij,quòd domestică tegere dedecus optarem. Sic tamen habe:quanuis vbique variè iactetur Ecclesia,Geneuæ tamen non secus atque in diluuio arcam Noah,fluctuari. Hinc etiam collige,quantopere mihi displiceat,Clariff. Senatum vestrum fatigari quæstionibus.Quod tamen luculento documento nuper vobis testatum fuit,quum de spirituali Ecclesiæ gubernatione non fueritis consulti.Ego verò quid facerem,cui boni omnes ingemiscunt,remedium verò nequeunt afferre? Bene tamen habet quòd nobis præsidet nauclerus,sub quo tuti à naufragio erimus:deinde quòd non procul di stamus à portu.Interim d fcenda est eorum conditio,quibus eadem nauigatio subeunda est.Seruetiçç impietatis refutatio prius tibi missi erit,vt spero,quàm ad te literæ meæ perueniant.Libellus breuis est ac tumultuarie conscriptus.Præstabit tamen,quod continet,scriptum esse, quàm nihil.Angliæ motus iam istic notos esse arbitror : & interim dum in itinere adhuc erit epistola, forte aliquid certius erit allatum. units.tr: I did not want to write except once matters were settled, lest our conflicts leave you troubled and anxious, a distress that would have been shared with our best and most faithful brothers. We were tossed about with such changes that no day dawned on us without depending on the next. At last it has come to this, that everyone is reconciled. The Senate was openly divided into factions, and hatreds had burst out so plainly that the wicked felt God's vengeance pressing on their necks. Yet the good did not have the spirit to set about settling the state of the Church, over which the struggle had been so bitter. Only right hands were given, with an oath interposed, that no one would henceforth favour bad causes. By this the opposing party tacitly condemned itself. But under the plausible colour of peace it came about that the lawful order, the sole guardian of peace, was neglected or at least set aside. I was summoned to the Council and declared that I forgave all who repented from the heart; yet I was only one member of the Consistory, and I would rather die a hundred times than arrogate to myself what belonged in common to the whole Church. We have noticed that Satan wants nothing more than for some occasion of disturbance to be available in future, while matters are doubtful and unsettled. We, however, intend to forestall him. Although the enemies will perhaps stir up with less vehemence than before, we shall soon have to fight again. You see more clearly the cause of my silence: I wished to cover a domestic disgrace. Yet know this: although the Church is tossed about variously everywhere, at Geneva it nonetheless floats, as Noah's ark did in the flood. Gather also from this how much I dislike that your distinguished Senate is worn out with questions, though this was recently shown to you by a clear proof, since you were not consulted about the spiritual government of the Church. But what should I do, when all good men groan and cannot bring a remedy? Still it is well that a pilot presides over us, under whom we shall be safe from shipwreck, and that we are not far from harbour. Meanwhile the condition of those who must undertake the same voyage has to be endured. The refutation of Servetus's impiety was sent to you before this, I hope, and will reach you before my letter does. The little book is short and written in haste, yet it will be worth what it contains, since it is written rather than nothing. I think the disturbances in England are already known there, and meanwhile, while the letter is still on its way, something more certain may have been reported. Farewell, distinguished and most honoured man, and brother I hold very dear. Greet Master Gual-

units.la: t.j. therum,generos & reliquos fratres. D.Marchio Caraciolus, Budeus nolter,& College mei te saluere optant.Dominus vos tueatur manu sua,& Spiritu suo regat,laborésque vestros benedicat. Amen.Geneuæ,v 1 i.Calendas Martij. M. D. LIIII.
units.tr: therum, your sons-in-law and the other brothers diligently in my name. Marquis Caraciolo, our Budé, and my colleagues wish you well. May the Lord keep you under his hand, guide you by his Spirit, and bless your labours. Amen. Geneva, 1 March 1554.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: IOANNES CALVINUS DILECTISSIMIS FRATRIBUS Orb̃,qui puram Euangelij prædicationem, & Dei cultum syncerum cum Regni Christi promotione exoptant.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO THE MOST BELOVED BRETHREN AT ORBE, who desire the pure preaching of the Gospel and the sincere worship of God together with the advancement of the Kingdom of Christ.

units.la: Charitas Dei Patris, & Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi, per Spiritus sancti communicationem vobis semper adsit.
units.tr: May the love of God the Father and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ always be with you through the communion of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: QVum præter ordinariam sanæ doctrinæ auditionem, cui etiam lectio verbi potest accedere, non dubitem, quin optimi fratres Farellus & Viretus strenuè in illud incúbant, vt vos sanctis exhortationibus ad pietatis studium accendant, quasetiam à vobis prompto & propenso animo excipi confidà: volui tamè dilectiss.fratres hoc ad vos litterarũ dare, quò meum de vobis ac rebus vestris iudicium haberetis. Etsane non vulgari confirmatione nunc vobis opus est,ex quo turbæ illæ à Satana aduersum vos excitatæ sunt.Meum verò erga vos studium probatum iri facilè mihi persuadeo,cùm de recto affectu constiterit, vt opera mea apud vos inutilis futura non sit. Equidem non dubito, quin pro vestro illo intèto desiderio ad purum Dei cultum inter vos solidè restituendum, magno vobis mœrori sit status ille vestræ vrbis,dum nempe superstitio & impietas Papistmi,quæ Dei cultum corrupit,& nomen sacrum blasphemiis operit,sedem suam adhuc apud vos retinent.Interea magni vobis thesauri loco esse debet,quòd Dominus dederit,vt vos quidè iam nihil commune cum malo habeatis. Imò vt non modò à malo abstinere liceat, sed etiam extet ordo aliquis Ecclesiæ inter vos,quo vos sub Domini iugo cötineatis. Magnum omnino & incomparabile Dei beneficium,si in illorum conditionem oculos nò iecceritis, qui crudelissimæ seruitutis iugo miserabiliter premuntur.Superest tamen illa anxietas,quòd nō pauca in ocu los vestros incurrunt, quæ Dei gloriæ aduersantur. Præsertim cùm omnia istic tam certò & ex voto comparata essent, vt nec aliter statueremus,quàm vos plenè tandem Antichristi sordibus perpurgatum ac semel liberatum iri:quare quòd à tanta spe deiici contigit,non potuit non esse molestissimum. Insideles verò meta metu illo iam vacui,non desunt etiam occasioni ,quin & triumphum sibi canant, & Deo insultent, quo vobis extremus dolor super dolorem accedat. Atqui nouum videri non debet, quòd Satan qui totus in eo est, ut promouionem Regni Christi impediat, suas illas artes adhibeat, ad cumulum benedictionis Dei porrò mouendū:cùm nisi obstaret Dominus,omnia semel disiicere, ac veluti per auras verrere paratissimus sit. Interea verò, dum à Domino constringitur, seipsum nihilominus excutit, ut damnum det quantum potest. Vobis autem singulare solatium illud afferre debet,quòd verè constet,ius & litem Domini à vobis propugnari:proinde spes illa vos erigat, Dominum veritati suæ quæ ipsi vnicè pretiosa sit,nō defuturum. Durate igitur animos ad tempus, ac non minus constanter in eo quod coepistis pergite. Statuite vos ad illud à Domino positos esse, ut ipse vestram fidem & patientiā exerceat.Ac si nulla spes & ratio affulgeret efficiendi in posterum quod intenditis: illud vos tamē sustinere deberet,& animum addere q; vobis conscij sitis,ita Deo vos impendisse, ac vestrum illi obsequium probari. Est verò q; in recto studio vos multò magis confirmet, cùm laboris vestri fructus insignis in hoc etiam immaturo emixu extiterit. Viget enim illa Domini promissio,nos operam non ludere, etsi aërem cædere videamur ,vbi verbum illius nobis præibit. Agnoscite igitur istius promissionis effectum,illam quoq; sese ostendit gregis Domini amplificationem,quæ haud dubiè abominationes Antichristi ex vrbe profligatura sit.Quod enim hoc tempore dilatū voluit Dominus,suo tempore confecturum statuendum est.Hoc est igitur luctæ tempus & certaminis aduersus varias tentationes:vt sanè introductio principatus& dominationis Filij Dei inter homines, non sine sudore & extremo nixu procedere solet. Cùm verò Satan ita inflatus & furens fertur aduersum vos,quis erit pudor,si vobis ipsis defueritis? Quid enim illë in exitiu suū contendit,vos & pro causa illa statis,quæ cum salute vestra conjuncta est,& victoriam vobis paratam esse, si cordatè pergetis, certò persuasi estis. Infideles porrò qui sua caecitate bis miseri, gratiam Dei quantum in ipsis est,repellunt,commiseratione dignì sunt potius,quàm vt illorum occasione commoueri vos oporteat. Sic se prodit letalis ille morbus, quo à Satana fascinantur,cùm suam vnam salutem tam deploratè fugiunt, & exosam habent. Quare vestra erga illos commiseratio,vobis animum non imminuat, quin etiam inuitis bonum incognitum procuretis.Hoc demum effectum dabitur,eùm non iam vt laceri corporis membra, vno eodémq; Spiritu & animo eundem omnes Dominum inuocabitis. Quod vt detur,neq; illi rei parcendum est,neq; illa hic remissio excusari potest: quò magis postulādus vobis à Deo est Spiritus fortitudinis & verae constantiae, ne vn-quam animum despondeatis. Nec minus necessaria est pia illa & sancta prudetia, vt cum aduersarij in omnes occasiones sad vos intercipiendos intenti sint, aduersus illorum conatus inoffensi perstetis. Cum hanc viam tenebitis, aut Dominus retundet illorum tumorem, qui ita erga vos male sunt animati: aut aequiores & pacatiores reddet, ne ita ferociter aduersus stimulos calcitret. Vtut sit, hoc agite tanquam mente deliberata, vt quod stadium vobis decurrendum statuit Dominus in illo vos strenue ad extremum vsque conficiendo pergatis. Illud vobis vel vnum abunde sit, quod approbari veStrum laborem à Domino non dubitatis, cum abominationibus illis bellum ἀπροσωπ indicitis, quae ipsius cultui & honori aduersantur. Neque vero mihi non veniunt illa in mentem, quae in hoc Domini negotio sese vobis obiectura sunt, vt vos à constantia vestra dimouceant, nisi virtus vna ex alto omnia illa impedimenta in vobis exuperet, a qua etiam pendet progressus nostrer & non fallax expectatio. Nos hic omnes ita omnia ista vobis à Deo bene cedere comprecamur, atque vt & sua protectione complectatur & spiritualibus donis cumuler, vt magis ac magis accensi sitis, ad vos illi in solidum adducendos. Genevae I III Martij. M. D. LIIII.
units.tr: Although you have the regular hearing of sound doctrine, to which the reading of the Word may also be added, and although I do not doubt that the excellent brethren Farel and Viret are labouring hard at this, to stir you up to the pursuit of godliness by holy exhortations, and I am confident that you receive these with a ready and willing mind, nevertheless, most beloved brethren, I wished to send you this letter, so that you might have my judgment concerning you and your affairs. Indeed you now need no ordinary encouragement, since those disturbances have been stirred up against you by Satan. I am easily persuaded that my zeal towards you will be shown to be sound, since my right disposition is established, so that my labour will not be useless among you. Truly I do not doubt that, given your earnest desire to restore the pure worship of God firmly among you, that state of your city grieves you greatly, namely that superstition and the impiety of the Papists, which have corrupted the worship of God and cover the sacred name with blasphemies, still keep their seat among you. Meanwhile, you ought to count as a great treasure the fact that the Lord has granted that you now have nothing in common with evil; and not only that it is permitted to abstain from evil, but also that some order of the Church exists among you, by which you are held under the yoke of the Lord. It is altogether a great and incomparable benefit of God, if you do not turn your eyes to the condition of those who are miserably oppressed under the yoke of the most cruel servitude. Yet that anxiety remains, that not a few things fall under your eyes which are opposed to the glory of God; especially since everything there seemed to have been arranged so surely and according to our wish that we did not think otherwise than that you would at last be thoroughly purged of the filth of Antichrist and set free once and for all. Therefore, that you have been cast down from such hope could not but be most troubling. Unbelievers, however, now empty of that fear, are not lacking in opportunities; they even sing their triumph and insult God, so that extreme grief is added to your grief. Yet it ought not to seem new that Satan, who is wholly intent on hindering the advance of the Kingdom of Christ, employs his arts to stir up further obstacles to the blessing of God; since, unless the Lord stood in the way, he would be fully ready to scatter everything at once and sweep it away like the wind. Meanwhile, though he is restrained by the Lord, he nonetheless shakes himself, so as to do as much harm as he can. But this singular comfort ought to be brought to you: that it is truly established that the right and the cause of the Lord are being defended by you; therefore let that hope lift you up, that the Lord will not fail the truth, which is uniquely precious to him. Hold fast your spirits for the time being, and press on no less steadfastly in what you have begun. Be assured that the Lord has placed you there so that he may exercise your faith and patience. And even if no hope or reason shone forth of accomplishing in future what you intend, you ought nevertheless to endure and take courage, and be aware that you have devoted yourselves to God and that your obedience to him is approved. There is also something that should strengthen you much more in your right purpose: the fruit of your labour has been remarkable even in this immature effort. For that promise of the Lord flourishes, that we do not labour in vain, even if we seem to beat the air, when his word goes before us. Acknowledge therefore the effect of that promise; it also shows itself in an increase of the Lord's flock, which will undoubtedly drive out the abominations of Antichrist from the city. For what the Lord has willed to be deferred for now, it must be settled that he will accomplish in his own time. This, then, is the time of struggle and of conflict against various temptations; for indeed the introduction of the rule and dominion of the Son of God among men is not wont to proceed without sweat and extreme effort. Since Satan is thus reported to be puffed up and raging against you, what shame will it be if you yourselves fail? For he strives to his own destruction; and you stand for that cause which is bound up with your salvation, and you are certainly persuaded that victory is prepared for you if you press on wisely. As for unbelievers, who in their blindness are doubly wretched and repel the grace of God as far as lies in them, they deserve pity rather than that you should be moved by their occasion. Thus that deadly disease by which they are bewitched by Satan reveals itself, since they so desperately flee and hate their one salvation. Therefore let your compassion for them not diminish your courage; indeed, even against their will, procure for them a good they do not know. This will at last be granted when, no longer as the torn members of one body, you will all call upon the same Lord with one Spirit and one mind. That this may be given, no effort is to be spared, nor can any slackness here be excused; so much the more must you ask of God the Spirit of fortitude and true constancy, that you never lose heart. Not less necessary is that godly and holy prudence, so that, since the adversaries are intent on every occasion to ensnare you, you may persevere unhurt against their attempts. When you keep to this way, either the Lord will beat down the pride of those who are so ill-disposed towards you, or he will make them more fair and peaceable, so that they do not kick so fiercely against the goads. Whatever happens, act as those who have deliberately resolved to press on strenuously through that course which the Lord has set you to run, bringing it to its end. Let this one thing be enough for you, that you do not doubt that your labour is approved by the Lord, since you declare war on those abominations which are opposed to his worship and honour. Nor do those things which are to stand in your way in this work of the Lord fail to come to my mind, to turn you aside from your constancy, unless one power from on high overcomes all those hindrances in you, on which also depends our progress and our unfailing expectation. Here we all pray that God may bring all these things to a good outcome for you, that he may both embrace you with his protection and enrich you with spiritual gifts, so that you may be kindled more and more to bring them wholly to him. At Geneva, 1 March 1554.

units.la: Bullingerus Calvino s. d.
units.tr: Bullinger to Calvin, greeting.

units.la: NON desunt satscio & saepe audio qui cuperent à te, mi Calvine, domine colende & frater charissime, illud argumentum non fuisse tractatum. Sed suntrursus qui & gratias tibi agunt pro laboribus, in quorum numero & nos qui huic Ecclesiae ministramus, sumus, & agnoscunt argumentum hoc necessarium esse quod tractetur hodie. Dudum D. Vrbanus Regius vna cum omnibus Lunebur gen. Ecclesiae Ministris, edito etiam libro Germanico ostendit iure diuino & humano coerceri haereticos, tum etiam iure ciuili, si impia nō desinunt spargere, aut blasphemia in Deum sparserunt. Cur illi non irascuntur, qui in te hodie reprehendunt, quod probarent, si certius rem expendeerent? Nuper Titianus quidam Italus Anabaptista & Hebionita & Heluidianus in carcerem coniectus à tribus Rhetiae foederibus igni concremandus fuisset, nisi cecinisset palinodiam: nihilominus Curiae virgis caesus à Rhetio eiectus est. Quis ibi erat saevitiae & atrocitatis magister? Calvinus hoc non fecit nec suasit. Sunt etiam alij vbique viri boni qui intelligunt impios & blasphemos homines non tantum admonendos & in carcerem concludendos, sed etiam capite esse mulctandos. Ne ergo pigeat te suscepti laboris. Dominus sanctis conatibus & studiis non deerit. Scio tibi nec crudele esse ingenium nec te vllam atrocitatem approbare: quis nesciat etiam hic modum adhibendum esse? At quomodo Serueto lernæ hæresEon & pertinacissimo homini parci potuerit non video. Vale in Christo cum omnibus bonis. Orate pro nobis. Tiguri, xii. Iunij. M. D. LIIII.
units.tr: I am well aware, and I often hear, that there are some who wish you had not treated that subject, my dear Calvin, honoured lord and dearest brother. But there are also others who thank you for your labours, among whom are we who minister to this church, and who acknowledge that this question needs to be discussed today. Some time ago Dr Urbanus Regius, together with all the ministers of the churches of Lüneburg, published a German book showing that heretics are to be restrained both by divine law and by human law, and even by civil law, if they do not stop spreading impious teachings or have spread blasphemies against God. Why are those not angry who now find fault with you, when they would approve of it if they weighed the matter more carefully? Recently a certain Italian, Titianus, an Anabaptist, Ebionite and Helvidian, was thrown into prison by the three leagues of Rhaetia and would have been burned at the stake, had he not sung a palinode. Nevertheless, he was whipped by the court and expelled by the Rhaetian authorities. Who was the teacher of this cruelty and savagery there? Calvin did not do this, nor did he advise it. There are also other good men everywhere who understand that impious and blasphemous men must not only be admonished and shut up in prison, but also be punished with death. Do not, then, regret the labour you have undertaken. The Lord will not fail holy endeavours and studies. I know that your temperament is not cruel and that you approve of no atrocity; but who does not know that a measure must be observed here too? Yet I do not see how Servetus, that Lernaean hydra of heresies and most obstinate of men, could have been spared. Farewell in Christ, with all good people. Pray for us. Zurich, 12 June 1554.

units.la: SVLCERVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: Sulcerus to Calvin, greetings.
