units.la: Cæterum, quia vobis certamen est, non (solùm cum domesticis hostibus, sed qui se religionis Antistites, custodes sacrorum & Ecclesiæ patres ac tutores esse iactant: pt rpllexa forte in hoc metu hærebit Vestra Maiestas, ne quid præter officij sui rationem tentet. Et certè hoc filiis Dei propositum esse debet in omni actione, ac penitus fixum, ne vocationis suæ metas transiliant. Ergo ne quis vanus terror vos impediat vel moretur, paucis quatenus timendum sit, differam. Vt suam Hierarchiam nobis assiduè obtrudunt Papistæ: ita non dubito, quin eodem apud vos clypeo se muniat. Nam, quia nos in singulis doctrinæ capitibus longè superiores videntad hanc miseram latebram victi confugiunt: quanquam corruptissimus sit Ecclesiæ status, non licere, tamen Laicis, eius vitia attingere. Nec subterfugio contenti, cri-stas erigunt: quia Petro datus est in Ecclesiam Primatus, & totus Clerus Papalis continua successione ab ipsis Apostolis huc vsq; descenditad ipsos solos spectare ius & potestatem spiritualis regiminis. Quare hæc duo breviter discutere operæpretium fuerit. Neque tamen de Primatu Romanæ sedis quasi ex professo hic tractabo: quia hanc causam sic mihi egisse videor, vt iam non sine summa impudentia sibi arroget Papa, quod antea solebat: totius scilicet Ecclesiæ se esse caput. Nam quum Paulus ad vnitatem nos iortari volens, vnum Deum, vnam Fidem, vnum Baptismum, vnum Spiritum, vnum Dominum & vnum Ecclesiæ corpus esse docet minimè quod ad id probandum maximi ponderis erat, omittere debuisset, vnum esse summiū Pontificem, cuius auctoritas totam Ecclesiam in coniunctionis ordine retinet. Fuisset igitur hæc turpis obliuio, non monere fideles, vt sub vno capite diuin tus sibi præfecto maneant: si hoc verum fuisset, datum in omnes Ecclesias vni homini esse Primatu. Sed alibi satis idem se ipsum explicat, dum sibi eundem inter Gentiles Apostolatum esse assert, qui Petro datus erat inter Iudæos. Hic certè non modò statuitur æqualitas inter duos, sed talis sit partitio, vt propriè loquendo, minimè ad nos pertineat Petri Apostolatus. Denique in illo, quem nuper citaui loco, modum regendæ Ecclesiæ à Christo sancitū definiens, non dicit Vicarium vnum ab eo creatum esse, qui absentiā eius in terris supplerei: sed Apostolos, Pastores, & Doctores fuisse institutos, qui in commune secundum mensuram gratiæ vnicuique datam laborent. Certè si vnū omnibus præesse vellet Deus, non aliqua Spiritus portione cum donaret, sed plenitudinem conferret. Cauillum autem illud, ꝗ Petro datæ fuerint claues, ideo in præsentia nō refuto, quia plus satis alibi oftèsum fuit, Papæ nihilo magis prodesse, ac si id cuius Apostolorum dictum foret. Quæ enim illi cognatio vel affinitas cum Petro, vt se pro hæredeg̃ rat? Nam ꝗ loco ius datū esse ob-
units.tr: However, since you have a contest not only with domestic enemies but with those who boast that they are the prelates of religion, the guardians of the sacred rites, and the fathers and protectors of the Church, Your Majesty may perhaps be held back by this fear, lest you attempt something beyond the bounds of your office. Certainly this should be the purpose of the sons of God in every action, and it should be fixed deep within them, not to overstep the limits of their calling. So, lest some empty terror hinder or delay you, I will briefly explain how far it is to be feared. As the Papists constantly thrust their hierarchy upon us, so I do not doubt they shelter themselves behind the same shield before you. For since they see us far superior on each head of doctrine, they flee, beaten, to this wretched hiding-place: that although the state of the Church is most corrupt, it is nevertheless not lawful for laymen to touch its vices. Nor content with this subterfuge, they raise their crests again, because Primacy was given to Peter in the Church, and the whole Papal clergy, by continuous succession from the Apostles themselves down to this day, claims for itself alone the right and power of spiritual rule. Wherefore it will be worthwhile to discuss these two points briefly. Yet I will not treat the Primacy of the Roman see here as if ex professo, for I seem to have pleaded this cause so well that the Pope can no longer, without the greatest impudence, claim what he used to claim: namely, that he is the head of the whole Church. For when Paul, wishing to exhort us to unity, teaches that there is one God, one Faith, one Baptism, one Spirit, one Lord, and one body of the Church, he would have had to omit, since it was of the greatest weight for proving the point, that there is one supreme Pontiff whose authority holds the whole Church in the order of communion. It would then be a shameful oblivion not to warn the faithful to remain under one head divinely set over them, if it were true that a primacy had been given to one man over all the Churches. But elsewhere he explains himself sufficiently, when he asserts that he has the same apostleship among the Gentiles that Peter had among the Jews. Here not only is equality established between the two, but such a division is made that, properly speaking, the apostleship of Peter does not pertain to us at all. Finally, in the passage I cited a little while ago, where he defines the mode of governing the Church sanctioned by Christ, he does not say that one vicar was created by Christ to supply his absence on earth; rather, Apostles, Pastors and Teachers were instituted, who labour in common, each according to the measure of grace given to him. Certainly, if God had wished one man to preside over all, he would not have given a portion of the Spirit to each, but would have conferred the fullness upon one. As for that quibble, that the keys were given to Peter, I do not refute it here, because it has been shown sufficiently elsewhere that it profits the Pope no more than if it had been said of any of the Apostles. For what kinship or affinity has he with Peter that he should claim to be his heir? For what he pleads, that the right was given to one place,

units.la: v.iiij. tendit,plusquàm ineptum est.Cur enim Hierosolymæ potius nō esset sedes Primatus, vbi Filius Dei sine controuersia summus Pontifex Sacerdotio fundus est? Vetùm hæc,vt dixi,aliunde petere satius est,vbi plenius sunt exposita, quæadmodum & illud, nihil minus Christo fuisse propositum, quàm vnum inter Apostolos principem erigere.Nam summo Pontifici,qui sub lege viguit, ideo abrogata fuit dignitas, vt nunc solus Dei Filius emineat tanquam caput, omnibus in ordinem membrorum coaptis. Ac sacrilega audacia illud Apostoli dictum Papistæ ad probandum idoli sui tyrannidem detorquent, Translato Sacerdotio,necesse esse transferri legem.Neque enim illic Apostolus disputat, honorem summi Pontificis ab homine ad quemuis hominem translatum esse, sed residere in vnico Dei Filio cōtendit. Ita vt non alius quærendus sit successor: quia secundum ordinē Melchisedech ordinatus est Sacerdos, vt sine circat. Et nobis quidem abundè sufficere deberet vna Dei voluntas, sicuti vera est legi imæ gubernationis regula, & lex inuiolabilis. Sed accedit etiam,quòd neque possibile est,neque expedit, Vnum esse in terris totius Ecclesiæ caput:quia & hoc humanę infirmitatis modum longè excederet,neque aptari posset ad communem vsum. Denique sola ambitio & superbia Primatum hunc, quem nobis opponunt Romanenses,fabricauit. Vetus quidem Ecclesia Patriarchias instituit, & singulis etiam Prouinciis quoddam attribuit Primatus,vt hoc concordiæ vinculo melius inter se deuinēti manerent Episcopi. Quemadmodum si hodie illustrissimo Poloniæ regno vnus præesset Archiepiscopus,non qui dominarētur in reliquos,vel ius ab illis ereptum sibi arrogaret: sed qui ordinis causa in Synodis primum tenēret locum,& sanctam inter collegas suos & fratres vnitatem foueret. Essent deinde vel prouinciales, vel vrbani Episcopi, qui peculiariter ordini conseruando intenti forent.Sicuti hoc natura dictat, Vnum ex singulis collegiis deligendum,cui præcipua cura incumbat. Sed aliud est,moderatum gerere honorem,quatenus scilicet hominis facultas se extendit,quàm totum orbem terrarum immenso imperio complecti. Nugatorium ergo est,quod de vno capite Romanenses garriunt: quia nec sacra Dei ordinatio est,nec veteris Ecclesiæ vsu receptum,Christo, quem vnicum omnibus præfecit cœlestis Pater,adiungi secundum caput. Iam quanuisiure in Romanum Pontificem competeret summus honor: eo tamen se priuauit ipse,quum & à fide Apostolica defecit, & locum deseruit sibi diuinitus commissum. Nam vt primus sit inter Episcopos,ipsum esse Episcopum oportet. Porrò,quum Episcopi titulo indignum esse constet, qui officio docendi non fungitur: quid de eo sentiendum, qui non solùm deposito onere docendi, profanis pompis exultat, sed Christi doctrinam non minus crudeliter quàm impiè extinguere conatur? Si vult à Paulo aliquid mutuari Papa, sit minister Christi, & disspensator mysteriorum Dei. Si Petri elogiis vult se ornare, sit fidelis gregis pastor, & testis passionum Christi. Ab his vero quum sit ex professo alienus, ac ne simulet quidem se unum esse ex verbi Dei ministris: vltrò se & Primatu si quo alioqui fuisset ante præditus, abdicat. Adhæc, quo modo Ecclesiarum mater erit Roma, quæ Ecclesia nihilo magis censeri meretur, quàm Babylon? Ecclesiæ anima est doctrinæ puritas: quam Romæ esse prorsus abolitam quum certò certius sit, sequitur illic restare duntaxat mortuum cadauer. Denique nihil absurdius, quàm pro religionis Antistite coli in Christi grege, qui n anifestus est veri & germani Christianissimi hostis. Porrò longè fallitur Majestas Vestra, si expectat, dum ad ritè formandum regni Polonici statum, eius sedæ auctoritas interueniat, quam delectat vasta & horrenda confusio. Regnare cum sua caeruna non potest Papa Rom. nisi oppressa Ecclesia, fœdato Dei cultu, lacerato ordine, imò tota pietate deleta. An igitur sperandum est, vt qui Ecclesiæ exitio pascitur, remedium sanandis eius morbis vel afferat ipse, vel adhiberi consentiat? Nec verò, si pio & Christiano Principi res cofufas in melius restituere cordi est, vel vnius momenti remoram afferre debet, Pastorum ignauia, si in munere suo cessant. Tantum abest, vt iustè sanctos eius conatus impediat contumax eorum superbia, qui Pastores falsò vocitantur. Inane ergo terriculamentum est, nihil in Ecclesiæ re formatione nisi ex Papæ nutu, mouendum, vel tentandum esse, Quin potius quod exoriente primum Euangelio experti sunt Apostoli, hodie quoque impleri oportet: Christum ab architectis reprobatum, hoc est, qui Præsulum titulo se venditant; quia tamen constitutus est in caput anguli, minimè æquum esse, vt impiis eorum obstaculis cedat. Superest nunc altera quæstio: vt legitima sit successio, à quibus ordinandi sint Pastores. Ego quia magnopere referre video, nihil in Ecclesia confuse geri, ne hoc modo cuiusque libidini fræna laxentur, & nobis à Spiritu Dei difeste per os Pauli esse præscriptum, vt decenter & compositè fiant omnia, ordinarium ministerium reuerenter semper colendum esse censeo. Sic igitur fert vera ratio, & Dei mandatum, vt nemo se temere ingerat, nec priuatus quisque sibi Pastoris munus vsurpet. Sed vt Pastorum iudicio electus, & gregi oblatus ipso consentiente approbetur. Huc accedat solenis manuum impositio, quam ordinationem vocant. De qua sola dum tantopere nobiscum litigant Papistæ, satis ostendunt quod præcipuum erat se negligere, nempe electionem. Et sine apud eos tam frigida est exanimis cura, vt merus sit ludus coniunctus cum Dei ludibrio. Tantum in ceremoniæ pompa insistunt: nec contenti vetusto il lo ritu manuum imposi ionis, vnctione consecrant suos Sacer dotes: cuius neque in Scriptura fit mentio, neque vsus in Apo stolorum Ecclesia traditus. Quum vero eum ex fæce Iudaismi hauserint, vbicunque vigebit purior religio, cum aliis Papatus corruptelis abolenda erit. Sed alia superstitio longè deterior est, quòd suos Sacrificos non ad pascendi, vel docendi munus ordi nant, sed vt sacrilega audacia ius & officium Christi ad se rapi ant, & vsurpent, dum eos instituunt ad peragendum Missæ sacri ficium, quo fingunt Deum placari. Quare totum Sacerdotium Papisticum non solùm impia est veri ministerij profanatio, sed execrabilis in Christum contumelia: vt quisquis est Sacerdos Pa palis donec titulum illum abiecerit, Christi seruus esse nequeat. Itaque quanuis indelebilis secundum eos sit character, eradi ta men, & deleri necesse est, vt pa ros habeat Sacerdotes Dei Eccle sia. Altera etiam ignominiæ nota merito piis detestabile est Pa pale Sacerdotium. Nam quum secundū vetustos Canones quis quis ab hæreticis, vel schismaticis ordinationem petit, eodem se crimine implicat, non ignorat. V. Maiestas qualesiam multis se culis fuerint cornuti Vnctores. Nunc quisquis in illorum ordi nem se cooptari appetit, an non oblique in horrendam illam dissipationem cōsentit, cuius illi coram Deo & Angelis rei sunt? Nondum tamen soluta est quæstio: quia si promiscuè sas non est, quosu s ad Pastorum munus ascendere, rite vocari & insti tui necesse est, qui se probare volent legitimos, & honore dig nos. Hic, fateor, oprandum esset, vt valeret continua successio, vt functio ipsa quasi per manus traderetur. Sed memoria tenen dum est, quod prius attigi, quum Ecclesiæ anima sit doctrinæ pu ritas, frustra quæ Ecclesiæ propria sunt, & ab integro eius statu dependent, apud eos homines requiri, quos constat esse profes sos Euangelij hostes. Quia autem Papæ tyrannide abrupta fuit vera ordinationis series, nouo subsidio nunc opus est ad Eccle siæ instauratione m. Frustra quidem superbiunt Papistæ vincu lo illo, quod ab illis ruptum esse dixi. Quid enim aliud est Pa patus, quàm à Christo defectio? Qua autem fronte se Apostatæ, iactabunt successores? Remedium verò affert Deus ipse, dum i doneos & probos Doctores excitat, qui Ecclesiam in deformi bus Papatus ruinis iacentem ædificent. Atque omnino extraor dinarium fuit hoc munus, quod Dominus nobis iniunxit, du m opera nostra ad colligendas Ecclesias vsus est. Qui ergo ita præ ter spem hominum insolito modo repente apparuerunt, synce ræ pietatis vindices, eorum vocatio à communi regula æstima ri non debet. Cæterum, hac lege d uinitus vocati sunt, vt Eccle siis rectè compositis, alios Pastores substituant in suum locum. Quare praestantissime Rex, quicquid de hereditario Sacerdotij iure garriat Papalis Clerus, ne impediant futiles istae nugae, quo minus coelestibus auspiciis opus omnium maxime praeclarum, & coram Deo & Angelis laudabile aggrediatur Maiestas Vestra, vt Christus vnus in sua ditione cum puta Euangelij doctrina emineat. Haec vero & proba & utilis esset agendi ratio: quia nunc lupi Pastorum locum occupant, & nimis violentum remedium videri posset, si Pastores soli Regis auctoritate creati vocatione aliam non haberent: vt Maiestas Vestra tantum Doctores institueret, qui passim Euangelij semen spargerent. Esset autem hoc temporale munus, quantisper res incompositae manerent ac suspensae. Neque enim fieri potest, vt protinus mutetur publica Ecclesiae gubernatio. Sed hoc exordio, quod dixi, vel praeludio, com modus ad renouandam Ecclesiam transitus fieret. Denique non reformatio esset Ecclesiae sed quaedam solum praeparatio. Rebus autem maturis, regia auctoritate & suffragiis ordinum constitui posset in posterum certior ratio de Pastoribus creandis. Caeterum, quia sanae doctrinae hostes piis & synceris Doctoribus ianuam praecludere summa vi tentabunt, manum illis adiutricem a Vestra Maiestate porrigi necesse foret, vt libere plebem ab erraticis superstitionibus ad rectum pietatis cursum deducerent. Sed quia iam longius progressum me esse video, quam initio statueram, vt tædium Vestrae Maiestatis praeueniam, finem hic faciam scribendi. Dominus caelestis Pater manu vnigeniti Filij sui Vestram Maiestatem dirigat, praesidio tueatur, virtute sustineat, ac Spiritu gubernet. Rex praestantissime. Geneuae Nonis Decembris. M. D. LIIII.
units.tr: Indeed, it is more than foolish. For why was Jerusalem not rather the seat of the primacy, since the Son of God, beyond any dispute the supreme High Priest, was established there in his priesthood? But, as I have said, it is better to seek these matters elsewhere, where they are set out more fully, as also the point that Christ never intended to set up one prince among the Apostles. The dignity of the supreme pontiff, who held power under the law, was abolished so that the Son of God alone might stand out as the head, with all others fitted into the order of the members. The Papists, with sacrilegious audacity, twist the saying of the Apostle, "When the priesthood is changed, the law must necessarily be changed too," to prove the tyranny of their idol. Yet the Apostle is not arguing there that the honour of the supreme pontiff has passed from one man to any other man. He insists that it resides in the one Son of God alone, so that no other successor is to be sought, since he was ordained a priest "after the order of Melchisedec," without succession. And the single will of God ought to be quite enough for us, as it is the true rule of right government and an inviolable law. But it is also the case that it is neither possible nor expedient for there to be one head of the whole Church on earth, since this would far exceed the measure of human weakness and could not be adapted to common use. Finally, ambition and pride alone have fabricated this primacy which the Romanists set against us. The ancient Church did indeed institute patriarchates, and also granted a certain primacy to individual provinces, so that the bishops might remain more closely bound to one another by the bond of concord. It is as if, today, the most illustrious kingdom of Poland were presided over by one archbishop, not one who would lord it over the rest or claim for himself a right taken from them, but one who, for the sake of order, held the first place in the synods and fostered the holy unity among his colleagues and brethren. Then there would be provincial or city bishops, intent on preserving order in their own sphere. Nature itself dictates that one should be chosen from each college, to whom the chief care would fall. But it is one thing to hold an honour in moderation, that is, as far as human ability extends, and another to embrace the whole world under an immense empire. So what the Romanists chatter about a single head is trifling. It is neither a holy ordinance of God, nor a practice received in the use of the ancient Church, that a second head should be joined to Christ, whom the heavenly Father set over all as the only one. Now, although the highest honour might rightly belong to the Roman pontiff, yet he has deprived himself of it, since he has both fallen away from the apostolic faith and abandoned the place committed to him by God. For to be first among bishops, one must indeed be a bishop. Moreover, since it is clear that one who does not discharge the office of teaching is unworthy of the title of bishop, what should we think of him who not only lays down the burden of teaching and exults in profane pomp, but also tries to extinguish the doctrine of Christ no less cruelly than impiously? If the Pope wishes to borrow something from Paul, let him be a minister of Christ and a steward of the mysteries of God. If he wishes to adorn himself with the praises of Peter, let him be a faithful shepherd of the flock and a witness of the sufferings of Christ. But since he is quite openly a stranger to these things, and does not even pretend to be one of the ministers of the Word of God, he voluntarily renounces both the primacy, if he had possessed any, and everything else. Besides, how will Rome be the mother of the Churches, when she deserves to be counted no more a church than Babylon? The soul of the Church is the purity of doctrine, and since it is more than certain that this has been utterly abolished at Rome, it follows that only a dead carcass remains there. Finally, nothing is more absurd than to be worshipped in the flock of Christ as the champion of religion one who is manifestly the enemy of the true and genuine Christian faith. Moreover, Your Majesty is greatly mistaken if you expect that, until the authority of that see intervenes, the Polish kingdom's condition can be properly reformed, a see which delights in vast and dreadful confusion. The Roman Pope cannot reign with his crowd unless the Church is crushed, the worship of God defiled, good order torn apart, and indeed all piety destroyed. Can we then hope that he who feeds on the destruction of the Church will either himself bring a remedy to heal its diseases, or consent to its being applied? Nor indeed, if it is the desire of a pious and Christian prince to restore disordered affairs to a better state, ought the sloth of the ministers, if they neglect their duty, to cause the slightest delay. So far is the stubborn pride of those who are falsely called shepherds from justly hindering his holy efforts. It is therefore an empty scare-tactic that nothing in the reform of the Church may be moved or attempted except at the nod of the Pope. Rather, what the Apostles experienced when the Gospel first dawned must be fulfilled today as well: Christ, rejected by the builders, that is, by those who puff themselves up with the title of prelates, yet since he has been set as the head of the corner, it is by no means fair that he should give way to their impious obstacles. There remains now another question: by whom ministers should be ordained, so that the succession may be lawful. Since I see that it matters greatly that nothing in the Church be done in disorder, lest in this way the reins be loosened for each man's lust, and since the Spirit of God has prescribed to us through the mouth of Paul that all things be done decently and in order, I judge that the ordinary ministry must always be reverently observed. This, then, is what sound reason and the command of God require: that no one thrust himself in rashly, nor that any private person seize for himself the office of minister. Rather, let him be chosen by the judgement of the ministers, and presented to the flock, and be approved with the consent of the people themselves. Let the solemn laying on of hands, which they call ordination, be added to this. Concerning this alone the Papists quarrel with us so fiercely, and they sufficiently show that they have neglected what was chief, namely the election. And among them the care for it is so cold and lifeless that it is mere play joined with mockery of God. They insist only on the pomp of ceremony; and not content with that ancient rite of the laying on of hands, they consecrate their priests with anointing, of which there is no mention in Scripture, nor any practice handed down in the Church of the Apostles. Since they have drawn this from the dregs of Judaism, wherever a purer religion flourishes it will have to be abolished along with the other corruptions of Papistry. But another superstition is far worse, namely that they ordain their sacrificers not for the office of feeding or teaching, but so that, with sacrilegious audacity, they may seize and usurp for themselves the right and office of Christ, while they train them to perform the sacrifice of the Mass, by which they pretend God is appeased. Therefore the whole Papist priesthood is not only an impious profanation of the true ministry, but an execrable insult to Christ, so that whoever is a priest of the Pope cannot be a servant of Christ until he has cast off that title. And so, although according to them the character is indelible, it must nevertheless be erased and blotted out, so that the Church may have true priests of God. The Papal priesthood also bears another mark of infamy, which rightly makes it detestable to the pious. For, as the ancient canons provide, whoever seeks ordination from heretics or schismatics is not unaware that he entangles himself in the same crime. Your Majesty knows what sort of horned anointers they have been through many ages. Now, whoever desires to be co-opted into the order of those men, does he not obliquely consent to that dreadful ruin for which they are answerable before God and the angels? Yet the question is not yet resolved: for if it is not lawful to ascend indiscriminately to the office of the ministry, it is necessary that those who wish to prove themselves lawful and worthy of honour be duly called and instituted. Here, I confess, one would wish that a continuous succession might hold, so that the office itself might be handed down, as it were, from hand to hand. But it must be remembered what I touched on before: since the soul of the Church is the purity of doctrine, it is pointless to seek from those men, whom it is plain are professed enemies of the Gospel, the things that are proper to the Church and depend on its sound state. But because the true order of ordination was broken by the tyranny of the Pope, a new help is now needed for the restoration of the Church. The Papists indeed vainly boast of the bond which, I have said, they have broken. For what else is Papacy than a falling away from Christ? And with what face will apostates boast of their successors? God himself, however, provides the remedy, by raising up fit and upright teachers who may build up the Church lying in the ruins of the deformed Papacy. And truly this was an extraordinary office which the Lord laid upon us, when he used our labours to gather the Churches. Those, therefore, who have appeared so suddenly, beyond the hope of men, in an unusual manner, as champions of sincere piety, ought not to have their calling judged by the common rule. Moreover, they were called by God under this law: that, once the Churches were rightly constituted, they should put other ministers in their place. Therefore, most excellent King, whatever the Papal clergy may prattle about the hereditary right of the priesthood, let not these futile trifles hinder Your Majesty from undertaking, under heavenly auspices, the most distinguished of all works, one that is praiseworthy before God and the angels, so that Christ alone, with the pure doctrine of the Gospel, may stand out in his own dominion. Indeed this would be a proper and useful course of action, since now wolves occupy the place of pastors, and it might seem too violent a remedy if the ministers, created by the authority of the King alone, had no other calling. Your Majesty might establish only teachers, who would scatter the seed of the Gospel everywhere. This would, however, be a temporary office, for as long as affairs remained unsettled and in suspense. For the public government of the Church cannot be changed at once. But by this beginning, or prelude, as I have called it, a convenient transition to the renewal of the Church would be made. In short, it would not be a reformation of the Church, but merely a certain preparation. Then, when matters had matured, a more certain plan for the creation of ministers could be established in the future by royal authority and the votes of the estates. Moreover, since enemies of sound doctrine will strive with all their might to close the door against pious and sincere teachers, it would be necessary for Your Majesty to extend a helping hand to them, so that they might freely lead the common people from wandering superstitions onto the right path of piety. But since I see that I have gone further than I had intended at the start, I will here make an end of writing, so as to spare Your Majesty's weariness. May the heavenly Father direct Your Majesty by the hand of his only-begotten Son, protect you with his help, sustain you with his strength, and govern you by his Spirit. Most excellent King, Geneva, on the Nones of December, 1554.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS PIO CVIDAM FRATRI, S. D.
units.tr: John Calvin to a certain pious brother, greetings.

units.la: Benedictus Dominus qui tua opera tam opportune vsus est hactenus, ad subleuanda fratrum nostrorum vincula: & qui te in sancto opere confirmauit spiritu suo, vt nulli rei pereceris. Hoc est inquam, certissimum argumentum ad praedicandam ipsius gloriam: cum tantum opus non alij quam ipsi ad scribendum sit, quum & illius aggrediendi tibi auctor fuerit, & perpetuo te etiam direxerit. Tibi vero non vulgare gaudium hinc percipiendum est, cum agnoscis quo te honore affecerit, qui te functione tam nobili & gloriosa ornauit, & manum porrexit tibi, vt tanto muneri par esse posses. Vt cunque enim miseri fratres, qui Euangelij nomine laborant, contemptibiles sint & reiecti a mundo: scimus tamen, vt Dominus sacri peculij loco habeat, vt nō aliud ipsi sacrificium sit acceptius, quam vbi ad illos subleuandos, & opem ferendam strenuē nos impendimus. Et quum Dominus Iesus testetur agnicurum fe quasi erga fe præ-stitum,quod in quemlibet ex suis collatum fuerit,quid speran-dum nobis ab illo est, quum illis ipsis aderimus qui ipsius nomi ne laborant? Nam & illi quasi procuratores mandato Domini instructi,ad Euangelij defensionem ab ipso sistuntur. Quare ne poculum quidem aquæ frigidæ ipsis oblatum , nobis etiam de- periturum promisit. Proinde quū ita animatus fueris hactenus, ad legitimum illud sacrificium Domino offerendum,contendē porrò, vt eodem animo deinceps pergas. Neque vero nescio, quid insusurraturus sit tibi Satā, vt à sancto opere te auertat. Sed vide vt Dominus suum in te supremum illud ius vt æquum est, semper habeat. Acquiesce etiam in hoc testimonio,quod qui o-peram in eo collocant, vt opitulentur Filiis Dei persecutionem sustinentibus propter Euangelium, ipsi eo nomine Coadiutores Euangelij appellentur. Nam quanti momenti hoc est,quod in-signe illud Martyrum nomen in nos transcribat Dominus, e-tiamsi persecutio ad nos vsque non pertingat,tantum quia ipsius Martyribus officia nostra impendimus? Quicquid igitur ex op-posito auditurus sis, caue ne tam laudabili cœpto renunties,aut in medio cursu deficias. Equidem mihi sic persuadeo,te nullo pa-sto hominum de te iudicia tibi proposuisse, cùm hoc primum agere cœpisti. Fac igitur vt te illi semper impendas,cui fides ad extremum vsque seruanda est. Cogita etiam quàm multi ex piis qui propter te nunc Deum glorificant, si te propositi minus te-nacem agnoscerent,grauiter offenderentur! Nam quad vinctos ipsos attinet,illi de te ita sentiunt,& in te sunt affecti,vt si libe-ris esse daretur,caput suum pro te etiam morti obiicere non du bitent,nedum vt sua fraude vel improbitate tibi creent periculum. Illud etiam veniat tibi in mentem,quod piis illis ita opem & auxilium adsert, hoc ad illos confirmandos valere plurimùm, cùm præsentem ergà se Dei manum in tuo beneficio , vti par est,agnoscant. Sic inquam,crescit ipsis in Deum fiducia,de cu-ius paterno erga se studio,ipsis per te tam appositè constat. Ro-borare igitur,& vir esto, cùm opus illud sanctissimum non Deo tantùm & Martyribus,sed toti etiam Ecclesiæ impendas. Vale mi frater.Deum oro,vt & sua in te dona cumulet magis ac magis, & ad suam gloriam efficacia reddat, & te præsidio suo singulari complestatur. x.Augusti.
units.tr: Blessed be the Lord, who has so opportunely made use of your work until now to relieve the chains of our brothers, and who has strengthened you in his holy work by his Spirit, so that you might be frightened by nothing. This, I say, is a most certain proof for proclaiming his glory, since such a great work was not undertaken by anyone other than himself, seeing that he was its author from the start and has guided you throughout. Indeed, you ought to take no small joy from this, since you recognise the honour with which he has favoured you, who has adorned you with a function so noble and glorious, and has stretched out his hand to you so that you might be equal to so great a task. However wretched our brothers who suffer for the name of the Gospel may be, and however despised and rejected by the world, we know that the Lord regards them as his sacred treasure, and that no sacrifice is more acceptable to him than when we devote ourselves vigorously to relieving and aiding them. And since the Lord Jesus testifies that he will regard as done to himself whatever is bestowed on any one of his own, what may we hope for from him, when we stand by those who labour in his name? For they, as agents instructed by the Lord's command, are presented by him in defence of the Gospel. Therefore he has promised that not even a cup of cold water offered to them will go unrewarded. Accordingly, since you have been so inspired until now to offer that lawful sacrifice to the Lord, strive onward so that you may continue with the same spirit from now on. Nor indeed am I unaware of what Satan will whisper to you in order to turn you away from this holy work. But see that the Lord always keeps his supreme right over you, as is only fair. Take comfort also in this testimony: that those who devote their labour to helping the sons of God who suffer persecution for the Gospel are themselves called fellow-workers of the Gospel. For how great a thing it is that the Lord should transfer that distinguished name of Martyrs to us, even though persecution does not reach us, simply because we render our services to the Martyrs themselves! Whatever you may hear from the opposite side, take care not to renounce so laudable an undertaking or to fail in the middle of the course. Indeed I am persuaded that you have not set before yourself any human judgments of yourself, since you began this work. Therefore see to it that you always devote yourself to him to whom faithfulness must be kept to the end. Consider also how many of the godly, who now glorify God on your account, would be gravely offended if they recognised you as less steadfast in your purpose! As for the prisoners themselves, they think of you in such a way and are so disposed towards you that, if it were granted to them to be free, they would not hesitate to expose their own heads to death for you, let alone bring you danger by their own fault or wickedness. Let this also come into your mind: that the help and assistance you bring to these godly people is of great value in strengthening them, since they recognise, as is fitting, God's present hand in your kindness. Thus, I say, their trust in God grows, since through you they are so clearly assured of his fatherly zeal towards them. Be strong, then, and be a man, since you devote that most holy work not only to God and the Martyrs but to the whole Church as well. Farewell, my brother. I pray God that he may heap his gifts upon you more and more, make them effective for his own glory, and surround you with his singular protection. 10 August.

units.la: EPISTOLA CVIVSDAM NOMINE SCRIPTA, qui se à Patre Religionis nomine subduxerat.
units.tr: A LETTER WRITTEN IN THE NAME OF A CERTAIN PERSON, WHO HAD WITHDRAWN FROM THE FATHER OF THE RELIGION.

units.la: {a}Quod facti mei ratione scripto & absens potius quàm præsens exhibeo, peto à te, obseruàde Pater, vt me excusatum habeas. Duo in causa sunt: vnum, quòd veritus sim, vt, in re odiosa & in speciem aliena, satis facilem ad me audiendum te haberem: alterum, quòd summa illa reuerentia qua te prosequor, mihi apud te quicquam istorum proferre hactenus nō permiserit. Nunc verò ineundam mihi hanc rationem esse duxi, qua vel te placarem, quatenus offensionem de me conceptam retineres, vel saltem quicquid istud est, emollirem, dum oblata meliori occasione, tibi ad plenum satisfacerem. Dolet tibi, quia cultus Dei ratione quem pro vero habes, te non sequar. Hoc si contemptu facerem, vt leues multi homines, quibus susque deque est omnis religio, quique omni affectu in cultus Dei obseruatione vacui sunt, nulla venia non esset indignissimus. Sin verò Dei timor, & conscientiæ testimonium eo me impulerunt, sic mihi persuadeo, vtroque illo nomine meum à te factum tolerabilius iudicatum iri. Iam ne te multis obtundam, negari hoc nō potest, quin multi & crassi abusus & corruptelæ in Ecclesia locū habeant, qui Dei nomine teguntur: & bona intentio ista omnia eluere creditur. Interea qui sic viuunt, vt sine Dei voluntatis auctoritate, Deo se approbatum iri statuant, illi vt vulgo dicitur, rationem suam sine hospite subducunt. Siquidem fixum esse illud debet, Deum non ex nostro, sed ex ipsius arbitrio colendum esse. Me verò ferendum nō esse, fateor si his de rebus ex meo sensu pronuntiare audeam, quasi aliis iudicio plus valeam. Sed non hic agitur quis melius sapiat inter homines: illa enim regula & nota est, & communi omnium sensu comprobata, Deum præferre obedientiam sacrificiis omnibus. Quare vt res subtilius nō expendatur, satis constat, à Deo reici, quicquid ipsius voluntati non respondet. Testimonium autem voluntatis Dominiex vna Scriptura in qua consignatum extat, petendum est. Vnde fit, vt quicquid se offerret, quod repugnet Scripturæ ab eo mihi cauendum sit, nisi sciens in Deum peccare velim. Hoc autem loco habere me quæ communi consensu tam sancta esse credantur, absurdum tibi videri poterit. Verum hoc vnum à te mi pater postulo, vt cum ea sim ætate, quæ ad quiduis admittendum magis prona iudicari solent, ne tamen hoc meum tatis de rebus iudicium iuuenili leuitate adscribas: cum potius idoneo & omni exceptione maiore veritatis testimonio pressus ac peruictus, ita sentire cœperim. Quod enim per Dei gratiam, & legendo & audiendo
units.tr: {a}Since I am presenting my action to you in writing and in absence rather than in person, I ask you, honoured Father, to hold me excused. There are two reasons. The first is that I feared that, in a matter that is hateful and in appearance alien, you would have too little patience to listen to me. The second is that the great reverence with which I follow you has until now not allowed me to bring any of these things before you. But now I have thought that I should adopt this method, by which I might either appease you, insofar as you still hold the offence conceived against me, or at least soften whatever it is, so that when a better occasion is offered I may fully satisfy you. It grieves you that I will not follow the worship of God in the way that you hold to be true. If I did this out of contempt, like many frivolous men for whom all religion is a matter of indifference, and who are empty of all feeling in the observance of God's worship, I would be most unworthy of any pardon. But if the fear of God and the testimony of my conscience have impelled me to it, I persuade myself that my action will be judged more tolerable on both counts. Now, not to weary you with many words: it cannot be denied that many gross abuses and corruptions exist in the Church, which are covered over in God's name, and that this good intention is believed to wash all of them away. Meanwhile, those who live in such a way that they judge they will be approved by God without the authority of God's will, they, as the common saying goes, reckon their account without the host. For it must be fixed that God is to be worshipped not according to our own judgment but according to his own decision. I admit that I should not be borne with if I dared to pronounce on these matters from my own sense, as though I carried more weight in judgment than others. But the question here is not who is wiser among men. That rule and mark is known, and approved by the common sense of all: that God prefers obedience to all sacrifices. Therefore, even if the matter is not weighed more subtly, it is quite clear that whatever does not correspond to his will is rejected by God. The testimony of the Lord's will, however, must be sought from Scripture alone, in which it is recorded. Hence, whatever presents itself to me that is contrary to Scripture I must guard against, unless I wish knowingly to sin against God. That I should hold to things which by common consent are believed to be so holy may seem absurd to you. Yet this one thing I ask of you, my father: although I am of that age which is usually judged more prone to admit anything, do not ascribe this judgment of mine on these matters to youthful levity. Rather, I have begun to think thus, pressed and overcome by a suitable testimony of truth, which admits of no exception. For what, by the grace of God, I have learned both by reading and by hearing...

units.la: {a} Epist. 151. Ex Gall. assequi datum est,illi refragari tandem non potui. Quamobrem mi Pater,vbi ex illa certa scientia,quæ conscientiam meam regere debet,aliquid malu n esse mihi constat, illi interesse nefas mihi iudico:etsi mihi non parum dolet,quod ab illis rebus abstinere sine tui offensione non possum. Nihil enim mihi & optabilius est,& meo voto accommodatius, quam vt meum tibi obsequium præstem,atque approbem. Vnum me impedit,cuius a re imputatio nem supplex deprecor, quod reluctante conscientia si quid aggrediar,meipsum in me iudicem ferre cogar. Absit vero a moribus meis omnis arrogantia, & de me supra alium quenquam existimationis labes. Tantum hoc volo,quod qui a Deo edoctus sim, quid rectum sit vel secus,illud insuper habere iam non possim. Cumque singulis de se apud illum ratio aliquando reddenda sit, vt aliis sua ignorantia in Dei iudicio fraudi etiam non sit, non video tamen quid a me obtendi possit, si a Dei notitia & vero ipsius cultu mihi explorato semel deflectam. Quid porro in ipsis rerum obtineat argumentis, neque pro meo captu hic apud te attingo, neque etiam eo tibi molestiam augere nunc quidé velim. Quod si mihi non denegas, vt vel perstringam aliquid eius, quo summa fere momenta verti video,sic accipe. Me cum a gratuita illa peccatorum remissione,quæ Christi Domini morte no bis parta,ac eiusdem gratiæ obsignatione,quæ sacrosancto Cœnæ Mysterio nobis exhibenda & applicanda ab ipso Christo instituta est,in sacrificium illud sua vi operatorium,& mortis Christi per se applicatiuum, & illam elementi adorationem (quid autem hoc sit tacendo satis indico) oculos & mentem conuerto,plane aliter sentire non posse, quam cum illa e cælo sint, vt omnino constat,ista ab hominibus(ne quid grauius dicam)pro fœda videri. Proinde nullius esse momenti, vbi de Deo colendo, & veritate ipsius sine fermento retinenda agitur. Sed & ista fortasse minus parce hoc loco,si mei captus & tenuitatis rationem tantum habeas. Tandem vero illud a te contendam,mi Pater,vt si ad me audiendum vsque propendere dignaberis,Patruum tecum admittere graue non sit,quod tibi non incommodè cessurum,mihi non temere persuadeam. Bene vale,obseruande Pater,ac tuum propter Deum subductitium,tua benevolentia non magis indignum agnosce.
units.tr: {a} Letter 151. From the French. I could not in the end refuse to agree with. Therefore, my father, when it is clear to me from that certain knowledge which ought to govern my conscience that something is wrong, I judge it wrong for me to take part in it, although it grieves me not a little that I cannot abstain from those things without offending you. For nothing is more desirable to me, or more in accord with my wish, than to render and show you my obedience. One thing hinders me, and I humbly beg you to pardon the charge against me: if I undertake anything while my conscience resists, I shall be forced to pass judgment on myself. Far be from my manners all arrogance, and any stain of esteem above anyone else. I want only this: since I have been taught by God what is right and what is not, I can no longer set that aside. And since each one must one day give account of himself before him, so that ignorance is no defence for anyone in God's judgment, I do not see what I could plead, if I should turn aside once I had securely grasped the knowledge of God and his true worship. As to what weighs in the very arguments of these matters, I neither touch on it here according to my capacity before you, nor do I now wish to add to your trouble. But if you do not deny me this, that I may touch on some part of what I see the chief points turn upon, accept it thus. When I turn my eyes and mind from that free forgiveness of sins, which was won for us by the death of Christ the Lord, and from the sealing of that same grace, which Christ himself instituted to be offered and applied to us in the most holy mystery of the Lord's Supper, to that sacrifice which works by its own power and applies the death of Christ by itself, and to that adoration of the element (what this is I indicate sufficiently by my silence), I cannot feel otherwise than that, since those things are from heaven, as is entirely plain, these things appear foul to men (not to say anything more harshly). Therefore nothing is of any moment where the worship of God and the keeping of its truth without leaven are at issue. But perhaps these matters too you would treat less sparingly here, if you took account only of my capacity and humble understanding. Finally, however, I press this upon you, my father: if you deign to lean toward hearing me, it would not be grievous to admit my uncle along with you, which I think will not turn out inconveniently for you, though I do not rashly persuade myself of it. Farewell, respected Father, and acknowledge that the one who has, for God's sake, secretly withdrawn from you is no less unworthy of your goodwill.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: John Calvin sends greetings in his own name.

units.la: Quum de facie tibi ignotus sim,absurdum tamen non videbitur, quod ad te scripserim, si tuos liberos istius consilij auctores apud te citauero. Hoc etiam ad illud valere cupio, vt sine vllo excusationum circuitu,te quamprimum hic cöpellem. lem. Etenim hoc de te accepi, si quid ad te scriberem, non tantum à te placidè admissum iri, sed neque molestum tibi futurum illud perlegere, & apud te deinde meditari & expendere. Illud eam de te spem mihi iniecit, ut cum pietatis semen in te subesse videam, cultura demum adhibita, fructum inde consecuturum suo tempore apud me cōstituerem. Cùm igitur ad teipsum exco lendū hoc scriptum pertineat, imprimis hoc tecū reputes velim, Nihil magis decere Christianū hominem, quàm vt dum abusus & corruptelas in Dei cultu (qui habetur) palpabiles notare potest, ac debet, det etiam operam, ne promiscuo consensu sese in illo cœno volutari sinat: inde potius discat sibi de Dei veritate inquirendum esse, vt in illa tuto acquiescat. Alterū etiam addo, vt quod de nostra doctrina subiiciā, placidè audias: breui enim faciam, vt tanto facilius agnoscas quam viam sequamur, & quò illa etiam ferat. Primùm igitur satis constat quamplurimos in ignorantia & superstitione hærere, cùm ne oculos quidē ad lucem oblatam aperire sustineant: quorum te in numero cum habeā, aperte significo, vt ad illud demōstrandum vel persuadendum tibi, lōgior à me exhortatio adhibenda non sit. Atqui illud vnum præcipuè Christianum hominem facit, si in certa Dei colendi ratione sibi attēdendum statuat, ne spōte decipiatur, in re præsertim tanti momenti, vbi æterna animæ salus vertitur. Notum est autem Christianismū adulterarum & corruptum fuisse, Pastorū Ecclesiæ tum cessatione, tum imperitia, ambitione, auaritia. Neq; hanc degenerationem ad illorum vitam & mores restringo, cùm in illa primas obtineat, ipsius Dei veritatis in mendacium & impostura transformatio: cultus Dei innumeris supersti-tionibus adductis cōtaminatio: ordinis Ecclesiæ extrema perturbatio: vsus Sacramentorū confpurcatio: vt vno verbo finiā, stupenda & omnem sensum exuperans inordinatio. Hoc verò si pauci animaduerterint, inde fit, quod regula Lesbia hic pro norma tantum obtinet. Iā si Religioni illi Catholicæ pura & natiua Dei institutio opponatur, eadem illic cōuenientia quæ lucis ad tene bras deprehenditur. Quare vt quis istis de rebus vere cognoscat & sentiat, neq; Principis auctoritati, neq; cōsuetudinis præscriptioni, neq; suo ipsius sensui standū est: consulendum verbum D. & quid illic mādet aut vetet. Nā neq; Dominus in angulo locutus est, & suā voluntate tum summis tū infimis patefactā esse voluit.
units.tr: Although I am unknown to you by sight, it will not seem absurd that I have written to you, if I cite your own children as the authors of this plan. I also want this letter to serve the purpose that I may summon you here as soon as possible, without any round-about excuses. For I have heard this about you: if I should write to you, you would not only receive it kindly, but also would not find it burdensome to read it through and then to consider and weigh it for yourself. This hope has been planted in me, that since I see the seed of piety in you, once it is cultivated, I may expect to gather fruit from it in due time. Since this writing therefore concerns your own improvement, I would especially have you consider this: nothing becomes a Christian man more than that, when he can and should notice the plain abuses and corruptions in the worship of God as it is commonly practised, he should also take care not to let himself be tossed about in that mire by universal agreement. Rather, he should learn from this that he must inquire into the truth of God, so that he may rest securely in it. I add one more thing: please hear calmly what I will set out about our doctrine. For I will briefly make it easier for you to see which way we follow and where it leads. First, it is quite clear that very many remain in ignorance and superstition, since they cannot even bring themselves to open their eyes to the light offered to them. I openly say that you are among their number, so there is no need for a longer exhortation from me to prove or persuade you of this. Yet one thing above all makes a Christian man: if he resolves to pay attention to a fixed way of worshipping God, so that he is not deceived of his own accord, especially in a matter of such great weight, where the eternal salvation of the soul is at stake. It is well known that Christianity has been adulterated and corrupted, both through the negligence and through the ignorance, ambition and greed of the ministers of the Church. Nor do I restrict this degeneration to their life and morals. For among these evils the first place is held by the transformation of the very truth of God into lies and deceit; by the contamination of the worship of God with countless superstitions; by the extreme disorder of the order of the Church; by the defiling of the use of the sacraments; and, to sum up in one word, by a stupefying disorder that surpasses all understanding. If few have noticed this, the reason is that the Lesbian rule is the only standard here. Now if the pure and native institution of God is set against that so-called Catholic religion, the same agreement is found there as is found between light and darkness. Therefore, if anyone is to know and judge these matters truly, he must rely neither on the authority of a prince, nor on the prescription of custom, nor on his own opinion. Instead, he must consult the Word of the Lord, and see what it commands or forbids. For the Lord has neither spoken in a corner, nor has he willed that his will be revealed only to the great or only to the lowly.

units.la: Illud verò vbi à teipso obtinueris, vt patiente autem Deo loquē ti accōmodes, illis quæ verbo nobis tradidit acquiescas, vnā salutis viam ab eo vno petendam & percipiēdam tibi statuas, magnum tibi aditum adea quæ nostrūm quemque tenere expedit, pernosceuda cōparaueris. Ad nostram doctrinam veniō: quā ple riq; inauditam & inexploratā suo quodam præiudicio damnāt, occupati nimirum nescio qui opinione, quae aciem mëtis ipso-rum hac in re prorsus obtundat. Non attingo contumelias, & scelera etiam, quae nobis imponuntur, vt à nostris degustandis cuertátur omnes. Atqui hoc vnum nobis imputari potest, quod eos omnes qui Christi nomine censentur, adhuc miserè palantes, ad sua illa signa, Verbum Dei nempe reuocare cötendimus. Simul etiam cuincimus, controuersias omnes de Dei cultu, ex verbo ipsius esse dirimendas, vt vnusquisque teneat, quod à Deo esse cõstabit, quid hic aduersarij? Ecclesiam scilicet, vt Aiacis clypeum ementiuntur, vt sub illius larua secure lateant. Nec vero alia fuit ratio Prophetarum & Apostolorum cum res ipsis effet cum illis, qui etiam Ecclesiae nomen, & summam in ea auctoritatem eadem mala fide vsurpabant. Quid igitur? Nouimus vero Ecclesiam illam quae certo fundamento nititur doctrinę Prophetice atque Apostolicæ, cuius caput angulare & immotum Christus est & manet. Adulterina vero illa est, in qua nö regnat Dei verbum. Eo posito hoc inferimus, cultum Dei ex mandato ipsius institruendum esse. Nihil hic humanitus traditum inuectum-ve ferri posse. Vnius enim Dei est, legem figere conscientiis. Vnius ius esse, praescribere, quid ipse fieri à nobis velit. Hinc illæ querimoniæ, Vos sanctæ matris Ecclesiæ stutata pessum dedi-stis: quoniam post Euiam auctore Christo testamur, fructra Dei coli mandatis hominum: item ex Iacobo, Vnum Legislatorem esse, penes quem sit seruare & perdere. Ac si quid illud est, quod Dei cultus nomine ab istis ornatur, interdum inspexeris, merum illic commentum ex hominum cerebro conflatum reperies. Iam si de fide & invocatione agitur, quia Scriptura nos ad vnam Christi gratiam amandat, miserabilem conditionem nostram ob oculos ponit, quæ certissimam condemnationem secum afferat: nos vero præeunte Scriptura, homines ad illam vnius Christi gratiæ agnitionem & prædicationem reuocamus, quod rursum statui non potest, quin momento abfurdissimum illud meritorum commentum ad vitam æternam lucrifacien-dam corruat. Hinc & illæ obnuntiationes, Vos omnem bonorum operum doctrinam & studium de medio tollitis? Scilicet illa aduersum nos calumnia stare potest, cum omnis aduersariorum istis de rebus in suis cōcionibus docendi ratio plusquam euanida fit, si ad feriam & exactam quæ ministerio nostro traditur & inculcatur sanctæ vitæ institutionem vel eminus admonita conferatur. Hoc vero sic assidue procuratur à nobis, vt tamen qu sseipsum fallat aliqua operum furorum iactatione, sic aperte doceamus: neque posse nos quicquam boni, nisi Spiritu Dei nos dirigente, neque adeo sancte viuentibus (cum innumeri sint nostri defectus, nihil in nobis non caducum in sese, & nullius lius ad iustitiam coram Deo exhibendam momenti) fundamen- tum aliud non extare, quo solida iustitia nobis cõstet, quàm vt Christi vnius crucem ac mortem omnibus aliis post tergum re- iectis, ambabus manibus complectamur. Huic fidei fundamen- to, veram inuocationem ita connectimus, vt & ad Deum vnum preces nostras dirigendas esse ostendamus, cum nos ad se com- pellet: & ne nostrae indignitatis conscientia ab illo nos auertat, per Christum vnum, vti apud Patrem Mediatior nobis offertur, ad thronum gratiae cum certa fiducia accurrendum nobis sit. Hinc & illae lacrymae, Vos in sanctos & sanctas Dei contume- liosi estis: vos illorum cultum & honorem sustulistis! Scilicet! cum sanctorum Dei hominum memoriam eo quo Dominus nos docet loco habendo, syncero studio illam retinemus, & ho- nore prosequimur: ferre autem non possumus vt Sancti ipsi in idola transformati, Dei aut Christi loco habeantur. Imò etiam affirmare audemus, si quid istorum per quae mundus insaniens suo more, creaturis semper affixus Creatorem secure despicit, si quid inquam, istorum piae illae & iam felices animae sentiunt, totas zelo accendi ad Dei iudicium in sacrile gos istos suos cul- tores accersendum. Quod ad sacramenta attinet, cum illorum & vsus & scopus sit, vt nos in Dei timore, reuerentia, & miseri- cordiae fide confirment, dici non potest, quàm indigne omnia hic etiam inuersa atque interpolata sint. Et nobis adhuc obiici- tur, vbi illa suae puritati quasi veris natalibus restituere cona- mur, Sacramenta à nobis exinaniri. Expendatur verò nostra o- mnis ratio ad vnam institutionem Domini, vt si quid ab illa dif crepet, adnotetur. Exulat quidem hinc Missa, vt istic regnat. Sed postliminio rediit Coena Domini, ipsa inquam Coena Domini, vti ab ipso semel instituta est, quod neq; ipsi aduersarij inficiari possunt. Tantum suum ritum & receptum seruitium diuinum, quod vocant, obiiciunt pro omni defensione. Nos verò meliori iure & firmiori nitimur, mandato Domini ipsius, quod inuiola- tum itare oportet vsque ad finem seculi. Hoc faciendo inquit Paulus, mortem Domini annunciabitis donec veniat. Hic igi- tur nemo quicquam immutare potest, quin rebellionis crimi- ne coram Domino teneatur. Prolixior sim, si reliqua attingam, quae magis praetermittam. Et satis etiam nunc fuerit, te ex istis quae hic habes gustum aliquem percepisse, quite ad vberiorem cognitionem pleniore tractatione accedente perducat. Vale in D.Dominus te Spiritu suo regat, à quo ipsius voluntati respon- dere discas, & tuae saluti ac tranquillitati consultum velit. Geneuae.
units.tr: But once you have brought yourself to accommodate yourself to God speaking, to rest in what he has handed down to us in his Word, and to resolve that the one way of salvation is to be sought and grasped from him alone, you will have prepared for yourself a great entrance into those things which it is useful for each of us to know thoroughly. I come to our doctrine, which many condemn as unheard of and untested, out of a prejudice of their own, being occupied, I know not by what opinion, which utterly dulls the edge of their mind in this matter. I do not touch on the insults and even the crimes that are imputed to us, so that everyone may be turned away from tasting our teaching. Yet this one thing can be charged against us: that we strive to recall all those who are counted in the name of Christ, who are still wandering wretchedly, to their proper marks, namely the Word of God. At the same time we also show that all controversies about the worship of God must be settled from the Word of God itself, so that each person may hold what is shown to be from God. What do our opponents say to this? They pretend, like Ajax's shield, that it is the Church, so that they may lie safely hidden beneath its mask. Nor was the method of the Prophets and Apostles any different when they had to deal with those who used the very name of the Church, and its supreme authority, with the same bad faith. What then? We know that the true Church is the one that rests on the sure foundation of the prophetic and apostolic doctrine, whose cornerstone and immovable head is and remains Christ. But that other church is an adulterous one, in which the Word of God does not reign. Having laid this down, we infer that the worship of God must be ordered according to his command. Nothing introduced or brought in by human hands can be admitted here. For it belongs to God alone to fix his law in consciences, and to him alone belongs the right to prescribe what he wishes to be done by us. Hence those complaints: "You have trampled the holy mother Church underfoot." For we testify, on the authority of Christ, that "in vain do they worship me with the commandments of men"; likewise from James: "There is one lawgiver, who has the power to save and to destroy." And if you look at whatever it is that they adorn with the name of the worship of God, you will find that it is nothing but a fiction fabricated in the human brain. Now if the matter concerns faith and invocation, since Scripture sends us to the one grace of Christ alone, and sets before our eyes our wretched condition, which carries with it most certain condemnation, we, following Scripture, call men back to the recognition and proclamation of that one grace of Christ. This in turn cannot stand without the immediate collapse of that most absurd fiction of merits for gaining eternal life. Hence also those accusations: "You take away all teaching and zeal for good works?" Of course that slander cannot stand against us, since the whole method our opponents use in their sermons to teach these matters is more than empty, if it is compared, even from a distance, with the sound and exact instruction in holy living that is handed down and impressed by our ministry. This is so constantly pursued by us, yet we teach so plainly that no one may deceive himself by some boasting about works. We teach that we can do nothing good unless the Spirit of God directs us, and that, since our defects are countless and nothing in us is not perishable in itself and of no weight for showing justice before God, there is no other foundation on which solid righteousness may be established for us, than that we embrace with both hands the cross and death of Christ alone, casting all else behind our backs. To this foundation of faith we so join true invocation that we show that our prayers must be directed to the one God, since he summons us to himself; and so that the awareness of our unworthiness may not turn us away from him, we must with sure confidence run to the throne of grace through Christ alone, who is offered to us as Mediator before the Father. Hence also those tears: "You are insolent against the saints of God; you have taken away their worship and honour!" Of course! While we keep the memory of the saints of God with sincere zeal, holding it in the place where the Lord teaches us to hold it, and we honour it, we cannot bear that the saints themselves should be transformed into idols and held in the place of God or of Christ. Indeed we even dare to affirm that if those pious and now blessed souls perceive anything of those things by which the raving world, as is its custom, fixed to creatures, securely despises the Creator, they are all set on fire with zeal to summon these sacrilegious worshippers of theirs to the judgment of God. As for the sacraments, since their use and purpose is to strengthen us in the fear of God, in reverence, and in faith in his mercy, it cannot be said how unworthily everything here too has been turned upside down and corrupted. And we are still objected to: when we try to restore the sacraments to their purity, as to their true birth, they say that we empty them out. But let our whole reasoning be weighed against the single institution of the Lord, so that if anything departs from it, it may be noted. Certainly the Mass is banished from here, as it reigns there. But the Lord's Supper has returned by right of return: the Lord's Supper itself, I say, as it was once instituted by him, which even our opponents cannot deny. They put forward only their own rite and the service of God that has been accepted, as they call it, as their whole defence. But we rest on a better right and a firmer ground: the command of the Lord himself, which must remain inviolate until the end of the age. "As often as you do this," says Paul, "you shall proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes." Therefore no one here can change anything without being held guilty of the crime of rebellion before the Lord. I would be more lengthy if I touched on the rest, which I will rather pass over. And it will be enough for now that you have tasted something of what you have here, so that a fuller treatment may lead you to a richer knowledge. Farewell in the Lord. May the Lord govern you by his Spirit, so that you may learn to answer to his will, and may he be pleased to care for your salvation and peace. Geneva.

units.la: DOlet mihi plurimùm dilectiss.in Domino, quòd non satis videcam, quid consolationis vobis nunc quidem adferre possim. Mihi enim iusta est tacendi causa, vbi plus quàm sciam,possimq́ue,à me expectatur aut quæritur.Agnoscitis nem pe ex meo quodam scripto,cùm Deum non colitis,nullam vobis pacem conscientiæ constare posse. At illud multò peius habet, quòd omnem ex illo vestro carcere effugiendi rationem præcisam vobis statuitis. Quid dicam? Miseret me vestræ fortis & constrictionis. Sed quorsum illud?nempe vt Dominum pro vobis supplex orem, vt in tantis infirmitatibus vos respiciat, quod nobis omnibus mutuò ac perpetuò precari debemus: ac non vt hîs meas preces interponédo, quod à vobis malum admittitur,eleuem. Neque etiam expectatis fortasse,vt vobis blandiar: sed cùm ita meam consolationem requiritis, vt mali aliquando tollendi occasionem omnem vobis negatam adiiciatis, illud me plane constringit, ne quid vlterius vobis respondere valeâ.Ego verò si vestræ illæ angustiæ veros ac feruentes gemitus ad Dominum in vobis excitarent, sperarem exitum à Domino vobis oblatum iri. Sed quemadmodum extra spem in illum sperandum est, ita etiam extra media ad ipsius vocationem sequendam enitendum est,ne illi desimus.Idque ita statuendum est,vt cùm omnia sese opponere videbuntur,& viæ omnes clau di atque obstrui, nihilominus perrumpamus omnia, & nullus nostris commodis vel rationibus in rei tantæ deliberatione detur locus .Si penes me esset vobis manum quouis modo porrigere, non committerem vt meum hîc officium à vobis merito desideraretur.Quum aliud non possim,nolite expectare,vt quod Dominus à vobis requirit,illud à me remitti possit. Vestrum est potius,vt consolationem accipiant corda vestra, vosmet inter vos ad illud ipsum exhortari, quod à vobis pro impossibili habetur. Veniat enim in mentem quantum sit illud malum, quo adhuc detinemini. Cùmque illud ita vt est, persenseritis, tum à Domino vires postulate ad luctam,etiamsi ad sanguinem vsque decertandum sit. Inducite porrò in animum, non esse præscriptam vobis vnius diei luctam, cùm ex Satanæ vinculis euolauerítis: neque aliter omnia peractum iri cogitate, quàm si vesmel maledictum illud quod vobis incumbit, iugum exueritis, ita etiam in sanctà & recta constantia reliqua deinde vita perstetis. Nimis enim frequentia sunt illarum exempla,quæ builarum instar momento à pietate exciderunt Atque ita sibi consulunt pessimè,qui in aëre ædificant. Iam vbi serió meditatæ eritis, quàm non minus arduum sit perseuerātiæ exemplum quàm plane necessarium in Domini vocatione, vt ad illud praestandum impares nimium sumus, illud vos excitet, vt ad Domini opem & praesidium vos conferatis. Sic enim illum abunde instructum competietis ad suos ad cumulum suae erga ipsos liberalitatis perducendos, vti iam ab ipso primitias illius semel perceperunt. Atque hic est meae ad vos exhortationis scopus. Dominus vobis adsit, ac vestras illas quae eum non latent infirmitates, ipse corrigat, augeatque in vobis dona sui Spiritus, animum & vires suppeditet ad illud quod ipsi probari edoctae iam estis, vosque adeo manu praesenti regat & protegat, vt luporum vobis inhiantium fauces inoffensae euitare possitis. Geneuae.
units.tr: I am deeply grieved, most beloved in the Lord, that I cannot see what consolation I can offer you at present. I have a fair reason for keeping silent when more is asked of me, and more than I know or am able to give. You acknowledge, I think, from something I once wrote, that while you do not worship God you cannot have any peace of conscience. But what troubles you far more is that you have decided there is no way at all of escaping from that prison of yours. What can I say? I pity your strength and your distress. But what is the point of this? Only that I should pray to the Lord on your behalf as a suppliant, that he would look upon you in such great weakness, as we all ought to pray for one another continually. I should not try to relieve the evil you have taken on by offering my own prayers in its place. Perhaps you do not expect me to flatter you either. Yet since you seek my consolation and at the same time rule out every opportunity of ever removing the evil, that plainly restrains me from answering you any further. Indeed, if those straits of yours stirred up true and fervent sighs to the Lord in you, I would hope that the way out offered by the Lord would come to you. But just as we must hope in him beyond hope, so we must also strive, beyond the means at hand, to follow his calling, so that we do not fail him. And this must be settled so that, even when everything seems to stand in our way and every road appears closed and blocked, we nevertheless break through everything, and no place is given to our own convenience or reasoning in deliberating on so great a matter. If it lay with me to stretch out a hand to you in any way, I would not allow my duty here to be rightly demanded of you. Since I cannot do otherwise, do not expect that what the Lord requires of you can be remitted by me. It is rather for you to let your hearts receive consolation and to exhort one another to that very thing which you regard as impossible. For let it come to mind how great the evil is by which you are still held. When you have truly felt it as it is, then ask the Lord for strength for the struggle, even if it must be fought to the point of blood. Furthermore, bring this to mind: the struggle of a single day is not the whole of what is set before you, once you have escaped the chains of Satan. Do not think that everything will be accomplished merely because you have once thrown off that accursed yoke that weighs upon you, unless you also persevere in holy and upright constancy for the rest of your life. For there are all too many examples of those who, like bubbles, fell away from godliness in a moment. Those who build in the air do themselves the worst service. Now, when you have seriously considered how no less arduous, and yet plainly necessary in the Lord's calling, is the example of perseverance, and how far we are too weak to achieve it, let this rouse you to betake yourselves to the help and protection of the Lord. For thus you will find him amply equipped to bring his own to the fullness of his kindness toward them, as they have already received from him the first fruits of it. And this is the aim of my exhortation to you. May the Lord be with you, may he himself correct those weaknesses of yours which are not hidden from him, may he increase in you the gifts of his Spirit, supply mind and strength for that which you have already been taught to be approved before him, and so guide and protect you with his present hand that you may escape unharmed the jaws of the wolves that gape for you. Geneva.
