units.la: QVum de statu vestro verba facerem apud Collegas meos, & inter alia referrem, iam de sacra Christi Coena exortum esse aliquid dissidij inter vos, rogarunt me, vt de communi omnium sententia hoc vobis scriberem. Quàm noxia sit pestis dissensio, pluribus verbis differere superuacuum foret: nam & optime nouistis non modo in fidei vnitate, sed etiam fraterno consensu sitam esse Ecclesiae salute: & dum ad vos oppugnandos vires studiaque sua coniungit hostium factio, quàm solicitè sancta conspiratio vobis fouenda sit, experientia ipsa docet. Et hoc artificio haud dubie molitur Satan Euangelij cursum vel abrumpere, vel remorari. Neque verò nos latet magis pretiosam esse synceram fidei doctrinam, quàm vt redimendae pacis gratia, minimum ab illa deflectere nobis fas sit: sed quantum probabili coiectura assequimur, non tam in controuersiam vocatur ipsa doctrina, quàm moderatio quaeritur, quae minimum pariat offendiculi. Pars, vt audimus, Augustanam confessionem complectitur. Alij Valdensium doctrinam mordicus retinent. Sunt qui desiderant puram & dilucidam mysterij explicationem. Et de Augustana quidem confessione non videtur iusta esse ratio, cur inter se litigent serui Christi, modò de genuino sensu conueniat. Valdenses etiam cupimus vobis semper coniunctissimos manere. Sed non videmus cur magis arrideat cuiquam Augustana confessio, quàm eius auctori. Atqui profiteri non dubitat clarissimus ille vir, tradendam esse posteris plenam & liquidam huius doctrinae lucem. Et sanè quò minus omnes ad tollendam ambiguitatem confentiâ, nihil aliud obstabit, quàm crucis metus. Quia de hoc capite doctrinae infoeliciter nostro seculo pugnatum fuit, nonnulli dum pro ingenij sui mansuetudine turbas fugitant, leuiter & obscure attingi vellent, quod perspicue in Ecclesia docendum est. Sed lôgè falluntur, dum hoc remedio componi sedariqué posse certamina existimant. Neque tamen haec erit ab Augustana confessione discessio, si clarior fidei vestrae expositio accedat, sicut vos diuortium cum Valdensibus facere minimè veilemus, quibuscum fraterna coniunctio ad extremum vsque colenda sit. Tantùm cupimus vltro citroque alios aliis accedere, vt communibus studiis quaeratur sacrum Vnitatis vinculum. Nec certè putamus adeo morosos esse bonos illos fratres, quin liberter recipiant, quae aliunde allata fuerit, explicationem: si modò in vsum Ecclesiae commoda aptáque esse videbitur. Legimus locum illum vbi suam de sacra Christi Coena sententiam exponunt.Breuiter,& fere concisè alserunt, panem & vinum esse verum Christi corpus & sanguinem. Statim ad confessionem transeunt, quæ nostro iudicio doctrinam obscurat vel inuoluit magis quàm illustret.Queruntur iniustis secalumniis grauari, imò traduci ludibriis & subsannationibus : sed primos libi aduersarios statuere videntur, quicunque certius finiri postulant, quomodo panis sit corpus.Tantum dico, quum non satis diserte vel enucleatè de hoc mysterio loquuti sint Valdenses, fastidium à Christiana modestia procul remotum fore, si ab ipsis omnis interpretatio repuitur.Formulam vero confessionis ampletli, quæ sine discrimine, in unum fasciculum damnationis omnes inuolvit, qui præcipiè non fatentur pane esse præsentissime Christi corpus(hic recitamus eorum verba)an fas sit Christiano homini, vt deritis:nos certè non putamus.Et si vero nostrum non est, quicquam vobis præscribere, quæ tamen veltra est moderatio & humanitas, si vobis ingenuè ostend mus quid cæsamus factu optimum, æqui boniqué vt sperameus, consuletis hanc nostram fiduciam.Quando pro veritate prudentia exitiale fore malum persipicitis, si in contentionem erumpat dissensio, non est is prolixius monendi, vt sibi quisquam temperet. Verum simul adhibenda est di uersa cautio, ne si gratificandi causa, ambiguum nescio quid & perplexum receperitis, hinc inde ex caecis vel obscuris simultatibus deinde emergat deterius certamen.Quid autem obstat quò minus in consensionem piam, sanctam ac dilucidam coalescatis simul omnes? Neque enim hoc modo violabitur confessio Augustana: & Valdenses, si recte sentiunt, cómodè nulla sua iactura diluent offensionem, quæ ex breuibus & obscuris eorum verbis alioqui concipi potest: quæ opportunitas merito illis est optanda. Primò itaq; vbi clare fuerit expolita mysterij vis & efficacia, luculenta etiam definitio tradita fuerit de vera carnis & sanguinis participatione, qua contilet Christū non ludere inanibus rigu-ris, nec quicquā fallaciter promittere, sed præstare re ipsa quod per externa symbola testatur, saltem addenda esset exceptio, quo caro Christi nobis datur in cibum, & sanguis in potum, arcana & incoprehensibili Spiritus sancti virtute hoc fieri, nec ideo fingendam esse immensitatem, quæ palàm naturæ humanæ repugnat.Nos certè libenter recipimus, panem & vinum non modò esse symbola vel arras, sed certa testimonia quibus coniuncta est vera rerum exhibitio: ita fatemur panem esse corpus Christi, & vinum sanguinem, quia hæc symbola nobis porrigendo Christus verè animas nostras carne sua sanguineq; pascit. Libenter etiam ferimus dum spiritualis vocatur hæc communicatio, interpretationem adiungi: hac voce no debere intelligi imaginarium nescio quid, ac si cogitatione tantùm essemus Christi participes, sed potius intelligi cœlestem virtutem, quæ crassa terrenæ præsentiæ figmenta exclu dit, nihil autem minuat de ipsa veritate. Sed vbi clarè expositum fuerit, per symbola panis & vini propo ni nobis & re vera offerri Christi carnem & sanguinem & spiritu ale alimentum, absurdis delitiis, quibus fascinata est maior pars mundi obuiam ire expedit atq; adeo necesse est. Itaq; ne sin gatur immensum esse Christi corpus, & esse vbique quasi naturâ exuisset, explicàdus est communicationis modus. Quod scilicet Christus secundum corpus suū in cœlo manens, admirabili Spiritus sui virtute ad nos descendit, & simul nos ad se sursum attol lit. Nam hoc nodo expedito, simul carnalis & superstitiosa ado ratio soluetur. Porrò nisi vnu ex præcipuis fidei nostræ articu lis sponte nobis perire volumus, retinenda est humanæ naturæ in Christo veritas. Nisi enim illud fixū maneat, resurrexisse Chri stum vt nos sibi conformet, vbi erit spes resurrectionis! Et ꝙ præ- posteri quidam homines terrena signa cum substantia vel re spi ritualí confundunt, non omittenda esset distinctio, sine qua ex singulis Sacramentis totidem idola sibi fabricat mundus. Qua- uis ergo panis non figuratiuum modo (vt loquuntur) sed exhi bitiuum quoque signum sit: sciendū tamen metonymicè vocari corpus secundū communem analogiam, quæ in Scripturis sa- cris passim occurrit inter signa & res signatas. Atque hæc mode- ratio indignè hac calumnia grauatur, ac si fidei iugum excutiat ex hominum cordibus, vel extraneum aliquod glossema assuat Christi verbis: quoniam nō alio documento probari certius po- test fidei obsequium: quando in toto cœlestis doctrinæ tenore harmonia quæritur, quæ omnem repugnātiæ speciem discutiat. Nec minus futilis est obiectio, dum falsis commentis occurritur (quale illud est de immeso Christi corpore) rationem humanā præferri Dei verbo: quia neq; ingenij nostri captu metimur my sterium hoc incomprehensibile, neque quæstionem mouemus de potentia Dei, neque vocamus in dubiū Christi promissiones, nec repudiamus, quod à sensu carnis nostræ abhorret: sed huius my sterij intelligentiam ex communi Scripturæ vsu petimus. Quia etiam altera quæstio hodie agitatur, an promiscuè increduli cum fidelibus percipiant Christi corpus & sanguinem, vtilis esset expositio, offerri comuniter omnibus: & quanuis oblata gratia nō omnes fruantur, nihil tamen de Sacramenti efficacia decedere, & Christum nihilominus manere veracem: sed quanuis ex parte ipsius panis sit omnibus corpus Christi, non omnes tamen tā præclari doni capaces sunt. Nec vero excidit, quod paulò ante præfati sumus, nostrum non esse formulam vobis dictare, quæ vos obstringat: sicut tamen visi est vtilis hæc admonitio, ita vobis gratam fore sperauimus. Si qua alia in re nostrā erga vos beneuolentiam licebit testari,officia nostra vobis semper para-ta fore promittimus. Valete clarissimi Domini & generosissimi viri fratresque plurimum obseruandi. Dominus vos regere pergat prudentiæ Spiritu,& inuicta virtute sustinere, donisque suis vos in dies locupletet, quò Regnum Filij eius apud vos magis ac magis propagetur.Geneuæ,1 x.Calendas Nouembris. M. D. LVII.
units.tr: When I was speaking about your situation before my colleagues, and among other things reported that some dissension had already arisen among you over the holy Supper of Christ, they asked me to write to you in the name of everyone's common opinion. How harmful a plague dissension is would take too many words to explain, for you yourselves know very well that the safety of the Church rests not only on unity of faith but also on brotherly agreement. And while the faction of enemies joins its strength and efforts to attack you, experience itself shows how carefully that holy harmony must be cherished. Undoubtedly Satan is working by this device either to break off or to delay the course of the Gospel. Nor are we unaware that sound doctrine of faith is more precious than that we should depart from it in the least, even to buy peace. But as far as we can conjecture with some probability, it is not so much the doctrine itself that is called into question; rather, a moderate way is sought that will give the least offence. Some of you, as we hear, embrace the Augsburg Confession; others hold stubbornly to the doctrine of the Waldenses; and there are those who desire a pure and clear explanation of the mystery. As for the Augsburg Confession, there seems to be no just reason why the servants of Christ should quarrel among themselves, provided they agree on its genuine sense. We also desire that you remain always most closely united with the Waldenses. But we do not see why the Augsburg Confession should please anyone more than its author, who does not hesitate to profess that a full and clear light of this doctrine is to be handed down to posterity. Indeed, the only thing that will stand in the way of all agreeing to remove the ambiguity is the fear of the cross. On this article of doctrine our age has unhappily fought, and some, fleeing disturbances out of the gentleness of their disposition, would have it touched lightly and obscurely, whereas what must be taught in the Church should be taught plainly. But they are greatly mistaken if they think that quarrels can be settled and calmed by this remedy. Yet this will not be a departure from the Augsburg Confession if a clearer exposition of your faith is added, just as we would not wish you to make a breach with the Waldenses, with whom fraternal union is to be cherished to the very end. We only desire that they and you move towards one another from either side, so that the sacred bond of unity may be sought by common effort. Nor do we think those good brothers so stubborn that they would not willingly receive an explanation brought from elsewhere, provided it seems useful and suitable for the good of the Church. We have read the passage where they set out their view of the holy Supper of Christ. Briefly, and almost tersely, they assert that bread and wine are the true body and blood of Christ. Straightaway they pass to a confession, which in our judgement obscures or wraps the doctrine more than it illuminates it. They complain that they are burdened with unjust calumnies, and even held up to ridicule and mockery; yet they seem to treat as their first enemies all who demand a more certain definition of how the bread is the body. I say only this: since the Waldenses have not spoken plainly or clearly enough about this mystery, a squeamishness far removed from Christian modesty would result if they rejected every interpretation. But as for the formula of confession which, without distinction, bundles all who especially do not confess that the bread is most truly the body of Christ into one heap of damnation (here we quote their words), whether it is right for a Christian man to do so, we certainly do not think it is. Although it is not our place to prescribe anything to you, your moderation and humanity are such that if we openly show you what we think is the best course, you will, as we hope, weigh this our trust with fairness and goodwill. Since you see clearly that, for the truth, it would be a pernicious evil if dissension broke out into strife, there is no need to advise at length that each should restrain himself. But at the same time caution must be applied, lest, to please, you admit some ambiguous and perplexing formula, and a worse conflict afterwards emerge from hidden or obscure enmities here and there. What then stands in the way of your all coming together into one pious, holy and clear agreement? In this way the Augsburg Confession will not be violated; and the Waldenses, if they think rightly, can easily wipe away, without any loss to themselves, the offence which might otherwise be taken from their brief and obscure words. This opportunity is rightly to be wished for them. First, therefore, when the force and efficacy of the mystery has been clearly set forth, and a lucid definition has been given of the true participation in flesh and blood, by which it is made plain that Christ does not play with empty signs or promise anything deceptively, but actually performs what he attests by the outward symbols, it would at least be necessary to add a qualification: that the flesh of Christ is given to us for food and his blood for drink, and this takes place by the hidden and incomprehensible power of the Holy Spirit; and that for this reason we should not invent an immensity which plainly contradicts human nature. We certainly gladly accept that bread and wine are not only symbols or pledges but sure testimonies by which the true presentation of the things is joined to them. Thus we confess that bread is the body of Christ and wine his blood, because in offering these symbols to us Christ truly feeds our souls with his flesh and blood. We also gladly tolerate, when this communication is called spiritual, that an interpretation be added: by this word one should not understand some imaginary thing, as if we were partakers of Christ only in thought, but rather a heavenly power which excludes the gross fictions of an earthly presence, yet takes nothing away from the truth itself. But once it has been clearly explained that through the symbols of bread and wine Christ's flesh and blood are set before us and in truth offered to us, as spiritual food, then it is expedient, and indeed necessary, to meet the absurd delusions by which the greater part of the world is bewitched. Therefore, lest it be imagined that the body of Christ is immense and everywhere, as if it had put off its nature, the mode of communication must be explained: namely, that Christ, remaining in heaven according to his body, descends to us by the wonderful power of his Spirit and at the same time lifts us up to himself. For once this knot is untied, carnal and superstitious thinking will be dissolved at the same stroke. Moreover, unless we wish of our own accord to lose one of the chief articles of our faith, the truth of human nature in Christ must be retained. For if this stays fixed, that Christ rose again in order to conform us to himself, where will be the hope of our resurrection? And since certain perverse men confuse earthly signs with the substance or spiritual reality, a distinction must not be omitted, without which the world fashions for itself as many idols as there are sacraments. Therefore, although the bread is not only a figurative sign (as they say) but also an exhibitive one, it must be understood that it is called the body by metonymy, according to the common analogy which occurs throughout the holy Scriptures between signs and the things signified. And this moderation is unworthily burdened with the calumny that it shakes the yoke of faith from men's hearts or attaches some foreign gloss to the words of Christ. Yet by no other proof can the obedience of faith be more surely shown than when, across the whole tenor of heavenly doctrine, a harmony is sought which dispels every appearance of contradiction. Nor is the objection less trifling which, when false inventions are opposed (such as that about the immense body of Christ), argues that human reason is preferred to the Word of God. For we neither measure this incomprehensible mystery by the capacity of our intellect, nor raise a question about the power of God, nor call Christ's promises into doubt, nor reject what shrinks from the sense of our flesh; but we seek the understanding of this mystery from the common use of Scripture. Since another question is also being debated today, namely whether unbelievers receive the body and blood of Christ indiscriminately along with the faithful, an exposition would be useful: that it is offered in common to all, and that although not all enjoy the grace offered, nothing is lost from the efficacy of the sacrament, and Christ nonetheless remains true; for although from the side of the bread itself it is the body of Christ for all, yet not all are capable of so excellent a gift. Nor has it escaped us that we said a little earlier that it is not our place to dictate to you a formula to bind you; yet just as this admonition seemed useful to us, so we have hoped it will be welcome to you. If in any other matter we are allowed to bear witness to our goodwill towards you, we promise that our services will always be ready for you. Farewell, most distinguished lords, most noble men and brothers most deserving of respect. May the Lord continue to rule you with the Spirit of prudence, to sustain you with unconquered courage, and to enrich you day by day with his gifts, so that the Kingdom of his Son may be spread more and more among you. Geneva, 23 October 1557.

units.la: VINCTO TAVRINI PROPTER EVANGELIVM.
units.tr: Imprisoned at Turin for the Gospel

units.la: ETsi tristis nobis fuit vinculorum tuorum nuntius, optime frater, grauius tamen nos vulnerasset, nisi Deus qui solet ex tenebris lucem elicere, mœrorem temperasset aliquo gaudio. Est enim cur nobis gratulemur, quòd tam fructuosa in ipso carcere iam opera tua esse cœpit, vt magis quàm si liber fuisses ac solutus, Christi Euangelium illustraueris. Itaque merito animum tibi addere debet illa Pauli gloriatio, quanuis te captiuum teneant hostes, sermonem Dei non esse alligatum: nec modo apertam esse ianuam auditoribus, qui semen illud viuificum ex ore tuo exceptum longius spargant, sed f uctum coram oculis tuis emergere. Quod si te in angustias restringi contingit, erit tamen hoc laboris tui pretium non vulgaris solatij loco. Nam si fidei confessio coram gente tortuosa & peruersa gratum Deo sacrificium est, quanto suauius spirabit odor in multorum salute diffusus? Cæterum, vides fraterad quam militiam vocatus sis, idque tibi sedulò reputandum est. Quum enim à priuatis quibuslibet suo Euangelio testimonium exigat Christus,sanctiori iure te obstrictum tenet, quem publicum creauit eius doctrinæ præconem, quæ nunc in tua persona oppugnatur. Ergo ab eodem qui te hoc honore dignatus est, testem te produxit esse memineris, vt quod ore antea docuisti, proprio sanguine, si opus fuerit, obsignes. Interea fidum vitæ tuæ custodem fore ne dubita: & quando mortem sanctorum pretiosam sibi fore pollicitus est, qualiscunque erit euentus, tibi sufficiat hæc compensatio, nunc Filium Dei per te agere triumphũ, vt te in æternæ gloriæ societatem colligat. Pluribus tecum non agam, quia te in eius fide & patrocinio recumbere mihi persuadeo, cui dum morimur, & viuimus, morie do sumus beatiores, quàm terreni profanique homines viuendo. Vale optime & charissime frater. Salutant te Collegæ mei Dominus tibi semper adsit, prudentia Spiritus suite gubernet, inuicta fortitudine sustineat, præsidióq; tueatur, x v i i. Decemb. M. D. LVII.
units.tr: Although the news of your imprisonment saddened us, best of brothers, it would have wounded us more deeply had not God, who is accustomed to draw light out of darkness, tempered our grief with some joy. For we have cause to rejoice that your work has already begun to bear such fruit in prison, so that you have shed more light on the gospel of Christ than you would have done if you had been free and at liberty. Therefore that boast of Paul's should rightly encourage you: though your enemies hold you captive, the word of God is not bound. Not only is a door opened to the hearers who will carry that living seed, received from your mouth, farther afield, but fruit is springing up before your very eyes. And if it happens that you are confined to narrow limits, this will nonetheless be the reward of your labour, and it is no common consolation. For if the confession of faith before a crooked and perverse nation is an acceptable sacrifice to God, how much sweeter will the fragrance be when it is spread abroad for the salvation of many? Furthermore, brother, you see to what warfare you have been called, and you must weigh this carefully. For since Christ demands testimony to his gospel even from private persons, he holds you bound by a more sacred right, you whom he has made a public herald of that doctrine which is now being assailed in your person. So remember that he who has honoured you with this office has put you forward as a witness, so that you may seal with your own blood, if need be, what you have previously taught with your mouth. Meanwhile, do not doubt that he will be a faithful guardian of your life; and since he has promised that the death of his saints is precious in his sight, whatever the outcome, let this recompense suffice you: that the Son of God is now winning his triumph through you, and will gather you into the fellowship of eternal glory. I will not say more to you, because I am persuaded that you rest upon his faithfulness and protection, and that, whether we die or live, we are happier than worldly and profane men are in their living. Farewell, best and dearest brother. My colleagues salute you. May the Lord always be with you, may he guide you with the prudence of his Spirit, sustain you with invincible strength, and keep you under his protection. 17 December 1557.

units.la: Ioannes tuus quem nosti. CAL.
units.tr: Your John, whom you know. CAL.

units.la: QVum tam familiari vitæ vsu atque etiam contubernio mihi olim fuer sdeuinctus, nunquam fore putassem, mi Petre,vt mihi difficilis ac perplexa esset ad te scribendi ratio. Sed quia mundi illecebris implicitus præter spem meam,& magno meo dolore te à nobis subduxeras,ac si via mihi periculosa foret,à scribendi consuetudine abstinui. Citius forte quàm oportuit:sed quia verebar,si literas non postulanti obtruderem,ne tibi ludibrio sedulitas mea esset, nolui saltem properare, donec signum aliquod melius dares. Amorem interea, quo te ac fratrem tuum semel complexus fueram, quanuis externis officiis non testarer, animo fouebam,sicuti nondum excidit,vel excussus est. Iam vero fratrum tu rum aduentu,quo noua occasio videri oblata poterat,ideo restrictior factus sum,quòd vos suo exemplo comites non traxissent,quum duces fore sperassem. Certè tam insperata mutatione non modò perculsus sum, sed fere obstupui:quum tibi manum porrigerent,& migrationis adiutores forent ac socij,qui tibi prius erant obstaculo,& à quibus solis te retineri sæpe conquestus es,nido tamen affixum suauiter quiescere. Verùm vt querimoniis vtrinque valere iussis, placidè tecum agam,quid sibi,mi Petre,vult hæc mollities, ac ignauia,vel quo prætextu excusabitur? Non est hic mihi texenda disputatio de fugiendis superstitionibus, quarum odio & detestatione relinquenda potius erat vita,quàm vt te amore patriæ in illis sic poluere s. Te satis ac super,me tacente,conuictum tenet conscientia, vix vllum effluere diem, quo non abs te Deus legitimo suo cultu,honoréque fraudetur. Imò simulatio ista,qua impiorum gratiam fouest,quid aliud est quàm obliqua defectio à confessione, quæ præcipui sacrificij loco ab omnibus Dei filiis exigitur? Atqui centies mori præstarer,quàm ita vindictam Dei quotidie prouocare. Quòd verò plusquam seruiliter timidus,quantùm in te est,lumen in corde tuo pridem diuinitus accensum suffocas, vide ne quicquid reliduum est vsque ad minimis quasque scintillas extinguat idem Deus, si torpori tuo ad finem vsque indulges. Potius aliquando expergiscere ne præterea tempus illud acceptabile, quo Deum quæri iubet Propheta dum inueniri potest. Me quidem non modò tuæ tarditatis pudet ad piget,sed terret illa seuera Christi denuntiatio,vbi clausa fuerit ianua, frustra pulsaturos,qui occasionem neglexerint. Aperiorfum quàm vellem: sed vt tibi Deus parcat, parcere ipse non audeo. Saltem quod à syncera fraterni amoris solicitudine profectum esse agnoscas, non adeo morosus eris, vt repudies. Vale eximie vir. Dominus te Spiritu prudentiæ & rectitudinis gubernet,instruat sancta constantia, virtute sua tueatur, iiii. Calendas Januarij. M. D. LVII.
units.tr: Since I was once bound to you by such familiar intercourse, and indeed by living under the same roof, I would never have supposed, my dear Peter, that it would become so difficult for me to find a way of writing to you. But because you had withdrawn from us, entangled in the allurements of the world, beyond my hope and to my great sorrow, I refrained from writing, as if the way were dangerous for me. I did so perhaps sooner than I ought; but since I feared that if I forced letters on you when you did not ask for them, my eagerness would become a laughingstock to you, I at least did not wish to hurry until you gave some better sign. Meanwhile I cherished in my heart the affection with which I had once embraced you and your brother, even though I did not bear witness to it by outward acts, and it has not faded, nor has it been shaken off. Now, indeed, with the arrival of your brothers, which might have seemed a new opportunity, I became more reserved, because they had not drawn you along with them by their example, though I had hoped they would be your leaders. Truly, I was not only shaken but almost stunned by such an unexpected change, when they were offering you their hand and were to be your helpers and companions in your departure, they who had formerly been an obstacle to you, and by whom alone you had often complained that you were held back, yet, fixed to your nest, you rested sweetly. But, to set aside complaints on both sides, let me deal with you gently: what, my dear Peter, does this softness and cowardice mean, and under what pretext will it be excused? It is not for me here to weave a discussion about the superstitions that must be fled, which ought rather to be left behind with hatred and detestation than that you should be so steeped in them out of love for your homeland. Your own conscience, even without my words, convicts you more than enough: hardly a day passes on which God is not robbed by you of his lawful worship and honour. Indeed, that pretence by which you cherish the favour of the wicked, what else is it than a sidelong defection from the confession which all the children of God are required to make as the chief sacrifice? Yet I would rather die a hundred times than thus provoke the vengeance of God every day. But when, more than slavishly timid, you stifle, as far as you can, the light divinely kindled in your heart long ago, take heed lest the same God extinguish whatever remains, even to the least sparks, if you indulge your sluggishness to the end. Rather, wake up at last, lest that acceptable time pass by, when the Prophet bids us seek God while he may be found. As for me, I am not only ashamed of your slowness and grieved by it, but I am terrified by that severe warning of Christ, that when the door is shut, those who have neglected the opportunity will knock in vain. I have spoken more openly than I wished; but, so that God may spare you, I do not dare to spare you myself. At least, since you recognise that this comes from the sincere concern of brotherly love, you will not be so peevish as to reject it. Farewell, excellent man. May the Lord guide you with the Spirit of prudence and uprightness, instruct you with holy steadfastness, and protect you by his power. 29 December 1557.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN SENDS GREETING IN THE NAME OF OUR LORD

units.la: ME vero angustiae tuae anxium habent. Sed quicquid difficultatum opponat Satan, eniti nos tamen contra infracto animo decet. Nec vero desinendum est, donec emerserimus. Quando nos ad se Dominus invitat, eundem est. Si per solitudinem et vasta loca iter est nobis, ne propterea fatigemur. Nam cum ideo nobis manum porrexerit, ut in coelum visq; attollat: dabit procul dubio, ut omnia mundi huius obstacula superemus. Tantum ne corpore animi nostri flaccescat. Si ea quae tibi adiutrix esse debuerat, aduersari se praebet: nihilo illi magis quam carni, indulgedu. Et sane multa sunt quae te in contrariam partem solicitent, ne prauis eius suasionibus acquiescas. Miserum est inter continuos motus stuare: quod tibi visu venire no dubito. Atq; ut periculi nihil insteteo tamen progressus es, vnde pede referre erit turpissimum. Deinde cogitare debes, non te unum esse ex vulgo, ut privatim tibi pecces. Tot enim in te coniecti sunt oculi, ut grauissime exemplo noceas. Et quam interea pacem cum tua conscientia habere potes? Non est necessarium rare, quae te istic retineat. Sed non tanti esse omnia agnoscis, ut ea indigna mercede rediman-tur. Bellum enim te cum Deo suscipere non ignoras, ut pace habeas cum hominibus. Hoc vero omnium pessimum, qp in hoc labyrintho adeo nullus errandi finis appareat, ut te indices magis inuoluas. Nam de exitu nulla iam fieri mentio dicitur. Vide obsecro, ne vxori, & sub eius praetextu, tibi delicias faciens, iram in te summi iudicis provoces. Nihil dico, nisi quod mihi audire & expediret, & optabile foret, si tuo loco esset. In illa enim procellosa caligine, saepius homine ante opprimere mors solet, quam sentiatur. Itaq; melius ex sereno loco tua pericula cernere mihi videor. Neque vero migrationem vrgeo, quasi nusquam, nisi apud nos, fuluus esse nequeas. Tantum vereor, ne accensus in te pij zeli ignis vel sopiatur, vel euanescat. Haec solicitudo non ex constantia tua diffidenti, sed ex singulari erga te amore nascitur. Vale ornatissime vir & honorande in Domino frater. Dominus Iesus te Spiritu consilij & fortitudinis instruat. Amen.
units.tr: Your distress indeed troubles me. Whatever difficulties Satan may throw in our way, we ought nonetheless to press on with an unbroken spirit. Nor must we stop until we have come through. When the Lord invites us to himself, the same applies. If the road takes us through solitude and waste places, we should not on that account grow weary. For since he has stretched out his hand to us in order to lift us up to heaven, he will without doubt enable us to overcome all the obstacles of this world. Only let the vigour of your spirit not wither away. If the flesh, which ought to have been your helper, shows itself hostile, you should yield no more to it than to the flesh itself. And indeed there are many things that tempt you toward the opposite course; do not give in to their wicked persuasions. It is wretched to be tossed about by constant agitation, and I do not doubt that you feel this. And although you have advanced without any danger, it would be most shameful now to turn back. Further, you ought to consider that you are not one of the common crowd, so that you might sin in private. So many eyes are fixed upon you that you will do the gravest harm by your example. And meanwhile what peace can you have with your conscience? There is no need for me to say what it is that holds you there. But you recognise that not everything is worth so much that it should be bought back at the price of such unworthy wages. For you know that you are waging war against God, so that you may have peace with men. Yet the worst thing of all is this: in this labyrinth no end of wandering appears, so that you entangle yourself the more. For no mention of an exit is now made, I am told. I beg you to see to it that you do not provoke the wrath of the supreme Judge, by indulging yourself in pleasures for the sake of your wife and under the pretext of her. I say nothing except what I would have liked, and what would have been welcome for me to hear, had I been in your place. For in that stormy darkness death often overwhelms a man before he is aware of it. Therefore I seem to myself to see your dangers better from a calm place. I do not urge you to migrate, as if you could not be safe anywhere except among us. I only fear that the fire of holy zeal kindled in you may either be smothered or fade away. This anxiety arises not from distrust of your constancy but from a particular love for you. Farewell, most distinguished man and brother to be honoured in the Lord. May the Lord Jesus strengthen you with the Spirit of counsel and courage. Amen.

units.la: CAL. N. OFFICIALI S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO OUR OFFICIAL, SENDS GREETING

units.la: NE mireris, eximie vir, quod hominem mihi tantum ex fama motum, literis meis perinde familiariter aggredior, ac si maior inter nos consuetudo mihi aditum patefaceret. De
units.tr: Do not be surprised, distinguished sir, that I address you in my letter so familiarly, a man moved toward me only by reputation, as if some greater acquaintance between us had opened the way for me. Concerning

units.la: officio meo breuiter hoc præfari cogor, quia non semper vltro accedunt, qui tamen sunt ex Christi grege, plerósque esse procul quærendos, atque vt subterfugiant, inuitá dos esse. Ego verò adeò in excusanda fiducia anxiè non laboro, vt mihi persuadeam of ficium meum tibi & gratum fore, & vtile. Certè minimè vereor, ne tibi quem reuerenter cœlestis magistri doctrinam excipere audio, ludibrio sit mea sedulitas: dum te non malè quidem animatum, sed in profundiore luto hærentem incitare studeo, vt paulò alacrius ad metam contendas. Asperius forte quod dictus sum, tibi videbitur: sed tamen & dictu vtile, & verissimum esse agnoscens, si in te paulisper descenderis, non maius est ignis & aquæ dissidium, quàm locus ille quem tenes, à legitima vocatione procul alienus est. Quahquam non tam longa vel accurata disputatione te vincendum, quàm acribus stimulis pungendum esse arbitror, vt tibi fætió diffilicet sub illa barbara Papatus tyrannide, qua premuntur communiter alij omnes. Quàm difficile sit purum atque integrum Deo obsequium præstare, quisque pro se experitur. Tua verò peculiaris est ratio, qui iniustæ illius & sacrilegæ dominationis satellles esse cogeris ac minister. Disciplinæ quidem præesse honorificum est: sed videt quàm strenuè in purgandis flagitiis labores, quæ pueris quoque ipsis notæ sunt. Tuum est vt de ebrietate aliisque vitiis taceam, scortandi licentiam in clero cohibere: nec tecum reputa, quàm in hac crassa quæ omnibus nota est, obscœnitate, tolerabilis sit tua dissimulatio. Atque vt seuerissimus sis hac in parte censor, nempe hoc erit operæ tuæ pretium, vt idolis maneat integer cultus, vt sua sacrilegia exerceant veneri sacerdotes. Præcipuam enim iurisdictionis tuæ partem in hoc sitam esse non negabis, vt salua sit & intacta Papatus religio, quam sensinnumeris corruptelis scatere. Vna est culpæ tuæ leuatio, quòd filiis Dei parcis, ne tyrannicè ad superstitiones per te cogantur. Sed quantumuis tibi humaniter temperes, inuitas tamen ad peccandum, quos violenter non trahis. Excipies, tibi id non esse in animo. Sed quid tergiuersando proficies, quum res ipsa palàm clamitet, quoties tribunal conscendis, signum erigiruendis pollutionibus, quæ totum Dei cultum perverterunt? Atque vt optimè te geras, simulas tamen nihil te vel le Satanæ derogare. Fallor enim si vltrà progrederis, quàm vt falso prætextu elabi sinas ex laqueis, quos tamen tendunt aucupes tui, ad omnes animas æterno exitio implicandas. Atqui tuum potius erat palàm abigere, quod adeò non præstas, vt silentio tuo prodantur, ne quid grauius dicam. Vt dicam vno verbo, etiamsi re ipsa Christo tuum obsequium offerre conearis, titulus ipse Antichristi vexilli ferunt esse docet. Ad tam exitiale fœdúmque exemplum res ipsa accedit: quia si furtim nescio quid boni admisces, nunquam tamen e tribunali surgis, quin multa officii praestitetis in pia dominatione, cui mancipatus es. Reliqua iurisdictio in caulis ciuilibus consumitur: vbi vtcunque summam aequitatem colere studeas, fines tamen a Domino praefixos euertis, dum sub salaci regiminis Ecclesiastici praetextu, alienam prouinciam vsur-pas. Sed ne ego tibi molestus sim, tecum potius loquere, & sine blanditiis reputa, sitne sancta Dei vocatio, haec adulterina praeclarae functionis larua, quae & Dei nomen profanat, & multis labyrinthis est implicita. Quod si viuendi ratio Deo non probatur, quibuscunque virtutibus excellas, nihil tamen miserius quam extra metas semper vagari. Aliam petendae veniae excusationem non affero, nisi quod libere scribendum fuit vel tacendum. Vale ornatissime vir & mihi honorande. Dominus te Spiritu prudentiae, aequitatis & fortitudinis guberner.
units.tr: my office I am obliged to say this briefly by way of preface: those who nevertheless belong to Christ's flock do not always come forward of their own accord, and most of them must be sought out from afar and urged, though they try to escape. I, however, do not anxiously labour to excuse my boldness so much as persuade myself that my service will be pleasing and useful to you. I am certainly not afraid that my diligence will be a mockery to you, since I hear that you receive with reverence the teaching of the heavenly Master. I am eager to rouse you, who are not badly disposed but stuck in deeper mud, so that you may press a little more briskly toward the goal. Perhaps what I am about to say will seem rather harsh to you, but I think it is both useful to say and most true; if you will descend into yourself for a while, you will see that the disagreement between fire and water is no greater than the distance between the place you hold and a lawful calling. Although I think you must be conquered not by a long or careful argument, but pricked with sharp goads, I will say that you are in a special position, since you are forced to be a servant and minister of that unjust and sacrilegious domination. It is indeed an honour to preside over discipline; but see how vigorously you labour in cleansing the crimes that are known even to children. It is yours, to say nothing of drunkenness and other vices, to restrain the licence of whoring among the clergy; and do not reckon with yourself how tolerable your connivance is in this gross obscenity known to everyone. And even if you are the most severe censor in this respect, this will be the reward of your labour: that the worship of idols remains intact, and that the priests may practise their sacrileges for Venus. For you will not deny that the principal part of your jurisdiction lies in this, that the religion of the Papacy, which you know teems with countless corruptions, remains safe and untouched. There is one excuse for your fault: that you spare the sons of God, so that they are not forced by you tyrannically into superstitions. But however humanely you temper your conduct, you invite to sin those whom you do not drag into it by violence. You will reply that this is not your intention. But what will you gain by evasion, when the very thing itself openly cries out, every time you mount the tribunal, that you raise a sign for the defilements which have perverted the whole worship of God? And although you conduct yourself well, you pretend nevertheless that you wish nothing to detract from Satan. For I am mistaken if you go further than to let yourself slip out of the snares, under a false pretext, which your fowlers set to entangle all souls in eternal destruction. Yet it was rather your task to drive out openly what you so far from doing, that by your silence these things are betrayed, not to say something more severe. To put it in one word: even if you try in fact to offer your obedience to Christ, the very title of the banner of Antichrist shows that they are carried by it. To this deadly and foul example is added the fact itself: for if you secretly mix in something good, you never rise from the tribunal without having performed many services of duty to the pious domination to which you are bound. The rest of your jurisdiction is spent in civil matters; there, however much you strive to cultivate the highest equity, you overturn the limits set by the Lord, while under the pretext of an ecclesiastical government you usurp a province not your own. But that I may not be a nuisance to you, rather speak with yourself, and without flattery consider whether this adulterous mask of an illustrious office, which both profanes the name of God and is entangled in many labyrinths, is a holy calling of God. And if the manner of your life is not approved by God, however much you excel in whatever virtues, nothing is more wretched than to wander always outside the bounds. I offer no other excuse for asking your pardon, except that I had to write freely or else remain silent. Farewell, most distinguished man and one to be honoured by me. May the Lord guide you with the Spirit of prudence, justice and courage.

units.la: CALVINVS AGANTHIO.
units.tr: Calvin to Aganthius.

units.la: Si in castiganda tua fragilitate paulo sim acrior quam vellem, non est quod de asperitate mea queraris: quin potius te ipsum accusa, qui me coegisti. Scis quid pridem fueris pollicitus, quum vrgerem, ne diutius in illis facibus maneres. Quia per suasus eram, te hominem esse bonae fidei, non modo credidi fasturum, sed quodammodo sponsorem me interposui. Ab eo tempore sustinui multas obliquas exprobrationes, quarum taedio durioresque aliquando nuntios tibi misi. Nunc quoque me undique appellant: nec habeo quid respondeam, nisi ad fidem soluendam mox accurras. Et quando tandem, frater mihi ex animo dilecte, tergiuersandi modum facies? Hactenus certe & Christum iusto obsequio & eius Ecclesiam opera tua indigne fraudasti. Negabis te interea fuisse otiosum. Agnosco tuum laborem alicubi profuisse. Verum quid si haec tua sedulitas, qualiscunque sit, neque bonis probatur, & communem seruorum Christi cursum impedit, ac moratur? Certe quicquid excipias, solus tibi metus hac in parte consiliarius est, quem merito suspectum habere debes. Proinde fieri non poterit, quin omnibus cordatis & syncerris, qui ingenue Christo nomen dederunt, displiceat haec tua astutia. Quanquam in deterius rapiunt multi clandestinos tuos circuitus, dum suspicantur diuersum aliquid spargere, quod puram fidei vnitatem scindat. Reclamo quidem, neque vnquam assentiar, tibi quicquam nobiscum esse dissidij, nisi palam oflenderis: quod nunquam fore confido. Sed tuum est videre, ne infirmos, quibus te Deus obstrinxit, nimia securitate contubes. Iam bienium fere praeteriit, quum te hortatus sum, vt te ad eos coetus aggrega-res,
units.tr: If I am somewhat sharper in rebuking your weakness than I would like, you have no reason to complain of my harshness. Rather, blame yourself, since you forced me to it. You know what you promised me not long ago when I urged you not to stay any longer among those torches. Because I was persuaded that you were a man of good faith, I not only believed you would do it but in a manner stood surety for you. From that time on I have endured many oblique reproaches, and weary of them I have sometimes sent you harsher messages. Even now people call on me from every side, and I have no answer to give them unless you hurry to keep your promise soon. And when at last, brother whom I love from my heart, will you make an end of your evasions? Up to now you have certainly cheated both Christ of his due obedience and his Church of your labour, and unworthily so. Meanwhile you will deny that you have been idle. I admit that your labour has been of some use somewhere. But what if this diligence of yours, whatever it is, is not approved by good men and hinders and delays the common course of Christ's servants? Whatever you may plead, fear alone is the counsellor you have in this matter, and you rightly ought to distrust it. Therefore it cannot but be that all sensible and sincere men who have openly given their name to Christ will dislike this craftiness of yours. Yet many people interpret your secret wanderings for the worse, suspecting that you are spreading something different that would split the pure unity of the faith. I protest, and I will never agree, that there is any disagreement between you and us, unless you show it openly; and I trust that this will never happen. But it is for you to see that you do not, by excessive carelessness, sin against the weak, whom God has bound to you. Nearly two years have now passed since I urged you to join those assemblies

units.la: Ires, res,in quibus scis Deum pure inuocari. Non solum tempus extraxisti: sed ex tuo silentio coniicere licuit, meam illam admonitionem abstete fuisse spretam. Nunc vero non rogabo tantum, vel hortabor: sed obsecrabo, atque etiam si opus est, adiurabo, ne moris neglendis diutius suspensa teneas bonorum desideria. Si nihil impetro, mature iam tecum reputa, quale te iudicium apud coelestem tribunal maneat, coram quo brevi nos sisti oportet. Nam etsi tibi adhuc aetas est vegeta: quia tamen maturitas ad senium vergit, festinandum est, ne te ex inopinato nox occupet.
units.tr: (in which you know God is purely invoked). Not only have you prolonged the time, but from your silence it has been possible to conjecture that my admonition has been scorned. Now, however, I will not merely ask or urge you but beg you, and even, if need be, adjure you, not to keep the good desires of believers suspended any longer by delaying your duty. If I obtain nothing, consider in good time with yourself what judgement awaits you before the heavenly tribunal, before which we must shortly stand. For although your age is still vigorous, yet since maturity is tending towards old age, there is need for haste, lest night overtake you unexpectedly.

units.la: CALVINVS MACARIO S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO MACARIUS, GREETING

units.la: FRater mi, dulcissime frater, si metu omni et sollicitudine vacuus te nunc et collegas ad obeunda, quae impendent certamina impellerem, merito frigeret apud vos, imo putidus esset fortis illa garrulitas. Nunc vero dum vestro periculo anxius ipse ac trepidus ad fiduciam et constantiam vos exhortor, epistola haec quae viva erit cordis mei imago, omnesque intimos eius affectus repraesentabit, vos non secus afficiet, ut spero, quam si coram omnium curarum socius adessem. Et certe si ad extremA veniendum sit, cuperem vobiscum in morte potius coniungi, quam superstes tantam Ecclesiae calamitatem lugere. Caeterum quicquid accidat, satis ex coelestis magistri praescripto, me tacen te, scitis centies potius moriendum, quam stationem, cui estis addicti, timide deseratis. Seditionis ignominiam, qua non modo vos sugillare, sed sacrum Christi Euangelium aspergere conantur improbi, ego etiam exhorreo. Verum ubi vobis probe cognita est, iniqueque vos hac falsa invidia gravari, hoc innocentiae vestrae testimonio fretos calumniam hanc aequo et sedato animo ferre convenit, quam ne ipse quidem Filius Dei potuit effugere. Bene est quod vobis quiescentibus hostium maledicentiam refellet, quae ex tenebris mox emergit veritas. Nam simul ac triduo volitaverit rumor, sponte concidet, ac auctores ipsi pudore obmutescent. Certe ut omnium mendaciorum pater et artifex diabolus tota mole ad vos odio et infamia obruendos incumbat, non tamen eo visque proficiet, quin hoc praeclaro et memorabili conflictu nomen suum illustret Deus, et ex caligine eliciat plenum gloriae suae fulgorem. Nulla unquam ad regis aures peruenerat libera et ingenua confessio. Si vltima primis respondeant (quod perandum est) centies, crede mihi, pallescet rubicundus leo. Si n grege multa erit repidatio, ne vos coturbet, sed placide non minus quam strenue occurrite dissipationi. Forte aliquid relaxationis breui praeter spem dabitur. Quod si durius vestram patientiam exerceri cōtigerit,quoniam ita cœlesti Patri decretum est, fixum tamen maneat,fidelem esse, qui vltra modum suostenta- ri non sinet.
units.tr: My brother, my dearest brother, if I were free of all fear and anxiety and were urging you and your colleagues to face the struggles that lie ahead, my bold talk would rightly grow cold among you, or rather would seem foolish. But now, anxious and trembling myself for your danger, I exhort you to confidence and steadfastness. This letter, which will be a living image of my heart and will set forth all its inmost feelings, will move you, I hope, no less than if I were present as a sharer in all your cares. And indeed, if it came to the last extremity, I would wish to be joined with you in death rather than survive and mourn so great a calamity for the Church. Whatever happens, you know well, from the precept of our heavenly Master, that it is better to die a hundred times than timidly to desert the post to which you have been assigned. I too shudder at the disgrace of sedition, with which wicked men try not only to defame you but also to smear the holy Gospel of Christ. But since the truth about you is well known, and since you are unjustly burdened by this false charge, it is fitting that you, relying on the testimony of your innocence, bear this calumny with a calm and even mind, a calumny which not even the Son of God himself could escape. It is good that, while you keep quiet, the truth will refute the slander of your enemies, for it will soon emerge from the darkness. As soon as the rumour has flown about for three days, it will fall of its own accord, and its authors themselves will fall silent in shame. Certainly, although the devil, the father and inventor of all lies, may hurl his whole weight against you to overwhelm you with hatred and infamy, he will not advance so far that God does not, through this distinguished and memorable conflict, make his own name illustrious and draw out from the darkness a radiance full of his glory. Never before has a free and frank confession reached the king's ears. If the last things answer the first (as must be hoped), a hundred times over, believe me, the ruddy lion will turn pale. If there is much rebuke from the flock, do not be disturbed by it, but meet the scattering calmly no less than bravely. Perhaps some relief will be granted shortly, beyond our hope. But if it should happen that your patience is tested more harshly, since this has been decreed by our heavenly Father, let this remain fixed: that he is faithful, and he will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you can bear.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N.N. S. D.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO N.N., GREETING.

units.la: Accepi,fratres dilectissimi, nouas & pergraues molestias vobis exhiberi ab hostibus veritatis, vt totus in eo est Satan, dum Filij Dei Regnū promoueri,ac piorum numerū auge ri animaduertit,vt nullū non lapidem ad ipsos deiiciendos mo- ueat.Quōd autem Dominus interdū laxar habenas impiis,vt nō bis noceāt,mirum videri non debet.Æquissimum est nempe ita prob ri fidem nostram nōsque vere testari quo in pretio nobis illa sit,dum afflictionibus in nos propter salutis doctrinā sæuien tibus,immoti tamen omnibus peractis stamus.Quōd autem in- nata infirmitas nos hic quoque cōstringit,tanto maturius ad il- lius præsidiū accurramus,quem posse & velle nostra causa dubi tare non possumus. Vt autem impetus illi aduersariorū,dum in nos impingunt,non mediocrem ad ipsos sustinendos fortitudi- nem & robur requirūt,ita etiam illorum artes, & doli singulari quadam cautione nobis sunt euitandi. Durum est multis,quōd in vita & facultatum discrimen vocentur pietatis nomine: sed illud longè deterius,vbi obliquis rationibus, & cuniculis à spe in Deum, & timore abducendi lacantur. Et hoc illud est rete, quod à bicorni illo Episcopo nunc vobis iniectum est,dum tri- mestre spatium ad remittendū Euangelio nuntium indulget.Sic infirmæ animæ in exitiū perrahuntur. Attedite vobis igitur,at- que ab istiusmodi cogitatione non secus atque à certissima sug- gestione Satanæ abhorrete.Cui enim hoc vel leuissime in men- tem venire potest,renuntiandūne sit & abnegandus sibi,à quō tam charo redemptus in ipsius ius & seruitium omnino trasie- rit. Neque vero vlli flammarū etiam æstus & veluti inundatio- nes, quæ corporibus minantur tantūm,ṗ vnum possunt, quic- quam sunt ad illam animarum pestilentem inhalationem,quæ in æternum exitium tandem adducturā sit.Quare cum illos ve- ritatis hostes nihil non moliri animaduertitis,vt vos à via abdu cāt,agnoscite simul illo artificio vobis retecto,Dominum rece- pruissuis canere.Ergo vbi seriō res agitur,præstate vos Christi mi lites, ac constanti fide Satanæ insultando, vniuersas ipsius ad- uersum vos instructas machinas dissiicite: à mundo quoque vos subducite,à quo non minor pernicies vobis etiam imminet. Il lud denique cogitate, sic esse voluntatem Domini, vt præsentis examinis occasione retecti, tanto fœlicius sub ipsius præsidium accurrendo quiescatis,modo etiam in illo abscondito Altissimi firmi & immoti perstetis: & quæ ad vos alliciendos ostentat Satan per nequitiæ suæ instrumenta, illa semel vobis vt infames scopulos prætereuehenda statuatis. Valete dilectissimi fratres. Dominus sua dona in vobis cumulet, vt quæ instant aduersa, elucemini, vosregat suo Spiritu, vt in recta via ad extremum vsque pergatis. Breuior autem fui, cum N. fratrem nostrum pluribus ista complexurum pro Dei in ipsum gratia confisus sum.
units.tr: I have received word, most beloved brothers, that new and very grievous troubles are being inflicted on you by the enemies of the truth. Satan is wholly intent on this, since he sees the Kingdom of the Son of God being advanced and the number of the godly increasing, and so he stirs up every stone to cast them down. That the Lord sometimes loosens the reins on the wicked, so that they may do harm, ought not to seem strange. For it is most just that our faith should be tried in this way, and that we should truly bear witness to how much we value it, when, though afflictions rage against us on account of the teaching of salvation, we nevertheless stand firm after everything has been done. And since our inborn weakness binds us here too, let us all the more eagerly run to the protection of him whom we cannot doubt to be both able and willing to help us in our cause. Just as the assaults of our adversaries, as they hurl themselves upon us, demand no small measure of courage and strength for us to withstand them, so their tricks and deceits must be avoided with a particular caution. It is hard for many people to be called, in the name of piety, to risk their life and property; but it is far worse when they are enticed by indirect arguments and underground tunnels, and drawn away from hope in God and from the fear of God. And this is the net that the two-horned Bishop has now cast over you, when he grants a space of three months for the message of the Gospel to be given up. In this way weak souls are dragged to destruction. Take heed, therefore, and abhor such thoughts no less than the most certain suggestion of Satan. For who could even in the slightest way think it right to renounce and deny himself, having been redeemed at so dear a price and having wholly passed into the right and service of Him? Nor indeed can the heat of flames and their like floods, which threaten only the body, do anything at all, when set against that pestilential breath into the soul which will at last bring about eternal destruction. Therefore, since you notice that these enemies of the truth leave nothing untried so that they may lead you from the way, recognise at the same time, now that their device has been uncovered, that the Lord has taken you up as his own. So when the matter is serious, show yourselves Christ's soldiers, and by steadfast faith mocking Satan, shatter all the machines he has set up against you. Withdraw yourselves also from the world, which threatens you with no less ruin. Finally, consider this: it is the will of the Lord that, being revealed by the occasion of the present trial, you should rest all the more happily by running to his protection, provided you also persevere firm and unmoved in that hidden refuge of the Most High; and those things which Satan displays to draw you in through the instruments of his wickedness, decide once and for all to sail past them as infamous rocks. Farewell, most beloved brothers. May the Lord heap his gifts upon you, so that you shine forth amid the adversities that press on you, and may he guide you by his Spirit, so that you may continue in the right way to the end. I have been briefer, since I trust in the grace of God toward our brother N., who will treat these matters at greater length.

units.la: M. D. LVII.
IO. CALVINVS N.N. S.D.
units.tr: John Calvin to N.N., greeting

units.la: Charitas Dei Patris, & Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi vobis semper adsit per Spiritus sancti communicationem.
units.tr: May the love of God the Father and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ always be with you through the fellowship of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: NON dubito, dilectissimi fratres, quin illud plerisque vestrum in metem venturù sit, me alienissimo tempore hoc ad vos scribendi munus aggressum esse, cùm ita passim feruet impiorum erudelitas, vt vel ad minimam olei guttam immanius exarsuram timendum sit. Atqui longè falluntur, qui in eo vno timore defixi his de rebus ita sentiunt. Ego vero hoc illud tempus esse vobis confirmo, quo veri exhortationis stimuli figendi sunt, qui omnes sèrio excitent, animosque reuocent ad bellum hoc Domini strenuè militandum. Persecutiones nimirum ab impiis luctæ Christianorum sunt, quibus fidei & constantiæ suæ documentum edant. Nunc igitur ad arma currendum est, quæ nimirum vno Dei verbi nomine aptissimè cõtinentur. Quo vero suç quisque infirmitatis sibi conscius est magis, eo sese maturius ad Domini armamentarium conferat. Atque hic sese detegit pudenda illorum indignitas, qui suis malis adeò secure indormiunt. Qui quum sese omnium debiles maximè offendant, & ad solij cadentis strepitum consternentur, iidem omnium maximè à singulari remedio quod offert ipsis Dominus abhorrent. Vos vero dilectiss. fratres agnoscite omnino, quàm opportunum sit istud erga vos meum studium, dum flamma persecutionum exæstuat, præsentémque piis intentant omnia mortem. Nam & hic mos erat olim apud sanctos illos martyres, vt quo desperatiorem tyrannorum rabiem aduersus Christi nomen in ipsorum suppliciis insectandum experiebantur, eo magis laborarent ad se mutuò excitandos, & sanctis admonitionibus conglutinandos: sic etiam Dominus ipse propositò discipulis turbulento illo statu rerum omnium, cuius nunc faciem intuemur, Vos interea, inquit, exultate, & attollite capita vestra, quia appropinquat redemptio vestra. Hoc si apud nosipsos non ita
units.tr: I do not doubt, most beloved brothers, that many of you will think it strange that I have undertaken this task of writing to you at so unseasonable a time, when the cruelty of the impious rages everywhere, so that one must fear it will blaze up more fiercely at the smallest drop of oil. But those are greatly mistaken who, fixed on this one fear, judge these matters in this way. I for my part assure you that this is the very time when the goads of true exhortation must be driven home, goads that will rouse everyone earnestly and call their spirits back to fight vigorously in the Lord's war. Persecutions, after all, are the struggles of Christians against the impious, in which they give proof of their faith and constancy. Now, therefore, we must run to arms, and these are most fittingly contained in the one name of the Word of God. Yet the more each person is aware of his own weakness, the sooner he should betake himself to the Lord's armoury. Here the shameful unworthiness of those is revealed who sleep so securely in their evils. Although they show themselves the most fearful of all, and are dismayed at the rustle of a falling leaf, these same men shrink most of all from the unique remedy the Lord offers them. But you, most beloved brothers, must recognise fully how opportune this zeal of mine for you is, now that the flame of persecution blazes and everything threatens the pious with present death. For it was also the custom long ago among those holy martyrs that the more desperate the rage of the tyrants against the name of Christ they found in their punishments, the more they laboured to rouse one another and to bind themselves together by holy exhortations. So also the Lord himself, setting before his disciples that turbulent state of all things whose face we now behold, said: "Meanwhile, rejoice and lift up your heads, for your redemption draws near." If among ourselves this is not yet so
