units.tr: Those who, when admonished, repeatedly relapse into the same vices and do not make an end of sinning, but rather mock the Church with empty promises, I judge should be treated more severely, not with simple words, since they do not cease to deceive with words. For if this gentleness is tolerated without penalty, it will afterwards leap into obstinacy and shamelessness.

units.la: In rudibus difficile est perpetuam legem tradere: sed hic non vulgari prudentia opus est, ut discernat Pastor inter tarditatem qua plurimi laborāt, & inter socordiam, quae vulgò crassa ignorantia vel affectata dicitur. Multi enim reperiuntur Idiotae satis astuti in priuatis negotiis, satis acuti ad lucrum captandum, & ad damnum vitandum perspicaces, qui ne verbo quidem ad testandam pietatem idonei sunt. Ergo quos ira videmus spòte indociles, incuria magis & contemptu, quàm ingenij penuria, pro hibendos à sacra Coena non dubito, donec pudefacti studiū ad discendū applicent. In aliis semifatuis modum hunc tenendum censeo, ne admittantur nisi modicè salem rudimentis imbuti: vt formulam precandi sciant, confessionem fidei, Legis praecepta, salutem sibi esse repositam in vno Christo fateantur, eúmque vnicum Mediatorem agnoscant, finem et Baptismi sui, & vsum Coenae non prorsus ignorent. Qui suspensa sacra Cœna proterue iudicium Ecclesiæ respuunt, hac sua contumacia declarant se extraneos: ac proinde nihil senioribus restare video, nisi vt Magistratum extimulent ad eos durius coercendos. Nam in pœnis Ecclesiasticis vltima est excommunicatio. Quod vero ad censuras spectat, nota est illa Pauli admonitio, non esse noxium de his qui foris sunt iudicare. 1.Cor.5.13.
units.tr: With the untaught it is hard to lay down a fixed rule. Here, however, no ordinary prudence is needed, so that the minister may distinguish between the slowness from which most suffer and the sloth that is commonly called gross ignorance or affected ignorance. For many are found who are simple and yet shrewd enough in private affairs, sharp enough to seize gain and quick to avoid loss, yet who are not fit even to bear witness to their piety in a word. Therefore I do not doubt that those whom we see to be unteachable by their own choice, through carelessness and contempt rather than poverty of intellect, must be kept from the holy Supper until, shamed, they apply themselves to learning. For other half-witted people I think this measure should be kept: that they be admitted only if they are moderately imbued with the rudiments, so that they know the form of prayer, the confession of faith, the precepts of the Law; that they acknowledge that salvation is laid up for them in Christ alone, and recognize Him as the only Mediator; and that they are not wholly ignorant of the purpose of their Baptism and the use of the Supper. Those who, when the Supper is suspended, wantonly reject the judgment of the Church, by this stubbornness declare themselves outsiders; and accordingly I see nothing left for the elders but to spur the magistrate to restrain them more sharply. For excommunication is the last of the ecclesiastical penalties. As for censures, the well-known admonition of Paul applies, that it is not my business to judge those who are outside. 1 Cor. 5.13.

units.la: Optandum quidem est, vt præter diem Dominicum pauci retineatur disciplina: nam vt tollantur e medio superstitionum reliquiæ, semper ad hoc vitium plus æquo propensi erunt homines. Hodie autem maior pars feriis Papatum fouere appetit. Vt tamen obuiam eatur dissidiis, cauendum est, ne quisque proprio arbitrio feriasabrogans æmulationem accendat. Sed qui malum hoc finatu cupiunt, studeant in eundem consensum fratres suos adducere. Hoc si impetrari non poterit, singuli quoad citra tumultum fieri poterit, paulatim ex superuacuo numero rescindant, quas videbunt magis esse noxias, quo facilius sibi conciliént populi suffragia.
units.tr: It is indeed to be wished that, apart from the Lord's Day, few holidays be retained; for, so that the remnants of superstition may be removed from the midst, men will always be more than enough inclined to this vice. Today, however, most people wish to cherish the Papacy through holidays. Yet so that disputes may be averted, care must be taken that no one, by his own judgment, abrogating holidays, kindles rivalry. But those who wish to remedy this evil should strive to bring their brothers to the same agreement. If this cannot be obtained, let individuals, as far as it can be done without tumult, gradually cut from the superfluous number those which they see to be more harmful, so that they may more easily win the votes of the people.

units.la: Pauperes, quibus Ecclesiæ liberalitas ignauiæ est occasio, eleemosynis minime alendos esse, tum communis sensus dictat, tum etiam clare docet Paulus. Nam vbi pigros ventres otioque deditos excommunicatio iussit, tandem subiicit, Qui non vult operari, neque comedat. 2. Thess. 3.10. Vale eximie vir, & mihi colende frater. Geneuæ, 11 11. Calendas Martij. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: The common sense of mankind dictates, and Paul also clearly teaches, that the poor, for whom the liberality of the Church is an occasion of idleness, ought not to be supported with alms. For when excommunication has bidden the lazy bellies and those given over to idleness to be put out, he finally adds: "If anyone will not work, neither let him eat." 2 Thess. 3.10. Farewell, outstanding man and brother to be honoured by me. Geneva, 11 days before the Kalends of March, 1559.

units.la: CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: Calvin sends greeting to N.

units.la: Vum tibi aduersus illecebras, quibus te corrumpere tentabant Satanæ lenones, inflexibilis pridem sueri animus, ac continuis experimentis fidei & pietatis tuæ constantiam probaueris: longius nunc, vt audio te Christus produxit ad ferendum crucis suæ opprobrium, ne cui obscurum foret, quia Deo placere cuperes, te hominum gratiam fuerint quæ spernere. Et certè res ipsa ostendit, te probe hoc in corde habuisse concoctum, vbi nos non solum ad manifestam defectionem & perfidiam solicitant homines, sed etiam ad obliquas dest xiones inducunt, neque blanditiis præbendas esse aures, neque imperio morem gerendum, neque cedendum minis ac terroribus. Etsi autem duros ac violentos insultus inter principia sustinu ne non dubito: memineris rame plures tibi & magis arduas difficultates adhuc restare, vt eo alacrior in certamen descendas. Interea quod illo mundi præsidio orbatus, quod iam non aliter quam turpissima mercede redimere poteras, palàm militès sub crucis vexillo, tibi ex animo gratulor: aliquanto etiam magis, quod in sacra functione
units.tr: Since you have long had a mind unbending against the allurements by which Satan's pimps tried to corrupt you, and since by continual proofs you have shown the steadiness of your faith and piety, Christ, as I hear, has now led you further, to bear the reproach of his cross. It is plain that you did not care for the favour of men, because you wished to please God. And the facts themselves show that you have thoroughly digested this in your heart, when men urge us not only to open defection and treachery but also to indirect evasions, and tell us that ears should not be given to flattery, nor obedience rendered to command, nor should we yield to threats and terrors. Although I do not doubt that you have endured harsh and violent assaults at the beginning, remember that more and harder difficulties still remain, so that you may enter the struggle all the more eagerly. Meanwhile, that you have been stripped of that worldly protection, which you could now recover only at the most shameful price, and that you openly fight as a soldier under the banner of the cross, I heartily congratulate you. I congratulate you even more that you labour so sincerely and wholeheartedly in the sacred office to which God has devoted you.

units.la: Epist. 279. functione cui te Deus addixit, tam syncere & cordate laboras. Certe non sine admiratione audimus, quod de tua strenuitate & diligentia referunt oculati testes. Quo magis te eniti conuenit, quod te sedulo facere persuasus sum, ut primis vltima respondeant, neque vel vlla discrimina reformides, vel taediis fragaris, vel ad obstacula resilias, vel fatigeris laboribus, quorum onus tibi grauissimum incumbere me non latet. Vtinam in me esset, aliquid adiumenti vel leuationis tibi adferre: idem & collegae mei cuperent. Sed quia nihil melius suppetit, non definimus coeptam Patrem rogare, ut tibi vires inuitas suppeditet. Ignoscens breuitati: imo etiam quod fessus has dictare coactus sum. Nam & quartana me adhuc detinet, neque mihi virium debilitas multum permittit. Vale igitur eximie vir, & frater mihi colende. Dominus tibi semper adsit, te gubernet, laboresque tuos benedicat. Collegae mei tibi plurimam salutem precantur. XXVII. Martij. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: Epist. 279. Indeed we hear with no little admiration what eyewitnesses report of your energy and diligence. All the more should you strive, since I am persuaded that you do this diligently, so that your last deeds answer to your first. Neither shrink from any dangers, nor faint from weariness, nor recoil at obstacles, nor give way under labours, the weight of which I know lies very heavily on you. Would that it were in my power to bring you some help or relief; my colleagues would wish the same. But since nothing better is at hand, we do not cease to ask the Father, whom we have begun to ask, to supply you with unconquered strength. Forgive the brevity; indeed I was compelled to dictate this while tired. For a quartan fever still holds me, and the weakness of my strength does not allow much more. Farewell, therefore, distinguished man and brother to be cherished. May the Lord always be with you, govern you, and bless your labours. My colleagues send you their warmest greetings. 27 March 1559.

units.la: FARELLVS CALVINO.
units.tr: FARELLUS TO CALVIN.

units.la: Audiuimus magno perfusi gaudio te liberatum a febri bene habere, & concionari. Dominus hoc tam opportunum erga suos beneficium quam diuturnum tibi & nobis reddat. Principes bene in Metensis affecti, magis nunc afficiuntur, quum videant eos numero & animis crescere. Rasi magis & magis insaniunt: licet maior eorum pars de alia ratione vitae cogitet, ac repugnare frustra Euangelio nolit, iudicetque satius esse verbo parere, si praedicetur, quam reluctari. Nescio an resciueris, quid Cardinalis nomine fratris, nimirum ducis Guisiani, scripserit Richroco primario duci equitum, qui ante Saxonem exceperat: nempe vt ducem commonefaceret, Regi nihil acerbius posse euenire, & nihil minus ferre posse, quia Religionem suam alterari. Literae missae fuerunt ad Principes, ac compertum fuit non Guisiani ducis, sed Cardinalis esse. Nam sigillum quo obsignatae erant, galerum habebat Cardinalis, & quum Dux subscripsit Francois, manus erat Cardinalis, vt probe nouit N. & ita habebat, Voftre bon ami le duc de Guise. Voluit Saxo omnes Principes videre literas. Metenses fratres maiori quam vnquam numero libellum supplicem porrexerunt iis, qui praesunt vrbi Metensi, & nunquam tam amicum responsum acceperunt: quod vt videas, ad te mitto libelli exemplar, & quod fratres scribunt de responso. Quae audio de fratribus & eorum literis, quas ad me scribunt, & alios, & vt video omnes in eos affectos mire moueri, faciuntque vt sperem bene. Mirum est omnium affectus in Viretum, cupiuntque omnes vt eum eo perducere possim, quod
units.tr: We have heard, filled with great joy, that you are freed from fever, are doing well, and are preaching again. May the Lord grant this so timely a benefit to his people, and may it last as long for you as for us. The princes in Metz, who are well disposed, are now more strongly disposed, since they see their number and spirit growing. The tonsured clergy rage more and more, although the greater part of them think of a different way of life, and do not wish to resist the Gospel in vain, judging it better to obey the word, if it is preached, than to struggle against it. I do not know whether you have heard what the Cardinal wrote in the name of his brother, namely the Duke of Guise, to Richrod, the chief leader of the horsemen, who had earlier received the Saxon. It was to warn the duke that nothing more bitter could happen to the King, and that he could bear nothing less, because his religion would be altered. Letters were sent to the princes, and it was discovered that they were not from Duke Guise but from the Cardinal. For the seal with which they were sealed bore the Cardinal's hat, and although the Duke signed Francois, the hand was the Cardinal's, as N. knows well, and the letter read: Voftre bon ami le duc de Guise. The Saxon wished all the princes to see the letters. The brethren of Metz presented a supplicating petition, with a greater number than ever, to those who govern the city of Metz, and never received so friendly an answer. So that you may see this, I send you a copy of the petition, and what the brethren write about the response. What I hear about the brethren and their letters, which they write to me and to others, and, as I see, the feeling of all is wonderfully moved in their favour, and makes me hope well. Wonderful is everyone's affection for Viret, and all wish that I could bring him to them, which would that it happen soon. Farewell, and keep well the Church of Christ with Viret, whom I wish to serve the Lord long and safe. I do not omit Beza, nor all the pious syndics with the Senate. Strasbourg, 11 April 1559.

units.la: Epist. 280. vtinam breui fiat. Vale bene & te Ecclesiæ Christi serua cum Vi-reto, quem opto saluum diu D.seruire, Bezam quoque & omnes ne prætereram Syndicos pios cum Senatu. Argentorati, 11 1.Aprilis, M. D. LIX.
units.tr: Epist. 280. May it happen soon. Farewell, and may you keep the Church of Christ well, with Viret, whom I pray the Lord keeps safe for a long time. I do not omit Beza also, and all the pious syndics, with the Senate. Strasbourg, 11 April 1559.

units.la: Tuus totus Farellus.
units.tr: Wholly yours, Farel.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N.N. S. D.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO N.N., GREETING.

units.la: PEriucundum nobis fuit, dilectiss. fratres, quod de bona illa vestra spe tenuntiatum est, quam Dominus vobis ostendit de pura Euangelij ipsius doctrina vobis restituenda, cum facultate ipsius pure inuocandi, colendi, & glorificandi. Atqui nō parum dolet, quòd vestra timiditas atque pusillanimitas vos ita conspringit, adeoque congelat, ne, vt par est, tesfemini, quanti vobis fiat res adeo incomparabiles. Tantum abest enim vt promoueatis aliquid hac in parte, vt potius retroferamini, ac proin de gratia Dei ianuam claudatis. Cœtus vestri effluunt vt audimus à cantu Psalmorum abstinetis & sancta illa Dei laudum exercitia apud vos amplius non vigent. Scimus fieri hoc à vobis propter aliquas minas: atqui si vestram conditionem conseris cum illa tot fratrum, qui alibi durissima captiuitate constricti, non se continent tamen, quin panem illum vitæ constanter requirat, quis vos excusabit à pudenda pusillanimitate, si minima quæque prohibitio vos ita pertutbat, quoniam ipsi apud vos pondus & fidem additis? Vnde magis etiam metuedum est, ne ita pedem referendo, à via penitus aberretis. Vetus est illud malum, quod se quidam ab Ecclesia subducat: contra quod non frustra nos ita exhortatur Apostolus ad Hebræos, videamus nec ne cœtum nostrum deseramus, vt à nonnullis fiat. Cum igitur illa exhortatio remedium ipsum complectatur, quo adiuersus malum nobis consulendum sit, tanto magis videndum est, vt gregi ipsi agglutinati stemus, cui nos semel immensa sua benitate Dominus adiunxit. Agnoscite & illud eiusdem Apostoli, Nondum restitistis vsque ad sanguinem. Date igitur operam vt omnia illa impedimenta superetis, quæ à Satana suggeruntur, vt officium deseratis. Cogitate vero quo spectet Euangelij vocatio, vt illa iustum apud vos pretium obtineat. Cogitate etiam quòd iustius vitæ caducæ, & eum ses centis tam indigua mercede conseruandæ operæ pretium esse possit. Atque hinc colligite, quo me rito honore prosequendus sit vobis Filius Dei qui vobis se offert, quo animo ad Regnum cœleste adspirandum sit, dum vobis aperitur, quid valeant spiritus illi thesauri, quorum vos participatione dignatur. Neque hic illud à vobis afferendum est, quòd nullo modo de Euangelij professione deccessuri sitis, vtcunque aduersariorum impetus vestra quadam ratione declinetis.Non enim frustra institutam voluit Dominus ordinariam verbi auditionem,cuius pœrpetuum nobis vsum esse vellet. Etenim qui nullum tempus à corporis alendi cura & studio vacuum abire sinimus,quomodo ferendi fumus,vbi quod ad animæ vitam & pastum attinet, ita remissi & obliuiosi deprehendemur? Offertur vero omnibus expedita ratio,quam tanto minus negligere ipsi debetis,aut ab ea plenius obeunda quicquam remittere, cùm iam vobis ipsam ex parte ad manum esse constet. Et quot piæ animæ illud ipsum esuriunt, qu bus si eadem quæ vobis facultas semel osferretur, longè alius ardor & zelus in ipsis extaret. Expergiscimini igitur di leƈtiss quàm serio à vestro illo somno, ac nouum vigorem colligite, ad resistendum constanter instrumentis Satanæ,neque vllo modo vestram vobis libertatem eripi sinite. Dominus enim qui tanto nos priuilegio dignatus est,vt Patrem se à nobis inuocari iubeat,idem etiam iubet vt à confidenti & alto quodam animo hæc nostra confessio prodeat. Non possumus illud etiam reticere,quod gra-uissimam reprehensionem meretur,quòd nempe & verbo Dei & ipsius Ministris fores vestræ iam vix pateant. Obiicietis interdiƈtum. Scilicet cùm ita vos Dominus honorat,vt domos vestras sua templa esse iubeat,ac tam sanƈto vsui dedicet,quid momenti habere debent aduersus illud Dei placitum,quæruis hominum interdiƈta? Quid si sub capitis pœna interdiƈtum esset,quanto ad deficiendum procliuiores essetis? Pessimè verò vobis consulitis, dum illud Satanæ artificium nò anteuertitis, quo vobis certam occasionem præripere meditatur, quæ semel elapsa è manibus, nunquam deinde restituenda sit. Quare tam vt mali superioris memoria sepeliatur, quàm vt cauea sis,ne vestra ingratitudine eo bono destituamini, quod est adhuc ad manû, pergite ea via qua cœpistis Domino auƈtore; atque illud reipsa constet in vobis, Dei veritatem nempe omnibus huius vitæ commodis à vobis merito suo anteferri, atque ipsius vniuscultui & gloriæ reliqua omnia quæ ab illo vos auersura erant, quàm longo interuallo post-haberi. Nostram porrò præscri scribendi rationem à vobis æquì & boni consultum iri speramus, quam noster pro vestra salute procurāda affeƈtus ita dictauit, ac necessitas ipsa stimulos vobis adhibendi expressit, Dominus vos, dileƈtissimi, virtute inuiƈta Spiritus sui confirmet, atque ita vos regat, vt nomen sanƈtum ipsius glorificetur in vobis, vos etiàm præsidio suo vnicè complećtatur. x i x. Iulij. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: It was most pleasing to us, most beloved brothers, that the good hope you express was announced to us, the hope the Lord has shown you of the restoration to you of the pure doctrine of the Gospel itself, together with the ability to call upon, worship and glorify him purely. Yet it grieves us not a little that your timidity and pusillanimity so cramp and chill you that you do not, as is fitting, show how much such incomparable things are worth to you. For you are so far from advancing anything in this matter that you rather draw back, and so shut the door on the grace of God. Your assemblies, as we hear, are falling away: you abstain from singing the Psalms, and those holy exercises of praising God no longer flourish among you. We know this is done by you on account of some threats. But if you compare your condition with that of so many brothers who, held elsewhere in the harshest captivity, nevertheless do not restrain themselves from constantly seeking that bread of life, who will excuse you from shameful pusillanimity, if each least prohibition so disturbs you, since you yourselves add weight and credit to it among yourselves? Hence there is all the more reason to fear that by drawing back your foot in this way you will wander altogether from the path. The old evil is that some withdraw from the Church, and against this the Apostle, in his letter to the Hebrews, exhorts us not in vain that we consider whether we forsake our assembly, as some do. Since that exhortation holds out the very remedy by which we must guard against the evil, so much more must we take care to stand cemented to the flock itself, to which the Lord, in his immense goodness, once joined us. Acknowledge also that saying of the same Apostle: "You have not yet resisted unto blood." Take pains, therefore, to overcome all those impediments which are suggested by Satan, so that you do not desert your duty. Consider well to what end the calling of the Gospel tends, so that it may obtain its due price among you. Consider also that it can be worth the effort to preserve a life so brief at the cost of so unworthy a reward. And from this gather how worthily the Son of God, who offers himself to you, is to be honoured, with what mind we ought to aspire to the heavenly kingdom, now that it is opened to you, and what those spiritual treasures are worth, the participation in which he deigns to give you. Nor should you bring forward here the objection that you will in no way depart from the profession of the Gospel, however you may in some way avoid the assaults of the adversaries. For the Lord did not wish the ordinary hearing of the word, which he wished us to use perpetually, to be instituted in vain. For how shall we bear ourselves if we allow no time to pass free from care for feeding the body, and yet are found so careless and forgetful as to the life and food of the soul? The means are offered to all readily, and you ought the less to neglect them or to remit anything of their full use, since it is now plain that they are already partly at hand for you. And how many pious souls hunger for that very thing, to whom, if the same opportunity as yours were once offered, a far different ardour and zeal would appear in them. Awake, therefore, most beloved, and how seriously, from that sleep of yours, and gather new vigour to resist steadfastly the instruments of Satan, and by no means allow your liberty to be snatched from you. For the Lord, who has honoured us with so great a privilege that he bids us invoke him as Father, also bids that this our confession come forth from a confident and lofty spirit. Nor can we keep silent about what deserves the gravest reproach, that your doors are now scarcely open to the word of God and to its ministers. You will object the interdict. Surely, since the Lord honours you so much that he bids your houses be his temples and dedicates them to so holy a use, what weight should the commands of men have against that pleasure of God? What if the interdict were under pain of death: how much more prone to fall away would you be? But you counsel yourselves very badly while you do not forestall that artifice of Satan, by which he plans to snatch from you a certain opportunity, which, once slipped from your hands, is never to be restored. Therefore, both so that the memory of the former evil may be buried and so that you may be on guard lest by your ingratitude you be deprived of the good that is still at hand, press on by the way on which you began, with the Lord as your author; and let it be made plain in fact among you that the truth of God is deservedly preferred by you to all the comforts of this life, and that all the rest, which would turn you aside from him, is held far beneath his sole worship and glory. Moreover, we hope you will take in good part and kindly the manner of writing we have adopted, which our affection for your salvation has dictated, and which necessity itself has forced us to use as a spur to you. May the Lord, most beloved, confirm you with the unconquered power of his Spirit, so govern you that his holy name may be glorified in you, and embrace you alone with his protection. 19 July 1559.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: IO. CALVINVS N. S. D.

units.la: BInas abs te,integerrime frater,intra breue tempus literas accepi,quibus de statu Ecclesiæ Metenfis fecisti me certiorem. Etsi autem eadem fere quidam alij boni viri vel narrarunt, vel scripserunt:quia tamen & interiores morbos prudenter notas, & de remediis admones, & quantulum affulgeat spei doces (quod ab illis prætermissum fuerat) gratissimum mihi officium præstitisti. Quod & Psalmos canere,& conuentus agere destiterunt,nescio quibus inanibus minis territi, in eo apparuit pudéda eorum ignauia & timiditas:in hospitio autem negando (ad quod officium certatim fe ingerere debuerât) turpius flagitium. Sed bene est,q; neque animi tui constantiam debilitauit eorum mollities,quin torpidis & propè recusantibus te sponte offerres: neque offendit ingratitudo vel alió reflexit, quin semper operâ illis tuam impendere fis paratus,modò admittât. Nos acriter,vt videbis,eos stimulare conati fumus.Te vero cur strenuè currentem horter,nulla est causa. Tantùm Dominum precabor, vt te Spiritu prudentiæ, moderationis & zeli regere pergat, inuiétâq; virtute fulcire,compescat omnes aduersarios,benedicat sanctos tuos conatus & labores. Vale integerrime frater.Viretus,Beza & reliqui Collegæ mei tibi multam salutem precantur.xiiii.Calendas Augusti. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: Recently I received a letter from you, most upright brother, within a short time, by which you made me aware of the state of the church at Metz. Although certain other good men have either related or written almost the same things, nonetheless you have performed a most welcome service for me, since you both note prudently the inner diseases, advise on remedies, and show how much hope glimmers (which those others had passed over). That they have ceased both to sing Psalms and to hold assemblies, I know not what empty threats having frightened them, has shown their shameful cowardice and timidity; and in refusing hospitality (a duty for which they ought to have eagerly offered themselves) an even more disgraceful crime. But it is well that their weakness has not weakened the steadfastness of your spirit, so that you have offered yourself willingly even to those who were sluggish and nearly refusing; nor has ingratitude offended you or turned you aside, so that you are always ready to devote your labour to them, provided they accept it. We, as you will see, have tried sharply to goad them. As for urging you on to run vigorously, there is no reason. I will only pray the Lord that He continue to guide you with the Spirit of prudence, moderation and zeal, to strengthen you with unconquered courage, to restrain all your adversaries, and to bless your holy endeavours and labours. Farewell, most upright brother. Viret, Beza and my other colleagues send you many greetings. 19th July 1559.

units.la: KNOXVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: KNOX TO CALVIN, GREETINGS.

units.la: Ad disciplinam Ecclefiinterrogata.
units.tr: Questions concerning church discipline.

units.la: QVæ fit rerum mearum conditio, fratres in Christo colendiff.quibus armis & machinis impetiti fuimus & fimus, & quomodo Dei auxilio tuti hactenus inimicis nostris non cessimus,vos docere potest hic frater non mihi foli, sed vniuersæ Ecclesiæ propter pietatem charus. Quem vt viscera mea precor suscipite:eidem significantes quæ fit vestra de subscriptis articulis sententia.
units.tr: Dear brethren in Christ, this brother, who is dear not only to me but to the whole Church for his piety, can tell you what my situation is, with what weapons and machines we have been and still are assailed, and how, by God's help, we have so far been safe and have not yielded to our enemies. I beg you to receive him as you would my own heart, and to let him know your opinion on the following articles.

units.la: 1. An ad Baptismum ad nitti debeant spurij, idololatrarum & excommunicatorum filij priusquam vel parentes per refipifcentiam sese subdiderint Ecclesiæ,vel ij qui ex huiusmodi prognati sunt,Baptismum petere possint.
units.tr: 1. Whether the children of idolaters and excommunicated persons ought to be admitted to baptism, before either their parents have submitted themselves to the Church by repentance, or those born of such parents can themselves ask for baptism.

units.la: 2. Vtrum monachis & sacrificulis Papifticis, qui neque Ecclesiæ Dei seruiunt, neque propter habitudinem seruire possunt, annui reditus persoluendi sunt, etiamsi errorem pristinum ore fateantur.
units.tr: 2. Whether annual revenues should be paid to Papist monks and priests who neither serve the Church of God nor are able to serve it on account of their condition, even if they confess their former error with their mouths.

units.la: Hæc quia nego,plusæquo seuerus iudicor, non à solis Papisticis, sticis, verumetiam ab iis qui sibi veritatis patroni videntur. Plura scribere vetant febris qua crucior, laborum moles qua premor, & Gallorum bombardæ, qui vt nos opprimant nunc appulerunt. Aderit suis is, cuius caûsam tuemur. Memores nostri sitis in precibus. Gratia vobiscum. Raptim xxviii.Augusti. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: Because I deny these things, I am judged too severe, not only by the Papists but also by those who seem to be the champions of truth. A fever that torments me, the weight of my labours that presses upon me, and the Scottish cannon, which have now been brought up to crush us, forbid me to write more. Help will come from the one whose cause we defend. Remember us in your prayers. Grace be with you. Hastily, 28 August 1559.

units.la: Vobis addictissimus Ioannes Knoxus.
units.tr: Your most devoted, John Knox.

units.la: CAL. P. MARTYRI S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO PETER MARTYR, GREETINGS.

units.la: COmmodè accidit, vt biduo postquam mihi redditæ sunt tuæ literæ, venerande frater, discederet hic nuntius, cui meas tutò committerem, etsi nihil in præsentia quod scribä, nisi triste, occurrit. Inuitus autem facio, vt te mecum in easdem inuoluam molestias: nisi qu vtrique nostrum hæc anxietas est commu-nis. Magno dolore me conficit, nec minore cura ac metu me torquet misera fratrum nostrorum quibus cordi est syncera pietas in Gallia, conditio. Promptum erat in manu Regis Nauarræ his malis remedium: & mira pollicitus fuerat, sed quum eius ignauia nihil fuerit turpius, accessit tandem & proditio. Socrus Principis Condæi à Regina matre impetrauerat, vt ex Ministris Ecclesiæ Parisiensis vnum admitteret ad colloquium. Vocatus ille dimittitur cum ludibrio. Interim ad horrendam stragem omnia inclinant: quia à desertoribus fuerunt derecti, quicunq; professi erant se Christi discipulos, & occultos cœtus frequentabat. Res plusquam luctuosa. Tamen expectandum æquis & quietis animis, donec è cœlo appareat vindex nolter: quod opportunè faturum scio. Sed rogandus simul est, vt debiles animos sustineat. Ego te & Collegas tuos non hortabor, vt eorum salutem Deo commendetis: quia scio ad hanc curam sponte propensos esse. Vale clarissime vir, & frater ex animo mihi obseruande. Saluta amicos. Dominus te incolumem tueatur cum vxore, gubernet, confirmet, donisque suis locupletet. Geneuæ, IIII. Nonas Octobris. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: It happened conveniently that two days after your letter, most venerable brother, was returned to me, a messenger was leaving here, to whom I could safely entrust my reply, although at present I find nothing to write except sad news. I do it unwillingly, so as not to involve you with me in the same troubles, unless this anxiety is common to us both. I am worn down by great grief, and I am tormented by no less care and fear for the wretched condition of our brethren in France who hold sincere piety dear. A remedy for these evils lay ready in the hand of the King of Navarre, and he had promised wonderful things; but since nothing was more shameful than his cowardice, treachery has finally come too. The mother-in-law of Prince Condé had obtained from the Queen Mother that she would admit one of the ministers of the Church of Paris to a conference. He was summoned and then dismissed with mockery. Meanwhile everything is tending towards a horrible slaughter, since all who professed themselves disciples of Christ and attended secret assemblies have been betrayed by deserters. The matter is more than lamentable. Yet we must wait with calm and quiet minds until our avenger appears from heaven, which I know he will do at the right time. But at the same time he must be asked to sustain our faint spirits. I will not urge you and your colleagues to commend their safety to God, since I know you are of your own accord inclined to this care. Farewell, most distinguished man and brother, whom I heartily esteem. Greet our friends. May the Lord keep you safe with your wife, guide and strengthen you, and enrich you with his gifts. Geneva, 4 October 1559.

units.la: Ioannes Caluinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: CAL. D. IOANNI KNOXO SCOTO, DE libertis ad Baptismum admittendis.
units.tr: CALVIN TO JOHN KNOX OF SCOTLAND, ON ADMITTING THE CHILDREN TO BAPTISM.

units.la: SI expectatione tua tardius, integerrime frater, literis tuis respondeo, qui eas attulit contertaneus tuus optimus mihi erit testis, pigritiam non fuisse causam morae. Ipse quoque satis intelligis, quàm rara scribendi commoditas nobis detur, quià rebus turbatis difficiles sunt in patriam tuam omnes accessus. Non mihi solum, sed piis omnibus quos laetitiae meae feci participes, audire iucundum fuit de vberrimo laborum tuorum successu. Porro vt miramur incredibilem successum tam breui temporis spacio, ita ingentes pariter agimus Deo gratias, cuius singularis Dei benedictio hic refulget: quae & amplam fiduciae materiam in futuru tempus suggerit, & proinde ad superanda quaelibet certamina animare vos debet. Quia non ignoro, quam ftre nuus fis hortator, & quid facultatis ac neruorum Deus ad has partes obeundas tibi contulerit, fratres stimulare superuacuum esse duxi. Interea non aliter fumus periculis vestris anxij, quam si communis esset militia: & quod vnum superest, vota nostra cum vestris coniungimus, vt caelestis Pater hostes vestros furentes, amentia & caecitate percutiat, eorum consilia dissipet, conatus omnes & apparatus frangat. Certe in classe armanda multu laborant, praecipue ob nummorum penuriam. Draconi tamen certius est omnia miscere, quam non aliquid moliri.
units.tr: If I answer your letter later than you expected, most upright brother, the one who brought it, your fellow-countryman, will be a good witness to me that it was not laziness that caused the delay. You yourself also understand how rarely an opportunity for writing is given to us, since in these troubled times all access to your country is difficult. It was not only pleasing to me, but to all the godly whom I have made sharers in my joy, to hear of the most abundant success of your labours. Indeed, just as we marvel at the incredible success in so short a time, so too we give equal thanks to God, whose singular blessing shines out here. It both supplies ample ground for confidence for the future, and ought therefore to encourage you to overcome whatever struggles lie ahead. Since I am not unaware what a vigorous encourager you are, and what strength and vigour God has given you to undertake this task, I have thought it superfluous to spur you on. Meanwhile we are no less anxious about your dangers than if the war were our own; and as for what remains, we join our prayers to yours, that the heavenly Father may strike your raging enemies with madness and blindness, scatter their counsels, and break all their attempts and preparations. Certainly they labour hard to arm their fleet, especially because of a shortage of money. Yet it is more certain for the dragon to stir up everything than not to attempt something.

units.la: De quaestionibus quarum solutionem postulas, postquam retuli ad collegas meos, de communi sententia ita respondendum censuimus. Merito quaeris, an idololatrarum & excommunicatorum liberos ad Baptismum admittere liceat, donec resipiscentiam parentes sint testati. Semper enim arcte cauendum, ne profanetur mysterij huius sanctitas: quod fieri certum est, si promiscue alienis conceditur, vel quisquam recipiatur, fine idoneis sponsoribus, & qui numerari queant inter legitimos Ecclesiae ciues. Sed quia in recto Baptismi vsu respicienda est Dei auctoritas, ac eius institutio pro certa ratione valere debet: hic im primis expendere conuenit, quos Deus sua voce ad Baptismum inuitet. Promissio autem non sobolem tantum cuiusque fidelium in primo gradu comprehendit, sed in mille generationes extenditur. Vnde etiam factum est, vt pieratis interruptio, quae gratiae fuerit in Papatu, vigorem & efficaciam Baptismi non abstulerit. Origo enim spectanda est, & ipsa Baptismi ratio, & natura ex promissione aestimanda. Nobis ergo minime dubium est, quin soboles ex sanctis & piis atauis progenita, quanuis apostatae fuerint aui & parentes, ad Ecclesiae tamen corpus pertineat. Sicut enim praua & vesana superstitio fuit in Papatu, Iudaeis & Turcis furari vel eripere liberos, & mox ad Baptismum ingerere ita vbicunq; non prorsus intercidit, vel extincta fuit Christianismi professio, fraudantur iure suo infantes, si a communi Symbolo arcentur: quia iniquum est, cum Deus ante annos trecentos vel plures, adoptione sua eos dignatus fuerit, vt quae deinde sequuta est parentum impietas, caelestis gratiae cursum abrumpat. Deniq; sicuti non recipitur quisque ad Baptismum, vnius duntaxat taxat patris sui respectu, vel fauore, sed propter continuum Dei fœdus: ita vnius parentis odio ab Ecclesiæ ingressu prohiberi infantes, nulla ratio patitur. Interea fatemur necessariam esse sponsionem. Nihil enim magis præposterum quàm inseri in Christi corpus, quos non speramus fore eius discipulos. Quare si nullus ex cognatis appareat qui fidem suam obliget Ecclesiæ, ac curam suscipiat docendi infantis, luxoria est actio, & Baptismus polluitur. Verùm quisquis ex infantibus offertur, legitima pactione interposita, cur reiici debeat non videmus. Adde quòd alia est nunc renascentis Ecclesiæ ratio, quàm rite formatæ & compositæ. Dum enim ex horrenda dissipatione colligitur Ecclesia, quoniam posteffio Baptismi per longam ætatum seriem ad nos vsque viguit, retinenda est: successu autem temporis corrigenda quæ obrepsit licentia, & cogendi parentes, vt suos ipsi liberos offerant & primi sint sponsores. Nam si inter principia seuerè exigitur summa perfectio, valde timendum est, ne multi hac occasione cupide arrepta, in sordibus suis iaceant. Fatemur quidem nihil debere nobis tanti esse, vt vel tantillum deflectamus à linea diuinitus nobis præscripta: sed putamus nos breuiter ostendisse, si reiicimus à Baptismo quos constat esse Ecclesiæ domesticos, nimis seueram fore prohibitionem. Itaque dum melior expectatur progressus, ac vim suam obtineat disciplina, recipiantur infantes qua diximus lege, vt promittant sponsores, curæ ac studio sibi fore probam syncerámque eorum institutionem. Quanquam interea non negamus, idololatras, quoties nascuntur ipsis liberi, acriter monendos & stimulandos esse, vt se Deo vere addicant: excommunicatos etiam vt se reconcilient Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: As to the questions whose solution you ask, after I had referred them to my colleagues, we judged that the answer should be given as follows, by common opinion. You rightly ask whether it is lawful to admit the children of idolaters and excommunicated persons to baptism before the parents have given evidence of repentance. For the holiness of this mystery must always be guarded with close care, lest it be profaned; and it is certainly profaned if it is granted indiscriminately to strangers, or if anyone is received without suitable sponsors who can be counted among the lawful citizens of the Church. But since in the right use of baptism the authority of God must be regarded, and his institution ought to hold good as a sure rule, it is first of all fitting to consider whom God invites to baptism by his own voice. Now the promise embraces not only the offspring of each believer in the first degree, but extends to a thousand generations. Hence it has also come about that the interruption of godliness, which existed under the Papacy as a kind of grace, has not taken away the force and efficacy of baptism. For the origin must be looked at, and the very nature of baptism, and its nature must be judged from the promise. It is therefore by no means doubtful to us that the offspring born of holy and godly ancestors, although their grandfathers and parents became apostates, nevertheless still belong to the body of the Church. For just as in the Papacy it was a perverse and mad superstition to steal or snatch away children from Jews and Turks and then to force them into baptism, so wherever the profession of Christianity has not altogether perished or been extinguished, infants are robbed of their right if they are shut out from the common creed; for it is unjust that, since God has deigned to adopt them three hundred or more years ago, the impiety of the parents that followed should cut off the course of heavenly grace. Finally, just as no one is received to baptism out of regard or favour for one parent alone, but on account of the continuing covenant of God, so no reason allows infants to be kept from entering the Church because of one parent's hatred. Meanwhile we admit that a sponsorship is necessary. For nothing is more absurd than to be grafted into the body of Christ those whom we do not hope will become his disciples. Therefore, if none of the kin appears who will bind his faith to the Church and take up the care of teaching the infant, the action is a mockery and baptism is polluted. Yet we do not see why whoever of the infants is offered, with a lawful agreement interposed, should be rejected. Add to this that the situation of the Church now being reborn is different from that of one duly formed and organized. For while the Church is being gathered out of a dreadful dispersion, the practice of baptism, which has flourished among us through a long succession of ages, must be retained; but in time the licence that has crept in must be corrected, and parents must be compelled to offer their own children and to be the first sponsors. For if supreme perfection is strictly demanded at the outset, it is greatly to be feared that many, eagerly seizing upon this occasion, will remain lying in their filth. We admit indeed that nothing should be so important to us that we deviate even slightly from the line prescribed to us by God; but we think we have briefly shown that if we reject from baptism those who are known to be members of the household of the Church, the prohibition will be too severe. Therefore, while a better progress is awaited, and discipline gains its force, let the infants be received under the condition we have stated, so that the sponsors promise that they will take care, with diligence and zeal, that their instruction is upright and sincere. Meanwhile, however, we do not deny that idolaters, whenever children are born to them, must be sharply admonished and urged to devote themselves truly to God, and excommunicated persons too, to reconcile themselves to the Church.

units.la: Monachis & sacrificulis victum ex publico non deberi certũ est, vt in otio inutiles degant. Si qui ergo apti sint ad ædificandam Ecclesiam, in partes laboris vocentur. Sed quia maiori ex parte indocti sunt, & omni dexteritate carent, humaniter cum illis videtur esse agendum. Nam etsi nullo iure exigere possunt alimenta, qui nullam Ecclesiæ operam impendunt: durum tamen esset, cum per inscitiam & errorem laqueos induerint, & partem ætatis consumpserint in desidia, eos spoliari. Monendi quidem sunt, vt iusto potius labore victum sibi quærant, quàm vt deuorent quod Ecclesiæ ministris & pauperibus est destinatum. Media etiam ratio tenenda, vt ex optimis sacerdotiis pars aliqua in sanctos vsus erogetur. Interim tamen dum sacras oblationes recuperet Ecclesia per illorum mortem non videtur de annuo redditu certandum: nisi quòd monendi essent, precario & tolerantia, nō approbatione ipsos retinere, quod nunquam iure acceptifunt. Hortandi etiā ne sibi nimium indulgeant, sed contenti frugali victu, restituant potius Ecclesiæ quod suû est, quàm eam sinant destitui fidis Pastoribus, vel sinant Pastores ipsos esurire. Vale eximie vir & frater nobis charissime. Totum piorum coetum cupimus salutari nostro nomine, Deúmq; precamur, vt vos omnes Spiritu suo vsque in finem gubernet, virtute sustineat, præsidio tueatur. Geneuæ, VII Novemb. M. D. LIX.
units.tr: It is certain that monks and little priests should not be supported from public funds so that they can live idle and useless. So if any of them are fit to build up the Church, let them be called to share in the work. But since most of them are unlearned and lack all skill, it seems we should deal with them humanely. For although they cannot claim maintenance by any right, since they render no service to the Church, it would still be harsh for them to be stripped of their support when, through ignorance and error, they have entangled themselves in these snares and spent part of their lives in idleness. They should indeed be urged to seek their living by honest labour rather than devour what has been set aside for the ministers of the Church and for the poor. A middle course should also be kept, so that some part of the better benefices is devoted to holy uses. Meanwhile, while the Church recovers the sacred offerings, there seems to be no need to contend over the annual income until these men die. Only they should be warned that they hold these revenues by sufferance and toleration, not by approval, since they never received them by right. They should also be exhorted not to indulge themselves too much, but to be content with a frugal diet, and to give back to the Church what is its own, rather than allow it to be left without faithful ministers, or allow the ministers themselves to go hungry. Farewell, outstanding man and brother most dear to us. We wish you to salute the whole company of the godly in our name, and we pray God that he may guide you all by his Spirit to the end, sustain you by his power, and keep you under his protection. Geneva, 7 November 1559.

units.la: COMITI IN TARNAVV IOANNES CALVINVS. S. D.
units.tr: TO COUNT IN TARNOW, JOHN CALVIN SENDS GREETINGS

units.la: Q Vando ex tuis literis, Generose & Illustris Domine, meum tibi in scribendo studium placuisse intelligo, hinc magis obstrictus videor ad te sedulò monendum, & huius quoque officij liberè præstandi mihi crescit fiducia. In hoc portò cardine vertitur quicquid mihi est cum Tua Excellentia disceptationis, quòd partium tuarum non esse existimas, quidquam tentare vel aggredi, vt repurgetur à sordibus Papatus Ecclesia Polonica. Nam pro tua æquitate non solum probas nostrum studium, quòd in curanda pietatis restitutione satagimus, sed agnoscis munus clamandi nobis esse iniunctum. Sed eadem necessitate officij te & alios regni Proceres constringi negas, quibus cura incumbit tuendæ publicæ tranquillitatis. Ego autem excipio, non minorem denuntiari pœnam surdis auditoribus, quàm mutis Prophetis: quia non vult Deus frustra clamore nostro aërem verberari, sed aures ferio feriri, & penitus affici corda. Proinde non minus ad agendum promptas vobis esse manus conuenit, quàm Deus linguas nostras ad docendum & hortandum expeditas esse iubet. Nam quòd obtendis, reipublicæ præsidibus quietem & pacem commendari, falleris fi vnum hoc onus tibi impositum esse putas. Audienda potius vox Pauli, Reges & Magistratus ritè tunc demum officio suo defungi, dum per eos nobis datur, tranquillam vitam agere cum omni pietate & honestate. Hæc quæ Deus sacro vinculo simul deuinxit, separare fas non effet. Quanquam tibi minimè concedo, vel conuelli regnorum statum, vel pacem turbari nostris actionibus. Dicrum etiam quod scribis, tot perturbationibus, quæ totum orbem intus & foris concutiunt, occasionem à Religione datam esse. Nam etsi inde ansum litigandi arripit multorum proteruia vel ambitio, alios contumacia & impietas ad digladiandum impellit: perperam tamen culpa in cœlestem doctrinam confertur: nec impune Deus tantam sibi contumeliam irrogari sinet, vt dum sibi homines reconcilians ad mutuam eos concordiam invitat, turbarum auctor censeatur. Atque vt cœlum terræ misceri contingat, merito tamen pluris esse nobis debet fyncerus rus Dei cultus, & sacrosancta eius veritas, in qua nobis reposita est æterna salus,quàm centum mundi.Quin pro sua ingratitudine & malitia tumultuentur multi,& sacrilego furore insurgant contra sanam doctrinam : quin professi etiam eius hostes vaesano impetu ad illius oppugnationem feruntur, non est nostrum præstare. Sed an ideo obmutescet Deus, quia loquenti ferociter maior pars obstrepit? Quod Deum precatus, ut te in hac caligine gubernet, atque illustret suo Spiritu, laudo:& verissimum esse fateor quod addis, nisi partes architecti suscipiat, irritos fore omnes omnium conatus. Sed non exigit Dei gratia, ut ignavi iaceant qui ad opus vocati sunt. Nam quòd facetè nostram fiduciam derides, quasi ad nos rapiamus Dei partes, dum corda hominum conuertere studemus, quæ in manu eius & arbitrio sunt: nihil hæc subsannatio cordatos Euangelij præcones mouebit, quibus probè & penitus infixa est sententia: bonum & suauem odorem esse ipsos Deo, sive mortem, sive vitam spirent. Verùm quidem esse fateor, non esse sperandum, ut toti mundo persuadeatur, quæ à nobis asseritur Religio: sed non obstitit mundi incredulitas & obstinatio Apostolis, quò minus in cursu vocationis suæ pergerent. Tenebant enim, quod pronuntiat vnus ex ipsis paratam esse horribilem vindictam contemptoribus, qui res- puerint oblatam gratiam. Quòd autem iocaris, verendum esse, ne qui cœlum duntaxat quærunt posthabita terra, simul vtrunque amittant, absit vt fidem Tuæ Excellentiæ potius habeam, quàm Filio Dei, qui iubet primum quærere Regnum Dei, & alia deinde accessura promittit. Metuere etiam te obtendis, ne populares vestros dissentionibus implices. Atqui iam dissentiunt, & palàm sua dissidia profitentur. Non igitur aliud superest remedium, quàm vt reconciliare ipsos studeas: quod fieri absque legitima cognitione non potest. Longius demum trahilis, & iniquè, (pace tua dixerim) non minus quàm odiose causam nostram grauas. Quorum certè criminum facilis promptaque esset defensio, si æquis auribus à Tua Celsitudine admitteretur. Nunquam enim vel disciplinam conuellere tentauimus, vel ordinis dissolutionem moliti sumus. Longè alio tendere nostra consilia, & studia multis experimentis planum est. Quòd sectas & hæreses hinc fluxisse dicis, cum Christo vnico iudice litiga, cùm exiguo post Euangelij promulgationem tempore subitò emerserint tam multi ac prodigiosi errores. Scripta obiicis acerbitatis plena, hostiles pugnas, contrarias opiniones. Optandum sanè esset, vt idem omnibus cor esset ac vna lingua. Sed quà lege postulas, vt hominum dissidia vel contentiones Dei veritatem aboleant? Mihi pugnandum fuit cum præstratis multis capitibus, & nunc quoque ito in eodem conflictu. Si piæ sanæque doctrinæ patro-
units.tr: Since I understand from your letter, Noble and Illustrious Lord, that my eagerness in writing to you has pleased you, I feel all the more bound to warn you earnestly, and my confidence in freely performing this duty grows. The whole of my disagreement with Your Excellency turns on this point: you think it is not your part to attempt or undertake anything to cleanse the Polish Church of the filth of Papistry. For in your fairness you not only approve our zeal in working to restore piety, but you also acknowledge that the task of crying out has been laid upon us. Yet you deny that you and the other nobles of the kingdom, to whom the care of preserving public peace falls, are bound by the same obligation of duty. I, however, reply that deaf hearers are threatened with no lesser punishment than dumb prophets, because God does not want our cry to beat the air in vain, but to strike the ears and deeply move the hearts. Therefore it is fitting that your hands be no less ready for action than God commands our tongues to be prepared for teaching and exhorting. As for your objection that rulers of the commonwealth are charged with keeping quiet and peace, you are mistaken if you think this burden has been laid on you alone. Rather, we should hear the voice of Paul, that kings and magistrates then fulfil their office rightly when through them we are granted to lead a quiet life in all godliness and honesty. What God has joined together by a sacred bond it would not be right to separate. Yet I by no means grant you that the state of kingdoms is overturned or peace disturbed by our actions. As to what you write, that the many disturbances which shake the whole world, at home and abroad, have been occasioned by religion, I say this: although the arrogance and ambition of many seize on this as a pretext for strife, and the obstinacy and impiety of others drive them to fight it out, the blame is wrongly laid on the heavenly doctrine. God will not allow such great insult to be done to himself, that while he reconciles men to himself and invites them to mutual concord, he should be thought the author of disturbances. And even if heaven should happen to be mingled with earth, the pure worship of God and his most holy truth, in which our eternal salvation is laid up, ought nonetheless to be worth more to us than a hundred worlds. As for many raging in their ungodliness and malice, and rising in sacrilegious fury against sound doctrine, and even those who profess it being carried with a frenzied assault against its overthrow, that is not for us to prevent. But will God therefore fall silent because the greater part of the people fiercely shout down the one who speaks? I praise you for praying God to guide you in this darkness and to enlighten you with his Spirit, and I acknowledge as most true what you add: unless he takes up the part of architect, all the efforts of all men will be in vain. But the grace of God does not require that those who have been called to the work should lie idle. For when you wittily mock our confidence, as if we were seizing God's part while we strive to convert the hearts of men, which lie in his hand and at his disposal, this scorn will not move the wise heralds of the gospel, who have deeply and thoroughly fixed in their minds that they are a good and sweet fragrance to God, whether they breathe out death or life. Indeed I admit it is true that we should not hope that the religion we assert will be persuaded to the whole world; but the unbelief and obstinacy of the world did not prevent the apostles from pressing on in the course of their calling. For they held to what one of them declares, that a dreadful vengeance is prepared for those who despise the grace offered to them. As for your joke that those who seek heaven alone, neglecting the earth, should be feared lest they lose both together, far be it from me to put more trust in Your Excellency's word than in the Son of God, who bids us seek first the kingdom of God and promises that other things will be added afterwards. You also plead that you fear lest you entangle your fellow countrymen in dissensions. Yet they already disagree, and openly profess their quarrels. Therefore no other remedy remains than that you should strive to reconcile them, which cannot be done without proper examination. Finally, you burden our cause at too great length and unjustly, (with your leave I say it) and not less than hatefully. The defence of these charges would certainly be easy and ready, if it were admitted by Your Highness with fair ears. For we have never attempted to overthrow discipline, nor have we aimed at dissolving order. That our plans and efforts tend in a very different direction is plain from many experiences. As for your claim that sects and heresies have flowed from this, you argue with Christ, the only judge, since within a short time after the promulgation of the gospel so many and such monstrous errors have suddenly arisen. You object to writings full of bitterness, hostile battles, and contrary opinions. Certainly it would be desirable that all have one heart and one tongue. But by what law do you demand that the disagreements or contentions of men should abolish the truth of God? I have had to fight against many heads of error at the same time, and I am still in the same conflict now. If it were right to abandon the defence of sound and pious doctrine, I would gladly rest; but when the glory of God is attacked together with the salvation of men, it is unjust that hatred should be stirred up against me for resisting.

units.la: G.j. cinium deferere fas esset,libenter quiescerem: sed vbi vnà cum hominum salute oppugnatur Dei gloria, ex repugnantia mihi inuidiam conflari,iniustum est.Quòd si quæ libet certamina defugere oportet, facessat Christus e medio, qui lapis est offensionis.Prudenter obseruare conuenit locorum & temporum circunstantias: modò ne vafrities locum prudentiæ obtineat. Quanquam vt cœlum terræ misceatur, nunquam Christo claudendæ sunt portæ, quin ad nos cum sacro Euangelij sceptro penetret. Ac valde miror,quum fatearis Principibus onus hoc incumbere, vt huic Summo Regi portas aperiant, subiicere quod ex diametro repugnat.Asperior forte stylus te offenderet,nisi Tua Celsitudo veniam necessitati daret. Vel tacendum mihi prorsus est, vel ingenuè scribendum quod sentio:quia nihil aliud mihi propositum est, quàm Tuæ Celsitudini prodesse. Negas tibi videri confultum de abolendis superstitionibus & restituendo vero Dei cultu agere: an tibi melius suppetere consilium, quàm ipsi Deo iudicas?Nec miror hominem prudentissimum & in maximis rebus exercitatum ita sentire & loqui:quoniam nulla deterior est pestis quàm humana ratio,quæ te certè nunc extra metas rapuit, vbi Deo consilium tuum opponere non dubitas. Quòd obiicis Deum forte nondum patefacere quid velit, quorsum spectet nō assequor:quando sic iam vobis illuxit Euangelij claritas,vt cæcutire in meridie non liceat. Equidem de syncericate animi tui longè aliud mihi persuadeo,quàm literæ tuæ sonant.Atque vtinam adhibitus amanuensis fuisset à Tua Excellentia,qui fideliter exciperet quæ visum fuisset dictare: quia Secretarius (vt video)mentem suam potius quàm tuam expressit.Pluribus itaque supersedere cogor, ne fines modestiæ excedere videar, si aulicæ ciuilitatis oblitus, ad multas profanas subsannationes veré, vt par est,respondeam.Quanquam autem adulari nescio,& ab officio meo alienislimum est: quum tamen infimæ plebis homines & rudissimos quosque placidè ferre didicerim,non tam sum rusticus vel morosus, vt posthabito Amplissimæ Tuæ dignitatis respectu,tam præcise agam. Sed veniam mihi dabit Tua Excellentia,si indignè fero sacrum Dei nomen,vnà cum studio Religionis per iocum & lusum traduci.Deum Patrem nostrum daturum mihi confido, vt quod ipse mandauit, neglecto mundi plausu & omnibus dicteriis valere iussis, quod iniunxit fideliter & constanter exequar:eúmque precabor,vt Tuam Excellentiam Illustris Domine, incolumem tueatur, Spiritu suo gubernet,omníque benedictione locupletet. Amen. x v. Nouembris.
units.tr: G.j. If it were permitted to desert the defence of sound and pious doctrine, I would gladly keep quiet; but when the glory of God is attacked together with the salvation of men, it is unjust that hatred should be kindled against me for resisting. If we must avoid whatever struggles, let Christ, who is the stone of stumbling, be removed from the midst. It is fitting to observe prudently the circumstances of places and times, provided craftiness does not take the place of prudence. Yet, although heaven should be mixed with earth, the gates must never be closed to Christ, so that he may not enter to us with the sacred sceptre of the gospel. And I am greatly surprised that, while you admit that the rulers bear this burden, that they should open the gates to this Supreme King, you put forward something that directly contradicts it. My style might perhaps offend you more harshly, were it not that your Highness pardons it for the sake of necessity. Either I must be silent altogether, or I must write frankly what I think, since my only aim is to be of service to your Highness. You say it does not seem to you advisable to deal with abolishing superstitions and restoring the true worship of God: do you think you have a better plan than God himself? I am not surprised that a man so wise and practised in great affairs thinks and speaks thus, since no worse plague exists than human reason, which has certainly now carried you beyond your limits, where you do not hesitate to set your counsel against God. As for your objection that God perhaps has not yet revealed what he wills, I do not grasp where it tends, since the clarity of the gospel has so shone upon you that it is not permitted to be blind at midday. Indeed, I am persuaded of the sincerity of your mind in quite another way than your letter sounds. And would that your Excellency had employed a scribe who would faithfully take down what you wished to dictate, for your secretary (as I see) expressed his own mind rather than yours. So I am compelled to pass over many things, lest I seem to exceed the bounds of modesty if, forgetting courtly civility, I answer truly and as is fitting the many profane jeers. Although I know not how to flatter, and it is most alien to my office, yet since I have learned to bear calmly the common folk and the rudest of men, I am not so rustic or peevish that I would act so bluntly without regard for the dignity of your most eminent position. But your Excellency will pardon me if I take it badly that the holy name of God and the cause of religion should be made a matter of jest and play. I trust that God our Father will grant me to follow faithfully and constantly what he has commanded, neglecting the applause of the world and bidding farewell to all abuse, and I will pray that he keep your Excellency, illustrious lord, safe, guide you by his Spirit and enrich you with every blessing. Amen. 15 November.

units.la: M. D. LIX.
Ioannes Caluinus tuus.
units.tr: John Calvin, yours.

units.la: IOAN.
units.tr: John.

units.la: Charitas Dei Patris, & Gratia Domini nostri Iesu Christi augeatur in dies in vobis per Spiritus sanctu communicationem.
units.tr: May the love of God the Father and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ increase in you day by day through the communion of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Benedictus Dominus, qui & suorum inter vos numerum in dies cumulatiorem reddit fratres dilectissimi, & vos ipsos in veritatis suę agnitione vti adeam prius vocare dignatus est, nunc etiam fouet, quantumuis Satan omnia moliatur & omnibus modis resistat, vt euertat aut interturbet opus salutis vestrę. Atque vt quod ita se bene habet, exultandi in Domino argumentum suppeditat, ita me in illo bona spes erigit, futurum vt qui tam liberaliter sua in vos dona effudit, largam illam manum faciè non subducat. Sic enim cogitandum est, nullum singularis & Paterni ipsius erga nos affectus testimonium certius extare, quàm dum Euangelij sui cognitionem nobis patefecit: quando istic natiua illius in Christo facies nobis apparet, vt côstet omnino nos ab ipso recipi in filios in Christi nomine, ac pro filiis etiam diligi. Atque illud tanto est admirabilius, quanto ab vna ipsius infinita bonitate proficiscitur, quum in nobis nihil aliud agnoscat, quàm egestatem ac miseriam, quæ nos illi potius exosos quàm acceptos redderet, nisi ex ipsa nostra infœlicitate occasionem miserricordiæ erga nos testificandæ desumeret. Mementote igitur, dilectissimi fratres, Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, ita vt ab initio mera Dei Patris gratia promissus fuit patribus, Patriarchis nempe atque vniuerso Israëli, vt nulla dignitas ex illorum parte hoc ipsis beneficium conciliaret: vt deinde vnius Patris misericordia morti addictus est, vt filios ipsius redimeret: eadem plane benignitate & misericordia nunc etiam in salutem vobis oblatum esse. Siquidem in nobis ipsis simul experimur omnes, vti Deus reipsa verum ostendat quod est apud Prophetam: quòd seipsum, nempe illis patefecerit, qui ipsum non quærebant: quòdque illis apparuerit, qui de eo non inquirerent. Eramus nempe vt oues palantes & disperse, quum bonus Pastor ille Patris mandato nos requisiuit, vt ad suum ouile adduceret. Recordamini etiam, quanta ex abyso emersetitis, vt ingrederemini in Regnum Dei: quibus ex tenebris eductì, vt ad ipsius lumen deduceremini: quadenique ex morte excitati, vt ab illo vocaremini ad spem vitæ. Agnoscite & illud ex eodem merę ipsius erga vos bonitatis fonte, quod nunc etiam faciat, vt in verbi ipsius obedientia perstetis. Quantulæ enim sunt vires nostræ, nisi sua vnius virtute nos ad plenum fulciret: Porro vsus istius ad vos meæ admonitionis duplex esse debebit. Primum quidem, vt ferio timore & humilitate decieđi, ac vobis plane diffidi vestrum omne præsidium & roburin illo vno repositum habeatis, attenti & vigiles in precibus & orationibus statis, ac semper vti in procinctu aduersusSatanam stetis, ipsiúsq; vnius virtute sitis instructi, qui potens est vt victores tandem præstet. Alterum deinde coniunctum esse oportet,nimirum vt huius doctrinæ perceptio,vos etiá ad optimum illum Patrem tanto impensius deamádum accendat,quanto ipsius erga vos amor omnem alium amorem superat,éstque plane incomparabilis,ne vestra ingratitudine beneficiorum ipsius erga vos tenorem interuertatis. Plane enim aut ipsius vocationi respondere nos par & æquum est, aut ab ipso deserendi atque reiiciendi sumus,vt insigne vindictæ ipsius exéplar exterin nostram ingratitudinem, & tantæ gratiæ contemptum. Quare vestrum est operádare, dilectissimi fratres,vt tum sermone tum factis doceatis,vos ad filiorum Dei numerum pertinere. Scio quòd ad Christianismi confessionem,in quibus angustiis versemini. Neque ita inhumanus sum,quin periculorum vestrorum consideratio me quoque ad habendam infirmitatis vestræ rationem adducat: quum palam non profitemini, quod à Domino de ipsius Euangelio acceptum tenetis.Sed tamen nul lius periculi metus ab officio vos excusatos reddat,quin det operam vnusquisque pro sua virili,& pro oblata occasione,vt ædificando proximo se impédat.De doctrina hoc intelligo. Videndum etiam vt hoc prudenter fiat, ac dispiciatur quando & quatenus. Prudentiam autem requiro,quæ carnem & mūdum non sapiat, vt quæ vos impelleret potius ad lucem ipsam suffocandam, quàm ad periculum non detrectandum pro Dei gloria, & proximi perignorantiam errantis salute. Sic enim prudentiam interpretarur plerique,vt sepeliant Christum ipsum,ne in mundi odium incidant. Quando autem illa non est ferenda peruersitas,vbi nos ita respicimus, vt anteponamus aut etiam compa remus nostram tranquillitatem cum summo illo officio, quo Deo vni ante omnia obstricti tenemur,vestrùm est dilectiss.fratres,Spiritum discretionis ab illo postulare,quo præditi apposite vtriusque temporis,tum loquendi,tum etiam tacendi delectum habeatis. Atque hic etiam imprimis cauédum est,ne quidquam proferatis curiositate quadam,aut ambitione,aut etiam leuitate impulsi,sed maturè perpensa demum,& quæ à syncero proficiedi affectu prodeunt. Illud igitur ex omnibus à vobis audiatur, quod plurimùm ad ædificationem collaturum videbitur. Ac si quid inde periculi vobis creandum sit, accingite vos multò ante,& ad illud confirmate,ne impares sitis ad tentationes eluctádas, quæ vobis intenduntur, vt ad defectionem impellant. Meministis ministis vero quid nonnullis acciderit, qui non mediocre periculum adierunt, multúmque vexationis pertulerunt: quos tamen Dominus ita eripuit, vt exitus longe optatior affulserit quàm sperare ausi fuissis. Nunc de vobis comperti nihil habemus: adeóque valde solliciti & anxij sumus, dum expectamus quem exitum dederit Dominus persecutioni quæ istic accens est. Atqui quèadmodum bonus Dominus suis semper se affuturum pollicitus est, vtque illud reipsa præstitit: erga omnes qui ipsum invocarunt, nolite dubitare quin proximus vobis etiam futurus sit in posterum, tum vt opem & auxilium ferat, tum vt aduersariorum rabiem comprimat, ne quicquid audeant, reipsa exequantur. Atq; vt ea esset voluntas ipsius, vt ipsis per illum liceret furorem in vos suum aliquatenus cuomere, vt vestra tolerantia ita adexamen vocetur, non ideo ab officio deflectere, aut retro pedem ferre fas esset. Satis enim esse debet, quòd Dominus in mediis malis & tribulationibus seipsum nobis consolatorem interponat.
units.tr: Blessed be the Lord, dearest brothers, who has deigned first to call you into the knowledge of his truth, and who now also cherishes you, though Satan strives by every means and resists in every way to overturn or disturb the work of your salvation. Just as your present good state gives me cause to rejoice in the Lord, so a sure hope raises me up in him, that he who has so generously poured out his gifts upon you will not withdraw his open hand. For we must think that there is no more certain witness of his singular and fatherly affection toward us than when he reveals to us the knowledge of his Gospel, when his native face shines forth to us in Christ, so that it is entirely plain that we are received by him as sons in the name of Christ and are also loved as sons. And this is all the more wonderful because it proceeds from his sheer infinite goodness, since he finds in us nothing but need and misery, which would make us hateful rather than acceptable to him, unless he took from our very unhappiness an occasion to show his mercy toward us. Remember therefore, dearest brothers, that our Lord Jesus Christ was promised from the beginning by the pure grace of God to the fathers, namely the patriarchs and all Israel, so that no worthiness on their part won this benefit for them; that he was then given over to death by the mercy of the one Father to redeem his sons; and that in exactly the same kindness and mercy the salvation has now been offered to you. For we all experience at the same time in ourselves how God in fact shows the truth of what is said by the Prophet: that he revealed himself to those who did not seek him, and appeared to those who did not inquire after him. For we were like wandering and scattered sheep, when that good Shepherd, by the Father's command, sought us out to bring us to his fold. Remember also how you emerged from the abyss to enter the Kingdom of God; how you were led out of darkness to be brought to his light; and how you were finally raised from death to be called by him to the hope of life. Acknowledge also, from the same fountain of his pure goodness toward you, that he now also makes you persevere in obedience to his word. For how slight our strength is, unless he supported us fully by his power alone! Moreover, my admonition should be of twofold use to you. First, that, humbled with a serious fear and humility and wholly distrustful of yourselves, you may place all your protection and strength in him alone, standing watchful and alert in prayers and supplications, and always standing as if in battle array against Satan, armed by his virtue alone, who is able at last to make you victors. Second, this must be joined to it: that the grasp of this doctrine should kindle you to love that best Father all the more earnestly, as his love for you surpasses every other love and is altogether incomparable, lest by your ingratitude you overturn the course of his benefits toward you. For it is plainly right and fitting either that we answer his calling or that we be forsaken and rejected by him, as a notable example of his vengeance upon our ingratitude and contempt of so great grace. Therefore it is your task, dearest brothers, to show by word and by deeds that you belong to the number of the sons of God. I know in what distresses you are placed on account of your confession of Christianity. Nor am I so inhuman that the consideration of your dangers does not also lead me to take account of your weakness, since you do not openly profess what you have received from the Lord concerning his Gospel. Yet let no fear of danger excuse anyone from duty, but let each one, according to his strength and the opportunity offered, take pains to edify his neighbour. I mean this concerning doctrine. It must also be seen that it is done prudently, and that it is weighed when and how far it should go. But I require a prudence which does not savour of the flesh and the world, lest it urge you rather to suffocate the very light than not to shun danger for the glory of God and the salvation of a neighbour who is erring in ignorance. For most people interpret prudence in this way, so that they bury Christ himself lest they fall into the hatred of the world. But when that perversity is not to be borne, namely when we so regard ourselves that we prefer our tranquillity to, or even weigh it against, that supreme duty by which we are bound above all to the one God, it is your task, dearest brothers, to ask of him the Spirit of discernment, by which, endowed with it, you may make a fitting choice of both speaking and keeping silence according to the time. And here above all care must be taken that you put forward nothing driven by a certain curiosity, or ambition, or even levity, but only what has been weighed carefully beforehand and comes from sincere affection. Let that be what you say above all, which will seem most likely to contribute to edification. And if any danger is to be incurred from it, gird yourselves well beforehand and strengthen yourselves for it, lest you be unequal to resisting the temptations aimed at you to drive you to apostasy. Remember indeed what happened to some who faced no small danger and endured much vexation, whom nevertheless the Lord so rescued that a far more desirable outcome shone forth than you had dared to hope. Now we have no certain news of you, and therefore we are very anxious and troubled while we await what outcome the Lord will give to the persecution kindled there. Yet, just as the good Lord has always promised to be present with his own and has truly done so toward all who called upon him, do not doubt that he will be near you in the future too, both to bring help and aid and to restrain the rage of the adversaries, so that they do not carry out in deed whatever they dare. And even if it were his will that they should be permitted by him to vent their fury upon you to some extent, so that your endurance is thus brought to the test, it would not be right to turn aside from duty or draw back a step on that account. For it should be enough that the Lord interposes himself as our consoler amid evils and tribulations.

units.la: Meditemini igitur tot támque insignes Scripturæ locos, quibus officij ratio præscribitur: atque eorum meditationem pro exercitatione ordinaria vobis constituite: vt pote quibus confirmandi simus ad illa omnia subeunda, quæ nobis inferentur propter verbum Dei. Sic inquam, Scripturam præ manibus habete, vt si tim memoriæ occurrat, atque ipsa necessitas tulerit. Illud enim plus quàm indignum est, si vt mortem corporea euitemus, cùm vult Dominus constantiæ nostræ facere periculum, Dei veritatem abnegemus, in qua vna vita nobis reposita erat. Accipiamus vero hoc vt videbitur. manet tamen illud Domini verbum ir-refixum, Quis me, inquit, abnegauerit coram hominibus, ego vi-cissim abnegabo ipsum coram Patre meo. Væ illis igitur qui sibi imponent, atque in re tanti momenti sibi blandientur. Attendite etiam ne commodi quæstúsvetemporalis causa vos auertat, quò minus vos ipsos ad optimum Seruatorem adiungatis, atque re ipsa vos ad illum pertinere ostendatis. Nostis quid de ipso testati sint Pharisæorum & Scribarum ministri, cùm ad ipsum comprehendendum missi essent, nunquam àse auditum hominem qui perinde loqueretur. Agnoscùt nempe pro supra humana doctrinam Christi. Sed affectus illi perditus agendi in otio, atque loci sui retinendi, ministros per p-tuos reddit aduersariorum tum Christi, tum etiam doctrinæ ipsius.Quare dilectissimi fratres, ne ad istiusmodi exemplum vllo modo accedite. Neque etiam Esaum sequimini, quem pro vili offula ius primogenitorum vendidisse scimus. Vere enim nihil aliud est quàm offula, quicquid ad corpus pertinet, præ vna adoptionis gratia, quæ piis offertur singulariter. Quare ne ita defixi simus in ea quæ nullius sunt momenti, vt obliuiscamur cœlestis illius hæreditatis vnicè in-
units.tr: Meditate therefore on so many and such notable passages of Scripture in which the rule of duty is prescribed, and make their meditation a regular exercise for yourselves, since they are the means by which we are strengthened to endure all that is inflicted on us for the sake of the Word of God. Keep Scripture in hand, I say, so that it may come to mind when need itself requires. For it would be more than shameful, if to avoid bodily death, when the Lord wishes to test our constancy, we were to deny the truth of God, in which alone life was laid up for us. Let us take this as it may appear, but the word of the Lord remains fixed: "Whoever denies me before men, I in turn will deny him before my Father." Woe therefore to those who deceive themselves and flatter themselves in a matter of such great moment. Take care also that the desire for temporal gain does not turn you away from joining yourselves to the best Saviour, and from showing by your deeds that you belong to him. You know what the officers of the Pharisees and scribes testified about him when they had been sent to arrest him: that no man had ever spoken like this. They recognised, of course, the doctrine of Christ as more than human. But that perverse desire of acting at ease and keeping their own position made them continual servants of the adversaries, both of Christ and of his doctrine. Therefore, dearest brothers, do not in any way approach such an example. Nor should you follow Esau, whom we know sold his birthright for a paltry morsel. For truly everything that pertains to the body is nothing but a morsel, when set against the one grace of adoption which is offered singularly to the pious. Therefore let us not be so fixed on things of no moment that we forget that heavenly inheritance which is offered by the Lord alone.

units.la: Ioan.7.46 comparabilis, quæ à Domino offertur. Iam si aduersus tentationes quæ corpus petūt, præsidia vobis comparanda sunt, haud minus vero de illis etiam eluctandis cogitādum est, quas Satan fallis doctrinis inuehendis inferre conatur. Non frustra nempe tum homicida, tum pater mendacii nominatur. Vos ipsi experiendo discetis. Nunc enim totus in eo est, ut in persecutione quam per instrumenta ad illud appositā intendit, ad Christum eiurandum vos cogat: nunc nescio quos cauponatores excitat, qui totam Euangelii puritatem inuertunt, ut vos seducant, & à via omnino abducant. Et prior illa impressio à persecutionibus suam asperitatem habet, aduersus quam Dei manus vna potest nos confirmare, ne illarum impetu abrepti deficiamus. Atqui lögè pernicio fior est tentatio, vbi aduersarius inspergit zizania tritico, vt plane corrumpat. Illud enim est belli latentis genus, & quod cuniculis sub terra geritur, vt nisi serio nobis attendimus, incogitantes circumcipiamur. Cum autem nullum praeux doctrinæ genus non sit venenatissimum, vix tamen aliud ei comparari poterit, quo vestram regionem inhalauit Satan. Infamem & execrādam illam Libertinorum sectam intelligo, qui Spiritualium nomen sibi affingunt. Accertissimum illud est exundantis in mundum furoris Dei flagellum, cum eoúsque Satanæ habenas laxat, vt tam detestanda quæ illic habentur, Christianis persuadeat, quæ profanis ipsis vel audita horrorem incuterent.
