units.la: Surrexit Admiraldus praeter omnium expectationem, ac libellum supplicem Regi porrexit, in quo postulabant, qui cupiunt in Normania Deum pure colere, ut sibi liceret interdiu conuenire, ne obnoxij essent variis calumniis ob clandestinos vel nocturnos conuentus. Rogatus vnde haberet, respondit publico bono se fuisse curiosum, ut propius sciret quid quaererent Lutherani. Esse autem homines ad quinquaginta millia, quorum subscriptionem afferrent, si Regi placeret. Duo in toto consessu cordate loquuti sunt, ipse, & Archiepiscopus Viennensis. Omnibus auditis, quorum melior pars e pedariis constabat, Dux Guisianus licentiose cuomuit, quod alibi esset intolerabile. Specimen stoliditatis accipe in vno verbo. Quum dixisset Admiraldus, Barbarū morem non placere, vt Rex nō modo corporis custodes habeat, sed cingatur exercitu: neque hac educationem dignam esse Gallia, neque adolescentem Regem ita instituendum, vt sibi metuaret a suis, quos beneuolentia retinere fouereque potius deberet. Ille Regem non opus habere nutritiis vel educatoribus respondit, vtpote qui educatus in plenitudine virtutis foret: (verba refero & syllabas) quod si erudiendus esset, matrem eius ad has partes sufficere. Ausus est etiam dicere, quicquid decerneret millo Concilia, sibi fixum esse maiorum institutā sequi. Frater Cardinalis grauius & acutius: frustra peti a Conciliis vllam in doctrina mutationem. Neq; enim fas esse, quae prius a Spiritu sancto profecta sunt, in controuersiam vocare. Si qua essent in moribus vitia, permittendum esse Episcopis, vt vltro corrigerent. Pupugerat eum Viennensis qui dixerat hoc turpe & pudendum esse confusionis signum, quod Episcopi religiis Ecclesiis aulas Principum sequerentur: & vehementer Regem obtestatus fuerat, ne Pastoribus boni publici vano praetextu Ecclesias orbaret. Hinc illud, vt nemo lege vel necessitate obstringeretur: sed quisque sponte quod liberet. Quaeris quis exitus? Viennensis domum se recepit. Postquam quatuor aut quinque dies absumpti sunt vanis consultationibus, Statuum conuentus indictus est in mensem Decembris. Episcopi vocati ad vigesimum Ianuarij, non vt quicquam decernant, sed agitent quid sit in Concilio proponendum. Ne ordinum conuentus fieret, pertinaciter hactenus pugnauerant. Nunc collectis animis rationem excogitarunt, quibus facete eludant qui sperabant aliquid leuationis. Exceptio enim addita est, vt singulae prouinciae dispiciant coram suis Praefectis, de quibus negotiis tractari expediat. Hic vero nulla libertas: deinde vt suos legatos eligant iisdem Praefectis arbitris. Venient ergo empti adulatores, quos N. nominare placuerit. Concilij autem quam friuola sit & nugatoria ostentatio, ex formula edicti intelliges, quam tibi interpretabitur quispiam ex amicis. Interea erumpit EuanEuangelij veritas. In Normania palàm iam concionatur fratres nostri: quia tria & quatuor millia hominum non capiunt ædes priuatæ.Apud Pictones & Xantones,in tota Aquitania maior li-bertas.Regio linguæ Occitanæ,Prouincia,Delphinatus intrepi-dos habet multos Christi discipulos. Cur cesset Cardinalis, non obscure professus est: detegendam esse scilicet amentium impu-dentiam breui tempore. Verùm Dominus,vt spero,non modo sceleratas eius cogitationes producet in lucem,sed etiam impios conatus dissipabit.Quòd puerorum qui istuc erudiendi mittun-tur,curam suscipere grauati nonestis,vt idoneos magistros nā-cifcerentur,& in familiis bene moratis agerent:Senatus pro hoc tam propenso studio quas potest vobis maximas gratias agit, mutuam vicem libenter repensurus, si quando dabitur occasio. Præter quatuor qui ex publico aluntur, priuatim etiam mittun-tur quidam alij, quos non minus commendatos vobis esse cu-pio. Trium nomine rogatus sum Sed quia duobus iam certum esse hospitium audio, vt tertio prospiciatur magnopere cupio: quia & mater singulari pietate est prædita, & pater familiaris & charus mihi fuit.Ignosce si precibus victus,plus tibi quàm velim molestiæ iniungam.Vale clarissime vir,& mihi imprimis hono-rande frater. Salutem plurimam dices fratribus & Collegis tuis, & reliquis amicis. Dominus vos omnes semper incolumes ser-uet,Spiritu suo regat,& labores vestros benedicat. Geneuæ,Ca-lendis Octob. M. D. LX.
units.tr: The Admiral rose beyond everyone's expectation and handed the King a supplication, in which those who desire to worship God purely in Normandy asked that they be allowed to meet openly by day, so that they would not be exposed to various slanders because of secret or nocturnal meetings. Asked where he had got it, he replied that he had been curious about the public good, so as to learn more closely what the Lutherans were seeking; and that there were some fifty thousand people who would bring their signatures, if it pleased the King. In the whole assembly only two spoke sensibly, he himself and the Archbishop of Vienne. When everything had been heard, most of which came from the rank and file, the Duke of Guise ranted without restraint, which would have been intolerable anywhere else. Take one word as an example of his stupidity. When the Admiral said that the barbarous custom was not pleasing, namely that the King should not only have bodyguards but be surrounded by an army; that this was neither a training worthy of France, nor a way to bring up a young King so that he would fear his own people, whom he ought rather to keep and cherish by goodwill, the Duke replied that the King had no need of nurses or tutors, since he had been brought up to the full measure of virtue (I report the words and syllables); and that if he needed to be taught, his mother was sufficient for that role. He even dared to say that whatever the councils decreed, it was settled for him to follow the institutions of his ancestors. The Cardinal, his brother, spoke more gravely and sharply: that it was vain to ask the councils for any change in doctrine; for it was not right to call into question what had first come from the Holy Spirit. If there were any faults in morals, the bishops should be left to correct them of their own accord. The Vienne man had pricked him by saying that it was a shameful and disgraceful sign of confusion that bishops should follow the courts of princes rather than their churches; and he had earnestly begged the King not to strip the churches of their ministers under the empty pretext of the public good. Hence that proposal, that no one should be bound by law or necessity, but each should do freely what he pleases. You ask what the outcome was? The Vienne man withdrew home. After four or five days had been spent in empty consultations, a meeting of the Estates was announced for December. The bishops were summoned for 20 January, not to decide anything, but to discuss what should be proposed to the Council. They had stubbornly resisted holding an assembly of the orders until now. Now, with their minds gathered, they have devised a plan by which they may cleverly mock those who hoped for some relief. For an exception has been added, that each province is to consider, before its own governors, what matters it is expedient to treat. Here, however, there is no freedom; and then that they choose their own delegates, with the same governors as judges. So bought flatterers will come, whom it pleases N. to name. You will understand from the wording of the edict how frivolous and trifling this display of the Council is, which some friend of yours will explain to you. Meanwhile the truth of the Gospel is breaking out. In Normandy our brothers now preach openly, because private houses cannot hold three or four thousand people. Among the Poitevins and Saintongeais, in all of Aquitaine, there is greater freedom. The region of the Occitan tongue, Provence and Dauphiné have many fearless disciples of Christ. Why the Cardinal delays he has not hidden: namely that the impudence of madmen must be exposed within a short time. But the Lord, as I hope, will not only bring their wicked schemes to light, but will also scatter their impious attempts. As to your taking up the care of the boys who are sent there for training, so that they may find suitable teachers and live in well-ordered households, the Senate, for this so willing service, gives you the greatest thanks it can, ready to return the favour in turn whenever an occasion is given. Besides the four who are supported at public expense, some others are also sent privately, whom I wish to be commended to you no less. I was asked on behalf of three; but since I hear that two already have lodging arranged, I very much wish that provision be made for the third, because his mother is endowed with singular piety, and his father was a familiar and dear friend of mine. Forgive me if, won over by prayers, I impose on you more trouble than I would like. Farewell, most distinguished man and brother, to be honoured above all. Give my many greetings to your brothers and colleagues, and to the rest of our friends. May the Lord keep you all always safe, guide you by his Spirit, and bless your labours. Geneva, 1 October 1560.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO HIS LORD AND SON (N. S.), GREETING

units.la: Quod te vltimo congressu minus hilariter accepi,neque fa-ftidio,neque contemptu factum est : sed quia nolebam a-liud simulare,quàm esset in animo. Audieram certè, vt tu suspicaris, aliqua de te vel sinistra,vel quæ non placerent. Con-strictus ergo quadam anxietate tenebar,quò minus liberè atque aperte sensus meos tibi exponerem.Si nimis credulum me fuisse putas,quia non prorsus contempserim quod erat probabile:sci-to alios rursum de mea tarditate conqueri, dum fidem non ha-beo quibuslibet sermonibus. Si te meo præiudicio damnassem, re nondum bene comperta,fuisset iniquus,fateor. Verùm re-puere quicquid defertur,& piorum virorum iudicia floccipende re, superbæ morositatis esset. Ego verò neque tibi iniuriam fa-cere volui,nimis facile credendo quod audieram: & tamen pu-taui non de nihilo esse dictum. Iam hucspectare visus est totus sermo,quem apud me habebas,vt tibi gratularer.Non poteram, quia res non fercbat:neq; tamen volebam,si fuisset magis præ-cifus,te offendere,ne ad officium segnior aut frigidior esses.Fuit igitur & suspensa oratio mea,& vultus,vt ita loquar,medius:qui neque signum daret odij vel receptionis,neque fatis eff texporre &us: quia fi actiones tuas omnes praeme tulissem mihi probari, fucus & simulatio fuisset. Quanquam non hae tantum rationes perplexum me tenebant, sed magis labyrinthi vestri horror. Nam dum video ad fanandas vestras miserias,vel saltem leuan das nihil esse in me remedij,non libenter admitto earum narra tionem,doloris & tædij plenam.Hoc idem experti sunt alij quo que pij fratres:in quibus etsi aliquid defidero,non tamen desino amare: quia ignosco eorum infirmitati. Sic ergo tibi persuade, quanuis in te & similibus correcta cupiam quaedam, me tamen fraternam coniunctionem vobiscum fouere. Quo magis tibi & illis displicebit tristis status vestri confusio, eo magis mihi placebitis. Vale,Dominus tibi semper adsit, gubernet te Spiritu suo,& cum familia benedicat. Geneuae,xiii.Octobris. M. D. LX.
units.tr: That I received you less cheerfully at our last meeting was not due to disdain or contempt, but because I did not want to pretend anything other than what was in my mind. I had indeed heard, as you suspect, some things about you that were either unfavourable or not to my liking. Held back by a certain anxiety, I therefore hesitated to lay out my feelings to you freely and openly. If you think I was too credulous because I did not entirely disregard what was plausible, I know that others again complain of my slowness, since I do not believe every kind of report. If I had condemned you on my prejudgment, before the matter was well established, I would have been unjust, I admit. But to reject whatever is reported and to think lightly of the judgments of godly men would be the mark of a proud peevishness. Indeed I did not wish to wrong you by believing too readily what I had heard; yet I thought it was not said for nothing. Moreover, the whole discourse you were holding with me seemed to aim at my congratulating you, and I could not do so, because the matter would not bear it; yet I did not want, even if it had been put more plainly, to offend you, lest you should become more sluggish or cooler in your duty. So my speech and my countenance were, if I may put it so, neutral: they gave no sign of either hostility or welcome, yet they did not sufficiently expose my mind, for if I had professed approval of all your actions, it would have been pretence and feigning. Yet it was not only these considerations that held me in perplexity, but still more the horror of your labyrinth. For while I see that there is no remedy in me for healing your miseries, or at least for easing them, I do not gladly admit the account of them, which is full of grief and weariness. Other godly brothers have had the same experience, and in them, although I miss something, I do not cease to love them, because I pardon their weakness. So be persuaded that, although in you and others like you I desire certain things to be corrected, I nonetheless cherish our brotherly fellowship with you. The more the confusion of your sad state displeases you and them, the more it will please me that you are such. Farewell; may the Lord always be with you, govern you by his Spirit, and bless you with your household. Geneva, 13th October 1560.

units.la: IOAN. CALVINVS GASPARI OLEVIANO. S. D.
units.tr: John Calvin to Gaspar Olevian, greetings

units.la: ETsi alius disputationis apud vos habitae exitus nobis optan dus erat:quod tamen totam rei summam distincte mihi ex ponere grauatus non es,optime Gaspar,grata mihi diligentia tua fuit.Vtinam hoc saltem experimento discat ille aliquid ex confidentia, qua nimis turget,remittere. Petrum Martyrem hortatus sum,fi ab illustrissimo Principe vocetur,vt non modo ad suscipiendam prouinciam voluntarius fit,sed Collegis etiam persuadeat ita expedire. Quam laboriosum munus tu sustineas, video: fructus tamen laboris adeoque necessiras ad strenue pergendum te excitare debet.Accedit alter stimulus ex eorum pertinacia,qui nihil omittunt ad turbandum. Quod spes aliqua instituendae disciplinae vobis ostenditur,valde gaudeo.Si quid forte adiumenti adferat gubernationis ratio quam hic tenemus, summam eius complexus sum.
units.tr: Although the outcome of the disputation held among you was not what we had hoped for, you, best Gaspar, were not reluctant to set out the whole sum of the matter clearly for me, and your diligence pleased me. I only wish this experience might at least teach that man to lessen somewhat the overweening confidence in which he swells. I have urged Peter Martyr, if the most illustrious Prince calls him, not only to take up the charge willingly but also to persuade his colleagues that this is expedient. I see how laborious a duty you are undertaking. Yet the fruit of your labour, and the necessity itself, ought to spur you on to press forward vigorously. There is a further goad in the obstinacy of those who leave nothing undone to cause trouble. I rejoice greatly that some hope of establishing discipline is being held out to you. If the method of government we follow here brings any help, I have summarised its substance.

units.la: Primum eligutur Ministri a nostro Collegio:ac datur illis Scripturae locus, in cuius interpretatione specimen suae dexteritatis edat.Deinde examē habetur de praecipuis doctrinae capitibus:tandem coram nobis perinde vt apud populū cocionatur.Adsunt etiam duo ex Senatu. Si probatur eorum eruditio,eos Senatui cum testimonio offerimus:in cuius arbitrio est non admittere,si minus idoneos iudicet. Quod si recipiuntur (vt semper hactenus cōtigit) tum nomina promulgamus coram populo,vt si quod vitium latu erit,liberū sit singulis ante octo dies indicare. Qui tacitis omnium suffragiis probantur,eos commendamus Deo & Ecclesiae. Infantes non baptizamus, nisi pro publica concione: quia absurdum videtur, vt solennis illa receptio paucos tantum habeat testes. Patres nisi quid negotij impediat, iubentur adesse, vt stipulationi respondeant vna cum fideiussoribus. Nemo tamen ad fideiubendum admittitur, nisi qui eiusdem nobiscum est professionis. Arcentur & excommunicati ab hoc honore.
units.tr: First, ministers are chosen by our College, and they are given a passage of Scripture in whose interpretation they display a sample of their skill. Then an examination is held on the chief heads of doctrine. Finally, they preach before us just as they would before the people. Two members of the Senate are also present. If their learning is approved, we present them to the Senate with a testimony, and it is for the Senate to decide whether to admit them, if it judges them less suitable. If they are accepted (as has always happened hitherto), we then publish their names before the people, so that if any fault has come to light, each person is free to point it out within eight days. Those who are approved by the silent assent of all, we commend to God and the Church. We do not baptise infants except at the public sermon, because it seems absurd for such a solemn reception to have only a few witnesses. The fathers are ordered to be present, unless some business prevents them, to answer the undertaking together with the sureties. Yet no one is admitted to stand surety unless he belongs to the same profession of faith as we do. The excommunicated are also barred from this honour.

units.la: Nemini ante ad sacram Christi Coenam patet accessus, quàm fidem suam professus sit. In eum finem quotànis habentur quatuor examina, vbi interrogantur pueri, ac de profectu cuiusque cognoscitur. Nam etsi singulis diebus Domini cis in Catechismo iam incipiunt aliquod testimonium dare: donec tamen cognitum fuerit Ministri iudicio mediocriter in summa Religionis profecisse, ad sacram mensam accedere non licet. Quod ad maiores natu spectat, à nobis quotannis repetitur inspectio cuiusque familiae. Distribuimus inter nos vrbis regiones, vt ordine singulas decurias excutere liceat. Adest Ministro comes vnus ex Senioribus. Illic noui incolae examinantur. Qui semel recepti sunt, omittuntur: nisi quòd inquiritur sine domus pacata, & rectè composita, num liTes cum vicinis, num qua ebrietas, num pigri sint & ignaui ad concionesfrequentandas.
units.tr: No one has access to the holy Supper of Christ until he has professed his faith. To that end, four examinations are held each year, at which boys are questioned and each one's progress is assessed. For although on each Lord's day they already begin to give some account from the Catechism, yet until it is known by the minister's judgment that they have made moderate progress in the sum of religion, they are not permitted to approach the holy table. As for those of riper age, we repeat an inspection of each household every year. We divide the districts of the city among ourselves, so that each group of ten may be examined in turn. One elder accompanies the minister. There the new inhabitants are examined. Those who have once been received are passed over, except that it is enquired whether the household is peaceful and well ordered, whether there are quarrels with neighbours, whether there is any drunkenness, and whether any are lazy and idle about attending the sermons.

units.la: In censuris obseruatur haec ratio. Deliguntur quotannis duodecim Seniores: nempe ex minore Senatu duo reliqui ex Ducentis, siue sint indigenae, siue ascripitij ciues. Qui probè & fideliter munere suo perfuncti sunt, loco non mouentur: nisi forte eos occupet alia cura Reipublicae. Antequam ab electione sua sedeant, eorum nomina publicè eduntur, vt si quis eos indignos cognouerit, maturè denuntiet.
units.tr: In the censures, the following method is observed. Twelve elders are chosen each year: namely two from the lesser Senate, and the rest from the Two Hundred, whether they are natives or naturalised citizens. Those who have discharged their office uprightly and faithfully are not removed from their place, unless some other concern of the commonwealth occupies them. Before they take their seats after election, their names are published publicly, so that if anyone knows them to be unworthy, he may denounce them in good time.

units.la: Ad iudicium Ecclesiasticum nemo citatur, nisi ex communi omnium sententia. Itaque rogantur singuli, num quid velint in medium afferre. Nemo autem citatur, nisi qui vel priuatis admonitionibus non obtemperauit, vel qui Ecclesiam offendit malo exemplo. Ita blasphemi, ebriosi, scortatores, percussores, rixosi, saltatores, qui choreas ducunt, & similes vocatur. Qui leuius deliquit, humanis verbis castigatus dimittitur. Grauiorib9 peccatis animaduersio sequitur. Eos enim Minister excommunicat, saltem ad breue tempus. Ex cluduntur autem à Coena, donec veniam petierint idem Minister Ecclesiae reconciliet. Si quis praefracte auctoritate Ecclesiae sperna, nisi ante elapsum annum à contumacia destiterit, à Senatu in exilium annuum eiicitur. Siquis etiam proterujus fuerat, Senatus cautam suscipit, & animaduertit. Qui redimédq vitae causa apud Pa-pistas abiurarunt Euangelij doctrinam, vel Missis interfuerunt, iubentur se coram Ecclesia sistere. Minister illic rem exponit pro suggestu: tu qui excommunicatus fuit, procidit in genua & supplicer veniam postulat. Ea autem est Cōsiliorum ratio, vt ciuilis iurisdictio... dictionis cursum nihil moretur. Ac ne plebs queratur de immodico rigore, non tantum iisdem poenis subiacent Ministri, sed si quid excommunicatione dignum admiserint, simul etiam abdicantur.
units.tr: No one is summoned to the Church's judgment except by the common consent of all. Therefore each is asked whether he wishes to bring anything forward. No one, however, is summoned unless he has not obeyed private admonitions, or has offended the Church by a bad example. Thus blasphemers, drunkards, fornicators, murderers, brawlers, dancers who lead the dances, and the like are summoned. One who has sinned more lightly is rebuked with kindly words and dismissed. More serious sins are followed by punishment. For the minister excommunicates such people, at least for a short time. They are shut out from the Supper until they have sought pardon, and the same minister reconciles them to the Church. If anyone stubbornly scorns the authority of the Church, and does not desist from his contumacy within a year, the Senate banishes him for a year. If someone has been even more shameless, the Senate takes him into custody and punishes him. Those who, to save their lives, have among the Papists abjured the doctrine of the Gospel, or have been present at the Masses, are ordered to present themselves before the Church. There the minister sets out the matter from the pulpit, and the one who was excommunicated falls on his knees and asks pardon. This is the plan of the counsels: that civil jurisdiction is in no way delayed in its course. And lest the common people complain of excessive severity, not only are the ministers subject to the same penalties, but if they have committed anything deserving excommunication, they are at the same time removed from office.

units.la: Compendium hoc satis putaui fore, ex quo formam aliquam conciperes, quam praescribere non debui. Tu quod putabis vtile isticfore, modeste suggeres, vt boni & prudentes viri, quibus moneri graue non erit, dispiciant quid sit factu optimum. Dominū Thomam Eraftum scholae vestrae rectorem reuerenter meis verbis saluta. Librum Tilemani, quem Bulingero miserat, percurrere coepi non sine fastidio. Putidior tamē est illius rabulae loquacitas, quàm vt mihi bilem moueat. An sim responsurus, nōdum apud me statui. Certè multorum dierum opera nugas illas non dignabor, quia tot scriptionum piget. Breuem huius controuersiae definitionem nuper composui, quae forte propediem edetur. Si tibi quis patebit aditus ad Illustrem ac Generosum D. Comite ab Erpach, velim exemplar, quod reperies his literis inclusum, oftedas meo nomine. Quòd non scripserim in praesentia, pudori meo adscribet: velim tamen sibi persuadeat, suam amplitudinē, qua decet obseruatia, semper à me coli. Vale integerrime frater, & mihi ex animo charissime. Dominus te Spiritu suo gubernet, virtute sustineat, tueatur, & labores tuos benedicat. Geneuae, Nonis Nouembris. M. D. LX.
units.tr: I thought this summary would be enough to give you some outline of the form, which I ought not to prescribe. Whatever you think useful there, you will suggest modestly, so that good and prudent men, to whom it will not be burdensome to be advised, may consider what would be best to do. Greet respectfully, in my words, Master Thomas Erastus, rector of your school. I have begun to run through the book of Tilemann, which he had sent to Bullinger, not without disgust. Yet the chatter of that wrangler is too foul to stir my bile. I have not yet decided whether I shall reply. Certainly I shall not give many days' labour to those trifles, since I am weary of so many writings. I lately composed a brief definition of this controversy, which perhaps will be published shortly. If any access to the illustrious and noble Count of Erbach is open to you, I would like you to show him, in my name, the copy you will find enclosed with this letter. Let my modesty answer for the fact that I have not written to him in person; yet I would like him to be assured that his dignity is always honoured by me with the respect it deserves. Farewell, most upright brother, and most dear to me from my heart. May the Lord govern you with his Spirit, sustain and protect you with strength, and bless your labours. Geneva, Nones of November, 1560.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N.N. S. D. Dilectio Dei Patris nostri, & Gratia D. nostri Iesu Christi vobis semper adsit.
units.tr: Joan. Calvin to N.N., greetings. May the love of God our Father and the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ always be with you.

units.la: Quod à nonnullis vestri studiosis rogatus sum pridem, vt ad vos scriberem, illud ipsum facere valde etiā exoptabā, pro meo erga vos iusto & praecipuo quodam affectu: abstinui tamen hactenus, cùm meum laborem inutilem futurum iudicarem, & bonos quosdam viros & vobis viciniores, has sibi partes sumpsisse intelligerem. Nunc verò vbi occasionem elapsam nōdum esse audiui, quin meae ad vos literae suo loco & tempore ad ueniret, officio deesse nolui: vt vobis constet cùm corpore à vobis sim remotus, vos ipsos nihilo minus prae oculis & pectore à me ferri, atque ita studere me saluti vestrae, vt quicquid ad illam promouendam praestare potuero, nunquam sim negleturus. Primùm igitur Domino gratias ago, & à natali solo propter verbū ipsius exulare coactis de receflus loco prospexit, in quo pura conscientia ipsum inuocare liceat: adeoq; vos vnā quasi in nidulum quendam ita appositè collegit, vt hoc ad mutuam vestram con-solatio folationem appositissimum fit. Illud vero me ad illius erga vos opus praedicandum vnice impellit, quod ea constantia per Dominum praediti fitis, vt in persecutione non fatiscatis: feratis etiam aequo animo detrimentum facultatum vestrarum, animis in coelestem remunerationem intentis: quod denique quicquid vobis in mundo deceflit, tardium vobis non afferat, quando ad Dei honoris incrementum pertinuit: qui demum a nobis ita honorem quem ipsi debemus, reposcit, vt nos perinde gloriae suae participes efficiat. Cum igitur ea fit nostra fragilitas, non vulgare illud Dei donum agnoscendum est, cum nos ita in ipsa necef fitate confirmet, ne quando vlli tentationi manum demus. Iam vero, quia bene coepisse nihil est, vt neque ad tempus perstitisse, attendite vobis nunc etiam, incitate vofipfos ac ipso exhortamini, atque omnia illa quae vobis animum possunt addere, comparate: imprimis vero apud Dominum ipsum precibus instate, vt manu perpetuo porrecta ad scopum vocationis suae tandem vos perducat. Vos vero sic apud vos cogitate, quod Christi nomine persecutionem passi estis, illud honorificum imprimis esse, cum Filius Dei sua vobis stigmata ita imposuit, vt certior in vobis veritatis ipsius nota extaret. Atque illud facere debet, vt tanto magis enitamini perpetua vita, vt ipsum glorificetis. Cum ex aduerso, fi aliam quam rectam viam nunc ingrederemini, illud plane duplicaret scandalum, atque coram Domino longe in grauiorem reatum adduceret. Extet igitur in vobis apud omnes alios exemplum, quo ad Deum glorificandum excitentur, cum agnoscent nempe vos non frustra pro Euangelij testimonio, tot casus & discrimina pertulisse. Ne vestra culpa ipsi Filio Dei & Redemptori maculam aut labem aspergi sinatis: atque illud nominatim, propterea quod apud gentem exteram vobis nunc viuendum est quae facile offendatur, fi quae in vobis vitia deprehendat, illud vobis incitameto fit, vt tanto incedatis prudentius, atque omnia scandala vel leuissima anteuertatis. Cumque ante omnia vnam Dominus pacem & concordiam nobis commendet, illiusque sedulo fouendae studium, sic statuite, retineri a vobis rem tanti momenti non posse, nisi vofipfos inter vos sustineatis, atque mutuo toleretis. Ergo nisi ad multa leuiter commissa condonanda parati fumus, certum est materiam rixis & iurgiis nunquam defuturam. Fons autem mali ille est, cum suo quisque iudicio addictus est, vt aliis nihil omnino concedum velit. Illud igitur non secus ac sonticum morbum ita praecauete, vt contra propensi fitis ad vos ipsos aliis mutuo submittendos, ad mutuam inter vos & fraternam communicationem in omnibus, bonis consiliis obtemperetis, neque ipsi mul um sapere & confulti haberi affectetis. Sic Domini Spiritum in vobis habitatem ipsi agnoscetis, sic illum perpetuum directorem in vestris rebus experiamini. Nunquam igitur hoc vobis excidat, ambitionem nempe aemulationem & inuidentiam parere, ex quibus demum contentiones, & obtrectationes, & reliqua emanent: atque ita ignem ut plurimum accendi, ex quo litium & concertationum scintillae volitent: quas quidem vbi eo ventum est semel, repelle re deinde & sedare iam non sit integrum. Porro illa vna est ac summa ratio, quae vos certo coniunctos & copactos teneat, tum in doctrina, tum etiam in aliis omnibus, si omnem diligentiam vno animo adhibueritis, vt concionibus verb Dei frequentes in terfitis. Quemadmodum enim in bello nemo se a vexillo subdu cere sustinet, vt communibus animis & viribus hostis excipiatur: ita etiam Verbum Domini pro vexillo nobis ab ipso erectum est, ad quod omnes sese recipi nt, & extra quod mera tantum di sperfio notari possit. Sic oues dispersae fauc ibus luporum expo- nuntur: sic eadem sub pastoris custodia in ouile reducta secura sunt. Et sane nobis omnibus summum Pastorem Dominum Iesum Christum praefectum habemus, vt ipse nos in suum protectione admiserit: sed hoc ita procedit, vt instituat simul Ministros verbi, qui fungantur ipsius munere in nobis ipso auctore verbo regendis: eumque ordinem pro conseruanda Ecclesia sua semel ipse posituum voluit, vt docet Apostolus. Statuite igitur singulare hoc effecerga vos Domini beneficium, quod verbum ipsius apud vos extet, vt praedicatione illius vobis offeratur. Quare videndum est ne quo modo negligatur, aut remissius admittatur: quod cum apertam ingratitudinem prodituri sint, impune latu- ri non sitis. Habemus in Davide appositum exemplum, ex quo discamus quo loco esse piis debeat facultas adeundi sacros coe- tus: cum nempe & patria ipsa per se & familia, & facultatibus in suo per habitis, vnum illud requireret, quod ipsi im no daretur fan- ctis coetibus interesse. Neque vero ita perperam: cum satis esti- mari a nobis fructus ille non possit, quem ex visu fanctii illius or dinis percipimus, cum & vna conuentus vt eadem doctrina e- rudiamur, vno corde & ore nomen Domini inuocemus, vsu sa- cramentorum adhibito in fide confirmemur, sacramentum etiam Christianae militiae ita coram Deo & Angelis dicamus atque palam praestemus. Hoc vero plus quam necessarium est. Neque vlla vobis perniciosior tentatio a Satana intendi potest, quam si ad tanti boni contemptum vos adducat, aut ab illo quouis praexctu affectum distrahat. Nec quisquam hic supra Deum sapere audeat, vt sibi persuadeat non deesse & alia ratione quia in Christo profectum faciamus, quam quae ab ipso instituta sit, maxime cum & illa sit nobis ad manum. Fateor enim plerosque ex electis seruari a Domino in media ipsa Antichristi dissipa-ione quibus tamen quatum ab hominibus existimari potest, in speciem etiâ, desunt & pascua & pastores: sed & illud ad extraordinariam rationem & miraculo coniunctam referendum est. & agnoscedum illic est etiam irae ipsius flagellum, quod istiusmodi tamé verbi auditione participanda in Ecclesia dignatus non sit. Amplesten dum est igitur incomparabile Domini beneficium, cum aliter ipsius vocationi respondere non possimus. Quod siqua vobis in doctrina difficultas occurreret, ad Pastorem qui ordinatus erit, recurrite. Sic enim, mutua & amica collatione, melius peruenitur ad plenâ & liquidâ eorum, de quibus ambigimus, comprehensionem. Illud vero plus quàm dici potest, perniciosū est quod plerique hodie ita de se ac suo sensu praesumunt, ut quicquid in mentem venerit, pro rato & vero habeant, antequam rem ipsam bene sint assequuti: atque suo iudicio acquiescant, ut nullam cum doctioribus communicationem admittant. Satis quidé scio, nos omnes ab vno praeceptore Christo pedere sed itademum, ut i- dem sese paruulorum tantùm & verè demissorū ac humilium preceptoré praeferant: neque porro illud veritatis ipsius obsequii nomine cèferi, si ita iactemur audacia, ut erraticas opiniones & dogmata sestanda nobis proponamus, ac nullis habenis & repagulis nos contineri sinamus. Imprimis vero fratres, Attédite, ne Satan vos diuertat à natiuo illo gustu simplicitatis Euangelii, ut vanissimo curiositatis fermento vos illaqueet. Haec porro illa sunt quae Dominus ipse nos docet, quae à nobis perdisci & retineri iubet, quaeque vnà ad nostram aedificationem conferunt, si docemur nempe ipsum timere, diligere, in illo plenè fidem collocare, illum vnicum praesidium nobis statuere, illum glorificare, illius obsequio vitam in solidum consecrare, totam in Christo salutis fidem repositam habere. Et hoc est quod tradit Paulus, Totam Scripturam diuinitus inspiratam, vtilem esse ad doctrinam, ad redargutionem, ad correctionem, ad institutionem quae est in iustitia, ut perfectus sit homo Dei, ad omne opus bonum perfectè instructus. Quare qui verbum Dei ad subtilitates nullius vsus applicant, pessimè illud profanant, & sacrilegij tenentur. Et constat satis Deum hoc in illis seuerissimè vindicare. Portenta siquidem illa errorum & haereseon, quae hodie inuehuntur, riuuli sunt ab illo fonte deducti. Pleraque ingenia scilicet subtilitatem in Scriptura soliditati praetulerunt & verae vtilitati: illúdque vnum quaesiuerunt, quod ipsorum ventoso palato gratum esset. Atque Dominus iustus iudex permisit, ut in deliria adeò absurda laberentur, ut cu uis sano vel audita horrorem afferant. Neque aliunde quàm ex vicinia vobis exempla quaerenda sunt, vbi malum illud si visplam alibi grassatum scitis. Prospicite ergo vobis, ne quis ad vos intercipiendos aditus Satanæ pateat. Atque illud reputate, Domini nempe adesse tum vobis propugnatorem, cum gladium illum verbi sui exercit ad infultus aduersarii repellendos: hoc autem ita vobis constare, quum fidum pastorem eius beneficio habetis, qui vos instruat quibus opus est, ne artibus & dolis feduclorum, commoueri abducive contingat. Enimuero fiue de malo in posterum euitando, siue de quibusdam in viam reducendis agitur, vnum vobis est plane expeditum, nempe vt ordini alicui inter vos locus fit, vti extet aliqua disciplinæ forma, ad admonendos qui peccant, contumaces coercendos, & vnumquemque in officio continendum. Cum enim superioribus annis tyrannidi Papatus subiecti fuerimus, longe æquissimum est Christi iugum admittere, illudque agnoscere, legitimum libertatis nostræ vsum tam ab effræ si licentia remotum esse quam ad veram obedientiam voluntatis ipsius omni ex parte referatur. Disciplinæ igitur commodæ institutio inter vos, non tantum valeret ad illam opinionum diuersitatem componendam, sed etiam ad scandala, vitia, & alias morum corruptelas reprimedas, quod ad Dei honorem amplificandum multum prodesset. Porro sub illo nomine, quod necesse sit omnino exstare formam Ecclesiæ inter nos, vt in Dei no mine conueniamus, ipsum quoque sacramentorum vsum comprehensum volui. Non est enim existimandum, illa nobis a Deo instituta esse, quasi res essent leuis momenti. Nam si nostram in firmitatem expendimus, facile erit iudicare, quam nobis confultum sit, ad vsum nostrum illa adhibere. Non cōllamus quippe ex natura spirituali vt Angeli, vt rerum quæ sensus afficiant vsu carere possimus. Iam cum Dominus immensa sua bonitate, nostræ illi ruditati eo vsque consuluerit, vt media illa nobis offerret, quæ ad nostrum captum accommodata essent, qui a nobis reiici possunt, negligive, quin ipsius in nos ira prouocemus? Facite igitur vt tam Baptismus quam sacra D. Cœna summo in pretio sint apud vos. Quanuis enim Baptismus semel a nobis susceptus, sit nobis sigillum perpetuum Dei gratiæ & adoptionis in filios, cum tamen alterum sigillum, Cœnam nempe, apposuit ad nouam confirmationem, fatis prouidit vno sine altero nobis confirmandis fatis non futurum. Hoc inquam se videre Dominus ipse significauit, vt ab illo discereremus. Qui igitur a Cœna abstineret, quasi illa carere posset, seduceretur & excæcaretur omnino a Satana, cum seipsum ita agnoscere dedidicisset: neque illud rationibus multis confirmare opus est. Nisi enim mendacium Christo impingere volumus, agnoscere oportet, ipsum, dum Cœnam instituit, fatis significasse, illam ad nostram leuationem & adiumetum infirmitatis nostræ necessariam esse. Carere quidem illa cogetur qui aut in carcere erit, aut in deserto vagabitur, gabatur,quia adeundę facultate nõ habet:ac tum Dominus isti- ufmodi defectû gratia sui Spiritus supplebit. Neq; enim Dei Spiritum Sacramentis ipsis alligo:sed tantùm illa à nobis agnoscen da sunt,vt media & instrumenta,per quæ in nobis ordinarìo operatur,quandiu vsum illorum nobis ipse offert. Quamobrem, cùm vobis vsus Sacramentorum ad manum sit, videte ne si neglexeritis,tantiDei beneficij à vobis negledi rei coram illo sitis, quod vtraque manu vobis erat ampleãendum. Recordemini dierum superiorum quibus dum in Babylonis carcere iacueretis, ad hæc Dei gratię dona, & pignora tam ardêter sufpiraftis. Veniat etiam in mentem acerba illa conditio tot piorum hominum,qui hoc vnum mœrent,& perpetuis votis exquirunt,quod ipsis vt vobis fruendum nunc quidem non datur. Sic quidem ac cepi obiectam hic vobis nonnullam difficultatem esse,propter quasdam ceremonias,quas à vobis vsurpari voluerunt vestri illi hospites. Sanè nihil consultius video,quàm parcissimis ceremoniis vti in Ecclesia Christiana. Satis enim experietia ipsa constat,quàm procliuis sit lapsus in superstitionem. Aliud est verò cùm nobis ius non est admittendi,vel repudiandi quòd videbitur:sed & illæ res eiusmodi non suntquarum occasione, sponte nobis ipsis Cœnam Domini interdicamus. Exoptandû quidem quod optimum esse constat, ac quantùm in nobis est,vt locum etiam habeat procuràdum. Si non licet obtinere quod cupimus, feramus illos defectus,non approbemus: modò ne subsit illic impietas,aliúdve Dei verbo repugnans. Vt si quod, verbi gratia, idololatriæ specimen exisseret, illi ad mortem vsque resisti à nobis oporteret. Vbi verò doctrina ipsa sana atque pura est,ac ceremoniæ ad ciuilem quandam honestatem vel decorum vsurpantur,silentio nobis prætereunda sunt ista magis,quàm vt eorum occasione,ad disceptationes, & grauiores motus veniedum sit. Tandem igitur à vobis peto , dilectissimi fratres , per Dominum,vt quemadmodum de meo erga vos intimo affectu probe estis persuasi , sic etiam certò statuatis nihil mihi hac mea admonitione propositum fuisse,quàm vestrum ipsorum commodum & salutem. Accipite igitur hoc quicquid est, ea qua par est humanitate:ac rem ipsam expendite mature, cum mansuetudine & humilitate. Videte etiam ne qua in vobis pertinacia resideat, quæ vobis vim obstruat, quò minus quæ ad vestram vtilitatem faciat, admittatis. Dominus sua in vobis Spiritualia dona adaugeat, dirigat vos in omni sapientia & prudentia, confirmetin tolerantia & constantia,vt in vobis ad extremum vsque glorificetur, nósque vnà vobiscum ex vobis ipsis consolationem vberrimam percipiamus. Geneuæ.
units.tr: Although I was some time ago asked by some of your students to write to you, I very much wished to do so, out of my own particular and warm affection for you; yet until now I have held back, since I judged my labour would be useless, and I understood that certain good men who are nearer to you had taken this task upon themselves. But now that I have heard the opportunity has not yet passed, and that my letter could still arrive in its proper place and time, I was unwilling to fail in my duty. Let it be clear to you that, although I am absent from you in body, you are nonetheless borne before my eyes and in my heart, and that I am so concerned for your salvation that I shall never neglect whatever I can contribute to promoting it. First, then, I give thanks to the Lord, who, to those compelled to exile from their native soil for his Word, has provided a place of retreat in which it is lawful to call upon him with a clear conscience; and who has gathered you together, as into a little nest, so aptly that this is most suitable for your mutual consolation. What moves me above all to praise his work among you is that you are endowed by the Lord with such steadfastness that you do not faint under persecution; that you also bear with equanimity the loss of your goods, your minds being fixed on the heavenly reward; and finally, that whatever is taken from you in the world does not seem a loss to you, since it serves the increase of God's honour. He, in turn, so reclaims from us the honour we owe him that he makes us partakers of his own glory. Since, then, such is our frailty, we must acknowledge it as no ordinary gift of God that he so strengthens us in the very midst of necessity that we never yield to any temptation. Now indeed, since to have begun well is nothing, nor is it enough to have persevered for a time, consider yourselves further: stir yourselves up, exhort one another, and procure all those things which can add courage to you. Above all, press on with prayers before the Lord himself, that he, stretching out his hand continually, may at last bring you to the goal of your calling. And think thus within yourselves: that since you have suffered persecution in the name of Christ, this is especially an honour, since the Son of God has so impressed his marks upon you that a surer token of his truth stands out in you. This ought to make you strive all the more to live a holy life, so that you may glorify him. On the contrary, if you were now to walk in any other than the right way, this would plainly double the scandal and bring you into a much graver guilt before the Lord. Let there therefore stand among you, before all others, an example by which they may be stirred to glorify God, when they recognise that you have not endured so many trials and dangers for the testimony of the Gospel in vain. Do not allow, through your fault, a stain or blemish to be cast upon the Son of God and Redeemer himself; and this especially, because you must now live among a foreign people who are easily offended if they detect any vices in you. Let this be an incentive to you to walk the more prudently, and to avoid all scandals, even the slightest. And since the Lord commends above all else peace and concord among us, and the zeal for preserving it, be assured that a matter of such importance cannot be kept among you unless you bear with one another and tolerate each other mutually. Therefore, unless we are ready to pardon many lightly committed offences, it is certain that the material for quarrels and disputes will never be lacking. The source of the evil is this: each man, clinging to his own judgement, is unwilling to concede anything at all to others. Guard against this, then, as against a dangerous disease; be inclined rather to submit yourselves to one another, and in all things, in mutual and brotherly fellowship, obey good counsels, and do not desire to be thought very wise or consulted. Thus you will recognise that the Spirit of the Lord dwells in you, and thus you will experience him as your perpetual director in your affairs. Let it never escape you that ambition, rivalry and envy give birth to contentions, backbiting and the rest, from which at length a fire is kindled, from whose sparks the flying embers of strife and quarrels arise; and once things have come to that point, it is no longer in your power to repel and calm them. Moreover, there is one sole and supreme reason which will keep you firmly joined and bound together, both in doctrine and in all other matters, if you apply all diligence with one mind to being frequent in attending the sermons of the Word of God. For just as in war no one allows himself to withdraw from the standard, so that the enemy may be met with common minds and strength, so the Word of the Lord has been raised by him as a standard for us, to which all betake themselves, and outside which nothing but mere dispersion can be noted. Thus scattered sheep are exposed to the jaws of wolves; thus the same sheep, led back into the fold under the custody of the shepherd, are safe. And truly we all have the Lord Jesus Christ as our supreme Shepherd and captain, so that he has admitted us into his protection; but this takes place in such a way that at the same time he appoints ministers of the Word, who discharge his office among us, with the Word itself, by his authority, governing us; and he willed that this order, once established by himself, should be kept for the preservation of his Church, as the Apostle teaches. Consider, therefore, this singular benefit of the Lord towards you: that his Word is among you, so that it is offered to you by its preaching. Hence care must be taken that it is in no way neglected or admitted with less than full readiness; since in doing so you would display plain ingratitude, and you will not be going unpunished. We have in David an apt example, from which we may learn in what place the godly ought to have the opportunity of attending the holy assemblies: since both his country itself and his family and the goods he possessed, all these things, required of him only one thing, namely that he be granted to take part in the holy assemblies. Nor is this unreasonable, since we cannot sufficiently estimate the fruit we perceive from the sight of that holy order: when we are together in one assembly, we are instructed in the same doctrine, we call upon the name of the Lord with one heart and mouth, we are confirmed in faith by the use of the sacraments, and we also pronounce the sacrament of Christian warfare before God and the angels, and publicly perform it. This is more than necessary. Nor can any more pernicious temptation be aimed at you by Satan than if he should lead you to despise so great a good, or draw your affection away from it under any pretext whatever. Nor let anyone here presume to be wiser than God, persuading himself that we make progress in Christ by some other means than that which he has instituted, especially since that means lies ready at hand. For I grant that many of the elect are preserved by the Lord in the very midst of the Antichrist's dispersion; yet, as far as men can judge, even in appearance, pastures and pastors are lacking to them. But this must be ascribed to an extraordinary plan joined with a miracle; and there one must also acknowledge the scourge of his wrath, in that he has not deigned to grant them the hearing of the Word in the Church of this kind. Therefore the incomparable benefit of the Lord must be embraced, since we cannot otherwise respond to his calling. And if any difficulty in doctrine should occur to you, have recourse to the pastor who has been ordained; for by mutual and friendly conference we more readily arrive at a full and clear understanding of those matters about which we are in doubt. But that which is more than can be said is pernicious, namely that many today presume so much about themselves and their own opinion that they hold whatever has come into their minds to be settled and true before they have properly grasped the matter itself; and they rest so content in their own judgement that they admit no fellowship with the more learned. I know well enough that we all depend on the one teacher, Christ; yet it does not follow that they should set themselves before the teachers of little ones only and truly humble and lowly men; nor should it be excused in the name of obedience to the truth if we are so carried away by audacity as to propose to ourselves wandering opinions and dogmas, and allow ourselves to be restrained by no reins or barriers. Above all, brethren, take heed lest Satan turn you aside from that native taste of the simplicity of the Gospel, and ensnare you with the most vain leaven of curiosity. Moreover, these are the things which the Lord himself teaches us, which he bids us learn thoroughly and retain, and which together contribute to our edification: if we are taught, namely, to fear him, to love him, to place our full faith in him, to set him up as our sole safeguard, to glorify him, to consecrate our whole life to his obedience, and to hold the whole hope of salvation laid up in Christ. And this is what Paul hands down: that all Scripture, divinely inspired, is profitable for teaching, for refutation, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, so that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly equipped for every good work. Wherefore those who apply the Word of God to subtleties of no use profane it most wickedly, and are guilty of sacrilege. And it is sufficiently clear that God avenges this most severely in them. For those monstrous errors and heresies which are brought in today are streams drawn from that fountain. Indeed, many minds have preferred subtlety to the solidity of Scripture and to true profit, and have sought only that which might be pleasing to their windy palate. And the Lord, a just judge, has permitted them to fall into such absurd delirium that they horrify even a sound man who hears of it. Nor need you seek examples anywhere but from your neighbourhood, where you know that this evil has spread elsewhere. Take care, then, that no access for Satan to entrap you lies open. And consider this: that the Lord is present as your defender when he wields the sword of his Word to repel the assaults of the adversary; and you have this assurance when, by his kindness, you have a faithful pastor who instructs you in what you need, so that it does not happen that you are moved or drawn away by the arts and tricks of seducers. Indeed, whether the matter concerns avoiding evil in future or bringing certain persons back into the way, one thing is quite clear to you, namely that there should be some order among you, and some form of discipline, to admonish those who sin, to restrain the contumacious, and to keep each person in his duty. For since in former years we were subject to the tyranny of the Papacy, it is most fitting that we accept the yoke of Christ, and acknowledge that the lawful use of our liberty is as far removed from licence as it is directed to true obedience of his will in every respect. Therefore the proper establishment of discipline among you would avail not only to settle that diversity of opinions, but also to repress scandals, vices and other corruptions of morals, which would greatly help to advance the honour of God. Moreover, under that name I meant also to include the use of the sacraments, since it is necessary that some form of the Church exist among us, so that we may come together in the name of God. For we must not suppose that those things were instituted for us by God as if they were of slight importance. For if we weigh our own weakness, it will be easy to judge how advantageous it is for us to employ them. For we are not, like the angels, made of spiritual nature, so that we could do without the use of things which affect the senses. Now since the Lord, in his immense goodness, has so provided for our rudeness that he offers us those means which are adapted to our capacity, why should we reject or neglect them, unless we provoke his anger against us? Therefore see that both Baptism and the holy Supper of the Lord be held in the highest esteem among you. For although Baptism, once received by us, is for us a perpetual seal of God's grace and of adoption into sons, yet when he added the other seal, namely the Supper, for a renewed confirmation, he sufficiently foresaw that neither would be enough for our confirmation without the other. This, I say, the Lord himself signified that he saw, so that we might learn it from him. Therefore whoever abstains from the Supper, as if he could do without it, would be seduced and utterly blinded by Satan, since he had unlearned to recognise himself as such; nor is it necessary to confirm this by many arguments. For unless we wish to impute a lie to Christ, we must acknowledge that he, when he instituted the Supper, sufficiently signified that it is necessary for our refreshment and for the help of our weakness. Indeed, he who is in prison, or wanders in the wilderness, will be compelled to lack it, since he has no opportunity of approaching it; and then the Lord will supply this defect by the grace of his Spirit. For I do not bind the Spirit of God to the sacraments themselves; but they must be acknowledged by us only as means and instruments through which he ordinarily works in us, for as long as he himself offers us their use. Wherefore, since the use of the sacraments is at hand for you, see that if you neglect it, you are not guilty before him of neglecting so great a benefit of God, which you ought to have embraced with both hands. Remember the days past, when, while you lay in the prison of Babylon, you so ardently sighed after these gifts and pledges of God's grace. Let there also come to mind the bitter condition of so many godly men, who mourn this one thing alone and seek with perpetual prayers what is not now granted to them to enjoy as you may. Thus I have understood that some difficulty has been raised for you here, on account of certain ceremonies which those guests of yours wished to introduce among you. Certainly I see nothing more advisable than to use the most sparing ceremonies in the Christian Church; for experience itself shows how easy the slide into superstition is. But it is another matter when it is not in our power to admit or reject what seems good to us; and such matters are not of a kind that we should, on their account, voluntarily forbid ourselves the Lord's Supper. It is indeed to be desired what is known to be best, and, as far as lies in us, we should also take care that it obtain a place. If we cannot obtain what we wish, let us bear those defects without approving them, provided only that there is no impiety in them, nor anything opposed to the Word of God. For if, for instance, some sign of idolatry should appear, we ought to resist it even unto death. But where the doctrine itself is sound and pure, and the ceremonies are used for some civil decency or propriety, these things are rather to be passed over in silence, lest on their account we come to disputes and more serious disturbances. Finally, then, I beg you, most beloved brethren, through the Lord, that just as you are well persuaded of my heartfelt affection towards you, so you may also be firmly assured that in this my admonition I have had no purpose other than your own advantage and salvation. Accept therefore whatever this is with the humanity that befits it; weigh the matter maturely, with gentleness and humility. See also that no obstinacy dwell in you, which might hinder you from admitting what is for your profit. May the Lord increase his spiritual gifts in you, direct you in all wisdom and prudence, and strengthen you in patience and constancy, so that he may be glorified in you to the end, and that we together with you may receive from you the most abundant consolation. Geneva.

units.la: M. D. I X.
AD ILLVSTRISS. PRINCIPEM QVENDAM Germaniae Epistola.
units.tr: To a certain most illustrious Prince of Germany: a letter.

units.la: Illustrissime Princeps, Clementissime Domine, Exc literis Illustrissimae Clementiae vestrae ad doctorem Bernardum Bozemium intelligo, angi Clementiam Vestram hoc dissidio Theologorum: idque in ea re, quae maxime debebat parere nobis qui Christiani nominis sumus, concordiam: quae est doctrina de participatione corporis & sanguinis Domini nostri Iesu Christi. Ego certe in eorum numero sum, qui Augustanam confessionem sequi & probare volunt, cum in aliis omnibus, tum etiam in illo capite quod est de Coena Domini: sed hanc licentiam novae Stoae Theologorum probare non possum, qui ipsis Papistis malunt accedere, quam cum hominibus nostrae Religionis concordiam revocare, quae a Martino Luthero, & Martino Bucero caeterisque Saxoniae & superioris Germaniae Theologis conciliata atque constituta, ab iis dissuta ita est: ut amplius coire posse non videatur, nisi Principum intercedat auctoritas. Legi Heshusii librum: qui ut ne inter Theologos solum hoc dissidium exardescat, etiam Principes provocat. Ponit in definitione Coenae Dominicae, id quod controversum est. Pauli definitionem praeterit: & suam novam atque inauditam adfert: & propter suam tacitam Pauli condemnat. Auctoritates adfert quae pro se non faciunt, sed pro aduersariis. Scribit non ut doceat, sed ut iudicet atque condemnet. Satis enim condemnat, qui sua uti mauult quam Apostoli. Quain retamen excuso ipsum: non enim videtur intelligere vim verbi Graeci κοινωνία: illud enim verbum non additionem singularem nos deiicit: sed ad communem & caelestem revocat: non enim κοινόνητιν vocat, sed κοινωνίαν: qua fit ut κοινωνοὶ efficiamur mensae, id est, corporis & sanguinis, vitae & mortis participes, sed fideles. Fide enim furtum vsque in caelestem societatem ascendimus, cum singuli pro se homines, tum omnis Ecclesia & sese cum suo sponso coniungit Iesu Christo: ut hic in terra & ille in nobis & nos in illo viuamus. Qui credat verum Iesum Christum dicere: & verum dare, qui dicit, Commedite hoc est corpus meum: bibite hoc est sanguis meus: praesertim cum addat ad verbum Domini, verum corpus sese fumet: item qui approbat Pauli definitionem, quod fit κοινωνία τοῦ σώματος καὶ αἵματος: Et sequitur Augustini interpretationem, qui scribit manducare carnem Christi, esse participem corporis eius fieri: denique qui confitetur sese viuificationem Spiritus sancti in Christi corpore & sanguine immortaliter viuificari, Christumque in sese viuere, & sese in Christo: qui hoc omnia, inquit, confitetur & docet: quo exemplo & auctoritate aut Prophetarum,
units.tr: Most illustrious Prince, most gracious Lord, from your most illustrious Clemency's letter to Doctor Bernhard Bozemius I understand that Your Clemency is troubled by this dispute among the theologians, and over the very matter which ought above all to bring us who bear the Christian name into agreement, namely the doctrine of the participation in the body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ. For my part I am certainly among those who wish to follow and approve the Augsburg Confession, both in all its other articles and in the article concerning the Lord's Supper. But I cannot approve the licence of this new Stoa of theologians, who would rather draw near to the Papists themselves than recall concord with men of our own religion. That concord was reached and established by Martin Luther, Martin Bucer and the other theologians of Saxony and upper Germany, and these men have torn it apart, so that it no longer seems able to be restored unless the authority of princes intervenes. I have read Heshusius's book, which, so that this dispute may not blaze up only among theologians, also summons the princes. In his definition of the Lord's Supper he puts forward the very point in question. He passes over Paul's definition and brings forward his own new and unheard-of one, and by his silence about Paul's he condemns Paul. He adduces authorities which do not support him but his adversaries. He writes not to teach but to judge and condemn. For he condemns enough who prefers to use his own words rather than the Apostle's. Yet I excuse him to some extent, for he does not seem to understand the force of the Greek word koinōnia [κοινωνία]. That word does not thrust us down into something singular, but calls us back to something common and heavenly. For he does not call it koinōnēsis [κοινόνησις], but koinōnia [κοινωνία], by which we are made partakers of the table, that is, sharers in the body and blood, in life and death, but faithful ones. For by faith we ascend even into heavenly fellowship, both each man for himself and the whole Church, and she joins herself to her bridegroom Jesus Christ, so that he lives here on earth in us, and we in him. Whoever believes that Jesus Christ speaks truly, and that he who says, "Eat this, it is my body; drink this, it is my blood," gives truly, will also hold that the true body is himself received, especially since he adds to the Lord's word that the true body is taken. Likewise he who approves Paul's definition, that it is a communion [κοινωνία] of the body and blood, and follows Augustine's interpretation, who writes that to eat the flesh of Christ is to be made a partaker of his body; finally, he who confesses that he is quickened to immortal life by the life-giving of the Holy Spirit in the body and blood of Christ, and that Christ lives in him and he in Christ: this man, I say, confesses and teaches all these things. By what example or authority of the Prophets

units.la: {y} Latin text continues on next page. rum,aut Euangelistarum, aut Apostolorum, aut Patrum hunc hominem haereticum esse, & priuata auctoritate excommunica-tum condemnare possunt: praesertim cum ab ipsis huiusmodi multa absurda dicantur? Christi corpus naturale, quod scilicet carne & ossibus praeditum est, vbique non esse: & tamen vbique vna cum carnibus & ossibus eius sumi & vere manducari: & id proprie dici, hoc est natiuo verbi vsu: item panem non transub-stantiari, tamen panem esse corpus: & in eo hoc vtuntur συλσο-ματικῶς, & corporaliter corpus (quod idem est quod corporale nominant: item corpus Christi non esse localiter, sed tamen in pane dari & manducari, idipsum scilicet cum carne & ossibus. Et cum eo descendunt, vt ad imperitā plebem dicant: quemadmo-dum in cunis iacuit cum fasciis Christum fumi, id est māducari quis aut plebeiorum, aut eruditorum loquendi farraginem & li-centiam, & impudentiam intelligit? Vnde hęc noua Theologia, nouæ scholæ, noua Stoicorum ἀπαθείας δόγματα? Lutherus venerationem & adorationem sustulit: his grati sunt qui cōtra-ria faciunt, capita nudant, genua flectunt, ore non manu accipi-unt, gratiores si adorarent: vt apud Pontificios chari sunt & ac-cepti qui statuas adorant, ad illas supplices procumbunt, & ad il-las lumina collocār. Sed hæc ego pluribus persecutus sum quàm constitueram. Verùm me dolor impulit & impellit, cùm consi-dero quàm scribant confidenter, ita vt hominum doctorū iudi-cia non extimescant: nō formident posteritatis existimationem, quibus vtrisque turpe constituitur exemplū, viuis qui cùm pos-sint non refutant: venturis, quantæ miseriæ eos adiudicent, & stultitiæ, vt necessarium putent suam illos sequi debere stultitiam. Quōd autē ad I.C.V.scribo, hæc causa est ista. Magna in spe sunt posit hunc conuentum Principum, Theologorum fore synodū: & eò spectare aliqui videntur & id agere, vt illius synodi auctoritate Heluetiæ & Gallicæ Ecclesiæ condemnentur, ob hoc caput de Cœna Domini. Quòd si id fiet indicta causa, re inter vtrāque partem non disceptata, neque cognitis rationibus vtriusq; partis, ab arbitris viris prudentibus, doctis, non sociis horum dif-ferentiorum, quot & quanta inde incommoda? Licebit idem facere Papistis & à concilio generali nos excludere, nostram omnem doctrinam & Religionem condemnare. Offendentur maximæ & potentissimæ nationes Italicæ, Hispanicæ, Gallicæ, Anglicæ, Heluticæ, apud quos populos propè omnes docti nolunt ad no-uas his verborum formulas adstringi: Patrū tamen verba liben-ter admitterent, si ipsi vt Patres verecundè & sentirent & loque-rentur. Ægerrimè feret Nauarræ Rex sese & suos à Saxonicis Ec-clesiis excommunicari: dolen-ter etiam Angliæ Regina, quę ta-metsi Augustanam confessionem approbet, tamen has carnales verborum formulas recipere nō potest. Præterea nt Martini Lu-theri puram de hoc Sacramento doctrinam, & illius hyperbo-las arripiunt,& obtrudunt populo. Philippum Melanchthonem pars delirare dicit in fenefiute, pars incon stantem in dogmati-bus, pars id non sensisse quòd ad V.C. scripsit: quasi vero illud scriptum deliri senis sit, aut quasi sententiam suam non communicarit primùm per annos iā viginti inde à Vvormatiensi priore colloquio: post Haganoicia Comitia cum Ioanne Caluino: deinde cum Petro Martyre:cum amicis etiam aliis multis,cum illisq; perpetuam amicitiam coluerit, autquasi nesciamus quid senserit de Vvestphali scriptis:aut ego ignorem quid mecum locutus sit,& quid ad me scripserit. Quos viros ille vir amauit, ad quos amanter scripsit,cum quibus amicitiam coluit, eos isti ma ledictis lacessere & de Ecclesia deturbare audent. Nihil est, in quo se Pontificij magis iactent,quàm in his nostris dissidiis:nihil est,quod magis alienet animos hominum,quàm hæc eadem. Metuo etiam,ne hæc eadem quotidie obiiciantur Regi Nauarrę, in hoc principio administrationis totius Regni. Ex Brabantia scribitur illum in consilio Cardinalium per Legatos suos Pontifici promittere filialem obedientiam. Idem scribitur Lugduno. Et credo ĉum id cogi facere,Cardinalium importunitate,aduer sariorum calumniis:interea tamen ipse Prouincialesin partiam & in suas sedes reuocat: captiuos propter Religionem liberat; non impedit priuatos conuentus,& Dei inuocationem,& Sacra mentorum administrationem.
