Ambrose too, expounding the passage of Paul to the same effect: "Because there is one Father, not in person but in one undivided nature, so that the Son of God might be the arbiter of God and men, he was born man by taking on flesh, so that he might be Mediator of God and men, man and Son. This is not without the Deity, because in God he was man, and God in man; and so that from both he might be Mediator, and reconcile both. He did these things first in himself; for he could not be Mediator by the unity of the fruit." It is not necessary to pursue this at length; it is enough that readers have been reminded once that whenever this way of speaking occurs among the ancients, that Christ is Mediator in the flesh, if it is taken exclusively, their genuine sense is corrupted. Concerning the question proposed, we judged that we should answer freely and clearly in this way. And indeed we would have preferred, leaving Stancarus aside, to explain the substance of the matter calmly; but he himself has forced the refutation from us against our will. Meanwhile, however, nothing bitter, nothing contentious, nor any desire to fight in our response will offend godly and humane readers.

units.la: Pastores & Ministri Ecclesiae Genevensis.
units.tr: The Pastors and Ministers of the Church of Geneva.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus omnium nomine.
units.tr: John Calvin, in the name of all.

units.la: SVMMA QVAEDAM DOCTRINÆ de Ministerio Verbi & Sacramentorum, cuius auctoris nomen adscriptum non erat.
units.tr: A SUMMARY OF CERTAIN DOCTRINE concerning the Ministry of the Word and the Sacraments, the author's name not being appended.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: TOtius Ministerij Euangelici finis est, vt nobis à Deo fonte omnis felicitatis per peccatum seiunctis, ac proinde perdi tis, Christus communicetur, vt vitam æternam ex ipso hauriamus: omnes denique cœlestes thesauri ita nobis applicentur, vt non minus sint nostri quàm ipsius Christi.
units.tr: The whole purpose of the Gospel ministry is that Christ should be communicated to us, who have been cut off from God, the fountain of all happiness, through sin and so are lost, that we may draw eternal life from him; and, in short, that all heavenly treasures should be so applied to us that they are no less ours than Christ's own.

units.la: 1. Thess. 2.12. Vocauit nos per Euangelium in participationem gloriæ Domini nostri Iesu Christi.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 2.12. He called us through the Gospel into the fellowship of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: II.
units.tr: II.

units.la: Communicationem hanc fatemur esse a mysticâ, & rationi humanæ incomprehensibilem & b spiritualem, quòd eius effector sit Spiritus sanctus: qui cum sit virtus Dei viuentis, procedes à Patre & Filio, omnipotentiam ei adscribimus, quæ non imaginaria, sed potentissime, & veritatem nos Christo capiti nostro coniungat, vt simus caro de carne eius, ossa de ossibus eius, & ex viuifica eius carne vitam æternam in nos transfundat.
units.tr: We confess that this communion is mystical, and beyond human comprehension, and spiritual, because its author is the Holy Spirit. Since he is the power of the living God, proceeding from the Father and the Son, we ascribe to him an omnipotence that is not imaginary but most effective, and that joins us in truth to Christ our head, so that we are flesh of his flesh and bones of his bones, and pours eternal life into us from his life-giving flesh.

units.la: a Ephes. 5.32. Mysterium hoc magnum est, loquor autem de Christo & de Ecclesia.
units.tr: a Eph. 5.32. This is a great mystery, but I speak concerning Christ and the Church.

units.la: b 1.Cor. 6.17. Qui adglutinatur Domino, vnus spiritus est.
units.tr: b 1 Cor. 6.17. He who is joined to the Lord is one spirit.

units.la: Augustus Epist. 57. ad Dard. Peccatum factum est relictio Dei: iustitia non fit sine Deo. Ac per hoc non moreremur, nisi per carnalem propaginem de membris illius veniremus, nec viueremus, nisi per spiritualem connexionem membra huius essemus.
units.tr: Augustine, Letter 57 to Dardanus. Sin came about by forsaking God; righteousness does not come about without God. And so we would not die unless we came from his members through carnal descent, nor would we live unless we were members of this one through a spiritual connection.

units.la: III.
units.tr: III.

units.la: Quòd autem confitemur Spiritum sanctum huius coniunctionis esse effectorem, certo innititur fundamento, huic nimirum: Quicquid a Patre aut Filius b operantur ad salutem adducedis fidelibus, id per Spiritum sanctum vtrumque personam operari testatur sacra Scriptura: Et non aliter c Christum in nobis habitare, quàm per suum Spiritum, neque alio modo se nobis communicare, quàm per eundem Spiritum.
units.tr: Moreover, when we confess that the Holy Spirit is the author of this union, we rest on a sure foundation, namely this: whatever the Father or the Son works for bringing the faithful to salvation, Holy Scripture testifies that both persons work it through the Holy Spirit; and Christ dwells in us only through his Spirit, and communicates himself to us in no other way than through the same Spirit.

units.la: a Ioan. 14.16. Ego rogabo Patrem, & alium Consolatorem dabit vobis, Spiritum illum veritatis, quem mundus non potest recipere, &c.
units.tr: a John 14.16. I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, etc.

units.la: Et Paulo post. 25. Hæc locutus sum vobis apud vos manens, Paracletus autem ille Spiritus sanctus, quem mittet Pater in nomine meo, ille vos docebit omnia, & suggeret vobis omnia quæ dixi vobis.
units.tr: And a little after, John 14.25. I have spoken these things to you while remaining with you; but the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.

units.la: b Ioan. 15.26. Cum autem venerit Paracletus, quem ego mittam vobis à Patre meo, Spiritus ille veritatis, qui à Patre procedit, ille testabitur de me. Item Ioan. 16.7. Sed ego veritatem dico vobis, expedit pedit vobis vt ego abeam. Nam nisi abiero, Consolator ille non veniet ad vos: sin autem abiero, mittam eum ad vos.
units.tr: b John 15.26. But when the Paraclete comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness concerning me. Likewise John 16.7. But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.

units.la: Vos autem non estis in carne, sed in spiritu, si quidem Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis. Quod si quis Spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est eius. Ibidem paulo post 11. Si Spiritus eius, qui excitavit Iesum a mortuis, habitat in vobis, is qui excitavit Christum ex mortuis, vivificabit & mortalia corpora vestra, per inhabitantem eius Spiritum in vobis. Item paulo post 14. Quotquot Spiritu Dei ducuntur, hi sunt Filii Dei. Item 1.Cor.6.19. Nescitis quod corpus vestrum templum est Spiritus sancti, qui habitat in vobis, quem habetis a Deo? Item 1.Cor.3.16. An nescitis quod templum Dei estis, & Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis?
units.tr: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his. Likewise, a little after, Rom. 8.11: If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you. Likewise a little after, Rom. 8.14: All who are led by the Spirit of God, these are the sons of God. Likewise 1 Cor. 6.19: Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, who dwells in you, whom you have from God? Likewise 1 Cor. 3.16: Do you not know that you are God's temple, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

units.la: IIII.
units.tr: IV.

units.la: Ad efficiendam hanc coniunctionem Spiritus S. duplici vtitur in strumento, praedicatione Verbi, & administratione Sacramentorum.
units.tr: To bring about this union, the Holy Spirit uses a twofold instrument: the preaching of the Word and the administration of the Sacraments.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Quum dicimus Spiritum sanctum externo ministerio uti ut instrumento, sic intelligimus: Tam in praedicatione verbi quam in usu Sacramentorum duos esse Ministros, qui distincta habeant officia. Minister a externus administrat verbum vocale, & sacra signilla quae externa sunt, terrena & caduca. Minister vero internus, qui est Spiritus sanctus, libere agit interne, dum in quorumcunque vult cordibus arcana sua virtute communicationem cum Christo per unam fidem operatur. Quae communicatio res est interna, coelestis & immarcessibilis.
units.tr: When we say that the Holy Spirit uses an external ministry as an instrument, we understand it thus: in the preaching of the Word as much as in the use of the Sacraments there are two ministers, who have distinct offices. The external minister administers the spoken word and the outward signs, which are external, earthly and perishable. The inner minister, however, who is the Holy Spirit, acts freely and inwardly, while in whatever hearts he wills he works, by his hidden power, communion with Christ through faith alone. This communion is an inward, heavenly and unfading thing.

units.la: De toto ministerio ita loquitur Paulus: Quis est Paulus? Quis est Apollos? nisi Ministri per quos credidistis, & ut cuique Dominus dedit: Ego plantavi, Apollos rigavit, sed Deus dedit incrementum: itaque neque is qui plantat est aliquid, neque is qui rigat, sed qui incrementum dat, Deus.
units.tr: Paul speaks thus of the whole ministry: Who is Paul? Who is Apollos? Only ministers through whom you believed, and as the Lord gave to each: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase. So neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God, who gives the increase.

units.la: VI.
units.tr: VI.

units.la: In praedicatione verbi Minister externus verbum vocale porrigit & auribus percipitur. Internus Minister Spiritus sanctus rem quae per verbum annuntiatur, utpote Christum, quorum vult mentibus, vere communicat, ita ut non sit necesse Christum aeque atque verbum per corporis organa recipi, sed arcana sua virtute hanc coniunctionem operatur Spiritus sanctus, creando in nobis fidem, qua facit nos viva membra Christi veri Dei & veri hominis.
units.tr: In the preaching of the Word, the external minister offers the spoken word, which is perceived by the ears. The internal minister, the Holy Spirit, truly communicates the thing announced through the word, namely Christ, to whomever he wills, in their minds. It is not necessary for Christ to be received through the organs of the body, as the word is; rather, the Holy Spirit works this union by his hidden power, creating faith in us, by which he makes us living members of Christ, who is true God and true man.

units.la: Act.16.14. Quaedam mulier nomine Lydia, ex urbe Tyatirorum quae purpuram vendebat, Deum colens, nos audivit, cuius Dominus aperuit cor, ut attenderet iis quae dicebantur a Paulo.
units.tr: Act. 16.14. A certain woman named Lydia, of the city of Thyatira, a seller of purple, who worshipped God, heard us, and the Lord opened her heart to attend to the things that were said by Paul.

units.la: VII.
units.tr: VII.

units.la: In Baptismo a Minister externus baptizat externo elemento, vtpote aqua,quæ corpore percipitur. ita vt non sit necesse Christum corporis organis recipi, vt abluantur animæ nostræ ipsius sanguine, sed sufficit ar cana & potentissima spiritus sancti operatio.
units.tr: In Baptism the external minister baptizes with an external element, namely water, which is perceived by the body. It is not necessary for Christ to be received by the organs of the body, so that our souls may be washed in his blood; the hidden and most powerful operation of the Holy Spirit is sufficient.

units.la: a Mat.3.11.Ioan.1.26. Ego baptizo vos aqua ad pœnitentiam.
units.tr: a Matt. 3.11; John 1.26. I baptize you with water unto repentance.

units.la: b Tit.3.5. Salvos nos fecit per lavacrum regenerationis & renovationis Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: b Titus 3.5. He saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 1.Cor.6.11. Et hac eratis quidam, sed abluti estis, sed iustificati estis, sed sanctificati estis in nomine Domini Iesu, & per Spiritum Dei nostri.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 6.11. And such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were justified, but you were sanctified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.

units.la: VIII.
units.tr: VIII.

units.la: In Cœna Domini Minister externus porrigit externa symbola, panem Domini, & vinum Domini, quæ organis corporis nostri accipiuntur, comeduntur & deglutiuntur.
units.tr: In the Lord's Supper the external minister offers the external signs, the bread of the Lord and the wine of the Lord, which are received by the organs of our body, eaten and swallowed.

units.la: a 1.Cor.10.3.4. Omnes eandem escam spiritualem ederunt, & omnes eundem potum spiritualem biberunt: bibebant enim ex spirituali sequente petra; petra autem erat Christus.
units.tr: a 1 Cor. 10.3-4. They all ate the same spiritual food, and they all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

units.la: IX.
units.tr: IX.

units.la: Vt corpore Christi pascamur in vitam æternam, non vult Christus vt credamus corpus suum aut sanguinem suum descendere de cœlo super altare, aut circum altare in panem aut sub pane, aut non procul à pane: non magis quàm in Baptismo opus est, vt vera membra corporis Christi fiamus ipsum corpus Christi de cœlo in aquam aut sub aquam descendere, aut non procul ab aqua stare: quemadmodum nec in verbo vocali tali corporis descensu est opus, vt tot us Christi fiamus participes, sed satis potentia Spiritus Domini, qui à Patre Filioque procedit, inesse credimus, vt vere nos in Baptismo eius corporis faciat membra, quod est & manet in cœlo. Et in sacra Cœna eodem corpore manente in cœlo magis ac magis nos nutriat per arcanam atque efficacissimam potentiam suam & virtutem.
units.tr: That we may be nourished by the body of Christ unto eternal life, Christ does not want us to believe that his body or his blood descends from heaven upon the altar, or around the altar into the bread, or under the bread, or stands not far from the bread. It is no more necessary in the Supper than in Baptism that the body of Christ itself descend from heaven into the water, or under the water, or stand not far from the water, in order for us to become true members of the body of Christ. Likewise, in the spoken word there is no need for such a descent of the body in order for us to become partakers of the whole of Christ; rather, we believe that the power of the Spirit of the Lord, who proceeds from the Father and the Son, is sufficiently present to make us truly members of his body in Baptism, which body is and remains in heaven. And in the holy Supper, while that same body remains in heaven, he nourishes us more and more through his hidden and most effective power and virtue.

units.la: Hæc doctrina, quod corporis Christi nullus fit descensus aut illapsus, visibilis, aut invisibilis, fundata est in clarissimis Scripturæ testimoniis. Quatenus enim Christus est homo, testatur Scriptura eum recessisse, Luc. 24.51. abiisse. Ioan.14.4. mundum hunc reliquisse, Ioan.16.28. sublatum esse, Act.1.11. in sancta ἀχειροποίητα, Heb.9.11. & 24 contineri cœlo ad tempus usque restitutionis omnium, Act.3.21. Nec pugnant cum hac doctrina verba Christi, Hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis,&c. Nam ipsius Christi optimus interpres est D.Paulus,qui hoc interpretatur panis quem frangimus:verba Christi, est corpus meum,interpretatur,est communicatio corporis Christi.
units.tr: This doctrine, that there is no descent or incoming of the body of Christ, visible or invisible, is founded on the clearest testimonies of Scripture. For insofar as Christ is man, Scripture testifies that he withdrew, Luke 24.51, that he departed, John 14.4, that he left this world, John 16.28, that he was taken up, Acts 1.11, into the holy places not made with hands [ἀχειροποίητα], Heb. 9.11 and 24, and that he is contained in heaven until the time of the restoration of all things, Acts 3.21. Nor do the words of Christ, "This is my body which is given for you," etc., conflict with this doctrine. For the best interpreter of Christ himself is St. Paul, who explains them by "the bread which we break"; and the words of Christ, "This is my body," he explains as "a communion of the body of Christ."

units.la: Iam autem ante demonstratum est, vnicam hanc esse communicandi rationem,qua per Spiritum sanctum eius fimus participes, qui effector est huius communicationis, cum sit virtus Dei viuentis à Patre Filióque procedens.
units.tr: Moreover, it has already been shown that this is the only way of communicating by which we are made partakers, through the Holy Spirit, of him who is the author of this communion, since he is the power of the living God proceeding from the Father and the Son.

units.la: Consentit etiam hęc doctrina cum Symbolo Apostolico siue articulis fidei, quorum inuiol ibilis & simplicissima inter pios omnes constare debet certitudo: his nimirum : Ascendit in cœlum,Sedet ad dexteram Dei Patris omnipotentis, Indè venturus est ad iudicandum viuos & mortuos.
units.tr: This doctrine also agrees with the Apostles' Creed, or the articles of faith, whose inviolable and simplest certainty ought to stand firm among all the godly; namely these: "He ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of God the Father Almighty, from thence he shall come to judge the living and the dead."

units.la: Hos articulos fidei ita vt nos intellexit D. Augustinus.Tom. >E-pistola 57. ad Dardanum,in qua hos articulos Confessione Christianam appellat,& vetat ne ab ea recedamus.Noli dubitare,inquit,ibi nunc esse hominem Christum Iesum,vnde veturus est: memoriterque recole,fi leliter tenet Christianam confessionem, quoniam resurrexit à mortuis,Ascendit in cœlum,Sedet ad dexteram Patris,Nec aliunde quàm inde venturus est ad viuos mortuosque iudicandos.Et sic venturus est, illa Angelica voce testate,quemadmodum ire visus est in cœlum,in eadem carnis forma atque substantia,cui profecto immortalitatem dedit,naturà non abstulit. Secundum hanc formam non est putandus vbique diffusus.Cauendum est enim ne ita diuinitatem adstruamus hominis,vt veritatem corporis auferamus. Non est autem consequens vt quod in Deo est,ita sit vbique vt Deus, nam & de nobis veracissima Scriptura dicit,quod in illo viuimus,movemur, & sumus:nec tamen sicut ille vbique sumus,sed aliter homo ille in Deo,quoniam aliter & Deus ille in homine, proprio quodam & singulari modo.Vnaenim persona Dei & homo est,& vtrumque vnus est Christus Iesus,vbique perid quod Deus est,in cœlo autem per id quod homo.Hactenus Augustinus.
units.tr: St. Augustine understood these articles of faith as we do, in Epistle 57 to Dardanus, in which he calls these articles the Christian confession and forbids us to depart from it. "Do not doubt," he says, "that the man Christ Jesus is now there, whence he will come. Remember faithfully, if you hold the Christian confession, that he rose from the dead, ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of the Father, and from there alone, and not from elsewhere, will come to judge the living and the dead. And he will come as the angelic voice testified, just as he was seen to go into heaven, in the same form and substance of flesh, which he certainly gave immortality, but did not take away its nature. According to this form he is not to be thought of as diffused everywhere. For we must take care not to assert the divinity of the man in such a way as to take away the truth of his body. Yet it does not follow that what is in God is everywhere as God is. For Scripture, which is most true, also says of us that in him we live, move, and have our being; yet we are not everywhere as he is, but that man is in God otherwise, since God too is otherwise in man, by a certain proper and singular mode. For there is one person of God and man, and both together are one Christ Jesus. He is everywhere according to what he is as God, but in heaven according to what he is as man." Thus far Augustine.

units.la: Consentit etiam & cum articulo , de assumpta vera humana natura a,cuius omnes conditiones,excepto peccato sponte Christus in se recepit,& b post glorificationem immortalitatem cair ni fuę dedit,naturam non abstulit.
units.tr: It also agrees with the article concerning the assumed true human nature, all of whose conditions, apart from sin, Christ willingly took upon himself, and which, after glorification, he gave immortality, but did not take away its nature.

units.la: a Heb.4.15. Non habemus Pontificem, qui non potest affici sensu infirmitatum nostrarum,sed tentatum in omnibus similiter,absque peccato.
units.tr: a Heb. 4.15. We do not have a high priest who cannot be touched with a feeling of our infirmities, but one who was tempted in all things like us, without sin.

units.la: b Luc.24.39. Videte manus meas, et pedes meos, quia ego ipse sum. Contrectate me, et videte, quia spiritus carnem et ossa non habet, sicut me videtis habere. Augustin. in Ioan.Hom.5. Secundum maiestatem suam, secundum providentiam, secundum incassabilem & inuisibilem gratiam, impletur quod ab eo dictum est: Ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus vsque ad consummationem seculi: Secundum carnem vero, quam verbum assumpsit, secundum id quod de Virgine natus est, secundum id quod a Iudaeis prehensus est, quod ligno confixus, quod de cruce depositus, quod linteis involutus, quod in sepulchro conditus, quod in resurrectione manifestatus, Non semper habebitis vobiscum. Quare? quoniam conuersatus est secundum corporis praesentiam quadraginta diebus cum discipulis suis, & deducentibus ipsis videndo non sequendo, ascendit in coelum, & non est hic. Ibi est enim, Sedet ad dexteram Patris, & hic est, non enim recessit praesentia maiestatis. Aliter: Secundum praesentiam maiestatis sem per habemus Christum: Secundum praesentiam carnis, recte dictum est discipulis: Me autem non semper habebitis. Habuit enim illud Ecclesia secundum praesentiam carnis paucis diebus, modo fide tenet, oculis non videt.
units.tr: b Luke 24.39. See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Handle me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see me to have. Augustine, in John, Hom. 5. According to his majesty, according to his providence, according to his unfailing and invisible grace, what he said is fulfilled: "Behold, I am with you all days, even to the end of the age." According to the flesh, however, which the Word assumed, according to what was born of the Virgin, according to what was seized by the Jews, according to what was fastened to the wood, what was taken down from the cross, wrapped in linen, laid in the tomb, and made manifest in the resurrection, you will not always have him with you. Why? Because he lived with his disciples in bodily presence for forty days, and while they escorted him, they saw but did not follow; he ascended into heaven, and is not here. For there he is, sitting at the right hand of the Father, and here he is too, for the presence of his majesty has not departed. Put another way: according to the presence of his majesty we always have Christ; according to the presence of his flesh, it was rightly said to the disciples, "But you will not always have me." For the Church had that according to the presence of the flesh for a few days; now it holds him by faith, and does not see him with the eyes.

units.la: Consentit etiam cum articulis fidei de Diuina natura Christi, de omnipotentia, & de Spiritu sancto. Credimus enim vere nobis & potentissime praestare Christum per suum Spiritum, quod promittit, licet omnipotentiam ipsius ad euertendum illum articulum fidei pertinere non credamus: vt corpus Christi non ascenderit in coelum, & non sedeat ad dexteram Dei, quin potius multo magis credimus ita demum vere stabiliri omnipotentiam & articulos nostrae fidei, dum arcana & incomprehensibili virtute Spiritus sancti opus hoc in nobis multo certius fieri credimus, quam si corpus Christi e coelo super altare descenderet, manibus ministri porrigeretur, & ore corporis nostri commederetur. Tanto enim certior ac potentior est Spiritus sancti operatio, quanto Creator ipse omnibus creaturis quantumcunque excellentibus est superior.
units.tr: It also agrees with the articles of faith concerning the divine nature of Christ, his omnipotence, and the Holy Spirit. For we truly and most powerfully believe that Christ fulfils by his Spirit what he promises, although we do not believe that his omnipotence bears on overturning that article of faith, namely that the body of Christ did not ascend into heaven and does not sit at the right hand of God. Rather, we believe much more that our faith in the omnipotence and the articles of our faith is truly established in this way: while we believe that this work is accomplished in us much more certainly by the hidden and incomprehensible power of the Holy Spirit, than if the body of Christ descended from heaven upon the altar, were offered in the hands of a minister, and were eaten by the mouth of our body. For the operation of the Holy Spirit is as much more certain and powerful as the Creator himself is superior to all creatures, however excellent they may be.

units.la: a 1.Cor.15. Factus est primus homo Adam in animam viuentem: extremus Adam in Spiritum viuificantem. Hactenus.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 15: The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving Spirit. So far.

units.la: CAL. MYCRONIO CONTRA MENNONEM.
units.tr: Calvin to Mycronius, against Menno.

units.la: Tv vero, integerrime frater, minime literis tuis me obtudis, quibus interpellar gratum est ac iucundum. Tantum cuperem laetius tibi dari argumentum, vt mihi gaudium tuum commune esset: Sed quando ia Domino nos exercere placet, cum ras, quae te publica Ecclesiae causa angunt, inter nos communicari molestum esse non debet. Vtinam vero ad te iuuandum facultas voto par suppeteret. Caeterum quicquid in me est operae ac subsidii, libenter tibi impertiar. Mennonis doctrina quam ex delitiis Manichaeorum hausit, mihi non erat incognita. Fallacias non ita penitus tenebam: quibus vt obuiam eas fatendum est ac dilucidè explicandum, sicuti te fecisse non dubito, Christum Deum manifestatum in carne, verum esse Dei Filium. Et quanquam nomen Filii, proprie in naturam Diuinam competit, & ad eam refertur, hominem tamen illum ex Virgine genitum proprie Filium vocari. Quia quatenus Mediator est & caput Ecclesiæ Deus & homo, Filium Dei naturæ esse oportet, vt adoptionis gratia nos sibi coniungat. Cæterùm inde præposterè colligitur, genitum esse hominem ex Patris semine, quia propter arcanam sacramque vnionem Diuinitatis cum carne, totus Christus vere dicitur Filius, sicuti præcipuè ex Pauli verbis primo ad Rom. capite, item etiam nono liquet. Quibuscunque enim cauillis ludit Menno, perspicuus est sensus, Filium Dei esse ex semine Dauidis secundum carnem. Item, Christum, qui Deus est benedictus in sæcula, ex Iudæis originem trahere secundum carnem. Itaque frustra locos arripit, vbi vocatur Christus homo Dei Filius: quia in totam Christi personam nomen hoc merito confertur. Quòd autem è cœlo venille Christus dicitur & à Patre exiisse, ad carnis essentiam perperam trahitur. Quia etsi indecolligere licet Christum verum esse Deum, hoc tamen non tam de substantia sua, quàm de officio prædicat, quia testari vult nihil se tradere nisi diuinum.
units.tr: You, most upright brother, do not in the least weary me with your letter, and I am glad to be called upon by it. I would only wish that a happier subject had been given you, so that your joy might be shared by me. But since it pleases the Lord to exercise us, there should be no trouble in sharing between us the matters that trouble you for the public cause of the Church. I wish indeed that my ability to help you matched my desire. Meanwhile, whatever effort and support I have, I will gladly give you. Menno's teaching, which he drew from the delights of the Manichaeans, was not unknown to me. I did not grasp his sophistries so thoroughly. As for meeting them, and explaining them clearly, as I do not doubt you have done, Christ, God manifested in the flesh, is the true Son of God. And although the name Son properly belongs to the divine nature and refers to it, that man born of the Virgin is nonetheless properly called the Son. For insofar as he is Mediator and head of the Church, being God and man, he must be the Son of God by nature, so that by the grace of adoption he may join us to himself. But from this it is absurdly inferred that man was begotten from the seed of the Father; for because of the secret and sacred union of the Godhead with the flesh, the whole Christ is truly called the Son, as is especially clear from Paul's words in the first chapter of Romans, and also in the ninth. Whatever quibbles Menno plays with, the meaning is plain: the Son of God is of the seed of David according to the flesh. Likewise, Christ, who is God blessed for ever, derives his origin from the Jews according to the flesh. So he snatches at passages in vain, where Christ is called the man, the Son of God; for this name rightly applies to the whole person of Christ. But that Christ is said to have come down from heaven and to have gone forth from the Father is wrongly drawn to the essence of the flesh. For although it may be gathered from these that Christ is true God, yet this does not so much declare his substance as his office, since he wishes to testify that he hands on nothing but what is divine.

units.la: Porrò argumenta quibus orthodoxa doctrina probatur, diluere volens, nihil quàm friuolis cauillis elabitur. Si in carnem mutari potuit Spiritus, quia Deo sunt omnia possibilia, ergo & Pater verti in carnem potuit. Quòd si demus, vbi erit illud, Cœlum & terram impleo? Tota enim Diuinitas erit corpus vnum, quod loco comprehendi necesse est. Iam si corporea suisset diuinitas in Christo, falsò dixisset Deum esse Spiritum. Item à resurrectione sua, Spiritum carnem & ossa non habere, Nam si excipiat Menno, mutatum fuisse Spiritum in carnem, vt desineret esse quod erat, nihil absurdius fingi potest. Peribit enim æternitas essentiæ spiritualis. Addé quòd si ex Dei seminæ penitus est Christus homo, iam non vna nec simplex erit Dei essentia, sed in partes secabitur atque ita in Deo erit diuisio, quâ Menno inter duas Christi naturas non admittit. Quod obiicit non fore alioqui verum illud Ioannis, verbum carnem esse factum, quia fieri non significet assumere, nugatorium est. Nam certè Apostolus 2. ad Heb. cap. 2. in nne non dissentit, qui tamen assumendi verbo vtitur. Ersatis constat huius locutionis ratio: quia & fieri rex dicitur, qui ante homo pri... quia incipit esse quod ante non erat. Itaque & verè & apte, vbi carnem induit Filius Dei, dicitur caro factus.
units.tr: Furthermore, wishing to refute the arguments by which orthodox doctrine is proved, he slips away into nothing but frivolous quibbles. If the Spirit could be changed into flesh, because all things are possible with God, then the Father too could have been turned into flesh. But if we grant this, where will that saying stand: "I fill heaven and earth"? For the whole Godhead would then be one body, which must be confined to a place. Now if the divinity in Christ had been corporeal, he would have spoken falsely in calling God a Spirit; likewise after his resurrection, that a spirit does not have flesh and bones. For if Menno excepts this, that the Spirit was changed into flesh so that it ceased to be what it was, nothing more absurd can be imagined. For the eternity of a spiritual essence would perish. Add that if Christ as man was wholly from the seed of God, the essence of God would no longer be one and simple, but would be cut into parts, and thus there would be division in God, which Menno does not admit between the two natures of Christ. His objection that otherwise that saying of John, "the Word was made flesh," would not be true, because "made" does not mean "assumed," is trifling. For certainly the Apostle in Hebrews 2 does not disagree in this, though he uses the word "assumed." From this the reason for this way of speaking is sufficiently clear: a man who was previously a man is also said to become a king, because he begins to be what he was not before. And so, truly and aptly, when the Son of God put on flesh, he is said to have been made flesh.

units.la: Putidum est effugium, dici Filium hominis quia hominibus promissus fit. Secundum verò commentum adducens Menno satis declarat effugia se quærere. Palàm verò est Hebraico more vocari Filium hominis verum hominem. Nam Christus haud dubie phrasin linguæ suæ retinuit. Quid autem per filios Adam intelligi conueniat, extra controuersiam esse debet. Ac ne longius abeamus, locus Psalmi octaui quem ad Christum Apostoli accômodant, omnem controuersiam dirimit: Quid est homo quòd memor es eius, aut Filius hominis quia visitas eum? Quod de masculino genere nugatur, colore prorsus caret: quia Filius hominis vocatur, cuius origo verè ex Adam fluxit.
units.tr: The argument that the Son of man is so called because he was promised to men is a foul evasion. Menno, by bringing in a second fancy, sufficiently shows that he is seeking escapes. But it is plain that by Hebrew idiom the Son of man means the true man. For Christ undoubtedly kept the idiom of his own language. What is meant by the sons of Adam ought to be beyond dispute. And, not to wander further, the passage of Psalm 8, which the Apostles apply to Christ, settles every controversy: "What is man, that thou art mindful of him, or the son of man, that thou visitest him?" What he trifles about the masculine gender is wholly without colour, since he is called the Son of man whose origin truly flowed from Adam.

units.la: Cùm dicimus oportuisse in carne nostra expiari peccata mundi, frustra hoc principium conuellere nititur Menno: quod clarè à Paulo asseritur 5.ad Rom.cap. Nam quod contrà obiicit, ne minem ex carne peccatrice prognatum potuisse legem implere, solutio petenda est ex 8.ad Rom.cap.vb docet Paulus expiationem factam in similitudine carnis peccatricis. Naturam enim hominis non à principio fuisse corruptam notum est, sed vitio accidentali. Quid ergo obstat quò minus Filij sui carnem Deus sanctificare potuerit?
units.tr: When we say that it was fitting for the sins of the world to be expiated in our flesh, Menno tries in vain to overturn this principle, which Paul clearly asserts in Rom. 5. As for his objection, that no one born of sinful flesh could have fulfilled the law, the answer must be sought in Romans 8, where Paul teaches that the expiation was made in the likeness of sinful flesh. For it is well known that human nature was not corrupted from the beginning, but by an accidental fault. What then stands in the way of God having been able to sanctify the flesh of his own Son?

units.la: Argumentum etiam illud firmum manet, Nisi fuerit generatio hominis Christi, nouam fuisse creationem. Nam quod excipit non fuisse nouas creationes quoties miraculo aliquid in nouam naturam mutatum est, importunè huc torquetur, quia non potuit essentia Dei mutari, sicut creaturæ, & detestabile commentum est fingere Dei essentiam in Patre esse Spiritum, in Filio esse corpus.
units.tr: That argument also remains firm: unless the Man Christ was begotten, his coming would have been a new creation. For his objection, that there were not new creations whenever something was changed into a new nature by a miracle, is wrongly twisted here, because the essence of God could not be changed as creatures are, and it is a detestable fiction to imagine the essence of God to be spirit in the Father and body in the Son.

units.la: Argumentum quod sumitur à donorum participatione impudenter transfilit. Nam inde certè ad nos pertinet quicquid Christo contulit Pater: quia caput est ex quo totum corpus per iuncturas connexum simul coalescit. Imò non aliter conueniet quod dicitur: Spiritum ei datum esse absque mensura, vt de plenitudine eius hauriamus omnes. Nisi forte Mennoni absurdum non est, Deum in sua esse ita aduentitio dono locupletari. Hac etiam ratione dicit Christus ipse, Io. 17: Ego propter eos sanctifico meipsum. Improbè igitur mentitur nusquam hæc in Scripturis legi.
units.tr: The argument drawn from the participation of gifts he shamelessly skips over. For certainly whatever the Father conferred on Christ pertains to us; for he is the head from which the whole body, connected by its joints, grows together. Indeed, otherwise what is said would not fit: that the Spirit was given to him without measure, so that we all might draw from his fullness. Unless perhaps it does not seem absurd to Menno that God in his own essence should be enriched by such an accidental gift. For this reason Christ himself says, John 17: "For their sakes I sanctify myself." He therefore lies wrongly in claiming that these things are nowhere read in the Scriptures.

units.la: Quantum ad testimonium Mosis spectat, si probè expenditur, magis premit Mennonem, quàm vt se expedire queat. Neque enim de vno dicitur Christo illic sermo habetur, sed de toto humano genere. Verum quidem est partem esse à Christo victoriâ, sed generaliter pronuntiat Deus post eros mulieris superiores fore Diabolo. Vnde sequitur, Christum ex humano genere esse pro genitum. Totum verò sensum peruertit Cabalistica Mennonis allegoria, quòd mulier dicatur Ecclesia, quia consilium Dei est, Etiam quam alloquitur, bona spe erigere. Hoc etiâ loco solutionem
units.tr: As far as the testimony of Moses is concerned, if it is properly weighed, it presses Menno harder than he can escape. For it is not said there of one, that is, of Christ, that the discourse is held, but of the whole human race. It is true that the victory over the serpent belongs to Christ, but God pronounces in general that the offspring of the woman will be superior to the Devil. From this it follows that Christ was born of the human race. But Menno's Cabbalistic allegory perverts the whole sense, when he says that the woman means the Church, because it is the purpose of God, who addresses her, to raise her up with good hope. Here too the solution

units.la: Gen.3. num varietas tortuosum & lubricu angue ostendit. Interim vi-store serpentis ex muliere quæ ἀσπορος est, promitti dicens, ne-quaquam se extricat. Nisi enim semen esset in muliere, falsa esset promissio.
units.tr: Gen. 3. The very variety of the serpent, a tortuous and slippery snake, shows that. Meanwhile, by saying that the seed promised against the serpent comes from a woman who is [ἄσπορος] without seed, he by no means extricates himself. For unless there were seed in the woman, the promise would be false.

units.la: Testimonia vbi Christus semen Abrahæ & fructus ventris Dauidis vocatur, nimis improbe corrumpit. Nam si allegorice positum esset nomé feminis, Paulus certe 4. ad Gal.cap. hoc non tacuisset. Clare autem & sine figura affirmat, non esse plures Abrahæ filios redemptores, sed vnum Christum. Fateor ex analogia non aliter colligi Christum esse filium Dauidis, nisi quia ex Virgine genitus est. Sed nimis superbe, vt impium suum errorem stabiliat Menno, euertit naturæ elementa, mulieres cōtendens esse ἀσπορους.
units.tr: He corrupts far too boldly the passages where Christ is called the seed of Abraham and the fruit of David's womb. For if the name of woman were used allegorically, Paul would certainly not have kept silent about it in Galatians 4. But he clearly and without figure affirms that there are not many redeeming sons of Abraham, but one Christ. I admit that by analogy Christ is not otherwise gathered to be the son of David, except because he was born of a Virgin. But too proudly, in order to establish his impious error, Menno overturns the elements of nature, contending that women are [ἄσποροι] without seed.

units.la: Octauum argumentum de genealogia Christi sophistice eluidit. Etsi enim Matthæus non recenset Mariæ parentes, sed Iosephi; quia tamen de retunc vulgo cōperta verba facit, satis habet ostendere Iosephum ex Dauidis semine ortū esse: cūm satis constaret Mariam ex eadem esse familia. Magis etiam vrget Lucas, salutem à Christo allatam toti generi humano commune esse docens, quia Christus auctor salutis ex Adam communi omniū patre, sit progenitus.
units.tr: The eighth argument, concerning the genealogy of Christ, he explains away sophistically. For although Matthew does not recount the parents of Mary, but those of Joseph, yet, because he speaks of what was then commonly known, he is satisfied to show that Joseph was born of the seed of David, since it was well enough established that Mary was of the same family. Luke presses the point even more, teaching that the salvation brought by Christ is common to the whole human race, because Christ, the author of salvation, was born from Adam, the common father of all.

units.la: Aptè ex Matthæi verbis colligitur, quia ex Maria genitus est Christus, procreatum esse ex eius semine. Sicuti etiam cūm dicitur Booz genitus esse ex Rechab, similis notatur generatio. Nec verò Matthæus hic Virgine quasi canale describit, per quod fluxerit Christus, sed hunc mirificum generandi morem à vulgari discernit, quòd per eum ex semine Dauidis genitus fuerit Christus. Eadem enim ratione qua Isaac ex Abraham, Solomon ex Dauide, Ioseph ex Iacob, similiter Christus ex matre genitus esse dicitur. Sermonis enim seriem Euangelista contexit.
units.tr: It is rightly inferred from Matthew's words that Christ was born of Mary in the sense that he was produced from her seed. In the same way, when Boaz is said to have been born of Rechab, a similar kind of birth is indicated. Nor does Matthew here describe the Virgin as a mere channel through which Christ flowed. He distinguishes this remarkable manner of generation from the ordinary one, in that Christ was born of the seed of David through her. For by the same reasoning by which Isaac is said to be born of Abraham, Solomon of David, and Joseph of Jacob, Christ is likewise said to be born of his mother. The evangelist is simply following the thread of his narrative.

units.la: In decimo argumento suam impudentiā nimis turpiter prodit. Quomodo enim quadrabunt, secundum carnem Christum esse ex semine Dauidis, & tamen non aliter vocari Filium, nisi quia promissus est ac donatus? Nam postquam Filium Dei nominauit Paulus, continuò post subiiciens, secundum carnē esse ex semine Dauidis, distinctū certè aliquid à Diuina essentia notat. Sic & 9. cap. Deum benedictum prædicans, seorsum ponit, secundum carnem ex Iudæis descendere. Iam nisi verè genitus esset ex semine Dauidis, quid valebit locutio illa, vt sit fructus ventris eius & ex lumbis descenderit? Stulte autem obiicit, non posse dici naturalem Dauidis filium, quia verbum factum est caro, quia constat non alio sensu hoc dici, nisi quia carnem induit, & manifestatus est in carne. Mulieri non esse generatiuū semen dicit Menno: sed quis præter communem omnium sententiam
units.tr: In the tenth argument he betrays his impudence all too shamefully. For how will it square that Christ is of the seed of David according to the flesh, and yet is called Son only because he was promised and given? When Paul names him Son of God and immediately adds that he is of the seed of David according to the flesh, he certainly marks out something distinct from the divine essence. So too in chapter 9, when he proclaims God blessed, he sets apart that Christ descended from the Jews according to the flesh. Now, unless he was truly begotten of the seed of David, what will that expression mean, that he is "the fruit of the womb" and "came down from the loins"? Moreover, he foolishly objects that he cannot be called David's natural son because "the Word was made flesh", since it is plain that this is said in no other sense than that he put on flesh and was manifested in the flesh. Menno says that the woman has no generative seed, but who would believe this fiction of an unlearned man, against the common opinion of all?

units.la: P.j. indocti hominis figmento credet? Quinquam mirum est sic ipsum verum miraculum negare, dum salsissimum portentum de suo affingit, in quo admirabilior sit Dei potentia, si verum esset quod persuadet, aeternam Dei essentiam mutatam esse in mortale corpus. Nugatorium etiam est quod repetit non posse docere certo Mariam esse genitam ex femine Dauidis: quia Matthaeus probare volens Christum esse genitum ex femine Dauidis, dum hoc uno contentus est, ex Maria esse genitum, certe prore confessa sumit, Mariam fuisse consanguineam Ioseph. Quod autem adducit femen pro posteritate fumi, nimis dilutum est: quia non simpliciter vocatur femen, sed dicitur esse ex femine. Impudentia etiam minime tolerabilis est, clarum in verbis Pauli sensum pervertere, ut Christum ex femine Dauidis factum vel formatum esse neget.
units.tr: Yet it is strange that he denies the true miracle in this way, while he invents from his own head a most absurd monstrosity, in which the power of God would be more wonderful, if what he persuades us of were true, namely that the eternal essence of God was changed into a mortal body. It is also trifling that he repeats that one cannot teach with certainty that Mary was begotten of the seed of David. For Matthew, wishing to prove that Christ was begotten of the seed of David, is content with the one point that he was born of Mary, and certainly takes for granted, as an admitted thing, that Mary was a kinswoman of Joseph. As for his claim that "seed" stands for posterity, it is too feeble, because it is not simply called seed but is said to be "of the seed". It is also quite intolerable impudence to pervert the plain sense of Paul's words, so as to deny that Christ was made or formed of the seed of David.

units.la: Quod ad vndecimum argumentum spectat, fateor Ecclesiam spiritualiter esse carnem ex carne Christi, &c. Sed viciissim dico, ut hoc fieret, Christum sumpsisse ex hominibus carnem, in qua se pro ipsis sanctificaret.
units.tr: As for the eleventh argument, I grant that the Church is spiritually flesh of Christ's flesh, and so on. But in turn I say that, for this to happen, Christ took flesh from men, in which he might sanctify himself on their behalf.

units.la: Christum vocari coelestem e coelo, quia inde carnem attulerit, omni ratione caret: idq; antithesis clare euincit. Terrenus enim homo tantundem valet atque animalis: cum tamen animam ex terra profectam non esse fatis liqueat. Itaq; nihil certius quam coelestem vocari Christum viuificantis Spiritus respectu.
units.tr: The claim that Christ is called heavenly because he brought his flesh from heaven lacks every foundation, and the antithesis clearly refutes it. For "earthly man" is equivalent to "natural" man, although it is not sufficiently clear that the soul came from the earth. Therefore nothing is more certain than that Christ is called heavenly with respect to the Spirit who gives life.

units.la: Secundo ad Philip.cap.non inficior, quin forma hominis sit vilis & abiecta conditio: sed ex toto contextu facile colligitur in vera hominis natura exinanitum fuisse Christum. Quid enim hoc sibi vult, figura repertum fuisse tanquam hominem, nisi quia ad tempus non resplenduit diuina gloria, sed tantum apparuit humana species? Atque huc pertinet exaltatio: quia diserte nouam gloriam adeptus fuisse dicitur Christus, quia seipsum exinaniuit.
units.tr: Secondly, on Philippians chapter 2, I do not deny that the form of a man is a lowly and abject condition. But from the whole context it is easily gathered that Christ was emptied in the true nature of man. For what does it mean that he was found in fashion as a man, unless the divine glory did not shine forth for a time, but only the human appearance was seen? And to this belongs the exaltation: for Christ is expressly said to have obtained a new glory because he emptied himself.

units.la: Vtcunque locum ex 2. ad Heb.cap.torqueat, non tamen extri care se poterit. Ex vno esse dicit auctorem sanctitatis, & eos qui sanctificantur, nempe ex Deo. Atqui potius intelligi naturae communicationem ex contextu euincitur. Continuo enim post subiicit Apostolus, Ideo non erubescit eos vocare fratres. Si autem prius dixisset, fideles ex Deo esse, in tanta dignitate quaenam esset erubescentiae ratio? Sed ideo non erubescere dicitur Christus, quia pro immensa sua gratia ad sordidos & ignobiles se aggregat. Frustra autem obiectat Menno, impios alioqui fore Christi fratres: quia scimus filios Dei non ex carne & sanguine, sed ex Spiritu nasci per fidem. Proinde fraternam communicationem non facit sola carnis societas. De pueris inscite nugatur, quando simpliciter intelligit Propheta, cuius testimonio vtitur Apostolus, ftolus,seruos vel discipulos. Nec minus temere garrit,Mariam fratris sui fore matrem, si Christus secundum carnem frater non ster fit,cum plus satis trita sit phrasis Hebraica,Fratres vocari có sanguineos quoslibet.Tametsi autem Apostolus hunc honorem assignat solis fidelibus, quòd ex vno sint cum Christo : non tamen sequitur, quò minus ex eodem fonte nascantur increduli: quemadmodum vbi dicimus Christum factum esse hominé vt nos faceret Dei filios, non extenditur hæc locutio ad quoslibet: quia fides media interponitur, quæ nos in Christi corpus spiritualiter inserit.Nimis impiè & scelerate obiicit,debuisse Christũ statim ab initio ex Adam nasci, cum primogenitus sit inter fratres. Primogenitura enim non ad ætatem,sed ad gradum honoris & virtutis eminentiam refertur.
units.tr: However one twists the passage from Hebrews 2, one will not be able to escape from it. He says that the author of sanctification and those who are sanctified are of one, namely of God. But the context proves rather that a communion of nature is meant. For immediately afterwards the Apostle adds: "for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren." If he had said before that believers are of God, what reason would there be for shame at such great dignity? But Christ is said not to be ashamed because, in his immense grace, he joins himself to the lowly and the base. Menno's objection is also vain, that otherwise the impious would be brethren of Christ; for we know that the sons of God are born not of flesh and blood, but of the Spirit through faith. Therefore the brotherly communion is not created by fleshly kinship alone. He trifles foolishly about children, when he understands simply "servants or disciples" in the prophet whose testimony the Apostle uses. He chatters no less rashly that Mary would be the mother of his brother, if Christ were not a brother according to the flesh, since the Hebrew phrase is quite commonplace: "brethren" is used of any blood relations whatever. Although the Apostle assigns this honour only to believers, because they are one with Christ, it does not follow that unbelievers are not born of the same source. Just as when we say that Christ became man to make us sons of God, this expression is not extended to everyone, because faith intervenes, which spiritually grafts us into the body of Christ. He objects too impiously and wickedly that Christ ought to have been born of Adam from the beginning, since he is the firstborn among the brethren. For the firstborn is referred not to age, but to the rank of honour and eminence of virtue.

units.la: Argumentum decimumquintum nimis inscitè eludit. Clara sunt Apostoli verba,Quando pueri participant carne & sanguinem,eorum quoq; participem fieri Christum oportuit. Quod de natura humana dictum est, Menno sine ratione & sine pudore ad peccatum torquet.Improbius etiam est, q; relatiuum pluralis numeritantùm ad carnem restringit,& eam fictitiam:ac si nihil diceret Apostolus,Christum eiusdem nobiscum naturæ socium & confortem statuens.Nec quicquam est momenti in eius cauillo,Christum fore peccatorem ex peccatoribus,si verus homo sit: quia non concedimus naturæ corruptelam fuisse in Christo,sed docemus absque vitio creatum fuisse hominem.
units.tr: He mocks the fifteenth argument very unlearnedly. The words of the Apostle are plain: "since the children share in flesh and blood, he too ought to have shared in them." What is said of human nature, Menno twists to sin without reason and without shame. It is even more wicked that he restricts the relative pronoun of the plural only to flesh, and that fictitiously, as if the Apostle were saying nothing, when he establishes Christ as a partner and sharer of the same nature with us. Nor is there any weight in his quibble that Christ would be a sinner from sinners, if he were a true man; for we do not concede that corruption of nature was in Christ, but we teach that man was created without vice.

units.la: Locus ex secundo ad Hebræos,vbi dicit Apostolus,Christum sumpsisse semen Abrahæ, impium Mennonis & Serueti comentum repudiat,quòd receperit Christus in gratiam homines.Nam illic Apostolus vt gratiam amplificet, qua dignatus est Christus humanum genus,Angelos cum hominibus comparat,quòd sci licet præcelerit Angelis homines , hominum naturam induendo. Nam si per semen intelligit posteros,idem & de Angelis fateri cogetur: nempe sobolem ab illis procreari,ac si mentitus esset Christus,dicens nos Angelis similes fore post resurrectionem. In præsenti verbi tempore futilis est argutia. Nam vsitato more δικαιωσ loquutus est Apostolus, vt clariustam insignem gratiam ante oculos nobis poneret.
units.tr: The passage from the second chapter of Hebrews, where the Apostle says that Christ took on the seed of Abraham, refutes the impious fiction of Menno and Servetus, that Christ received men into grace. For there the Apostle, in order to magnify the grace by which Christ deigned to take up the human race, compares the angels with men, namely that he surpassed the angels by putting on the nature of men. For if by seed he means posterity, he will be compelled to confess the same about the angels, namely that offspring is produced from them; as if Christ had lied in saying that we shall be like the angels after the resurrection. The subtlety about the present tense of the verb is futile. For the Apostle spoke in the customary manner, so as to set before our eyes more clearly the outstanding grace [χάριτι].

units.la: De vtraque in Christo natura nõ modò inscitè garrit,sed con fuse omnia permiscens,secum ipse pugnat.Tradit Petrus nos divinæ naturæ fore consortes,sed hoc nonnisi ad qualitatem referri potest:quatenus scilicet renouabimut in cœlestem gloriam. Alioqui corruptibile hoc nostrum corpus fieret tum Deus. Quomodo autem non horret Menno & abominatur mutatione carnis peccatricis in Dei essentiam, cùm tantopere refugiat, quod tamé absurditate caret, Filium Dei carne nostra fuisse indutum?
units.tr: He not only talks unlearnedly about both natures in Christ, but, confusing everything in a jumble, he contradicts himself. Peter teaches that we shall be partakers of the divine nature, but this can refer only to a quality, namely insofar as we shall be renewed into heavenly glory. Otherwise this corruptible body of ours would then become God. But how does Menno not shudder at, and abhor, the change of sinful flesh into the essence of God, when he so greatly shrinks from the idea that the Son of God was clothed with our flesh, which nevertheless is free from absurdity?

units.la: P.ij.
units.tr: P.ij.

units.la: Adde ꝙ fecundum Petri metem societas diuinæ naturæ præsen- tem hominū naturam, quatenus infirma est, abolebit. In Christo autem lõge diuersa ratio, qui simul & semel Deus & homo fuit. Iam vero si humanam substantiam Christo tribuit integram & puram ab omnibus, qualis in Adam fuit ante lapsum, sequitur non ex Dei femine progenitam fuisse Christi carnem, sed ex homine: nisi dicere forte malit vel de nihilo vel ex terra creatam fuisse. Cur dictum Athanasij improbet, Christū constare ex duabus naturis, sicut homo personaliter cōstitutus ex anima & corpore, monstranda est ratio, cur tam apta similitudo displiceat.
units.tr: Add that, according to Peter's mind, the communion of the divine nature will abolish the present nature of men insofar as it is weak. But in Christ the case is entirely different, since he was at once and at the same time God and man. Now, if he attributes to Christ a human substance whole and pure, free from all defects, such as Adam had before the fall, it follows that Christ's flesh was not produced from the seed of God, but from a man, unless perhaps he prefers to say that it was created out of nothing or from the earth. Let him show the reason why he disapproves of the saying of Athanasius, that Christ consists of two natures, just as a man, personally constituted, consists of soul and body; for it must be shown why so apt a comparison should displease him.

units.la: Si locum Petri tergiuersando inuoluit, vbi Christū dicit mortuum esse carne, viuificatum Spiritu, nō miror. Quomodo enim se expediet, cum virtutem qua carebat Christi caro, Petrus Spiritui adscribat? Durius etiam eum premit Pauli dictum, vbi Christum asserit passum fuisse pro infirmitate carnis: quia si diuina fuit Christi caro, infirma fuit diuinitas. Huc etiam pertinet quod Christus passiones nostras & affectus sustinuit, similis per omnia nobis factus excepto peccato. Nam si dolori, & timori, cunctis denique nostris infirmitatibus subiecta fuit Dei natura, iam neque sol lucidus erit, sed totus cœli & terræ ordo informe erit & horrendum chaos.
units.tr: If he wraps up Peter's passage, where Peter says that Christ was put to death in the flesh and made alive by the Spirit, I am not surprised. For how will he extricate himself, when Peter ascribes to the Spirit the power which Christ's flesh lacked? Paul's saying presses him even harder, where he asserts that Christ suffered on account of the weakness of the flesh: for if Christ's flesh was divine, then the divinity was weak. To this also belongs the fact that Christ endured our sufferings and affections, made like us in all things except sin. For if the nature of God was subject to grief and fear, and finally to all our infirmities, then the sun will no longer shine, but the whole order of heaven and earth will be a shapeless and dreadful chaos.

units.la: Quicquid blaterat vt probet non esse mulieribus generatiuū semen, refutatione indignum est. Atque hoc potius medicis relinquo tractandum. Rationum tamen quas adducit, ea est futilitas, quæ nullo negotio refelli queat.
units.tr: Whatever he babbles in order to prove that the seed is not generative in women is unworthy of refutation. I leave this rather to physicians to treat. Yet the reasons he adduces are of such flimsiness that they could be refuted without any effort.

units.la: Onan filius Iuda semen effudit in terram. Idem nusquam legitur de muliere. Quasi vero reuelandis mulierum pudendis hic nebulo se oblectet.
units.tr: Onan, the son of Judah, poured out his seed on the ground. The same is nowhere read of a woman. As if this scoundrel delighted in exposing the private parts of women!

units.la: Vir immundus dicitur, de quo egreditur proiectio feminis. Nimis stulte infertnon contingere mulieribus immundum fluxū. Nam hac ratione nulla esset natiua immundities in fœminis, in cuius remedium solis viris data est circuncisio.
units.tr: A man is said to be unclean from whom an emission of seed proceeds. Too foolishly he infers that women have no unclean flux. For on that reasoning there would be no natural uncleanness in women, for whose remedy circumcision was given to men alone.

units.la: Sapientiæ septimo, coagulatus dicitur homo sanguine ex femine viri. Hinc contendit mulieri adscribi, quod eius proprium est, nempe sanguine. Quasi vero aliud sit sperma quàm sanguis ad generandum concretus. Unde sequitur fœtum tam ex mulieris, quàm viri substantia coalescere.
units.tr: In the seventh chapter of Wisdom, man is said to be curdled from blood, out of the seed of a man. From this he argues that what is proper to a woman is ascribed to her, namely blood. As if the seed were anything other than blood condensed for generation! Hence it follows that the foetus coalesces from the substance of the woman as well as of the man.

units.la: Locum Pauli, vbi docet non esse virum ex muliere, sed mulierem ex viro, scelestè hic nebulo corrumpit: quia illic minimè dubium est tractari de principio humani generis, non autem de continua propagatione, cuius statim altero membro memnit Apostolus, vbi dicit virum esse per mulierem.
units.tr: This scoundrel wickedly corrupts the passage of Paul where he teaches that man is not from woman, but woman from man: for there it is beyond doubt that the origin of the human race is treated, not its continual propagation, of which Paul himself makes mention in the next clause, where he says that man is through woman.

units.la: Quod obiicit, Aaron & Ioiada duxisse vxores ex tribu Iuda, ac inde colligit confusam tunc fuisse tribuum discretionem, si inesset. nesset mulieri generatiuum semen, nimis frigidum est. Satis enim notum est quantùm ad politicum ordinem spectat, concessi progeniem ex virili semine. Superior tamen sexus dignitas non facit, quò minus in generando coëat semen mulieris. Hæc quoque solutio ad omnes genealogias extenditur. Sæpe, vbi catalogum hominum recenset Scriptura, solos viros nominat, an ideo dicédum est mulieres nihil esse? Imò pueris ipsis notum est, mulieres sub viris comprehendi. Hac quoque ratione dicuntur fœminæ párere suis maritis, quia familiæ nomen penes masculos semper residet.
units.tr: What he objects, that Aaron and Jehoiada took wives from the tribe of Judah, and from this he concludes that the distinction of the tribes would then have been confused if the woman had generative seed, is altogether too cold. For it is well known that, as far as the political order is concerned, offspring was granted from male seed. Yet the superior dignity of the male sex does not prevent the seed of the woman from coming together in generation. This solution also extends to all genealogies. Often, when Scripture recounts a list of men, it names only the males: are we therefore to say that women are nothing? Indeed, even children know that women are included under men. For this reason also women are said to bear children to their husbands, because the name of the family always resides with the males.

units.la: In mysterio Ecclesiæ pueriliter prophetatur. Neque enim Ecclesia dicitur mater nostra, ideo protinus in carnali & spiritua li genera ione singulæ partes inter se respondent.
units.tr: He prophesies childishly about the mystery of the Church. For the Church is not called our mother for this reason, so that straightway in carnal and spiritual generation the individual parts correspond to one another.

units.la: Creatio nequaquam ostendit quod vult Menno, mulieres carere semine. Nam sicut ex viro creata est prima mulier, ita ex vtroque geniti sunt posteri.
units.tr: The creation by no means shows what Menno wants, that women lack seed. For just as the first woman was created from man, so from both are born the offspring.

units.la: Stultè à voce feminis ratiocinatur. Nam si femè hominis manu iactum terra excipitur, non inde sequitur, in coitu viri & mulieris idem valere. Quin potius contendere licebit, quia matres olim genitrices vocatæ sunt, semen earum ad generationem concurrere. Alioqui auunculi cum nepte sua perperam vetitum effet coniugium Lege Dei, quia nulla esset consanguinitas. Viro etiam liceret sorórem vterinam in coniugium accipere, modò ex altero patre esset genita.
units.tr: He reasons foolishly from the word "femen" [seed]. For if the seed of a man, thrown by the hand, is received by the earth, it does not follow that the same holds good in the coupling of man and woman. Rather, one may contend that, because mothers were of old called genitrices, their seed concurs in generation. Otherwise, it would have been wrongly forbidden by the Law of God for an uncle to marry his niece, since there would be no consanguinity. A man would also be permitted to take his uterine sister in marriage, provided she had been born of another father.

units.la: Non minus etiam inepta est ratiocinatio, quum dicit liberos censeri ex patrum conditione vel nobiles vel ignobiles. Sicuti enim virilis sexus præstantiæ hoc conceditur, ita etiá in seruitute partus ventrem sequitur, secundum Iurisconsultos. Vnde colligere promptum est t, ex materno semine fœtum procreari.
units.tr: His reasoning is no less absurd when he says that children are reckoned noble or ignoble according to the condition of the fathers. For just as this is granted to the male sex in its eminence, so also in servitude the offspring follows the womb, according to the jurists. Hence it is easy to gather that the foetus is procreated from the maternal seed.

units.la: Nec minus barbara est illatio Mennonis, si semen conferant mulieres, sore patres sui fœtus: quia mater non minus parens vocatur, quàm pater. Quum ergo parentum communi sit nomen, in patris & matris nominibus sola notatur sexus distinctio.
units.tr: Menno's inference is no less barbarous, that if women contribute seed, they will be the fathers of their own offspring, because the mother is called a parent no less than the father. Since therefore the name "parents" is common, the distinction of sex is marked only in the names of father and mother.

units.la: Vltimum argumentū per se euanescit. Sicuti enim fateor vim passiuam mulieribus adscribi, ita dico promiscué de mulieribus idem prædicari quod de viris. Neque enim Christus ipse factus dicitur per mulierem, sed ex muliere. Vnde apparet quomodo sine vlla verecundia latret hic canis. Quòd autem per ludibrium quærit, an dicere velimus ex semine mēstruali virginis procreatum esse Christum, scire rursum ex eo velim, an non in sanguine matris coaluerit Christus: siquidem matris partibus functam esse Menno ipse alibi non negat.
units.tr: His final argument vanishes of itself. For just as I admit that a passive power is ascribed to women, so I say that the same things are predicated of women indiscriminately as of men. For Christ himself is not said to be made through a woman, but from a woman. Hence it is clear how this dog barks without any shame. And as for his mocking question, whether we wish to say that Christ was procreated from the menstrual seed of the virgin, I in turn would like to know from him whether Christ did not coalesce in the blood of the mother: since Menno himself nowhere denies that she performed the functions of a mother elsewhere.

units.la: Solutiones quas colligit, Scripturæ testimonia non euertunt, vbi mulieribus tribuitur semen. Neque enim eadem vel æqualis est fœminæ acterræ conditio. Et quum dicitur quispiam esse ex femine mulieris,nō potest intelligi sub hac voce posteritas.Tet tio autem capite Genesis totum humanum genus semen mulie- ris non alio sensu vocatur,nisi quia verè ad generādum coope- ratur mulier.Locus etiam st.cap.ad Hebræos non tam facile elui se patitur,quòd Sara virtutem acceperit ad feminis pr oiectione, quia aperte verbum illud sonat emitti semen à mulieribus: & clara est allusio inter τεκνοποιοῦν... Quòd ad Christum attinet non efficiet sola & nuda promissio,vt dicatur prodiisse ex lumbis Abrahæ & Dauidis.
units.tr: The solutions which he gathers do not overturn the testimonies of Scripture where seed is attributed to women. For the condition of the woman and of the man is neither the same nor equal. And when someone is said to be "of the seed of a woman," this word cannot be understood as posterity. Moreover, in the third chapter of Genesis the whole human race is called the seed of the woman in no other sense than that the woman truly cooperates in generating. The passage also in the eleventh chapter to the Hebrews does not allow itself to be so easily explained away, that Sarah received power for the emission of seed, because that word plainly sounds that seed is sent forth by women, and there is a clear allusion between [the Greek word for procreating]... As far as Christ is concerned, a bare promise alone will not bring it about that it be said that he came forth from the loins of Abraham and David.

units.la: Absurda quibus nos grauare conatur,improbis calumniis reserta sunt. Nisi concedat Sermonem Dei ab initio fuisse eius quoque Filium,Deus tunc non fuit Angelorum pater: & tamen antequam nasceretur,matre caruit. Nos vero Christum homi- nem,qui ex Maria natus est, Dei non minus quàm hominis fi- lium esse concedimus,licet diuerso respectu. Neque enim instar Nestorij duplicem fingimus Christum,sed personam vnam con- stituimus ex duabus naturis,vt sit verè Deus manifestatus in carne. Doctrinam nostram hac in parte si respuit,Paulum ex quo verba mutuamur derideat.
units.tr: The absurdities with which he tries to burden us are stuffed with wicked calumnies. Unless he concedes that the Word of God was from the beginning also the Son of God, God would not then have been the Father of the angels; and yet before he was born he lacked a mother. We, however, concede that Christ the man, who was born of Mary, is the Son of God no less than of man, though in a different respect. For we do not, like Nestorius, imagine a double Christ, but we constitute one person from two natures, so that he is truly God manifested in the flesh. If he rejects our teaching in this part, let him mock Paul, from whose words we borrow.

units.la: Quòd Christum crucifixum contendit esse vnigenitum Fi- lium Dei,nos quoque idem docemus. Sed interea non tollitur distinctio, quam Christus ore suo diserte asseruit, corpus suum appellans Templum. Quomodo enim Templum esset Deus ipse, vel eius essentia?Deitatis ergo domicilium esse colligimus. Quò etiam spectat illud Pauli, habitare in eo plenitudinem Deitatis corporaliter.
units.tr: Where he contends that Christ crucified is the only-begotten Son of God, we too teach the same. Yet in the meantime the distinction is not removed, which Christ himself plainly asserted with his own mouth, calling his body a temple. For how would God himself, or his essence, be a temple? We therefore gather that his body is the dwelling-place of the Deity. To this also refers that saying of Paul, that in him dwells the fullness of the Deity bodily.

units.la: Quòd Christum diuidi calumniatur in Deum & hominem, si Deum & hominem esse dicimus,nullo negotio discutitur.Neque enim distinctio laceratio est. Eiusdem etiam impudentiæ est, quòd dicit Christum hoc modo conflari ex pura & impura natura,ex benedicta & maledicta: quia Paulus damnatum esse in carne peccatum pronuntians, prudenter nos ad similitudinem carnis peccati reuocat.
units.tr: That he slanders Christ as being divided into God and man, if we say that he is God and man, is easily disposed of. For distinction is not laceration. Of the same impudence is his saying that Christ is thus compounded of a pure and an impure nature, of a blessed and a cursed one: for Paul, pronouncing that sin was condemned in the flesh, prudently recalls us to the likeness of sinful flesh.

units.la: Pueriliter ratiocinatur, si per arcanam Spiritus operationem genitus fuit Christus ex matris femine, non fuisse igitur impu- rum semen muliebris,sed viri duntaxat. Neque enim ideo immu- nem ab omni labe facimus Christum,quia tantùm ex matre sit genitus,sed quia sanctificatus est à Spiritu, vt pura esset generatio & integra,qualis futura erat ante lapsum.
units.tr: He reasons childishly if, because Christ was begotten through the secret operation of the Spirit from the seed of the mother, the seed of the woman was therefore not impure, but only that of the man. For we do not make Christ immune from every stain because he was begotten only of his mother, but because he was sanctified by the Spirit, so that the generation was pure and whole, such as it would have been before the fall.

units.la: Quòd postea subiicit,totam Adæ sobolem absque exceptione sub peccato concludi, ideóque, Christum,si ex hominibus originem traxerit,non posse eximi à communi lege, facile soluit antithesis qua vtitur Paulus ad Rom.cap.5.v.12.Sicuti per vnum hominem
units.tr: As for what he subjoins, that the whole offspring of Adam is included under sin without exception, and therefore Christ, if he drew his origin from men, could not be exempted from the common law, this is easily resolved by the antithesis which Paul uses in Romans 5:12: "As by one man..."

units.la: Rom.14. hominem peccatum, & per peccatum mors, ita in gratia vnius hominis Christi abundauit gratia. Item 1.Cor. 15.v.47. Nec obstitit accidentalis corruptio Adæ, quo minus purus & integer ex eo nasceretur Christus.
units.tr: Rom.14. As through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, so in the grace of the one man Christ grace abounded. Likewise 1 Cor. 15:47. Nor did the accidental corruption of Adam stand in the way of Christ being born from him pure and whole.

units.la: Iam firmum est etiam illud, nec Mennonis cauillo eluditur, quoties de Christi puritate nos admonet Scriptura, notari verâ hominis naturam: quia superuacuum esset dicere, purum esse Deum. Sanctificatio etiam de qua loquitur Ioan. 17.v.19. in natura diui na locum non haberet. Nec vero duplex fingitur Adæ femen, quanuis nulla ad Christum contagio peruenerit, quia hominis generatio per se immunda aut vitiosa non est, sed accidentalis propter lapsum. Itaque nihil mirum, si Christus per quem restituenda erat integritas, à vulgari corruptione exemptus fuerit.
units.tr: Now this too is certain, and it is not undermined by Menno's sophistry: whenever Scripture reminds us of the purity of Christ, it signals his true human nature, since it would be superfluous to say that God is pure. The sanctification spoken of in John 17:19 would also have no place in the divine nature. Nor do we imagine a double seed of Adam, although no contagion reached Christ, because the generation of a man is not unclean or faulty in itself, but is so only accidentally, because of the fall. So it is no wonder that Christ, through whom integrity was to be restored, was exempt from the common corruption.

units.la: Frustra gartit Menno, si ex Mariæ femine progenitus sit Christus, illam fore patrem & matrem, quasi ad vulgarem regulam exigi debeat generatio, in qua Deus memorabile arcanæ & incomprehensibilis suæ potentiæ specimen edidit.
units.tr: Menno chatters in vain that, if Christ was begotten from the seed of Mary, she would be both father and mother, as if generation had to be measured by the common rule, when in it God displayed a memorable specimen of his hidden and incomprehensible power.

units.la: Illud porro axioma quod tam audacter subinde obtrudit, ἀπορον fuisse Mariam, probatione indiget, quia & philosophiæ & experientiæ repugnat.
units.tr: That axiom which he so boldly thrusts forward from time to time, that Mary was "without passage" [ἄπορον], needs proof, because it is opposed both to philosophy and to experience.

units.la: Idololatriam esse contendit, Deum in carne manifestatum adorare: nos vero negamus: cuius superbiæ est, nos suis placitis adstringere?
units.tr: He contends that it is idolatry to worship God manifested in the flesh; but we deny it. Whose pride is it to bind us to his own opinions?

units.la: Quod obiicit, si ex Maria progenitus sit Christus, Gentilem magis quàm Iudæum fore genere, quia progeniem ducat per foeminas à gentibus, eiusdem est futilitatis. Quasi vero Ruth proauia impediat, quominus censeatur Dauid Abrahæ filius.
units.tr: What he objects, that if Christ were born of Mary he would be a Gentile rather than a Jew by descent, because his lineage is traced through women from the nations, is of the same triviality. As if Ruth the ancestress prevented David from being counted a son of Abraham.

units.la: Quod etiam pro absurdo nobis obtrudit, si sermo Dei carnem induit, fuisse ig tur angusto terreni corpori sergastulo inclusum, mera est procacitas: quia etsi in vnam personam coaluit immen sa Verbi essentia cum natura hominis, nullam tamen inclusionem fingimus: quia mirabiliter è cœlo descendit Filius Dei, vt cœlum tamen non relinqueret: mirabiliter in vtero virginis gestari, in terris versari, & in cruce pendere voluit, vt semper mundum impleret, sicut ab initio profanæ etiam inscitiæ est, fingere verbum in morte ipsa à carne separatum. Sed velim rursum scire ex Mennone, quàm bene conueniat, essentiam Dei quam cœlum & terra non capit, exiguum corpus esse factum, quod in vtero virginis & in sepulchro latuerit. Nodum hunc si potest expediat, quomodo Deus eodem momento vbique fuerit Spiritus, & in terra fuerit homo palpabilis.
units.tr: What he also throws at us as an absurdity, that if the Word of God put on flesh, then the immense God was enclosed in the narrow prison of an earthly body, is sheer impudence. For although the immense essence of the Word has coalesced into one person with the nature of man, we imagine no enclosure at all. The Son of God descended from heaven in a wonderful way, yet did not leave heaven; in a wonderful way he willed to be carried in the womb of a virgin, to dwell on earth, and to hang on the cross, so that he always filled the world. Just as, from the beginning, it is a mark of profane ignorance to imagine the Word separated from the flesh even in death itself. But I would like to ask Menno again how well it agrees that the essence of God, which heaven and earth cannot contain, was made a tiny body that lay hidden in the womb of a virgin and in the sepulchre. If he can untie this knot, let him explain how God was at the same moment everywhere as Spirit, and yet on earth was a palpable man.

units.la: Hoc sanè video, nihil hoc asino posse fingi superbius, nihil petulantius hoc cane.
units.tr: This much I certainly see: nothing more arrogant can be devised than this ass, nothing more insolent than this dog.

units.la: Si fuisset vltrò moderatus, prodesse Ecclesiæ Dei poterat, sed dum ardet ostentandi acuminis studio, nulla religio vel modestia, vel etiam verecundia eum tenuit, quin omnia cōuellere tentaret. Atque ita dum suis speculationibus indulget, peruersis deliriis genuinam & simplicem pietatis doctrinam variè corrupit. Sed alia commenta nunc non attingam. In explicanda fidei iustificatione meris præstigiis se ipsum fascinauit, & aliios delusit. Admittit quidem quod negare ausus non est, remissionem peccatorum intercedere in homine iustificando: sed in primo & summo gradu locans spectrum essentialis iustitiæ, quod ipse finxit, nihil aliud relinquit gratuitæ Dei acceptationi, quâ vt sit inferior quædam appendix. Essentialem iustitiam sibi nulla ratione imaginatus est. Nam etsi eò trahit Scripturæ testimonia, quæ Deum in nobis habitare affirmant, & nos vnum cum ipso fieri: nihil tamen inde probatur, quàm arcana Spiritus virtute, dum coalescimus in Christi corpus, vniri simul Deo. Adde, quòd essentialis illa communicatio ex Manichæorum deliriis sumpta est. Nec video quomodo excusari possit hoc absurdum, essentialem Dei iustitiam esse accidens, quod adeò nunc homini possit, nunc abesse. Quanquam longa refutatione opus non est, si principium illud tenemus, iustitiam hominis in ipsa creatione fuisse rectitudinem, ad quam formatus erat, vt in singulis animæ partibus, adeóque in ipso corpore fulgeret Dei gloria. Quum ergo luce intelligentiæ præditus esset homo, & voluntate compositus in obsequium Dei, & eadem symmetria esset in singulis facultatibus, dicimus hominem fuisse iustum.
