Hac descriptione non contentus Osiander, Christum fingit non modò fuisse Idæam, sed primarium exemplar, vt Adam essentialis esset eius imago. Hinc commentum hoc, in quo ita se inebriauit, vt nullis absurdis sibi caueret.
units.tr: Had he been moderate of his own accord, he could have been of benefit to the Church of God; but while he burns with the desire to display his sharpness, no religion, no modesty, not even shame, has restrained him from trying to tear up everything. And so, while he indulges his speculations, by his perverse delirium he variously corrupts the genuine and simple doctrine of piety. But I will not touch on his other inventions now. In explaining the justification of faith, he has bewitched himself with mere illusions, and has deluded others. He does admit what he did not dare to deny, that the remission of sins intervenes in the justification of a man; but placing in the first and highest rank the phantom of essential righteousness, which he himself invented, he leaves to the free acceptance of God only some inferior appendage. He imagined essential righteousness for himself by no reasoning. For although he drags into it the testimonies of Scripture which affirm that God dwells in us and that we become one with him, nothing is thereby proved except that, by the hidden power of the Spirit, while we grow together into the body of Christ, we are at the same time united to God. Add that this essential communication is taken from the delusions of the Manichaeans. Nor do I see how this absurdity can be excused: that the essential righteousness of God is an accident, which can now be present to a man and now be absent. Yet no long refutation is needed if we hold to this principle: the righteousness of man in creation itself was rectitude, to which he was formed, so that the glory of God would shine in each part of the soul, and so in the body itself. Since, therefore, man was endowed with the light of understanding, and composed by his will to obedience to God, and there was the same symmetry in each faculty, we say that man was righteous. Not content with this description, Osiander imagines that Christ was not only the Idea but the primary exemplar, so that Adam would be his essential image. Hence this invention, in which he so drank himself drunk that he took no precaution against any absurdity.

units.la: Nunc postquam alienatus est homo à Deo, eum dicimus restituí iustitia, & sanctificatione, quarum prior gratuitam reconciliationem significat: altera renouatione hominis. Ergo quod ad voces spectat, perperam Osiander regenerationem confundit cū iustitia. Fixum enim manet illud Pauli, veram iustitiæ definitionem poni à Dauide his verbis, Beatus vir cui non imputat Deus peccata. Dicit Osiander, iustificari nos non tantum obedientia, quàm Christus præstitit, & satisfactione qua defunctus est pro expiandis peccatis: sed diuina æternaque eius iustitia. Longè aliter Paulus, qui simpliciter affirmat, iustificari nos obedientia vnius hominis, & alibi æqualiter pronuntiat datum esse nobis Christū in redemptionem, & iustitiam. Item factum esse sub Lege, vt nos à ma-
units.tr: Now that man has been alienated from God, we say that he is restored by righteousness and sanctification, of which the former signifies the free reconciliation, the latter the renewal of man. So, as far as the words go, Osiander wrongly confuses regeneration with righteousness. For that saying of Paul remains fixed, that the true definition of righteousness is given by David in these words: Blessed is the man to whom God does not impute sins. Osiander says that we are justified not only by the obedience which Christ rendered and by the satisfaction with which he died to expiate sins, but by his divine and eternal righteousness. Paul speaks very differently, who simply affirms that we are justified by the obedience of one man, and elsewhere equally declares that Christ was given to us for redemption and righteousness. Likewise that he was made under the Law, so that he might redeem us from the curse of the Law.

units.la: Rom.4.6 — Rom.5.19 — 1.Cor.1.30 — Gal.4.4 à maledictione Legis redimeret. Hæc porrò est iustitia, de qua vbique disserit, deleto reatu, recipi nos à Deo in gratiam. Et certè ad humanam Christi naturam refertur illud, Propter eos sanctifico me ipsum. Adhæc si caro Christi verè est cibus, & sanguis eius verè est potus, colligimus non aliter iustificari nos in ipso, nisi quatenus est propitiator. De recociliatione, quàm inscitè, ac peruersè loquatur Osiander, satis superque patet ex vno Pauli loco, Erat Deus in Christo mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputans hominibus peccata. Notanda est etiam quæ mox subiicitur iustitiæ ratio, Eum qui peccatum non nouerat, peccatum pro nobis fecit, vt iustitia Dei essemus in illo. Hæc breuis admonitio sanis & modestis lectoribus vtspero, contra Osiandri præstigias muniendis sufficiet. Neque enim longum volumen scribere nunc vacat, nec expedire iudico.
units.tr: Rom.4.6 — Rom.5.19 — 1.Cor.1.30 — Gal.4.4 Moreover, this is the righteousness of which he discourses everywhere: the guilt having been removed, we are received by God into favour. And certainly the words "For their sakes I sanctify myself" refer to the human nature of Christ. Furthermore, if the flesh of Christ is truly food and his blood truly drink, we conclude that we are justified in him only insofar as he is our propitiator. How foolishly and perversely Osiander speaks about reconciliation is quite plainly shown, and more than enough, by the one passage of Paul: God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing sins to men. Also to be noted is the reason for righteousness that follows immediately: he who knew no sin was made sin for us, so that we might become the righteousness of God in him. I hope this brief admonition will be sufficient for sound and modest readers, to fortify them against the illusions of Osiander. For I have no time now to write a long volume, nor do I think it expedient.

units.la: BLAVRERVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: Blaurer to Calvin, greetings.

units.la: EGo tibi tuisque omnibus omnia fœlicia ac fausta in vnica solidáque communi salute nostra Iesu Christo pro ineuntis nunc noui anni lætis auspiciis totis animis precor, mi colendissime charissiméque Caluine. Scripsi ad te proximis nundinis Lugdunensibus per Ioannem Linerum Sangalleum, mercatorem istac transfiturum, qui rediens sancte affirmabat suapte manu meas tibi esse redditas. Nihil verò vicissim abs te quod ad me perferret accepisse: quod ego sanè hoc ægrius tuli, quo maiori desiderio tuas expectaueram, ex quibus intelligerem, quibus rationibus illorum quorundam conscientiæ confirmandæ sint, qui in eadem flagitia, post toties perceptum Cœnæ Christi Sacramentum, subinde sunt relapsi. cùm tamen særiò nunc velle videantur resipiscere. Interim autem de impetranda peccatorum remissione, non satis fiduciæ sibi sumentes, quod dicant nulla eius rei in sacris literis exempla extare, quibus in omnibus aliis, quæ doceat, aut polliceatur, tantopere abundet. Ego profecto quanquam longissime abfuit à veteri ista hæresi, quæ relapsis pœnitentiam pertinaciter negabat, quacum etiam veteribus Ecclesiæ doctoribus nonnullis negotium fuit: nec quicquam dubitem omnibus quantumuis sæpe lapsis & relapsis, etiam in eadem grauissima peccata, aditum tamen ad gratiæ thronum, vt misericordiam consequantur, & gratiam inueniant, modò cum fiducia accedant. patere: ingenue tamen fateor, cùm fluctuantes illi adeò exempla desiderent ac flagitent, nulla me habere quæ proferam. Neque enim Dauidis, Petri, Pauli, latronis, aut peccatricis illius Euangelicæ exempla recipiunt, quorum singulorum longè sue rit alia ratio. Ad te igitur, mi præter cæteros semper mihi veneráde charißiméq; frater,confugio, vt hîc mihi tu adiuuas,quod facilè scio poteris,præsenti quapiam huius difficultatis disciffione, nè ipse aliis,magno ipsorum periculo desim. Scribas autem,per Iesum Christum te obsecro, vel exempla, si quæ forte nosti,quæ animo meo nulla ex scripturis succurrunt: vel certè ratione alí quam iuxta fidei analogiam afferr,cur nihil tale in scripturis no bis sit proditum, vt ex iis tandem angustiis boni quidam homines (sic enim mihi videntur) simul autem & ipse quoq; libere mur.Tu,ita me Christus amet,primus & solus es cui de hoc scribere visum est,quando nihil dubito,te imòDominum per te pro data tibi gratia,mihi,quæ animis nostris satisfaciant, perplexósque expediant,magna nostra consolatione,respondurum. Bene vale anime mi & fatisecntem senectutem meam,quò magis atq; magis in Christo ad æternæ vitæ nunquam intermoritura beatitudinem fœliciter reuiuiscat piorum vetorum auxilio,strenuè adiuua.Vituduri,v 11.Idus Ianuarij. M. D. L x.Sed quid Viretus? quid vero Beza nostr? Doctiss. & optimi viri. Beza valde miror nihil vel de Colignio,vel Galli rebus ad nos perscribere. Salutabis vtrunque mea vice quàm potes honorificè & amâter cum D. Archigrâmateo vestro Michaele Roseto, pariter & omnibus qui istic nos in Domino diligunt,quibus strenæ loco longissimæ ætatis curriculum,omnium corporalium & spiritualium bonorum concursu fœliciter fluentia,à nato mundi Saluatore(quæ vox au gustius quiddam ac diuinius quàm Seruator sonat)impetrata cū pio ac omnibus animi mei votis opto,ipsorum me facius precationibus diligentissimè commendans.
units.tr: I pray with all my heart that Jesus Christ, our one solid and common salvation, will grant you and all yours every happiness and blessing in this new year, which has just begun under happy auspices, my most honoured and dearest Calvin. I wrote to you at the last Lyon fair through John Liner of St Gall, a merchant who was passing that way. On his return he solemnly assured me that he had delivered my letters into your own hands. But I received nothing from you in return to bring to me, and I bore this the less patiently because I had waited with the greater longing for your letter, in which I hoped to learn by what arguments the consciences of certain people might be strengthened. These are people who, after receiving the Sacrament of Christ's Supper so many times, have again and again relapsed into the same wickedness, though now they seem to wish sincerely to repent. Meanwhile, they do not dare to hope for the forgiveness of their sins, because they say that Scripture gives no examples of this, although in everything else it teaches and promises so abundantly. I myself am far from that old heresy which stubbornly denied repentance to those who relapsed, a heresy with which some of the early teachers of the Church also had to contend. Nor do I doubt that all who have fallen, however often, and even into the same most grievous sins, still have access to the throne of grace, so that they may obtain mercy and find grace, provided they come with faith. But, to be frank, since those wavering souls long for and demand examples, I have none to offer. For they do not accept the examples of David, Peter, Paul, the thief, or that sinful woman in the Gospel, each of whose cases was certainly different. So I turn to you, my brother, who above all others have always been venerable and dearest to me, to help me here. I know you can easily do this by setting out some solution to this difficulty, so that I may not fail others, to their great peril. I beg you through Jesus Christ, write to me either with examples, if you happen to know any, since none come to my mind from Scripture, or at least with a reason, consistent with the analogy of faith, why nothing of this kind has been handed down to us in Scripture, so that at last these good people (for so they seem to me) may be freed from their distress. You, so help me Christ, are the first and only one to whom I have thought to write about this. I have no doubt that you will answer, and that the Lord will answer through you, with the gift he has given you, offering my people what will satisfy their minds and untangle their perplexities, to our great consolation. Farewell, my soul, and vigorously help my old age, so that more and more in Christ it may happily be revived to the blessedness of eternal life, which never ends, with the help of the pious. At Winterthur, 11 days before the Ides of January 1560. But what of Viret? What of our Beza, that most learned and excellent man? I am much surprised that Beza writes nothing to us about Coligny or the affairs of France. Greet both of them on my behalf as honourably and affectionately as you can, and likewise our chief secretary Michael Roset, and all who there love us in the Lord. To them, in place of a New Year's gift, I wish and pray with all my heart, and with all the desires of my soul, a very long life, happily flowing with a combination of all bodily and spiritual goods, obtained from the Saviour born into the world (a word that sounds more solemn and more divine than "Servant"). I commend myself most diligently to their prayers.

units.la: Tuus Ambrosius Bl.verum ita vt nullus sit magis.
units.tr: Yours, Ambrosius Bl., truly as no one is more so.

units.la: CAL. BLAVRERO DE RELAPSIS IN eadem peccata.
units.tr: Calvin to Blaurer, on those who relapse into the same sins.

units.la: TEmpestiuè domi meæ indicauerat Iacobus Linerts,ventu-ros hodie mercatores, qui literas meas tibi reddendas fideliter curarent:sed famuli mei obliuione factum est,vt tardius fuerim admonitus. Itaque si me ad breuitatem coget temporis angustia,dabis veniâ,præstantissime vir,& ex animo vene rãde frater.Quomodo in bonâ spem erigi possint eorum confcien tiæ qui in eadem sæpius peccata relapsi sunt,perinde me rogas,acsi mihi suppeteret melior ratio,quàm tibi,qui doctrina,vsu,& peritia me superas.Verùm vt intelligas nihil mihi esse pluris, quàm vt tibi morem geram,posthabito pudore aliquid tentabo.Ac primò tibi assentior, nullum in Scriptura reperiri singulare huius rei exemplum. Neque enim legimus vllū hominem,pòt datum poenipœnitentiæ signum, eiusdem delicti reatu sæpius implicitū fuisse. Verum ut fateor non parum valere exempla ad doctrinæ confirmationem, ita si hoc adminiculo carent, in ea una acquiescere tutò nobis non minus licet. Quid ergo scriptura doceat, nunc videndum. Prophetæ certè ad pœnitentiam passim hortantur, non qui semel deliquerant, sed qui obstinato Dei contemptu ruere non desiterant in omne scelerum genus, vel postquam simulauerant pœnitentiam ad ingenium postea redierant. Sæpe enim fraudis, aut malæ fidei accusant Israëlitas, quod falsò & dolosè præ se tulerint Dei timorem, quo vacui erant: & fallaci conuersionis prætextu Deum & seruos eius eluserint. Tamen ad pœnitentiam vocando, spem quoque proponunt veniæ impetrandæ. Hoc cum omnibus fere Prophetis commune est, tum luculentius ex Ieremiæ lectione patebit. Nec verò frustra Deus in Lege sacrificia, nunc totius populi, nunc priuati cuiuslibet nomine quotidie repeti voluit, tam pro ignorantiis, quàm pro voluntariis delictis. Nisi enim parata fuisset expiatio peccatoribus qui sæpius lapsi erant, non fatigasset eos inanibus figuris. Adde quòd Deum hypocritis & præsfractis exoratum fuisse vt ignosceret, ex Psalmo 78. colligitur: iam vbi cum suo Euangelio illuxit Christus, non semel atque iterum duntaxat propitium fore Deum promisit, si offensus esset, verùm toto vitæ curriculo suos ad deprecationem confugere iussit. Si non frustra ex illius ore & præscripto quotidie oramus vt remittat nobis Deus peccata, spes reconciliationis dubia esse non debet. Nec verò ipse idem magister, dum fratribus septuagies septies ignoscendum esse docet, plus indulgentiæ à mortalibus exigit, quàm à Deo sperare velit, qui misericordia omnes superat. Hac ratione Paulus quanuis fuerè queratur de Corinthiis, qui ante peccauerant, neque pœnitentiam egerant de immunditia, libidine, impudicitia: non tamen gratiæ veniam præcidit, sed metuere se dicit, ne cogatur suo aduentu eos lugere. Atque huc pertinet Pauli locus de perpetua legatione, qua sibi Deus Ecclesiam subinde reconciliat. Fideles enim non exteros illic alloquitur. Et Ioannes Christum nobis assignans aduocatum, qui nobis Deum propitiet, beneficium hoc non restringit ad diem vnum, sed continuationem designat. Sicuti etiam Daniel in illa solenni praecatione, qua obtinuit singularis vaticinij donum, peccata peccatis fuisse cumulata non dissimulat, & quidem continuo peruicaciæ tenore prouocat im fuisse Dei vindictam. Deniq; vbi in symbolo subiicitur post Ecclesiam remissio peccatorum, fiduciæ materiam nobis dari statuendum, ne desinamus ad mortem vsque in Dei clementiâ recumbere. Interea tamen acriter stimulandi sunt omnes, prout quisq; se peculiaribus vitiis obnoxium esse nouit,
units.tr: John Liner had told me at home, in good time, that merchants would come today to deliver my letter to you faithfully. But through the forgetfulness of my servant it happened that I was reminded too late. So if the shortness of time forces me to be brief, you will pardon me, most excellent man and my venerable brother in heart. You ask me how the consciences of those who have relapsed into the same sins so often may be raised to hope, as if I had a better argument than you, who surpass me in learning, experience and skill. But so that you may understand that nothing is more important to me than to meet your wishes, I will try something, setting aside my modesty. First, I agree with you that no single example of this is found in Scripture. For we do not read of any man who, after being given the sign of repentance, was again and again entangled in the guilt of the same offence. Yet, although I admit that examples carry considerable weight in confirming doctrine, if they are lacking we may safely rest in the doctrine alone. Let us now see what Scripture teaches. The prophets, certainly, everywhere exhort to repentance not those who had sinned once, but those who, with stubborn contempt of God, did not cease to rush into every kind of wickedness, or who, after feigning repentance, returned afterwards to their old disposition. For they often accuse the Israelites of deceit or bad faith, because they falsely and craftily displayed a fear of God which they did not have, and by a deceitful pretence of conversion they mocked God and his servants. Yet in calling them to repentance they also hold out the hope of obtaining pardon. This is common to almost all the prophets, and it will be more clearly seen from reading Jeremiah. Nor did God, in the Law, wish sacrifices to be repeated daily, sometimes in the name of the whole people, sometimes in the name of any private person, for sins of ignorance as well as for deliberate offences, in vain. For unless atonement had been prepared for sinners who had fallen again and again, he would not have wearied them with empty figures. Add that God was shown, from Psalm 78, to have been entreated by hypocrites and stubborn people, so that he would forgive them. Then, when Christ dawned with his Gospel, he promised that God would be propitious not merely once or twice if he had been offended, but commanded his people to take refuge in prayer for pardon throughout the whole course of their life. If it is not in vain that we pray every day, from his mouth and by his prescription, that God would forgive us our sins, then hope of reconciliation ought not to be doubtful. Nor indeed does that same Master, when he teaches that brothers must be forgiven seventy times seven, demand from mortals more indulgence than he himself is willing to hope for from God, who surpasses all in mercy. On this principle Paul, although he complains of the Corinthians who had sinned before and had not repented of their uncleanness, lust and impurity, nevertheless did not cut off the hope of pardon, but says he fears that when he comes he will be forced to mourn over them. To this also belongs Paul's passage about the continual embassy by which God from time to time reconciles the Church to himself. For he is speaking there to believers, not to outsiders. And John, when he gives us Christ as our advocate, who makes God propitious to us, does not confine this benefit to a single day, but indicates a continuing act. So too Daniel, in that solemn prayer by which he obtained the singular gift of prophecy, does not hide that sins had been piled upon sins, and indeed he proclaims that God's vengeance had followed with a continuous course of stubbornness. Finally, where the Creed adds after the Church the forgiveness of sins, we must maintain that a ground of confidence is given to us, so that we may not cease to rest in God's mercy until death. Meanwhile, however, all must be sharply stirred up, each as he knows himself to be liable to his own particular faults, so that they do not indulge themselves, but rather pay attention to the exhortation.
2 Cor. 5.18, and following

units.la: 1.Ioan.2.1; Dan.9.6. ne sibi indulgeant, sed potius attenti sint ad exhortationem Psal. Hodie si vocem eius audieritis:atque ut meminerint quàm graviter excandescat Deus aduersus eos qui trahunt funiculum iniquitatis.Etsi nihil fere est,quod scripsi:sentio tamen pro modulo penuriæ meæ longius prouectum esse,quàm opportuit:præsertim quia mihi cum homine prudentissimo & apprime exercitato negotiū erat.De rebus nostris prolixius & magis dextrè scripsisset Beza,nisi aliis curis fuisset distractus. Ipse & concionando & legendo strenuam operam impendit.Nihilo segnius in partes suas incumbit Viretus,qui aliquanto vegetior est quàm folebat. Me verò continuis fere morbis addictum puto:ita scilicet alios excipiunt. Videor quidé aliquid præstare: verum ut prælectionibus,concionibus,aliisque partibus mei muneris sufficiam, cogor decumbere bonâ temporis partem. Nisi me paululum recreet veris temperies,vale dicā posthac lucubrationibus.Molesta est crurum debilitas,sed magis infesta est imbecillitas ventriculi. Nuper enim largum sanguinis ex pulmonibus profluuium me prope suffocauit. Ergo non minus me ad migrandum incitat valetudo,quàm te senectus.Inter alias causas mihi ideo erit dies ille iucundior,quòd in hæreditatem nostrā recepti mutua nostra amicitia fruemur. Quò magis vota nostra coiungere par est,ut nos cœlestis Pater simul colligat.Statū Galliæ, partim quia valde urbulentus est,partim quia lugubris & calamito sus,vix attingere audeo.Sciuiiti,vt opinor,Regem quia audierat bonam partem Senatus Parisiensis ad fratres nostros mitius tractandos propensam esse,impulsu Cardinalis,venisse in Curiam, ac sententias rogasse.Quum censerent quidam non tam atrociter sæuiendum,neque tamen causam probari sibi ostenderent: vnus liberè & cordatè patrocinium causæ suscepit,neque dubitauit Regis excandescentiæ se opponere.Res Henrico indigna visa est,suo conspectu non percelli Consiliarios.Itaq; se extremo impetu proripiens,illum iussit in arce trahi.Sex horis potea in carcere alij sex coniecti,qui tamen moderatores fuerant, mò dissimulatione prodiderant sanctis doctrinam.Quidam honore sunt priuati:aliis multa impositæ:vnus tenetur.Ille verò in quē Rex exarserat,nuper exustus fuit. Virum modis omnibus egregium fuisse hostes quoque prædicant.Pollebat singulari iuris scientia, ingenio,& iudicio Rarae erat probitatis.Alius eius virtutes commendabat eius humanitas.Nepos erat Cancellarij à Birgo:&fratres eum inuitum traxerat ad gradum illum,quum priuatæ vitæ esset cupidior. Viri reuerentia & dignitas iudices tenuit diu suspensos.Coacti tandem sunt imperio Cardinalis supplicio addicere. Cùm sententia crudelis pronunciata esset, vt viuus cremaretur,prostratus in terram egit Deo gratias,qui tanto eum honore dignatus esset, ut pro defensione æternæ veritatis mortem oppeteret. Quatuor horis hilari vultu mortem expectauit. Vbi ad locum supplicij ventum est, quanquam eum quadringenti satellites circundabant: fuerunt tamen qui obseruarent, eum sponte acsi dormitum iret, togam & tunicam exuere. Sed quia laqueü collo iniecerat carnifex, admonuit non opus esse, quia læto igni erat ex more vstulandus. Respondit carnifex, aliud sibi esse man datum, vt eum strangulando cruciatum minueret. Iam victimam precationem fuderat: iterum tamen in genua procumbens gratias Deo egit. Iam sesquimensis elapsus est ab eius morte. Plures deinde fuerunt exusti. In singula momenta varij nobis ingeruntur terrores. Vtinam ex his documentis probe discamus, quid sit vita hominis super terram: ego præsertim cuius torpor non potest satis expergefieri. Vale.
units.tr: 1 John 2.1; Dan. 9.6. Ps. "Today, if you hear his voice," and that they may remember how grievously God is angered against those who drag the cord of iniquity. Although there is almost nothing I have written, I feel that I have gone further than was fitting, given the poverty of my abilities, especially since I was dealing with a most prudent man, thoroughly trained. Beza would have written more fully and more skilfully about our affairs, had he not been distracted by other cares. He labours vigorously both in preaching and in reading. Viret applies himself to his own duties no less, and is somewhat livelier than he used to be. As for me, I think I am bound by almost continual illnesses; so it is that others take the blow. I seem indeed to accomplish something, but to keep up with lectures, sermons and the other parts of my office, I am forced to lie in bed for a good part of the time. Unless a spring mildness restores me a little, I shall bid farewell to my studies from now on. The weakness of my legs is troublesome, but the weakness of my stomach is more hostile. For recently a heavy flow of blood from my lungs almost suffocated me. So my health urges me to depart no less than your old age does. Among other reasons, that day will be the more pleasant to me because, once received into our inheritance, we shall enjoy our mutual friendship. All the more reason, then, to join our prayers together, so that the heavenly Father may gather us together too. I scarcely dare to touch on the state of France, partly because it is very turbulent, partly because it is mournful and calamitous. You have heard, I think, that the King, because he had been told that a good part of the Parisian Parliament was inclined to treat our brothers more mildly, at the instigation of the Cardinal came to the court and called for opinions. When some judged that they should not rage so savagely, yet showed that they did not approve of the case, one man freely and wisely took up the defence of the cause, and did not hesitate to oppose the King's anger. The King thought it unworthy that his councillors should not be struck down in his presence. So, rushing forth in extreme fury, he ordered him to be dragged to the citadel. Six hours afterwards six others, who had been moderators, were thrown into prison, because by their dissimulation they had betrayed sound doctrine to the saints. Some were deprived of honour, many burdens were laid on others, and one is held in custody. But the man with whom the King had flared up was lately burned. Even his enemies proclaim that he was in every way an outstanding man. He excelled in singular knowledge of law, in talent and judgment, and he was of rare integrity. Another commended his virtues by his kindness. He was a nephew of the chancellor Du Bourg, and his brothers had against his will drawn him to that rank, although he was more eager for private life. The reverence and dignity of the man kept the judges long in suspense. At last they were compelled by the Cardinal's command to hand him over to punishment. When the cruel sentence was pronounced, that he should be burned alive, he prostrated himself on the ground and gave thanks to God, who had deemed him worthy of such honour as to meet death in defence of eternal truth. For four hours he awaited death with a cheerful countenance. When he came to the place of execution, although four hundred guards surrounded him, there were some who noticed that he, as though going to sleep, took off his toga and tunic of his own accord. But when the executioner had put the noose around his neck, he reminded him that there was no need, since he was to be burned by the joyful fire as is customary. The executioner replied that he had been given another order, namely to lessen his torment by strangling him. Already the victim had poured out his prayer; yet again, kneeling down, he gave thanks to God. A month and a half has now passed since his death. Many more have been burned since then. Every moment various terrors are heaped upon us. Would that from these examples we might learn well what the life of man upon the earth is; I especially, whose sluggishness cannot be sufficiently roused. Farewell.

units.la: AD QVAESTIONES ET OBIECTA Iudæi cuiusdam.
units.tr: Answers to the questions and objections of a certain Jew.

units.la: Quære, vicissim, quomodo vos dicitis Iesum venisse, vt mundare tho mines à peccatis, & vt educeret eos à gehenna, quum ille dum occisus est, auxerit peccatum Iudæorum, qui cruci affixerunt eum? Nam non potest inueniri maius peccatum, quàm sufpenfio Dei.
units.tr: Ask in turn how you say that Jesus came to cleanse men from sins and to lead them out of hell, when by being killed he increased the sin of the Jews who fastened him to the cross. For no greater sin can be found than the hanging of God.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quomodo lex data esse dicatur in salutem, quum tamen & transgressiones & reatum auxerit. Constat enim Iudæos statim irritum fecisse pactum Dei, & iustitiam legis violando iram Dei magis in se prouocasse. Imò quære, quomodo fœdus Dei quod singulare bonitatis testimoniū fuit, & adoptio qua filios Abrahæ sibi in peculium assumpsit, multis causa fuerit duplicis interitus: sicuti Ezechiel Israelem Sodoma & Gomor rha peiorem esse pronuntiat, hac sola de causa, quòd salutem sibi oblatam contempserit. Hinc certè apparet, improbis istis canibus nihil aliud curæ esse, nisi vt maledicant.
units.tr: Ask in turn how the law is said to have been given for salvation, when it has increased both transgressions and guilt. For it is clear that the Jews at once made void God's covenant, and by violating the righteousness of the law they provoked the wrath of God even more against themselves. Indeed, ask how the covenant of God, which was a unique testimony of his goodness, and the adoption by which he took the sons of Abraham to himself as his own people, have been the cause of a double destruction for many. Just so, Ezekiel pronounces Israel worse than Sodom and Gomorrah for this one reason: that they despised the salvation offered to them. From this it certainly appears that these wicked dogs have no concern except to curse.

units.la: Porrò ad eorum quæstionem facilis est responsio, venisse qui dem Filium Dei, vt Iudæis primum, deinde & toti mundo lucem vitæ afferret: sed tam Iudæos ab initio, quàm maiorem hominū partem sua malitia lucem vertisse in tenebras. Neque mirum est vel nouum, sic homines abusos esse Dei gratia, vt sibi exitiale redderent quod destinatum erat eorum saluti. Certè quum Deus se populi Redemptorem fore promittit, simul tamen denuntiat se fore in lapidem offendiculi Regno Israel & Iuda. Quomodo hæc inter se conueniunt, nisi quòd Deus vere & non fallaciter gratiam offert, vnde pendet solida populi fœlicitas? Sed increduli dum illam repudiunt, duplex sibi accersunt exitium: cuius rei documentum extitit in Dauide,qui Rex in huic finem creatus fuit,vt postea ex eo proueniret Meffias, & tamen vocatur lapis reprobatus à præcipuis architectis.Adde quod in persona Iesu, Meffiæ nostri, nihil accidit,quod non prædixerat iudæis Prophetæ deMeffia:ac præsertim Ifaias, qui magnifice extollere volens, quam per illius manum gratiam populo uo datuta erat, ita præfatur, Quis credet sermoni nostro? & brachium Domini cui reuelatum est?Dicturus erat paulo post, Meffiam reconcilia turum homines Deo,vt salui fierent,sed prius excla mat,magnà partem, cæcitatis suæ causa, priuatam iri tanto bono, quia virtus Domini sepulta illis erit,& incognita. Albi etiam clarius duo hæc coniungit, parum esse vt Meffias restituat desolationes Israel:sed fore salutem Iehouæ vsque ad fines orbis: & tamen non fore plenam restitutionem Israelis,quia bona parts ad Dominum non redibit. Denique perinde loquuntur Iudai ac fi nunquam gens eorum ingrata fuisset Deo,& ex medicina mortifierum sibi venenum fecisset.Certe exitum & reditus libertate illis Deus ab exilio Babylonico promittens, memorabile gratiæ specimen in illorum salutem edidit. Atqui maior pars impio contemptu culpam suam & reatum duplicauit: longe enim illis satius fuisset,non redimi,quàm abiicere & pro nihilo ducere tantum Dei beneficium.Sed hoc modo impleri vaticinium Ifaiæ oportuit,Si fuerit populus tuus vt arena maris,reliquiæ faluç fiet. Atque vt finem faciam, primum redemptio luculente ostendit oblatam Dei gratiâ non semper hominibus prodesse: quin potius fieri bis noxiam,vbi indigne prophanatur. Deus certe per manum Mosis populû eduxerat,vt omnium effet seruator. Atqui scimus horrendis vindictæ exèplis sæpius contra multa mil lia fulminaffe:tàdem immensa illa multitudo,exceptis duobus, miserè consumpta in deferto periit.Annon melius reprobis fuif set,nunquam egressos esse ex Ægypto?imò nunquam esse natos, quàm sic Dei manu prosterni?
units.tr: To their question the answer is easy. The Son of God indeed came to bring the light of life first to the Jews and then to the whole world; but both the Jews from the beginning and the greater part of mankind, by their malice, turned light into darkness. Nor is it strange or new that men have so abused the grace of God that what was intended for their salvation has become deadly to them. Certainly, when God promises to be the Redeemer of his people, he at the same time declares that he will be a stone of stumbling to the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. How do these agree with each other, except that God truly and not deceitfully offers grace, on which the solid happiness of the people depends? But unbelievers, while they reject it, bring a double destruction on themselves. Evidence of this appeared in David, who was made king for this very purpose, so that the Messiah would afterwards come from him, and yet he is called the stone rejected by the chief architects. Add that in the person of Jesus, our Messiah, nothing has happened that the prophets had not foretold to the Jews about the Messiah; especially Isaiah, who, wishing to extol magnificently by whose hand grace had been given to his people, begins thus: "Who will believe our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?" He was about to say shortly afterwards that the Messiah would reconcile men to God so that they might be saved, but first he cries out that for the most part, because of their blindness, they would be deprived of so great a good, since the power of the Lord would be buried and unknown to them. There too he joins these two points more clearly: it is too little that the Messiah should restore the desolations of Israel, for the salvation of Jehovah will reach to the ends of the earth; and yet there will not be a full restoration of Israel, because the greater part will not return to the Lord. Finally, the Jews speak as if their nation had never been ungrateful to God, and had never turned medicine into poison for itself. Certainly God, promising them a going out and a return from the Babylonian exile into freedom, displayed a memorable instance of grace for their salvation. Yet the greater part, by impious contempt, doubled their guilt and blame; for it would have been far better for them not to be redeemed than to cast away and count as nothing so great a benefit of God. But in this way the prophecy of Isaiah had to be fulfilled: "If your people be as the sand of the sea, a remnant will be saved." And to make an end: first, the redemption clearly shows that the grace of God, when offered, does not always profit men, but rather becomes doubly harmful when it is shamefully profaned. God indeed had led the people out of Egypt by the hand of Moses so that he might be the saviour of all. Yet we know that he often struck with dreadful examples of vengeance against many thousands; at last that immense multitude, except two, miserably perished in the desert. Would it not have been better for the reprobate never to have gone out of Egypt? Indeed, never to have been born, rather than be laid low in this way by the hand of God?

units.la: 1. Quære,quum scriptum fit in Matthæo,Non veni vt detrahe rem,&c.Et in lege Mosis habetur, Die autem octauo circuncidet carnem præputii fui.Itern,Omne præceptum quod præcipio tibi hodie,obseruabitis & facietis: non addes nec minues ex eo. Quod fi ita est,constat quòd legemMofis dissoluerit.
units.tr: 1. Ask, since it is written in Matthew, "I came not to take away anything," etc., and in the law of Moses it is found, "On the eighth day he shall circumcise the flesh of his foreskin," and again, "Whatever I command you today, you shall observe and do; you shall not add to it nor take away from it." If this is so, it is clear that he dissolved the law of Moses.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quum lex Mosis vetet quidquam operis fieri diefeptimo,quomodo eodem die iubeat masculos infantes circuncidi? Item quomodo Moses diem vnum e septem Deo sanctificari iubeat:Ifaias autem sub Christi Regno promittat continua Sabbatha,& continuas Neomenias,nisi quod in Circuncifione ostendit Deus opera sua eximia à communi lege:Ifaias vero aliquid excellentius promittens, quàm sub lege exhibitû fuerit. ritIudæis,significat præceptum de Sabbatho fuisse vmbratile?
units.tr: Ask in turn: since the law of Moses forbids any work to be done on the seventh day, how does it command that male infants be circumcised on the same day? Likewise, how does Moses command that one day in seven be sanctified to God, while Isaiah promises under the reign of Christ continual Sabbaths and continual new moons? Unless it is that in circumcision God shows his remarkable works to be exempt from the common law; but Isaiah, promising something more excellent than was exhibited to the Jews under the law, signifies that the commandment about the Sabbath was shadowy?

units.la: Plenior autem quæstionis solutio hæc est,quuam voluerit in vno tantùm altari Deus sibi offerri sacrificia,Ezechiel tamé pro mittit sub Regno Messiæ altaria in Ægypto,& Assyria fore:quû nefas alibi fuerit quàm Hierosolymæ Dei faciem quærere,& illi offerre sacrificia: Ifaias tamen templû illi fore in Ægypto dicit.Et Malachias discrimen omne locorum tollit his verbis, Offeretur incensum nomini meo in toto orbe.Certè clara externi cultus mutatio sub Regno Messiæ ostenditur:neque tamen hoc modo dissoluitur lex,vel apex vnus ex ea minuitur:quin potiùs hæc vera est legis sanctio,non fuisse in veteribus figuris obiectû oculis inane spectaculum,sed eorum quæ significabant,exhibitam in Christo substantiam.Nunc videndû,quorsum Deus Sabbathum instituerit, nempe vt symbolum esset sanctificationis, vt docet per Mosem & Ieremiam. Sequitur ergo præceptû illud inter vmbras numerandum esse.Quid enim mirû,si exorto Sole cesset stellarum lumen? Atque hæc est cœli & terræ nouitas,de qua Ifaias concionatur.
units.tr: A fuller solution of the question is this. Although God wished sacrifices to be offered to him at only one altar, Ezekiel nevertheless promises that under the kingdom of the Messiah there will be altars in Egypt and Assyria, whereas it was unlawful anywhere except Jerusalem to seek the face of God and offer sacrifices to him. Isaiah, however, says there will be a temple to him in Egypt. And Malachi removes every distinction of places with these words: "Incense will be offered to my name in the whole world." Certainly a clear change of external worship under the kingdom of the Messiah is shown; yet the law is not thereby dissolved, nor is one jot of it diminished. Rather this is the true sanction of the law: that in the old figures the objects set before the eyes were not an empty spectacle, but the substance of what they signified was exhibited in Christ. Now we must see why God instituted the Sabbath, namely to be a sign of sanctification, as he teaches through Moses and Jeremiah. It follows, therefore, that this commandment must be counted among the shadows. For what wonder is it if, when the sun rises, the light of the stars ceases? And this is the newness of heaven and earth of which Isaiah preaches.

units.la: 3. Quære,si Deus est,quare se ipse vocat filium hominis,quum in multis locis Scripturæ moneat lex, ne Deum similem faciamus homini:vt,Deus non est homo vt mentiatur,aut filius hominis,vt illum pœniteat.Præterea dicit Dauid,Nolite confidere in principibus,in homine &c. Item , maledictus qui confidit in homine. Hæc autem omnia fuerunt in Iesu, qui vocatur filius hominis.
units.tr: 3. Ask: if God is God, why does he call himself the son of man, when in many places Scripture warns by the law that we should not make God like man? "God is not a man, that he should lie, or a son of man, that he should repent." Moreover David says, "Put not your trust in princes, in man," etc. Likewise, "Cursed is he who trusts in man." But all these things were in Jesus, who is called the Son of man.

units.la: Quære,cur Deus in CaticoMosis vocetur vir bellicosus?Cur Ezechiel in illa memorabili visione memoret Iudicé in folio sedé tem esse similé filio hominis? Cur sibi toties Deus nares,oculos manus,& pedes attribuat?Cur Ieremias deFilio Dauidis locutus, pronùciet nomé Iehouæ in eû cõpetere? Cur Ifaias Meschiâ vocet Immanuel,Patre futuri sæculi, Deû fortem?Cur in Psal.quoque Meschiam sub Solomonis persona ornetur nomine Elohim?
units.tr: Ask why God in the Song of Moses is called a man of war? Why does Ezekiel, in that memorable vision, say that the Judge sitting on the throne was like the Son of man? Why does God so often attribute to himself nostrils, eyes, hands, and feet? Why does Jeremiah, speaking of the Son of David, declare that the name of Jehovah belongs to him? Why does Isaiah call the Messiah Immanuel, Father of the age to come, the mighty God? Why in the Psalm too is the Messiah adorned under the person of Solomon with the name Elohim?

units.la: Cæterum solutio quæstionis minimè difficilis est. Lex Deum vetat fieri similem homini,nempe ne sub hominis imagine pingatur eius maiestas.Alioqui & igni,& soli,& leoni,& vrso,& lapidi se comparat,quæ vel bruta sunt animalia, vel mortua elementa.Porro in MeschiaDeus non factus est similis homini:sed carne humanâ indutus,ita factus est homo, vt integer in æterna sua & immutabili natura maneret. Neque enim vt somniat Iudæi, credimus Deum esse mutatû,sed in carne manifestatû,&interea sui simile. Ita non fuit ex vulgari hominû ordine mendax, aut vanitati obnoxius,sed ratione Deitatis veritas in æternû perma nens:neque in eo tanquâ in homine mortali fiduciâ locamus,sed quia corpus eius Deitatis templû est,in quo habitat perfecta Dei gloria :& quatenus Deus est,in humanam naturam viuificam Spiritus sui potentiam transfundit. Nam certe locis compluribus non aliis salutis fiduciam Deus seruis suis proponit, quàm in Mschia,sicut in vaticinio Iacob apud Mosem, in te Gentes sperabunt. Vnde sequitur quod dixi, eundem esse Deum fortem& verum Immanuel, & Filium hominis, qui est ex progenie Dauid.
units.tr: Moreover, the solution of the question is not at all difficult. The law forbids God to be made like man, namely so that his majesty should not be painted under the image of a man. Otherwise he compares himself to fire, to the sun, to a lion, to a bear, and to a stone, which are either brute animals or dead elements. Further, in the Messiah God was not made like man, but clothed in human flesh; he became man in such a way that he remained whole in his eternal and unchangeable nature. For we do not believe, as the Jews dream, that God has been changed, but that he has been manifested in flesh, and yet remains like himself. Thus he was not from the common order of men, a liar or subject to vanity; rather, by reason of his Deity, truth abides in him forever. Nor do we place our trust in him as in a mortal man, but because his body is the temple of the Deity, in which the perfect glory of God dwells; and insofar as he is God, he pours the life-giving power of his Spirit into human nature. For certainly in many places God sets before his servants no other ground of hope for salvation than the Messiah, as in the prophecy of Jacob recorded by Moses: "In you the nations will hope." Hence follows what I said: that the same one is the mighty God and the true Immanuel, and the Son of man who is of the line of David.

units.la: 4. Quære,scriptum est in Ifa.c.66.17.Qui comedunt suillam, aut abominationem, aut murem aut mustelam vnà consumetur,dicit Dominus,Ergo suilla nunquam est permissa.
units.tr: 4. Ask: it is written in Isaiah 66:17, "Those who eat swine's flesh, or the abomination, or the mouse or the weasel, shall be consumed together, says the Lord." Therefore swine's flesh was never permitted.

units.la: Quære vicissim,quum scriptum sit apud Ifaiam,qui immolat bouem,perinde acsi hominem occideret,qui ouem mactat,perinde ac si interficeret canem,si quis inde colligat, Deum semper abominatum fuisse sacrificia, quo cauillo effugiunt Iudæi?Solutio autem ex abrogatione legalis cultus pendet,cuius ignorantia Iudæi tam stultè nuganter. Tenendum erat hoc principium, in omnibus ceremoniis quas præcepit Moses,instar regulæ suisse illi exemplar,quod Deus ostenderat in monte.Iam cum exemplar illud in Mschia fuerit exhibitum , nihil absurdi est, & aduentu suo vmbras omnes aboleuerit.
units.tr: Ask in turn: since Isaiah says, "He who sacrifices an ox is as if he slew a man, and he who slaughters a sheep is as if he killed a dog," if someone infers from this that God had always abhorred sacrifices, by what sophism do the Jews escape? The solution depends on the abrogation of the legal worship, and it is through ignorance of this that the Jews talk such foolish trifles. This principle had to be held: in all the ceremonies which Moses prescribed, the pattern that God had shown on the mountain served him as a rule. Now since that pattern was exhibited in Messiah, there is nothing absurd in this, and by his coming he has abolished all the shadows.

units.la: 5. Quære,quare vos affligitis diefexto,quo crucifius est,vt dici tur, quum crucifixione eius & pœnis sitis liberati ex gehenna. Debuistis potiùs festum agitare,epulari & gaudere.
units.tr: 5. Ask: why do you afflict yourselves on the sixth day, on which he was crucified, as they say, since you have been freed from hell by his crucifixion and sufferings? You ought rather to hold a feast, to feast and rejoice.

units.la: Quære vicissim,quare in die festo expiationis,Iudæi ex Legis præscripto animas suas affligant?quum tamen celebrent suam cum Deo reconciliationem.Decebat enim ipsos quoque cum lætitia potiùs epulari.
units.tr: Ask in turn: why on the festival day of atonement do the Jews afflict their souls according to the prescription of the Law, since they nevertheless celebrate their reconciliation with God? For it would have been fitting for them rather to feast with joy.

units.la: Nullo autem negotio refellitur eorum cauillum. Fatemur si quibus propositum est die mortis Christi sanctificare ieiunio & luctu, superstitiosè hoc modo & perperam fictitium cultum instituere.Nec verò corruptelam,quæ regnauit in Papatu defendi mus:sed interim nihil obstat,quò minus tota vita fideles redem ptionis suæ memoriam cum gaudio & canticis celebrent:& tamen cum gemitu suppliciter coram Deo reatu suum deplorent.
units.tr: Their objection is refuted with no trouble at all. We admit that if some have resolved to sanctify the day of Christ's death with fasting and mourning, they institute a superstitious and wrongly fabricated worship in this way. Nor do we defend the corruption which reigned in the Papacy. But meanwhile nothing prevents the faithful from celebrating the memory of their redemption all their life with joy and songs, and yet, with groaning, from humbly lamenting their guilt before God.

units.la: 6. Quære,quid fecit Iesu vltra reliquos sanctos? Nam Henoch & Elias ascenderunt in altum.Moses mutauit aquam in sanguinem , dulces reddidit aquas amaras,deduxit Israelem per medium maris. Elifæus fecit fontem olei,ex quo impleta sunt multa vasa,curauit lepram Naaman,& suscitauit duos mortuos : nihilominus tamen non credimus,quòd illi fuerint dij,sed viri iusti.
units.tr: 6. Ask: what did Jesus do beyond the other saints? For Enoch and Elijah ascended on high. Moses turned water into blood, made bitter waters sweet, and led Israel through the midst of the sea. Elisha made a spring of oil, from which many vessels were filled, healed Naaman's leprosy, and raised two dead men. Nevertheless we do not believe that they were gods, but righteous men.

units.la: Quære,an Moses hominem mortuum suscitauerit,quod fecit Elifæus,qui tamen Mose fuit inferior. Fateri etiā cogentur Mosen Iosuè discipulo suo maiore fuisse: neque tamen cursum solis moratus est,vt diem vnû efficeret ex biduo. Vnde sequitur,peram peram de personæ excellentia iudicium fieri ex nudis miraculis.
units.tr: Ask whether Moses raised a dead man, as Elisha did, though Elisha was inferior to Moses. They will also be compelled to admit that Moses was greater than Joshua his disciple; yet he did not delay the course of the sun so as to make one day out of two. Hence it follows that a judgment of a person's excellence is made foolishly and wrongly from bare miracles.

units.la: Puerilis autem hæc obiectio facile solui ur,quia non modò quærendum erat,quæ miracula ediderint Prophetæ,sed qua virtute.Christus autem quum discipulos maiora facturos dicit,quæ ipse fecisset, non eos sibi vel præferre, vel æquare voluit: quia penes vnum ipsum manet gloria operum, quæ sic per manum hominum exequitur,vt solus vere sit auctor. Quinetiam dicimus quæcunque Moses edidit miracula & post eum Prophetæ,proprie manant à Christo:quia fuit Angelus ille,quem Moses prædicat ducem populi & custodem. Quòd si qua funi gustus particula in Iudæis esset, statim agnoscerent quanta sit Christi præstantia & dignitas supra Mosen etiam in miraculis.Nō enim cœlesti panem quo nos Christus pascit, Patres aluit Moses in vitâ æternâ,& spiritualem.Sed vt profani sunt homines,imò impuri canes,nihil mirum,si ad gustandas cœlestes delicias sint prorsus insipidi.Cum bruto itaque suo stupore omittendi sunt.
units.tr: This childish objection is easily solved, because it was not only necessary to ask what miracles the prophets performed, but by what power. Christ, when he says that the disciples will do greater things than he himself had done, did not wish to set them above himself or make them equal, because the glory of the works remains with him alone. He carries them out through human hands in such a way that he alone is truly their author. Moreover we say that whatever miracles Moses performed, and the prophets after him, properly flow from Christ, because he was that Angel whom Moses names as leader and guardian of the people. But if there were even a small taste of this in the Jews, they would at once recognise how great is Christ's excellence and dignity above Moses, even in miracles. For Moses did not feed the fathers with that heavenly bread with which Christ feeds us unto eternal and spiritual life. But since men are profane, indeed unclean dogs, it is no wonder if they are utterly insipid to the taste of heavenly delights. So they are to be set aside with their brutish stupidity.

units.la: 7. Quære,quòd vos dicitis,illum esse Filium Dei, quum repetriamus in multis locis,Israelitas vocari filios Dei,vt filij estis Domino,est minimè verum,aut omnes Israelitæ sunt Dei.
units.tr: 7. Ask: when you say that he is the Son of God, since we find in many places that the Israelites are called sons of God ("you are sons to the Lord"), is that by no means true? Or else all Israelites are God's.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quum promisçue Israelitæ omnes sint filij Dei,cur peculiari elogio ornetur Dauid, vbi de ipso Deus pronuntiat,Filius meus es. Item,cur alibi Solomonem extollat supra omnes reliquos,his verbis,Ero ei in Patrem, & ipse erit mihi in Filium.
units.tr: Ask in turn: since all Israelites are indiscriminately sons of God, why is David adorned with a peculiar title, where God pronounces concerning him, "You are my Son"? Likewise, why does God elsewhere exalt Solomon above all the rest, in these words: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son"?

units.la: Iam satis refutata esset friuola eorum quæstio, nisi quòd pauca verba docendis simplicibus addere libet.Vocantur Angeli filij Dei.Idem nomen ad Reges & iudices transfertur: Dauidi autem tribuitur singularis priuilegij loco,cuius etiam respectu Angelos ipsos superat. Colligitur ergo,inter Filios Dei plures esse distinctos gradus. Quare nihil mirum, si Mefchia supra omnes eminet. Filium vero vnigenitum dicimus, & quidem natura, per quam adoptionis gratiam consequimur , vt reputemur ipsi quoque inter Dei Filios.
units.tr: Now their frivolous question would already be sufficiently refuted, were it not that it pleases us to add a few words for the instruction of the simple. Angels are called sons of God. The same name is transferred to kings and judges. But David is given it as a singular privilege, in respect of which he even surpasses the angels themselves. It is gathered, therefore, that among the sons of God there are several distinct grades. Hence it is no wonder if Messiah stands out above all. We call him the only-begotten Son, and indeed by nature, through which we obtain the grace of adoption, so that we too are reckoned among the sons of God.

units.la: 8. Quære,quomodo fuit Messias vester Rex pacis, quum toto illius tempore fuerit lis, & ab hinc non quieuerit mundus à bel lis.Scribitur tamen:Multitudini dominij & pacis non est finis, Isa.6.7. Et Iesu dicit, Non veni vt ponerem pacem in terra, sed gladium : quod si ita est, eius verba contradictoria sunt verbis Prophetarum.
units.tr: 8. Ask: how was your Messiah the King of peace, when throughout his time there has been strife, and from then until now the world has not rested from wars? It is written, nevertheless: "Of the increase of his dominion and peace there shall be no end," Isa. 9.7. And Jesus says, "I came not to send peace on earth, but a sword." If so, his words contradict the words of the prophets.

units.la: Quære vicissim,quando venerint Reges ex terris longinquis, & facti fuerint tributarij populo Israelitico:quando coacervatæ fuerint omnium gentium opes , vt cederent in prædam Iudæis: quomodo dicat Isaias extento vexillo rediturosab exilio in patriam esse: vbi sit splendor ille Templi secundi,quem pollicitus est Aggæus. Certe nisi istis nebulonibus ludibrio essent omnes Prophetæ, totaque Religio, longe alia reuerentia expenderent quicquid de suis beneficiis pronunciat Deus.
units.tr: Ask in turn: when have kings come from distant lands and become tributaries to the Israelite people? When have the riches of all nations been heaped up to fall as spoil to the Jews? How does Isaiah say, with a raised banner, that they will return from exile to their homeland? Where is that splendour of the second Temple which Haggai promised? Certainly, unless all the prophets and the whole religion were a laughing-stock to these scoundrels, they would weigh whatever God declares about his benefits with a far different reverence.

units.la: Solutio quæstionis est, quod allata per Christum pace non fruitur mundus, culpam alibi non hæreræ, quàm in hominibus ipsis quibus magis placuit sacrilegum bellum aduersus Deum gerendo, seipsos turbare. Neque tamen obstitit eorum prauitas, quo minus Messias & munus suum & muneris titulum retinuerit. Nec verò si pax non esset impiis, ideo sua virtute priuatus est illeimo quia spreta ab illis fuit reconciliatio cum Deo, oportuit horribili Dei vindicta in cæcum furorem impelli, vt mutuò inter se confligerent. Primi hominum Iudæi sua peruicacia montrarunt se cum Deo pacem nolle. Merito igitur sua ipsi viscera crudeliter ad vltimam vsque patriæ cladem laniarunt. Sequuti postea sunt alij, quisque suo ordine: quia nulla gens fuit extra hanc noxam. Sed eò melius experti sunt fideles Christum esse pacis principem, quia inter tam graues & atroces bellorum motus, quietis tamen & tranquillis animis Deum inuocarunt. Atque hanc pacem commendat Isaias cui subscribut omnes Apostoli, dum hunc præcipuum fidei fructum esse docent, vt Deo propitio freti, nō amplius tumultuemur, sed pacatis animis sternimus inter mundi agitationes. Quòd autem se Christus afferre bellum potius dicit, quàm pacem, id est accidentale: quia mundi impietas dissidia accendit, ex quibus graues pugnæ emergunt.
units.tr: The solution of the question is that the world does not enjoy the peace brought by Christ. The fault lies nowhere else than in men themselves, who preferred to wage a sacrilegious war against God and so to disturb themselves. Yet their perversity did not prevent the Messiah from retaining both his office and the title of his office. Nor, if peace was not granted to the impious, was he therefore deprived of his power. But because reconciliation with God was spurned by them, they had to be driven by God's dreadful vengeance into blind fury, so that they would clash with one another. The Jews first showed by their obstinacy that they did not want peace with God. Rightly, therefore, did they cruelly tear their own vitals, down to the final ruin of their country. Others followed afterwards, each in his turn, because no nation was outside this guilt. But the faithful have all the better experienced Christ to be the Prince of peace, because amid such grave and atrocious movements of war they nevertheless called upon God with quiet and tranquil minds. It is this peace that Isaiah commends, and to which all the Apostles subscribe, while they teach that this is the chief fruit of faith: that, relying on God's favour, we are no longer thrown into tumult, but with calmed souls rest amid the agitations of the world. But when Christ says that he brings a sword rather than peace, this is incidental, because the impiety of the world kindles dissensions, from which grave conflicts arise.

units.la: 9. Quæres, Si Deus est, quare texit sese carne, & quare non venit aperte, vt palam innouaret legem suam, vt non perirent homines huius ætatis? Maior enim est numerus eorum qui pereunt propter huius ignorantiam, quàm eorum qui redempti sunt. Obscuritate enim separantur ab illo, ne in illum credant.
units.tr: 9. You will ask: if God exists, why did he veil himself in flesh, and why did he not come openly, so as to publicly renew his law and prevent the men of this age from perishing? For the number of those who perish through ignorance of this is greater than the number of those who are redeemed. For they are separated from him by obscurity, so that they do not believe in him.

units.la: Quære vicissim, cur Deus qui cœlos inhabitat, voluerit latere inter Cherubim? & cur sibi domicilium sub pellibus elegerit? cur sacrum fœderis sui Symbolum insculpi voluerit pudendis hominum membris? cur elegerit Regem populo suo ex tugurio ignobili, & caulis ouium, qui etiam domi suæ contemptus, ab aliis repulsetur? cur obscurum & tenuem riuulum Siloe potius elegerit, quà celebres ac rapidos fluuios? & Iudæis exprobret, quod externæ magnitudinis pompam appetant?
units.tr: Ask in turn: why did God, who dwells in the heavens, choose to lie hidden among the Cherubim? Why did he choose for himself a dwelling under skins? Why did he will the sacred symbol of his covenant to be engraved on the shameful parts of men's bodies? Why did he choose a King for his people from a humble hut and the sheepfolds, one who, even when despised in his own house, is rejected by others? Why did he choose the obscure and slender stream of Siloam rather than famous and rapid rivers? And why does he reproach the Jews for seeking the pomp of outward greatness?

units.la: Facile autem refellitur eorum petulantia Isaiæ verbis, qui Messiam proponi deformé, multisque probris fœdatum, ac sine vllo decore, plagis afflictum, & diuinitus humiliatum, à quo fere omnes oculos auertant. Certe quin Messias vitæ sit imago gloriæ Dei, non audebunt Iudæi negare. Qui fit ergo vt Rex, per cuius manum potentiam suam exerere vult Deus, tam sordidus, imò infar leprosi deformis prodeat? Belluæ autè istæ pro sua superbia bia Deü ad leges suas adigere cuperent. Quasi verò vel nō viderit quid optimum esset factu, vel per incogitantiam prædixerit sibi ita placere. Atqui pietatis sobrietas hoc saltem requirit, vt Dei ar bitrio lōgè plus deferat homines, quàm propriæ imaginationi. Oblatrant isti canes, perire maiorē hominū partem, quia Christi obscuritate offensi, ab eo abhorreāt: quasi frustra exclamet Isaias obscuram fore eius notitiā, quia paucis reuelabitur Dei virtus. Et tamen verum est quod docet Apostolus, refulsisse in eo gloriā vnigenito Dei Filio dignam. Verum est etiam Euangeliū in quo refulget cœlestis Dei Maiestas, non esse obscurum nisi reprobris qui pereunt. Mirum autem est cur quærantur non magis confspi cuum fuisse Dei fulgorem in Christo, quorum patribus tolera bilis non fuit aspectus Mosis, donec velata esset eius facies.
units.tr: Their wantonness is easily refuted by the words of Isaiah, who sets forth the Messiah as deformed, defiled with many reproaches, without any comeliness, afflicted with blows and humbled by God, from whom almost all turn their eyes. Surely the Jews will not dare to deny that Messiah is the image of God's glory. How is it, then, that the King through whose hand God wishes to exert his power comes forth so squalid, indeed like a deformed leper? These beasts, in their pride, would wish to force God to their own laws, as if either he had not seen what was best to do, or had foretold through thoughtlessness that this pleased him. But the sobriety of piety at least requires this: that one should defer to God's judgment far more than to one's own imagination. These dogs bark that the greater part of men perish, because, offended by Christ's obscurity, they shrink from him, as if Isaiah cried out in vain that his knowledge would be obscure, because God's power would be revealed to few. And yet it is true what the Apostle teaches, that a glory worthy of the only-begotten Son of God shone forth in him. It is true also that the Gospel, in which the heavenly majesty of God shines, is not obscure except to the reprobate who perish. But it is strange why they complain that the splendour of God was not more conspicuous in Christ, when their fathers could not endure to look upon the face of Moses until it was veiled.

units.la: 10. Quære, quemadmodum fuit Iona in vīscerib̄us pīscis tri- bus diebus, & tribus noctibus, sic fuit Iesu in terra tribus diebus & tribus noctibus? Hoc non est verū. Nam etiam secundū verba vestra fuit tantum in terra tribus diebus, & duabus noctibus.
units.tr: 10. Ask: as Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights, so was Jesus in the earth three days and three nights? This is not true. For even according to your own words he was in the earth only three days and two nights.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quomodo sæpe totum populum nemine ex- cepto perfidiæ & impiæ defectionis accusent Prophetæ. Nam si ita est, vbi reliduum semen? quomodo dicatur totus populus Israeliam flagitasse ad necem: quum tamen certum sit, fuisse saltem nonnullos qui saluum optarent.
units.tr: Ask in turn: how do the prophets so often accuse the whole people, without exception, of treachery and impious revolt? For if that is so, where is the remnant seed? How can it be said that the whole people of Israel demanded his death, when it is certain that there were at least some who wished him saved?

units.la: Ad quæstionem breuis est ac expedita responsio. Satis notum est quàm trita sit etiam in Lege & Prophetis synecdoche, dum pars pro toto, vel totum pro parte sumitur. De numero dierum ne ipsi quidem Iudæi litem nobis mouere audent. In noctibus putant magis plausibilem esse calumniam, quia ante initium tertiæ noctis resurrexit Christus. Sed quum nox sit quasi diei accessio, non dubitauit Christus tres dies, & totidem noctes produo ponere, quò melius aptaret exemplum Ionæ ad præsentem causam. In re autem quum nulla sit ambiguitas, de verbis cauillari nugatorium est. Si excipiant non quadrare similitudinem, quia dimidio fere plus temporis transfegerit Ionas in ventre piscis, quàm Christus in sepulchro: responsio iterum facilis est, in exemplis plenam conformitatem exactè non requiri, nec absurdum esse, si qu dissimile notetur.
units.tr: The answer to this question is brief and simple. It is well known how commonplace synecdoche is, even in the Law and the Prophets, when a part is taken for the whole or the whole for a part. As to the number of days, not even the Jews themselves dare to raise a quarrel with us. As to the nights, they think the calumny more plausible, because Christ rose before the third night had begun. But since night is, as it were, an addition to the day, Christ did not hesitate to speak of three days and as many nights, so that the example of Jonah would fit the present case better. Since there is no ambiguity in the matter, to cavil at words is trifling. If they object that the likeness does not match, because Jonah spent nearly half as much time again in the belly of the fish as Christ did in the tomb, the answer is again easy: in examples a full conformity is not strictly required, and it is not absurd if some dissimilarity is noted.

units.la: 11. Quære, quum scriptum sit, Non videbit me homo, & viuet, quomodo Iesu fuit Deus, vt eum omnes homines viderint: & ne vnus quidem mortuus est ex his omnibus qui viderunt eum?
units.tr: 11. Ask: since it is written, "No man shall see me and live," how was Jesus God, if all men saw him, and not even one of all those who saw him died?

units.la: Quære vicissim, quomodo viderit Iacob Dei facie ad faciem, nec mortuus sit? quomodo Deus seruū suum Mosen discernat à reliquis Prophetis, quia familiariter facie ad faciem cum eo loquatur: nō autem per visiones, & somnia? quomodo toti populo apparuerit in nube, & columna ignis? quomodo visibilé glorię suæ formå ostenderit Ezechieli, & Isaiæ, qui tamen subita mor-te ideo extincti non sunt?
units.tr: Ask in turn: how did Jacob see God face to face and not die? How does God distinguish his servant Moses from the other prophets, because he spoke with him familiarly face to face, and not through visions and dreams? How did he appear to the whole people in a cloud and a pillar of fire? How did he show the visible form of his glory to Ezekiel and Isaiah, who nevertheless were not on that account struck dead?

units.la: Si qua perditis istis hominibus esset ingenuitas, pudareret ipsos tam crassis obiectis pugnare, imò effutire putidas nugas refuta-tione prorsus indignas. Negat Deus immensam gloriam suæ di-uinitatis humano sensu posse capi: quod sine controuersia fateN-tur omnes. Ergo notitiam sui ad captum, vel mensuram piorum attemperat, vt ipsum videant: nec tamen pleno adhuc aspectu pa-tiantur. In Christo autem viua sua imagine apparuit, quatenus tali facultas quàm salus piorum ferebat. Tunc autem videbunt eum qualis est, dum ei similes erunt. Hoc verò brutum stup[…]orem spi-rat, quod Deum in Christi persona visum fuisse garriant, acsi diuina eius essentia carneis oculis conspicua fuisset.
units.tr: If these wretched men had any ingenuousness, they would be ashamed to contend with such crude objections, or rather to spout putrid trifles wholly unworthy of refutation. God says that the immense glory of his divinity cannot be grasped by human sense, and all acknowledge this without dispute. Therefore he tempers the knowledge of himself to the capacity, or measure, of the godly, so that they may see him, and yet they do not yet suffer a full sight. In Christ, however, he appeared as his living image, in so far as the capacity and salvation of the godly could bear it. Then indeed they will see him as he is, when they are like him. But this brutal stupidity breathes out what they babble, that God was seen in the person of Christ, as if his divine essence had been visible to carnal eyes.

units.la: Quære, scriptum est, quod quicunq; fidem habuerit in Iesu, etiam tantùm quantùm sunt grana sinapi, poterit iuxta eius ver-bum, transferre montem è loco suo. Nos autem vidimus etiam sanctiores eorum, qui ne leuem quidem rem facere possunt. Er-go quanto minus reliquum vulgus? Quòd si ita est, nulla est in eorum manu neque dominatio, neque potetia, qua possint quic-quam præstare, quanuis credant in eum.
units.tr: Ask: it is written that whoever has faith in Jesus, even only as great as a grain of mustard, can, according to his word, move a mountain from its place. But we have seen even the holier of them unable to do even a slight thing. How much less, then, the common crowd? If that is so, there is in their hands neither lordship nor power by which they could accomplish anything, however much they believe in him.

units.la: Quære, quum scriptum sit de môte Zion, hæc requies mea in seculum seculi, hic habitabo quoniam elegi eam, quid sibi velit vastitas & desolatio, quæ tot iam seculis durauit? Quære iterum, quid sibi velit, quòd miserè dissipati per totum orbem vagantur, & prostrati in ruinis suis iacent, quum Isaias pronunciet redem-ptos esse ab exilio Babylonico, vt ruinas mundi totius instau-rent, & in corpus suum colligant omnes dispersos?
units.tr: Ask: since it is written of Mount Zion, "This is my rest for ever and ever; here will I dwell, for I have chosen it," what does the waste and desolation mean, which has now lasted for so many centuries? Ask again, what does it mean that they, miserably scattered, wander through the whole world and lie prostrate in their ruins, when Isaiah declares that they have been redeemed from the Babylonian exile, to restore the ruins of the whole world and gather into one body all who are scattered?

units.la: Si granum salis vel sanæ intelligentiæ in istis pecudibus esset, sine controuersia verissimum esse cognoscerent Christi dictum, in quo absurditatem venatur. Quod obiiciunt, cur Christus suis discipulis dixerit notandum est, nempe vitio eorum fieri expro-brans, vt miraculaedere frustra tentarent. Quid ergo si fateamur dono miraculorum, quo suos instruxit Christus, nos proprià cul-pa destitui? Pudenda quidem nobis est hæc confessio: sed cur po-tius in crimen trahetur ille, qui æterna est Dei veritas, & lucu-lentis documetis se in hoc dicto veracem ostendit, potius quàm vanis coloribus tegatur nostra infidelitas, quæ Dei gratiæ viam præcludit. Quanquà aliud simul tenendum est, fidem de qua nunc agitur, non illam esse communem, quâ piis omnibus & Christi membris affert adoptionis Spiritus: sed qua oportuit Apostolos iniunctu sibi munus amplecti, nempe vt nouam Euangelij do-ctrinam, quæ nondum publico consensu recepta erat, miraculis sancirent. Idem verò donum nequaquam promiscuè ad omnes pertinet. Sicuti enim satis fuit in monte Sinai signis & prodigiis semel
units.tr: If there were a grain of salt or of sound understanding in these beasts, they would without doubt recognise as most true the saying of Christ, in which they hunt for absurdity. As to what they object, why Christ said it to his disciples, it should be noted that he said it to reproach their fault, since they tried in vain to work miracles. What then if we confess that we are deprived of the gift of miracles, with which Christ equipped his own, through our own fault? This confession is indeed shameful for us; but why should he rather be charged with the crime, who is the eternal truth of God and who in this saying shows himself truthful by clear teaching, than our unbelief, which closes the way to God's grace, be covered with empty colours? Yet at the same time another point must be held: the faith now under discussion is not that common faith by which the Spirit of adoption is brought to all the godly and members of Christ, but that by which the Apostles had to embrace the office laid upon them, namely to confirm by miracles the new doctrine of the Gospel, which was not yet received by general consent. Moreover, this gift by no means pertains indiscriminately to all. For just as it was enough that the Law was confirmed once by signs and prodigies on Mount Sinai when it was promulgated, so the Gospel ought to have been sufficient to win faith and authority through continual miracles for thirty years. For we do not read that the individual Prophets were endowed with this power, because it did not seem good to God. Whatever spiritual goods Christ bestows on his own, it is no wonder that they are held as nothing by those profane men, who are more than insipid when it comes to tasting all parts of heavenly life.

units.la: Ind. 12.
units.tr: Judg. 12.

units.la: Cal. semel confirmari Legem dum promulgata fuit:sic abunde suffi-cere debuit Euangelium per triginta annos continuis miraculis fidem & auctoritatem acquirere. Nam Prophetas singulos non legimus hac virtute fuisse prœditos:quia expedire Deo visum nō est.Quicquid vero spiritualium bonorum Christus suis confert, non mirū est à profanis istis pro nihilo duci,qui ad omnes cœ-leftis vitæ partes gustandas plufquàm insipidi sunt.
units.tr: Once, when it was promulgated, the Law was confirmed; so the Gospel ought to have been sufficient to acquire faith and authority through continual miracles for thirty years. For we do not read that the individual Prophets were endowed with this power, because it did not seem good to God. Whatever spiritual goods Christ bestows on his own, it is no wonder that they are held as nothing by those profane men, who are more than insipid when it comes to tasting all parts of heavenly life.

units.la: 13. Quære, si Messias vester Deus est, quare inequitauit bestiæ pollutæ,quum scriptum fit in lege,Neque oues neque boues pas-cent e regione montis illius. Quid igitur? si prohibuit ne bestiæ quidem mundæ pascerent,quàtò magis ne immundæ? Is autem ipsemet insidet bestiæ pollutæ.
units.tr: 13. Ask: if your Messiah is God, why did he ride on an unclean beast, since it is written in the Law, "Neither sheep nor oxen shall feed over against that mountain"? What then? If he forbade even clean beasts to graze there, how much more the unclean? Yet he himself sits upon an unclean beast.

units.la: Quære vicissim,an sanctus Rex & Propheta Dauid super mulum equitando sese polluerit? an alij præterea sancti homines, quorum passim occurrunt in Scripturis exempla,quoties asinis vecti sunt,maculam contraxerint?
units.tr: Ask in turn: did the holy king and prophet David defile himself by riding on a mule? Did other holy men, of whom examples occur everywhere in the Scriptures, contract a stain whenever they rode on asses?

units.la: Primùm quando ne Diuinis quidem vaticiniis parcit eorum petulantia,non videtur operæpretium pluribus verbis eam refu-tare.Quemcunque sibi tandem Messiâ fingant,non de alio quàm de Messia locum Zachariæ exponere licebit,Lætere filia Sion,ecce Rex tuus venit tibi,equitâs super asinum,&c. Quid cum Pro-pheta litigando proficient? imò an non putida ista subsannatio fatis conuincit quod prius dixi,non tam ludibrio illis esse Chri-ftum nostrum,quàm legem.& omnes Prophetas?Nam si Zachariæ sunt discipuli,nodum hunc nobis expediant. Nimis autem infulsi est cauillatio , prohibitas fuisse in legis promulgatione bestias ab accessu montis: quia si Deus locum illum sibi ad pau-cos dies segregare voluit,vt neque homo,neque vllū aliud animal illuc accederet,non ideo excluditur Messias à communi vitæ humanæ vsu Quid autē cōtagionis in eo reperient,si filius Daui-dis super afinū conscenderit? Nec verò dubiū est quorsum spe-ctaue-rit Zacharias,nempe venturū Redemptorem, qui non fulgeat regia pompa & apparatu,sed pauper fit,& quasi vnus ex vulgo.
units.tr: First, since their wantonness does not spare even the divine prophecies, it does not seem worthwhile to refute it at length. Whatever Messiah they finally imagine for themselves, the passage of Zechariah cannot be expounded of anyone but the Messiah: "Rejoice, daughter of Zion; behold, your King comes to you, riding on an ass," and so on. What do they gain by quarrelling with the Prophet? Indeed, does not this putrid mockery sufficiently prove what I said before, that it is not so much our Christ who is the derision of these men as the Law and all the Prophets? For if they are disciples of Zechariah, let them untie this knot for us. But the cavil that beasts were forbidden access to the mountain at the promulgation of the Law is too silly. For if God wished that place to be set apart for a few days, so that neither man nor any other animal should approach it, the Messiah is not thereby excluded from the common use of human life. What contagion will they find in it if the son of David mounted an ass? Nor is it doubtful to what end Zechariah looked, namely that a Redeemer would come who would shine not with royal pomp and display, but would be poor and as one of the common people.

units.la: 14. Quære,quare esuriit Iesu?Si dixeris propter carnem,nos vi dimus Mosen, qui fuit etiam caro, & sanguis, & ieiunauit qua-draginta diebus & quadraginta noctibus quum accessit Diuini-tatem,nec esuriit:hic autem,qui erat ipsemet Deus,quare esuriit caro eius?
units.tr: 14. Ask: why did Jesus hunger? If you say, because of the flesh, we see Moses, who was also flesh and blood, and who fasted forty days and forty nights when he drew near to the divine majesty, and did not hunger. But this one, who was himself God, why did his flesh hunger?

units.la: Quære.cur Angeli apud Abraham comederint?quomodo vexati fuerint contumeliose à Sodomitis? quomodo dicat Deus Mosen sibi obstare,ne vindictam quam statuit exerceat?
units.tr: Ask: why did the angels eat with Abraham? How were they shamefully handled by the Sodomites? How does God say that Moses stood in his way, so that he could not carry out the vengeance he had determined?

units.la: Nullius apud istos porcos momenti solutio est, Chriftū ideo esuriisse,quia carnem nostram induens,simul famem,& huma-nos alios affectus,excepta tantùm omni corruptela,induit. Rationem afferunt, quia non idem legatur de Mose. Sed an putant sanctum Prophetam postea rediisse ad solitum victum, nisi eum cogeret naturæ infirmitas? Luxuria enim alioquin fuisset, alimenta superfluo abusu consumere. Quid de Elia quoque sentiut? Nam certe quum de utroque diserte pronuntiat Spiritus quadraginta diebus ieiunasse, satis offendit non longius pertinuisse ipsos in mediam. Christus ergo ad præcdicandum Euangelium se accingens, exordium a ieiunio quadraginta dierum fecit, ne Mose vel Elia esset inferior. Ita liquido apparuit, cœlesti virtute eximii a necessitate cibi et potus, cui subiecti sunt cuncti mortales. Sed quia non minus utile erat, fratrem a nobis agnosci, cui nobis cum humanæ vitæ conditio esset communis, ad ea quæ propria sunt hominis, statim reuersus est. Non quod in eo dominatę sint humanæ infirmitates, nisi quatenus mero suo arbitrio se submittit, ut nobis esset similis.
units.tr: The solution of these swine is worth nothing: that Christ hungered because, by putting on our flesh, he also put on hunger and the other human affections, excepting only corruption. They give as their reason that the same is not read of Moses. But do they think the holy prophet afterwards returned to his usual diet unless the weakness of nature compelled him? Otherwise it would be luxury to consume food with superfluous abuse. What do they think about Elijah too? For since the Spirit expressly says that both fasted for forty days, it is clear enough that they did not hold out any longer than that. Christ therefore, girding himself to preach the gospel, began with a fast of forty days, so as not to be inferior to Moses or Elijah.
