Thus it became plain that he was set apart by heavenly power from the necessity of food and drink, to which all mortals are subject. But since it was no less useful for us to recognise him as a brother, whose condition of human life was common with ours, he returned at once to the things proper to man. Not that human infirmities ruled over him, except insofar as by his own free will he submitted himself so that he might be like us.

units.la: 15. Quære, si agnus Paschatis designabat Iesum, sequitur multos Iesus nascendos et subpendendos. Nam non præcepit filiis Israël, ut unum tantum agnum Paschatis acciperent.
units.tr: 15. Ask: if the Passover lamb designated Jesus, does it follow that Jesus was to be born and hanged on the cross many times? For he did not command the sons of Israel to take only one Passover lamb.

units.la: Quære, an nihil significauerint omnes victimæ, quæ in Templo immolabantur? Nam si ita esset, nihilo præcellerent Ægyptiis superstitionibus. Deinde scimus Mosi præceptum esse, ut omnia formaret ad exemplar quod in monte viderat. Atqui Diuinū illud fuisse negare non audebunt. An ideo concedent plures, imo innumeros esse Deos? Quære etiam, quum Pascha memoriale et pignus fuerit redemptionis, an totidem fuisse dicent redemptiones, quot agnos per singulas familias Deus iussit mactari?
units.tr: Ask: did all the victims sacrificed in the Temple signify nothing? For if so, they would in no way surpass the superstitions of the Egyptians. Next, we know that Moses was commanded to form everything according to the pattern he had seen on the mountain. Yet they will not dare to deny that this was divine. Will they then concede that there are several, indeed innumerable, gods? Ask also: since the Passover was a memorial and pledge of redemption, will they say that there were as many redemptions as lambs God ordered to be slaughtered through the individual households?

units.la: Nos vero liberè profitemur quod dictat ipsa pietas, non modo agnum Paschalem fuisse Christi figuram, sed et omnia sacrificia: quia nimis crasse somniant Deum adipis fœtore, vel aspectu sanguinis vel pecudum cæde placatum fuisse hominibus, et talibus piaculis purgata fuisse peccata. Ergo in toto legali cultu aliquid præstantius adumbrauit Deus. Sed hinc plusquam sto lidè colligunt, plures nobis reperiendos Christos. Nam ut scirent Patres sub Lege non dum se stare in perfecto gradu, voluit Deus in quærenda reconciliatione ad eadem illos remedia confugere. Si ad expiationem efficax fuisset bouis aut vituli immolatio, satis fuisset vno tantum sacrificio defungi. Sed repetitio admonuit, in figuris illis nihil esse perfectum. Eadem ratione diximus Sacerdotes omnes gestasse Christi personam, ideoque plures fuisse, quia mors honore singulos priuabat. Christus autem, qui ideo resurrexit a mortuis, ut perpetuo Sacerdotio fungatur, unicus est. Ne longior sim in re plusquam facili, apud sanos omnes fateri licebit, Regnum quod erexit Deus in familia Daui-dis, ab ipso usque ad omnes eius successores, futuri Messiæ fuisse prælapræludium. Nemo tamé vsque adeò desipiet, vt nobis propterea exprobret plures esse Christos.
units.tr: But we freely profess what piety itself dictates: not only was the Paschal lamb a figure of Christ, but so were all the sacrifices. For they dream too crudely that God was appeased toward men by the stench of fat, or by the sight of blood, or by the slaughter of cattle, and that sins were purged by such expiations. So in the whole legal worship God foreshadowed something more excellent. But from this they very absurdly conclude that many Christs are to be found by us. For that the Fathers under the Law might know they did not yet stand in the perfect degree, God willed them, in seeking reconciliation, to flee to those same remedies. If the immolation of an ox or calf had been effective for expiation, it would have been enough to discharge the duty with one sacrifice. But repetition warned that nothing in those figures was perfect. By the same reasoning we have said that all the priests bore the person of Christ, and that there were many of them because death deprived each of the honour. Christ, however, who for this reason rose from the dead so that he might exercise the priesthood perpetually, is unique. Not to be longer on a matter that is more than easy: all sane people will admit that the kingdom which God set up in the house of David, from David himself to all his successors, was the prelude to the future Messiah. Yet no one will be so foolish as to reproach us on that account for there being many Christs.

units.la: 16. Quære, Accipite hunc panem, hoc est corpus meum: & hoc vinum, est sanguis meus pro nouo fœdere, quomodo factū est hoc? Aut fregit fructum carnis suæ, & dedit illis: aut eius corpus factum est ex pane & vino, dedítque illis ex reliquiis, & hoc est corpus, quod comederunt & biberunt.
units.tr: 16. Ask: "Take this bread, this is my body; and this wine is my blood of the new covenant": how has this come about? Either he broke the fruit of his flesh and gave it to them, or his body was made from bread and wine and he gave them the remnants, and this is the body they ate and drank.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quādo inuitat Deus omnes per Ifaiam, vt gratis ad satietatem bibant lac & vinum, & mel comedant, an lacte vel melle corruptibili saginare tantum vult suorū ventres? Quære item, quādo in Psalmo dicitur, Satiabis eos copia domus tuæ, & fluuio deliciarum tuarum potabis eos, an cœlestem vitam Propheta alimentis sustineri intelligat?
units.tr: Ask in turn: when God invites all through Isaiah to drink milk and wine and eat honey freely, to the full, does he wish to fatten the bellies of his people only with perishable milk or honey? Ask likewise: when it is said in the Psalm, "They shall be satisfied with the abundance of your house, and you shall give them drink from the river of your delights," does the prophet understand that heavenly life is sustained by food?

units.la: Quæstionis solutio expura & dextra verborum Domini interpretatione pendet, quæ si crasso commento sub Papatu fuerunt corrupta, non est cur propter hominum inscitiā recte fidei insultent istæ bestiæ. Christus certè neque fructulatim secuit cor pus suum, neque illud ex pane & vino conflauit: sed tamen spiritusali modo vescendum dedit Apostolis, sicuti quotidie arcana Spiritus sui virtute facit, vt caro sua cibus sit noster. Dicimus ergo vere comedisse Apostolos carnem Christi, non qualiter comedi solet caro ex macello empta, sed quia non aliter animas ipsorū aluit Christus, sicut nostras quotidie alit in spiritualem vitam, quàm pane & cibo corpus pascitur.
units.tr: The solution depends on a pure and correct interpretation of the Lord's words. If these were corrupted under the Papacy by a crude invention, there is no reason why those beasts should insult sound faith because of men's ignorance. Christ certainly neither cut up his body piece by piece, nor fused it together from bread and wine. Yet he gave it to the apostles to eat in a spiritual manner, as he does daily by the secret power of his Spirit, so that his flesh may be food for us. We therefore truly say that the apostles ate the flesh of Christ, not in the way that flesh bought from the butcher is usually eaten, but because Christ nourished their souls no otherwise than he daily nourishes ours to spiritual life, just as the body is fed by bread and food.

units.la: 17. Quære, quorsum angustia animæ eius propter mortem? Si dixeris id esse propter carnem quæ patet, nōne ille dicit, angustia animæ meæ, nō autem angustia carnis meæ? Itē, nullus est qui nesciat, carnem non lapidem, nisi adsit vis Spiritus.
units.tr: 17. Ask: why was his soul in anguish because of death? If you say that this was because of the flesh, which is exposed, does he not say "the anguish of my soul", not "the anguish of my flesh"? Likewise, there is no one who does not know that flesh is not a stone, unless the power of the Spirit is present.

units.la: Quære, si caro sensu & motu omni caret, quomodo dicat Iaias, Videbit omnis caro gloriam Dei? Cur dicat Moses, Omnis caro corrupit viam suam? Imò cur vbique tota Lex carni adscribat, quæcunque in hominem competunt?
units.tr: Ask: if flesh lacks all sense and motion, how does Isaiah say, "All flesh shall see the glory of God"? Why does Moses say, "All flesh had corrupted its way"? Indeed, why does the whole Law everywhere ascribe to flesh whatever belongs to man?

units.la: Hinc verò planū fit, quàm sine iudicio artôdat rabiosi isti cahes, quicquid ex nouo Testamento proferri audiūt. Nihil notius est, vel magistritū quàm sub carnis voce designari homines: atque itatā animā, quā corpus cōprehēdi. Quōd ergo Christū mortem exhorruisse in carne dicimus, ad humanā eius naturam referrtur: quia fieri non potuit, quin verus homo naturaliter mortem refugeret: mœrorem interea hunc & angustias pertulit in anima, quia corpus induedo simul animā passibilem assumpsit.
units.tr: Hence it is plain how, without judgment, those rabid dogs bark at whatever they hear brought forward from the New Testament. Nothing is more familiar, even to schoolboys, than that men are designated by the word flesh, and so the soul is comprehended under the body. Therefore when we say that Christ shrank from death in the flesh, this is referred to his human nature: for it could not be that a true man should not naturally shrink from death. Meanwhile he endured this grief and anguish in the soul, because in taking on a body he at the same time took on a passible soul.

units.la: 18. Quære, si est Filius Dei & si Pater, & Filius vnū tātum sunt, necessariò etiam eadem est eorum volūtas. Ipse tamen quum orāret ante Patrem suum, dixit, Pater mi, si fieri potest vt non bibam calicem hunc, fac: sin minus,fac vt est bonum in oculis tuis:non fiat fecundum voluntatem meam,sed fecundū voluntatem tuam.Ergo non sunt eorum voluntates similes.
units.tr: 18. Ask: if the Son of God and the Father and the Son are only one, their will must necessarily be the same too. Yet when he prayed before his Father he said, "My Father, if it can be that I do not drink this cup, let it be done; but if not, let it be as is good in your eyes; let it not be done according to my will, but according to yours." Therefore their wills are not alike.

units.la: Quaere vicissim, quomodo Deus pronunciet se nolle mortem peccatoris,reprobos tamen exitio destinans, Moi dixerit,Miserebor cuius miserebor, & misericcordiam praestab ,cui misericordiam praestitero. Nam discrimen omne inseruandis vel perdendis hominibus ad arbitrium suum reuocans, se non omnibus spiritum resipiscentiae dare ostendit. Quaere etiam,quomodo poenitentiam Deus sibi tribuat,quasi mutabilis, vel parum prouidens.Quid enim fugiet eorum proteruiam, dum sibi tam licentiose Dei mysteriis obstrepere permittunt?
units.tr: Ask in turn: how does God declare that he does not wish the death of a sinner, while destining the reprobate to destruction, when he says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy"? For by referring all distinction in saving or destroying men to his own decision, he shows that he does not give the spirit of repentance to all. Ask also how God attributes repentance to himself, as if he were changeable or somewhat improvident. For what will restrain their insolence, while they are permitted so licentiously to clamour against the mysteries of God?

units.la: Solutio huius quaestionis ex principio Iudaeis incognito pendet,quia percussi sunt spiritu vertiginis & amentiae.Quòd Christus idem est cum Patre Deus,non obstat quò minùs homo factus,humanos affectus susceperit. Distincta ergo ei fuit à Patre voluntas, quia nihil à se alienū esse voluit,quod esset hominis proprium.In Deum verò non cadit vel spes,vel metus,vel gaudium,vel tristitia.Denique nisi caput hoc fidei nostrae euertant, Christum esse Deum & hominem,frustra & stultè de voluntate duplici contendunt.
units.tr: The solution of this question depends on a principle unknown to the Jews, since they are struck with a spirit of giddiness and madness. That Christ is the same God as the Father does not prevent him, having been made man, from taking up human affections. His will was therefore distinct from the Father's, because he wished nothing alien to him that was proper to man. But in God there is no place for hope, or fear, or joy, or sadness. Finally, unless they overturn this head of our faith, that Christ is God and man, they contend in vain and foolishly about a twofold will.

units.la: 19. Quaere, si ille fuit Deus, quare dum oraret dixit Patri suo, vt faceret voluntatem suam? Hinc apparet quòd non haberet potentiam in manu sua,qua quidquā posset facere: sed tantùm faciebat ex voluntate Patris sui,non autem ex potentia sua.
units.tr: 19. Ask: if he was God, why, while praying, did he say to his Father that he should do his will? Hence it appears that he did not have power in his hand by which he could do anything; he acted only according to the will of his Father, and not by his own power.

units.la: Quaere, quum Angelus qui ad Abraham & Loth descendit,se faciat Iudicem Sodomae,omnémque Dei potentiam sibi vendicet:paulò post tamen neget se quicquā posse facere,donec Loth fuerit egressus, an hominis arbitrio alligata erat virtus Dei, & ligatae eius manus donec mortalis homo annueret? Hic verò nihil nobis obiectant quod non intrepidè Apostolus praedicet, Christum ex infirmitate carnis mortuum esse, qui resurrexit in virtute Spiritus. In Christo semper nobis obseruandum est Mediatoris munus, quod praestare non potuit sine obsequio, sicuti nec obsequio potuit defungi,quin se humiliaret. Christus ergo secundum hominem non modò infirmus esse sustinuit, sed assumpta serui forma,exinaniuit seipsum,non quòd ex aeterna eius virtute quidquam decesserit,vel fuerit imminutum.sed quia quietam se continuit eius Diuinitas,donec in hominis persona plenam obedientiam Patri suo praestaret. Hoc modo conueniunt duae istae sententiae, Ego à me ipso animam meam pono & iterum sumam eam:Item,Pater glorifica Filium tuum.
units.tr: Ask this: when the angel who came down to Abraham and Lot declares himself judge of Sodom and claims for himself all the power of God, yet shortly afterwards says that he cannot do anything until Lot has gone out, was the power of God bound to the will of a man, and were his hands tied until a mortal man gave a nod? Here they object nothing that the Apostle does not boldly preach, that Christ was put to death in the weakness of the flesh, yet rose in the power of the Spirit. In Christ we must always observe the office of Mediator, which he could not perform without obedience, just as he could not discharge obedience without humbling himself. Christ therefore, according to the man, not only consented to be weak but, taking the form of a servant, emptied himself. This was not because anything was lost or diminished from his eternal power, but because his Divinity held itself quiet until, in the person of the man, he rendered full obedience to his Father. In this way those two sayings agree: "I lay down my life of myself, and I will take it up again"; and likewise, "Father, glorify your Son."

units.la: 20 Quaere,quare dixerit,datum est mihi omne dominium coeli & terrae:Quis enim dedit ei?si est Filius Dei & Deus,vt vos dici tis,non erat opus dono.Nonne enim totus mundus illius est?
units.tr: 20 Ask why he said, "All dominion of heaven and earth has been given to me." Who gave it to him? If he is the Son of God and God, as you say, there was no need for a gift. For is not the whole world his?

units.la: Quære,quomodo dicatur populus Israel fuisse Dei sanctificatio,dum ex Ægypto redemptus est,si Dei sanctitas neq; mutuatur quidquam ab hominibus, neque vel principium vel finem habet. Quære etiam,cur Deus,in cuius manu est rerum omnium copia,dicitur accepisse dona ab hominibus deuictis ac si se hostium spoliis ditasset?Quære item, quomodo in Psalm Rex dicatur vnctus fuisse oleo laetitiae pro consortibus suis: qui tamen ibidem vocatur Elohim.qui in folio aeterno sedet?
units.tr: Ask how the people of Israel is said to have been God's sanctification when it was redeemed from Egypt, if God's holiness borrows nothing from men and has neither beginning nor end. Ask also why God, in whose hand is the abundance of all things, is said to have received gifts from conquered men, as if he had enriched himself with the spoils of enemies. Ask likewise how, in the Psalm, the King is said to have been anointed with the oil of gladness above his companions, yet is there called Elohim, who sits on an eternal throne.

units.la: Certe nisi Christus cum hominis personam inopiam nostram vel nuditatem in se sumpsisset, superuacua esset iftadonatio,de qua loquitur. Nec vero Deitatis suae intuitu precarium se imperium habere dicit Christus:sed prædicat qua imperii gloria ornatus fuerit se cundum hominem,sicut alibi, Pater glorifica Filium gloria quam apud te obtinui,antequam creatus esset mundus: quibus verbis satis superque diluitur putidum hoc cauillum:quia gloriam quæ prius abscondita fuit ab oculis hominum,distincte petit in carne patefieri. Eodem quoque modo Paulus optime di stinguit,quia sejpsum exinaniuit.datum ei fuisse nomen quod est super omne nomen, vt coram eo flectatur omne genu.
units.tr: Certainly, unless Christ had taken upon himself in the person of a man our poverty and nakedness, that gift of which he speaks would be superfluous. Nor does Christ say that he holds a dominion granted as a favour in view of his Deity. Rather, he proclaims with what glory of dominion he was adorned according to the man, as elsewhere: "Father, glorify your Son with the glory which I had with you before the world was made." By these words that stinking cavil is refuted well enough and more, because he asks that the glory which was previously hidden from the eyes of men be made manifest in the flesh. In the same way Paul distinguishes excellently: because he emptied himself, there was given to him the name which is above every name, so that at it every knee should bow.

units.la: 2. Quære,quemadmodum caro & spiritus simul sunt homo, sic secundum verba vestra Diuinitas & humanitas simul sunt Messias.Quod si verum est,quod est occisa humanitas,occisa est Deitas. Fuit enim Iesu secundum verba vestra,Deus & homo,& occisus est. Ergo occisa est eius Deitas.Si autem occisa est eius Deitas,is non fuit Deus.Nam Deus non occiditur.
units.tr: 2. Ask this: as flesh and spirit together are man, so according to your words Divinity and humanity together are the Messiah. If it is true that the humanity was slain, the Deity was slain too. For Jesus, according to your words, was God and man, and he was killed. Therefore his Deity was slain. But if his Deity was slain, he was not God, for God is not killed.

units.la: Quære,quum mortui sint omnes sancti Patres,an credat eorum animas vna cum corporibus extinctas esse : & quum toties Scriptura dicit sanctos dormisse, an putent vno interitu animas cum corporibus inuolui?imo quod Scriptura dicit Abfalom fuisse procerae staturae,Daauidem autem pusillae inter fratres suos, an corporum mensuram ad animas simul transferat?
units.tr: Ask this: since all the holy Fathers are dead, do they believe that their souls were extinguished together with their bodies? And since Scripture so often says that the saints slept, do they think that souls are involved in the same destruction as bodies? Nay, since Scripture says that Absalom was of tall stature, and David small among his brothers, do they transfer the measure of bodies to souls as well?

units.la: Verum est quod vulgari proverbio iactatur, nullum simile esse idem. Sed porci isti sic omnia naturae elementa peruertunt, vt nulla apud eos ratio locu inueniat. Dicimus, sicut anima & corpus hominem vnam efficiunt,ita Christum ex duabus naturis constare: nam quod similitudo omni ex parte conueniat,sed quia apta, & communa est ad exprimendam personae vnitatem. Caeterum vt demus,quod postulant nihil esse diuersum: præpostere tamen inferunt Christi Diuinitatem cum carne fuisse occisam.Nunquid emim Tyranni olim quum in sanctos saeuiret,trucidarunt eorum animas? An Abel quum occisus fuit à Cain,totus periit?Quod si super festes & illæsa fuit eius anima post mortem, quæ tamen pars hominis erat, cur nō potius intacta fuisset Christi Diuinitas in morte, licet naturæ humanæ vnita esset.
units.tr: It is true, as is commonly tossed about in proverb, that nothing is exactly the same as anything else. But these swine so pervert all the elements of nature that no reason finds a place with them. We say that just as soul and body make one man, so Christ consists of two natures. For the likeness does not agree in every respect, but it is apt and commonly used to express the unity of the person. Moreover, even granting what they demand, that nothing is different, they wrongly infer that the Divinity of Christ was slain along with the flesh. Did tyrants, when once they raged against the saints, slaughter their souls? Or when Abel was killed by Cain, did he perish entirely? But if his soul, which nevertheless was a part of the man, was above harm and unhurt after death, why should not the Divinity of Christ rather have remained untouched in death, although it was united to human nature?

units.la: Quære, Si venit in terrâ vt traderet seipse vinculis & morti pro vobis, quare dixit quòd Iudas Iscariot tradidit illum, fi ideo venerat vt iudicaretur & damnaretur?
units.tr: Ask this: if he came into the earth to hand himself over to chains and death for you, why did he say that Judas Iscariot betrayed him, if he had come precisely so that he might be judged and condemned?

units.la: Quære vicissim, quomodo dicat Iob ablata sibi fuisse bona à Domino, quibus tamen cum prædones spoliauerant? quomodo dicat Deus se libilo excitare Ægyptios, & Assyrios armare suo nutu, & omnes esse instar securis in manu sua: interim tamen praues eorum conatus damnet, fequè pronunciet fore vltoré? Quære denique, quid de suo Mesechia sentiant ipsi. Pronunciat enim Isaias posituram animam suam pro sacrificio, vt infirmitates populi sustineat: dicit cæsum à Deo & vulnerarum. Certe vel fateri cogentur ipsum periturum sua manu, vel morte ab aliis percussoribus illatum iri.
units.tr: Ask in turn how Job says that goods were taken from him by the Lord, though robbers had plundered them. How does God say that he will stir up the Egyptians with a whistle, arm the Assyrians at his nod, and that all are like an axe in his hand; and yet meanwhile condemn their wicked efforts and declare that he will be their avenger? Ask finally what they think of his Hezekiah. For Isaiah pronounces that he would lay down his soul as a sacrifice to bear the infirmities of the people; he says that he was struck and wounded by God. Certainly they will either be forced to confess that he would perish by his own hand, or that he would be brought to death by other murderers.

units.la: Ex eo quæ nunc citaui Isaiæ loco, liquet nihil in his duabus sententiis esse dissimile, vt sponte se offerat Messias ad mortem, & tamen ab impiis occidatur. Nam ideo morte sua nos Deo reconciliauit, quia eius obedientia sepultæ sunt ac deletæ nostræ iniquitates. Sacrificium igitur voluntarium esse oportuit: arcano autem & admirabili Dei consilio factum est, vt idem qui sponte mortem obibat, ab impiis traheretur ad crucem. Sic Deus qui statuerat populum suum redimere ex Ægypto, Mosi iniunxit hoc munus, & simul Pharaonem excitauit, cuius contumacia magis illustraret nomen suum. Ergo Christus sic Patri obsequium præstitit ad expiauda mundi peccata, vt tamen proditoris scelerii nō consenserit.
units.tr: From the passage of Isaiah that I have just cited, it is clear that there is nothing unlike in these two statements: that the Messiah offers himself willingly to death, and yet is killed by the impious. For he reconciled us to God by his death precisely because by his obedience our iniquities were buried and blotted out. Therefore the sacrifice had to be voluntary; yet by the secret and wonderful counsel of God it came about that the same one who undertook death willingly was dragged by the impious to the cross. So God, who had determined to redeem his people from Egypt, enjoined this office on Moses, and at the same time stirred up Pharaoh, whose obstinacy might the more illustrate his name. Thus Christ rendered obedience to the Father to expiate the sins of the world, yet did not consent to the traitor's crime.

units.la: 23 Quære ab iis qui dicunt, quòd pro occisione Iesu nos fumus in hoc exilio, quod non est verum, quum ante morte eius essemus in exilio. Et quanuis ita esset, quum scriptū sit, in horâ mortis eius illum periisse à Patre, & dixisse, Pater mi condona illis quod faciunt, quia illi nesciunt quid faciant. Si autem Pater & Filius idem sunt, & est illis eadem voluntas, esset certè condonata hæc iniquitas, quam ille ipsemet condonaret.
units.tr: 23 Ask those who say that we are in this exile because of the killing of Jesus, which is not true, since we were in exile before his death. And even if it were so, since it is written that at the hour of his death he was forsaken by the Father, and said, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do." If, however, the Father and the Son are the same and have the same will, then this iniquity would certainly have been forgiven, since he himself forgave it.

units.la: Quære vicissim, quum Deus optet sanam mente Iudæis, vt fiant suum intelligant: quomodo tamen cæci maneant & vecordes, quia in manu Dei fuit sanam mentem qui priuati erant, restituere? Quære item, quum dicat apud Isaiam se contentum esse septuaginta annorum exilio, perpetua misericordia velle prosequi Iudæos, cur tam seuerè vindicet nunc in eorum filios?
units.tr: Ask in turn: since God wishes the Jews to be of sound mind, so that they may understand and become his own, how do they nevertheless remain blind and senseless, when it was in God's hand to restore a sound mind to those who had been deprived of it? Ask likewise: since he says in Isaiah that he is content with the seventy years' exile, and wishes to pursue the Jews with perpetual mercy, why does he now avenge so severely upon their sons?

units.la: Primò me retur eorum perdita obstinatio & indomabilis, vt immensa miseriarum congerie fine fine & modo oppressi, omnes exhilarent suis malis, nemo autem eorum miseretur. Quale enim est huius stuporis portentum, quod iam tot secilis assiduè palam infesta Dei manu attriti, de causa tam securi sunt? Constat Hat ex Prophetis quàm horrenda scelerum omnium colluuies grassata fuerit in populo illo longè ante exiliū. Iam centū ante annis principes Sodomæ,& populum Gomorrhæ nominauerat Isaias:ex eo non cessarunt Diabolica sua duritie prouocare in se Dei vindictam: Deus tamen postquam septuaginta annorū exilio eos multauit,dicit se duplicè pœnâ exegisse de peccatis eorū.
units.tr: First, I marvel at their lost and untamable obstinacy: that, crushed with an immense heap of miseries without end or measure, they all rejoice in their evils, and none of them takes pity. For what a monstrous stupor is this, that after so many ages, plainly worn down by the hostile hand of God, they are so unconcerned about the cause? It is established from the Prophets how horrible a flood of every wickedness raged among that people long before the exile. Already a hundred years earlier Isaiah had named the princes of Sodom and the people of Gomorrah; since then they have not ceased to provoke God's vengeance upon themselves by their diabolical hardness. Yet God, after he punished them with a seventy-year exile, says that he has exacted double punishment for their sins.

units.la: Responsio D. Calvini ad aliquot Lælij Sofini Senensis quæstiones. 1555. Nonis Iunij Genevæ.
units.tr: Calvin's reply to some questions of Lelius Socinus of Siena. 1555, on the Nones of June, at Geneva.

units.la: Responsio ad primam quæstionem.
units.tr: Reply to the first question.

units.la: REgula vulgaris est,quæ subalterna sunt,nō pugnare. Ergo nihil obstat,quò minus gratuita sit hominū iustificatio ex mera Dei misericordia: & simul interueniat Christi meritum. Atque ideo nostris operibus aptè tam gratuitus Dei fauor, quàm Christi obedientia opponitur,vtrunque suo ordine. Nam Christus non nisi ex Dei beneplacito quidquam mereri potuit, sed quia ad hoc ordinatus est, vt irâ Dei sacrificio suo placaret, suâque obedientia deleret transgressiones nostras.In summa,quâdo ex sola Dei misericordia , quæ hunc nobis constituit salutis modu n,dependet meritum Christi, non minùs aptè,quàm illa humanis omnibus iustitiis opponitur. Probationes.
units.tr: It is a common rule that things which are subordinate do not conflict. Therefore nothing prevents a man's justification from being wholly free, from the sheer mercy of God, while at the same time the merit of Christ intervenes. So God's free favour and Christ's obedience are rightly set over against our works, each in its own order. For Christ could merit nothing except by God's good pleasure, but he was ordained for this purpose, that by his sacrifice he should appease God's wrath and by his obedience blot out our transgressions. In sum, since the merit of Christ depends wholly on God's mercy, which has established this manner of salvation for us, it is set against all human righteousness no less aptly. Proofs.

units.la: Ita Deus dilexit mundū, vt filium vnigenitum daret,vt quis quis credit in eum non pereat. Videmus vt priorem locum tenet Dei dilectio, tanquam summa causa, vel origo sequatur fides in Christum,tanquā causa secunda, & propior.Si quis excipiat Christum non nisi formalem esse causam, nimiū extenuat eus virtutem.Nam si fide, quæ in ipsum recumbit iustitiā consequimur,salutis nostræ materia in eo quæreda. Quod pluribus locis clarè probaturiNon quòd priores dilexerimus eum,sed ipse nos prior dilexit,ac Filiū suū misit ἱλασμὸν pro peccatis nostris. Clarè his verbis monstratur,Deum,ne quid suo ergi nos amori obstaret,reconciliandi modum statuisse in Christo.Ac magnum pondus habet nomen placationis:quia Deus ineffabili quodam modo,quo tempore nos amabat,simul tamen erat infensus nobis,donec reconciliatus est in Christo.Quò pertinent omnes istę sententiæ.Ipse expiatio est pro peccatis nostris.Item,Placuit Deo reconciliare per ipsum omnia erga se pacificans per sanguinem crucis eius &c. Item.Erat Deus in Christo mundum sibi reconcilians,non imputans hominibus peccata.Item,Gratos nos habuit in dilecto Filio.Item.Vt ambos in vnum hominem reconciliaret Deo per crucem.Ratio huius mysterii ex 1.ad Ephef.cap. setéda est,vbi postquâ docuit Paulus,nos inChristo fuisse electos, simul addit,nos in eodem gratiam esse adeptos. Quomodo coe-pit Deus fauore suo complecti quos ante conditum mundum dilexerat,nisi quia amore suum exeruit,vbi reconciliatus est Christi sanguine?Nam quia fons est omnis iustitiae, necesse est,vt ho mo quandiu peccator est,illum habeat hostem,& iudicem.Quare principium amoris est iustitia,qualis a Paulo describitur,Eum qui peccatum non nouerat, pro nobis peccatum fecit, vt esse-mus iustitia Dei in ipso. Significat enim gratuitam iustitiam a-deptos Christi sacrificio, vt Deo placeamus, qui natura fumus filij irae,& per peccatum alienati.
units.tr: So God loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish. Here we see that God's love holds the first place, as the highest cause, and faith in Christ follows as a secondary and nearer cause. If someone objects that Christ is only the formal cause, he greatly diminishes his power. For if we obtain righteousness by the faith that rests in him, the matter of our salvation must be sought in him. This is clearly proved in many places: "Not that we loved him first, but that he first loved us and sent his Son as the propitiation [ἱλασμός] for our sins." By these words it is plainly shown that God, lest anything stand in the way of his love for us, established the means of reconciliation in Christ. The word "placation" carries great weight, because God, in an ineffable way, at the very time he loved us was at the same time hostile to us, until he was reconciled in Christ. To this belong all those sayings: "He himself is the expiation for our sins"; likewise, "It pleased God to reconcile all things to himself through him, making peace by the blood of his cross," and so on; likewise, "God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not imputing men's sins to them"; likewise, "He has made us acceptable in the beloved Son"; likewise, "that he might reconcile both into one man to God through the cross." The reason for this mystery is to be found in Ephesians 1, where, after Paul has taught that we were chosen in Christ, he adds that in him we have obtained grace. How could God begin to embrace with his favour those whom he had loved before the foundation of the world, unless he showed his love when he was reconciled by the blood of Christ? For since God is the fountain of all righteousness, it is necessary that man, as long as he is a sinner, has him as enemy and judge. Hence the beginning of love is righteousness, which Paul describes thus: "He who knew no sin he made to be sin for us, that we might become the righteousness of God in him." This means that by Christ's sacrifice we obtain a free righteousness, so that we may please God, we who by nature are children of wrath and alienated through sin.

units.la: Quod autem vere Christus sua obedientia nobis gratia apud Patrem acquisierit,ac promeritus sit,ex pluribus Scripturis locis certo & solide colligitur. Nam teste Paulo,reconciliati fumus, & reconciliationem accepimus per eius mortem.Atqui reconciliatio locum non habet,nisi vbi offensio praecessit. Sensus ergo est,Deum cui propter peccatum eramus exosi,morte filij sui placatum fuisse,vt nobis sit propitius. Ac diligenter notada est quae paulo post sequitur antithesis, Sicut per transgressionem vnius peccatores constituti sunt multi,sic per obedientiam iusti constituentur.Sefus enim est,sicut Adam peccato alienati a Deo fumus, & destinati ad interitum:ita Christi obedientia nos in fauorem recipi tanquam iustos.Nec futurum verbi tempus praesentem iustitiam excludit,sicuti ex contextu apparet. Nam & prius dixerat χάρισμα ex multis delictis esse in iustificationem.Caeterum, quum diximus Christi merito partam nobis esse gratiam, hoc intelligimus, sanguine eius nos fuisse mundatos, & eius morte expiatione fuisse pro peccatis: Sanguis eius emundat nos a peccato. Hic sanguis est qui effunditur in remissionem peccatorum.
units.tr: That Christ truly acquired grace for us with the Father by his obedience, and merited it, is gathered with certainty and solidity from many passages of Scripture. For, as Paul witnesses, "we were reconciled, and have received reconciliation through his death." But reconciliation has no place unless offence has gone before. The sense, therefore, is that God, with whom we were hateful on account of sin, was appeased by the death of his Son, so that he might be propitious to us. The antithesis that follows shortly must be carefully noted: "As through the transgression of one many were made sinners, so through the obedience of one many will be made righteous." The sense is that, just as through Adam we were alienated from God and destined to perish, so through Christ's obedience we are received into favour as righteous. Nor does the future tense of the verb exclude present righteousness, as the context shows. For he had already said that the gift [χάρισμα] is of many offences unto justification. Moreover, when we say that grace was obtained for us by the merit of Christ, we mean that we were cleansed by his blood, and that by his death he was made an expiation for sins: "His blood cleanses us from sin." This is the blood that is poured out for the remission of sins.

units.la: Si hic effectus est suffi sanguinis, vt non imputentur nobis peccata,sequitur eo pretio satisfactum esse iudicio Dei. Quo pertinet illud Baptistae,Ecce agnus Dei qui tollit peccata mundi.Nam omnibus legis sacrificiis Christum opponit,vt impletum in eo fo lo docet,quod figurae illae mostrarunt.Scimus autem quod passim dicat Moses,Expiabitur iniquitas:peccatum delebitur,ac remittetur. Denique in veteribus figuris optime docemur,quae sit mortis Christi vis & efficacia.Et hanc re Apostolus dextre sumpto hoc principio in Epistola ad Hebraeos explicat, Quod remissio absque sanguinis effusione non fiat.Vnde colligit Christum in abolitionem peccati per suum sacrificium semel apparuisse. Item,Oblatum esse,vt multorum tolleret peccata. Dixerat autem prius,non per sanguinem hircorum,aut vitulorum,sed per sanguinem proprium semel intrasse in sancta,aeterna Redemptione inuenta. Iam dum in hunc modum ratiocinatur, Si sanguis vitulae sanctificat secundum carnis puritatem, multo magis sanguine guine Christi purificari conscientias ab operibus mortuis,facilè patet nimis extenuari Christi gratiam,nisi eius sacrificio vim expiandi, placandi, & satisfaciendi concedimus, quemadmodum paulò post addit,Mediator hic est noui Testamenti,vt morte interueniente in redemptionem prævedentiù delictorum,quę manebant sub lege, promissionem æternæ hæreditatis accipiant qui vocati sunt. Præsertim vero expendere conuenit analogiâ,quæ à Paulo describitur,Quòd pro nobis factus sit maledictio,&c.Su peruacuum enim,adeóque absurdum fuit onerari Christum maledictione, nisi vt quod alij debebant persoluens, iustitiam illis acquireret. Clarum est etiam Isaiæ testimonium, Quòd castigatio pacis nostræ Christo impositá fuit,& liuore eius nobis obtigit sanitas. Nisi enim satisfecissét pro peccatis nostris Christus, non diceretur placasse Deum, pœna cui eramus obnoxij, in se recepta.Cui respondet quod ibidem sequitur,Propter scelus populi mei percussi eum.Accedit etiam Petri interpretatio,quæ nihil ambiguum relinquet, Quòd peccata portauerit super lignū. Onus enim damnationis,quo leuati sumus,dicit in Christû esse reiectum. Nec obscurè pronuntiant Apostoli pretium soluisse, quo nos à reatu mortis redimeret.Iustificati gratia ipsius per redemptionem quæ est in Christo, quem posuit Deus ἱλαστήριον per fidem,quæ est in sanguine eius. Gratiam Dei in hoc commendat Paulus, quia redemptionis pretium dedit in Ghristi morte. Deinde iubet nos cõfugere ad eius sanguinem, vt iustitiâ adepti coram Dei iudicio stemus.Idem valet istud Petri,Redempti non auro,& argento,sed pretioso sanguine agni immaculati.Neque enim cõgrueret antithesis,nisi pro peccatis satisfactum esset hoc pretio. Qua ratione Paulus dicit nos pretiosè emptos esse. Non staret etiam alterum Pauli dictum, Vnus Mediator, qui se dedit ἀντίλυτρον,nisi reiecta in eum esset pœna, quam meriti eramus. Ideo Paulus redemptione in sanguine Christi definit Remissionem peccatorum : acû diceret iustificati nos,vel absolui coram Deo, quia sanguis ille in satisfactionem respondet. Cui & alter locus consonat,Delectum fuisse in carne chirographum,quod erat contrarium nobis. Solutio enim vel compensatio notatur, quæ nos à reatu absoluit.Magnum & his verbis Pauli subest pōdus, Si iustificamur ex operibus legis,ergo gratis Christus mortuus est.Nam hinc colligimus à Christo petendum esse,quod lex conferret si quis eam impleat : vel quod idem est, nos consequi per Christi gratiam, quod Deus operibus nostris in lege promisit,Qui fecerit hæc viuet in ipsis Eodem spectat quod postea tradit, Deus Filium suum misit legi subiectum, vt eos qui sub lege erant,redimeret.Quorsum enim subiectio hęc,nisi quòd iustitiâ nobis peperit,suscipies præstandû, cui nos soluendo nō eramus?
units.tr: If this is the effect of the blood of Christ, that our sins are not imputed to us, it follows that satisfaction was made to the judgment of God by that price. To this belongs the Baptist's saying, "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world." For he sets Christ over against all the sacrifices of the law, teaching that in him alone is fulfilled what those figures showed. We know, too, that Moses everywhere says: iniquity will be atoned for, sin will be blotted out and forgiven. Finally, in the ancient figures we are best taught what the power and efficacy of Christ's death is. The Apostle, skilfully taking up this principle, explains it in the Epistle to the Hebrews: that without the shedding of blood there is no remission. Hence he concludes that Christ has appeared once for the abolition of sin through his sacrifice. Likewise, that he was offered "to take away the sins of many." He had said before that he entered once into the holy places, not by the blood of goats and calves but by his own blood, having found eternal redemption. Now, since he reasons in this way, "If the blood of a heifer sanctifies according to the purity of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ purify consciences from dead works," it is easily evident that Christ's grace is much diminished unless we grant to his sacrifice the power of expiating, appeasing and satisfying. As he adds a little later: "He is the Mediator of the new covenant, so that, death intervening for the redemption of the transgressions that remained under the law, those who are called may receive the promise of eternal inheritance." Especially is it fitting to weigh the analogy that Paul describes: "that he was made a curse for us," and so on. For it would be superfluous, and indeed absurd, to burden Christ with a curse, unless by paying what others owed he might acquire righteousness for them. The testimony of Isaiah is also clear: that the chastisement of our peace was laid upon Christ, and by his bruises health came to us. For unless Christ had made satisfaction for our sins, it would not be said that he appeased God by taking upon himself the punishment to which we were liable. To this corresponds what follows in the same place: "For the transgression of my people he was stricken." Peter's interpretation adds to this, leaving nothing ambiguous: that "he bore our sins upon the tree." For he says that the burden of condemnation, by which we have been relieved, was cast upon Christ. Nor do the Apostles obscurely declare that he paid the price by which he redeemed us from the guilt of death. "Justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiatory [ἱλαστήριον] through faith in his blood." Paul commends God's grace in this, because he gave the price of redemption in the death of Christ. Then he bids us flee to his blood, so that, having obtained righteousness, we may stand before the judgment of God. The same holds for Peter's words: "redeemed not with gold and silver but with the precious blood of a spotless lamb." For the antithesis would not hold unless satisfaction for sins had been made by this price. For this reason Paul says we were bought at a high price. Another saying of Paul would also not stand, "one Mediator, who gave himself as a ransom [ἀντίλυτρον]," unless the punishment we deserved had been laid upon him. Therefore Paul defines redemption in the blood of Christ as the remission of sins; and since he says that we are justified or absolved before God, it is because that blood answers as satisfaction. Another passage agrees with this: "the handwriting that was against us was blotted out in the flesh." Payment or compensation is indicated, which absolves us from guilt. There is also great weight in these words of Paul: "If we are justified by the works of the law, then Christ died in vain." For from this we gather that what the law would give to one who fulfils it is to be sought from Christ; or, which is the same thing, that through Christ's grace we obtain what God promised in the law to our works: "He who does these things shall live by them." To the same point belongs what he teaches afterwards: "God sent his Son, made under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law." For why this subjection, unless that he, taking upon himself what we were unable to pay, won righteousness for us?

units.la: Hinc illa iustitiæ imputatio sine operibus, de qua Paulus disserit: quia scilicet accepta nobis fertur quę in solo Christo reperta fuit iustitia. Nec certe alia causa vocatur caro Christi cibus noster, nisi quia in ea reperimus vitæ substantiam. Ea porro vis non aliunde prouenit, nisi quia in iustitiæ nostræ pretium crucifixus fuit Filius Dei. Sicut dicit Paulus, quod seipsum tradiderit sacrificium in odorem bonæ fragrantiæ. Et alibi, Mortuus est propter peccata nostra, & resurrexit propter iustificationem nostrā. Inde conficitur, non modo per Christum salutem nobis datā esse, sed Patrem nobis eius gratia nunc esse propitiū. Nam solide in eo impleri non dubium est, quod per Isaiam sub figura pronuntiat Deus, Propter me faciam, & propter Dauid seruum meum. Cuius rei optimus testis est Apostolus, quum dicit, Remittuntur nobis peccata propter nomen eius. Nam etsi non exprimitur Christi nomen: Ioannes tamē suo more sub pronomine αὐτοῦ eum designat. Quo etiam sensu pronuntiat Dominus, Sicuti ego viuo propter Patrem, ita & vos viuetis propter me. Cui respodet quod dicit Paulus, Vobis datum est propter Christū, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ, non solum vt in eum credatis, sed etiam vt pro eo patiamini.
units.tr: Hence comes that imputation of righteousness without works, of which Paul speaks: namely, that the righteousness which was found in Christ alone is said to be reckoned to us. Nor is Christ's flesh called our food for any other reason than that in it we find the substance of life. Moreover, that power comes from nothing else than that the Son of God was crucified as the price of our righteousness, as Paul says, that he gave himself up as a sacrifice of sweet-smelling savour. And elsewhere: He died for our sins and rose again for our justification. From this it follows that salvation has been given to us not only through Christ, but also that the Father is now propitious to us by his grace. For there is no doubt that what God declares through Isaiah under a figure is solidly fulfilled in him: For my own sake, and for the sake of David my servant, I will do it. The best witness to this is the Apostle, when he says: Sins are forgiven us for his name's sake. For although Christ's name is not expressed, John nonetheless designates him in his own way under the pronoun [αὐτοῦ]. In this same sense the Lord declares: As I live because of the Father, so you also shall live because of me. To this corresponds what Paul says: It has been given to you for Christ [ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ], not only that you believe in him but also that you suffer for him.

units.la: Responsio ad secundam quæstionem.
units.tr: Answer to the second question.

units.la: Quanquam in fidem non illuminantur, nec Euangelij efficaciam vere sentiunt, nisi qui præordinati sunt ad salutem: experientia tamen ostendit reprobos interdum simili fere sensu atq; electos affici, vt ne suo quidem iudicio quicquam ab electis differant. Quare nihil absurdi est, quod cœlestium donorum gustus, & temporalis fides illis tribuitur: non quod vim spiritualis gratiæ solide percipiant, ac certum fidei lumē: sed quia Dominus vt magis conuictos & inexcusabiles reddat, se insinuat in eorum mētes, quatenus sine adoptionis Spiritu gustari potest eius bonitas. Si quis obiiciat, Nihil igitur amplius restare fidelibus, vnde certò adoptionem suam æstiment, Respondeo, quanuis magna sit similitudo, & affinitas inter Dei electos, & qui fide caduca ad tempus donantur: vigere tamen in solis electis fiduciam illam, quam celebrat Paulus, vt pleno ore clamet, Abba Pater. Ergo vt solos electos semine incorruptibili Deus in perpetuū regenerat, vt nunquam dispereat semen vitæ eorū cordibus insitum: ita fo-lide in illis obsignat adoptionis suæ gratiam, vt stabilis & rata sit. Sed hoc minime obstat, quin illa inferior Spiritus operatio cursum suum habeat etiam in reprobis. Interea docentur fideles solicitè & humiliter seipsos excutere, ne pro fidei certitudine obrepat carnis securitas. Adde q reprobi nūquam sensum gratiæ nisi confusè percipiunt, vt umbram potius apprehendant, quàm solidum corpus: quia peccatorum remissionem Spiritus proprie in solis electis obsignat, vt eam speciali fide in vsum suum applicent.
units.tr: Although men are not enlightened into faith, nor truly perceive the efficacy of the Gospel, unless they are predestined to salvation, experience nevertheless shows that the reprobate are sometimes affected in almost the same way as the elect, so that even by their own judgment they differ in nothing from the elect. Therefore it is nothing absurd that a taste of heavenly gifts and a temporary faith are attributed to them; not because they solidly grasp the power of spiritual grace and the certain light of faith, but because the Lord, in order to make them more convicted and inexcusable, insinuates himself into their minds, insofar as his goodness can be tasted without the Spirit of adoption. If someone objects: then nothing remains for the faithful by which they may surely judge their adoption, I answer: although there is great likeness and affinity between God's elect and those who are given a fleeting faith for a time, nevertheless that confidence which Paul celebrates, so that he cries out with full mouth, Abba, Father, flourishes in the elect alone. Therefore, just as God regenerates the elect alone in perpetuity with incorruptible seed, so that the seed of life implanted in their hearts never perishes, so he firmly seals the grace of his adoption in them, so that it is stable and sure. But this in no way prevents that lower operation of the Spirit from running its course in the reprobate also. Meanwhile the faithful are taught to examine themselves diligently and humbly, lest carnal security creep in under the pretence of the certainty of faith. Add that the reprobate never perceive the sense of grace except confusedly, so that they grasp a shadow rather than a solid body; for the Spirit properly seals the forgiveness of sins in the elect alone, so that they may apply it to their own use by a special faith.

units.la: Rom. 4. Ioan. 6. Ephes. 5. Rom. 4. Isa. 37. 1. Ioan. 2. Ioan. 6. Philip. 1. Rom. 8. Gal. 4. cent. Merito tamen dicuntur reprobi Deum credere sibi propi- tium,quia donum recociliationis licet confusè,nec satis distin- ēte suscipiunt:non q̄ vel eiusdem fidei, vel regenerationis partici- pes sint cum Filiis Dei:sed quia commune cum illis principiū habent. Nec verò nego, quin hucvsque eorum mentes irradiet Deus,vt eius gratiam agnoscant:sed sensum illum à peculiari te stimonio,quod reddit suis electis,ita distinguit, vt ad solidum ef- sectum & fruitionem non perueniant. Non enim ideo se propi- tium illis demonstrat, quia verè ex morte ereptos in custodiam suam recipiat:sed tantum illis demonstrat præsentem misericor- diam.Viua autem fidei radice solos electos dignatur,vt in finem vsque perseueret. Ita diluitur obiectio illa,Si verè gratiam suam demonstrat Deus,hoc perpetuò fixum est:quia nihil obstat quò minus præsenti gratiæ suæ sensu,qui postea euanescat,Deus aliquos illustret.
units.tr: Rom. 4. Ioan. 6. Ephes. 5. Rom. 4. Isa. 37. 1. Ioan. 2. Ioan. 6. Philip. 1. Rom. 8. Gal. 4. cent. Yet the reprobate are rightly said to believe God to be propitious to them, because they receive the gift of reconciliation, though confusedly and not distinctly enough; not that they are partakers of the same faith or of regeneration with the sons of God, but because they have a common principle with them. Nor do I deny that God enlightens their minds thus far, so that they acknowledge his grace; but he distinguishes that sense from the peculiar testimony which he gives to his elect, so that they do not attain solid effect and enjoyment. For he does not show himself propitious to them because he truly receives them, snatched from death, into his keeping; he only shows them present mercy. He deigns to count the elect alone as having the living root of faith, so that they persevere to the end. Thus that objection is answered: If God truly shows his grace, this is fixed forever; because nothing prevents God from enlightening some with a sense of his present grace, which afterwards fades away.

units.la: Responsio ad tertiam quæstionem.
units.tr: Answer to the third question.

units.la: Quanquā fides Diuinæ erga nos voluntatis notitia est,& certa de eius veritate persuasio,non mirum tamen est,Diuini amoris sensum in temporariis euanescere,qui licet fidei sit affinis,ab ea tamen multū differt. Voluntas Dei immutabilis est,fateor, & semper eius veritas sibi constat. Atqui nego hucusque progredi reprobos,vt in arcanam illam reuelationem penetrent,quam sōlis electis Scriptura vendicat. Nego igitur eos vel Dei voluntatē vt est immutabilis,capere:vel eius veritatem constanter ample- ctiquia in sensu euanido subsistunt: sicuti arbor non satis altè platana,vt viuas radices agat,temporis successu arescit,licet per aliquot annos non flores tantum & folia emittat,sed etiam fru- ctus. Denique sicuti primi hominis defectione deleri potuit ex eius mente & anima Dei imago:ita mirum non est, si quibusdam gratiæ suæ radiis reprobis illuceat,quos postea extingui patitur. Nec verò quicquam impedit, quò minus leuiter alios tingat Euangelij sui notitia,alios penitus imbuat. Hoc interim tenendū est,quantumuis exigua sit ac debilis in electis fides: quia tamen Spiritus Dei certa illis arra est, ac sigillum suæ adoptionis, nunquam ex eorum cordibus deleri posse eius sculpturam:reprobos verò tali luce aspergi,quæ postea dispereat:neque tamen fallace esse Spiritum,etiamsi femen quod in eorum corda iacit,non viuificet,vt semper maneat incorruptibile sicuti in electis.
units.tr: Although faith is a knowledge of God's will toward us and a certain persuasion of its truth, it is nonetheless no wonder that the sense of divine love fades away in temporary believers; this, although akin to faith, differs from it greatly. God's will is immutable, I grant, and his truth always holds to itself. But I deny that the reprobate advance so far as to penetrate that secret revelation which Scripture claims for the elect alone. I deny, therefore, that they either grasp God's will as it is immutable or constantly embrace his truth, since they remain in a fading sense. Just as a plane tree that has not struck its living roots deep enough dries up with the passing of time, though for some years it puts forth not only flowers and leaves but even fruit. Finally, just as the image of God could be destroyed from the mind and soul of the first man by his fall, so it is no wonder if the rays of his grace shine on some reprobate, whom he afterwards allows to be extinguished. Nor does anything prevent the knowledge of his gospel from lightly touching some while thoroughly imbuing others. Meanwhile this must be held: however slight and weak faith may be in the elect, since the Spirit of God is a sure pledge to them and the seal of their adoption, its engraving can never be erased from their hearts; but the reprobate are sprinkled with such a light as afterwards perishes. Yet the Spirit is not deceitful, even if the seed which he casts into their hearts does not quicken it, so that it remains incorruptible, as in the elect.

units.la: Responsio ad quartam quæstionem.
units.tr: Answer to the fourth question.

units.la: Quum ex Scripturæ doctrina,& quotidiano vsu cōstet reprobos interdum affici Diuinæ gratiæ sensu,quoddam mutui amoris desiderium in illorum cordibus excitari necesse est.Sic in Saul ad tempus viguit pius affectus ,vt eum amaret, à quo paternè se tractari sciens,aliqua eius bonitatis dulcedine capiebatur. Sed quemadmodum radicitus non haeret in reprobis paternus Dei amor, ita non solide eum redamant ut filij, sed mercenario quodam affectu ducuntur. Nam soli Christo hac lege datus est Spiritus ille amoris, ut eum membris suis instillet. Nec cerre longius quàm ad electos patet illud Pauli, Diffusa est charitas Dei in cordibus nostris per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis: nempe charitas quae illam quam supra attigi invocationis fiduciam generat. Dico etiam Deum mirabiliter irasci filiis suis quos amare non desinit: non quod apud se eos oderit, sed quia eos terrere vult ira sua sensu, ut superbiam carnis humiliet, corporem excutiat, ad poenitentiam solicitet. Itaque eodem tempore et iratum sibi vel peccatis suis, et propitium sentiunt, qui non fidè iram eius deprecantur, ad quum tamen cum tranquilla fiducia confugiunt.
units.tr: Since it is clear from the teaching of Scripture and from everyday experience that the reprobate are sometimes moved by a sense of divine grace, some desire for mutual love must be stirred in their hearts. Thus in Saul a pious affection flourished for a time, so that he loved the one by whom he knew himself to be treated as a father, and he was captured by some sweetness of that goodness. But just as the fatherly love of God does not take root in the reprobate, so they do not love him in return firmly, as sons do, but are driven by a kind of mercenary affection. For that Spirit of love has been given to Christ alone on this condition, that he might pour it into his members. Nor does that saying of Paul extend any further than to the elect: "The love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us." That is, it is the love that generates the confidence in invocation which I touched on above. I also say that God is wondrously angry with his sons whom he never ceases to love: not that he hates them in himself, but because he wants to terrify them by the sense of his anger, to humble the pride of the flesh, to shake off their corruption, and to urge them to repentance. So at the same time they feel both that God is angry with them, or with their sins, and that he is gracious to them; those who do not, in faith, pray against his anger nevertheless flee to him with calm confidence.

units.la: CALVINVS N. N. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN TO N. N., GREETING.

units.la: Si alter ex coniugibus in elephantiasim inciderit.
units.tr: If one of the spouses has fallen into elephantiasis.

units.la: ANtequam vestrae nobis redderentur, vltimae nostrae, ut speramus ad vos peruenerint. Nunc res de qua quaeritis valde perplexa est. Neque enim iusta diuortij causa est morbus, qualiscunque tandem sit. Quamdiu autem firmum manet coniugium, videtur alter alteri obstringi. Vtrôsque autem hortatur Paulus, vt debitam benevolentiam reddant, maritus uxori et uxor marito. Quòd ad coniugij vinculum spectat, insolubile esse statuimus, quanuis a thoro separetur uxor. Sequitur quaestio: an elephantiasis, quae vulgo dicitur lepra, si ea percussus fuerit vir, mulierem a lege concubitus separet. Dicunt genus illud hominum si prurigine laborat, esse maxime libidinosum. Causabitur ergo sibi opus esse uxore. Sed si quis effet humanitatis sensus in homine elephantiaco, primum uxori suae et liberis parceret: deinde consuleret generi humano, ne longius contagio serperet. In eo iam deprehenditur, non facere nec mariti, nec patris officium: atque etiam quodammodo boni publici esse inimicus. Praeterea nisi bruto stupore percussus est, sicut aliis omnibus est foetidus, ita sponte propria modestia seipsum sepeliret. Certè ne simus crudeles, non audemus hac necessitate mulierem obstringere, ut contubernio et thoro iungatur viro, qui omnes naturae leges obliuiscitur: sed concedendum censemus, ut cognitione iudicium interposita viduitatem colat. Interea verò quibuscunque poterit officiis, non desinat maritum prosequi, modò ne, quod fere prodigiosum est, ab ea exigat. Valete optimi et integerrimi fratres. Dominus vobis semper adsit, vos tueatur, et Spiritu suo regat. Genevae, 1111. Nonas Decemb. M. D. LXI.
units.tr: Before yours were delivered to us, our last letters, as we hope, reached you. Now the matter you ask about is very perplexing. For illness, of whatever kind, is not a just cause for divorce. As long as the marriage remains firm, each seems bound to the other, and Paul exhorts both of them to render due kindness, the husband to the wife and the wife to the husband. As far as the bond of marriage is concerned, we hold that it cannot be dissolved, although the wife may be separated from the marriage bed. The question follows: whether elephantiasis, which is commonly called leprosy, if it strikes the husband, separates the wife from the lawful intercourse of marriage. They say that people of that kind, if they suffer from lust, are very lustful, and so he will claim that he has need of a wife. But if the elephantiac man had any feeling of humanity, he would first spare his wife and children, and then he would consider the human race, lest the contagion creep further. In this he is found not to perform the duty either of a husband or of a father, and indeed in some way he is an enemy of the common good. Moreover, unless he is struck by brutish stupor, just as he is loathsome to everyone else, so by his own modesty he would bury himself. Certainly, lest we be cruel, we do not dare to bind the woman by this necessity, to join herself in cohabitation and bed to a husband who forgets all the laws of nature; rather we think it must be conceded that, with the judgment of a court interposed, she should keep widowhood. Meanwhile, by whatever duties she can, let her not cease to attend upon her husband, provided only that he does not demand of her what is almost monstrous. Farewell, best and most upright brothers. May the Lord always be with you, keep you, and rule you by his Spirit. Geneva, on the Nones of December, 1561.

units.la: A D QV AE-
units.tr: TO THE QUESTION

units.la: AD QVAESTIONEM DE QVIBVSDAM Ecclesiæ ritibus.
units.tr: On a Certain Question concerning Some Rites of the Church.

units.la: COnfessioni publicæ adiungere insigne aliquam promissionem, quæ peccatores ad spem veniæ & reconciliationis erigat, nemo nostrum est qui nō agnoscat vtilissimum esse. Atque ab initio hunc morem inducere volui: sed cum offensionem quidam ex nouitate metuerent, nimium facilis fui ad cedendum: ita res omissa est. Nunc vero non esset opportunum hic quicquam mutare: quia antequam ad finem Confessionis venit, magni pars incipit surgere. Quo magis optamus, dum vobis integrum est, populum vestrum ad vtrunque assuefieri.
units.tr: None of us can fail to see that it is most useful to attach to public confession some notable promise that raises sinners to hope of pardon and reconciliation. From the beginning I wished to introduce this custom, but since some people feared offence at its novelty, I gave way too readily, and so the matter was dropped. Now, however, it would not be fitting to change anything here, because before the end of the Confession a large part of the congregation begins to rise. We therefore wish, while it is still in your power, that your people be accustomed to both.

units.la: In Cœna administranda aliquando Pauli verbis vsus sum: sed quia apud singulos repeti nō poterat, quin longior mora iniiceretur (si autem inter ipsam recitationem plures transirent, vix decimus quisque) assequebatur quid vellem, nemo percipiebat integram sententiam) desistere malui. Iam vero singulis mensibus Cœnam celebrari maximè nobis placeret: modò ne vsus frequentior negligentiam pariat. Nam dum maior pars à communione abstinet, quodammodo dissipatur Ecclesia. Malimus tamen singulis mensibus inuitari Ecclesiā, quàm quater duntaxat in singulos annos: vt apud nos fieri solet. Quum huc primum veni, non distribuebatur nisi ter quotannis: & quidem vt inter Cœnam Pentecostes, & Natalis Christi, leptem toti menses intercederent. Mihi placebant singuli menses: sed quum minimè persuaderem, satius visum est populi infirmitati ignoscere, quàm pertinacius contendere. Curaui tamen referri in acta publica vitiosum esse mo rem nostrum, vt posteris facilior esset ac liberior correctio.
units.tr: I once used Paul's words in administering the Lord's Supper, but since they could not be repeated for each individual without a long delay being imposed (and if, during the recitation itself, several people passed by, scarcely one in ten), and since people could not grasp the whole sentence, I preferred to stop. Indeed, I would very much like the Lord's Supper to be celebrated every month, provided only that more frequent use does not breed negligence. For while the greater part abstains from communion, the Church is in a sense scattered. Yet we would rather invite the Church every month than only four times a year, as is customary among us. When I first came here, it was distributed only three times a year, and indeed there were seven whole months between the Supper at Pentecost and the Nativity of Christ. Monthly celebration pleased me, but since I could not persuade people at all, it seemed better to pardon the weakness of the people than to contend more stubbornly. I have nevertheless arranged for it to be recorded in the public register that our practice is faulty, so that correction may be easier and freer for posterity.

units.la: Cur Cœnam ægrotis negandam esse non arbitror, multæ & graues causæ me impellùnt. Video interea quàm procliui in multos abusus sit lapsus, quibus prudenter sedulòque occurrendum esset. Nisi enim sit communicatio, perperam deflectitur à sacra institutione Christi. Conueniat ergo aliquis coetus oportet ex cognatis, familiaribus, & vicinis, vt fiat distributio ex mādato Christi: deinde coniuncta sit actio cum mysterii explicatione: nec quicquam à communi Ecclesiæ ratione diuersum. Promiscuè etiam huc & illuc deferre, valde periculosum est. Atque hic difficillimum est cauere, ne alios superstitio, alios ambitio & vana ostentatio ad petendum solicitet. Itaque iudicio opus esset ac de lectu, ne quibus daretur, nisi in magno vitæ discrimine. Panem tanquam sacrum è templo afferri præposterum est: gestari verò in pompa, nullo modo tolerabile. Valete eximij viri, & exanimo colendi fratres. Dominus vos regeatur gubernet, ac benedicat perpetuò. Genesis, xi 1. Augusti. M. D. LXI.
units.tr: Why I do not think the Supper should be denied to the sick, many weighty reasons compel me. Meanwhile I see how prone the practice has been to slip into many abuses, which ought to be met wisely and diligently. For unless there is communion, the sacred institution of Christ is wrongly departed from. A gathering should therefore be made of relatives, household members and neighbours, so that the distribution may be made in accordance with Christ's command; then the action should be joined with an explanation of the mystery, and nothing should differ from the common practice of the Church. To carry it hither and thither indiscriminately is also very dangerous. And here it is very difficult to take care that some are not moved by superstition, others by ambition and empty display, to seek it. Therefore there would need to be judgement and selection, so that it is not given to those to whom it should not be, unless in grave danger of life. To bring the bread from the church as though it were sacred is absurd; to carry it about in procession is in no way tolerable. Farewell, outstanding men and brothers to be cherished in spirit. May the Lord rule, guide and bless you always. Genesis [Geneva], 1 August 1561.

units.la: R.j.
units.tr: R.j.

units.la: {*}Voniam hic vir nobilis, qui & communes fratrum literas, & quas priuatim scripsisti, nobis reddidit, obseruande fra-ter, quàm parum otij nobis ad scribendum suppeteret, aliqua ex parte cognouit, non multis verbis petemus vt nostrae bre uitati ignoscas. Primo aduectu monitus fuit proximo biduo nullum fore nobis vacuum tempus: hodie tandem respondere licuit. Quia verò non dubitamus, alias Ecclesias sedulò vobis operam nauasse, breuiter summâ doctrinae complexi sumus, de qua Stan carsi molestiam exhibet. Quòd si vtile sit, Epistolam nostram promulgabimus, quae cosensus nostri apud omnes sit testis. Porrò caput vnum quod illic reperietis, vos commonefaciet, nobis nò probari quod de aeterno Christi sacerdotio scribitis, acsi prin cipiò careret, quando Sacerdos non minus quàm reconciliator creatus est. Quare si nostro consilio obtemperatis, aliquid in ea parte mutandum erit, ne ansam calumniandi inde hostis arripiat: deinde & si in colligendis veterum testimoniis vestra industria & dexteritas vnà cum eruditione & iudicio nobis non parùm pla-cet: cupimus tamen aliquid ex congerie rescindi, ne improbus & loquax sophista ex ambigu s vel minus luculentis nebulas spar gens, conspicuam lucem tergiuersando obscuret. Nomen etiam Ludouici Viuis in erpositum nonnihil de auctoritate minuet: quando neque vetus est scriptor, & vix pietatis rudimenta gu-stauit: tantum abest vt ceuseri mereatur inter Theologos. Seor-sum his de rebus vos monere visum est, ne vllis maculis asper-sa sit vestra confessio, dum in publicum prodibit. Alias de qui-bus nos consulitis quaestiones breuiter nos expedire cogit tem-poris angustia. Liberos qui ex scortatione progeniti sunt, ita de-mum pro legitimis habendos esse iure ciuili sancitum est, si pa-ter concubinam in vxorem ducta, hunc illis gradum assignet, id-que testetur publicis tabulis. Hoc verò parentibus concedi rectù ideo videtur, vt à vagis libidinibus tà viri, quàm mulieres se ad sanctum coniugium recipiant: atque haec aptissima est ad poeni-tentiam inuitatio, & mutui inter coniuges amoris conciliàdi pi-gnus. Nam sicuti iuste vetant leges, transferriad nothos haeredi-tate ita quod subsequitur còiugiù, si quid fuit viis aut defectus, abolet. Hinc pédet altera quæstio, an pro vxoribus habendae sint concubinae, quibuscũ nuptiae celebrantur. Certum est ad eum vsq; diem damnanda esse societatem, & Ecclesiae disciplina castigan damnò tamen protinus claudendâ esse ianuam resipiscetiç, vbi in legitimû coniugium ambo cõsentiunt. Tertia quaestio videtur ex stupiditate eorû nasci, qui nunquâ gustu aliquo humani-tatis fuerunt prediti. Negant fas esse, pęstis fugiendae causa locum mutare.
units.tr: Since this noble man, who has delivered to us both the common letters of the brothers and those you wrote privately, honoured brother, has learned in some measure how little leisure we had for writing, we will not ask you in many words to pardon our brevity. At first arrival we were warned that for the next two days we would have no free time; today at last it was possible to reply. But since we do not doubt that other Churches have diligently laboured on your behalf, we have briefly summarised the substance of the doctrine, about which Stancarus causes trouble. If it is useful, we will publish our letter, which will be a witness to the agreement of our colleagues among all. Moreover, one chapter which you will find there will remind you that we do not approve what you write about the eternal priesthood of Christ, as though he lacked a beginning, since a priest was appointed no less than a reconciler. Therefore, if you follow our advice, something in that part will have to be changed, so that the enemy does not seize an occasion for calumny from it. Next, although your diligence and dexterity in gathering the testimonies of the ancients, together with your learning and judgement, please us not a little, we nevertheless wish something to be cut from the collection, so that a wicked and garrulous sophist, scattering mists from things ambiguous or less clear, does not obscure the plain light by evasion. The name of Ludovicus Vives, too, if it is set forth, will diminish somewhat the authority [of the work]; for he is neither an ancient writer, and has scarcely tasted the rudiments of piety, so far is he from deserving to be counted among the theologians. It seemed right to warn you of these things separately, so that your confession may not be stained with any blemishes when it goes out to the public. The narrowness of time compels us to dispose of other questions on which you consult us only briefly. It has been established by civil law that children born of fornication are to be held legitimate only if the father takes his concubine as wife, assigns them this rank, and attests it in public records. This indeed seems rightly conceded to parents, so that both men and women may be drawn back from wandering lusts to holy marriage; and this is the most fitting invitation to repentance, and a pledge for winning mutual love between spouses. For just as the laws rightly forbid passing an inheritance to bastards, so what follows marriage abolishes any defect or lack in the earlier state. Hence arises another question: whether concubines with whom weddings are celebrated should be regarded as wives. It is certain that the association must be condemned up to that day, and chastised by Church discipline; yet the door of repentance and return should be closed at once, once both consent to lawful marriage. A third question seems to arise from the stupidity of those who have never been endowed with any taste of humanity. They deny it is lawful to change place in order to escape plague.

units.la: {*} Epist. 362 (margin reference). mutare.Ergo non licebit eligere salubrem aërem, Ergo in ædi-bus non licebit prospectum quoque salubrem præferre.Ergo caue-re à noxio fœtore non licebit.Ergo nulla contagio erit timeda. Facessant igitur paradoxa,quorum finis est,exuere nos omni sensu.Interea nostri consilij non est,eorum indulgere timiditati,qui obiecto periculi colore à vocatione sua discedunt:quemadmodum si vir vxorem,si maritum vxor, si liberi parentes,aut vicissim parentes liberos suos deserant,si Pastor Ecclesia relicta sibi consulat,si magistratus officio desit. Denique modò ne officium negligatur,non minus pestis contagio,quàm gladius aut ignis vitari potest.Vale eximie vir,& colende frater. D.tibi sem per adsit,virtute sustineat,prudentia regat,& labores tuos benedicat.Amen. Geneuæ,v.Idus Iunij. M. D. L X.
units.tr: Epist. 362 (margin reference). Therefore it will not be lawful to choose wholesome air; therefore it will not be lawful in a house to prefer even a wholesome outlook; therefore it will not be lawful to guard against noxious stench; therefore no contagion is to be feared. Let such paradoxes, whose end is to strip us of all sense, depart. Meanwhile it is not our counsel to indulge the timidity of those who, under the pretext of danger, desert their calling: just as if a husband deserted his wife, a wife her husband, children their parents, or parents their children in turn; as if a minister should abandon the Church entrusted to him and look to his own interests; as if a magistrate should fail in his duty. In short, provided only that duty is not neglected, contagion of plague can be avoided no less than the sword or fire. Farewell, outstanding man and brother to be cherished. May the Lord always be with you, sustain you by virtue, rule you by prudence, and bless your labours. Amen. Geneva, 9 June 1560.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS GASPARI OLEVIANO.
units.tr: JOHN CALVIN TO GASPAR OLEVIANUS.

units.la: An & quomodo Cœna ægrotis administrari possit.
units.tr: Whether and how the Lord's Supper may be administered to the sick.

units.la: ETsi pridem meam de Cœna ægrotis administranda senten-tiam rogasti, optime frater, ideo tamen nullum tulisti res-ponsum, quòd te procul abesse putabam. Ita factum est, vt Crispino nihil literarum dederim.Et nunc cùm superiores lite-ras clausissem,venit mihi in mentem,caput hoc fuisse omissum. Scio rem in disceptatione versari, quia non desunt vtrinque ra-tiones.Mihi verò non est propositum,nunc eas sigillatim excu-tere,neq; tempus suppetit.Ex natura quidem,sine,&vsu mysterij probè mihi colligere videor, nõ esse tanto bono priuandos qui vel diuturno morbo laborant,vel de vita periclitantur.Ad fidei confirmationem valet,testeram accipere quasi ex Christi manu, qua certiores siamus nos in eius corpore cèseri,carne eius & san-guine pasci in spe æternæ vitæ.Itaq; Cœnæ perceptio nos ad ob-eundas spirituales pugnas instruit. Iam si pius quispiā è mundo migrandū sibi videat,quia fieri non potest,quin oppugnetur ac vexetur multis tentationibus,merito se armari cupiet ad sustinē dos cōflictus.An eripiendum est singulare adiumentum,quo fre-tus ad lucram alacrius descendat,& victoriā obtineat?Iam pro-hiberi quominus liceat profiteri & testarum facere pietatis con-sensum cum Ecclesia,durum est ac mali exempli,siue quis in le-ēto diu iaceat,siue morti sit vicinus.Atqui Cœna sanctæ inter Fi-lios Dei vnitatis est Symbolum.Quauis streuiter rem attigerim, agnoscistamen quibus rationibus adducťus, ægrotos nõ esse ar-bitrer à cõmunicatione arcendos.Neque tamen ea de causa ve-lim turbas mouere.Scis in hac Ecclesia aliu m esse moré.Acquie-sco,quia vtile non esset cõtendere. Qui hanc administrationem non putant Christi mandato esse confentane m, obiiciunt fa-crum hoc epul im fuisse institutum,vt communiter illic vesce-rentur fideles,quod illis verum esse concedo.Sed quanuis nulla fit legitima Coena , nisi communis:quæ tamen ægrotis dabitur, quia priuata non erit,a dulterina non censebitur.Nam certe par-tem vel appendicem esse constat publicæ actionis. Neque vero Paulus, dum Corinthios admonet,domum cuique suam esse in qua comedat & bibat, Coenam excludit à priuatis aedibus.Tunc neque fidelibus patebant templa, nec vnquam permissum esset noua extruere.Sed tantum à communibus epulis discernit spiri-tuale mysterium,ne cum illis misceatur. Cæterum diligenter ca-uendum esse fateor,ne qua obrepat superstitio,ne spes slutis externo Symbolo affigatur:deinde ne se ingerat ambitio neve e-bulliat præpostera curiositas. Parce igitur & habito delectu,nec aliter quàm causa cognita, vellem Coenam apud ægrotos celebrari.Deinde ne à Christi institutione aliena foret vel minimè deflectere actio,nollem nisi in cœtu piorum,nollem absque doctrina & publico ritu. Fecit quorundam stultitia,qui paucad ægrotos deferendo,tanquam ferculum in pompa gestant, vt pij homines tanquam à corruptela non ferenda abhorreant. Corrigendum ergo esset illud quoque vitium.Ego verò eorum timori facilè ignosco,qui ad præcaueda pericula ab actu nō ita præcise necessario abstinendum censent: modò vicissim agnoscant me non temerè aliud sentire. Vale optime & integerrime frater.Saluta amicos.Dominus vos omnes conseruet,virtute inuicta ful ciat,Spiritu suo gubernet vestra consilia & studia. Geneuæ,Calendis Decembris. M. D. LXIII.
units.tr: Although you asked me some time ago for my opinion on administering the Lord's Supper to the sick, dear brother, you received no reply, because I thought you were far away. So it happened that I sent Crispinus no letter at all. Now, when I had already sealed my previous letter, it occurred to me that this point had been left out. I know the matter is disputed, since reasons are offered on both sides. It is not my intention to go through them one by one now, nor is there time. From the nature and use of the mystery, I think I can reasonably conclude that those who suffer from a long illness, or who are in danger of death, should not be deprived of so great a good. It helps the confirmation of faith to receive the pledge as if from Christ's own hand, by which we may be more certain that we are engrafted into his body, and nourished by his flesh and blood in the hope of eternal life. Thus the reception of the Supper prepares us to undertake spiritual battles. Now, if a godly man sees that he must depart from the world, since it cannot be that he will not be assailed and troubled by many temptations, he will rightly desire to be armed to endure the conflicts. Should we snatch away a unique help by which, strengthened, he might go down to his struggle more eagerly and win the victory? Moreover, to forbid him to be allowed to profess and bear witness to his agreement in piety with the Church is harsh and sets a bad example, whether someone lies long in bed or is near death. Yet the Supper is the symbol of the holy unity among the sons of God.
