Although I have touched on the matter briefly, you recognise the reasons by which I am led to think that the sick should not be shut out from communion. Nor, for that reason, would I wish to stir up disturbances. You know that in this Church the custom is different. I acquiesce, because it would not be useful to contend. Those who do not think this administration is consistent with Christ's command object that this sacred feast was instituted so that the faithful might eat together there. I grant that this is true. But although no Supper is lawful unless it is common, the one that is given to the sick will not be private, and so will not be judged adulterine. For it is certainly a part or appendix of the public action. Nor, when Paul admonishes the Corinthians that each should have his own house in which to eat and drink, does he exclude the Supper from private houses. At that time the temples were not open to the faithful, and it would never have been permitted to build new ones. Rather, he separates the spiritual mystery only from common meals, lest it be mixed with them. Otherwise, I confess, we must take care diligently that no superstition creeps in, that hope of salvation is not attached to the outward sign, and then that ambition does not intrude nor preposterous curiosity boil up. Therefore I would wish the Supper to be celebrated among the sick sparingly and with careful selection, and only when the cause has been examined. Further, lest the action depart in the slightest from Christ's institution, I would not wish it except in the assembly of the godly, and I would not wish it without teaching and public rite. The folly of some has done harm: by carrying it to a few sick people, as if they were bearing a dish in a procession, they make godly men shrink back as if from a corruption not to be tolerated. That fault too would need to be corrected. For my part I readily pardon the fear of those who think that, to guard against dangers, one should abstain from the act not so strictly necessary: provided that, in turn, they acknowledge that I do not think otherwise rashly. Farewell, excellent and most upright brother. Greet your friends. May the Lord keep you all, strengthen you with unconquered virtue, and govern your counsels and endeavours by his Spirit. Geneva, 1 December 1563.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: Your John Calvin.

units.la: CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN SENDS GREETING

units.la: Ad quasdam piorum fratrum controuersias.
units.tr: To certain controversies among pious brothers.

units.la: Ecclesiæ N.calamitas non paruo nos dolore affecit: sed quia nunc Deus,vt suos exerceat,laxare videtur Satanæ & impro-bis fræna,patienter nobis ferenda est nostra condition Rogandus interea,vt pro sua indulgentia teneri & pusilli gregis infirmitati parcat.Qui vero existimant infœliciter cū Ecclesia agi, quoties hostium furore,aut crudeli violentia impetitur, nōdum tenent Christianæ militiæ rudimenta. Hinc illa dubitatio,quæ multorum animis obrepsit,eósque nunc occupat, An piis liceat nocturnos habere vel clandestinos cœtus.Videmus enim præcipuè iudicium fieri ab cuentu,quo nihil est magis præpostepum.Nuper quum absque molestia convenirent, putarunt etiam absque controcontrouersia gratum esse Deo suum obsequio: nunc vbi exorta est persecutio, disputant an non poenas luant suae temeritatis? Hoc modo mox etiam damnabitur fidei confessio, quae impio-rum rabiem magis accendit. Denique fecundum istos censores non expediet Christum sequi, nisi prospero successu. Non abs re Paulus ludibrio Ifmaelis in summo persecutionis gradu statuit: quia plus est periculi a subsannatione, & opprobriis, quam ab armata saevitia. Si rebus aduersis premi nos videt impii, miseriis non ftris insultat. Hic si labascit nostra constantia, grauius verbis nocent, quam gladio. Atqui tenendum erat illud Pauli, Quia speramus in Deum viuum, non tantum persecutionem ferenda esse, sed contumelias. Veniat igitur nobis in mentem exemplu Christi, quem virulento isto telo vulnerare conatus est Satan. Speraiuit in Deo, liberet eum si vult, ne titubemus quoties expositi videmur hostium libidini. Quod si primo impetu vel attoniti fuerunt fratres vel turbati, tuum est eos fulcire, ne prorsus concidant: vel etiam erigere, vt animos iterum colligant: nec ideo deficiant a fanto instituto, quia impiis illud occasionem dederit sequendi. Nam si res ipsa per se aestimatur, expedita erit refpofio, non fuisse Apostolis vitio datos conuenimus & priuatos & clandestinos: & a quibus nihil differunt qui nunc sub Papatu habentur. Poterant tunc quoque maleuoli obiicere, non sine suspicio ne noctu & clam conuenire viros & mulieres. Nec dubium est, quin multis calumniis grauati fuerint: & quum stationem Hierosolymae haberet milites praesidiarii, potuit hoc videri tranquil litati publicae aduersum. Neque tamen propterea destiterunt. Videmus vt Petro capto, congregati fuerint apud vidua. Neque hic colligere exempla operaepretium est, quia scitur hoc fuisse illis in quotidiano vsu: sicuti restantur historiis, piis martyribus sp̃ luncas fuisse pro replis. Hoc quanquam non parua vituperationi fuit obnoxiū, vt vel latrocinii, vel aliorum scelerū suspecti esse possent: quia tamen ita cogebat necessitas, magnis animis spre-uerunt quae vulgo iactari sciebant probra. Ita nunc armati sunt optima defensione fratres nostri, si permitterent Magistratus liberè & palàm inuocare Dei nomen, libere in lucem se prodituros, nec quidquam se facturos occulte: sed quia prohibentur illorum tyrannide, rationem sequi quae longissime abest a tumultu. Idem sen iendum de in trimoniis, quo nam benedictio in Papatu, quam vocant, mera est prophana io. Et tamen quod ad po liticum ordinem spectat, non potest clam destinum vocari coniugium, cuius confectae erunt tabulae, sed eius sanctitatem superstitionibus pollui & foedari nullo modo: rendum est. Quanquam noctumae sepulturae non absre legibus ananturfiuftra tamen suam molliriem hoc praetexto tegunt, quii in suorum funeribus se inuoluûtur ac permiscent receptis sacrilegiis. Eadem in Baptismo valere debet ratio. Nam etsi inflat illis praesentissimum periculum, non ideo tamen licebit quod manifeste Deus improbat. Scimus in Papatu corruptum esse multis sordibus, & fere adulteratum Baptismum. Si nullus metus impediat, facile inter omnes pios conueniet, parentibus fas non esse liberos suos infantes ad vitiosum Baptismum offerre. Ergo ex periculo captare excusationem nimis est friuolum, ac si inde res ipsa naturam mutaret. Scimus enim magis pretiosum esse coram Deo pietatis testimonium, quàm ut minis, vel terroribus cedere debeat, saltem vbi ad simulationem vsque progredi cogit nos metus, quae tacita sit im pietatum approbatio. Quare licuit pro charitatis officio piis fratribus condolescimus, ita minimè nostrum est insolubili Dei lege eos soluere. Ac si olim nō dubitarunt in Ægypto Iudaicae mulieres, vt à gladio Pharaonis eriperent alienos infantes, sua capita offerre in discrimen, turpe est parentibus terreri metu, vt suorum animas quantum in se est, contaminent. Haec ex collegij nostri sententia breuiter ad te perscripsi, eximie vir, & ex animo colende frater, Dominus te Spiritu suo semper gubernet, benedicat sanctos tuos labores, teque incolumem cum Ecclesia tibi commissa tueatur. Symmystae quoque mei plurimum salutant. Genevae.
units.tr: The calamity of the Church (of N.) has affected us with no small grief. But since God now seems, in order to exercise his people, to loosen the reins for Satan and the wicked, we must bear our own situation patiently. Meanwhile we must ask him, in his kindness, to spare the weakness of his tender and little flock. Those who think the Church is treated unhappily whenever she is assailed by the fury or cruel violence of her enemies have not yet grasped the rudiments of Christian warfare. Hence that doubt which has crept into the minds of many and now troubles them: whether it is lawful for the godly to hold nocturnal or secret assemblies. For we see that judgement is formed chiefly from the outcome, and nothing is more absurd than this. Lately, when they could meet without trouble, they thought that their worship was pleasing to God, with no controversy at all. Now that persecution has arisen, they ask whether they are not paying the penalty for their rashness. In this way the confession of faith will soon be condemned too, though it only enrages the wicked more. In the end, according to these critics, it would not be worth following Christ unless success were assured. Paul rightly placed mockery, as Ishmael did, at the highest level of persecution, because there is more danger from scorn and insults than from armed savagery. When the wicked see us pressed by adversity, they mock our miseries without restraint. If our constancy wavers here, words do more harm than the sword. Yet that saying of Paul must be held fast: because we hope in the living God, we must endure not only persecution but also reproaches. Let the example of Christ come to mind, whom Satan tried to wound with this poisoned weapon. He trusted in God; let God deliver him if he wills. Let us not waver whenever we find ourselves exposed to the lust of our enemies. But if the brothers were stunned or disturbed by the first onslaught, it is your task to support them lest they collapse altogether, or even to raise them up so that they may gather their spirits again, and not on that account abandon their holy purpose, just because it has given the wicked an occasion to pursue them. For if the matter is judged in itself, the answer will be easy: the Apostles were not blamed for meeting in private and in secret, and they differ in nothing from those who are now held under the Papacy. Even then the malicious could object, not without suspicion, that men and women were meeting at night and in secret. Nor is there doubt that they were burdened with many slanders, and since a garrison of soldiers was stationed at Jerusalem, this could seem hostile to public tranquillity. Yet they did not for that reason cease. We see that when Peter was taken, they gathered together at the house of a widow. Nor is it worth piling up more examples here, since it is known that this was their daily practice, just as the histories report that the pious martyrs often used caves as their churches. Although this exposed them to no small reproach, so that they could be suspected of robbery or other crimes, nevertheless, since necessity compelled them, they scorned with a brave spirit the insults which they knew were commonly thrown at them. So now our brothers are armed with the best defence: if the magistrates would permit them to call on the name of God freely and openly, they would come forth freely into the light and would do nothing in secret. But since they are forbidden by the tyranny of those men, they follow a plan which is as far as possible from tumult. The same should be thought about marriages, in which what they call the blessing in the Papacy is sheer profanation. And yet, as far as the political order is concerned, a marriage cannot be called clandestine if its documents have been drawn up; but on no account must it be held that its sanctity is polluted and defiled by superstitions. Although night burials are not altogether contrary to the laws, they cover their own softness with this pretext in vain, since they involve themselves in the funerals of their own people and mix in with accepted sacrileges. The same reasoning ought to hold for Baptism. For although the most immediate danger threatens them, it will not therefore be lawful to do what God manifestly disapproves. We know that in the Papacy Baptism has been corrupted with many filths and is almost adulterated. If no fear stood in the way, it would easily be agreed among all the godly that parents are not permitted to offer their infant children to a vicious Baptism. So to seek an excuse from danger is far too frivolous, as if the thing itself were changed in nature by it. For we know that the testimony of piety before God is too precious to yield to threats or terrors, at least where fear drives us to the point of pretence, which is a silent approval of impiety. Therefore, although it was right for us to sympathise with pious brothers out of a duty of charity, it is by no means ours to loosen them from the indissoluble law of God. And if the Jewish women in Egypt once did not hesitate to offer their own lives to danger, so as to snatch the children of others from the sword of Pharaoh, it is shameful for parents to be frightened by fear into contaminating, as far as in them lies, the souls of their own. I have written these things briefly to you, by the opinion of our college, distinguished sir and brother to be honoured from the heart. May the Lord always govern you by his Spirit, bless the labours of his saints, and keep you safe together with the Church committed to you. My fellow-ministers also send you their warmest greetings. Geneva.

units.la: VATELLVS CALVINO S. D.
units.tr: Vatellus to Calvin, greetings.

units.la: Ad discipl. Ecclesiast. interrogata.
units.tr: Questions concerning church discipline.

units.la: Pater in Christo charissime ac venerande, ex multis causis quae me vt has ad te literas darem adduxerunt, vna est praecipua, quam primam omnium quàm breuissime potero expediam.
units.tr: Most honoured father in Christ, of the many reasons that have moved me to write to you, one is the chief. I will set it out first, as briefly as I can.

units.la: Proximis superioribus diebus huc venerunt Principes Duces, Bipontinus, & Vvirtembergensis, Principis nostri tutores. Hic quae essent, horum Ecclesiastae & Consiliarij aliquot, nobis omnibus verbi Ministris conuocatis, rursus proposuerunt ordinationem illam Ecclesiasticam, iam antea tribus circiter ab hinc annis nobis propositam: quae tribus potissimum capitibus absoluitur. Primum caput est de doctrina: quae esse iubetur in hac Ecclesia, quae à Prophetis & Apostolis est tradita, atque adeo in Confessione Augustana explicata. Secundum de ceremoniis est, ritibus formulisque catechizandi, Sacramenta administrandi, nuptiis benedicendi, & publicatum precum. Tertium disciplinam complectitur.
units.tr: In the last few days the Dukes of Zweibrücken and Württemberg, guardians of our Prince, came here. Some of their churchmen and councillors, having called all of us ministers of the Word together, again put before us that ecclesiastical ordinance which had been proposed to us about three years ago. It is made up of three main heads. The first concerns doctrine: that the teaching to be held in this Church is the teaching handed down by the Prophets and Apostles, and therefore explained in the Augsburg Confession. The second concerns ceremonies: the rites and forms for catechizing, administering the sacraments, blessing marriages, and public prayers. The third embraces discipline.

units.la: Quod ad primum & tertium attinet, vtrunque recepimus, addita explicatione articuli de Domini Coena, partim ne signa tantum nuda in ea recognoscere, partim ne absurdam impanationis opinionem admittere videremur. Secundū reiecimus. Quod quā ægrè tulerint præsides, tibi negotia eiusmodi non semel expertō cogitandum relinquo. Præcipua tamen controuersia de priuato Baptismo fuit: priuato inquam Baptismo, id est, ab obstetricibus administrato, quem in hanc Ecclesiam reuocare ita apud se constituerant, vt nullum non mouerent lapidē (quod aiunt) quo nos in suam raperent sententiam. Sed frustra. Porrò ne vitiorum ... (continued) ...
units.tr: As for the first and third heads, we accepted both, with an added explanation of the article on the Lord's Supper, partly so that we would not seem to recognise mere bare signs in it, and partly so that we would not seem to admit the absurd opinion of impanation. We rejected the second. I leave it to you to consider, since you have often had experience of such business, how badly the rulers took this. The chief controversy, however, was over private baptism: private baptism, I say, that is, baptism administered by midwives. They had decided to restore it to this Church, and they left no stone unturned, as the saying goes, to draw us over to their view. But in vain. Moreover, lest the threats ... (continued) ...

units.la: Caeterum an hoc Principes facturi sint, necne, pro certo non-dum teneo. Sed quoniam minæ illæ prorsus negligendæ nō sunt: ne forte ex improuiso vim suam exerant, iam quæro, Num idonea & sufficiens sit occasio Ministerij abdicandi, si nobis aut insciis, aut inuitis & reclamantibus, baptizandi potestas mulieribus in hac Ecclesia concedatur.
units.tr: Whether the Princes will actually do this or not, I still do not know for certain. But since those threats are by no means to be ignored, lest they suddenly put their power into effect, I now ask: is there a suitable and sufficient reason for giving up the ministry, if, without our knowledge or against our will and protest, the power of baptizing is granted to women in this Church?

units.la: Est & aliud de quo necesse est vt te consulam, propterea quod consilij quoque ambiguū me reddit. Ditiones tres angustæ quidem, sed iuris primarij & summi, anno proximè elapso in Principis nostri manu redierunt. Principes tutores vt significarent nobis fuit, statuerunt in singulas illas ditiones Ministros ex nostro cœtu selectos mittere, qui donec alii ex prospectum fuerit, relictis sacrificis, Missis & idololatria illic concionabuntur, & Sacramenta, iis qui illa volent, administrabunt. Dic nunc obsecro, num consilium illud accipere, improbareve prorsus an intactum potius relinquere debeamus: ne forte singuli audiamus, Gregè tuā cura non alienum. Quicquid sit, tamen ex te scire aueo, quid dicere, aut facere debeant qui ex nobis in ditiones illas cum illis conditionibus ablegabuntur. Hæc sunt de quibus sententiam tuam audire cupio, ne quid in iis vel temere, vel imprudentius quam par sit audendo, vel perfide turpiter conniuendo, dessignem.
units.tr: There is another matter on which I must consult you, since it also leaves me in doubt about what to advise. Three small but chief and sovereign territories have returned into our Prince's hands within the past year. The guardian Princes made it known to us that they have decided to send into each of those territories ministers chosen from our company, who, until others have been provided, will, having left off the sacrifices, the Masses and the idolatry there, preach and administer the sacraments to those who wish to receive them. Tell me now, I beg you, whether we ought to accept that plan, reject it outright, or leave it untouched; I do not want us to be heard as neglecting the flock committed to your care. Whatever the answer, I wish to learn from you what those of us who are sent into those territories, on those conditions, should say or do. These are the matters on which I desire to hear your judgment, so that I do not decide anything rashly or more hastily than is fitting in a bold venture, nor disgracefully and faithlessly by conniving.

units.la: Neque veto ego solus hoc in negotio hæreo. Sunt & alii quinque Symmystæ mei, tui amantissimi, qui consilio tuo, non minus quam ego iuuari percupiunt.
units.tr: Nor am I alone in being undecided about this business. My five fellow ministers, who love you dearly, are also eager to be helped by your counsel no less than I am.

units.la: Hi omnes mecum confessioni fidei Ecclesiarum Gallicarum subscripserunt, & vniuersam doctrinam, quam Dominus scriptis tuis non minus Christianis, quam eruditis, dispergi, & diuulgari voluit, orthodoxam & synceram esse fatenntur, atque idcirco approbant: hac praescriptio ratione motu, quod eam ex canonico literarum veteris & noui Testamenti promptuario desumptam est: satis superque constet. Vnde iudicamus tuam illam non esse, sed Domini, qui te eiusdem dispensatorem voluit, & praeconem constituit. Itaque ut eandem Christum aeternum Dei omnipotentis Filium cum Ecclesiis Genevensi & Gallicanis amplectimur, ita idem cum iisdem sentimus in Domino.
units.tr: All of them have subscribed with me to the Confession of the Gallican Churches, and they confess that the whole doctrine which the Lord wished to be spread and published through your writings, useful to Christians no less than to the learned, is orthodox and sincere, and therefore they approve it. This judgment rests on a ground that is quite sufficient, namely that it is drawn from the canonical storehouse of the Scriptures of the Old and New Testament. Hence we judge that this doctrine is not yours but the Lord's, who wished you to be its steward and appointed you its herald. Therefore, just as we embrace the same Christ, the eternal Son of the almighty God, together with the Churches of Geneva and of France, so we think the same things as they do in the Lord.

units.la: Qui vtinam faxit, vt in hac confessione ita perseueremus, vt eam non solum ore & scriptis: verumetiam vita & moribus ad extremum vsque spiritum, constanter & intrepide testemur ac profiteamur. Amen.
units.tr: May he grant that we so persevere in this confession that we bear witness to it and profess it constantly and fearlessly, not only with our mouths and writings but also with our lives and conduct, to the last breath. Amen.

units.la: Haec de me & Symmystis meis pluribus fortasse quam erat necesse. Non quod vererer, ne vni tantum prudentia tuam consulenti consilium denegaturus essem: sed vt pluribus alacrius dones, quod vni tantum alacriter daturus fueras. Atque haec sunt quae de consilio nobis in commune necessario, quod a te petimus, scribenda habui.
units.tr: I have said this about myself and my fellow ministers, perhaps at more length than was necessary. It was not that I feared you would deny counsel to one man who consulted your wisdom alone, but that you might give more readily to many what you would have given readily to one. And these are the things I had to write concerning the counsel we need in common, which we ask of you.

units.la: Superest vt ad alia leuia quidem, sed tamen negotij aliquid mihi faciendum mea festinent literae. Hic sunt non pauci qui vita defunctorum mentionem facientes verba haec addere solent: Gui Deus bonam & felicem det resurrectionem. Scimus quidem vanas & impias esse preces, quae pro defunctorum salute funduntur. Sed quoniam huiusmodi optatum ad carnis resurrectionem, quam fides nostra sperat, respicit, illud haud tenus reprehendere nondum suam ausus. Itaque: scire velim, an homini Christiano in Religione bene instituto ita loqui liceat. Et si liceat, quatenus id facere possit.
units.tr: It remains for my letter to take up some other matters, slight indeed, but still a piece of business I must attend to. Here there are not a few people who, when they mention the dead, are in the habit of adding these words: May God give him a good and happy resurrection. We know indeed that the prayers poured out for the salvation of the dead are vain and impious. But since such a wish looks to the resurrection of the flesh, which our faith hopes for, I have not yet dared to reprove it at all. So I should like to know whether it is lawful for a Christian who is well instructed in religion to speak in this way, and, if it is lawful, how far he may do so.

units.la: Praeterea Mosculus in suis locis communibus, & Bulingerus in sua locorum communium resolutione istic excusa, si lem a Deo petendam esse afferunt. Neque tamen Mosculus fidei nomine, fidei incrementum intelligit, vt qui eos qui pusilla fide sunt, adhortetur ad dicendum in suis ad Deum precibus: Domine auge nobis fidem. An Bulingus idem addat, affirmare non potest: quia nec satis memini, nec librum prae manibus habeo, vt amissam memoriam recuperem. Sed ambos in fide petenda consentire scio. Quomodo autem hinc me euoluere queam, non video. Nam qui fieri poterit vt id a Deo petam, fine quo nihil ab eodem petere possim, quod exorem? Quisquis enim Deum sine fide orat, frustra orat. Imo sic orando peccat, quum quicquid fit sine fide, sit peccatum. Adde quod nemo est qui possit Deum Patrem ex animo appellare, nisi prius fidei dono de paterno Dei in se amore, & fui in Filium adoptione, certior sit factus. Ego interea auctorum illorum auctoritatem conuulsam nolim, nec scio an vlla fit ignota mihi ratio qua defendi possint. Quare ta oro vt quicquid scrupuli in hoc mihi est loco, illud vno verbo mihi adimas.
units.tr: Moreover, Musculus in his Commonplaces, and Bullinger in his Resolution of the Commonplaces printed there, state that faith must be asked of God. Yet Musculus does not understand by the name of faith the increase of faith, so as to exhort those who have little faith to say in their prayers to God: Lord, increase our faith. Whether Bullinger adds the same, I cannot say, because I do not remember well enough and I do not have the book in front of me to recover my lost memory. But I know that the two agree in asking for faith. How I may extricate myself from this, however, I do not see. For how can I ask God for that without which I could ask nothing from him that I might obtain? Whoever prays to God without faith prays in vain. Indeed, in praying so he sins, since whatever is done without faith is sin. Add to this that no one can call God Father from the heart unless he has first been informed, by the gift of faith, of God's fatherly love towards himself and of his own adoption into the Son. Meanwhile I should not like the authority of those writers to be overthrown, nor do I know whether there is any reason, unknown to me, by which their view can be defended. So I beg you that whatever doubt I have on this point, you remove it for me with a single word.

units.la: Quod adlusiones, quibus homines tempus fallere solent, attinet, etsi optandum esset vt ab illis Christiani omnes, qui de omni verbo otioso rationem sibi reddendam esse scire debent, prorsus abstinerent: tamen vix ac ne vix quidem populus hic vnquam adduci poterit vt hoc praestet. Itaque finimus illum bombardulis & arcubalestis sese oblectare & exercere. Sed dubito an perinde liceat pyramidulas, chartas, & fritillos, vel animi relaxandi gratia, permittere. Quod si licet, quatenus id licite fieri possit, sicut peruelim.
units.tr: As for the jests with which men are accustomed to pass the time, although it would be desirable that all Christians, who ought to know that they must give an account of every idle word, should abstain from them altogether, yet this people can hardly, if at all, ever be brought to do so. So we allow them to amuse and exercise themselves with little cannons and crossbows. But I doubt whether little pyramids (a game), cards and dice-boxes may be allowed in the same way, even for the sake of relaxing the mind. If they may be, I should very much like to know how far they may be permitted lawfully.

units.la: De iactu lapidum planorum ad metam, & pila palmaria vsq; adeo animi dubius non sum, propterea quod arte constant, & corpori exercendo prosunt. Sed an diebus profestis siue operariis ludi illi concedi debeant, aliquatenus ambigo. Nam si iis qui opifices non sunt & sine manuum labore viuunt, denegentur, respondebunt paratum: si nobis licet die Dominico, quia a laboribus & manuum operibus cessatur, ludere, illud idem hodie quoque nobis licet: diebus enim quibuslibet laborum & operum sumus immunes. Sin concedantur, pauci erunt qui illorum numero se non inferant, addentes se habere vnde illo die viuant, etiamsi manibus suis nihil lucrentur. Itaque consilio tuo hic quoque mihi opus est.
units.tr: About throwing flat stones at a mark, and the game of palm-ball, I have no such doubt, because they rest on skill and help to exercise the body. But whether those games ought to be allowed on working days, I am somewhat uncertain. For if they are refused to those who are not craftsmen and who live without manual labour, they will reply that, if we are allowed to play on the Lord's Day because people then cease from labours and manual works, then we are allowed the same today too, since we are free from labours and works on any days whatever. But if they are allowed, there will be few who do not count themselves among those people, adding that they have something to live on that day even though they earn nothing by their hands. So I need your counsel here too.

units.la: Choreæ & saltationes sunt hic auctoritate Magistratus interdictæ. Vnde fit vt nullæ, aut paucissimæ publicè instituantur. Sed in triclinis in quibus nuptialia conuiuia agi consueuerunt, saltari audimus, nec possumus quicquid clamemus, malum illud auellere. Iam vero quæro, num maiores ædificationis esset, diebus profestis nuptias celebrari quàm Dominicis, quemadmodum in Ducatu Vvirtembergensi fieri audio. Nam etiamsi diebus profestis saltabitur, nulla tamen inde sequetur diei Dominici profanatio. Hæc sunt quæ familiariter, tanquam patrem benignum alloquens, proponenda habui, ad quæ singula vbi, si tibi est otium & si vis, responderis, maximo certe & grauissimo me leuaueris onere. Dominus Deus & Pater noster cœlestis Spiritu suo sancto semper te regat & gubernet, Ecclesiæque suæ incolumem quàm diutissime conseruet, per dilectum Filium Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum sibi coæternum, coessentialem, & Regni cœlestis ab æterno cofortem. Amen, Amen. Dabat Montbelgardi, x i. Calend. Octob. M. D. LXII.
units.tr: Dances and dancing are forbidden here by the authority of the magistrate, so few or none are held publicly. But we hear that dancing takes place in the halls where wedding feasts are customarily held, and however loudly we protest, we cannot root out that evil. I now ask whether it would be more edifying to hold weddings on working days rather than on the Lord's Day, as I hear is done in the Duchy of Württemberg. For even if there is dancing on working days, no profanation of the Lord's Day will follow from it. These are the points I have thought to put to you, speaking familiarly, as to a kindly father. If you answer each of them when you have leisure and are willing, you will certainly relieve me of a very great and heavy burden. May the Lord God and our heavenly Father always rule and govern you by his Holy Spirit, and keep his Church safe for as long as possible, through his beloved Son our Lord Jesus Christ, co-eternal and co-essential with him, and from eternity co-heir of the heavenly kingdom. Amen, amen. Given at Montbéliard, 21 September 1562.

units.la: Tuus omnino obediens filius Matthæus Vatellus.
units.tr: Your wholly obedient son, Matthew Vatellus.

units.la: PRolixæ tuç epistolæ breuiter respondere me cogit temporis angustia, integerrime, & ex animo colende frater. Mihi paulo ante meridiem reddita fuit. Duabus post horis ad confessum Ecclesiasticum profectus sum. Illinc tertia sum egressus. Adhuc cum fratre nostro colloquebar, dum adueniunt rursus Collegæ. Ergo breuitati quam extorquet necessitas, ignosces. Consiliarios Principum ita præcise vobiscum egisse, non miror, quia eorum more pridè cognoui. Quòd in capite de sacra Cœna differte addita fuit exceptio, recte & prudenter factum. Quamlibet enim morosi sint, apud eos periculosior est simul ratio quàm ingenua libertas. Articulo autem de disciplina, quæ apud vos nulla est, quin subscribere licuerit, non video. In Baptismo crassum illum abusum, qui non nisi ex bruta ignorantia manauit, & obrepsit inter multas errorum tenebras, improbari omnino necesse fuit. Si acquieuistis imperio, pessimo laqueo vos induistis. Primum tuipe fuit tacere: deinde si liberè vt oportet, in illa Baptismi profanatione inurit; deinde fuerinis, vos crimine leuitatis adeoque perfidiæ onerabunt. Atqui tacere nefas erit, quibus baptizādi munus à Christo fit iniunctum. Dixit mihi frater, vos iterū professos esse illa corruptela non posse à vobis ferri. Certè silentio vestro eam fouere consentaneum non est: neq; tamē iponte Ecclesia de ferenda est, nisi illi vos abdicent. Pergite in cursu vocationis vestræ. Si tantillum fuistis tyrannicis edictis abducere vos conentur, intrepidè ostendite vobis pluris esse Dei auctoritatem. Si deinde vos exturbent, cedendum erit violentiæ. Danda interim opera, vt testatum illis fit, vos iugum quod Christi feruis non est tolerabile, nequaquam subituros. Pastores qui iam certis Ecclesiis addicti sunt, ad alias nouas traduci rectum non effet, nisi ordine id fiat. Cæterum, si id vtile censuerint fratres, seniores, & Principum Consiliarij, nulla ratio, meo iudicio impedit, quominus nouis distionibus Christo acquirendis operam suam impendant, qui vocati fuerint. Exposuit mihi frater, timendum esse, ne tefpuatur illa doctrina, quia id vno in loco iam contigit. Ergo hæc tantùm lege experiamini. Reiicere enim, qui nullum adhuc contumaciæ ac obstinationis signum dederit, non satis humanum foret. Denique eiusmodi electio peraeq; legitima est, acsi pro communi vtilitate, qui in pago Ministèr fuit, in vrbe transferatur. Sic enim sua cuique tenenda est statio, ne simus loco affixi, vbi aliter de nobis statuit Ecclesia, cuius auctoritati parendum est. Nemo cupidus sit migrationis, neque ambiat nouam prouinciam, neque sponte locum mutet, neque etiam assentiatur eorū libidini qui Ecclesiæ ordine turbare moliuntur. Verùm vbi finis ille propositus
units.tr: The shortness of time compels me to reply briefly to your lengthy letter, most upright and sincerely honoured brother. It was handed to me shortly before noon. Two hours later I set off for the ecclesiastical assembly, and I came away from it three hours after that. I was still talking with our brother when our colleagues arrived again. So please forgive the brevity that necessity forces on me. I am not surprised that the councillors of the princes dealt with you so precisely, for I have already come to know their way of doing things. It was right and prudent that an exception was added to the chapter on the Lord's Supper. However morose they may be, a reasoned argument is more dangerous for you before them than open candour. But on the article on discipline, which among you does not exist, I do not see why you could not have subscribed. On baptism, that gross abuse, which springs only from brutish ignorance and has crept in among many shadows of error, had necessarily to be wholly condemned. If you have yielded to the command, you have entangled yourselves in a most wicked snare. First, it was for you to keep silent; then, if you speak out freely, as you ought, against that profanation of baptism, they will burden you with the charge of fickleness and even of treachery. Yet it would be wrong to keep silent, you to whom the office of baptizing has been enjoined by Christ. My brother told me that you have again declared that this corruption cannot be tolerated by you. Certainly it is not fitting to foster it by your silence; yet the Church should not be abandoned of your own accord, unless they dismiss you. Persevere in the course of your calling. If they try to lead you away by tyrannical edicts, boldly show them that God's authority counts for more. If then they drive you out, you must yield to violence. Meanwhile take care to make it plain to them that you will by no means submit to a yoke that is not bearable for the servants of Christ. It would not be right to transfer ministers who are already attached to certain churches to other new ones, unless this is done in due order. But if the brothers, the elders, and the councillors of the princes judge this useful, then, in my opinion, nothing prevents those who have been called from devoting their labour to winning new territories for Christ. My brother explained to me that there is a fear that this doctrine will be rejected, since this has already happened in one place. So try these things only on this condition. For it would not be humane enough to reject someone who has not yet given any sign of stubbornness and obstinacy. Finally, such a choice is just as lawful as if a minister who had served in a village were moved to a town for the common good. For each person must keep his own post, so that we are not fixed to a place where the Church decides otherwise about us, and to whose authority we must submit. Let no one be eager to migrate, nor seek a new province, nor change his place of his own accord, nor even assent to the wishes of those who seek to disturb the order of the Church. But where that goal has been set, namely the spreading of Christ's kingdom,

units.la: Epist.366. tus est, propagadi Regni Christi, praesto sint omnes ad obsequium. Precationis formula, ut Deus bonam & felicem resurrectionem det mortuis, quia ad regulam bene precandi non quadrat, repudietur. Tale quidem votum quin concipere liceat, non contendo. Si amicus sepeliatur, vel de eius morte allatus sit nuntius, optabo, ut ultimo die caelestis gloriae mecum sit particeps. Nulla in hoc voto superstitio. Verum alia in precibus tenenda sobrietas, ne quid temere excidat: nec quicquam postulemus, nisi praeeunte Dei verbo. In hoc enim principio acquiescere conuenit: Quomodo invocabunt in quem non crediderunt? Ergo qui sibi vel minimum indulgent in fingendis postulationibus, metas transiliunt. Quicquid vero ad praecipuum illud sacrificium vitiandum tendit, a piorum consuetudine longe remotum velim. Quare ut ab omni facie purgatus sit Dei cultus, mature occurre re expedit, ne in communem usum admittatur quod a vera pietate degenerat.
units.tr: Epist.366. all should be ready to obey. The formula of prayer that God grant the dead a good and happy resurrection should be rejected, since it does not fit the rule of praying well. I do not contend that one may not conceive such a wish. If a friend is buried, or news of his death is brought, I will wish that he may share with me in the glory of heaven on the last day. There is no superstition in this wish. But in other prayers a sober restraint must be kept, lest anything be uttered rashly, and we should ask for nothing except as the word of God leads. For we ought to rest on this principle: "How shall they call on him in whom they have not believed?" Therefore those who indulge themselves even slightly in inventing requests overstep the bounds. Whatever tends to spoil that chief sacrifice I would wish to be far removed from the custom of the pious. Therefore, so that the worship of God may be cleansed of every blemish, it is expedient to meet such things early, lest what degenerates from true piety be admitted into common use.

units.la: Incredulos a Deo petere, ut in fide illuminentur, prorsus est absurdum. Nulla enim oratio, nisi in fide sit fundata, Deo probatur. Et fides clavis est, quae nobis sola ianuam aperit ad precandum: ad eoque inuocationis est mater: & scite probat Augustinus, Cornelium fide fuisse praeditum, quia dicit Angelus preces eius fuisse exauditas. Apud eos tamen, qui sibi in torpore nimis indulgent, obiurgatio locum habet. Tu fidem non habes? pete ut detur: modo fixa maneat doctrina, sola fide nobis aditum ad Deum patefieri. Ergo quos tu nominas, arbitror duriusculc fuisse loquutos, ut ignauiam eorum experiefacerent, qui a suo vitio captant excusationis praetextum.
units.tr: It is utterly absurd for unbelievers to ask God to be enlightened in faith. For no prayer is approved by God unless it is founded on faith. Faith is the key, which alone opens the door to us for praying, and so it is the mother of invocation. Augustine rightly proves that Cornelius was endowed with faith, because the angel says that his prayers were heard. Among those, however, who indulge too much in their torpor, rebuke has its place. Do you not have faith? Ask that it be given, provided the doctrine stays fixed, that access to God is opened to us by faith alone. So I think those whom you name spoke rather harshly, in order to expose the laziness of those who seek a pretext for excuse in their own fault.

units.la: Quod ad lusus spectat, cupio moderationem teneri. Primum ne quaestus inde fiat, vel lucrandi illecebra multos homines implicet. Ad haec ne modum excedant, vel sumptu, vel assiduitate. Leges ergo ferendae essent, ut fratri exposui, quae vitia quantum fieri posset, coercerent: Ne lucrum quis reportet: ne quod in convivium destinatur, graviet lusores: ne saepius id fiat, & quae prudenter legislatores cauenda prospicient. Interea nostrae partes sunt, animaduertere si quis tempus & se ac sua consumat ludendo: neque ferre dissolutam illam licentiam, quae excommunicatione castiganda est, authore Paulo, 2. Thess. cap. 5. Quanquam nuptiarum praetextu diem Dominicum indigne profanent multi: praestat tamen liberos dies permittere, modo seuere omnia petulantia reprimatur. Qua in re summa diligentia opus est. Vale optime & colende frater. Dominum Quadratum & Tabellionem, & tuos Symmystas qui nobiscum sunt in syncera fide coniuncti, plurimum salutabis meo nomine. Collegae etiam mei vobis omnibus multam salutem precantur. Dominus tibi adsit te gubernet, sustineat sua virtute, labores tuos benedicat. Geneuæ, x xv. Septembris. M. D. LXII.
units.tr: As for games, I wish moderation to be kept. First, that no profit be made from them, and that the lure of gain not ensnare many people. Next, that they not exceed bounds, either in expense or in frequency. Laws therefore ought to be made, as I explained to the brother, which would restrain these vices as far as possible: that no one should gain profit, that what is set aside for the feast should not burden the players, that it should not happen too often, and such other matters as prudent lawgivers would foresee and guard against. Meanwhile it is our part to watch whether anyone wastes his time, himself and his goods in gaming, and not to tolerate that dissolute licence, which must be punished by excommunication, on the authority of Paul, 2 Thess. ch. 5. Although many profane the Lord's Day unworthily under the pretext of weddings, it is nevertheless better to allow free days, provided that all wantonness is severely repressed. In this matter the greatest diligence is needed. Farewell, most excellent and honoured brother. You will greet on my behalf Lord Quadratus and Tabellio, and your fellow-symmystae who are with us, united in sincere faith. My colleagues also wish you every good. May the Lord be with you, guide you, sustain you by his power, and bless your labours. Geneva, 25 September 1562.

units.la: CALVINVS N. S. D.
units.tr: CALVIN, to N., sends greetings.

units.la: Eiusdem cum superiori argumenti.
units.tr: On the same subject as the previous letter.

units.la: SI mihi ad manum fuisset fidelis nuntius quo tempore allatæ sunt tuæ priores literæ, statim responsuras eram: verum ubi præteriit occasio, mora segniorem me reddidit. Et nunc fere idem mihi accideret, nisi stimularet pudor: ignosces tamen brevitati, ad quam me adstringet temporis angustia. De tristi Eccle siæ vestræ dissipatione statim aduolauerat huc rumor: nec vero alium unquam exitum tam pertinacibus Gallicæ Ecclesiæ dissidiis fore putaui. Nunc quando aliena culpa vobis luenda fuit, meliorem rationem non video, quam ut sedem exilij mutent pij fratres. Nec me latet, quàm molesta res sit, quàm graues futuri sint sumptus, quibus incommodis implicita sit migratio. Sed dum aduersæ partis truculentiam mecum expendo, quiduis potius ferendum: hoc, meo iudicio, optimum compendium esset. Si vero manere omnino cogat necessitas, nimium seruilis erit dissimulatio, profestis Christi hostibus offerre baptizandos infantes & de fide contrariatacere. Quid captent minimè obscurum est, nempe vt de pura quam profitemur doctrina, triumphos agát. An æquum est nos illis esse vel adiutores, vel ministros ad Dei veritatem pedibus calcandam? Excipis, penes ipsos ordinarium esse minisferium Ego, vt taceam de indiuidua Cœnæ & Baptismi coniunctione, quam alius quisquam vrgeret, nõ existimo tanti esse quod sibi vendicant, quin profitenda sit ingenuè fides, ad cuius abnegationem oblique pios trahunt. Facessit omnis personalis respectus. Scio enim Sacramentum non pendere à dignitate ministri. Alia quæstio nunc vertitur, Liceatne pro Pastore agnoscere qui palàm oppugnet sacræ Cœnæ vim, rectum vsum, & institutionem: deinde spontaneam discessionem faciat à veris Christi Ecclesiis. Quanquam adeo præcise non ago, sed tantum exigo, vt qui infantem suum offert ad Baptismum, ingenuè profiteatur quod de Cœna sentit, ac simul testetur se fraternam coniunctionem colere cum omnibus Ecclesiis, quæ idem sentiunt. Atqui hanc conditionem non admittent. Proditor ergo, qui sciens & volens, impiam superbiam, & sacrilegum diuortiū silentio suo ratum habet. Morbis meis & occupationibus ignosces, si non accuratius de singulis differo. Adde quod summa rei, & simplici definitione contentus, ad minutissimos quosq; scrupulos discutiendos non libenter studium meum applico. De miseris Gallia perturbationibus malo vt te alij doceant. Vale eximie vir,& integerrime frater. Dominus te semper gubernet Spiritu suo,inuicta virtute sustineat,& incolumem tueatur. Salutant te plurimùm collegæ mei, ex quorû sententia tibi respondeo. Geneuæ.x v.i i i.Iunij. M. D. LXII.
units.tr: If a trustworthy messenger had been at hand when your first letter arrived, I would have replied at once. But once the opportunity had passed, delay made me more sluggish. Even now it would be much the same, were it not for shame pricking me. Please forgive the brevity, to which the shortness of time will confine me. News of the sad scattering of your Church reached us here at once, and I never thought that the stubborn quarrels of the French Church would end in any other way. Now that you must pay for another's fault, I see no better course than for the godly brothers to change their place of exile. I am not unaware how troublesome the matter is, how heavy the expenses of a move will be, and what inconveniences it involves. But when I weigh the savagery of the opposing side, I think that anything should rather be endured; this, in my judgement, would be the best shortcut. If, however, necessity forces you to remain altogether, it would be too servile a dissimulation to offer infants for baptism to the professed enemies of Christ and to keep silent about the contrary faith. What they are aiming at is not at all obscure: namely, to triumph over the pure doctrine we profess. Is it right for us to become their helpers, or their ministers, in trampling the truth of God underfoot? You reply that the ministry is ordinary among them. For my part, I say nothing of the inseparable joining of the Lord's Supper and Baptism, which anyone else would press; I do not think that what they claim for themselves is worth so much that the faith should not be openly confessed, although they draw the godly, by indirect means, toward its denial. All personal regard vanishes. For I know that a sacrament does not depend on the dignity of the minister. The other question now at issue is this: whether it is lawful to acknowledge as a pastor one who openly assails the power, right use, and institution of the holy Supper, and who has deliberately separated himself from the true Churches of Christ. Yet I do not press this so strictly; I only require that the man who offers his infant for baptism should frankly profess what he thinks about the Supper, and at the same time bear witness that he cultivates brotherly fellowship with all the Churches that think the same. But they will not accept this condition. He is therefore a traitor who, knowingly and willingly, ratifies by his silence their impious pride and sacrilegious separation. Forgive me for my illnesses and my occupations if I do not discuss each point more carefully. Add to this that I am content with the substance of the matter and a simple definition, and I am not inclined to apply my zeal to the examining of the smallest scruples. Concerning the wretched disturbances in France, I would rather that others instruct you. Farewell, excellent man and most upright brother. May the Lord always govern you by his Spirit, sustain you with unconquered strength, and keep you safe. My colleagues greet you warmly, and I reply to you in accordance with their opinion. Geneva, 18 June 1562.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus tuus.
units.tr: Your John Calvin.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. N. S.
units.tr: IO. CALVINVS N. N. S.

units.la: Eiusdem cum superiore Argumenti.
units.tr: By the same author, on the same subject as the previous letter.

units.la: VEhementer nobis dolet, optimi fratres, acsi non satis mali foret in misera tristique Ecclesiæ vestræ dissipatione, exorta esse in er vos certamina, quæ ad contentionem vsque erumperent. Quod eò nobis molestius est, quia ad reconciliandâ gratiam tollendumque dissidium non alia occurrit ratio, nisi vtrinque propria sententia cedatis: quod veremur ne difficile sit à vobis impetrare. Certè in literis vestris deprehendimus quod agnouit ille in Iliade Homeri peccari intus & extrà. Putat vna pars post clausa templa, vsquead vltimam litis decisionem manendum nihilominus fuisse in statione. Alij autem contendūt fas non fuisse diutius subsistere in eo loco, vbi per summum pro brum oppressa fuisset veritas, & quodammodo in exilium pulsa. Nos autem non aliter possumus statuere, quàm rectè fecisse eos, qui statim collectis vasis illinc migrarunt. Quibus verò cōmodum non fuit alio transfugere, eos misericordia potius, quàm insectatione esse dignos. Nam certè homines exteros hospitio affigere, acsi mancipia essent glebæ addicta, plusquam indignū esset. Fingamus integram adhuc stare Ecclesiam, priuatis tamen hominibus nulla esset religio solum vertere: quò magis concedendum est, vt locum deserant, vbi erepta sunt pietatis exercitia. Rursus eos, quibus domestica necessitas obstitit, ne se alio cò ferrent, exagitare tanquam sanæ doctrinæ proditores, minimè humanum est. Quòd autem obiicitur, Vbi liberos suos offerūt ad Baptismum, ita eos Christum ludibrio exponere: fatemur quidè si dissimulent tam errores & deliria, quàm tyrannidem, & barbaram superbiam eorum, quibus baptizandi munus concedunt, se detestari, præuaricationem esse non ferendam. Certum enim est, nihil aliud venari vmbratiles illos ministros, quâ vt de Christo, & sanâ doctrina triumphû agant. Hæc eorû insolētia foueri à nobis non potest, quin simus in Christū contumeliosi. Verùm si intercedat ingenua confessio, qua refellatur eorû arrogantia, nō videmus quid pios homines impediat, quò minus ab illis sinant liberos suos baptizari, quia ferre coguntur vt ordinarios ministros,quanuis non probent. Alia longè sacræ Cœnæ ratio est,quam nemo ex manu eorum sumet sine turpi sanæ doctrinæ abnegatione. In hac controuersia excutienda longius progredi non placuit: imò quæ hinc inde scripsistis consulto non attigimus,nescedulitas nostra oleum camino adderet. Itaq; vos rogamus & obtestamur,vt deposito litigandi studio,& sedato omni seruore vos mutuò amplexemini.Qui dura illa seruitute premü tur,gemant,& fratribus gratulentur quàm alibi nacti sunt libertatem.Quibus vero iniquâ illam dominationem effugere datû est,fratribus suis cõdolescant potius,quàm eos nimis præcisè vrgendo,exanimét.Interea q̃ hanc moderationem tenere malui-mus,quàm votis vestris obsequi,ign scite.Dominus vos Spiritu mansuetudinis,& simul inuictæ fortitudinis semper gubernet, yófquc iterum in vnum corpus colligat.Valete optimi,& nobis charissimi fratres.Geneuæ,xxvii.Octob. M. D. LXII.
units.tr: We are deeply distressed, most excellent brothers, that in addition to the wretched and sorrowful dispersal of your Church there should have arisen among you disputes that have broken out into open contention. This troubles us all the more because there is no other way to restore goodwill and end the division than for each side to yield something of its own opinion, and we fear this will be hard to obtain from you. Indeed, in your letters we find what Homer's Iliad recognised: that fault lies both within and without. One party thinks that, after the churches were closed, they should nonetheless have remained at their post until the final settlement of the dispute. The other side contends that it was not right to remain any longer in a place where the truth had been crushed by the greatest disgrace and, in a sense, driven into exile. For our part we can only judge that those who at once gathered up their belongings and left did right. As for those for whom it was not convenient to flee elsewhere, they deserve pity rather than harassment. For it would surely be more than shameful to tie strangers to their lodging as if they were serfs bound to the land. Suppose the Church were still standing whole: even so, for private individuals it would be no offence to leave the country, and so much more must it be allowed that they may abandon a place where the exercises of piety have been taken away. Again, to pursue those whom domestic necessity prevented from going elsewhere, and to denounce them as betrayers of sound doctrine, is by no means humane. As for the objection that, when they offer their children for baptism, they thereby expose Christ to mockery: we admit that if they conceal their detestation of the errors and follies, as well as the tyranny and barbarous arrogance, of those to whom they entrust the office of baptizing, that is a betrayal not to be tolerated. For it is certain that those shadowy ministers seek nothing else than to triumph over Christ and sound doctrine. We cannot encourage this insolence of theirs without becoming insulting to Christ. But if a frank confession intervenes, by which their arrogance is refuted, we do not see what hinders godly people from allowing their children to be baptized by them, since they are compelled to accept them as ordinary ministers, even though they do not approve of them. The case of the Lord's Supper is quite different, and no one should receive it from their hands without a shameful renunciation of sound doctrine. We have not wished to go further into this controversy; indeed, we have deliberately not touched on what you have written on either side, lest our scribbling add oil to the fire. So we ask and beseech you, laying aside the zeal for quarrelling and calming all heat, to embrace one another mutually. Let those who are oppressed by that harsh servitude groan, and rejoice with their brothers that they have found liberty elsewhere. Let those to whom it has been granted to escape that unjust domination grieve rather with their brothers, and not wear them out by pressing them too exactly. Meanwhile, forgive us that we preferred to keep this moderation rather than comply with your wishes. May the Lord always govern you with the Spirit of gentleness and at the same time of invincible fortitude, and gather you again into one body. Farewell, best and dearest brothers. Geneva, 27 October 1562.

units.la: SI QVA RATIO GENERALIS CONCILII Christianis dari possit.
units.tr: Whether any general council can be granted to Christians.

units.la: VT finem tádem habeant turbæ & dissidia,quibus Ecclesiam scissam & laceratam esse videmus, opus est libero & generali Concilio.
units.tr: So that the disturbances and dissensions by which we see the Church torn and rent may at last come to an end, a free and general council is needed.

units.la: Libertas in tribus capitibus continetur, in loco, in personis, in modo,vel ratione procedendi.
units.tr: Freedom is contained in three heads: in the place, in the persons, and in the manner or method of proceeding.

units.la: Quantum ad locum, nisi tutus pateat accessus omnibus qui audiendi sunt,vt illic de rebus controuersis disceptent,satis no tum est clausam esse ianuam libertati. Vrbs ergo deligenda erit media inter omnes regiones,vnde venturi sunt qui interesse debent Concilio.Deinde necesse erit Principes vicinos,per quorū ditionem transeundum erit,promittere & iurare saluum conductum omnibus qui illuc conuenient.
units.tr: As to the place: it is not enough that the door to freedom be shut, unless there is a safe approach open to all who must be heard, so that they may debate the matters in controversy there. A city must therefore be chosen that lies midway between all regions, from which those who ought to take part in the council will come. Then it will be necessary for the neighbouring princes, through whose dominions the journey must be made, to promise and swear a safe-conduct to all who assemble there.

units.la: Quantùm ad personas,iniquissimum esset solis Episcopis permitti sententias decisiuas: cùm satis superque notum sit,eorum cáusam tractari,in qua idonei non possunt esse iudices.
units.tr: As to the persons: it would be most unjust to allow the bishops alone to give decisive judgments, since it is sufficiently and more than sufficiently well known that their own cause is being dealt with, and in such a cause they cannot be suitable judges.

units.la: Deinde vt auctoritas,quam sibi vendicant, illis concedatur: nemo tamen eorum liber est:quia iureiurando adstricti sunt ad obsequium Papæ,& Rom. sedi sunt addicti, quod ex diametro pugnat cum libertate.
units.tr: Next, that the authority they claim for themselves should be conceded to them: yet none of them is free, because they are bound by oath to obey the Pope and are devoted to the Roman see, which is directly contrary to freedom.

units.la: Commodum remedium esset,si ds ligatur homines ex ea parte quæ Ecclesiæ reformationem tam in doctrina,quàm in moribus cupit & flagitat: quibus etsi non esset vox definitiua,vt loquuntur, liberum tamen esset intercedere omnibus decretis & determinationibus verbo Dei minùs consentaneis: vt iis etiam daretur audientia & admitterentur protestationes. Ipsi vero oitenderent iustas sibi esse contradicendi rationes, quo minus acquiescerent Episcoporum placitis.
units.tr: It would be a convenient remedy if men were appointed from that side which desires and demands the reform of the Church both in doctrine and in morals. Although these would not have a deciding vote, as they say, it would nevertheless be free for them to object to all decrees and determinations less in agreement with the Word of God, so that they too might be given a hearing and their protests admitted. Indeed, they would show that they have just grounds for opposing, and so would not be bound to acquiesce in the bishops' decisions.

units.la: Maxime vero intolerabile est, Papa prefidere Cocilio tanquam caput praesertim in hac noua qualitate, vt ab eo & eius arbitrio dependeant omnia. Atq; vt primum locum obtineat omnium permissu, ante omnia tamen ratio postulat, vt fe submittat Cocilio per omnia, iuretq; fe obseruaturum quicquid illic statutum fuerit: atque hoc modo fe abdicet dominatione quam sibi antehac arripuit, vt tantum fit vnus ex aliorum numero. Rursum adigé di effent Episcopi ad proprium iuiurandum, fe obsequentes fore Dei verbo, nec rationem habituros praefentis status: acsi quae inuentae fuerint corruptelae tam in doctrina, quam in ceremoniis & moribus, earum fe minime patronos fore vel fautores.
units.tr: Most intolerable of all is that the Pope should preside over the council as its head, especially in this new capacity, so that everything depends on him and his will. And although he should obtain the first place by the consent of all, reason nonetheless demands above all that he submit himself to the council in all things and swear that he will observe whatever is decided there; and in this way he would renounce the dominion he had seized for himself hitherto, so that he becomes merely one of the others. Again, the bishops should be bound by their own oath to obey the Word of God, and not to take account of the present state; as if they would in no way be patrons or supporters of whatever corruptions are found, in doctrine, in ceremonies, or in morals.

units.la: Modus procedédi omnino fruftratorius effet, fi mos qui nuper inualuit retineretur: nempe vt quicunque reformatione po ftulant, vel ore vel scripto exponerent suam doctrinam: deinde ipsis absentibus Praelati quod libitum effet, decernerent. Necesse igitur omnino est, omnes adesse, vt quicquid male & inscitè deliberare vellent Episcopi, corrigere liceat: atque ita integrum fit cunctis erroneis opinionibus obiicere rationes claras & validas.
units.tr: The method of proceeding would be altogether futile if the custom that has lately prevailed were retained: namely, that those who demand reformation should set out their doctrine by word or in writing, and then, with them absent, the prelates should decree whatever pleased them. It is therefore absolutely necessary that all be present, so that whatever the bishops might deliberate foolishly and unskilfully may be corrected; and thus it will be open to all to oppose clear and solid arguments to every erroneous opinion.

units.la: Operaepretium etiam est ante omnia, statuere quem ordinem sequi conueniat: nempe vt primo loco excutiantur articuli doctrinae, de quibus inter partes non conuenit: inde transitus fiat ad ceremonias: postremò de regimine Ecclesiae agatur.
units.tr: It is also worth while, above all, to determine what order it is fitting to follow: namely, that first the articles of doctrine about which the parties do not agree be examined; then the transition be made to ceremonies; and lastly the government of the Church be treated.

units.la: Capita doctrinae, de quibus hodie litigatur, sunt de cultu Dei: an scilicet ad vnicam & simplicem normam Scripturae exigi debeat, an vero fueritin hominum potestate & arbitrio leges ferre? Deinde an eorum traditiones animas obligent mortis reatu: Sub hoc capite comprehenduntur vota, prohibitio coniugij, confessio auricularis, & res similes. Deinde quaeredum erit, & definiendum vbi fundata fit salutis nostrae fiducia: meritone operū, an gratuita Dei misericordia feruemur. Hinc pendet materia liberi arbitrij, satisfactionum, purgatorij & similium rerum. Fidei certitudini annexa est Dei inuocatio, & secum trahit quaestionem de intercessione sanctorum.
units.tr: The heads of doctrine about which people are disputing today are these: concerning the worship of God, namely whether it ought to be measured by the single and simple rule of Scripture, or whether it lies within the power and discretion of men to enact laws. Next, whether their traditions bind souls under the guilt of mortal sin: under this head are included vows, the prohibition of marriage, auricular confession, and similar things. Then it will have to be asked and defined where the foundation of our confidence in salvation is laid: whether we are saved by the merit of works, or by the free mercy of God. On this depends the matter of free will, satisfactions, purgatory, and similar things. Connected with the certainty of faith is the invocation of God, and it brings with it the question of the intercession of the saints.

units.la: In secundo capite, quod est de ceremoniis, disputandum erit de congerie rituum, quam mutuati sunt ab vmbris legalibus: simul de numero Sacramentorum, & eorum accessionibus.
units.tr: In the second head, which concerns ceremonies, there will have to be discussion of the mass of rites which they have borrowed from the legal shadows; together with the number of the sacraments and their additions.

units.la: Tertiu caput, de regimine Ecclesiae, continet definitionem officij Episcopalis: vt sciatur quina sibi iure & merito hunc titulum vendicet. Huc etiā pertinent gradus, ordines, primatus, & alia similia.
units.tr: The third head, concerning the government of the Church, contains the definition of the episcopal office, so that it may be known whether he rightly and deservedly claims this title for himself. Here also belong the grades, orders, primacies, and other similar things.

units.la: Iam vero non sufficeret habere Cocilium, nisi vniuersale fuerit: siquidem animus est sedare & placare motus omnes, & cōtentiones, quibus turbatur Ecclesia. Verū quidé est, singulos Reges & Principes, vt suarum ditionum turbis remedium inuenient, posse cogere Nationale Concilium, si vicini suum consensum & studia non adiungant. Verum si partiale Concilium cogatur, quod nomen vniuersalis obtineat, id nihil aliud erit quàm igne magis ac magis accendere, augere pugnas, & creare nouos tumultus. Quare penitus necessarium est, eos omnes qui reformationem expetunt, in Concilium quod habebitur consentire, vt ita tota Christianitas coalescat: qui vero sanctam vnitatem & concordiam refugient, vt schismatici reputentur.
units.tr: Now indeed it would not be enough to have a council unless it were universal, since the aim is to calm and appease all the disturbances and contentions by which the Church is troubled. It is true that individual kings and princes may compel a national council, in order to find a remedy for the troubles of their own dominions, if their neighbours do not join in their consent and zeal. But if a partial council is held, which claims the name of universal, that will be nothing other than to kindle the fire more and more, to increase the fights, and to create new tumults. Therefore it is absolutely necessary that all who seek reformation agree to the council that will be held, so that all Christendom may be united; and those who shun holy unity and concord are to be regarded as schismatics.

units.la: AD QVAESTIONES CIRCA DISCIPLINAM Ecclesiae responsa.
units.tr: Answers to questions concerning the discipline of the Church.

units.la: HAc vbique astutia molitur Satan Christi Ecclesiam perfundare, quando puram doctrinam quae est velut anima, propter suas extinguere non poterit, vt fracta & soluta disciplina, nec nos corporis incidat, vnde luxatis membris paulo post sequatur tristis dissipatio. Atque vtinam probe expenderent, quicunque iugo reiecto permitti volunt cuique effrenem licentiam, hoc modo sequarere ruinam Ecclesiae & vastitatem. Certe non tantum moderationi studerent, sed placido, mansueto que spiritu, se ipsi quoque subiicerent communi disciplinae. Sed quoniam haec de re prolixius dissere re non est nobis propositum, breuiter litteris vestris respondebimus, optimi & integerrimi fratres. Vbi nos primum consuluitis, An adigendi sint ad fidem suam publice testandam, qui se in Ecclesiam admitti postulant: deinde sententiam nostram rogatis de ipsa confessionis apud vos receptae forma: tandem quaeritis, Annon excommunicandi sint e coetu fidelium, qui vel sua contumacia, vel turpitudine vitae ordinem peruertunt. Nos autem non videmus cur graue sit homini, qui inter Ecclesiae domesticos censeri vult, Christo capiti insolidum nomen dare. Quod fieri non poterit, nisi diserte subscribat syncerę pietati, & ingenuè errores damnet, quibus syncerita Religionis corrumpitur. Iam errorum detectatio saepe ex circunstantia temporum pendet. Quia prout nouas turbandi rationes excogitat Satan, prudenter occurrere necesse est. Scimus quantopere nobis commendet Paulus, vnitatem Spiritus, in vinculo pacis. Porro ad fouendum & retinendum inter pios consensum, pluris quam necessaria est illa solennis fidei professio. Denique quicunque optabunt Ecclesiam Dei illaté incolumem, non aegre ferent, hoc adminiculo eam fulciri. Non putamus esse, qui litem mouerant de generali illa professione: sed frigeret illa, nisi distinguitur quisque tam haereticis, quàm perversis dogmatibus renunciet. Iam in forma vestrae confessionis, nihil animaduertimus, quod nō sit sacris Dei oraculis & fidei orthodoxæ consentaneū. Itaq; summam doctrinæ quæ illic habetur, libenter probamus. Tantùm vellemus Epistolam ad Hebræos non adscribi Paulo, quum firmis argumentis persuasi simus alium esse auctore. Neq; tamen volumus nostro suffragio obstringi cōscientias, vel quasi præiudicio ligari Ecclesiam, quominus liberum sit singulis in medium proferre, si quid eos à subscriptione impediat. Etsi autē nobis displicet eorum morositas, qui ob leues scrupulos, à publi co consensu discedūt: si quis tamen verbum aliquod durius, vel locutionem amplecti nequeat, modò conueniat de re ipsa, tolerari forte poterit eius infirmitas, ne ob res quasq; minimas scindatur Ecclesia. Hortamur interea pios omnes ad hanc modestiā & sobrietatem, vt potius quisque ad reliquos omnes accedat, quàm sua peruicacia speciem præbeat tentandæ religionis. Cæterum, non aliter cōsistet Ecclesiæ incolumitas, quàm si ad eam purgandam, frænandas libidines, tollenda flagitia, corrigendos peruersos mores vigeat excommunicatio: cuius moderatum vsum quisquis recusat, præsertim admonitus, se ex Christi quibus non esse prodit. Valete eximij viri, & nobis ex animo colendi fratres. Dominus semper vobis adsit, vos gubernet suo Spiritu, & virtute sua confirmet ad implendum sanctæ suæ vocationis cursum. Genevæ, 11 i. Nonas Martij.
units.tr: Satan everywhere works this cunning, to shake the Church of Christ, since he cannot extinguish the pure doctrine, which is like its soul, by his own means. So, with discipline broken and dissolved, the body itself falls apart, and soon after the limbs are dislocated there follows a sad dispersion. Would that all who, having thrown off the yoke, want each person to be given unbridled licence would weigh this well: in this way they would follow the ruin and devastation of the Church. Certainly they would not only be eager for moderation, but would also, with a calm and gentle spirit, submit themselves to the common discipline. But since it is not our purpose to discuss this matter at greater length, we will answer your letter briefly, best and most upright brothers. You first ask us whether those who request admission into the Church should be compelled to testify publicly to their faith; then you ask our opinion on the form of confession received among you; and finally you ask whether those should be excommunicated from the assembly of the faithful who overturn the order of the Church by their obstinacy or by the disgrace of their life. As for us, we do not see why it should be a burden to a man who wants to be counted among the household of the Church to give his name fully to Christ, the Head. This cannot happen unless he clearly subscribes to sincere piety and frankly condemns the errors by which the purity of religion is corrupted. Now the detection of errors often depends on the circumstances of the times, because, as Satan devises new ways of disturbing, it is necessary to meet them prudently. We know how earnestly Paul commends to us the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Moreover, to foster and maintain agreement among the godly, that solemn profession of faith is more than necessary. Finally, whoever desires that the Church of God be preserved safe will not be vexed to see it supported by this aid. We do not think there are any who would stir up a quarrel over that general profession; but it would be cold unless each person renounced heretical and perverse doctrines alike. Now in the form of your confession we have noticed nothing that is not consistent with the holy oracles of God and the orthodox faith. Therefore we gladly approve the sum of the doctrine contained there. We would only wish that the Epistle to the Hebrews were not ascribed to Paul, since we are persuaded by firm arguments that it has another author. Yet we do not want consciences to be bound by our vote, or the Church to be tied by our prejudgment, so that it is not free for individuals to bring forward whatever prevents them from subscribing. And although we dislike the scrupulousness of those who depart from public agreement over slight scruples, still, if anyone cannot accept some harsher word or expression, provided they agree on the matter itself, perhaps his weakness may be tolerated, so that the Church is not torn apart over the smallest things. Meanwhile we exhort all the godly to this modesty and sobriety, so that each would rather join all the rest than show, by his obstinacy, the appearance of attempting to unsettle religion. Moreover, the safety of the Church will not be maintained otherwise than if excommunication flourishes to purge it, to restrain lusts, to remove disgraceful conduct and to correct perverse morals; whoever refuses its moderate use, especially when admonished, shows that he does not belong to Christ. Farewell, distinguished men, and brothers to be honoured from our hearts. May the Lord always be with you, govern you by his Spirit, and strengthen you by his power to complete the course of your holy calling. Geneva, 11 days before the Nones of March.

units.la: Ioannes Calvinus fratrum nomine.
units.tr: John Calvin, in the name of the brothers.

units.la: DE CŒLIBATV IN MINISTRO NON ITA requirendum esse.
units.tr: That celibacy should not be required of a minister.

units.la: Gratia tibi & Pax à Deo Patre nostro, & Domino Iesu Christo, frater mihi plurimum in Domino observandus,
units.tr: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, brother most to be honoured in the Lord,

units.la: Solemus, si quando ad eos scribendum est, quibuscum nulla nobis familiaritas aut necessitudo intercessit, diligenter primo excusare ac deprecari, ne vel temeritatis vel importunitatis, ea in re notemur. Ego tamē, etsi de facie prorsus tibi sum incognitus, satis causæ habere mihi videor, cur te meis literis sine ulla eiusmodi excusatione compellare audeam. Præterquam enim quod Christus noster, quem vno spiritu colimus & confitemur, satis firmum intimæ amicitiæ vinculum nobis esse debet: cùm mihi singularem tuam erga me beneuolentiam N. expositum fuisset, non dubitaui quin officij mei vicissim esset, similem erga te animi mei sensum, quo possem modo, testari ac declarare. Præcipuè verò mihi filiuciam addidit, & referebat te scriptis S.j.
units.tr: When we must write to people with whom we have no acquaintance or close tie, we are accustomed first to make careful apology and entreaty, so that we are not marked for rashness or importunity in the matter. Yet although I am wholly unknown to you by face, I seem to myself to have sufficient reason to address you by letter without any such apology. For apart from the fact that Christ our Lord, whom we worship and confess with one Spirit, ought to be a firm enough bond of intimate friendship between us, when your singular goodwill toward me was explained to me by N., I did not doubt that it was my duty in return to attest and declare, as best I could, a similar feeling of my mind toward you. What especially encouraged me was that he reported you were delighted by my writings, and promised that this service would not be unwelcome to you if you received a private letter from me. S.j.

units.la: Epist.371. meis obleƈtari, & tibi non ingratum fore officium hoc promis- sebat, si priuatas à me literas acciperes. Obtempe- raui igitur, eoque libentius, quòd me tibi non vulgariter obstrictum judica- bam, propterea tuum tam propensum in me studium: nec habebam in præsentia quod referrem, nisi hoc vnum quod ille postulabat, & mihi facile erat præstare. Fidem porrò non dubiam habui eius testimonio, quòd apud te annum vnum educatus totum animi tui sensum haberè in re perspeƈtum habere potest. Ergo vt iam dixi, cùm tu mihi aditum ad te non difficile patefeceris, diutius in longiori excusatione non imminorabor. Principio hoc tibi certum esse velim, nihil me magis cupere, quàm & interiore habere tecum amicitiam, & eam quibus licebit officiis confirmare. Ita enim mihi dotes tuas prædicauit pius hic frater, vt te inter eos facilè recenseam, quibus plurimum debent, quicunque Christiane esse volunt. Quò pauciores hodie boni sunt, eo maiore in pretio bonitas ipsa nobis esse debet, vbicunque apparet. Tu verò, vt audio, non exiguum & prudentiæ, & syncericatis & sanƈtitatis specimen in eo præbes, quòd cùm munus periculi & laboris plenum ingenti difficultate sustineas, ita egeris, vt piis ac cordatis omnibus abunde satisfacias. Proinde merito & istas tuas virtutes suspici, & te in Dominò sincere ac colere debent, quibus cordi est Ecclesiæ ædificatio. Quantum ad me attinet, vtinam suculentiore aliquo documento ostendere possem, quantopere te amem, quamtumque tibi deferam. Quòd tamen vnum mihi restat, possum si tibi meas ad Dominum preces testes fore huius charitatis, quam humanis officiis experiri non potes. Interim Ecclesiis vestris ex animo gratulor, quibus præter syncerioram doctrinam, tot egregia bona contulit Dominus. Neque enim paruo æstimandum est, quòd tales habent Pastores à quibus regantur & ordinentur, quòd adeò bene moratæ sunt, quòd adeò præclara forma constitutæ, quòd optima disciplina præditæ, quam iure vocare possumus optimum atque adeo vnicum retinendæ obedientiæ vinculum. Nos enim magna nostra molestia experimur quid valeat, dum eam desider�amus, nec vlla ratione possumus ad eam peruenire. Hæc res facit, vt sæpe animo vacillem ac minus strenuè functionem meam exequar. Quinetiam desperarem prorsus, nisi succurreret Ecclesiæ ædificatione semper esse opus Domini, quòd ipse virtute sua semper prosperabit, etiamsi nos adminicula omnia deficiant. Est tamen hoc magnū rarūm quoque bonum, adiuuari tam nec stirio præsidio. Itaque Ecclesias nostras tum demum rite suffultas arbitrabor, vbi isto nexuo colligatæ fuerint. Cæterum confessionem vestram quæ nuper fuit edita, inspexi tantum. Percurrere nondum per oppor tunitatem licuit. Habet tamen ab iis viris testimonium, quorum rum iudicio facile acquiesco. Tamen in commendatione caelibatus cuperem vos esse paulo parciores. Ignoscesc hac in re meae simplicitati, quod libere tibi exponere non dubito, quid mihi non ita placeat. Video consilium, vestrum non omnino detestitui aliqua ratione. Coniugio qui impliciti tenentur, minus sunt ad opus Domini expediti: ut magnopere ab hac remora solutos esse expediat, qui se totos volunt Domino consecrare: deinde ipsa continentia non minimam sacro ministerio dignitatem commendat. Postremo non vi nec tyrannice adigitis ad caelibatum qui in functione sunt Ecclesiastica: sed quod iudicatis in rem esse Ecclesiae, simpliciter illis consulitis, ac suadetis.
units.tr: Epist. 371. I therefore complied, and all the more willingly because I judged myself not slightly obliged to you for your so favourable zeal toward me. I had nothing at present to return except this one thing he asked, which was easy for me to grant. Moreover I held his testimony as no doubtful guarantee, since you were educated for a year with him, and he can have a clear view of the whole of your mind on the matter. So, as I have said, since you have made it easy for me to open the way to you, I will not linger over a longer apology. First, let this be certain to you: I desire nothing more than both to have inward friendship with you and to strengthen it by whatever services I can. He praised your gifts to me so highly that I readily count you among those to whom all who wish to be Christians owe very much. The fewer good men there are today, the greater the value that goodness itself ought to have for us wherever it appears. You, as I hear, give no small proof of prudence, sincerity and holiness in this, that although you bear an office full of danger and labour with great difficulty, you have so conducted yourself that you abundantly satisfy all the pious and sensible. Therefore those virtues of yours rightly deserve to be esteemed, and those who have the building up of the Church at heart ought to love and honour you sincerely in the Lord. As far as I am concerned, I wish I could show by some more substantial proof how much I love you and how much I esteem you. What remains to me is that I can be a witness of this affection before the Lord through my prayers to him, since you cannot test it by human services. Meanwhile I heartily congratulate your churches, to which the Lord has given, besides purer doctrine, so many excellent blessings. Indeed it is no small thing that they have such ministers by whom they are governed and ordained, that they are so well ordered, so finely constituted, and endowed with such excellent discipline, which we may rightly call the best and indeed the only bond of retaining obedience.
