For we experience to our great distress what this is worth, since we miss it and cannot in any way attain to it. This matter often makes me waver in spirit and carry out my function less vigorously. I would even despair altogether, were it not that the building up of the Church is always the work of the Lord, who will always prosper it by his own power, even when all our aids fail us. Yet this is a great and rare good, to be upheld by such a strong defence. Therefore I shall judge our churches to be properly supported only when they have been bound together in that bond. As for your confession which was published recently, I have only glanced through it; I have not yet had the opportunity to read it through. Still, it has the testimony of men whose judgment I readily accept. Nevertheless, in commending celibacy I would wish you to be a little more sparing. Pardon my simplicity in this matter, since I do not hesitate to tell you frankly what does not so much please me. I see that your plan is not wholly without some reason. Those who are bound up in marriage are less free for the work of the Lord; so it is expedient that those who want to consecrate themselves wholly to the Lord be loosed from this hindrance. Then continence itself commends no small dignity to the sacred ministry. Lastly, you do not force those who are in ecclesiastical office to celibacy by violence or tyrannically; but because you judge it to be for the good of the Church, you simply advise and urge them.

units.la: Atqui, ut fatear, coniugium multa & varia impedimenta secum trahere, a quibus optandum sit liberos esse Christi servos: non tamen eiusmodi esse concedam, quae ab officio illos revocent. Tum vicissim obiiciam, caelibatum quoque suas habere incommoditates, eaque non paruas nec vnius generis. Nondum de continentiae difficultate loquor. Sed dico caelibes non minoribus nec paucioribus distrahi auocamentis, quam coniugatos: aut certe parum esse discriminis, quin utrique exaequo distrahantur. Quod si etiam constaret nihil caelibatu liberius, coniugio nihil esse magis impeditum: obstare tamen id non debet, quominus necessitati consulatur. Certum est autem, coniugio multos vtiliter carere non posse, qui sunt prae aliis ad ministerium idonei. Ad secundum respondeo, Domino optime omnia prouidisse, quibus ornati dotibus suum ministerium conueniret. Videmus autem longe abesse, quin caelibatum inter eas commendarit. Quod non imperatis eam certa lege, probo. Sed vide ne illud ipsum legem sit praescribere, minoris aestimare eos qui vxores duxerint, quod videantur nonnihil ornamenti amisisse. Neque in veteri Ecclesia lex erat, quae cogeret. Sed ita in aluerat praepostera caelibatus admiratio, vt coniugium in Episcopis dedecore notaretur. Postea sensim irreplit Legis seueritas, quae innumeras malorum formas nobis peperit: quid boni attulerit, non possum iudicare. Proinde semper vereor, ne periculosum sit immodicum haberi caelibatui honorem, quo boni viri a coniugio abstrerreantur, etiam vbi vrget necessitas.
units.tr: Yet, to be frank, I grant that marriage brings with it many and various hindrances, from which it is to be wished that Christ's servants were free. I do not concede, however, that they are of such a kind as to call men away from their office. In turn, I would object that celibacy also has its inconveniences, and not small ones or of only one kind. I am not yet speaking of the difficulty of continence. I say that the unmarried are drawn away by distractions no less and no fewer than married men, or at least that there is so little difference that both are distracted about equally. Even if it were established that nothing is freer than celibacy and nothing more hampered than marriage, this should not stand in the way of meeting a necessity. It is certain, moreover, that many men who are, above others, fit for the ministry cannot do without marriage. As to your second point, I reply that the Lord has very well provided all the gifts with which those who suit his ministry are adorned. We see, however, that he is far from having commended celibacy among them. I approve that you do not impose it by a fixed law. But take care that it is not itself a law to set a lower value on those who have taken wives, as if they seemed to have lost some of their dignity. Nor was there a law in the ancient Church compelling celibacy. Yet such an absurd admiration for celibacy grew up that marriage in bishops was branded as a disgrace. Afterwards the severity of the law crept in gradually, and it has brought forth for us countless forms of evil; what good it has done I cannot judge. Therefore I always fear that it is dangerous to hold celibacy in excessive honour, since it deters good men from marriage even where necessity presses.

units.la: Non abs re igitur cupere mihi videor, vt siqua est hac in re apud vos auctoritas, mitigetur: non quia vobis in praesentia obsit: sed quia multum obesse posteris poterit, quibus scis esse consulendum. Quod si rationes vestrae ita nunc habent, vt periculum aliquod ex Pastorum coniugio vobis imminear, initam esse rationem velim, qua obuiaretur. Cogor iterum veniam huius meae rusticitatis petere. Non enim mihi temperare potui, quin timorem meum hac in breuiter iudicarem:
units.tr: It seems to me, therefore, not out of place to wish that, if there is any authority among you in this matter, it be moderated, not because it harms you at present, but because it may do great harm to posterity, whose interests you know you must consult. But if your considerations now stand in such a way that some danger threatens you from the marriage of ministers, I would like a plan to be devised by which it might be met. I am again compelled to beg pardon for this rusticity of mine. For I could not restrain myself from briefly setting out my fear on this point:

units.la: I.Tim.3.1
units.tr: I. Tim. 3.1

units.la: Tit.1. supervacuum illum fortassis: sed tamen non de nihilo conceptum. Atque ut intelligas me priuatam causam hic non agere: ego quem coelibatui tantopere infestum vides, vxorem nunquam duxi: & an ducturus aliquando sim, nescio. Quod si duxero, hoc consilio faciam, ut expeditior a multis tricis Domino vacare possim. Neque in ista actione incontinentiae meae praetextum capto, quam obiicere mihi nemo poterit. Verum occasionem cogitandi volui tibi praebere. Neque enim dubito, quin si animum semel ad hanc confuctationem ferio adieceris pro tua singulari prudentia longoque vsu, prouisurus sis quid sit maxime salutare: & quod optimum factu visum fuerit, facturus. Quantum ad hanc functionem cui praefectus es, sic te eam administrare confido, ut nullius exhortatione opus habeas. Magis optarem abs te admoneri, si quando tibi occasio daretur, & tantum otij haberes. Interim, quod sponte scio te facere, conseruandae vnitati studeas, obtestor. Tempora ipsa nos satis docent, quam necesse sit fideliter in Domino conspirare, quo ita iunctis animis aduer sus Satanam omnesque eius ordines militemus. Dominus Iesus te conseruet, frater integerrime, & mihi in Domino tenerende. Rogo ut meo nomine salutes, quos sperabis aequo animo salutem accepturos.
units.tr: Tit. 1. Perhaps that fear is superfluous, but it is not conceived without reason. And so that you may understand that I am not pleading a private cause here: I, whom you see so hostile to celibacy, have never taken a wife, and whether I shall ever do so, I do not know. But if I do marry, I shall do so with this purpose, that I may be freer to be at the Lord's disposal, unencumbered by many cares. Nor in this matter do I seek a pretext for my incontinence, which no one will be able to throw in my face. I have wished rather to give you an occasion for reflection. For I do not doubt that if you apply your mind to this matter, with your singular prudence and long experience, you will foresee what is most conducive to salvation, and will do what seems best. As for the office over which you have been placed, I trust you administer it so well that you need no exhortation from anyone. I would rather be admonished by you, if ever an occasion were given you and you had so much leisure. Meanwhile, I earnestly beg you to strive, as I know you do of your own accord, to preserve unity. The times themselves teach us well enough how necessary it is to agree faithfully in the Lord, so that, with minds thus joined, we may fight against Satan and all his ranks. May the Lord Jesus keep you, most upright brother, and hold you dear to me in the Lord. Please greet in my name those whom you think will receive the greeting with a calm mind.

units.la: AD QVAEDAM DOCTRINAE CAPITA aliquatenus infermentata.
units.tr: TO CERTAIN HEADS OF DOCTRINE, SOMEWHAT WEAKENED

units.la: Dilectissimi fratres, quia redditae nobis fuerunt literae vestrae quarto mense postquam datae fuerat, mirum vobis videri non debet, q; tardius expectatione vestra ad illa responsum a nobis acceperitis. Vt ad rem veniamus, valde nobis dolet quod ita sursum & deorsum agitari vobis contingit: & vbicunque pedem tuleritis, Satan cominifcatur aliquid, quo vobis nouas molestias inferat. Atqui non alia fuit Patrum conditio vt desse testatur Paulus, q; & ipse & reliqui pij incertis sedibus vagantur. Etsi igitur solum saepe vobis vertendum fit, & mutari subinde quod ad corpus cotingat: discenda est nihilominus vera animi statio & spiritus constantia. Atque illa doctrina in vsum deducenda est, quae filiis Dei peregrinandum esse in mundo tradit: quae etiam omnibus piis communis est, quanuis illius experientiam vnis prae aliis D.constare velit, dum illos huc & illuc circumducit. Vobis interea ipsi & condolemus, & ex animo vestrę quieti si qua nobis ratio ad manum esset, consultum vellemus. Et tamen haec nostra συμπάθεια erga vestras miserias efficere nō potest, vt vos liberemus ab officio: atque vt hoc nobis accideret, nihil aliud esset, quàm vobis imponere vanis blanditiis, neque hoc vobis
units.tr: Most beloved brethren, since your letter was delivered to us four months after it had been dated, you should not think it strange that you received our answer to those points later than you expected. To come to the matter: we are deeply grieved that you are so tossed up and down, and wherever you set foot, Satan contrives something to bring fresh troubles upon you. Yet the condition of the Fathers was no different, as Paul testifies that they were destitute, and both he and the other godly wander in uncertain dwellings. Therefore, although you must often change your ground, and what concerns the body must be changed from time to time, nevertheless you must learn a true steadiness of mind and constancy of spirit. And that doctrine must be put into practice which teaches that the sons of God must be pilgrims in the world; it is common to all the godly, although God wishes his experience to rest on some more than others, while he leads them hither and thither. Meanwhile we both sympathise with you and, if we had any means at hand, would gladly provide for your peace of mind. And yet this our sympathy [συμπάθεια] towards your miseries cannot free you from your duty; and if it did so, it would be nothing else than to impose on you with empty flatteries, and this would not be useful to you yourselves.

units.la: Epist. 372. Ex Gall.
units.tr: Epist. 372. From the French.

units.la: I. Cor. 4. 11. vobis ipsis vtile foret. Imò & ipsi scitis eò magis augeri nostram coram Deo condemnationem, cùm ab hominibus absolui studemus. Non aliud igitur superest, quàm vt pure & simpliciter aperiamus vobis, quid nobis videatur de eo quod est à vobis propositum. Ac primùm quidem valde mirati sumus, cùm audiuimus, in ea confessione quæ requiritur à vobis, nihil videri vobis inesse quod Dei verbo directè repugnet. Atqui in eo existimamus metu vobis præstrictos fuisse oculos. Nam in articulo Baptismi, damnantur nominatim, qui existimant infantes à natiuitate esse sanctificatos. Et quòd ad Cœnam, dicunt Iudam non minus corporis Christi participem fuisse, quàm Petrum. Idem illud, quod Christus in suà humana natura vbique sit, vti ipsi videtur, cùm Deus sit & homo: quasi vnitas personæ confusionem diuinæ & humanæ naturæ afferret. Quòd affertis ista non esse proprie confessionem fidei, nihil aliud est (quod cum bona venia dictum sit) quàm effugium, ad dissimulandum malum vel contegendum. Porrò Dominus non est sophista, vt sibi ludicrusmodi cauillationibus sinat. Vtcunque igitur aliud nomen vel titulum scripto illi imponatis, testamini tamen cum solenni iureiurando, ita vestram fidem habere. Atque vt ad Deum vsque non ascendatur, tamen apud homines etiam itâ spe pendendo bilinguesque estis, vt perfidiæ notam euitare non possitis. Vt enim bona sit illorum intentio, à quibus vobis ista proponuntur: non est hoc tamen satis, si ad rectum finem per media minus licita tenditis. Petimus igitur à vobis per Dominum, si ad tempus ita consopiti fuistis, vt nunc serio expergefiatis. Vt enim syncerè dicamus quod res est, non potest scriptu eiusmodi admitti, quin simul obliquè abrenuntietur Dei veritati, quæ vna nobis non quauis statione modo, sed vita ipsa charior debet esse. Hoc est autem remedium, si ita reponatis, Baptismum infantibus superfluum non esse, quia promissione sanctificati sint, cùm Sacramentum sit confirmatio necessaria propter humanam infirmitatem, vt ita promissio secum trahat comes sacramentum, nedum vt illius contemptu inuehat. In articulo de Cœna sic reponatis: Substantiam veri corporis & sanguinis Iesu Christi, vti ex vtero virginis illam semel accepit, præsentem esse in Cœna tam fidelibus quàm infidelibus: & quauis soli fideles reuera & effi-citer percipiant, non minus tamen infi-delestes teneri corporis & sanguinis Domini, quia Sacramentum polluerint. Item horum verborum loco: Reiicimus doctrinam illorum qui tradunt non percipi Christum nisi spiritualiter, reponatis, qui tradunt non percipi nisi Spiritum Christi, carne nimirum & sanguine exclusis. Scriptum est enim, Caro mea vere est cibus, & sanguis meus vere est potus. Et quanuis illa percepto spiritualis sit, non ideo minus tamen sit reipsa, neque in solá phantasia vel opinione consistit. Item horum vero borum loco: Christum secundum naturam humanam sedere: Confitemur Christum in caelo secundum humanam suam naturam; unde & illum expectamus, ut tamen pro infinita sua virtute quæ sese ubique porrigit, ex quo ad dexteram Patris cōsedit, possit nos incomprehensibili modo vere pascere corpore & sanguine suo, sine ulla mutatione loci. Ubi sit mentio Sacramentorum, sic illud nomen interpretandum erit, ut per illud intelligantur qui aut tollunt vim Sacramentorum, aut vsum corrumpunt.
units.tr: I. Cor. 4. 11. Indeed you yourselves know that our condemnation before God is increased the more we strive to be absolved before men. Nothing remains, therefore, but that we plainly and simply lay before you what we think of what has been proposed by you. And first of all we were greatly astonished when we heard that in the confession which is demanded of you, you see nothing that directly contradicts the Word of God. Yet we think your eyes were blinded by fear in this. For in the article on Baptism, those are condemned by name who think infants are sanctified from birth. And as to the Supper, they say that Judas was no less a partaker of the body of Christ than Peter. Likewise that Christ, in his human nature, is everywhere, as they themselves hold, since he is God and man, as if the unity of person brought confusion of the divine and human natures. As for your claim that these things are not properly a confession of faith, this is (to speak with due respect) nothing but an escape, to conceal or cover up the evil. Moreover, the Lord is not a sophist, to allow himself to be mocked by such quibbles. Therefore, whatever other name or title you give that writing, you nevertheless testify, with a solemn oath, that you hold the faith thus. And although you do not ascend to God, you are nonetheless so hanging in suspense and double-tongued before men that you cannot avoid the mark of treachery. For even if the intention of those by whom these things are proposed to you is good, it is not enough if you strive towards a right end by means that are less than lawful. We beg you, therefore, through the Lord, if you have been so lulled to sleep for a time, now to wake up in earnest. For, to speak sincerely as the matter stands, such a writing cannot be admitted without at the same time obliquely renouncing the truth of God, which ought to be dearer to us than any station, indeed than life itself. The remedy, if you answer thus, is this: that Baptism is not superfluous for infants, although they are sanctified by the promise, since the sacrament is a necessary confirmation on account of human weakness, so that the sacrament accompanies the promise as its companion, and does not rather lead to contempt of it. In the article on the Supper you should answer thus: that the substance of the true body and blood of Jesus Christ, which he once received from the womb of the Virgin, is present in the Supper both to the faithful and to the unfaithful; and although only the faithful truly and effectively receive it, nevertheless the unfaithful are no less guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, because they have polluted the sacrament. Likewise, in place of these words: "We reject the doctrine of those who teach that Christ is received only spiritually," you should answer: "We reject the doctrine of those who teach that only the Spirit of Christ is received, with flesh and blood excluded." For it is written: "My flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink." And although that reception is spiritual, it is not for that reason any less real, nor does it consist in mere fancy or opinion. Likewise, in place of these words: "that Christ sits according to his human nature": "We confess that Christ in heaven, according to his human nature, is thence also to be expected; yet, by his infinite power which extends itself everywhere, from the time he sat at the right hand of the Father, he can truly feed us, in an incomprehensible manner, with his body and blood, without any change of place." Where mention is made of the Sacraments, that name is to be interpreted so as to mean those who either destroy the force of the Sacraments or corrupt their use.

units.la: Si Episcopus vel Curatus ad Ecclesiam se adiunxerit.
units.tr: If a bishop or curate joins the Church.

units.la: Ogatus sententiam de Episcopis, Curatis, & aliis eiusmodi graduatis quos vocant, si quos Dominus ea gratia dignatur, ut ad Ecclesiam se adiungerent, quomodo se erga illos gerendum sit, illam ita hic in pauca contuli, ut a lectoribus breuitatis veniam deprecer: cum præter summas temporis angustias, quibus hæc dictare cogor, catarrho quoque afflictus sim, qui me denuo & tardiorem omnino reddit.
units.tr: I was asked for my opinion about bishops, curates and others of that sort called graduates, if the Lord graces any of them so that they join the Church, and how they should be treated. I have set out my view here briefly, and I ask readers to pardon its brevity: besides the great shortage of time under which I am forced to dictate these words, I am also afflicted with a catarrh, which makes me even slower.

units.la: Si ergo accideritut quis ex Papatu cui animarum cura commissa fuerit: Episcopus nempe vel Curatus. Domini gratia perceperit, ut puram Euangelij doctrinam profiteatur, si minus idoneus ad Pastoris munus deprehendetur, neque ea quæ requiritur prædictus scientia & dexteritate, temere fecerit omnino si tantæ rei se immiscere voluerit. Fructus igitur conuersionis ipsius in eo extabit, si omni ea cura abdicauerit, atque ita agnoscat nimis crassum illum abusum, quod priùs titulum inanem sine re gesserit. Ac proinde successori idoneo decedat, qui legitime institutur: ipsi satis erit si quis locum teneat in grege Domini.
units.tr: If, then, it happens that someone from the Papacy to whom the cure of souls was committed, namely a bishop or curate, has by the grace of the Lord come to profess the pure doctrine of the Gospel, but is found less fit for the office of pastor and not endowed with the required knowledge and skill, he will have acted rashly if he wishes to meddle in so great a matter at all. The fruit of his conversion will therefore appear if he gives up all that care, and so acknowledges that the crass abuse was that he held the empty title without the reality. He should accordingly yield to a suitable successor who is lawfully installed; it will be enough for him to hold a place in the flock of the Lord.

units.la: Si vero quis istiusmodi doctrina & dexteritate & affectu etiam prædictus erit ad porro etiam docendum, primum omnium edat fidei confessionem, ac sanctè testetur se puræ & syncerae Religioni adhærere: deinde vero agnoscat suam illam vocationem cum mero abusu fuisse coniunctam: petat nouam approbationem: ac nominatim iritum profiteatur, quod auctoritate Papæ institutus prius fuerit, ac simul abrenuntiet illicitis omnibus mediis & repugnantibus ordini, quem Dominus Iesus Christus in Ecclesia constituit.
units.tr: If, however, someone is endowed with such teaching, skill and zeal that he is fit to go on teaching, he should first of all make a confession of faith and solemnly testify that he adheres to the pure and sincere religion. Then he should acknowledge that his former calling was joined with plain abuse, seek a fresh approval, and expressly profess that his institution by the authority of the Pope was null. At the same time he should renounce all illicit means and everything that conflicts with the order which the Lord Jesus Christ established in the Church.

units.la: His præmissis nō video quid obstet, quominus ille admittatur ad munus Pastoris, modò promittat & reipsa præstet fidem, quæ ad munus fungendum requiritur: ac præsertim ut sese coniugat cum rum coetu Ministrorum, qui verbum pure docent, seseque subiiciat disciplinae & politiae, quae inter ipsos locum habet. Quod ad superioris ipsius v tae memoriam attinet, illa sepulta maneat: ne que quicquam illi tum admissum imputetur, tantum ut admonea-tur officij in posterum legitime praestandi. Si obiicitur Pauli canon ille, quo traditur eligendum Episcopum irreprehensibilem esse oportere, respondeo non hic agi, meo quidem iudicio, de simplici vel absoluta electione, sed de approbatione vel restitu-tione ad certum munus propter interuenientem corruptionem. Quemadmodum enim istiusmodi obtinuerunt tum gradum illum & titulum Pastorum ad suum iudicium: ita sane vbi sese ipsi offerent ad munus illud deinceps praestandum, non male illis ab Ecclesia conceditur quod ab ipsis ante minus legitime vsurpa-tum erat. Duo sunt in illo statu summa vitia. Vnum, quod no-ta ratione instituti sin: ad munus Ecclesiasticum. Alterum, qui de illo gradu sese ipsi deiecerint, dum nihil eius praestiterunt, quod ad rem pertineret. Sed illud non fecit, quominus agnoscantur pro Ministris ordinariis, vbi sese Ecclesiae coniungere patres ostenduntur: atque ita de nouo confirmentur demum, ad corrigendum praecedentem defectum.
units.tr: With these things premised, I do not see what prevents him from being admitted to the office of pastor, provided he promises, and in fact shows, the faith required for discharging that office; and especially that he join the company of ministers who teach the Word purely, and submit himself to the discipline and polity that obtain among them. As for the memory of his former life, let it lie buried: nothing admitted by him then is to be imputed to him, only let him be reminded to discharge his office lawfully in future. If the rule of Paul is objected, by which it is laid down that a bishop must be chosen blameless, I answer that here, in my judgement, the question is not one of simple or absolute election, but of approval or restoration to a certain office on account of the corruption that has intervened. For just as such men obtained that rank and title of pastors by their own choice, so when they offer themselves to discharge that office from now on, it is no bad thing that the Church grants them what they had previously usurped less lawfully. There are two great faults in that state: the one, that they were not installed by a sound rule of ecclesiastical office; the other, that they cast themselves down from that rank while performing nothing that pertained to it. Yet this does not prevent them from being acknowledged as ordinary ministers where they show that they join themselves to the Church; and so they are at length confirmed anew, to correct the earlier defect.

units.la: Imprimis autem hic vltro citroque ambitio caueda est: nam vt in nullus gratiam ordinem Ecclesiae fas est conuellere: ita etiam ea seueritas adhibenda non est, quae opinionem quandam afferat, quasi emolumentum priuatum hic quaeratur: vt voca-bulum illud ᾿επισκοπος quod hic adhibet Paulus, eo pertinet: sic expeditum erit in istiusmodi negotiis, vt nemo ludeat obtinere vnus prae aliis in Ecclesiae ministerio adeundo, vel suscipiendo. Si qui se in viam redire velle restantur, hoc iudicio sibi iniuriam fieri queruntur, peccant maxime. Constat enim non posse haberi pro Christianis Pastoribus, nisi prius abrenuntient Sacerdotio Papali, ad quod prouecti erant, vt Christum sacrificarent: quod est blasphemiae genus omnibus modis detestandum. Praeterea etiam requiritur vt aperte profiteantur, se abstinere omnino velle ab omnibus illis superstitionibus & foeditatibus, quae simpliciati Euangelij repugnant. Quomodo enim sanctam Coenam administrabunt, nisi ab illa Missae abominatione alienissimos se ostendant? Vt neque Baptismi idonei Ministri esse possunt, nisi aperte ei is illis contaminatiis, quibus ex parte hominum depravatus fui. In summa non possunt admitti pro Pastoribus ab Ecclesia, nisi se ad officium praestandum ipsi obstringant.
units.tr: Above all, ambition must be guarded against on both sides. For just as it is not right to overturn the order of the Church for anyone's favour, so too that severity should not be applied which gives the impression that private advantage is being sought here. As the word episcopos that Paul uses here implies, in such matters it should be made plain that no one seeks to obtain one office above others in approaching or accepting the ministry of the Church. If some who refuse to return to the right way complain that they are wronged by this judgement, they sin most grievously. For it is agreed that they cannot be regarded as Christian pastors unless they first renounce the Papal priesthood, to which they were advanced in order to sacrifice Christ, a kind of blasphemy to be detested in every way. Furthermore, it is also required that they openly profess they wish to abstain altogether from all those superstitions and foulnesses that oppose the simplicity of the Gospel. For how will they administer the holy Supper unless they show themselves most remote from that abomination of the Mass? Nor can they be fit ministers of Baptism unless they openly renounce those corruptions with which men have in part depraved it. In sum, they cannot be admitted as pastors by the Church unless they bind themselves to discharge the office.

units.la: His praesuppositis, istiusmodi Episcopi partes serunt, dare operam quantum in se erit, vt omnes Ecclesiae quae ad ipsius Episcopatu pertinent, ab omnibus erroribus & idolorum cultibus reputent. gentur,dum ipse exemplo praebibit omnibus Curatis suae diœcesis,atque ipsos inducet ad admittendam reformationem,ad quam Dei verbo inuitamur : & quae tum statui,tum vsui primitiae Ecclesiae omnino respondet.Simul etiam demonstret,se non probare illos qui verbo Dei obedire detrectauerint:vti altera ex parte suum consensum cum veris Dei seruis retinetur, & fraternam cum eis coniunctionem colat. Quod attinet ad bona illa,quae temporalia vocantur,siue in iurisdictione, siue in redditu annuo consistant:quanquis illorum origo ab ea corruptione emanarit, quae nullo modo ferenda sit cum ministerij spiritualis pura sim plicitate:quandiu tamen res ita cófusae manent, poterit quodam sinendi modo ipsis possessio relinqui , adhibita illa exhortatione, Videant quomodo ea dispensent quae Deo dicata nouerint, tum vt ne profanent res Deo sacras,tum vtsefe in modestia continent,quae veros Episcopos decet.Quod reliquum est,si itiuf modi,ita suis prouentibus & dominiis additi sint,praestaret contentos esse nomine Protectorum Ecclesiae , operam dantes vti verbum Dei annuntiandum à Ministris suscipiretur , accultus Dei sartus tectus maneret:vt interea ministerio sese non immiscerent,sed illi adesse studerent, vt in specione quadam nomine & auctoritate regia freti vel subnixi. Atque eo casu, etiamsi illic subesset infirmitas,quae non esset excusabilis,tolerandi essent tamen , dum pro honoratis Ecclesiae membris, cui sese impendere nt,haberentur.
units.tr: Given these presuppositions, such bishops have the duty of taking pains, as far as in them lies, that all the churches which belong to their bishopric be cleansed of all errors and of the worship of idols, while they themselves set an example to all the curates of their diocese and lead them to admit the reformation to which we are invited by the Word of God, and which fully corresponds both to the order and to the practice of the primitive Church. At the same time let him show that he does not approve of those who have refused to obey the Word of God, while on the other hand he keeps his agreement with the true servants of God and cultivates fraternal union with them. As for those goods that are called temporal, whether they consist in jurisdiction or in annual revenue: although their origin has sprung from that corruption which in no way can be tolerated alongside the pure simplicity of the spiritual ministry, yet as long as things remain so confused, possession may in a certain manner be left to them, with this exhortation added: let them see how they dispense what they know is dedicated to God, both so that they do not profane things sacred to God, and so that they keep themselves within the moderation that befits true bishops. As for the rest, if such goods have been added to their revenues and lordships, it would be better for them to be content with the name of protectors of the Church, taking care that the Word of God be proclaimed and received from the ministers, and that the worship of God remain safe and sound; so that meanwhile they do not meddle in the ministry, but strive to be present at it, relying on or supported by a certain show of name and royal authority. And in that case, even if some weakness were present which was not excusable, they should nevertheless be tolerated, while they are regarded as honoured members of the Church to which they devote themselves.

units.la: IO. CALVINVS N. N. S. D.
units.tr: John Calvin to N. N., greeting

units.la: Ad diuersos articulos.
units.tr: On various articles.

units.la: Dilectissimi fratres, quia ad singulas Ecclesias quae apud vos sunt,hoc scriptum spectat maxima ex parte, commodissimum duximus nostras ad vos literas communes dare,non tam vt labori parceremus,quàm ne multum verborum fructra singulis literis insumendum effet:ac praesertim vt ita praesafi tis,nos diuersis literis nihil diuersum respondere,cum nostrum consensum omnibus perinde constare velimus.Primùm igitur, quia accepimus quibusdam non probari , cùm de fide interrogantur, vt si minus instructi deprehendantur , ad Coenam non tanti sper admittantur, donec melius profecerint, petimus ab illis, quibus iste rigor non placet,in nomine Domini, ne sibi in malo suo indulgeant : neque etiam hoc captent, vt indulgeatur illis, quod ad ipsorum exitium pertineret. Nota esse debet illa Apostoli sententia inter Christianos:sacrilegij teneri quicunque panem Domini indignè comederint. Vt verò quis illo digne vtatur,
units.tr: Most dear brethren, since this writing concerns for the most part all the churches that are among you, we have thought it best to send you one common letter from us, not so much to spare ourselves labour as so that much wordage would not have to be spent on separate letters to each church. We also wish you to see that we do not answer differently in different letters, since we want our consent to stand equally for everyone. First, then, since we have heard that some people are not approved when they are questioned about faith, and that if they are found poorly instructed they are not admitted to the Supper so readily until they have made better progress, we ask those who do not like this strictness, in the name of the Lord, not to indulge themselves in their own harm, nor to seek this, that they be allowed what would bring about their own ruin. The saying of the Apostle should be well known among Christians: whoever eat the bread of the Lord unworthily are guilty of sacrilege. But that anyone may use it worthily,

units.la: Epist.374. Ex Gall.
units.tr: Epist. 374. From the French.

units.la: 1.Cor.11. vtatur, requirit vt sese quisque probet: vbi satis docet, nō debere ad istam mensam accedere, qui ad sese probandum non sunt idonei. Quisquis igitur non ante in structus in fide, temere ad Coenam accedit, iram Dei provocat: vt qui ita indignè vetantur accedere, non habeant quod querantur, dum ita illorum salus potius procuratur. Ac si quisque satis saperet, sibi quisq; iudex idem esset: sed quia multi parum sibi attendunt, expedit certum ordinem extare in Ecclesia, vti nunquam non hoc obtinuit, ne profanentur Sacramenta. Vbi enim promiscuè omnes admittuntur sine delectu, contemptus est quem Dominus tolerare non potest. Dominus ipse Coenam solis discipulis distribuit. Quare quis quis non est institutus in Euangelii doctrina, nam debet accedere ad Domini institutum. Non igitur molestè ferat, dum ipsius Christiani sincerus probatur saltem tenuissimè, cum ad Coenam admittendus est. Idem etiam statuendum est in toto statu & ordine disciplinæ, quæ in Ecclesia vigere debet, ne admittantur illi qui indigni iudicati fuerint. Scimus hoc novū videri illis qui non tenent discrimen inter iugum Domini nostri Iesu Christi, & Papatus tyrann dem: sed vestrum est potius infspicere quæ sit Domini voluntas, vt illi vos submittatis, quàm vt frena laxetis vestris affectibus. Nam & infidelium olim exemplum hic nobis incutiat pudorem oportet. Vtcunque enim illi non eam reuerentiam adhibuerint in suis superstitionibus, quæ à nobis præstanda est in Sacramentis: hoc tamen habuerunt pro confesso, ab illis arcendos esse, quicunque aliquo crimine polluti censerentur. Cum vero Coena Domini alicui interdicitur, ne se perpetuò excludi existimet, neque coiici in desperationem, sed hoc fieri vt sese deiiciat, vtque alij per illum discant. Cum igitur hoc totum Dei verbo præscribatur, petimus à vobis per Dominum, ne vos subiicere pudeat rei de qua compertum habetis, quàm te ita quàmque sancta sit. Non est etiam nobis dubium, esse apud vos delectos homines & constitutos ad corrigenda scandala, ad monendos qui peccauerint, atque illos agnoscendos qui sese hoc neste gerunt. Qui autem ad ea munera vocantur, eam humanitatem eámque moderationem præ se ferre debent, ne censuræ prætextu quis infametur, aut premiatur calumniis, falsis delationibus aut suspicionibus. Atque hoc attingimus nominatim, vt ita admittantur quæ fient admonitiones, vt is ad quem pertinebunt, audiatur etiam si quam excusationem habeat, ne aperiatur fenestra detrahendi, & molestia afficiendi innocentes. Sic igitur expediet aliquem pro officio deferri apud Seniores, vt delato sese purgare liceat: ac si innocens comperiatur, delator seorsim corrigatur vt minus circumspectus: sin vero malus animus ad delationē calumniosam ipsum impulit, illud esset plane intolerabile. Vestrum est autem orare Dominum, vt quos ad istud munus elegistis,illos Spiritu suo regat cum vera prudentia, mansuetudine,zelo,restitudine.Vos vero ipsos finite frænis illis contineri,quibus omnes opus habemus,& quorum est inspicere in alios,primi illi & corrigantur & castigentur.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 11. Whether one uses it, the Apostle requires that each person examine himself. In that passage he teaches plainly that those who are not fit to examine themselves ought not to approach that table. Therefore, whoever has not first been instructed in faith and rashly comes to the Supper, provokes the wrath of God. Those who are thus forbidden to come unworthily have no ground for complaint, since their salvation is in this way rather looked after. If everyone were wise enough, each would be his own judge; but because many pay too little heed to themselves, it is expedient that a fixed order exist in the Church, as it has always done, so that the sacraments are not profaned. Where all are admitted without distinction, there is a contempt that the Lord cannot tolerate. The Lord himself distributed the Supper only to his disciples. Therefore, whoever has not been instructed in the doctrine of the gospel ought not to approach the Lord's institution. Let no one, then, take it ill that, when he is to be admitted to the Supper, the sincerity of his Christianity is tested, even if only very slightly. The same must also be decided for the whole state and order of discipline that ought to flourish in the Church, so that those who have been judged unworthy are not admitted. We know that this seems new to those who do not distinguish between the yoke of our Lord Jesus Christ and the tyranny of the Papacy. But it is more your business to examine what the will of the Lord is, so that you submit yourselves to him, than to loosen the reins for your own passions. For the example even of unbelievers ought here to put us to shame. Although they did not show in their superstitions the reverence that we must show in the sacraments, nevertheless they held it as settled that those who were judged polluted by some crime were to be kept away from them. When the Lord's Supper is forbidden to anyone, he should not think that he is shut out for ever, nor be cast into despair; rather, this is done so that he may humble himself, and so that others may learn through him. Since all this is prescribed in God's Word, we ask you, through the Lord, not to be ashamed to submit yourselves to a matter about which you know how holy it is. Nor do we doubt that among you there are chosen men appointed to correct scandals, to admonish those who have sinned, and to acknowledge those who conduct themselves in this way. Those who are called to these duties ought to show such humanity and such moderation that no one is defamed under the pretext of censure, or harassed by calumnies, false accusations or suspicions. We mention this specifically so that the admonitions that are given are received in such a way that the person they concern is heard, even if he has some excuse, so that no opening is left for slander and for troubling innocent people. Thus it will be appropriate for someone to be reported to the elders in the course of duty, provided the accused is allowed to clear himself. And if he is found innocent, the accuser should be corrected privately for being less careful. But if a malicious spirit has driven him to a calumnious accusation, that would be plainly intolerable. It is your task to pray the Lord that he may guide those whom you have chosen for this office by his Spirit, with true prudence, gentleness, zeal and uprightness. As for yourselves, let yourselves be restrained by those reins which we all need, and those who are in a position to look into the faults of others should first be corrected and chastised themselves.

units.la: Inter alia vitia quæ multi sibi condonari vellent, vnum est: nempe vt liceret ipsis beneficia illa Papatus,quæ vocant,restine-re,vel de illis negotiari,quod omnino extra disceptationem dã-nandum est.Crimen est enim quod Christianismo dis rte repugnat,si quis sese talibussacrilegiis contaminet.Alterum est non tanti momenti in speciem,offerre nempe infantes ad Baptismū Papisticum,aut prosequi funera mortuorum. Atqui vbi illi,qui hoc sibi licere aut non imputari volunt, seriò seipsos excusse-rint, ac Deum iudicem sibi posuerint ante oculos, facile in se-ipsos ferent sententiam. Satis enim est notum vobis,quàm fœ-dis & detestandis superstitionibus, adeóque meris Satanæ iudi-cris,fœdatus sit Baptismus in Papatu. Vt quisquis offert illic in-fantem, polluat ipsum quantum in ipso est, non autem benedi-ctionem Domini ipsi procuret. Participare etiam precibus quæ fiunt pro mortuis, hoc non aliud esse potest, quàm tantundem derogare vnico Christi Domini nostri sacrificio, quando purgatorium solis humanis satisfactionibus nititur. Videte igitur an illud sit excusabile, & an vbi quis ita scandalizauerit Ecclesiam,dissimulari debeat,aut pro leui delicto tolerari: acnon postus cam reprehensionem mereatur,quæ illum moneat,vt sit cautior in posterum , cui tale aliquid acciderit. Scimus in quibus versemini angustiis,ac vobis quoque pro charitatis officio con dolemus:sed quia nihil iuuatet à nobis absolui, sinite in vos po tus ex Dei verbo ferri sententiam, vt totum istud vestro bono & saluti cedat.
units.tr: Among the other faults that many would like to be pardoned, one is this: that they might be allowed to keep those benefices of the Papacy, as they call them, or to trade in them, which must without any question be condemned. For it is a crime that flatly contradicts Christianity, if anyone defiles himself with such sacrileges. Another, which seems of little importance, is to offer infants to Papist baptism, or to attend the funerals of the dead. Yet when those who want this to be permitted to them, or not to be held guilty, have seriously examined themselves and set God as judge before their eyes, they will easily pass sentence on themselves. For it is well enough known to you how baptism in the Papacy has been defiled by foul and detestable superstitions, and indeed by mere judgments of Satan. So whoever offers an infant there pollutes it as far as he is concerned, and does not secure the blessing of the Lord for it. To take part in prayers made for the dead can be nothing other than to detract just as much from the one sacrifice of Christ our Lord, since purgatory rests solely on human satisfactions. See therefore whether such a thing is excusable, and whether, when someone has so scandalised the Church, it ought to be overlooked or tolerated as a slight fault, and whether he should not rather deserve a rebuke that warns him to be more cautious in future. We know the straits in which you are placed, and we grieve for you as a matter of the duty of charity; but since it does nothing for us to absolve, allow sentence to be pronounced upon you from the word of God, so that this whole matter may turn to your good and your salvation.

units.la: Audimus aliud inter vos disceptari,nempe an liceat cuiquam ingerere sese ad prædicationem eò loci vbi Ecclesia reformata extet, etiamsi ab Ecclesia hoc ratum habitum non sit. Atque vt quis ita se gesserit, an etiam liceat ad illum audiendum venire. Hic autem oramus vt diligenter attendatis, vtcunque Dominus inter vos corpus aliquod Ecclesiæ constituerit, inde non sequi, multa non esse toleranda in ἀταξία publica quæ istic adhuc vi-get,quæ in Ecclesia bene constituta ferenda non sunt.Non lo-quimur de illis actionibus,in quibus peccatur in Deum,quæque ipsius verbo repugnant. Sed quum miseri Papistæ sint, vt oues dispersæ,vbi Dominus excitat certos homines, qui illos ex dissi-patione colligant,tamen abest vt talem opem illis oblatam im-pedire ipsi debeamus,vt potius eo casu nobis vsurpandum sit il-lud Domini,vt habeamus pro nostris tum, qui non sint aduer-
units.tr: We hear that another question is being debated among you: namely, whether anyone may thrust himself into preaching in a place where a reformed Church exists, even if the Church has not approved this; and whether, if someone so behaves, it is lawful to go and hear him. Here, however, we beg you to consider carefully that, however the Lord may have established some body of the Church among you, it does not follow that the many things still prevailing in the public disorder [ἀταξία] there are not to be tolerated, which in a well-established Church are not to be borne. We are not speaking of those actions in which sin is committed against God and which contradict his word. But since the Papists are wretched, like sheep scattered abroad, where the Lord raises up certain men who gather them out of their dispersion, far be it from us to hinder such help offered to them. Rather, in that case, we must adopt the saying of the Lord, that we should count as on our side those who are not against us,

units.la: Luc.9. tum nos. Quia hic non agitur de munere Pastoris, sed tantum de illius opera, qui ita docet, ut sensim ad Christū adducat, qui erat prius dispersi. Nō agitur etiam de ordine perpetuo, sed de medio quodam extraordinario, quo Dominus vitur in confusione Papatus. Recordamini etiam illius Apostoli sententiæ, qui non sunt Ecclesiæ domestici, ipsius regulæ & statutis nō sint subiecti. Obseruandum denique quod alibi tradit idem Apostolus, offerri nempe gaudij materiam, vbi Euangelium promouetur, etiāsi hoc per occasionem fiat. Quamobrem nobis non videtur interdicendum fidelibus ab istorum prædicatione, modò illic extet proba & pura doctrina: abest autem precatio omnis superstitiosa, aut quæuis alia mixtura. Neque tamen hoc eò pertinet, ut inde occasionem captent subducendi se à cœtu ordinario, aut etiā segnius conueniendi ad ordinarium Pastorem audiendum. Incitandi sunt potius & confirmandi ad tenendum ordinem, in quem ipsos semel introduxit Dominus. Ac proinde attendite vobis, ne circumueniamini ab illis qui obliqua via tentant abducere oues à grege, ut à pastu ordinario alienas reddant. Interea si qui illos adeunt non curiositate quadam illecti, neque ut à recta via declinent, tolerandi quidem illi videntur.
units.tr: Luc. 9. For here we are not concerned with the office of the minister, but only with the work of one who so teaches that he gradually leads to Christ those who were previously scattered. Nor is this a matter of a perpetual order, but of a certain extraordinary means, which the Lord uses in the confusion of the Papacy. Remember also the saying of the Apostle, that those who are not of the household of the Church are not subject to its rule and statutes. Finally, we must observe what the same Apostle teaches elsewhere: that an occasion for joy is offered when the gospel is advanced, even if this happens by chance. Therefore it does not seem to us that the faithful should be forbidden to hear these men, provided that sound and pure doctrine is preached there and there is no superstitious prayer or any other admixture. Yet this does not mean that they should take the occasion to withdraw from the ordinary assembly, or to come more sluggishly to hear the ordinary minister. Rather they are to be urged and confirmed in keeping the order into which the Lord has once brought them. Therefore take heed that you are not circumvented by those who, by a crooked path, try to lead the sheep away from the flock and make them strangers to the ordinary pasture. Meanwhile, if some go to them not drawn by any curiosity, nor so as to turn aside from the straight way, such people do seem to be tolerable.

units.la: Gravius est vero quod quidam adeunt etiam conciones monachorum, qui verbum aliquod veritatis inspergunt suis mendaciis, vt ita gratiam sibi conciliēt. Quasi vero non ipsi nimis propensi ad vanitatem sumus, & ad mendacia, vt noui Magistri quærendi sint, qui nos eò inducant. Neque immerito illos punit Dominus, qui talibus mixturis delectantur: vt reipsa constat illorum plurimos, & à veritate deflectere, & Satanæ impostoris infici. Neque id aliunde est, quàm ab ipsorum ingratitudine, quando putæ doctrinæ non acquiescunt, sed vento pasci cupiunt. Iusto vero iudicio Dominus istos inebriari finit. In genere cauendum vobis, ne sitis ex eorum numero qui semper discūt, vt ait Paulus, & nunquam scientiam veritatis assequuntur. Memores etiam esse vos velimus illius Domini admonitionis, vt caueatis vobis à fermento Scribarum & Pharisæorum: quando ita nobis difficile est qui eo semel aliquando imbuti fuimus, vt eo vere expurgemur, ac nihil ex illa corruptione fæcis in nobis hæreat. Quid iis igitur fiet, qui inter illos etiam viuere cupiunt, atque ita sponte Deum tentant? Idem exsistimandum est de toto genere precularum, quas horas & patinostras vocant, & cæteris eiusmodi idololatriæ instrumētis. Sic enim idola nobis prorsus esse debent execrationi, vt ne illorum quidem nomina nobis in ore sint, vt est in Psalmo 16. Cui respondet & illud Ezechielis, quòd si bene pœnitet anteactæ vitæ, & viarum nostrarum in quibus erravimus, illarum nos etiam non pudere non poterit. Sunt aliæ corruptelæ, quæ eò etiam accedūt. Aliæ enim & quasi Cartas vocant, vt ad superstitiones non pertinuerint, sed aliorum vitiorum fuerint instrumenta, multum quoque damni & malorum passim intulerunt. Ac quod iStiusmodi lusus attinet, non ita prorsus à nobis damnarentur, si in eorum vsu, quod licet, locum haberet: sed vbinam extat illa sobrietas? Primum nō est aliud vspiā, quod ita homines quasi viscō impediat, adeò vt totos eorum sensus occupet, non secus ac fascino correptos. Sed quemadmodum qui illis assueuerunt, non ita possunt illis valedicere: ita etiam qui pedem aliquantum retulerit, illa omnia facile fastidiet. Porrò qui sese ita iis rebus dedunt, atque ita insani-re pergunt, inciduntin multas molestias. Notum est, vix vnquâ lusus effluere sine blasphemiis, fraudibus atque excandescentia: quoties etiam familiæ inde accisæ. Nemo enim tenet modum, quin sese exhauriat, aut sensim ipse consumat. Maximè vbi de lucrando agitur, fieri vix potest, quin Deus ipse lædatur aliquo modo. Quare magnopere expedit ab illis esse alienos, quantū fieri potest. Optimum verò abstinere prorsus. Petimus etiam à vobis ne hoc à nobis audire molestum sit, vt quæ inter vos sunt Ecclesiæ, quorum Pastores oneribus similiarum numerosiorum premuntur, illis curetis prospectum & illorum necessitati. Non potest, enim qui inopia premitur, libero esse animo & quieto, vt sese totum muneri suo impendat, dum familia egens est, neque habet quo subueniat, ad manum. Atque omnino cum audimus ex Dei verbo, illos esse nobis alendos qui Ecclesiæ inseruiunt, non est hoc merè restringendum ad ipsorum personas. Nam & ipsi essent inhumani, nisi æquè de suis ac de se ipsis essent solliciti. Præstamus hic quod possumus: sed ea est inopia, cui plane subleuandæ impares sumus. Sed quia non dubitamus, quin satis per vos officium sitis facturi, vt non accedat nostræ exhortationis stimulus, satis erit verbo hoc apud vos indicasse. Atque (vt tandem absoluamus) quia non dubitamus vos impeti quotidie ab hostibus fidei, pe: imus à vobis, vt certetis constanter, neq; remittatis quidquā, donec omnes impetus Satanæ superaueritis, atque ad beatā metam ex intento cursu peruéneritis. Agnoscite verò quæ nobis cœlitus arma suppeditantur: nempe vt ad eum vnum nos recipiamus qui nos ea gratia dignatur, vt in suum præsidium recipiat, atque ita in patientia possideamus animas nostras. Vi enim peruincere nobis fas non est: & probè nostis quàm male succedat quicquid temerè aggredimur sine heri mādato. Dura omnino tentatio & superatu difficilis, dum impios ita videmus sævire aduersus innocentes: sed intruendū est ad quid vocati simus. Et quando ita fert voluntas Domini vt affligamur, idque pro causa tanti momenti, ne alienum à nobis videatur. Enitamur potius tius discere ea ratione quàm isti caducae vitae praeferenda sit Dei gloria, & quam illi debemus obedientia, ipsumque Christi regnum, & spes illa vitae aeternae. Hic igitur ut & in genere illud quod Scriptura docet in usu habete, ut vobis renuntiando, sacrificium sitis boni odoris Domino. Precamur Dominum, vobis primum impendio a nobis salutatis, ut vos respiciat atque asserat ab omnibus aduersariis, suo praesidio tueatur, regat Spiritu, atque omni bono cumulatos reddat.
units.tr: It is more serious that some people also attend the sermons of the monks, who sprinkle a little word of truth over their lies so as to win favour for themselves. As if we ourselves were not far too inclined to vanity and to lies, so that we must seek out new teachers to lead us into them! The Lord rightly punishes those who delight in such mixtures: as indeed is evident, since many of them both turn aside from the truth and are infected by Satan the impostor. And this comes from nothing else than their own ingratitude, since they do not rest content with sound doctrine but want to feed on wind. By a just judgment the Lord allows them to be intoxicated. In general you must take care not to be among those who, as Paul says, are always learning and never arrive at the knowledge of the truth. We also want you to remember the Lord's warning, that you beware of the leaven of the Scribes and Pharisees, since it is so hard for us, once we have been steeped in it at some time, to be truly cleansed of it, and so that nothing of that corrupt dregs clings to us. What, then, will become of those who want to live among them too, and so tempt God of their own accord? The same must be judged of the whole class of prayers which they call hours and paternosters, and of other instruments of idolatry of this kind. For idols ought to be utterly detestable to us, so that not even their names are on our lips, as is said in Psalm 16. To this corresponds also that word of Ezekiel: if we truly repent of our former life and of the ways in which we have gone astray, we will not be able to avoid being ashamed of them. There are other corruptions which also belong here. Some, which they call "Cartas," do not pertain to superstitions but have been instruments of other vices, and they have everywhere brought much harm and many evils. As for such games, we would not condemn them altogether if their use, which is permitted, had a place: but where is that sobriety? First, there is no other trap which so entangles people, as with birdlime, that it occupies their whole senses, just as if they had been struck by a spell. But as those who have grown accustomed to them cannot easily bid them farewell, so also one who has drawn back a little will easily come to loathe all those things. Moreover, those who give themselves over to such things and keep raging in this way fall into many troubles. It is well known that games seldom pass without blasphemies, frauds and anger; how often families have been ruined by them too. For no one keeps measure, but drains himself, or gradually wears himself away. Especially where gain is at stake, it can hardly happen that God himself is not in some way injured. Therefore it is greatly to your advantage to keep away from them as far as possible. Best of all is to abstain altogether. We also ask you, and may it not be troublesome to hear this from us, that you take care for the churches among you, whose ministers are burdened with the weight of very many families, and provide for their need. For a man pressed by want cannot have a free and quiet mind, so as to devote himself wholly to his office, while his household is needy and he has no means at hand to help. And indeed, when we hear from the Word of God that those who serve the Church must be supported, this is not to be restricted merely to their persons. For they themselves would be inhuman if they were not equally concerned for their families as for themselves. We do here what we can: but the need is such that we are plainly unequal to relieving it. But because we do not doubt that you will do your duty sufficiently through yourselves, so that the spur of our exhortation is not needed, it will be enough to have indicated this word to you. And (to conclude at last) because we do not doubt that you are attacked daily by the enemies of the faith, we ask you to fight constantly and to give up nothing, until you have overcome all the assaults of Satan and have reached the blessed goal by a steady course. But recognise what weapons are supplied to us from heaven: namely, that we betake ourselves to that one who deigns to grant us this favour, that he receive us into his protection, and so in patience we may possess our souls. For it is not right for us to conquer by force: and you know well how badly whatever we rashly undertake without the Lord's command turns out. The trial is indeed harsh and hard to overcome, while we see the wicked raging thus against the innocent: but we must consider to what we have been called. And since it is the will of the Lord that we be afflicted, and that for a cause of such great importance, let it not seem strange to us. Let us rather strive to learn by this means how much the glory of God is to be preferred to this fleeting life, and what obedience we owe him, and Christ's own kingdom, and that hope of eternal life. Here, then, keep in use, as in general, what Scripture teaches, that by renouncing yourselves you may be a sacrifice of sweet odour to the Lord. We pray the Lord, first for you, whom we salute with the greatest affection from ourselves, that he may look upon you, defend you from all adversaries, protect you by his help, rule you by his Spirit, and heap you with every good.

units.la: AD QVINQVE ARTICVLOS.
units.tr: ON THE FIVE ARTICLES.

units.la: AD primum articulum in quo quaeritur quousque extendi possit consilium relinquendi viri vel uxoris, vbi agitur de idololatria vel persecutione fugiēda. Ego sane auctor fuerim coiugatis, ne sese mutuo relinquat, nisi prius omnibus quae ad comparem lucrifaciendum, & secum deducendum facere potuerint. Tam arcta enim coniunctio tale officium partium requirit, & constat praeter scandala & alia mala quae ex leui & temerario discessu nasci possunt, qui se ita gerit, non praestare fidem quam parti religio tenebatur. Primum igitur si vir vel uxor quae repugnat Euangelio finit parte alteram pure Deum colere, eo casu neque viru ab uxore, neque uxore a viro discedere fas esse censeo. Si vero una pars alteri hic obstiterit, pars fideli se am constantia retineat, ne a recta via vsquam deflectat: studeat etiam ita amice se gerere, ut animum partis quae obstitit, emolliat. Atque ita nemo discedat nisi vrgeatur manifesto periculo, ut si una partium alteri minas intendat, atque id saepe fieri contingit, aut aliunde insteret persecutio: ut, in summa, certa necessitas eo fidele adigat, neque spōte diuortia facta dici possint. Neque tamen sequitur ex tali etiam discessu libertatem acquiri parti fideli nouae conditionis quaerendae: cum discessus ille non pertineat ad vinculum coniungi soluendum, sed ad euitandum hostium Euangelij furorem. Imo qui ita discesserit, dare operam debet, si qua fieri possit, ut partem infidelem ad se perducat, donec diuortij causa manifesta deprehendatur. Qui igitur ita separati sunt, agant tanquam in viduitate. Vbi autem adulterium intervenit, nisi illud probari possit, sustinendum est adhuc: nam etiam in eiusmodi casu diuortio locus esse non poterit, sine idonea causae cognitione. Neque vero iudicum iniquitas ad eiusmodi crimen persequendum, parti laesae fraudi erit, quin ipsa coquisitis probationibus det operam, ut rei veritas patefiat. Quod si reus adulterij a lite contestata in iudicio conuictus fuerit, etiamsi non secuta sit iudicis sententia, quae is Ecclesia Christiana admittet ad nouum matrimonium parti tem lęsam, quae talibus primum documentis Ecclesiā de suo iure certiorem reddiderit. Secus enim non admitteretur ab Ecclesia. Ad fecundum articulum vbi de vestibus luctus quas vocant, quæritur, non video magnam illic hærendi occasionem. Res enim per se non ita mala est, vt tolerari non possit, quem admodū & alij quidam defectus, seu infirmitatis humanæ politiæ. Quia igitur non ita præcisè requiritur, vt ab illis rebus abstineatur: si propter illarum neglectum scandalum vel turba vel molestia quæuis creari possit, nolim hic in parte auctor esse abscisæ cuiusdam seueritatis & austeritatis. Monitum simul vnumquemque velim, vt omnes illas pompas, excessus & tot illa minutula quæ dam ita caueat, vt agnosci inde possit eos qui in Dei schola profecerint, non delectari istiusmodi rebus, sed illis vti quasi perfunctorie, vt sese ad vsum receptum accommodent.
units.tr: As to the first article, which asks how far the counsel of leaving a husband or wife may extend, where the matter concerns fleeing from idolatry or persecution: I for my part would advise married people not to leave one another, unless they have first done everything they could to win over their spouse and bring them along. Such a close union requires this kind of dutiful conduct between the partners, and it is plain that, apart from the scandals and other evils that can arise from a light and rash departure, anyone who behaves in this way does not keep the faith that religion requires of each partner. First, then, if a husband or wife who opposes the Gospel does not allow the other to worship God purely, I hold that in that case neither husband may leave wife nor wife husband. If, however, one partner resists the other in this way, the faithful partner should hold fast to their steadfastness and never turn aside from the right way. They should also take care to behave so kindly that they soften the mind of the partner who resists. And no one should depart unless pressed by a manifest danger, as when one partner threatens the other with violence (which often happens), or when persecution presses in from elsewhere. In short, a certain necessity should drive the faithful partner to it, so that the separation cannot be called a divorce made of their own accord. Nor does it follow that by such a departure the faithful partner acquires freedom to seek a new union, since that departure does not concern dissolving the bond of marriage but avoiding the fury of the enemies of the Gospel. Indeed, whoever has departed in this way ought to labour, if it can be done, to bring the unbelieving partner to himself or herself, until the cause of divorce is clearly established. Those who are separated in this way should live as if widowed. But where adultery has intervened, unless it can be proved, the marriage must still be endured; for even in such a case there can be no divorce without a proper examination of the cause. Nor will the unfairness of judges in prosecuting such a crime be a loss to the injured party, so that she or he should not make an effort, by seeking proofs, to bring the truth of the matter to light. But if the accused adulterer has been convicted in court after the case was contested, then even if no sentence of the judge has followed, the Christian Church will admit the injured party to a new marriage, provided that the party has first made the Church aware of their right by such evidence. Otherwise the Church would not admit them. As to the second article, concerning the garments of mourning, as they are called, I do not see much occasion for dispute there. The thing itself is not so evil that it cannot be tolerated, just as certain other defects of human weakness are tolerated. Since it is not required so strictly that one must abstain from those things, if any scandal, disturbance or annoyance could be stirred up by neglecting them, I would not wish to be the author, in this matter, of some cut-off severity and austerity. At the same time I would like to advise each person to take care to avoid all those pomps, excesses and so many little trifles of that kind, so that it may be recognised that those who have made progress in God's school do not delight in such things, but use them rather casually, so as to accommodate themselves to the customary practice.

units.la: Ad tertium articulū, An à Principe peti possit confiscatio bonorum, illorū nomine & gratia, quibus persecutio intenditur. Certum est illud fieri non posse sine peccato. Rescriptū enim siue indultum Principis cōpleētetur omnino blasphemias apertas contra Dei gloriā, quia fiet illic mentio errorum & criminum, & læsæ maiestatis diuinæ damnatis: quod rescriptū erit deinde in iure exhibendum illi, qui eo vti cogitabit. Atque illud est approbationis genus quoddam nullo modo ferendum. Quare nō video vt pio viro & recte instituto in Euangelio eiusmodi fictio nibus sese liceat inuoluere. Tātum si quis existeret bene affectus erga Euangelium, si illi nomen non dedisset, qui beneficium aliquod in tali occasione offerret, non nego quin ea occasione vti liceat: dummodo is qui suis facultatibus cautum vult, non ita eliciat eiusmodi rescriptum Principis, vt vllam Euangelio maculam inurat, aut illius publicationi consentiat, sed ea demum ratione sibi prospiciat, vt cum malo nihil affine habeat.
units.tr: As to the third article, whether a prince may be asked for confiscation of goods in the name and for the sake of those against whom persecution is directed: it is certain that this cannot be done without sin. For a rescript or grant of the prince would wholly contain open blasphemies against the glory of God, since mention would be made there of errors and crimes, and of the majesty of God being violated and condemned; and that rescript would then have to be produced in court by the person who intends to use it. And this is a kind of approval that must in no way be tolerated. Therefore I do not see how it could be permitted to a godly man, rightly instructed in the Gospel, to entangle himself in such fictions. Only if someone who was well disposed toward the Gospel, and had not given his name to it, were offered some benefit on such an occasion by a person, I do not deny that it may be lawful to use that opportunity, provided that the one who wishes to secure his own property does not procure such a rescript of the prince in a way that stains the Gospel or consents to its publication, but makes provision for himself in such a way that he has nothing in common with the evil.

units.la: Ad quartum, liceātne procurare fideli detento liberationem à carcere clauibus suppositis, aut pretio oblato, vel alia quauis methodo. Quod ad me attinet neque eiusmodi cōsilium darem neque probarem etiam: & tamen vbi quid tale tentabitur, commendabo precibus exitum Domino, & gaudiū inde percipiam, si quis sine turba vel scandalo euaserit. Video inter veteres Christianos ipsosq; primum discipulos, vbi quis detinebatur in carcere, Ecclesiā preces adhibuisse, non alia media. Neque Paulus ipse pretio redimi curauit. Quare vt omne malum euitetur, præstiterit ab eiusmodi rationibus abstinere. Ac nihilominus si cui ita euadere contigerit, vt illius factum non approbem, Deum quidem laudabo pro liberatione eiusmodi, tolerabo etiam potius qui ita sibi consuluerit, quàm vt illum condemnem.
units.tr: As to the fourth question, whether it is lawful to arrange for a faithful man held in prison to be freed by false keys, or by an offered bribe, or by any other method: as far as I am concerned, I would neither give nor approve such counsel. Yet whenever something of that kind is attempted, I will commend the outcome to the Lord in prayers, and I shall feel joy if someone escapes without disturbance or scandal. I see that among the early Christians, and the first disciples themselves, when someone was held in prison, the Church applied prayers and no other means. Paul himself did not take care to be redeemed with money. Therefore, so that every evil may be avoided, it would be better to abstain from such methods. Nevertheless, if it should happen to someone to escape in this way, I will not approve his action, but I will praise God for such a deliverance, and I will tolerate the one who has so provided for himself rather than condemn him.

units.la: Ad vltimum, quomodo agendum cum illis qui Cœnæ Domini facti participes ad idololatriam redierint: maximè necessarium est, ordinem aliquem extare: qui sit fræni instar, & simul hīc hic vt in omnibus modū tenere expediat. Nempe vt neq; Cœna profanata ita fuerit, vt nulla censura & correctio subsequatur delectum: neque ea seueritas adhibeatur, quæ infirmorum animos labefactet. Satis igitur erit, exempli causa, si cui semel contigerit ad superstitiones defl ectere, modo in lapsu non perstiterit, aut nihil grauius admiserit, vnde idololatriæ scelus exaggeretur, & veluti conduplicetur, satis erit inquam, si illi Cœna Domini semel interdicatur. Ante omnia autem inspiciendū serio, qua resipiscentia præditus quisque sit. Quod ad bis terve relapsos, maiori seueritati debet esse locus multis de causis: tum ne nimia facilitas illos in peccato lactet & foveat, unde certum exitium sibi accersant tandem, tum vero ne exponatur ludibrio nomen Dei, & quæ concipiuntur sponsiones: ac ne etiā inde sensim quis que diffluendi occasionem caperet, unde tandem legitimæ reuerentiæ loco merus contemptus succederet.
units.tr: As to the last question, how one should deal with those who, having been made partakers of the Lord's Supper, have returned to idolatry: it is most necessary that some order should exist, which acts as a bridle, and at the same time it is expedient here, as in all things, to keep due measure. That is, the Supper should not be so profaned that no censure and correction follows the offence, nor should such severity be applied as would weaken the minds of the weak. It will therefore be enough, for example, if someone has once happened to turn aside to superstitions, provided he did not persist in the lapse or commit anything more grave by which the crime of idolatry is magnified and, as it were, doubled; it will be enough, I say, if he is forbidden the Lord's Supper once. Above all, however, one must examine seriously what repentance each person has. As for those who have relapsed two or three times, there ought to be a greater severity for many reasons: partly so that excessive indulgence does not flatter and foster them in sin, whereby they finally bring certain ruin upon themselves; and partly so that the name of God and the vows that are made are not exposed to mockery; and also so that people do not gradually take an occasion to fall away, whereby in the end bare contempt would take the place of due reverence.

units.la: QVAE RATIO A VIRO PIO TENERI POSSIT, vbi Religionis causa domo migrare cogetur.
units.tr: What course a godly man may hold when he is forced to leave home for the sake of religion.

units.la: SI quis coniugatus sub Papatus tyrannide, solum mutare cogatur, cum ei minus liceat apud suos pure Deum colere: Primum consulam vt omnem operam det, quo vxori persuadeat, vt ipsi comitem se adiungat. Cum enim vir mulieris sit caput, maximè ad officium ipsius pertinet, vt ad viam salutis eam perducam curet, quantum in ipso erit. Quare fas non erit Christiano homini prætextu Religionis deserere vxorem: enitatur potius omnibus modis vt ipsam Domino lucrifaciat, vt vterque deinde illi vno affectu obsequatur. Acsi res primum non succedet, pergendum nihilominus, vtcunque illam præduram & peruicacem experiatur: adeoque ne vitæ quidem parcendum est. Præterea dum ad eam docendam & admonendam intentus est, precetur Dominum, vt Spiritu suo ipsam afficiat, cum fine illius ope omnis labor frustra impendendus sit. Si quæritur, quousque sese extendant huius officij limites, non ita pollum hic quicquam præscribere. Tantum admonitum velim, vt tam cordate & recto zelo opus perseguatur, vt intra paucos dies tanto magis illud promoueat. Sicenim adest Dominus illis qui integrè in eo se gerunt: quicquid sit, non debet molestius ferre moram illam vxoris, aut frangi animo propter illius duritiem: modò ipse interea ab idololatria alienus sit. Cauédum enim ne dum vxorē ad Deum ducere studet, ipse sese ab illo auertat. Tandem vbi ita omnibus perfunctus est, vt iam ei citum non sit apud suos agere extra omne idololatriæ cōfortium: quin potius ad migrandum adigetur persecutionibus, minis, aut alia vi maiore: tū demū si se subduxerit, habebit idoneam excusationem, quòd per eum non fleterit, quò minus suam secum comparem adduceret. Neque tamen ita etiam um discedat, quasi se ab illa omnino subduce- ret: quin potius ita se erga illam gerat, ut nullam rationem omittat, qua eam è luo illo educat ex quo ipse prior emerserit, ut am bo simul Deum colant. Quum se ita gesserit, non erit quòd illi imputetur, quasi diuortium sponte captarit, aut à consorte sese subduxerit. Vbi enim vrget necessitas, ius nullum amplius est e- iusmodi vxoris in virum, cui ut satisfaciat, à Dei cultu sese auer- tere cogatur. Sic igitur officio functus erit, qui omnibus prius tentatis, ex illo carcere tandem euolauerit.
units.tr: If a married man under the tyranny of the Papacy is compelled to change his place of residence, since he may not worship God purely among his own people, I would first advise him to make every effort to persuade his wife to join him as his companion. For since the husband is the head of the wife, it belongs especially to his duty to bring her to the way of salvation, as far as lies in him. Therefore it will not be lawful for a Christian man to desert his wife under the pretext of religion; rather he should strive by every means to win her for the Lord, so that both may then obey Him with one mind. And if the matter does not succeed at first, he must nonetheless persevere, however stubborn and obstinate he finds her; and so he must not spare even his life. Moreover, while he is intent on teaching and admonishing her, let him pray the Lord to move her by His Spirit, since without His help all labour must be spent in vain. If it is asked how far the limits of this duty extend, I do not presume to prescribe anything precise here. I would only advise that the work be pursued with such a sincere and right zeal that within a few days he may advance it all the more. For the Lord is present with those who conduct themselves faithfully in it. Whatever happens, he ought not to bear the wife's delay more impatiently, or be broken in spirit because of her hardness, provided that meanwhile he himself keeps free from idolatry. For he must take care lest, while he seeks to lead his wife to God, he himself turn away from Him. At last, when he has tried every means, so that it is no longer possible for him to live among his own people apart from all fellowship with idolatry, but he is driven to depart by persecutions, threats, or some other greater force, then, if he withdraws, he will have a fitting excuse, namely that it was not through him that his wife failed to bring her companion with him. Yet he should not depart in such a way as though he were wholly withdrawing from her; rather he should so conduct himself towards her that he omits no means by which he may lead her out of that bondage from which he himself has first emerged, so that both may worship God together. When he has behaved in this way, it will not be held against him as though he had sought a divorce of his own accord or had separated himself from his partner. For where necessity presses, a wife of this kind has no further right over her husband, such that he should be forced to turn away from the worship of God to satisfy her. Thus he will have discharged his duty, who, having tried everything beforehand, at last escapes from that prison.

units.la: Si quis liberorum Pater cogatur etiam solum mutare, siue vi præsente siue etiam sponte ut idololatriam fugiat, cõsulo ut eos secum deducat tanquam præcipuum thesaurum & peculium ipsi collatum à Domino. Nam ipsis semel relictis imminebunt statim ea vincula, quæ perpetuum illi officij erga ipsos neglecti mœrorem afferent. Nisi fi emancipatis facultates deinde diuidendo adsignet, quod nullo modo ei committendum est: quia vel eo modo vincula ipsis induet, donec vigesimum quintum annum impleuerint. Atque ut contingat tutor bene affectus, nihil tamen per se audebit: neque etiā penes illum erit quicquam vendere vel alienare. Imò vix ex ipso reditu annuo quicquam in Patris vsum decidet, quia ad reddendam ipsius quoque reditus rationem tenebitur. In summa, qui suas facultates ita relinquit liberis, aut illis induit laqueum, aut saltem ita implicat, ut ex voragine vix sit deinde emergendi locus, quantumuis ad eam rem bene ex sese illi affecti essent.
units.tr: If a father of children is compelled to change his place of residence, whether by force being present or even of his own accord, in order to flee idolatry, I advise that he take them with him as his chief treasure and property entrusted to him by the Lord. For once they have been left behind, those bonds will at once press upon him which will bring him the lasting grief of having neglected his duty towards them. Unless, indeed, he assigns to them, once they have been emancipated, their property by dividing it, which must in no way be entrusted to him, since in this way he would fasten bonds upon them until they have completed their twenty-fifth year. And although the guardian may be well disposed, he will not dare to do anything on his own; nor will it be in his power to sell or alienate anything. Indeed, scarcely anything from the annual income will be spent for the father's use, since he will also be bound to render an account of that income. In sum, whoever leaves his property to his children in this way either sets a noose for them or at least entangles them so that there is scarcely any place left for them to emerge from the abyss, however well disposed they might be of their own accord towards that end.

units.la: AD CERTA QVAEDAM CAPITA.
units.tr: CONCERNING CERTAIN CHAPTERS.

units.la: Cum de augendo Ministrorum numero agitur, pertinet tum ad Cõsistorium, tum ad totam Ecclesiam illius rei iudicium. Videndum autem & an facile reperiri possint, & an Ecclesiæ rationes idoneæ sint, ad incrementum illud ut par est sustinendum vel secus. Quod ad idoneitatem tum Pastorum, tum etiam Presbyterorum siue Inspectorum, ut nemo tam exacte munere fungi potest, quin melius aliquid etiamnum desiderari in optimo quoque possit, ita etiam nisi illi admittuntur, qui & legitime sunt electi, & quod possunt, præstät, nullus erit turbarū & contentionum finis in Ecclesia. Statuere vero ut locupleres, & qui dignitate ac nomine sunt cõspicui ad munera Ecclesiastica eligatur, illud plane repugnat ordini & regulæ Christianæ. Imò eo vno constat maxime nos veros esse Christi discipulos, vbi non pudet illorū administrationi nos subiicere, quorū in mūdo minus erit pretium & commendatio Functio Consistorij habet suos fines ac limites, intra quos sese contineant qui ad illam exercendam vocantur. Eorum est igitur inuigilare gregi Domini, vt Deus pure colatur. Admonere item tam priuatim quam publice: ac porro excommunicare etiam cum res exiget. Vbi ita se Consistorium continebit, neque sese vlterius porriget, quam per Dominum liceat, nul la obstrependi occasio dabitur. Iam vero praeter cofessum illum Ecclesiasticum qui habetur in Consistorio, instituere consilium aliquod Ecclesiasticum vt vocant, non videmus vt hoc cum ipsius Domini institutione coueniat: imo mere nouum opus illic agnoscendum atque denuntiandum est, ne variis mutationibus deinde fenestra aperiatur. Ac praesertim illud nonnisi certa ruinam afferre potest, cum qui aduersantur veritati, inde occasione insultandi arrepturi sint, quasi eo nomine aduersus statum politicum aliquid fieret. Nec tamen improbamus vbi necessitas inciderit, eligi viros consultos & experientia praeditos, qui videant, quid sit ere Ecclesiae: ita tamen vt hoc etiam munus sit ad tempus, & extraordinarium, ordinarium vero nullo modo.
units.tr: When the question of increasing the number of ministers arises, the judgment on that matter belongs both to the Consistory and to the whole Church. It must be considered both whether suitable men can easily be found, and whether the resources of the Church are adequate to sustain such an increase, as is fitting, or not.
